dsid_54754e549f154f24a6f897d662cfde5d, source_type: confluence, title: observability safety gates and export contract for the serving runtime, content: summarynnthis page defines the observability safety gates and the telemetry export contract for redwood inferences serving runtime. it is intended for runtime engineers, sres, and profiling/observability owners who implement collection pipelines, ci gates, and on-call automation. the document covers: the canonical telemetry schema we export from the runtime, automated safety gate thresholds and actions, sampling/bandwidth budgets, build-time validation, and an operational runbook for escalations.nngoalsnn- provide a single source of truth for the telemetry fields the runtime must emit.n- define deterministic safety gates that prevent regressions in visibility, regressions that could materially affect slo investigations, or excessive telemetry costs.n- ensure export formats and tags are stable enough for downstream consumers (dashboards, tracing, billing, ml evals).n- provide a clear rollout and ci strategy so instrumentation changes are reviewed and verified.nnscopennapplies to:n- all changes to the serving runtime codepath that add/modify telemetry exports (traces, metrics, logs, profile payloads).n- telemetry export agents (forwarders) shipped with the runtime.n- ci/bench gating that validates telemetry contract.nnout of scope:n- consumer-side dashboard changes.n- third-party observability services that only transform data downstream (but contract-breaking transforms are subject to this doc via related_pages).nnhigh-level contract summarynn- every request processed by the runtime must emit: a request-level trace span, a request metrics sample, and a compact request provenance blob when trace_sampling1.n- telemetry keys and types must match the schema in the telemetry schema section below.n- any change to the schema must include: (1) feature flag guarded codepath, (2) ci validation using canonical examples, (3) rollout with shadow-mode 4872 hours, (4) automated rollback on gate failures.nntelemetry schema (canonical fields)nnbelow we list the canonical fields and expected types. downstream consumers rely on these exact keys. columns: field type description requirednn- request_id string globally unique per logical request requiredn- model string model identifier (eg: redwood/gptx-7b-v1) requiredn- model_variant string quantization/precision/variant tag (eg: awq-8, q3f) optionaln- tenant_id string customer tenant if present, otherwise system requiredn- route string api route or logical operation (generate, embedding, rerank) requiredn- seq_len integer request token count or prompt length requiredn- tokens_generated integer tokens produced by model (post-generation) optionaln- start_timestamp iso8601 when request first entered runtime requiredn- end_timestamp iso8601 when response left runtime requiredn- kernel_hint string selected kernel identifier (eg: kernel-v2-mma32) optionaln- kvcache_hit_ratio float 0.01.0 estimate for prefix cache effectiveness optionaln- alloc_bytes integer peak additional gpu allocation during request optionaln- error_code string runtime/serving error when applicable optionalnnexport contract and delivery expectationsnn1) formats supported: json-lines for metrics/profile blobs otlp/http for traces prometheus-compatible summaries for aggregated series.n2) field names must be snake_case as above. no field renames without formal change process.n3) each exported record must include a schema_version field (string) and an event_type tag (tracemetricprofile).nnsafety gates (automated checks executed pre- and post-deploy)nnwe operate two classes of gates: ci-time (build/test) and production-time (runtime monitors rolling-deploy blockers).nna. ci-time gates (unit/integration tests)n- telemetry schema compile check: any change to exported structs must pass jsonschema validation against canonical_examples/.json.n- example generation: build generates canonical telemetry samples (1 per api route) and asserts presence of required fields.n- diff alert: pr adds a one-line human-readable change note in telemetry-changelog.md.nnb. production-time gates (automated monitors)n- visibility slo: 99.0 of successful requests must contain request-level trace_id and start_timestamp. if visibility drops below 98.5 for 5m, auto-open an incident and roll back the rollout wave.n- schema compliance: 99.5 of telemetry ingested in the last 1h must match schema_version vx.y or acceptable backward-compatible versions. if compliance 2.5x and cost estimate 20/hour/node, apply automatic sampling increase (see sampling rules) and notify on-call.n- high-cardinality protection: unknown tag cardinality (unique tenantroutekernel_hint pairs observed) must not grow 20 per hour. exceeding threshold triggers temporary cardinality-cap enforcement (truncate tag) and throttles diagnostics.nnactions associated with gate failuresnn- alert and create incident if threshold breached.n- circuit-break to conservative telemetry mode (reduced sampling, drop heavy profile payloads).n- if degradation coincides with increased error rates 0.5 p95 request latency percentiles, start automated rollback of rollout wave.nnsampling and bandwidth budgetnn- default request trace sampling: 0.1 per-tenant baseline global floor 0.01.n- profiling payload sampling (heavy): 1 in 10,000 by default.n- adaptive ramping: if latency slo violations are detected for trace-sampled requests, decrease trace sampling proportionally to reduce overhead.n- bandwidth control policy (node-local): token-bucket that allows up to b1000 telemetry items/min sustained with burst 2000 for short spikes. config snippet: nn--- yamlntelemetry_export:n node_budget_per_min: 1000n burst_allowance: 2000n budget_cost_weights:n small_metric: 1n trace: 5n profile_blob: 50n---nnbuild-time validation and ci integrationnn1. telemetry unit-tests: each new pr touching runtime exports must add a test that 1) introspects the exported proto/struct, 2) serializes a canonical sample, and 3) validates against jsonschema.n2. integration smoke: canary job runs runtime in local harness and verifies that the exported telemetry can be ingested by the canonical ingestion lambda.n3. preflight: as part of release build, generate a telemetry-change report artifact. pr must have explicit sign-off from at least one telemetry reviewer.nnruntime enforcement mechanismsnn- export agent shields: an ffi agent process buffers and enforces budget it will drop or compress payloads if budget exceeded.n- feature flags: new fields are behind feature flags. feature flags are two-phase: opt-in test, shadow export, then opt-in full.n- telemetry schema adapter: small compatibility layer that translates older schema_version to latest normalization for downstream consumers during transition.nnoperational runbook (if a gate trips)nn1. pager: receive pagerduty alert (observability-gate).n2. initial triage (within 5 min): confirm gate (query ingestion).n3. if visibility slo violation confirmed, set export_agent to conservative mode via runtime api: post /admin/telemetry/mode - mode:conservative.n4. if conservative mode does not restore visibility within 10 minutes, roll back the rollout wave following runtime rollback sop (see related_pages).n5. post-incident: create a telemetry incident ticket and attach canonical payload samples.nnintegration checklist for changing schemann- add fields behind ff and document intent in telemetry-changelog.md.n- add unit and integration tests with canonical samples.n- create rollout plan with shadow period (minimum 48 hours).n- notify owner teams and sre with scheduled rollout.n- add automatic fallback that strips new fields when consumers report errors.nnexamplesnnexample exported request metric (json-lines):nn dsid_786575bd28b844a0a155a158f8d0057e, source_type: confluence, title: kv-prefetch audit and experiment guide, content: overviewnthis document is a pragmatic audit experiment playbook for evaluating and iterating on kv-cache prefetch strategies in the redwood serving runtime. it consolidates instrumentation, test-corpus design, hypothesis-driven experiments, safety gates, and clear remediation steps to validate that a prefetch change improves throughput or cost without regressing latency or output fidelity.nnintended audiencen- runtime engineers (kernel and scheduler owners)n- performance and profiling teamsn- sres running capacity and incident drillsn- release engineers validating runtime rolloutsnngoalsn1) provide a repeatable audit checklist to assess existing prefetch behaviour and its observability gaps.n2) define experiment templates (canary, a/b, ramp) with required telemetry, sample sizes, and slo-aligned success criteria.n3) offer rollout and rollback runbook steps with specific threshold values and playbook actions.nnscope and non-goalsn- scope: kv prefetch heuristics, warmup policies, prefetch batch sizing, prefetch prioritisation across tenants/model variants, and their impact on kernel scheduling and kv cache hit/miss behavior.n- non-goals: changes to model serialization or offline model compile pipeline (handled elsewhere). this guide does not substitute for security or compliance sign-off for customer-sensitive telemetry.nnbackground and terminologyn- kv prefetch: pro-active population of a models key-value cache before predicted use (e.g., during warmstart or after canary shadowing).n- warmstart: placement of a model variant onto a gpu with pre-warmed kv state for a target user session.n- prefetch window: sequence-length- and token-count-derived horizon for which we request early kv population.n- shadow traffic: mirrored request streams used for dry-run experiments.nnobservability contract (what to collect)ncollect these signals for all experiments. instrumentation must be enabled at service, runtime-shard, and kernel levels.n- metrics (per-second or histogram as noted):n - kvcache.prefetch.requests_total (counter)n - kvcache.prefetch.success_ratio (gauge) success / attempts per minuten - kvcache.hit_ratio_by_prefix_length (histogram buckets by prefix tokens)n - kvcache.prefetch_latency_p50/p95 (histogram ms)n - kernel.queue_wait_ms (histogram) labeled by priority bucketn - runtime.topology.eviction_rate (counter per shard)n - gpu.memory.oversubscription_events (counter)n - request.latency.p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end including network kernel)n - request.tail_slo_breaches (counter) where tail slo : requests configured target (e.g., 95th 120ms)n - cost.per_token.estimated (derived using token counts kernel accounting)n- traces: request span with children: prefetch.call, prefetch.cache_write, kernel.exec, kv_lookup include tags: model_id, variant_tag, session_id, shard_id, kernel_id, tenant_id, prefetch_hint_id.n- logs: structured event for prefetch decisions: decision:prefetchskip,reason:prefix-matchheuristicmanual,estimated_tokens:n,evicted:truefalse,latency_ms:n as newline-delimited json to the observability pipeline.nnaudit checklist (baseline assessment)n1) baseline traffic capturen - capture at least 72 hours of representative production traffic or use a validated synthetic corpus (see test corpus section).n - ensure sampling includes peak hour and low-hour slices.n2) reproduceability of prefetch eventsn - verify prefetch events are traceable to requests in shadow logs. correlate prefetch_hint_id across traces.n3) telemetry completenessn - confirm all metrics and traces listed in observability contract are present. if any are missing, add target instrumentation and replay a synthetic subset to validate.n4) heatmaps and correlation checksn - build the following diagnostics:n - heatmap: prefix_length - prefetch_success_raten - scatter: per-request prefetch_latency vs request_latencyn - timeline: eviction_rate vs memory_pressuren5) failure mode inventoryn - enumerate cases found in logs (e.g., prefetch eviction within 2s, prefetch causing kernel queueing). classify severity and likely root causes.nntest corpus recommendationsn- canonical corpora: use a mix of (a) production-scrubbed request traces, (b) replayable synthetic sessions (session bundles), and (c) jittered-edge sequences to exercise long prefixes.n- session bundle format (jsonl, one session per line):n session_id:s-123,model:vicuna-13b-q4,turns:hello,summarize: ...,followup: ...,timestamps:...n- size guidance: minimum 5000 sessions covering 10k prefix variations for a statistically meaningful p95 comparison in canary windows.nnexperiment designsnall experiments must be hypothesis-driven and limited in blast radius. follow the experiment checklist below.nna) shadow (no impact) hypothesis testn- goal: validate prefetch hit-rate and false-positive eviction costs without affecting production latency.n- method: mirror 1:1 traffic to a shadow runtime with the new prefetch strategy. do not route responses.n- duration: 4872 hours or until 10k prefetch decisions observed.n- required metrics: kvcache.prefetch.success_ratio, eviction_rate, prefetch_latency.n- success criteria: improvement in prefetch.success_ratio by 5 or reduction in cold-start kernel execs by 10 with no increase in eviction_rate 2 over baseline.nnb) canary small ramp (impactful but controlled)n- goal: measure end-to-end latency and kernel queue impact under production conditions.n- method: route 1 of traffic to canary pool with the new prefetch strategy. use canary tags and separate metrics.n- observation windows: 1 minute, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours.n- safety gates (auto-rollback triggers):n - request.tail_slo_breaches increases by 20 relative to baseline in a 15-minute window - immediate rollback.n - kernel.queue_wait_ms.p95 increases by 30 sustained for 10 minutes - immediate pause and manual review.n - gpu.memory.oversubscription_events 0 (new events) in canary - pause.n- success criteria: no slo breach increase p95 request latency change within /- 5 and prefetch.success_ratio improved or neutral.nnc) a/b experiment with fidelity measurementn- goal: measure fidelity / model output drift when prefetching influences kv state timing (rare but possible).n- method: 50/50 split where identical prompts are sent to control (no change) and candidate (new prefetch). collect deterministic evaluation prompts and human-eval random sample.n- fidelity metrics: bleu/rouge/embedding-similarity on deterministic prompts, plus small human quality cohort (n200) to detect hallucination/regression.n- success criteria: embedding cosine similarity 0.995 on deterministic prompts and no statistically significant decrease in human-score (alpha0.05).nntelemetry and sample size calculationsn- latency experiments: to detect a 5 p95 change with 90 power typically needs o(20k) p95 samples per group for canaries prefer longer duration instead of increasing blast radius.n- hit-rate experiments: to detect a 5 absolute increase in hit rate with alpha0.05/power0.8, thousands of prefetch events are required depending on baseline rate use exact binomial test calculator.nnexperiment orchestration and dashboardsn- dashboards: create kernel.queue_wait_ms.n- failure: prefetch evicts hot state for other tenants.n - mitigation: implement tenant-aware prefetch budgeting and soft reservations.n- failure: memory oversubscription from source_type: confluence, title: microprobe-operator-manifest-and-sampling-economics-playbook, content: title: microprobe operator manifest and sampling economics playbooknnsummaryn-------nthis playbook defines the microprobe operator (mpo): a lightweight runtime component and operational pattern for high-signal, low-cost instrumentation inside the redwood serving runtime. the mpo is intended for short-duration probes that diagnose kernel-level behavior, kv-cache warmup characteristics, and burst-tail latency without blowing observability budgets or perturbing production scheduling.nnpurpose and scopen------------------n- purpose: provide a repeatable contract and operational playbook for introducing, tuning, and retiring microprobes across the runtime surface.n- scope: in-process and sidecar probes that run on serving nodes (gpu hosts and inference routers). not intended for deep kernel modifications or external end-to-end tracing frameworks.n- audience: runtime engineers, profiler owners, oncall sres, and experimenters.nnownership and stakeholdersn-------------------------n- mpo owner: runtime-profiling team (team contact: @priya).n- observability integration: telemetry-adapters team (reviewer: daniel wu).n- scheduling/kernel impact review: kernel-scheduler team (reviewer: marco alvarez).n- release gate: must pass profiling lab acceptance criteria (see benchmarks section).nndesign principlesn------------------n1. non-invasive: probes must avoid long-lived locks or changes to scheduler behavior.n2. budgeted: every probe is assigned a fixed cost budget (cpu ms, bytes emitted, average frequency).n3. lightweight sampling: prefer probabilistic micro-sampling over continuous tracing.n4. amortize work: aggregate telemetry at the operator boundary and send compacted summaries.n5. kill-switchable: mpos must honor a single operator-level remote flag for immediate global disablement.nnmicroprobe operator architecturen-------------------------------n- components:n - controller (central): issues probe manifests and budgets via configstore.n - agent (node-level mpo): receives manifests, enforces local budgets, collects samples, and emits compressed summaries.n - exporter: adapts compressed summaries to the telemetry pipeline and decides real-time vs batched ingestion.nnprobe typesn-----------n1. touch probes: measure cold-start wall time of model shard activation (100-200ms probe).n2. kernel rendezvous probes: sample kernel launch latencies and kernel queue lengths during busy windows.n3. kv-cache sweep probes: light samplers that touch a small prefix/slot distribution to estimate hit rates.n4. tail request microtraces: capture 1-in-n full traces for requests above a latency threshold.nnbudgeting and economics (mandatory fields)n-----------------------------------------neach probe manifest contains a table of required budget fields. operators must supply limits before activation.nntable: probe budget schema (csv-like)nprobe_id,owner,probe_type,cpu_budget_ms_per_min,node_emit_bytes_per_min,max_sample_rate_per_min,ttl_minutes,backoff_policynmp-touch-01,priya,touch,200,50000,20,60,exponentialnmp-kernel-queue-01,marco,kernel-rendezvous,500,120000,10,30,linearnmp-kv-sweep-01,analytics,kv-sweep,150,30000,30,120,exponentialnmp-tailtrace-rare-01,sre,tail-trace,1000,500000,2,1440,manualnnsampling policy and heuristicsn-----------------------------n- default mode: budgeted probabilistic sampling. node agent maintains a leaky-bucket counter per-probe.n- threshold triggers: probes may be promoted to higher fidelity if a health rule fires (e.g., rising tail latency 99th percentile threshold).n- reservoir caps: maximum number of retained microtraces kept in memory (default 32 per node).n- backoff behaviors: exponential backoff when emission errors 5 for 2 consecutive minutes.nnoperational lifecycle (step-by-step)n-----------------------------------n1. draft manifest: profiling owner prepares probe manifest with budgets and rationale.n2. risk review: submit to kernel-scheduler and telemetry-adapters for capacity and perturbation review.n3. canary rollout (week-long): enable mpo at 1 of serving fleet with debug-level local sampling, validate no scheduler jitter.n4. acceptance: run the profiling-lab acceptance checklist and cost simulation (see benchmarks).n5. production rollout: ramp to target fraction with progressive budget tightening.n6. retention and sunset: every probe must include a sunset_date or a quarterly review ticket.nndeployment checklistn---------------------n- manifest fields populated: probe_id, owner, budgets, safe-mode flag, ttl.n- canary matrix defined: which clusters, node classes, and models.n- observability: metrics defined (probe_success_rate, emit_errors, budget_utilization).n- kill-switch validated end-to-end.nnrunbook: probe-overload incident (short)n---------------------------------------n1. symptoms:n - sudden spike in exporter queue length or telemetry pipeline backpressure metrics.n - increased scheduler soft-evictions during probe windows.n2. immediate actions:n 1. trigger mpo global kill-switch via configstore.n 2. identify offending probe_id using controller logs and budget_utilization panel.n 3. notify probe owner and kernel-scheduler oncall.n3. recovery:n - after kill, verify exporter queues drain and scheduler quota stabilizes for 10 minutes.n - if safe, re-enable in canary with 10x tighter budget and monitoring.nnbenchmarks and acceptance criterian----------------------------------n- cpu overhead: 1) in 95th percentile latency for the canary cohort.n- safety: killing mpo must restore baseline within 2 minutes.nnmeasurement harness (how to verify)n----------------------------------n1. use the profiling dsid_32b82510542a43e09e67cbf403ec639d, source_type: confluence, title: stratified latency replay and microburst sampling playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook defines the stratified latency sampling (sls) pipeline and the microburst sampler for redwoods serving runtime. the goal is to capture representative traces across latency bands and microburst events with bounded cost, enable high-fidelity replays for kernel-sensitivity debugging, and produce actionable signals for autotune and regression detection. this is operational guidance for engineers on the runtime, telemetry, and replay tooling.nnwhy this existsnn- static uniform sampling misses rare high-latency clusters and transient microbursts that correlate strongly with kernel regressions.n- sls guarantees coverage across p50/p95/p99 bands while keeping the sampling budget predictable.n- microburst sampling captures short-lived queuing spikes and nvlink/pcie anomalies that are often the root cause of degraded tail latency.nnaudience and scopenn- primary: runtime engineering, profiling, and sre teams.n- scope: production-hosted and dedicated clusters (not air-gapped private installations unless customer opts in). provides config recommendations, playbook run steps, and troubleshooting guidance.nnkey concepts and terminologynn- stratified latency sampling (sls): sampling policy that partitions requests by latency buckets and assigns per-bucket rates.n- microburst: brief (100ms to 10s) increase in request concurrency or kernel contention causing tail latency spikes.n- shadow replay: deterministic replay of sampled requests in a sandboxed profiler service (prof-run) to reproduce kernel execution history.nnslos and budget constraintsnn- sampling budget: target telemetry overhead 10 rps.nnhigh-level pipelinenn1. runtime annotates each request with runtime.request.latency_ms, request.signature (hash of model, seq_len, route, user_tier), and sample_hint fields.n2. sampler service (samplerd) consumes metrics stream and applies stratification policy.n3. selected samples are persisted to the trace-store (s3 prefix: s3://redwood-profiles/cluster/date/) and indexed in the replay-catalog.n4. shadow replays are scheduled to prof-run with kernel tracing enabled and archived as replay-artifacts.nnsampling policy (recommended config)nn bucket latency range (ms) target share sample rate (requests/sec per 1k rps) rationale n----------------------------:-------------:---------------------------------------:----------n hot 0 - 50 60 300 captures normal traffic shape n warm 50 - 200 30 150 captures slow tails and emergent drift n cold 200 - 2000 8 40 focuses on p99 anomalies n burst 2000 or queued50 2 10 microburst and severe degradation cases nnoperational knobs dsid_6f1ab3eb8b6140358789c13b5ddb0523, source_type: confluence, title: kernel determinism investigation and replay protocol, content: summarynnthis playbook documents a structured protocol for investigating non-deterministic latency or correctness regressions that appear to originate from kernel execution or kernel-selection behavior in the serving runtime. it provides a hypothesis-driven replay workflow, the required data artifacts, checklist of signals to inspect, and a reproducible sandbox procedure for iterating on kernel-level fixes. the intent is to reduce mean time to root cause for kernels that produce intermittent slow paths or divergent outputs across retries.nnscopenn- applies to runtime versions 2023.11 and later and to kernels managed by the kernel mapper (kmux).n- focuses on issues where the same request input produces different execution characteristics (latency, kernel choice, memory usage) across retries or across replicas.n- excludes: pure network/transit issues (see eng-sre incident runbooks), and model-level randomness that is expected by design (e.g., sampling).nndefinitionsnn- determinism failure: the same complete request (headers, model version, prompt, session kv state) produces different kernel selection, resource consumption, or tail latency without legitimate reason.n- replay corpus: a saved set of requests runtime context used to deterministically re-run workload in a sandbox.n- kernel trace: annotated timeline of kernel lifecycle events (select, load, handshake, exec_begin, exec_end, evict).nnwhen to use this playbooknn- tail latency spikes that correlate with kernel-change events in traces (kernel_swap, kernel_fallback).n- flaky regression test failures in the throughput bench that cannot be reproduced by simple load replay.n- divergent telemetry across cold and warm runs where kv cache and kernel-choice paths differ.nnprerequisites and permissionsnn- access to the runtime profiling cluster and ability to create sandbox sandboxes (incubation clusters) request via infra-ticket-jenkins with tag profiling-sandbox.n- read access to kernel binary registry and kernel metadata (kmux/catalog service).n- tools: local replay harness (repo: infra/replay-harness), trace-analyzer (repo: infra/trace-tools), a copy of the production request-sampler export (stored in /artifacts/profiles/year-month).nnhigh-level workflow (quick view)nn1) triage: capture representative requests and runtime traces.n2) isolate: build a minimal replay corpus that reproduces divergence.n3) replay: run deterministic replay under the sandbox with full kernel telemetry enabled.n4) hypothesize: enumerate kernel-level causes and validate by controlled experiments.n5) patch validate: deploy kernel fix to canary and run regression suite.nndetailed procedurenn1) triage and initial capturenn- collect the request payloads and full trace ids for 10-100 affected requests. include: request headers, model namecommit, session_id, router route, and exact timestamp. example required metadata json (single-line):nn request_id:,model:redwood-open-7b-v2,seq_len:128,route:text.generate,trace_id:abcd-1234nn- pull the trace events using trace-analyzer:nn trace-analyzer export --trace-id abcd-1234 --out /tmp/trace-abcd.jsonnn- identify kernel events: search for event types select_kernel, kernel_load, kernel_exec_begin, kernel_exec_end, kernel_evict. record kernel binary hash, node id, and slot_id.nn2) build a deterministic replay corpusnn- for each request record: full body, headers, kv cache snapshot (if available), and the exact model variant string (e.g., redwood-open-7b-v2@2025-11-03-rc2).n- prefer requests that: previously triggered both fast and slow outcomes have identical inputs and show kernel-choice flip in traces.n- store corpus under: /artifacts/replay-corpora/kernel-determinism//corpus.jsonl . each line is a json object with flat fields.nn3) configure sandbox for deterministic replaynn- provision a sandbox cluster with identical software abi and kernel catalog. use the infra playbook to pin: runtime image (sha256), kmux catalog revision, and kernel binaries revision.n- enable deterministic runtime flags in /etc/runtime/conf.d/replay.toml:nn replayn enforce_kv_snapshot truen disable_dynamic_kernel_prefetch truen seed_kernel_mapper fixednn- start the sandbox runtime with kernel telemetry level 5 and trace sampling 100.nn4) run replay and capture outputsnn- command (example):nn replay-harness run --corpus /artifacts/replay-corpora/kernel-determinism//corpus.jsonl --target --concurrency 4 --repeat 3 --write-traces /tmp/replay-tracesnn- for each replay iteration, collect: latency percentile distribution, kernel trace files, kernel binary checksums, and any divergence in model output tokens.nn5) hypothesis generation and controlled experimentsnn- common hypothesis patterns to test: n - kernel handshake race: two concurrent requests caused a different kernel to be selected due to a timing window.n - eviction-induced cold path: aggressive eviction policy allowed a kernel to be reloaded on hot path causing startup overhead.n - kernel compatibility fallback: kmux selected a binary variant with different quantization profile under memory pressure.n - kernel threading/sm occupancy variance: same kernel executed at different gpu occupancy causing execution time variability.nn- for each hypothesis, design a minimal controlled change and re-run the replay:n 1. handshake race: serialize kernel selection with a 10ms mutex and observe if flip disappears.n 2. eviction: increase kernel hot-cache ttl to 300s during replay.n 3. compatibility fallback: pin kernel selection to the primary binary (force_kmux_binary ).n 4. occupancy: pin gpu affinity to single sm mask to measure per-kernel exec time variance.nn6) observability signals and acceptance thresholdsnn- signals to inspect (table described in text):n - metric: kernel_select_rate_change - acceptable: acceptable: p95 within 10 of baseline for stable kernelsn - event: kernel_fallback_count - acceptable: 0 for deterministic-corpus runsn - log: handshake_timeout - acceptable: nonenn- if any signal exceeds the threshold, mark the hypothesis as plausible and escalate to kernel-owner.nn7) patch, canary, and regression suitenn- if a kernel binary or kernel-selection policy change is required:n - build a kernel binary with debug symbols and a short-lived toggle flag.n - canaries: deploy to a single sandbox shard and run the full replay corpus 10x.n - regression: add a synthetic test to the microbench that replays the failing corpus and assert medianp95 latency and kernel_fallback_count 0.nn8) postmortem artefacts and documentationnn- required artifacts for closure: replay corpus, raw traces, diff of kernel catalog, patch pr, canary run logs, and regression test entry. attach these in the incident ticket and link to this playbook.nnownership and escalationnn- primary owner: runtime-kernel-team (pager: oncall-kernel).n- secondary owner: eng-sre (for sandbox provisioning and capacity).n- escalation path: kernel oncall - runtime tech lead - infra reliability director. use the standard oncall escalation timeline (15/45/90 minutes).nnexample artifactsnn- minimal trace extract (abbreviated):n n trace_id:abcd-1234,n events:n ts:1678891200123, type:select_kernel, binary:khash:aa11,n ts:1678891200150, type:kernel_load, node:gpu-17,n ts:1678891200450, type:kernel_exec_begin, slot:3,n ts:1678891200788, type:kernel_exec_end, duration_ms:338n n nn- sample replay harness command for deterministic pinning:n replay-harness run --pin-binary aa11 --concurrency 1 --repeat 5 --write-traces /tmp/fixednnrunbook checklist (quick reference)nn- collect 10 representative traces and request payloads.n- build deterministic replay corpus and upload to artifacts storage.n- provision sandbox with pinned runtime kernels.n- run replay with telemetry 100 and collect kernel traces.n- validate hypothesis with at least one controlled experiment.n- patch and run canary regression tests.n- document artifacts and close incident with owners tagged.nnappendix a: common pitfallsnn- missing kv snapshot: if kv cache snapshot is not available, some nondeterminism will persist. always prefer requests sampling orchestrator and fidelity proxy playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook documents the dynamic sampling orchestrator (dso) and fidelity proxy components used by the serving runtime to coordinate low-cost, high-signal profiling. it describes the architectural intent, sampling contracts, fidelity downgrade/upgrade semantics, operational runbook for experiments, benchmarks to validate signal quality, and the rollout/rollback checklist. this doc is intended for runtime engineers, sres, and applied ml engineers running fidelity experiments.nnmotivationnn- profiling every request at full fidelity (full traces kv captures kernel timings) is too expensive at production scale.n- we need a way to: 1) sample requests adaptively to maximize root-cause signal, 2) ensure fidelity changes preserve slos, and 3) make sampling decisions auditable and reproducible for offline analysis.nngoalsnn1) maintain production p95 latency slo (default target: 95th cohort - global) and automated safety checks (latency regressions, kernel slowdowns, cost delta).nnarchitecture (high level)nn- dynamic sampling orchestrator (service name: trace-orch): central policy engine decides which requests to sample and at what fidelity.n- fidelity proxy (service name: fidelity-proxy): per-node agent that enforces sampling decisions and manages local buffering of high-fidelity payloads (kv snapshots, kernel timelines) to avoid backpressure on the request path.n- telemetry gateway (telemetry-gw): shuffles sampled payloads to the trace storage cluster (efficient path: clickhouse for lightweight signals, tempo for full traces, and s3 for archived kernel captures).n- signal bus (kafka topic: profiling.signals): publish sampling decisions and metadata for downstream validation and audit.nndecision flownn1) incoming request passes through request-classifier (runtime sidecar).n2) request-classifier sends a minimal decision-query to trace-orch (0.5ms p99 target).n3) trace-orch evaluates active policies and returns a sampling token with fidelity profile id (fpid).n4) fidelity-proxy receives token and applies local capture hooks. large captures are stored to node-local disk and streamed to telemetry-gw asynchronously.nnsampling contracts and fidelity profilesnn- fidelity profile (fpid): a small json manifest (versioned) describing captures and retention. example fields: trace_level: lightstandardfull, kv_capture: noneheadersprefixfull, kernel_timings: offsummaryfull, max_size_mb: n, sample_weight: float.nn- contract guarantees:n - if trace-orch returns an fpid, the fidelity-proxy will attempt to apply that profile failures fall back to the next-fallback fpid(typically standard).n - the orchestrator will not assign an fpid whose expected resource cost would exceed configured budget for the node or tenant.n - fpid manifests are immutable after release updates produce new fpids (semver).nn- default profiles we maintain:n - low-signal: trace_levellight, kv_capturenone, kernel_timingsoff, sample_weight0.01n - standard: trace_levelstandard, kv_captureheaders, kernel_timingssummary, sample_weight0.1n - high-fidelity: trace_levelfull, kv_captureprefix, kernel_timingsfull, sample_weight1.0nnadaptive sampling algorithm (summary)nn- inputs: recent latency cohorts, kernel error rates, cold-start frequency, historical entropy of outputs.n- outputs: an fpid assignment probability per request class.n- key features:n - burst protection: stop increasing sampling during node-level thermal events.n - diversity heuristic: prioritize sampling across user cohorts to avoid measurement bias.n - reproducible seeding: sampling decisions derive from request_id fpid salt so experiments can be replayed deterministically.nnfidelity proxy internalsnn- components: enforcer (applies fpid), capture buffer (capped circular buffer on local disk), uploader worker pool (streams to telemetry-gw), circuit-breaker (drop captures under pressure).n- safety invariants:n 1) if disk usage 65 of capture partition, circuit-breaker engages and downgrades to standard for new captures.n 2) uploader concurrency is rate-limited by node-configured egress bandwidth (default 25mb/s).n 3) captures accepted for telemetry have an upper bound max_size_mb oversized captures are truncated with metadata note.nnoperational runbook: quick triagenn1) symptom: sudden increase in p95 latency correlated with deployment of a new fpid.n - step 1: check trace-orch policy list: kubectl -n observability get cm fidelity-policies -o yamln - step 2: validate per-node circuit-breaker: kubectl logs fidelity-proxy- grep circuit_breakern - step 3: inspect sampling rate stream: kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --topic profiling.signals --from-beginning jq .fpid uniq -cn - step 4: if majority of nodes report circuit-breaker engagements, revert latest fpid roll (trace-orch rollback api).nn2) symptom: missing high-fidelity traces for a specific tenant cohort.n - step 1: confirm active fpid for tenant: curl -s - step 2: check fidelity-proxy accept logs for that tenant: journalctl -u fidelity-proxy grep n - step 3: verify telemetry-gw ingress metrics (telemetry-gw/metrics http). if telemetry-gw is saturated, enable graceful backpressure mode (telemetry-gw api /v1/backpressure/enable).nnbenchmarks and validationnn- purpose: ensure sampled traces have sufficient signal and that sampling scheme does not materially change runtime slos.n- minimum validation suite:n 1) replay fidelity parity test: sample n10k requests with both standard and high-fidelity fpids in shadow mode and compare kernel timing distributions (ks-statistic 2x planned budget.nnbenchmark harness commands (examples)nn- start a shadow sampling run:n curl -x kernel_fails/sec, fidelity-proxy_truncations, telemetry-gw_ingress_errors.n - duration: min 2 hours at 99th percentile load.n3) cohort rollout (20 traffic):n - run benchmark parity test on cohort traffic.n - if any of the alerts fire (latency, cost, or disk pressure), immediately revert to previous fpid.n4) global rollout: ramp to 100 over 6 hours with automated guardrails.nnautomated safety playbook, content: summaryn-------nthis playbook defines an operational pattern for using variance-driven sampling of runtime telemetries to detect and triage episodes where cost per inference increases without a corresponding improvement in quality, or where latency and cost diverge across model variants and request shapes. it describes instrumentation signals, adaptive sampling algorithms, alert thresholds, an investigation checklist, and recommended mitigations for common root causes (batching, kv cache misses, kernel fallbacks, and topology shifts).nngoalsn-----n- detect sustained or transient incidents where per-token cost increases by 15 at p95 or where p99 latency regresses 20 relative to baseline.n- reduce alert noise by focusing on high-variance cohorts (request shapes, model versions, customer tiers).n- provide a repeatable triage procedure that links telemetry to kernel-level causes and cost drivers.n- recommend automated mitigations (sampling rate changes, fallback model routing, cache warmups) and manual runbook steps.nnscope and audiencen------------------n- audience: runtime sres, serving runtime engineers, performance engineers.n- in-scope: host-level and request-level telemetry, kernel selection traces, kv cache hit/miss streams, batching metrics, model variant rollouts.n- out-of-scope: model quality evaluation (use eval-harness), billing reconciliation (use finance tooling).nnkey signals to collectn----------------------n1. per-request fields (high-cardinality):n - request_id, route, model_version, sequence_length, input_tokens, output_tokens, customer_tiern - observed_latency_ms (end-to-end), kernel_latency_ms, queue_time_ms, batch_size_at_execn - kvcache_lookup_count, kvcache_miss_count, quantization_variantn2. host kernel telemetry (low-cardinality):n - gpu_util_pct, sm_occupancy, memory_bytes_used, kernel_name, kernel_duration_msn3. cost proxies:n - per-token_cpu_cycles_estimate, gpu_kernel_time_ms, amortized_gpu_seconds_per_calln4. sampling metadata: sampling_bucket, sampling_score, sample_decision_reasonnndesign: variance-driven samplingn--------------------------------nrationale: static uniform sampling underweights rare but high-cost request cohorts (large seq len, model rollouts). the variance-driven sampler adapts sampling probabilities to prioritize cohorts with high observed variance in cost and latency so investigations capture explanatory examples with fewer total samples.nnalgorithm (overview)n1. define cohort key hash(route, model_version, sequence_length_bin, customer_tier).n2. maintain rolling window (w 30m default) for each cohort with sample_count n and sample variance s2 of cost-per-token and p95 latency.n3. compute score alpha normalized(s_cost) beta normalized(s_latency) gamma recent_regression_indicator. (alpha0.5, beta0.4, gamma0.1 default).n4. map score - sampling probability p min(p_max, base_p (1 score)). defaults: base_p0.01, p_max0.5.n5. persist sampled traces to the central profiling sink for kernel traceback and storage.nnimplementation notesn--------------------n- use probabilistic reservoir per cohort to bound memory.n- normalize variances using robust scaling (median absolute deviation) to avoid outlier blowup.n- ensure sampling decisions are deterministic per request_id sampling_window to prevent double-sampling across retries.n- emit sampler telemetry: sampling_rate_by_cohort, missed_samples_due_to_quota, reservoir_overflow_count.nnconfiguration table (recommended defaults)n----------------------------------------n parameter description recommended value rationale n------------------------------------------------------n w rolling window length 30m captures transient episodes without excessive state n base_p baseline sampling probability 0.01 keeps storage costs low n p_max sampling cap 0.5 ensures hot cohorts dont overwhelm storage n alpha,beta,gamma score weights 0.5,0.4,0.1 weight cost more than latency n sequence_length_bins bins for cohorting 15 and sampled p95 cost-per-token increases 10 over baseline for w.n - severity: p2.n - pager: sre on-call.nn- alert: cost-latency divergencen - trigger: cohort where cost-per-token recent rollouts and routing rules (route table changes, firmware/drivers, gpu topology reassignments).n7. if hardware-level (sm occupancy low, gpu underutilized) correlate with small batch sizes or content: summary:nnthis playbook documents the procedures, signals, and automated probes we use to detect, stabilize, and harden execution cohorts in the redwood serving runtime. an execution cohort is a set of requests that share scheduling, kernel, and fidelity characteristics (for example: short-text-high-priority, long-sequence-batch, or embedding-burst). cohort instability manifests as tail-latency spikes, throughput collapse, or fidelity regressions. this document provides detection heuristics, triage steps, remediation actions, and automation recipes for safe experimentation and production rollouts.nnscope and goals:n- scope: per-region, per-cluster cohorts observed by the runtime scheduler and kernel dispatcher.n- goals: detect cohort divergence within 2x of historical variance restore stable latency slos (p95/p99) within the incident window record a reproducible trace for postmortem.nnkey definitions:n- cohort: logical grouping of requests by route, model_variant, priority_class, and sequence_length_bucket.n- stabilization: actions taken to restore steady-state (admit-rate tuning, kernel rollback, quota adjustments).n- probing: controlled injection of synthetic/recorded traffic to validate remediation.nnsignals to monitor (ranked):n1) latency quantiles per-cohort: p50, p95, p99 sliding 1h/6h windows. thresholds in the metric table (below).n2) kernel execution time histogram for the cohort (microsecond buckets).n3) kv-cache hit ratio and miss spike events.n4) slot reservation churn: rate of slot aborts per minute for cohort slots.n5) backpressure indicators: queue depth, admission queue time, and admission rejection rate.n6) model fidelity regressors: eval-set perplexity/accuracy delta if available.nnmetric thresholds (operational table):n- p95 latency increase 30 relative to 7d baseline - severity: warningn- p99 latency increase 50 relative to 7d baseline - severity: incidentn- kv-cache miss rate baseline 10ppt and sustained 60s - severity: action requiredn- slot abort rate 0.5/min/cohort - severity: action requiredn- admission rejection 1 sustained over 5m - severity: action requirednn(these thresholds are tuned per-customer team owners should publish cohort-specific overrides to the cohort registry.)nntriage checklist (first 15 minutes):n1) confirm signal: cross-check p99 spikes across both telemetry and shadow channels. use ri-metrics query: n ri-metrics query latency.quantilecohortcohort,quantile0.99 - baseline(7d) --window15mn2) capture a live execution trace: n rictl trace collect --cohort cohort --duration 120s --priority high --label incident/incident_idn3) determine scope: single node, shard, or cluster-wide. inspect dispatcher logs for kernel handoffs: n rictl node inspect node_id --filter handoff --since 30mn4) look for concurrent changes: kernel rollouts, kernel plugin activations, quantization-profile updates, or recent canaries.nnisolation containment steps (minutes 1545):n- if p99 ymd)n- if slot aborts are high and localized to a node: cordon node from scheduler for new slot reservations (not evict running work) and migrate new reservations: n rictl node cordon node_id --drainfalsen- if kernel hint mismatch detected (e.g., quantized kernel selected with incompatible sequence length): disable experimental kernel variant for the cohort: n rictl kernel variant disable create deterministic synthetic inputs that exercise known hot paths (kv cache thrash, long-sequence attention, quantized kernel fallbacks) and to run a scheduler shadow to evaluate policy changes without impacting production traffic.nnscope: covers tooling, safe injection channels, synthetic trace templates, experiment run matrix, telemetry correlation, post-run analysis, and rollback/cleanup. this playbook is intended for runtime engineers owning kernel scheduling, profiling, and the benchmarking suite.nnowner and contactsnn- doc owner: maya patel (runtime profiling team)n- primary oncall for injections: runtime-sre rotation (see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations)n- reviewers: ethan zhang (scheduler), lina fernández (observability), jordan kim (benchmarks)nnwhen to use this playbooknn- investigating reproducible tail-latency spikes suspected to be scheduling interactionsn- validating scheduler policy changes (crediting, preemption thresholds) against representative workloadsn- debugging kv cache coherence regressions under composite load shapesn- generating controlled regression candidates for the benchmarking and perf-suitennsafety model and constraintsnn- never inject synthetic traces into live customer traffic channels. use the dedicated shadow ingress (ingress-shadow.redwood.internal) or the local experiment harness.n- all experiments must run in the sandbox cluster or a reserved staging ring do not point to dedicated customer pools.n- maximum allowed synthetic qps: 25 of the node pool baseline for the targeted cluster (enforced by the shadow-admission controller).n- if any of the slo gates (95p latency, error rate, gpu utilization) degrade by 20 compared to baseline within the first 5 minutes, abort automatically. abort uses the circuit-breaker endpoint (post /admin/experiment/id/abort).nnprerequisitesnn1) access: experiment-runner role and shadow-cluster credentials (see /confluence/eng-sre/credentials).n2) tooling: experiment-runner cli (v1.14) and trace-injector service binary. install: curl -fss shn3) baseline capture: a 30-minute production shadow capture (compressed protobuf) representative of the workload you will emulate. see capture naming convention: capture-service-date-env.pb.gznnhigh-level flownn1) derive synthetic trace templates from baseline capture using the extractor.n2) augment templates to produce fault/edge cases (e.g., long prefix reuse, kvcache cold starts, model-variant switch).n3) validate templates locally in the sandbox harness (dry run trace-level assertions).n4) launch scheduler-shadow run in a staging ring with the current scheduler and an alternate policy patched into the shadow controller.n5) collect and correlate kernel traces, scheduler telemetry, and application observability.n6) run benchmark-suite scenarios to quantify delta and generate regression tickets if necessary.nnstep-by-step procedurenna. generate synthetic traces from a capturenn1. model_variant_hint.nn3. edit the template to add edge cases. example additions (append to array):nn - a long-prefix case: seq_len: 4096, prompt_token_counts: 1024, 3072, kv_key_prefixes: user:prefetch-heavy, model_variant_hint: llama-2-q8n - kvcache cold-flush windows: add interval markers for forced cache evictionnnb. sanity-check templates in local harnessnn1. start local harness scheduler shadowingnn1. create experiment record: nn experiment-runner create --name sched-shadow-kvcoh-2026-06 --cluster staging-shadow --owner @maya --config experiments/sched-shadow-config.yamlnn2. kernel executions, and network transfers with bounded overhead, and how to configure adaptive and tail-aware samplers to maximize signal for debugging and regression detection.nngoals:n- provide a grpc.nnsampling strategy (high level):n- default global policy: probabilistic reservoir sampling at 0.5 for steady-state production traffic. this keeps storage cost bounded while ensuring random coverage.n- route-priorities: override probabilistic sampler per-route. important routes (e.g., admin endpoints, high-rpo customers, new-model routes) should be sampled at higher rates (220).n- tail-aware sampling: implement tail-sampler in the otel collector that keeps a short window (5m) and promotes traces with high observed latency ( p95), error flags, or kernel anomalies to persisted storage regardless of initial sample decision.n- adaptive sampler: dynamically increase sampling for a route when its error rate or tail-latency growth exceeds thresholds. see algorithm below.nnadaptive sampler algorithm (pseudocode):n1) for each route r, maintain sliding metrics: rps(r), error_rate(r), tail_latency_p95(r). 5-minute windows.n2) evaluate every 30s: if error_rate(r) 0.5 and rps(r) 10 sampler_rate(r) : min(0.2, sampler_rate(r) 4).n3) if tail_latency_p95(r) increases by 25 vs baseline sampler_rate(r) : min(0.1, sampler_rate(r) 2).n4) decay: every 10 minutes without triggers sampler_rate(r) : max(default_rate, sampler_rate(r) 0.7).n5) ensure a global budget: sum(expected_spans_per_minute) 95 of traces with request latency above configured p99 threshold.nninstrumentation checklist (developer-facing):n1) add span entry/exit for each high-level component: request router, multiplexer, model executor, kv-cache check.n2) annotate spans with these required attributes: model.name, model.version, batch.size, requested_tokens, response_tokens, kv_cache_hit, kernel.id.n3) emit kernel spans at kernel launch and kernel completion with start_ts and end_ts and resource tags (gpu_index, sm_util).n4) expose a lightweight debug flag to force-sample traces for a request_id when doing customer debugging.n5) ensure traces are scrubbed of pii by default only hashed client ids and truncated prompt previews are allowed.nnrollout procedure (recommended):n1) canary: enable redwood-trace-agent on 1 of nodes in a non-prod environment and validate basic end-to-end ingestion.n2) staged prod rollout: 1 - 5 - 25 - 100 with 1 hour observation windows. verify overhead metrics after each step.n3) enable route overrides incrementally: start with low-risk routes, then business-critical routes.n4) turn on gpu kernel probes separately: measure overhead with nsys for 24h before enabling tail-promotion for kernel anomalies.n5) full tail-sampler enablement only after tail recall verification in a loaded test environment.nnrollback plan:n- if collector cpu or trace agent memory exceeds thresholds or p50 latency regressions 10ms observed, roll back to previous sampling global_default and disable gpu/net probes.n- use the sidecar healthcheck endpoint (/health/trace-agent) to drain and stop forwarding.nncommon troubleshooting patterns and remediation:n- symptom: many traces missing kernel spans.n - cause: cupti permission or probe not loaded on container runtime.n - action: check redwood-trace-agent logs for gpu-probe: init failed and ensure container has cap_sys_admin or appropriate device access verify driver/ cuda version compat.nn- symptom: sudden spike in trace volume and storage pressure.n - cause: misconfigured route override or accidental debug-forced sampling.n - action: temporarily set sampling.global_default to 0.001 and scale down overrides throttle ingress to collector.nn- symptom: high tail latency captured but not correlated to kernel durations.n - cause: network egress or kv-cache serialization.n - action: enable ebpf nic microspans for the suspected nodes and re-run tail-sampling for 1 hour.nndiagnostic cli snippets and examples:n- force a trace for a single request_id (debug only):n curl -x post n -h x-redwood-debug-force-trace: request:12345 n -d input:... example otel-collector content: summaryn-------nthis document describes the compact trace annotation (cta) format and the downstream causal latency map (clm) workflow we use to convert sparse, high-throughput traces into actionable latency attribution for inference requests. ctaclm provide a low-overhead instrumentation pattern suitable for production gpu pools and multi-tenant serving, enabling root-cause identification for p95/p99 regressions without capturing full trace payloads.nnwhy this existsn----------------n- full-span tracing is too heavy for production inference: memory, disk, and network overheads degrade throughput and interfere with kernel scheduling.n- we need deterministic, reproducible attributions: whether latency comes from kernel contention, queueing, inter-node nvlink transfer, or kv cache misses.n- on-call and sre teams require a compact artifact that can be stored for weeks and replayed into investigation tools.nnscopen-----nthis doc covers:n- cta schema (telemetry fields included and required)n- collector configuration and rate controlsn- cli and pipeline to generate the clm (processing and causal inference steps)n- investigation runbook tied to slo thresholds and alertsn- dashboard and alert configuration snippetsnnaudiencen--------nprimary: eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, profiling engineers, incident responders. secondary: product reliability, platform owners.nntelemetry contract: compact trace fieldsn-------------------------------------nwe intentionally limit fields to keep artifacts small (14kb per trace). required fields are bold. optional fields are encouraged when available. keep field types primitive (string/number/boolean) to simplify downstream processing.nn field type required? description n-------------------------------------n request_id string yes global request identifier (uuid v4).n ts_start int yes epoch ms when request first arrived at entry router.n ts_end int yes epoch ms when response sent to client.n stage_events list yes ordered small tokens representing stage boundaries see allowed tokens below.n kernel_slots list no compact histogram of per-kernel execution duration buckets (ms). format: count_lt1ms, count_1_5ms, count_5_10ms, count_gt10ms.n kvcache_hits int no number of kv cache hits during request.n kvcache_misses int no number of kv cache misses during request.n shard_id string yes shard or node id handling primary compute for request.n tenant string yes customer/tenant id (for multi-tenant pool attribution).n kernel_hint string no optional model kernel hint (e.g. fused-attn-v2, triton-gemm).n sampling_reason string yes p95-sample, error-sample, system-sample, random.n trace_version string yes e.g. cta-v1nnallowed stage_events tokens (alphabetical): entry, enqueue, dequeue, kernel_start, kernel_end, kv_lookup_start, kv_lookup_end, network_tx_start, network_tx_end, fallback_switch, response_sendnncompact trace example (cta payload)n----------------------------------nexample cta (json single-line):nrequest_id:b6f3c2d4-8e9f-4a2b-9cde-aa11bb22cc33,ts_start:1700000123456,ts_end:1700000123590,stage_events:entry,enqueue,dequeue,kernel_start,kernel_end,response_send,kernel_slots:0,1,0,0,kvcache_hits:2,kvcache_misses:0,shard_id:shard-eu-12,tenant:acct-42,sampling_reason:p95-sample,trace_version:cta-v1nncollector configuration and rate controlsn---------------------------------------n- service name: inference-trace-collector (k8s: infra/observability).n- default retention: compact traces stored in hot-s3 (14d), cold-s3 (90d).n- sampling policy (k8s configmap):n 1) p95-sampler: deterministic capture of requests where request_latency 95th percentile (computed via streaming aggregator), priority 1.n 2) error-sampler: capture on any 5xx or model-runtime exception, priority 0 (always capture).n 3) system-sampler: capture 0.05 random traffic for long-term health signal, priority 2.n- backpressure: if collector ingestion queue 75 capacity, reduce system-sampler to 0.01 and drop random-samples older than 10s. always preserve error-sampled traces.nncollector config snippet (yaml)n-----------------------------napiversion: v1nkind: configmapnmetadata:n name: cta-collector-configndata:n sampling.p95.threshold-ms: 200n sampling.system.rate-per-minute: 50n retention.hot-days: 14n retention.cold-days: 90n ingestion.queue-soft-limit: 0.75nnprocessing pipeline to build the causal latency map (clm)n------------------------------------------------------nhigh-level steps:n1) ingest cta artifacts from hot-s3 for window w (typically last 6h).n2) enrich each cta with node-level kernel telemetry (kernel queue lengths, kernel dispatch times) from the kernel-metrics store (tsdb).n3) group traces by shard_id tenant model_variant.n4) build causal graph using stage_events ordering and per-stage timestamps: compute edge weights for queueing delay, kernel duration, network transfer, and kvcache penalty.n5) aggregate graphs into a clm that reports per-path contributions to request latency percentiles.nncommand-line helpers (example)n-----------------------------n pull ctas into local file for window 1hnredwoodctl trace fetch --from now-1h --to now --out ctas.ndjson --filter sampling_reasonp95-samplenn enrich and build clmnredwoodctl trace enrich --ctas ctas.ndjson --kernel-store tsdb://kernel-metrics --out enriched.ndjsonnredwoodctl clm build --in enriched.ndjson --group-by shard_id,tenant,model_variant --out clm-20260218.jsonnninterpretation semanticsn------------------------n- edge weights are additive: total request latency sum(edge weights on primary path) residual.n- an edge labeled kernel_queue indicates time spent waiting for kernel slot kernel_exec indicates execution time.n- kv cache penalty: modeled as (miss_count avg_kv_lookup_ms) miss-induced-kernel-delay.nninvestigation runbook (p95 alert)n--------------------------------ntrigger: alert runtime-p95-slo-violation firing (slo: p95 kernel dispatch - shard x.n b) if queue length 5 for 5m, consider immediate temporary mitigation: scale out shard pool or reroute low-priority tenants.n6) if root cause is kv cache misses:n a) confirm model variant and session affinity changes.n b) trigger kv cache prefetch for affected sessions (see kv prefetch playbook).n7) if root cause is network/nvlink transfer: verify network device errors and open infra incident.n8) document findings on incident page and attach clm artifact.nnescalation thresholds and ownershipn----------------------------------n- sre responder: pager duty - eng-sre oncall.n- if clm shows 40 contribution from kernel_queue across multiple shards for 10min, escalate to runtime-platform@redwood.com and cc oncall infra.n- if kv-miss contribution 30 for a tenant with reserved capacity, page the assigned solutions engineer.nndashboards and alerts (suggested panels)n---------------------------------------n- clm: stacked contribution chart (kernel_exec / kernel_queue / kv_penalty / network) per severity: criticalnannotations:n runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026nnperformance cost and storage sizing guidancen-------------------------------------------n- cta size: 14kb typical. expect 0.5gb/day per 10k p95-sampled requests at default sampling.n- hot-s3 retention cost: plan for 14 days hot latency metric synthesis and normalization guide, content: purposen-------nthis guide standardizes how we synthesize, normalize, and interpret latency signals across the serving stack so that dashboards, alerts, and post-incident analyses compare like-for-like. it documents the telemetry fields we require, the normalization math we use for cross-model and cross-hardware comparisons, and a step-by-step triage procedure for metric anomalies.nnscopen-----n- applies to all runtime telemetry emitted by redwood-serving components: dispatcher, scheduler, kernel dispatcher, kv cache, model-host pools, and the network fabric observed in the control plane.n- target audiences: runtime sres, profiling engineers, performance qa, and anyone authoring slos or dashboards.nnbackground and motivationn-------------------------nwe observed repeated confusion when correlating percentiles across heterogeneous cohorts (different model sizes, sequence lengths, and gpu classes). raw p95/p99 numbers are insufficient because:nn- different workloads have different token distributions and tail behaviorn- kernels exhibit different steady-state vs warmup profilesn- hardware differences (a100 vs h100 vs cpu) change latency skew and variancen- sampling biases (e.g., production sampling favoring low-entropy requests) distort percentiles.nnthis document prescribes: a canonical telemetry contract, normalization transforms, recommended histogram bucketing, and an investigation checklist.nnkey terms and definitionsn-------------------------n- slo unit: the atomic unit we measure against (e.g., per-token generation latency for hosted-api model x at seq_len256).n- cohort: grouping by model, model_variant, region, accel_class, seq_len_bucket, customer_tier.n- normalized latency (l_norm): latency after applying transforms to remove known covariates used for cross-cohort comparison.nnrequired telemetry fieldsn-------------------------nall runtime spans/events used for latency synthesis must include the following attributes (table):nn field type description retention/notes n-------------------------------------------n request_id string unique per request keep 30d indexed n customer_id string optional, helps cohorting pii rules apply n model string model name version n model_variant string quantized/float/etc. n seq_len int input sequence length (tokens) use computed bucket if large n output_tokens int tokens generated n accel_class string e.g., h100-80g, a100-40g, cpu n kernel_id string identifier for kernel path executed correlate to kernel telemetry n kernel_queue_ns int nanoseconds spent queued for kernel n kernel_run_ns int nanoseconds kernel executed n kv_cache_hit boolean true if kv cache served prefix n cpu_network_ns int control-plane network time n trace_start_ts iso8601 trace root start nn(if a field cannot be present due to privacy or perf constraints, document why and propose a fallback.)nnhistogram and bucket recommendationsn-----------------------------------n- for raw span latency: use log-linear buckets from 0.1ms to 30s with finer granularity under 200ms.n- emit both cumulative and delta histograms: cumulative for percentile computation, delta for rate-based anomaly detection.n- ensure at least 100 buckets for sub-200ms region when using gpu-backed models (helps tail decomposition).nnnormalization strategy (overview)n--------------------------------nwe normalize in three stages: cohort alignment, per-request covariate adjustment, and variance stabilization.nn1) cohort alignmentn- define cohorts by model, accel_class, and seq_len_bucket. only compare percentiles within cohorts by default.n- when comparing across cohorts (e.g., h100 vs a100), apply a hardware baseline multiplier derived from weekly calibration runs (see calibration protocol below).nn2) covariate adjustment (per-request)n- use a linear model: l_raw beta_0 beta_1 seq_len beta_2 output_tokens beta_3 kv_cache_miss epsilon.n- fit model on a sliding 7-day window per-cohort compute residual l_raw - l_pred. the normalized latency l_norm residual cohort_median_baseline.n- for non-linear effects (e.g., seq_len2), prefer gams when sample size permits fall back to linear for small cohorts.nn3) variance stabilizationn- apply a robust transform to reduce heavy tails for visualization: use a log1p transform for dashboards but preserve raw percentiles in alerts.n- for alerting, use percentile bands on raw or residual latencies (do not alert on transformed values).nncalibration protocol (weekly source_type: confluence, title: adaptive observability and kernel hinting playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook documents the adaptive observability kernel hinting subsystem: the design, telemetry model, operational controls, and runbook for using kernel hints to steer the serving runtime. the goal is to reduce tail latency and per-token cost by leveraging request-level signals to select kernel execution paths and sampling strategies while keeping trace overhead bounded.nnwhy this existsnn- production inference workloads have widely varying sequence lengths, model architectures, and client slas. static monitoring and static kernel selection produce suboptimal latency/cost tradeoffs.n- kernel hints are lightweight signals (tagged on request metadata) that bias scheduler choices (kernel variant, prefetch, kv warmstart) for the current request cohort.n- adaptive observability is necessary to validate that hints are safe, reduce false positives, and capture causal signals for regression detection.nnscopennthis playbook covers:n- design and components of the hinting observability pipelinen- data model, sampling policies, and trace budget rulesn- operational thresholds and incident runbooks for common failure modesn- rollout and canary guidance for hinting rules and kernel profilesnnout-of-scope: model training, model quality evals, and on-device kernel internals beyond documented control signals.nndesign overviewnnarchitecture (text diagram)nnclient - ingress router - request classifier - hint enricher - hint broker - scheduler/kv prefetch/kernelsn u2022 shadow tracer - sampling controller - observability sink (tsdb / tracedb)nncomponentsnn- request classifier: lightweight policy service that maps headers, route config, and proto attributes to request_cohort ids. runs in the edge ingress so hint decisions travel with requests. owned by serving-runtime/classification.n- hint enricher: attaches hint metadata (kernel_hint, prefetch_hint, expected_seq_len_bucket, sampling_weight) to the request context. hints are cryptographically signed by the control plane to prevent tampering in dedicated/private deployments.n- hint broker: central service that resolves cohort-kernel_variant mappings and exposes a fast grpc lookup for the scheduler. supports versioned mappings and rollout tags.n- scheduler hooks: scheduler reads kernel_hint and sampling_weight, consults runtime policy, and chooses a kernel variant, batch-slice, and prefetch action.n- shadow tracer sampling controller: decides which requests get full end-to-end traces. sampling is adaptive: when a hint is new or flips mapping, sampling weight temporarily increases for affected cohorts.nndata model and fieldsnntable: (rendered as text)n field description type examples n------------------------------------n request_id globally unique id for a request string r-0a1b2c n cohort_id classifier-assigned cohort string search-embed-small n kernel_hint suggested kernel profile tag string fast-fp16, stable-quant n prefetch_hint kv cache warmstart preference enum none, aggressive, conservative n expected_seq_len_bucket bucketed input length string short(512) n sampling_weight relative trace sampling weight float (0.0-1.0) 0.05 nnoperational invariants and slosnn- hint safety: kernel_hint should not increase cpu gpu utilization 5 above baseline for steady cohorts. monitored via kernel_variant_resource_delta.n- hint efficacy: cohort p95 latency with kernel_hint-enabled should be 10 triggers automatic rollback.nnhow sampling works (algorithmic summary)nn1. baseline sampling rate per cohort (configurable).n2. change amplification: if a cohorts kernel mapping is changed, sampling controller increases sampling_weight by factor 5 for 30 minutes for that cohort.n3. entropy hedging: if trace diversity drops (identical stack signatures exceed 90 of traces), controller reduces weight to focus on unique traces.nnconfig example (runtime hint controller yaml)nnhint_controller:n default_sampling_rate: 0.01n change_amplification_factor: 5.0n amplification_window_minutes: 30n max_trace_budget_percent: 0.5n cohort_overrides:n - cohort: search-embed-smalln sampling_rate: 0.02n allowed_kernel_variants: fast-fp16, stable-quantnn(place this in /etc/redwood/hint-controller.yaml on control plane nodes for hosted equivalent k8s configmap for dedicated.)nntrace schema example (json line format)nnn request_id: r-0a1b2c,n cohort_id: search-embed-small,n kernel_hint: fast-fp16,n expected_seq_len_bucket: short,n latency_ms: 12.3,n kernel_variant: fast-fp16-v7,n cpu_pct: 23.4nnnrunbook: tail-latency spike after hint rolloutnnsymptomsn- p99 latency for cohort x increases by 15 within 10 minutes of hint rollout.n- kernel variant kernel_hint. use the trace window 15m back.n3. if traces show higher kernel_cpu_pct or prefetch stalls, rollback the mapping in hint broker to previous version:nn rollback using hint-brokerctlnhint-brokerctl rollback --cohort search-embed-small --to-version v12nn4. if rollback is not possible or unexpected: cascade to scheduler soft-fallback: set policy: honor_hintfalse for affected nodes.nnpost-incident analysis (within 48 hours)n- run a fidelity experiment: replay representative requests against both kernel_variant a and variant b in the lab using the operational workload simulator. capture per-token cost, p95, and resource deltas.n- update decision log with hypothesis and root cause.nnrunbook: missing or malformed hints observednnsymptomsn- hints absent for dsid_3115121c62804064a447789d80e2f7ba, source_type: confluence, title: caching batching cost signals (serving runtime profiling playbook), content: purposenthis playbook documents the serving-runtime signals we rely on to explain changes in unit cost (blended /1m output tokens). it focuses on the three most common runtime drivers:nn1) batching utilization (how much gpu time is spent doing useful work vs waiting/underfilled)n2) kv/prefix cache effectiveness (how much compute we avoid by reusing previous work)n3) prefill vs decode mix (how request shape and context length shift gpu cost per output token)nnthis page is referenced by the unit economics dashboard and the on-call discrepancy playbooks. it is intended for serving runtime, telemetry/analytics, and sre.nn---nn how runtime signals map to blended /1m output tokensn the mental modelnat a high level:nnblended /1m output tokens (gpu overhead allocations) / (output tokens) 1,000,000nnwhen the metric moves, one (or more) of these must be true:nn- numerator increased: we spent more gpu-hours for the same output tokens (e.g., lower batching efficiency, more prefill work, cache regression, slower kernels, lower quant efficiency).n- denominator decreased: we reported fewer output tokens for the same gpu-hours (e.g., metering bug, streaming path undercount, increased truncation, more failures).n- mix shifted: traffic changed in a way that makes output tokens more expensive (e.g., longer prompts prefill-heavy, shorter generations with high prompt overhead, different model/quant profile, region/provider changes).nn cost-driver decomposition (runtime-focused)nthe unit cost typically correlates with the following derived factors:nn- effective throughput: output_tokens / gpu_second (higher is better)n- batching efficiency: useful_compute_time / allocated_compute_time (higher is better)n- cache savings: avoided_prefill_tokens (or avoided_attention_work) / total_prefill_work (higher is better)n- prefill load: prefill_tokens / output_tokens (lower is better, but workload-dependent)nnthese are not accounting numbers they are explanatory signals that should directionally match changes in blended cost.nn---nn required dimensions (to make signals actionable)nall runtime signals used for unit economics must be taggable by the dimensions the dashboard supports, within cardinality limits:nnrequired dimensions (where available):n- model_id (canonical)n- model_version (if pinned or surfaced via routing policy)n- quantization_profile (allowed-values only)n- region (normalized)n- customer_tier (self-serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)n- streaming (true/false)nnimportant: do not tag by customer_id, route_id with high uniqueness, or raw prompt hashes. see the cardinality standard referenced above.nn---nn signal 1: batching utilizationn why it mattersncontinuous batching is the primary lever for improving gpu utilization for decode. underfilled batches waste gpu cycles, increasing per output token.nnbatching issues are one of the most common causes of sudden regional or model-specific unit cost spikes.nn definitionsnuse these terms consistently:nn- batch size (decode): number of active sequences decoded per step.n- batch occupancy: batch_size / max_batch_size (or / capacity at the current kernel/sequence length).n- batching wait time: time requests spend queued to form a batch.n- compute time: time spent executing kernels.nn recommended runtime metrics (names are illustrative)ncollect at least:nn- redwood_runtime_decode_active_sequences_avgmodel_id,region,quantization_profile,streamingn- redwood_runtime_decode_max_active_sequences... (or configured max)n- redwood_runtime_batch_wait_ms_p50/p95model_id,regionn- redwood_runtime_gpu_busy_ratioregion,cluster (if available)n- redwood_runtime_decode_tokens_totalmodel_id,region,quantization_profilenn derived metrics interpretationn- decode batch utilization active_sequences_avg / max_active_sequencesn - healthy ranges vary by model/hardware, but sustained drops (e.g., 0.70 0.40) usually show up as a unit cost increase.nn- queueing vs compute tradeoffn - if batch_wait_ms_p95 increases sharply while utilization remains low, we likely have fragmentation (many small pools), admission control issues, or a routing policy change.n - if batch_wait_ms_p95 increases and utilization increases, we may have intentionally optimized cost at the expense of latency (confirm against slos).nn common root causesn- traffic fragmentation across too many pools (by model version, quant profile, region, tier)n- overly strict routing/affinity rules preventing consolidationn- misconfigured max_batch_size for new model or kernel regimen- increased request concurrency variance (bursty traffic) conservative batching windowsn- increased prefill pressure causing decode starvationnn what to do when batching utilization dropsn1) confirm the issue is real (not a missing-tag or sampling artifact).n2) check for recent changes:n - routing policy updatesn - canary rollout that split trafficn - autoscaling events / pool resizingn - model version pinning changesn3) compare by dimension:n - model_id quantization_profilen - regionn - customer_tiern4) mitigation options (runtime-owned):n - increase consolidation (reduce pool fragmentation)n - adjust batching window/limits for affected pooln - revisit admission control thresholdsn - consider fallback to a compatible model variant during capacity stress (if policy allows)nn---nn signal 2: kv cache and prefix cache hit ratesn why it mattersncache hits reduce prefill compute. prefill can be a large fraction of gpu work for long-context workloads, so cache regressions can materially raise blended /1m output tokens.nnimportant nuance: cache benefits can be workload-specific and may not show in all traffic (e.g., highly unique prompts).nn cache typesn- prefix cache (a.k.a. prompt cache): reuses computed attention states for a shared prefix across requests.n- kv cache reuse within session: reuses per-sequence kv as decode progresses (normal decode state). this is not a hit rate in the same sense the cost signal here is more about kv cache pressure/evictions and context growth.nn definitionsn- prefix cache hit: requests prefill can reuse a stored prefix representation, reducing prefill tokens processed.n- prefix cache hit rate: hits / (hits misses)n- cache saved tokens: estimated prefill_tokens_avoided due to cache hitsn- evictions / churn: how often cached entries are removed due to memory pressure or ttlnn recommended runtime metricsnprefix cache:n- redwood_runtime_prefix_cache_hits_totalmodel_id,region,quantization_profilen- redwood_runtime_prefix_cache_misses_total...n- redwood_runtime_prefix_cache_saved_prefill_tokens_total... derived metrics interpretationn- prefix cache hit rate hits / (hits misses)n - use as a qualitative indicator. it can be misleading if hit does not imply a large token savings.nn- prefill tokens saved rate saved_prefill_tokens / total_prefill_tokensn - prefer this for cost attribution. a small hit rate can still save a lot if hits are on long prefixes.nn- cost mappingn - when cache effectiveness drops, expect:n - prefill_tokens / output_tokens to risen - gpu-seconds per output token to risen - blended /1m output tokens to risenn common root causes of cache regressionsn- cache key changes diversity (fewer repeated prefixes)n- region or pool split lowering reuse probabilitynn what to do when cache hit rate dropsn1) validate the workload changed (e.g., product launched new prompt isolated to:n - a region (config divergence)n - a quantization profile (different cache capacity/behavior)n - streaming vs non-streaming (request metadata differences)n4) mitigations:n - increase cache capacity (bytes) or ttl (if safe)n - revert/adjust prompt formatting to stabilize prefixesn - consolidate pools to increase reuse raten - fix cache key/versioning if mismatched between gateway/runtimenn---nn signal 3: prefill vs decode ratio (request shape)n why it mattersneven if batching and caching are stable, unit cost can move due to request mix:nn- longer prompts increase conditions.nnthis is the most common explanation for no regression found in runtime code, but unit cost still increased.nn definitionsn- prefill tokens: input tokens processed to build attention state windows or by product features that add system/tool context.nn- output tokens per request decode_tokens_total / request_countn - falling output/request increases fixed overhead per output token serving runtime. it is intended for on-call engineers, runtime owners, and sres who operate model-serving fleets. unlike manual kernel tuning runbooks, this document specifies the signals, control loop design, safety gates, rollout and rollback procedures, and observability required to safely operate automated kernel autotuning in production.nnmotivationn---n- kernel characteristics and the optimal scheduling strategy can vary by model, sequence-length distribution, and traffic mix.n- manual tuning is slow to react to changes (new models, workload shifts, infra upgrades).n- a closed-loop
