overviewnnthis playbook documents the recommended approach for profiling, benchmarking, and operationalizing multi-model request chains (model chaining) in the redwood serving runtime. model chaining occurs when a single api request triggers sequential or conditional invocations across multiple model variants or pipelines (for example: classifier - reranker - generator). these patterns are increasingly common in production flows (routing, tool-calling, multimodal pre- and post-processing) and expose unique scheduling, caching, and batching interactions that require targeted profiling and shaping to meet latency and cost slos.nnaudiencen- runtime engineers who implement scheduler/kernel changesn- performance engineers owning microbenchmarks and end-to-end slosn- oncall sres and platform owners responsible for incident triagen- solutions engineers validating customer workloads that chain modelsnngoalsn- provide a repeatable procedure to attribute latency and cost across a chained execution path.n- offer batch-shaping and warmup recommendations that preserve p95 slos while minimizing per-token cost.n- define benchmark scenarios and acceptance thresholds to gate releases that impact chained workloads.nnwhen to use this playbookn- adding a new chained pipeline to productionn- observed p95 regressions correlated with multi-model invocationsn- rolling out kernel or scheduler changes that affect batching/eviction logicnnkey concepts and termsn- link: one hop in the chain (e.g., token-classifier).n- chain: ordered list of links that execute per request.n- interlink latency: time window between link completion and next link start. includes network, marshalling, and scheduling delay.n- batch shaping: runtime techniques to control how requests in a chain are aggregated into kernel batches.n- prefetch/warmstart: proactive loading of kv cache or kernels prior to link execution to reduce cold latency.nnobservability checklistn- per-link latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) with distinction of kernel vs scheduling vs marshalling time.n- interlink gap histogram and correlation with kernel admission events.n- kernel occupancy and batch size distribution per link.n- kv cache hit ratio per model link and warmup success rate.n- cost per request and per-token cost tagged with chain-id and feature flags.nnsuggested metrics (examples)n- chain.request.count (tags: chain_id, customer_tier)n- chain.latency.p95 (tags: chain_id, link_index)n- kernel.batch.size (tags: kernel_variant, link_index)n- kvcache.prefetch.success_rate (tags: chain_id, model)nnprofiling procedure (step-by-step)n1) identify representative chainsn - for the workload under investigation, extract the top 10 chain shapes by request volume and by p95 contribution. use tracing to enumerate link types and their average token lengths.nn2) baseline capture (shadow/topology snapshot)n - capture a 10-minute tracing window in shadow mode with full span collection and kernel annotations. use the replay harness to export the trace as a synthetic corpus.n - command example: n ./tools/trace-export --serviceingress --filterchain_id:checkout_v2 --outcheckout_v2.tracenn3) microprofile each link in isolationn - replay links individually against the same model-variant to collect kernel-level latency and batch distributions. use the microbenchmark agent with kernel annotation turned on.n - command example: n ./bench/replay --tracecheckout_v2.trace --link2 --annotate-kernel --concurrency50 --duration60s --outlink2-profile.jsonnn4) end-to-end chain replay with controlled shaping knobsn - re-run the synthetic chain while toggling shaping knobs: contiguous-batching, interlink-throttle, slot-reservation, kv-prefetch. capture per-link breakdowns.n - command example: n ./bench/replay --tracecheckout_v2.trace --shapingslot_reserve2interlink_throttle50mskv_prefetchon --duration600s --outchain-run-1.jsonnn5) attribution and root cause analysisn - for each chain run, compute: per-link kernel median/p95, interlink gap median/p95, batch-size vs latency correlation, and cost per request.n - if p95 regressions are kernel-localized, open a kernel performance investigation. if regressions are due to interlink scheduling gaps, follow the scheduler tuning steps below.nnbatch shaping strategies (patterns and trade-offs)n- tight slicing: enforce small, bounded batch slice per link to guarantee lower tail latency at higher per-token cost. use when tail slo is high priority.n- opportunistic coalescing: allow larger batches across links when background load is stable to improve cost efficiency but monitor p95 drift.n- slot reservation for sequential links: reserve n kernel slots across link boundaries for a chain to prevent preemption and eviction mid-chain. useful for long kv warmup sequences.n- interlink throttle: impose a minimal delay between links to allow the scheduler to co-locate subsequent link work into an opportunistic batch. useful when immediate re-invocation results in wasted small batches.n- adaptive prefetch: trigger kv/model prefetch for the next link when the probability of continuation exceeds a threshold. tune by observing prefetch hit success and added upstream latency.nnconfiguration examplesn- yaml example for batch shaper (runtime config):nn key type description threshold (0-1) for prefetch 0.65 nnexample yaml snippet:nnshaping:n mode: reservedn slot_reservations: 2n interlink_throttle_ms: 30n kv_prefetch_enabled: truen prefetch_confidence_threshold: 0.65nnkernel scheduling tuning checklistn- ensure link affinity: tag chains with affinity labels so the scheduler prefers the same gpu/numa domain for adjacent links.n- verify slot-reservation should be admitted with lower admission latency guarantees to reduce cold-link penalties.n- backpressure integration: interlink backpressure should surface as a chain-level signal to the admission controller.nnbenchmarking suite additions (how to add chain tests)n1) add synthetic corpus: export representative chain traces (see baseline capture) to the corpus repo under benchmarks/chains/.n2) content: overview:nnthis playbook defines the predictive bundling model and sla crediting algorithm used to (1) recommend bundled credit products for tenants, (2) apply automated sla credits when latency or availability slos are missed, and (3) simulate the downstream financial impact of different bundling strategies. the goal is to enable predictable customer billing while preserving fairness and operational incentives across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.nnkey objectives:n- provide a transparent, auditable algorithm for sla credit calculations tied to measurable telemetry signals.n- surface predictive bundle recommendations that balance expected token consumption, latency slos, and cost-to-serve.n- offer a simulation harness (offline and lightweight online mode) to estimate revenue and credit exposure before packaging changes.nnscope:n- applies to all hosted api customers and dedicated plans that opt-in to usage-bundles. private deployments may use the same algorithm as a reference but must explicitly opt into centralized billing behavior.n- covers per-route and per-tenant slos for latency (p50/p95/p99) and availability (error budget burn).n- excludes paper credits/goodwill adjustments which remain a manual cs workflow.nndefinitions and primitives:n- unit: a billing unit equivalent to 1,000 embedding tokens or 1,000 generation tokens depending on product sku.n- bundle: named package with n units slo promise (e.g., baseline-50k-20ms) and an associated monthly price and credit terms.n- credit pool: per-tenant ledger where automatically applied sla credits are deposited and visible on invoices.n- exposure: estimated future credit liability (usd) under current observed slo miss rates.nnalgorithm overview (high-level):n1) consumption forecast: estimate next-period token usage per tenant using exponential smoothing feature adjustments (seasonality, recent growth spikes, marketing campaigns).n2) cost projection: map forecasted consumption to expected cost-to-serve using model variant and quantization profile mapping (sku-cost-per-unit matrix).n3) bundle scoring: for candidate bundles compute a score utility(consumption_coverage, cost_savings, latency_hedge) - risk(exposure, sla-violation-rate).n4) sla credit mechanism: when observed slos in a billing window fall below threshold, compute credit min(max_credit_cap, severity_weight usage_fraction bundle_price).n5) simulation: run monte-carlo scenarios for the next 12 billing windows and produce an expected credit liability classifier and safety catalog, content: overviewnnthis document defines the runtime workload classifier used by the serving runtime, catalogs safety-related workload types, and provides operational guidance for classifier changes, profiling, and benchmark integration. the classifier is the central input to: scheduler profiles, kernel selection hints, kv cache policies, batching windows, and quality-of-service (qos) safety gates.nnscopen- applies to hosted, dedicated and private chains of the runtime orchestration layer.n- covers classifier taxonomy, schema for rules, rollout and canary testing, telemetry contracts, and runbook actions for misclassification incidents.n- does not define model-level safety filters (those live in product filter pipelines) this is focused on runtime routing and fidelity safety.nnmotivationn- workloads present radically different cost/latency/fidelity trade-offs. a small mismatch (e.g., treating streaming responses as short interactive) increases tail latency and kernel contention.n- explicitly declaring workload intent lets the scheduler / kernel mapper apply conservative or aggressive strategies while preserving slos and safety margins.nnclassifier design principlesn1. deterministic, signal-first: classification must be derivable from request metadata and the first n tokens (n configurable) avoid reliance on model outputs.n2. minimal changes to call paths: low-latency decision. the classifier runs inline in the ingress path or in the pre-routing sidecar for private deployments.n3. observable: emit classification events with version and feature flags to enable backfill analysis.n4. safe defaults: unknown/ambiguous requests map to the most conservative profile.nntaxonomy (canonical classes)n class_key description primary slo batch_target kernel_hint kv_cache_hint typical examples n---------:---:---------n interactive-short single-turn, latency-critical (512 tokens expected) sustained throughput token/sec target 8-32 streaming-optimized strong-prefetch audio transcription continuation, longform generation n embeddings-bulk offline or batch embedding jobs throughput cost target 64-1024 vector-batch-kernel n/a dataset embedding jobs, periodic reindexing n rerank-latent short prompt, multi-candidate scoring low-latency scoring 4-16 dense-matrix cold search reranking requests n multimodal-sync imagetext interactive interactive slo / extra memory 1-2 mixed-precision strong vision qa, ocr prompt n high-memory large context / long sequence buffers p99 memory usage guard 1-2 memory-friendly pin document summarization w/ 100k tokens n regulated-sensitive data flagged as regulated (pii/phi) additional audit logging kms conservative latency targets conservative-kernel disabled (no cache) medical notes, ssns n batch-notime best-effort, latency-insensitive background jobs cost-minimize 256 low-precision disabled nightly cleanup, offline scoring nnclassifier scheman- classifier_version: string (semver)n- rules: ordered list evaluated top-to-bottomn- rule: id, predicates, assign_class, confidence_threshold, metadata_hints expressed as yaml/json in reponnexample rule (yaml):nyamlnclassifier_version: 1.3.0nrules:n - id: regulated-headern predicates:n - header_exists: x-customer-regulatedn - header_value: truen assign_class: regulated-sensitiven confidence_threshold: 0.95n metadata_hints:n kernel_hint: conservative-kerneln kv_cache: disabledn - id: short-interactive-by-lengthn predicates:n - estimated_tokens: class. the header is read by downstream router and scheduler.nntelemetry contractnemit the following events at info sampling 100 for canaries, 1 for production by default (configurable per tenant):n- runtime.classify.request (fields: request_id, class_key, classifier_version, decision_latency_ms, source, rule_id)n- runtime.classify.fallback (fields: request_id, fallback_reason, original_signals)n- runtime.classify.change (fields: old_class, new_class, diff_reason)nnprofiling and benchmark integrationn- unit: every classifier change must have a microbenchmark that measures classifier latency and memory under representative rulesets. use the benchmark harness: bin/classifier-bench --rules tests/rules/synthetic-large.yaml --qps 500 --concurrency 128.n- end-to-end: run standardized workload replays labelled with ground-truth: scripts/bench/run-replay --trace labelled-replay.json --compare baseline-release. measure downstream p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel dispatches per second, and kv cache hit rate per-class.n- experimental: for any rule that changes kernel_hint or batch_target, run the kernel hint validation protocol (see checklist).nnkernel hint validation checklist (numbered procedure)n1. add the rule to a staging ruleset (classifier_version x.y.zstaging).n2. deploy staging classifier to a small fraction (5) of traffic or a dedicated shadow fleet.n3. run the kernel hint validation benchmark for 30 minutes: scripts/bench/kernel-hint-validate --class name --duration 1800s.n4. compare baseline kernel utilization, tail latency, and throughput for the class. if p99 degrades 20 for the class or sibling classes, abort.n5. if safe, proceed to 25 traffic for 2 hours, then gradual ramp with automated slo gates.nnoperational runbook: misclassification incidentntrigger: sudden spike in runtime.classify.fallback, or increase in p99 for a class with no config changes.nimmediate steps:n1. pager: owning runtime oncall (page).n2. short-term mitigation: flip classifier to previous stable version (classifierd supports quick rollback: curl -xpost if rollback not available, apply an emergency whitelist rule that routes to conservative class:n - id: emergency-conservativen predicates: match alln assign_class: interactive-shortn confidence_threshold: 1.0n4. capture traces for 100 of a small sample of requests using trace-mode: curl -h x-debug-trace:1 ... and upload to the runtime incident bucket.n5. post-incident: run a classification audit job to compute false-positive/false-negative rates using ground-truth replays.nnchange and release process (short bullets)n- author creates classifier rule pr in infra/classifier-rules repo. include yaml, unit tests, and a microbenchmark.n- reviewer checklist: semantics, telemetry hooks, kernel_hint impact, caching implications.n- staging rollout - kernel hint validation - canary (5/25/50/100) with slo gates.nnsecurity and privacy considerationsn- regulated-sensitive class must add kms envelope tag and disable kv caching operators must not allow cached payloads for these classes.n- all classification logs that include payload-derived signals must be redacted for tenants flagged with pii channel (runtime-reliability)., doc_id: dsid_bf65ea71738942c4bfd6001937e29760, source_type: confluence, title: stochastic eviction simulator and heuristic lab manual, content: summary:nthis document describes the design and operational playbook for the stochastic eviction simulator (ses): a lab-grade emulator used by runtime teams to validate eviction heuristics, measure fidelity impact, and generate rollout-safe parameters for the production kernel-mapper and admission controllers. ses is intended to be the primary tool for preflighting any kernel, scheduler, or fidelity-degradation change that touches eviction, cache warmup, or admission policies.nngoals:n- provide a repeatable experiment harness for eviction policy a/b testing under realistic traffic shapes.n- quantify fidelity vs cost tradeoffs (quality regressions per eviction aggressiveness).n- produce risk-bounded parameter sets for kernel rollouts and autoscaler admission controllers.nnscope:n- includes simulations of: kv cache eviction, session warmup, slot preemption, admission backpressure, and tiered-fallback routing.n- not for: full hardware-level gpu tracing or kernel micro-benchmarks (use runtime profiling playbook for kernel traces).nnquick concepts and definitions:n1) eviction aggressiveness: numeric 0.01.0 controlling willingness to evict warm kv entries or preempt active slots. higher lower memory usage but more fidelity risk.n2) fidelity score: a workload-anchored metric derived from evals (token-level logprob shift task-level metric like rouge/rouge-l or e2e pass rate). represented as percent change from baseline.n3) stochastic seed: ses can apply random jitter to eviction decisions to emulate real-world nondeterminism seed should be recorded in experiment metadata.nnarchitecture (high level):n- traffic generator (traffic-gen): replays traffic corpus or synthesizes session traces using shape profiles (burst, steady, diurnal).n- resource model (resource-sim): models gpu memory, kv cache shards, per-tenant quotas, numa zones.n- heuristic engine (heuristic-orch): executes eviction heuristics (lru-window, recencypriority, cost-aware eviction, stochastic-probabilistic, ml-guided scorer).n- fidelity model (fidelity-proxy): maps eviction events to expected quality delta using precomputed mapping tables from eval runs or an ml regressor trained on historical rollouts.n- metrics collector (ses-metrics): aggregates slos, fidelity deltas, throughput, and cost proxies.nnhow ses integrates with runtime artifacts:n- config inputs reference production feature flags and config keys from runtime-orch (e.g., runtime-orch.eviction.policy, kernel-mapper.slot-credit). test configs should mirror the production json structure.n- ses can import a lightweight snapshot of kvcache-service metadata (shard counts, hit rates) exported from a production day and then replay traffic against that snapshot.nnsimulator configuration example (yaml):n---nexperiment_name: 0.82neviction_policy:n type: ml-scorer-stochasticn aggressiveness: 0.46n jitter_stddev: 0.12n lookback_window_seconds: 900nfidelity_model:n type: regression-v1n trained_on: canary-evictions-2025-10n---nncommon heuristics catalog (table-style in-line):n- lru-window: deterministic, low cpu, baseline for comparisons. params: window_seconds, victim_fraction.n- cost-aware: prefers evicting low-cost tokens (shorter kv usage). params: token_cost_weight.n- priority-based: tenant/application-assigned priorities, used for enterprise isolation. params: priority_decay_half_life.n- ml-scored: model predicts future hit probability and eviction risk. params: model_version, score_threshold.n- stochastic-probabilistic: base_prob f(aggressiveness, recency) introduces randomness to smooth behavior.nnexperiment metrics and targets (examples):n- tail latency (p99 request latency): target 180ms.n- average throughput: baseline tokens/sec per-gpu, reported as tps/gpu. degradation 10 flagged.n- fidelity delta: median evals score drop across prompt set. acceptable rollback threshold: 1.0 drop triggers fail.n- cold-hit penalty: increase in average token compute due to cache misses target 0.5 but latency improves 8, schedule a focused eval run with the actual model on a held-out prompt set (see validation gating).nnvalidation gating (before production rollout):n- must pass: fidelity_delta 7.n- must not: memory pressure events per node 2 in a simulated 6-hour run.n- secondary check: run a 2-node hardware-in-the-loop (hil) smoke test with kvcache-service snapshots to validate non-linear cache effects.nnoutput artifacts produced by ses:n- per-tenant metric csv: tenant_id,timestamp,p99,throughput,fidelity_delta,mem_pressure_countn- ses seed to map back to simulated trace.n4) if canary passes, schedule staged ramp with throttles at 5, 25, 60, 100 over 4872 hours.n5) if failure at any stage, run the ses rewind harness to reproduce dsid_2f9c99fc8ec74495b4b08c49a6083ba8, source_type: confluence, title: deterministic playback manifest format (v1), content: overviewnthis page defines the deterministic playback manifest format (v1): a lightweight, self-contained json document intended to capture everything needed to deterministically replay an inference session (or an ordered set of requests) across model rollouts, runtime variants, kernel changes, and quantization profiles.nnthe primary goal is to make postmortems, regression triage, and model a/b comparisons reproducible without requiring full environment cloning.nn non-goalsnthe manifest is intentionally not a full provenance ledger.nnout of scope for v1n- capturing private customer data inline. manifests must reference redacted payloads or point to approved secure storage locations.n- general-purpose data lineage, training provenance, or governance/audit trails.nn design principlesn- minimal: reference large artifacts instead of embedding blobs.n- deterministic intent: include all inputs that can affect output (tokenizer, seeds, runtime config, policies/hooks).n- portable: json, human-readable, attachable to support tickets and github issues.n- privacy-aware: pii-bearing content must be referenced via controlled pointers and governed by a privacy policy token.nn applicability and versioningn- this page defines v1 of the format. breaking changes require a new manifest_version.n- forward-compatible additions must be optional and ignored by older runners.nn required top-level fields (v1)nall top-level fields are json keys.nnidentity and metadatan- manifest_version (required): must be 1n- manifest_id (required): short stable id (uuid recommended)n- created_by (required): name/email of authoring agent (person or system)n- created_at (required): rfc3339 timestampn- source_context (required): freeform string describing scenario (ui flow, api route, ticket)nnartifacts and executionn- model_artifact (required): model id artifact digestn- tokenizer (required): tokenizer id digestn- environment (required): runtime/environment snapshot string (see environment fields)n- requests (required): ordered list encoded as json array in the manifest each element is a request descriptor (see below)nndeterminism controlsn- runtime_flags (required): list of keyvalue strings affecting execution (e.g., use_kv_cachetrue)n- deterministic_seeds (required): list of seed assignments (e.g., global_seed42, sampler_seed42)n- determinism_mode (required): one of strict best_effortnnobservability and privacyn- telemetry_refs (optional but recommended): pointers to associated logs/traces/metricsn- privacy_policy (required): one of none partial strictn- payload_policy (required): one of inline_redacted pointer_requirednnintegrity (updated in v1)n- integrity (optional): a compact string describing integrity mechanism. v1 runners support:n - nonen - sha256-only (checksums required no signature)n - sigstore-oidc (signature envelope stored separately manifest contains reference)nn update vs. early draft: signature is no longer a direct embedded blob in v1. use integrity plus integrity_ref (see below) to avoid copying large envelopes into tickets.nn optional top-level fields (v1)n- telemetry_bundle_ref: uri to a packaged bundle (trace token metrics logs) when available.n- integrity_ref: uri to signature/envelope material when integrity ! none.n- notes: freeform human notes.nn request descriptor (v1)neach requests element represents one request in a deterministic sequence.nnrequired request fieldsn- request_id: short id, unique within manifestn- timestamp: rfc3339 timestamp of original requestn- api_route: e.g., /v1/generate or /v1/chat/completionsn- raw_payload_ref: pointer to stored payload (gcs/s3/secure-store) or inline redacted json string when permitted by policyn- input_checksums: list of checksums for payload-derived inputsn- sampling_config: canonical string encoding of sampling knobsnnrecommended request fieldsn- client_sdk: client library versionn- pre_hooks: ordered list of transformations applied pre-runtime (name@version checksum)n- post_hooks: ordered list of transformations applied post-runtimen- expected_response_fingerprint: fingerprint of original response for quick divergence checksn- fallback_policy_trace: record of any fallbacks (model switch, retry, safety downgrade) with timestampsnn update vs. early draft: v1 standardizes on expected_response_fingerprint rather than signature wording to avoid confusion with cryptographic signatures.nn environment fields (v1)nenvironment is represented as a compact semicolon-delimited string of keyvalue pairs to keep manifests small and friendly to ticket systems.nnrequired environment keysn- runtime_image: container name digest (must include digest)n- host_os: e.g., ubuntu-22.04n- region: e.g., us-west-2n- accelerator: e.g., a100-80gb or cpunnrecommended environment keysn- runtime_release: serving runtime release tagn- kernel_determinism: on off mixedn- concurrency_profile: single-req batchedn- num_shards: integernn update vs. early draft: runtime_image must include a digest (e.g., redwood/runtime-infer@sha256:...) because tags are not stable enough for deterministic repro.nn checksum and fingerprint rules (v1)n input checksumsn- checksums must be sha256.n- input_checksums entries are strings with a prefix:n - raw:sha256: for raw payload bytes (post-redaction if redacted inline)n - tok:sha256: for tokenized input ids (canonical serialization)nn response fingerprint (v1)nthe response fingerprint algorithm is fixed in v1 to avoid ambiguity:n- normalize model output by:n 1) converting crlf to lfn 2) trimming trailing whitespace on each linen 3) ensuring final newline is absentn- compute sha256 over utf-8 bytes of the normalized stringn- encode as resp:sha256:nn update vs. early draft: v1 explicitly uses sha256 of normalized text (not embeddings) for expected_response_fingerprint. embedding similarity is permitted in reports but not a manifest primitive.nn telemetry references (v1)ntelemetry_refs are uris (or internal artifact ids) pointing to:n- structured trace (jaeger/tempo trace id)n- token-level metrics (latency per token, logprobs if enabled)n- server logs (filtered range)n- resource utilization snapshotnnwhen available, prefer a single telemetry_bundle_ref that points to a packaged artifact.nn privacy and securityn- raw_payload_ref must comply with privacy_policy and payload_policy.n- for privacy_policystrict, manifests must not include raw text content use secure pointers only.n- redacted inline payloads are permitted only with privacy_policypartial and payload_policyinline_redacted.n- if payload pointers are used, the pointer must reference an access-controlled store with audit logs.nn json example (v1)nbelow is an illustrative example (fields shown as a single json document). values are representative.nnn overviewnnpurpose: this document defines a canonical mapping of serving runtime kernel failure modes to observable signals, the telemetry schema required to detect each class, an experimentation and profiling playbook for reproducing and triaging, additions to the benchmarking suite to validate mitigations, and a short incident runbook for field response. the goal is to reduce mttd/mttr for kernel-related degradations and provide a reproducible experiment surface for safety rollouts.nnscope: kernel execution layer and scheduler interactions within the redwood inference runtime (gpu kernels, slot scheduler, kv cache layer, kernel handoff glue). does not include control-plane orchestration (cross-region routing) except where it directly affects kernel affordances (e.g., fallback translation).nnownership and slasnn- primary owner_team: engineering (serving-runtime).n- secondary stakeholders: eng-sre (oncall), eng-infra (gpu fleet), security-and-compliance (if pii surfaced during traces).n- detection sla: new kernel regressions should be detectable via automated telemetry within 5 minutes of an slo breach signal (tail-latency 99.9th baseline).nnfailure modes taxonomy (high-level)nn1) slow kernel (increased p99p999 latency)n - cause examples: regressed kernel code-path, contention on tensor cores, thermal throttling.n - observables: rising kernel_exec_latency percentiles, increased gpu occupancy variance, drop in token throughput, tail-latency drift on specific request classes.nn2) kernel hang / watchdog-triggered node failn - cause examples: deadlock in kernel work-queue, nv driver regression, interconnect stall.n - observables: missing kernel completion events, cpu spin loops on dispatch threads, nvml/tdx node-level stalls, abrupt eviction traces.nn3) silent correctness degradation (numerical drift / quantization mismatch)n - cause examples: quantization kernel change, dtype mismatch, kernel reorder.n - observables: model output divergence vs baseline on shadow channel, increased invalid-token rates, eval-suite qa failures on golden prompts.nn4) resource mis-accounting (memory leak / fragmentation)n - cause examples: allocator regression, orphaned buffers across handoffs, fragmenting nvlink buffers.n - observables: sustained growth in gpu_alloc_bytes, higher oom counts on soft-gc, increased allocator fragmentation ratio.nn5) backpressure amplification (scheduler oscillation)n - cause examples: credit accounting bug, admission controller mis-synthesis.n - observables: cyclical admission/revocation, queue-depth oscillation, correlated spike in rejection_rate and tail-latency.nncanonical telemetry signals and minimum schemannthe runtime telemetry must carry both event and aggregated timeseries signals to map failures quickly. below is the minimal set required for each failure mode. operators should extend with local labels (region, topo_id, kernel_variant) for richer triage.nntable: signal type retention recommended key dimensionsn kernel_exec_latency_ms timeseries histogram 90d at coarse, 30d at full-resolution service, kernel_id, model_family, priority, slot_id n kernel_submit_event event (trace) 30d trace_id, request_id, kernel_variant, args_hash n kernel_complete_event event (trace) 30d trace_id, request_id, duration_ms, return_code n gpu_occupancy_pct timeseries 90d gpu_unit, host, instance_type n allocator_free_bytes timeseries 90d heap_name, slot_id n nvml_thermal_celsius timeseries 30d gpu_unit, host n kvcache_hit_rate_prefix timeseries 90d model_family, session_cohort n shadow_eval_delta_score timeseries 365d (for regression hunting) prompt_set, model_variant nnsignal naming and invariant: every kernel-level event must include a kernel_id, kernel_variant, and a monotonic timestamp_ns. events should be linkable to a request_id or to a synthetic shadow_id for benchmarked traces.nnprofiling experiment playbook (step-by-step)nn1) reproduce in shadow channeln - mirror a 15 production sample to a shadow pool tagged with the affected kernel_variant. ensure no traffic is returned to users.n - capture full trace for kernel_submit_event - kernel_complete_event and keep raw gpu profiling (nvprof or cupti) for at least one failing trace.nn2) isolate cohort and workload shapen - use request tagging to identify sequence_length, sampling_temperature, and model_family. group by these to find shape-sensitive regressions.nn3) kernel microprofilingn - run microbenchmarks (single-operator synthetic runs) using the runtime microprobe harness. sweep batch sizes, sequence lengths, dtype (fp16, bf16, int8) and collect per-kernel cycles, achieved occupancy, l2 hit rates.nn4) controlled perturbationn - use the controlled-kernel-perturbation harness: ramp kernel concurrency (1-n), inject temporary gpu thermal load, and simulate nvlink latency skew to observe failure thresholds.nn5) deterministic bisectingn - if regression introduced in a recent rollout, perform a binary search across kernel build artifacts using the release manifest. use shadow channels and run the fidelity eval-set on each midpoint.nn6) validate mitigation in bench-suiten - add the reproducer to the benchmarking suite (catalog entry with args), run full-suite including mixed-workload slo simulation, and verify regression is resolved across target hardware variants.nnbenchmarks to add (proposal)nn- microprobe-oscillatory-load: synthetic oscillation profiles to exercise scheduler crediting under cyclical arrival patterns.n- fragment-drift-run: long-run allocator stress to detect slow-growing fragmentation within 2448 hours.n- shadow-fidelity-sweep: golden prompt sweep across quantkernel combinations to catch silent correctness regressions.nnrelease-note checklist for kernel rolloutsnn1) include exact kernel abi/hash and compatible runtime commit.n2) list all known compatible gpu families and excluded hardware.n3) provide expected perf delta ranges by sequence_length and batch_size (p50/p95/p99).n4) document fallback/failopen policy (if kernel fails, which variant is chosen).nnshort incident runbook: kernel slow path (pseudocode)nn1) pager fires (p99 kernel latency threshold for 5m).n2) triage: pull the last 100 kernel_submit_event traces grouped by kernel_id. if the majority show increased internal steps, tag as kernel-slow.n3) mitigate: route new requests to fallback kernel_variant or lower-fidelity model variant via route policy for affected cluster.n4) remediate: collect nvprof slices from a warm replica, perform microprobe runs, and if a fast fix exists (config tweak: reduce concurrency, change cuda stream affinity), apply in a limited canary.n5) postmortem: record root cause, signal mapping, benchmark delta, and change the bench-suite to include the reproducer.nncommon triage heuristics (quick checks)nn- if nvml_thermal_celsius is rising concurrent with occupancy drops - thermal throttling suspect.n- if kernel_complete_event missing across many traces but submit events present - hang / watchdog path.n- if shadow_eval_delta_score shows high variance but latency normal - correctness/regression not performance.n- if allocator_free_bytes trending down steadily across nodes - memory leak or fragmentation.nnquality gates and automated detection rules (examples)nn- alert rule: kernel_exec_latency_mskernel_idk1.p99 baseline_p99(k1) 1.3 for 10 minutes - create sev2.n- auto-action: on sev2 for kernel slow path, enact routing policy to shift 10 of traffic to fallback variant and create an automated diagnostic job to sample 250 traces to shadow store.nndata retention and privacy notesnn- traces may contain prompt hashes and request metadata. store full traces only in restricted buckets. telemetry summaries (percentiles) can be internal. when sharing with third parties or including in vendor bug reports, minimize user-identifying fields and use prompt_set ids instead of raw prompts. security must approve any full-trace export.nnopen known issues mitigations (short catalog)nn- intermittent nvlink timeout under sustained cross-gpu kv cache prefetching (mitigation: serialize prefetch window and increase nvlink retry backoff).n- subtle int8 path reordering causing off-by-one token errors in legacy kernels (mitigation: promote failing input set to shadow-fidelity-sweep and disable int8 variant until fix).n- scheduler-label flapping when admission credits are recomputed under heavy churn (mitigation: apply 5s smoothing to credit recomputation).nnappendix: example cli commands and snippetsnn- capture a single failing trace (from operator machine):n rdwctl trace capture --request-id --output /tmp/trace-.json rollout runbook, content: overviewnnthis page defines the execution inspection proxy (eip): a lightweight, in-path inspection layer designed to enable low-overhead sampling, causal tracing, and feature experimentation against live inference traffic. the intent is to provide a safe way to surface execution-level signals (kernel selection, batching decisions, kv-cache warmup, and tail latency contributors) without modifying the core runtime or blocking production flows.nngoals and non-goalsn- goals:n - capture causal telemetry for sampled requests: kernel selection, batch composition, queue wait, dispatch, and kernel execution durations.n - support non-invasive shadow sampling and replay capture for downstream profiling.n - provide a controlled canary rollout pattern with clear safety gates and rollback criteria.n - emit structured events compatible with our observability pipeline (otlp/jaeger-compatible spans json payloads to kinesis).n- non-goals:n - this proxy is not a replacement for full kernel-level instrumentation. it intentionally samples and reconstructs rather than tracing every token event.nnarchitectural overviewn- deployment: the eip runs as a co-located process on runtime nodes (container sidecar or host process) and accepts a mirrored subset of requests via the request-router. it has two logical components: the fast-path forwarder and the asynchronous inspector.n- fast-path forwarder:n - for mirrored/inspected requests, forward to runtime with tcp passthrough and minimal packetization to preserve latency characteristics.n - add only a single hop and a configurable metadata header (x-eip-sampled: id, sample-rate, sample-reason).n- asynchronous inspector:n - receives sampling copies via the forwarder and enriches them by collecting decision traces from scheduler hooks and kernel handshake messages.n - persists captures to the profiling bucket and emits telemetry events.nntextual diagramn request router -- runtime node -- (eip forwarder) -- runtime coren n (copied sample) -- (eip inspector) -- telemetry / profiling-bucketnnkernel scheduling interactions and safety considerationsn- priority propagation:n 1) the eip must not change runtime scheduling priorities. to avoid priority inversion, the proxy only annotates metadata it never adjusts request priority headers unless explicitly enabled in experiment mode.n 2) when experiment mode is enabled, a separate gating service (priority-gate) authorizes transient priority hints stored in a short-lived config (ttl 60s) to the scheduler.n- backpressure and admission control:n - eip respects runtime admission controller signals. if the runtime returns http 429 for a mirrored request, inspector drops additional enrichment traffic for that request to avoid amplification.n- kernel handshake correlation:n - the inspector consumes the kernel handshake stream (read-only subscription) to correlate kernel id - execution timings. this subscription path is throttled to 1 of live handshakes by default.nnprofiling benchmarking plann- success metrics for experiment:n - end-to-end p50 overhead introduced by eip on observed requests 95 of sampled requests to kernel handshake when sampling rate is 1/1000.n- benchmarks to run:n 1) baseline synthetic workload: 10k rps mixed seq-lengths (8/64/512) using shadow-generator v2. command: n ./shadow-generator --rps 10000 --mix 0.6:8,0.3:64,0.1:512 --duration 30m --dest n 2) canary real-traffic mirror: 0.1 live traffic mirrored for 24 hours with continuous telemetry checks.n 3) load spike stress test: inject a 5x traffic spike for 10 minutes and observe eip behavior under kernel negotiation churn.n- measurement guidance:n - use histogram exports for latency (client-observed), eip forwarder add-on latency, and inspector processing time.n - collect kernel handshake correlation rate and amount of additional memory allocated for captured artifacts.n - compare generation token throughput and tail latency against baseline snapshots collected immediately prior to eip enablement.nnrunbook: canary rollout (step-by-step)n1) pre-checks (owner: runtime-ops)n - confirm benchmark baseline snapshots exist (p50/p95/p99 for last 24h).n - ensure profiling-bucket has 5gb free and write policy enforces retention 30d.n - verify otlp pipeline is green and downstream parsers accept eip schema.n2) deploy to 2 of fleet as sidecar in passive mode (sampling disabled, headers present) and run 2-hour smoke watch.n3) enable sampling at 0.01 (1/10000) for 1 hour run automated checks:n - cpu delta per node 5 absolute compared to baseline or 10 relative increase.n - node-level cpu increase 5 sustained for 10 minutes.n - any increase in error-rate or kernel oom/invocations threshold.n- immediate steps:n 1) title: session affinity and degraded routing playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook documents the recommended runtime configuration, operational runbooks, and troubleshooting steps for session affinity (sticky sessions) combined with graceful degraded routing for latency-sensitive tenants. it is intended for on-call engineers, runtime owners, and sres operating redwoods inference pools when we need to: preserve kv-cache locality, enforce soft slos for premium tenants, or gracefully degrade capacity during gpu pressure.nngoalsnn- keep 99th-percentile tail latency within slos for latency-sensitive tenants while minimizing token-cost overhead.n- preserve kv cache hit-rate for conversational sessions where possible.n- provide deterministic failover behavior and clear rollout / rollback procedures.nnscope and applicabilitynn- applies to workloads classified as: conversational chat (kv-cache dependent), low-latency text-completion, and mixed chat function-calling flows.n- targets: dedicated and hosted routing layers that support kernel affinity and shard locality.n- not intended for: batch embedding workloads or long-running non-interactive generation jobs.nnkey concepts and behaviornn1) session affinity modesn - strict: bind a session to a single runtime shard until explicit session end. best for very small sessions and when kv cache is critical.n - soft: preferential routing to the last-serving shard allow fallback after a short backoff. balances cache-hit vs availability.n - stateless: no affinity always route using policy (cost or region). only for cache-less or idempotent workloads.nn2) degraded routing strategies (in order of preference)n - local-evict-and-shed: if a shard is memory-starved, evict cold kv entries and continue serving with degraded cache-hit.n - variant-fallback: route to a quantized/cheap variant of the model on the same or nearby shard.n - inter-shard-redirect: if affinity cannot be preserved, redirect with a short-circuit session-transfer protocol.n - best-effort-broadcast (last resort): fan-out to multiple shards and return the first response (used only for low-qps, high-criticality flows).nnslos and thresholdsnn- primary slo for premium latency-sensitive tenants: 99th percentile p99 latency 85 for conversational sessions.n- degradation trigger thresholds (per shard):nn metric warning critical action n------:---:---n gpu memory free () 25 10 issue local-evict-and-shed (step a) n kernel queue depth 80 of capacity 95 escalate to priority-preempt and trigger variant-fallback n kv-cache eviction rate (entries/s) 50 200 mark as degraded prefer soft-affinity falls back nnconfiguration examplesnnexample runtime routing policy (yaml)nnyamlnrouting_policy:n name: premium-session-soft-affinity-v1n affinity_mode: softn max_sticky_duration_s: 3600n fallback_sequence:n - type: local-evict-and-shedn max_evictions: 500n - type: variant-fallbackn allowed_variants: gptq-8bit, int8-fastn - type: inter-shard-redirectn max_redirect_hops: 1n priority: highn sla_tags: premium, chatnnnscheduler kernel hints (json blob used by kernel mapper)nnjsonnpriority:high,expected_seq_len:256,kv_locality_weight:0.9,preferred_kernel_profile:low-latencynnnoperational runbook: automated response flow (on-call play)nn1) alert: shard memory critical (critical) or kernel queue saturation (critical). pager to runtime-oncall.n2) immediately mark incoming requests for the affected shard with route_hint:degraded. this activates soft-affinity-only routing.n3) execute step a: local-evict-and-shed (automated):n a) run: /opt/redwood/bin/kvctl evict --policycold-first --max 500n b) monitor kv_cache_hit_rate and memory_free for 30s.n c) if memory_free 18 within 30s, continue monitoring annotate incident.n4) if step a fails or kernel queue remains saturated for 60s, trigger variant-fallback: update edge routing table with allowed_variants priority.n5) if variant-fallback does not restore p99 within 2 minutes, perform inter-shard-redirect for new sessions only. sessions with strict affinity must be offered a graceful-transfer token (see api below).n6) if all above fail and p99 600ms for the premium tier after 5 minutes, activate cross-tenant shedding policy (move best-effort tenants off affected pool).nnsession transfer protocol (graceful-transfer)nn- purpose: move a sessions kv state to another shard without dropping the users experience. used when strict-affinity sessions must be migrated.n- steps:n 1) acquire ephemeral lock on session_id via rendezvous service: post /internal/rendezvous/lock session_id: , ttl_s: 30n 2) dump session delta: /opt/redwood/bin/kvctl dump --session --formatjson /tmp/session-.jsonn 3) post /internal/shard-transfer/import target_shard: s-1023, payload: n 4) update routing: put /internal/routing/sessions/ shard:s-1023,affinity_mode:strictn 5) release lock.nnobservability and dashboardsnnrequired dashboards and panels:n- shard_overview: p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel queue depth, gpu memory free, active_sessions, kv_cache_hit_rate.n- session_affinity_telemetry: session bind events, transfer attempts, transfer latency, transfer failures.n- degraded_routing_incidents: count and duration per shard, actions executed, rollback events.nnessential alerts (examples)n- alert: shard-mem-critical - expr: gpu_memory_free_pct severity: critical - runbook: this doc step 2n- alert: kernel-queue-saturated - expr: kernel_queue_depth / kernel_capacity 0.95 for 30s - severity: critical - runbook: escalate immediate preemptionn- alert: session-transfer-failures - expr: rate(session_transfer_failures5m) 1 - severity: high - runbook: inspect rendezvous logsnntesting and benchmarking guidancenn- synthetic test to validate affinity benefit: run parallel a/b across same shard (sticky) vs random routing for 10k sessions, 95th-percentile delta should show 8 latency improvement and 20 kv-cache hit-rate improvement for typical chat workloads.n- stress test for variant-fallback: overlay 50 additional burst and assert fallback switch completes within 45s and maintains functional correctness (no truncated json responses).nnmaintenance and rollout checklistnn1) canary rollout schedule: 5 traffic (10 minutes) - 25 (30 typical sequence length, prompt entropy (deterministic vs high-entropy), and inter-arrival distribution. we provide the recommended stress generator (loadkit) commands and expected runtime flags to enable consistent runs.nna. steady-state throughput (baseline)n- definition: constant qps with uniform sequence length used to calibrate nominal per-token overhead and bandwidth.n- parameters: qps50, seq_len128, concurrency25 clients, token_gen_modelllamav2-13bn- generator example:n loadkit run --shape steady --qps 50 --seq-len 128 --clients 25 --duration 15m --model llamav2-13b n- runtime flags: --kv-cacheon --batchingcontinuous --batch-max-tokens8192nnb. bursty microspikesn- definition: short (30s-2m) bursts at 510x baseline qps tests kernel preemption and queue admission.n- parameters: ramp --start-qps 5 --end-qps 500 --ramp-duration 10m --hold 5m --seq-len 256nnd. tail-heavy (sporadic large sequences)n- definition: mix of short (32 tokens) and long (2048 tokens) requests, with long requests at 2 frequency. validates sequence-length-dependent kernel breakpoints.n- generator example:n loadkit run --shape tail-heavy --short 32 --long 2048 --long-rate 0.02 --qps 80 --duration 20mnne. cold-fanout (many cold model initializations)n- definition: many clients create new sessions without sharing kv cache. designed to exercise warmup/warmstart paths and model load latency.n- generator example:n loadkit run --shape cold-fanout --clients 500 --session-duration 10s --seq-len 64 --duration 15mnnf. mixed-tenant blend (multi-tenant interference)n- definition: two synthetic confluence, title: experimental kernel stability matrix and run manifest, content: summarynnthis page defines the experimental kernel stability matrix and an associated run manifest used by the runtime, kernel, profiling, and benchmarking teams to systematically exercise kernel changes across production-like axes (model variants, quantization modes, sequence shapes, batching profiles, and hardware families). the intent is to provide a single-source-of-truth experiment catalog that: n- produces repeatable telemetry for stability/latency regressionsn- surfaces cross-layer interactions clear pass/fail criteria that teams can apply in ci and in lab runs.nnmatrix concept and axesn-----------------------nwe represent experiments as rows in the stability matrix. each row is a single run table)n- batch_shape: continuous bursty single-token-heavyn- admission_profile: normal preemptive low_priorityn- fidelity_flags: runtime flags that change fallback/kv behavior (e.g. async_prefetchon, kv_persistencesticky)n- pass_criteria: numeric slos and signal thresholds for this experimentnnexample experiment row (table-friendly text)n------------------------------------------------n row_id async_prefetchonkv_persistencesticky p50 ///n5) repeats: run each row at least 3 independent times compute median of medians for stable metrics.nnpass / fail and triage to the experiment bucket.n- triage steps on failure:n 1. confirm environment (pool id, driver/kernel versions) against the manifest.n 2. load last-good baseline artifact (baseline row id noted in matrix) and replay with the same trace.n 3. run the profiler diff (script: tooling/esm/profiler-diff.sh) to generate a delta report.n 4. if regression maps to kernel latency (vs. scheduling), open a kernel regression triage ticket and run the controlled-perturbation playbook (link in related_pages).nnintegrations with other artifactsn--------------------------------n- benchmarking suite: each row references a canonical bench workload id (bench-id) used by our throughput and cost simulations. add bench-id to manifest when exporting to the benchmark catalog.n- release notes: adds a short section playbooks replay harness. include the sample-rate and trace-filter used.nndefault run prioritization and scheduling rulesn------------------------------------------------nwe prioritize rows with the highest customer impact first:n1) model families that are in production for top-20 customersn2) quantization modes in active use (int8, q4_1)n3) hardware families with active capacity commitmentsn4) within budget across repeats, mark as flaky rather than failed.n- annotate known-noise sources in the manifest (network jitter, shared-nvlink traffic, scheduled maintenance windows).nnoperational title: runtime experimentation safety and governance checklist, content: overviewnnpurpose:n- provide a practical, repeatable checklist and governance guidance for running experiments that touch the serving runtime (kernel scheduling, eviction behavior, batch shaping, quantization rollouts, routing/fallback policies, and instrumentation changes).n- reduce risk to production slos and customer traffic while enabling safe iteration across runtime subsystems.nnscope:n- applies to any change or experiment that affects: kernel selection/variants, scheduler policies, kvcache behaviour, batching/cohorting logic, fallback routing, runtime-invoked model variants, telemetry sampling strategy, and external benchmarking harnesses that mirror production traffic.n- does not replace sync, telemetry pipeline).n- risk tier (low/medium/high) use the tier rules below.n- target cohorts/tenants and whether experiment will touch dedicated or private clusters.n- expected duration and content: summarynnthis page defines the execution telemetry quorum and sampling policy for redwoods serving runtime. it explains the signals we collect, the quorum rules used to trigger high-fidelity capture, the sampling knobs available to runtime operators and sres, and operational playbooks for incidents and benchmarks. the goal is to balance diagnostic fidelity for production incidents and regressions with telemetry cost and privacy constraints.nnwhy this mattersnn- full-fidelity traces for all requests are prohibitively expensive (bandwidth, storage, ingestion cost).n- certain failures and regressions only manifest under narrow execution cohorts a simple uniform sampler reduces reproducibility.n- kernel-level scheduling signals, kv-cache deltas, and cross-device handoff traces are high-value for root-cause analysis but high-cost to capture.n- we need a deterministic, auditable policy that: preserves slo observability, limits cost, enables postmortem reproducibility, and supports controlled ramping during experiments.nnscope and definitionsnn- execution telemetry: structured traces, kernel scheduling events, per-kernel latency histograms, kv cache hit/miss traces, device-to-device handoff events, and request provenance metadata.n- quorum: a multi-signal predicate that determines whether a specific request execution should be elevated to high-fidelity capture.n- sampling knob types: uniform, cohort-based, adaptive, and quorum-triggered.nnquorum signals (used in predicates)nn1) slo breach candidate: request latency 95th percentile for route/model for the last 15 minutes.n2) kernel anomaly: per-kernel execution time kernel_baseline 3 (fast local baseline).n3) cross-tenant contention signal: gpu kernel preemption or eviction events observed within request lifetime.n4) kv cache warmup failure: expected cached prefix missing for an established session (session age 1 minute).n5) error family match: any 5xx or structured runtime error matching the incident regex list.nnquorum policy (default production)nn- elevate to high-fidelity capture when any two distinct quorum signals are true for the same request or when a single critical signal is flagged (error family match or gpu preemption).n- high-fidelity capture includes: complete kernel event stream, full per-token scheduler decisions, gpu telemetry slice, request input/output payloads (redacted), and kv cache deltas.nnsampling tiers and retentionnn- baseline (always-on): lightweight request metrics and sparse trace ids (1 uniform). retention: 90 days aggregated metrics, 7 days indexed traces.n- diagnostic (cohort-based): 5 of traffic per high-risk route (see table below) or cohort sampling determined by route annotations. retention: 30 days indexed traces.n- quorum-captured (elevated): retained for 90 days in compressed archive with access controls access requires incident ticket and approval.nnoperational table: sampling defaults by route profilenn- low-latency-read: uniform 0.5 (embeddings, short completions).n- interactive-chat: uniform 1, cohort 3 for power users.n- long-generation: uniform 2, cohort 10 for pinned beta customers.n- batch-embedding-job: uniform 0.2, cohort capture via job-id sampling 1.nn(operators can override per-customer using route config in redwood console see how to override below.)nncost/benchmark impact guidancenn- turning on kernel-level event capture increases per-request telemetry payload by 812kb and ingestion cpu by 1.4x in our benchmarks. expect storage 10x for full request-level captures vs. aggregated metrics.n- benchmarks run with high-fidelity capture enabled should use the telemetry-isolated flag to prevent polluted baseline comparisons. see the cli section below.nnimplementation notes (runtime hooks)nn- kernel scheduler hooks: place a light-weight hook at kernel dispatch entry to emit a 64-byte token with request id and scheduling decision. hooks must be non-blocking and batch-emitted at 50ms intervals.n- kv cache tracing: emit a compact diff (keys touched, miss/hit) with session id and hashed prefix. do not include raw prompt text unless redaction pass is applied.n- device handoff: emit handshake events with device ids, estimated queue depth, and kernel queue latency.nnsample quorum predicate (yaml)nnquorum:n version: 1n rules:n - id: slo_and_kerneln description: latency spike kernel abnormalityn predicates:n - signal: slo_breach_candidaten - signal: kernel_anomalyn require: 2n - id: critical_errorn description: immediate capture on critical errorsn predicates:n - signal: error_family_matchn require: 1nnhow to override sampling in console (step-by-step)nn1) navigate to console runtime routes and select the route.n2) click telemetry tab.n3) edit sampling profile: choose baseline/cohort/quorum-enabled.n4) optional: attach a temporary experiment tag (telemetry.debugtrue, expiry in 24h). changes are audited and emitted as config diff to s3: s3://redwood-runtime-configs/telemetry-overrides.n5) monitor cost impact: console shows estimated daily ingestion delta before committing.nnrunbook: incident capture and access flow (for sres)nn1) triage: determine whether the incident is reproducible and whether quorum predicates would have captured examples.n2) if not captured, flip a cohort override for the affected route with a 10x cohort multiplier for 30 minutes. use the cli: redwood telemetry override --route --multiplier 10 --duration 30m --reason incident pid-.n3) collect captures: link to s3 tarball in the incident ticket. retain copy in incident workspace (encrypted).n4) postmortem: annotate the captured traces with kernel snapshot id, runtime version, and scheduler policy.nncli examplesnn enable ephemeral high-fidelity capture for routenredwood telemetry override --route /v1/generate--chat --set quorum_enabledtrue --duration 20m --owner sre-teamnn run benchmark without telemetry noisenredwood bench run --workload long-gen --telemetry-isolatedtrue --output ./bench-resultsnnprivacy and redaction rulesnn- request payloads are redacted by default: only prompt hashes and token counts are stored. full text is captured only when: (a) customer consent is present, or (b) explicit legal/incident approval is granted.n- pii redaction pipeline: apply token-level redaction that replaces probable pii tokens with and emits confidence score.nntesting and rollout plan for changes to quorum policynn1) developer preview: enable policy in the sandbox runtime (tag: telemetry-sandbox) for 1 week with 100 traffic in sandbox. verify schema, cpu overhead 5 - 25 - 100 over rolling four-day windows. sre gate: ingestion cost increase must be 2x forecast, page observability platform lead and sre. use incident channel telemetry-ops.nnappendix: schema snippets and sample json trace (compact)nn- compact trace example (fields explained):nn trace_id: abcd-1234,n route: /v1/generate,n model: rw-open-7b,n events: kernel_dispatch:ts:...,kv_cache_delta:...,handoff:...,n meta: schema_v1nnn- telemetry cost estimator quick lookup (console): per-100k requests estimated delta with kernel_captureon: 1,200/day grokking and telemetry orchestration playbook, content: purpose:nthis page documents the signal taxonomy and orchestration patterns we use to reason about end-to-end execution behaviour in the serving runtime. it is intended for runtime engineers, sres, and performance analysts who need a repeatable way to:n- find the right signal when debugging kernel regressions or slo violations,n- configure telemetry collection with cost-aware sampling, andn- run focused profiling and benchmarking experiments that map back to production observability.nnscope and goals:n1) make multi-layer signal mapping explicit: request surface - dispatch - scheduler - kernel - device.n2) provide a small, prioritized signal set for fast triage (the fast five).n3) standardize sampling and enrichment so production traces are high-signal for regression hunts.n4) define a profiling playbook and benchmark checklist to validate fixes and measure cost/latency trade-offs.nnfast five signals (priority order):n1) request.timeline.total_ms end-to-end wall-clock for the request.n2) kernel.exec_ms_p95 kernel execution time, p95 per kernel type.n3) gpu.dispatch_queue_depth instantaneous queue length at dispatcher.n4) kvcache.hit_ratio_prefix_ms prefix kv cache hit latency and ratio for session keys.n5) preempt.count_per_min count of scheduler preemptions per minute.nnsignal taxonomy and where to instrument:n- api layer (dispatch-proxy): request.id, client_token, request.timeline.. instrument with http middleware that injects x-request-id and logs entry/exit timestamps.n- orchestrator / dispatcher (execution-orchestrator): queuing_delay_ms, dispatch_to_scheduler_ms, queue_depth. emit counters and histogram aggregates at 1s granularity.n- scheduler (kernel-scheduler): scheduling_latency_ms (queue-launch), slot_allocation_reason, preempt_ events. attach a lightweight trace span for each kernel handoff.n- kernel runtime: kernel.exec_ms, kernel.memory_bytes, kernel_variant (int8/float16/fp32). export per-kernel histograms with bucket boundaries aligned to expected breakpoints (8ms, 16ms, 32ms, 64ms, 128ms, 256ms).n- accelerator/device: device_util_pct (1s), thermal_events, nvlink_retries. device exporter runs on node and tags metrics with node_id, rack_id.nncorrelation keys and propagation rules:n- request.id must be propagated across rpcs and attached to kernel spans. use header x-request-id and, inside the data plane, the 64-bit trace token rt_trace added to the first 8 bytes of the request header.n- session.id and kvcache.key_prefix should be attached to kv cache metrics and trace spans to correlate warm/cold behaviour.n- kernel_variant and model_version must be top-level tags on every telemetry object for cohorting.nnsampling policy (cost-aware):n- baseline: sample 0.5 of requests for full-span traces with detailed kernel traces.n- anomaly amplification: for any request where request.timeline.total_ms p95_slo_threshold 2, sample 100 of such requests for 30 minutes.n- experiment switch: when running a kernel rollout experiment (flag: kernel_experimenttrue), increase full-span sample to 5 for that cohort for the duration of the experiment.n- heavy-path profiling: for requests routed to dedicated pools (redwood-dedicated-), enable 2 always-on profiling to capture steady-state behaviour.nntelemetry configuration example (yaml):nntelemetry:n default_sample_rate: 0.005n anomaly_amplify_factor: 100n profiling:n dedicated_pools_sample: 0.02n enrichers:n - rt_tracen - kernel_variantn - model_versionnn(this yaml is a minimal example for the dispatcher operator config.)nntagging and metric naming conventions (summary table):n layer metric prefix key tags (examples) granularity kernel_variant event 1s n kernel runtime kernel.exec_ kernel_type, model_version, host_id histogram n device device.util_ node_id, gpu_index, thermal_state 1s nnprofiling playbook (step-by-step):n1) establish baseline: run the canonical benchmark suite (see benchmark checklist) to capture baseline kernel.exec_ms_p50/p95/p99 for the target model and sequence profile.n2) reproduce in staged environment: mirror 10 of production traffic to a canary dispatcher with identical telemetry sampling.n3) isolate the layer: use request.timeline. and scheduler. spans to determine whether the latency is in dispatch, scheduling, kernel exec, or device.n4) if kernel.exec_ms_p95 increased: capture 100 full-span traces for the offending kernel_variant and run kernel microbenchmarks (kernel-only runner) with the same batch/seq shapes.n5) if device_util_pct high but kernel.exec low: investigate device contention (nvlink, pcie stalls) using device exporters and nvlink_retries counter.n6) patch hypotheses: apply targeted fixes (kernel parameter, prefetch hint, batching change) behind an experiment flag.n7) validation: run the benchmark suite and mirrored traffic experiment require no regression on p95 and a measured unit-cost delta within acceptable range before rollout.nnbenchmark checklist (operational):n- use workload generator with the production sequence length distribution.n- run for 30 minutes steady-state 10x microbursts to test tail behaviour.n- collect: request.timeline.total_ms, kernel.exec_ms_ histograms, kvcache.hit_ratio, device.util_pct, preempt.count.n- pass criteria: p95 latency queue_depth_threshold (default 64): scale up dispatcher slots or divert low-priority cohorts.n5) if device_util_pct 95 for 60s on 2 gpus in the cluster: follow device incident playbook (see link in references).n6) communicate: post initial summary to runtime-ops channel with runbook correlation_id and owner.nnregression hunt heuristics (pattern catalog):n- pattern: sharp increase in kernel.exec_ms_p95 with no device_util_pct change - likely kernel codepath regression or input shape distribution change.n- pattern: rising preempt.count_per_min and growing tail - scheduler policy or admission change causing churn.n- pattern: kvcache.hit_ratio drop increased dispatch latency - session key format change or cache namespace collision.nnrelease tensor-parallel hangs under sustained load, content: summaryntensor-parallel (tp) replicas can intermittently hang (no forward progress) under sustained, mixed workloads (prefill decode, long-context, bursty concurrency). this typically presents as streaming responses stalling and eventually request timeouts. in the worst case, one or more gpus appear wedged until the replica is drained/restarted.nnthis page documents:n- observable symptoms and common signaturesn- affected configurations (models, tp sizes, hardware)n- how to detect and confirm a tp stalln- recommended mitigations (operational config)n- fix status by runtime version and feature flagsnn if you are actively in an incident: jump to immediate mitigations and then follow triage.nn---nn impact / why we caren- customer impact: streaming completions stall end-users see long hangs then timeouts. enterprise dedicated accounts are most affected due to higher sustained concurrency.n- operational impact: autoscaler thrash (p99 latency spikes trigger scale-up wedged replicas never recover), elevated error rates, sev1 potential.n- cost impact: stalled replicas waste gpu capacity and increase retry/duplicate compute.nn---nn symptoms (what youll see)n external (api / client-facing)n- streaming response starts and then stops emitting tokens mid-decode.n- requests remain in-flight until client timeout (commonly 60300s depending on route).n- retry storms (client sdk retries or application-level retries) amplify load.nn internal (replica-level)n- no tokens produced while gpu utilization may remain non-zero or drop unexpectedly.n- one tp rank appears stuck while others continue to enqueue work (or also stop).n- nccl may not throw an explicit error hangs can be silent without async error handling.nn common failure signatures (taxonomy)nwe currently bucket stalls into these high-level signatures (see runtime.tp_stall_reason below):n1. collective_wait: rank waiting for nccl collective completion.n2. collective_mismatch: collective ordering divergence across ranks (often manifests as silent wait).n3. scheduler_starvation: collectives not scheduled fairly under prefill-heavy batching.n4. stream_sync_gap: cuda stream/event ordering issue around nccl boundary.n5. kv_compaction_divergence: kv cache compaction/fragmentation causes rank-side divergence.n6. cancelled_stream_deadlock: client disconnect/cancellation leaves ranks in inconsistent step state.nn---nn affected configurationsnthis issue has been observed most reliably under the following conditions.nn workload characteristicsn- mixed prompt lengths (high variance) streaming decoden- long context (8k32k) high concurrent requestsn- bursty arrival patterns (spikes causing deep scheduler queues)n- prefill-heavy traffic interleaved with ongoing decodesnn deployment modesn- dedicated: most common due to steady saturation and strict p99 expectations.n- hosted: seen in a smaller number of high-throughput routes during peak bursts.nn models and tp sizes (most affected)n category examples notes n---------n large dense, long-context llama-70b class, qwen-72b class higher risk when tp4/8 and context 8k n moe models mixtral 8x7b class sensitive to scheduling/fairness under mixed prefill/decode n any model with aggressive batching any high-throughput route risk increases with deep queues and long prefill batches nn hardware / topologyn hardware topologies seen notes n---------n a100 80gb nvlink intra-node most reproductions and customer reports n h100 80gb nvlink intra-node also observed typically at higher throughput n pcie-only multi-gpu mixed less common in production higher sensitivity to comms latency nn runtime versionsn- observed most often on runtime 1.18.x in the presence of cuda graph capture mixed workloads.n- some signatures also present on early 1.19.0 canaries prior to watchdog ordering hardening.nn---nn detection signals (metrics, logs, traces)n dashboardsn- see: tp stall and timeout dashboard (confluence: tp-stall-and-timeout-dashboard).nn key metrics (authoritative)n metric names reflect the current standards agreed with sre older versions may differ.nn1) per-rank heartbeatn- runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_secondsreplica_id, tp_rank, model, clustern- signal: heartbeats stop updating for one or more ranks.n- rule of thumb: gap 10s during active traffic is suspicious gap 30s is a likely stall.nn2) stall reason countersn- runtime_tp_stall_reason_totalreason, model, tp_size, clustern- watch for spikes in collective_wait, scheduler_starvation, cancelled_stream_deadlock.nn3) in-flight collective countersn- runtime_nccl_inflight_collectivesreplica_id, tp_rank, collectiven- signal: counter remains 0 with no progress (and heartbeat gap).nn4) scheduler pressure indicatorsn- runtime_scheduler_queue_depthreplica_id, queuen- runtime_scheduler_prefill_decode_ratioreplica_idn- signal: queue depth grows while decode throughput collapses.nn5) customer-visible indicatorsn- gateway_request_timeout_totalroute, modeln- gateway_streaming_disconnect_totalroute, modeln- request_p99_latency_msroute, modelnn logs (what to grep)nlook for structured fields (availability depends on runtime version):n- tp_stall_detectedtruen- tp_rank and tp_sizen- stall_reasonn- inflight_collectivesn- last_progress_msnn nccl debug (use with care)nuse only for time-boxed windows due to verbosity/perf impact. coordinate with sre (see int: enable extra nccl debug logging).nsuggested minimal settings for targeted capture:n- nccl_async_error_handling1n- nccl_debugwarnn- nccl_debug_subsyscollnndo not leave nccl_debuginfo enabled broadly on production dedicated clusters.nn---nn immediate mitigations (incident-safe)nthese mitigations prioritize restoring service and preventing global gpu wedging.nn 1) drain/replace suspect replicasn- drain the affected replica(s) at the orchestrator level (preferred) rather than waiting for recovery.n- if multiple replicas show heartbeat gaps, drain in a staggered fashion to avoid full capacity loss.nn 2) reduce concurrency and/or batch size (fastest risk reduction)nrecommended temporary caps (starting point adjust per model/hardware):n- reduce tp.max_concurrency_per_replica by 3050n- reduce max_batch_prefill_tokens (or equivalent) by 2540n- prefer limiting prefill batch growth over decode to preserve streaming responsivenessnn 3) disable high-risk execution paths (if available)ndepending on runtime version and flags, consider:n- disable cuda graphs for tp decode on affected routes:n - runtime.tp.cuda_graphs_decode.enabledfalsen- enable conservative stream/event synchronization around nccl:n - runtime.tp.nccl_stream_sync_hardeningonnn 4) enable watchdog safe abort (where supported)nif the watchdog feature is available in your runtime build, enabling it can prevent indefinite hangs:n- runtime.tp_watchdog.enabledtruen- runtime.tp_watchdog.timeout_ms (see below)nn watchdog enables controlled abort replica drain semantics instead of indefinite waits. this will increase error counts during true stalls but improves overall availability.nn 5) load shedding / routing fallback (platform-level)n- if stall signals are present, enable overload protection to reject/redirect new requests away from the wedged replica pool.n- prefer fallback to a compatible model variant/region if configured for dedicated/hosted.nn---nn recommended default mitigations (non-incident)nfor clusters with frequent tp stall history, keep tp.max_concurrency_per_replica reduces scheduler pressure and mixed-step divergence risk n prefill batch cap limit max_batch_prefill_tokens prevents prefill-heavy batches from starving collectives/decodes n async error handling nccl_async_error_handling1 surfaces errors sooner reduces silent waits n stream sync hardening enable if perf impact acceptable avoids event/stream ordering aggressive thresholds that create false positives under long-context.n- small/medium (13b dense): start at 812sn- large dense (70b) tp4/8: start at 1525sn- long-context (16k): start at 2540snnalways dsid_615d0c7fec0c495d92742626f4f2bdac, source_type: confluence, title: runtime concurrency isolation and telemetry handbook, content: overviewnnthis handbook describes redwood inferences conventions and operational practices for runtime concurrency isolation, lane-based request shaping, and the minimum telemetry required to detect and diagnose cross-tenant or cross-model interference. it consolidates architecture rationale, configuration examples, diagnostics runbooks, and rollout guidance for changing isolation or sampling policies in production.nngoalsn-----n- ensure noisy tenants or long-context workloads do not violate p95/p99 latency slos for other tenants sharing gpus.n- provide a consistent taxonomy (lanes, credits, isolation zones) for engineers and sres to reason about scheduling and fairness.n- define telemetry, sampling, and alerting so incidents can be triaged without deep kernel-level tracing for every case.nnscopen-----nthis doc covers: request lanes, concurrency caps, credit accounting surface (what we expose to schedulers), required metrics, tracing annotations, recommended sampling rates, default configuration snippets for the runtime, and step-by-step operational procedures for common investigations. it does not attempt to re-specify kernel internals refer to kernel mapper docs for low-level execution mappings.nnkey concepts and terminologyn----------------------------n- lane: a logical request class (e.g., realtime, bulk-embed, batching-internal) that maps to priority and concurrency rules.n- concurrency cap: the maximum number of inflight tokens/requests the runtime will accept for a given lane on a shard.n- credit bucket: run-time accounting unit used for fair-share scheduling credits are consumed per request based on model type and sequence length estimate.n- isolation zone: grouping of shards and gpus with stronger anti-affinity guarantees (used for dedicated/private customers).n- soft preemption: a request can be signaled to yield before kernel dispatch when higher-priority work arrives used to reduce tail latency.nndefault lane taxonomy (recommended)n---------------------------------n1. realtime (default for host-api): low concurrency, highest priority, target p99 latency slo.n2. interactive (chat uis): medium concurrency, allow limited batching, mid priority.n3. bulk (embeddings, large generation jobs): high concurrency, low priority, throughput-optimized.n4. system (healthchecks, tracing-heartbeat): dedicated tiny lane, unthrottled internal access.nndefault slos by lanen---------------------n lane p50 latency p95 latency p99 latency throughput expectation n--------------------------------------------------------------------------n realtime batching - kernel_dispatch - kernel_exec - response_serialize.n- errors and preemption events must attach event annotations that include current_credit_balance and preempting_request_id.nnsampling policy (recommended defaults)n-------------------------------------n- 100 sampling for realtime lane traces for first 5 minutes following deploys or config changes (see rollout guidance).n- 2 uniform sampling for interactive lane (min 1 trace per 10 minutes per model).n- 0.5 sampling for bulk (unless latency tail is elevated, then escalate to 5).n- system lane: sample at 10 for health-periodic analysis.nnoperational runbook: diagnosing cross-tenant interference (step-by-step)n--------------------------------------------------------------------n1. get context: incident time window and affected tenant(s). correlate with deployment events in last 30 minutes.n2. query metrics: runtime.inflight_requests and runtime.kernel_queue_length by shard for the time window. look for queue spikes that align with latency regressions.n3. check admission_rejected counters: if rejects increased for realtime lane, inspect which tenants are contributing to credit exhaustion (runtime.credit_balance).n4. if kernel_queue_length high but inflight low, suspect backend kernel stalls: pull kernel_exec span durations from tracing and grep for specific kernel_kind anomalies.n5. if preemption events recorded, find preempting_request_id and evaluate its tenant and model.n6. mitigate: n a. if a single tenant is noisy, apply per-tenant temporary concurrency caps: post /admin/runtime/tenants/tenant_id/caps max_concurrency: 4, lane:bulk n b. if kernel stalls, switch the shard to a different kernel profile: post /admin/shards/shard_id/kernel-profile profile:low-latency (see kernel scheduling interactions below).n c. if kv-cache hot key miss storms present, enable request-level kvcache warmup for affected models.n7. validate: watch p95/p99 and credit_balance for 10 minutes if not recovered, escalate to sre on-call.nnkernel scheduling interactions (practical notes)n----------------------------------------------n- the kernel scheduler consumes credits to assign kernels to sms. when tuning lane caps, consider that lowering concurrency in the runtime can change observed kernel occupancy and shift breakpoints where attention kernels move between sharded and fused implementations.n- suggested guardrails: do not reduce runtime concurrency for a shard below 2 concurrent kernel dispatches for models with sequence_length_estimate 1024 below that risk of throughput collapse due to underutilized sms.nnrecommended configuration snippetsn--------------------------------njson example: runtime admission policy (place in
