document defines the fidelity budgeting model and the runtime cost governor (rcg) a declarative control plane that enforces per-tenant/route fidelity budgets at serving time. the goal of the rcg is to keep customer-visible slos within targets while bounding per-token and per-request spend across mixed workloads.nnintended audiencen- runtime and scheduler engineersn- product owners for dedicated/private customersn- sre and capacity-planning teamsn- benchmark and profiling engineersnnwhy this existsn- inference cost is variable by model variant, sequence length, batching shape and kernel choices.n- we need a single, auditable mechanism to trade fidelity for cost under pressure (autoscale, thermal events, capacity constraints).n- rcg ties scheduling signals, kernel hints, and quantization/variant routing decisions to a budget and provides a deterministic downgrade strategy.nnprinciplesn- predictability: budget enforcement must be explainable and reproducible.n- observability: every fidelity decision must be logged with provenance (trigger, score, pre/post metrics).n- minimize user impact: preservation of critical tokens and short requests is prioritized over long/low-priority generation.n- fast rollback: policy changes must be reversible within a single canary window.nnkey concepts and terminologyn- fidelity budget: numeric allowance per time window (tokens or token-equivalents) that a tenant/route can spend.n- fidelity credit: per-request currency derived from model variant cost and sequence projection.n- degradation ladder: ordered list of fidelity actions (e.g., small-quantize - shorter-prefix-cache - model-variant - response-truncation).n- governor evaluation window: default 30s sliding window for budget accounting.nnmetrics, signals investigation (530 minutes)n - check recent deployments: kernel or scheduler changes in the last 30 minutes (kubectl/ci links).n - correlate with capacity metrics: gpu_utilization, kernel_wait_time_ms, queue_depth.n - run profiling job: sample 2 of traffic for deep trace (use trace-capture cli below).n4) mitigation (30120 minutes)n - if degraded by thermal or hardware: move high-priority tenants to reserved pools.n - if caused by regression: revert policy or kernel flag and roll forward safe-mode config.n - if intentional load spike: negotiate temporary budget increase with product (document in audit).n5) postmortem requirementsn - within 48 hours: publish summary, root cause, timeline, and any policy code changes.nntrace capture cli (example)n- - -n capture 10k motivationnnwe observed a growing class of incidents where median latency is stable but per-request timelines diverge (e.g., 95th/99.9th spikes) without obvious capacity pressure. root causes frequently involve timing interactions across kernel scheduling, kv cache warmup, and ephemeral network backpressure. deterministic request timelines make capacity planning, autoscaling, and slo enforcement reliable. this playbook codifies instrumentation and procedures to diagnose and reduce nondeterministic behavior.nnhigh-level dependency mapnncomponent responsibility owner key page defines a single, operationally actionable taxonomy for runtime signals (conciliation) and a pragmatic approach to grouping traffic by latency cohorts (cohorting). the goal is to standardize how the runtime reconciles competing signals slos, kernel pressure, kv cache warm state, and cost guidance and how the scheduler harmonizes execution decisions across those cohorts to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput and cost targets.nnintended audiencen- runtime engineers (kernel, scheduler, dispatch)n- sres and oncall engineers owning latency slosn- performance and profiling ownersnnwhy this existsnwe observed repeated flapping between priority policies during mixed workloads: short chat requests bouncing against long generation jobs kv cache warmup causing transient tail spikes and adaptive batching oscillations that increase mean latency. those issues trace back to inconsistent interpretation of telemetry signals across components. this doc prescribes: 1) a shared signal vocabulary, 2) cohorting rules, 3) a scheduler harmonization contract, and 4) an operational playbook for experiments and incidents.nnkey conceptsn- signal conciliation: the deterministic process by which the runtime reduces multiple, possibly conflicting telemetry inputs into an ordered set of actions (e.g., throttle, preempt, hedging, fallback).n- latency cohort: a stable label assigned to a request (or request class) representing its expected latency distribution and tolerance (e.g., interactive-50ms, elastic-200ms, batch-1s). cohorts are used to drive scheduling, admission, and caching policies.n- steering signals: canonical telemetry used for conciliation. see table below.nnsteering signals (canonical)n- slo_gap: (slo_target_ms - observed_p95_ms) normalized by slo_target_ms. positive healthy.n- queue_depth: per-queue pending requests count and age histogram (0-10ms, 10-100ms, 100ms).n- kernel_pressure_index (kpi): weighted sum of gpu occupancy, active kernels, enqueue latency, and memory stall rate. range 0,100.n- kv_warm_fraction: fraction of requests expected to hit prefix/kv cache (0-1).n- cost_signal: per-token cost estimate and priority cost budget remaining for the route/customer.n- error_rate: percent of responses that triggered fallback/retry in the last minute.nnlatency cohorts (recommended defaults)n1) interactive-50ms: requests with strict p50/p95 targets (e.g., ui autocompletion).n2) interactive-150ms: session chat turns that can tolerate modest tail but expect snappy median.n3) elastic-400ms: longer generations where batching accelerates cost efficiency.n4) background-batch-1s: large offline or low-priority requests eligible for queueing and high batching.nncohort assignment rulesn1. assign cohort at ingress based on route metadata and model profile (explicit route overrides default).n2. if request includes max_latency_ms or max_tokens, map to cohort using the mapping table in appendix a.n3. dynamic reclassification: on warmstart/kvcache-warmup events, mark requests as warming-elastic for up to 2s to bias toward nodes with warm cache.nnscheduler harmonization contract (short)n- purpose: give a deterministic algorithm for turning conciliated signals into actions across the admission-controller, slot allocator, and kernel dispatcher.n- input: steering signals cohort label route sla tier model-variant cost guidance.n- output: admission decision (accept/defer/redirect), slot allocation (slots, preemptible flag), kernel hints (preferred kernel id, quantization path), and fallback instruction (model-variant or queue route).nndecision precedence (ordered)n1. safety blocks (oom, watchdog) immediate reject/evict.n2. slo preservation for interactive cohorts when slo_gap 80, favor elastic/background cohorts for eviction or delayed admission.n4. cost_controls if cost budget is exhausted for a high-cost route, redirect to quantized variant or lower-fidelity model.n5. kv_warm_fraction optimization prefer nodes with warm fraction 0.7 for cohorts that benefit from cache otherwise allow warmup cohort routing.nnoperational playbook (incident / experiment flow)n1. detection: alert triggers if p95_interactive slo_target 1.2 for 3 minutes or kpi 85 for 2 minutes.n2. triage rapid checks (2 min):n - check slo_gap, kpi, queue_depth, kv_warm_fraction across affected nodes.n - identify cohort skew (which cohorts show disproportionate latency).n3. rapid mitigation (515 min):n - if kpi high and elastic/background load is 40 of active kernels, temporarily drain new batch routes and redirect to spare pool.n - if kv_warm_fraction low and interactive cohorts are affected, enable warm-prefetch for interactive routes and nominate warm nodes using routing tag warm-preferredtrue.n - apply emergency hedging for interactive cohorts: spawn second probe request on separate slot and cancel slower completion.n4. follow-up (post-mitigation):n - run microbenchmark traffic shaped to reproduce cohort mix that triggered incident (see benchmarking protocol section).n - capture full traces for 30 minutes and export to profiling lab.nnbenchmarking protocol (cohort-aware replay)n- purpose: validate scheduler decisions under realistic mixed cohorts.n- core steps:n 1. build a traffic shape with 3 lanes: interactive-50ms (40 qps), interactive-150ms (30 qps), elastic-400ms (30 qps).n 2. run three scenarios: baseline (no harmonization), harmonization-lite (conciliation but no preemptive evict), harmonization-full (all rules enabled).n 3. measure: p50/p95/p99 per cohort, mean tokens/sec, kernel context-switches, kpi, kv hit delta, cost_per_1k_tokens.n 4. acceptance criteria: interactive-50ms p95 improvement 20 vs baseline and overall cost increase 10ms)n- kpi_preempt_threshold: 80n- warm_preferred_fraction_threshold: 0.7n- cost_redirect_threshold_usd_per_1k: 2.50nnexample yaml snippet (route-level override)n- route: /api/chat/fastn cohort: interactive-50msn reserve_slots: 0.25n max_batch_size: 8n fallback_variant: model-lite-quantized-v2nnrunbook excerpt: latency spike play actions (cheat sheet)n1. acknowledge alert and post on runtime-incidents.n2. run runtime-cli get-signals --nodes affected and snapshot kpi/queue/kv.n3. if kpi 85: scale out spare-pool by 10 and enable batch-drain on background pools.n4. if interactive p95 target1.2 and kv_warm_fraction 5, sudden kv_warm_fraction drop 0.2 in 5m.nnownership and contactsn- runtime scheduler owner: marcus lee (pager: eng-runtime-scheduler)n- kernel infra owner: elena garcía (pager: eng-kernel)n- profiling benchmarks: jordan kim (profiling@redwood.ai)nnappendix a cohort mapping guidelinesn- max_latency_ms interactive-50msn- 50 interactive-150msn- 200 elastic-400msn- max_latency_ms 600 or large token budgets - background-batch-1snnappendix b experiment checklist for safe rolloutn1. feature-flagged rollout (10 traffic) for 48h with continuous monitoring.n2. canary cluster with identical hw profile and kv warm snapshot.n3. compare p99 and error delta vs baseline gate at 2 p99 regression or 0.5 error rate increase.nnchange logn- 2025-09-14: benchmark suite described above prior to rollout., doc_id: dsid_250314cab0d44d29afdab1ad8d257312, source_type: confluence, title: runtime sandboxing experiment lab manual, content: overviewnnthis manual describes the lab-grade sandboxing environment used by the runtime team to run invasive performance experiments, kernel-scheduler patches, and mixed-workload benchmarks without risking production stability. it documents the sandbox architecture, isolation model, step-by-step experiment runbook, profiling and telemetry requirements, benchmark invocation patterns, known issues encountered during experiments, and incident runbooks specific to lab activities.nngoalsnn- create a reproducible, auditable environment for risky runtime changes.n- ensure experiments are isolated from production control planes and do not leak telemetry or credentials.n- provide a standard profiling and benchmarking workflow so results are comparable across runs.n- capture failure modes and required mitigation steps.nnaudiencenn- runtime engineers doing kernel and scheduler work.n- performance engineers running comparative benchmarks.n- sres supporting lab infrastructure.nnhigh-level sandbox architecturenncomponentsnn- lab-gateway: lightweight ingress that routes experiment traffic and enforces quotas.n- kernel-orchestrator: service that deploys custom kernel/kernelspecs into lab nodes.n- sandbox-runner: per-node agent that configures cgroups, mig partitions and gpu modes, and applies kernel module overrides.n- kvcache-sim: a synthetic kv cache used to emulate prefix / session caching behavior.n- telemetry-proxy: collects and stamps telemetry for lab runs, marks data with lab_run_id, and writes to the lab telemetry bucket.nnisolation modelnn- network: lab runs live in the lab vpc (vpc-lab-1). no cross-vpc peering with prod. all egress is via nat-lab with explicit allow lists.n- compute: nodes are labeled lab:true and exist in a separate autoscaling group. node os images include the debug kernel and a signed kernel module whitelist.n- gpu: two isolation modes supported: nvidia mps per-experiment (for multi-process concurrency experiments) and mig partitions (for perf isolation). sandbox-runner toggles these per experiment.n- storage and secrets: lab runs use ephemeral pvcs. secrets are provided by the lab kms with a short ttl and are not replicated to production kms.nnkernel-scheduling considerations for lab experimentsnn- scheduler variants: the lab supports several scheduler builds under kernel-orchestrator: baseline, preemptive-slice, adaptive-slice, and priority-decoupled. each build is tagged and has a known compatibility matrix for driver and cuda versions.n- mapping priorities to runtime classes: use the experiment configuration to map redwood priority classes to kernel priorities. for example: interactive - sched_rr with 10ms quantum batch - sched_deadline with ed50ms/1s.n- fairness accounting: when testing cooperative preemption, enable kernel credit accounting (lab flag: enable_credit_accountingtrue) to observe queue-smear effects.nnexperiment environment provisioningnn1) request sandbox allocationnn- open rfc in the experiments tracker with: title, hypothesis, required node types, gpu mode, expected run time, and roll-back criteria. example: rfc: preemptive-slice latency reduction vs baseline.n- on approval, run the allocation script: ./scripts/request-lab --project runtime --nodes 4 --gputype a100 --duration 8h --labels preemptive-testnn2) provisioning checklist (automated but must be validated)nn- confirm nodes in asg have label lab:true.n- confirm kernel-orchestrator has deployed the requested kernel tag.n- verify sandbox-runner applied requested gpu mode: kubectl get nodes -l doc_id: dsid_19c7edeabbf44c80b8bd678da041c64d, source_type: confluence, title: request classification and observability contracts for runtime routing, content: summarynnthis page defines the request classification model and the corresponding observability contract used across the serving runtime. the goal is to produce deterministic routing decisions, consistent slo mapping, and standardized telemetry that enables rapid triage and automated policy enforcement (e.g., cost-aware routing, fallback decisions, and quality guards). this is an engineering-facing spec intended for runtime, router, and telemetry consumers.nnscopenn- applies to all inbound inference requests processed by redwood public and dedicated runtimes.n- covers: request tagging, workload classes, priority heuristics, routing attributes, required telemetry fields, and common debugging workflows.n- excludes: iam/auth schemes, billing pipeline (except for reference label mapping), and model content inspection for privacy.nnwhy this mattersnninconsistent request semantics produce noisy slo attribution, incorrect capacity decisions, and inaccurate cost signals. aligning on a single classification scheme reduces variance in routing outcomes and enables reusable dashboards, alert rules, and automated remediation.nndefinitionsnn1) workload class: a short label describing the expected performance and quality envelope for the request. examples: realtime, interactive, batch, embedding-internal, low_priority_scrape.n2) priority: discrete integer (0..9) used by schedulers to shape kernel allocation and preemption policies. 0 is highest priority (system-critical).n3) route intent: high-level objective for the request (e.g., low_latency, low_cost, high_quality).n4) fingerprint: stable hash of request properties used to group similar requests across telemetry and cache keying.nncontract: required request attributesnnevery request that enters a runtime path must include at minimum the following envelope attributes. if missing, the router will fill with conservative defaults and emit a visibility warning (see debugging section).nn- request_id: uuid v4n- client_id: team or org identifiern- model: model name or alias (string)n- model_version: semver-like or sha tagn- workload_class: one of (realtime, interactive, batch, embedding, maintenance)n- priority: integer 0..9n- route_intent: one of (low_latency, low_cost, high_quality, degrade_gracefully)n- sequence_hint: expected token count (optional but recommended for long-form workloads)n- fingerprint: hex encoded sha1 of canonicalized attributes (see fingerprinting rules)n- provenance: origin (api, console, sdk, internal)n- ttl_ms: optional time-to-live for queued worknnfingerprinting rules (stable, language-agnostic)nn1) canonicalization order: client_id, model, model_version, workload_class, route_intent, sequence_hint (empty values omitted).n2) normalization: lowercase strings, trim whitespace, replace multiple spaces with single space.n3) hashing: sha1(canonical_string) and hex-encode.n4) example canonical string: acme:bert:2026-01-02:interactive:low_latency:512 - fingerprint: e6f3...nnworkload class semantics and slo mappingnn- realtime: target p95 latency compatible model variants)n3) cost policy (if route_intent low_cost)n4) capacity availability fallback (regional/variant fallthrough)n5) canary/rollout overrides (if in canary window and route matches)nntelemetry contract (required fields for ingestion)nntelemetry must be emitted at three points: router-in (accept), runtime-start, runtime-complete. each emission is a json line with the following flat keys. all keys are strings unless noted. timestamp fields are iso8601 utc.nnrequired fields (all events):n- ts_iso: timestampn- event_type: router-in runtime-start runtime-completen- request_idn- fingerprintn- client_idn- modeln- model_versionn- workload_classn- priority (stringified int)n- route_intentn- selected_variant (the variant/kind chosen or none)n- regionn- node_id (when available)n- seq_len_hint (if present)nnadditional fields (runtime-complete):n- latency_ms (integer)n- tokens_out (integer)n- tokens_in (integer)n- error_code (empty if success)n- preempted (truefalse)n- cost_estimate_usd (string)nnexample telemetry lines:nnrouter-in:nn ts_iso: 2026-02-12t20:34:12.123z,n event_type: router-in,n request_id: 4a1f...,n fingerprint: e6f3...,n client_id: acme,n model: gpt-redwood-3b,n model_version: v2026-02-01,n workload_class: interactive,n request_id: 4a1f...,n fingerprint: e6f3...,n latency_ms: 378,n tokens_out: 120,n tokens_in: 24,n error_code: ,n preempted: false,n cost_estimate_usd: 0.0032nnnderived metrics and dashboards (minimum set)nn- p50/p95/p99 latency per workload_class x model_variantn- success_rate (1 - error_rate) per priority bucketn- preemption_rate per client_id and workload_classn- cost_per_1k_tokens by model_variant and regionn- queue_depth and wait_time distributions for batch queuesnnalerting guidelinesnn- latency slo breach: if p95(realtime) 120ms for 10m with volume 10 req/s - p1 page and trigger fallback routing to low-latency variants.n- unexpected preemption spike: preemption_rate increase by 5x relative to 1h baseline - p2 investigate kernel fairness and priority inversion.n- fingerprint drift: sudden 40 increase in unique fingerprints for a client in 30m - p2 check client sdk changes or bot traffic.nndebugging checklist (fast path)nn1) confirm router-in event exists for title: runtime-qualification-circuit-and-chaos-lab-manual-2026, content: runtime qualification circuit and chaos lab manualnnpurposenthis document defines the standard experimental qualification circuit we use to validate changes to the serving runtime surface (kernel patches, scheduler policy changes, fallback routing, kv cache logic, and runtime config knobs). it pairs structured benchmarks with deterministic and stochastic chaos experiments and provides a single, reproducible gating checklist for releases.nnscopen- applies to any code or config change that affects: kernel selection/execution, request scheduling/admission, kv cache behaviour, batching/packing logic, or telemetry/trace collection paths.n- includes both pre-merge ci sanity tests and staged canary/qualification runs in the chaos lab.nnoutcome and acceptance criteria (high level)n- no p0 regressions in production slos during the canary window: 99th percentile tail latency pre-change baseline 15 and p75 baseline 8.n- resource efficiency: per-token gpu micros (measured by kernel-time-trace) must not exceed baseline by more than 12 for default load shapes unless feature flagged (requires business signoff).n- quality / fidelity: when applicable, outputs must pass the regression prompt set acceptance suite with zero critical regressions.n- observability contract: all new signals introduced by the change must be emitted and documented before rollout.nnqualification circuit: phases and expected artifactsn1) local dev and unit-level profilingn - fast path: run microbenchmarks from the repo /bench/local and the kernel unit harness. capture single-gpu kernel latencies and memory footprints.n - artifacts: kernel latency csv, memory allocation timeline, and a short explanatory note.nn2) ci integration smoke and deterministic benchmarkn - ci runs the integration harness that replays a fixed request corpus (low-entropy synthetic replayed production traces) across the runtime in a containerized fixture.n - pass/fail gates: no increased assertion failures, no trace reordering, and a per-test latency regression threshold.nn3) chaos-lab qualification (isolated cluster)n - target: a dedicated qualification cluster (tag: chaos-qualifier) sized to match the smallest production cluster.n - runbook steps (numbered):n 1. deploy change to 5 of nodes behind a controlled load generator.n 2. run the benchmark harness (see benchmarks below) under three traffic shapes: steady, burst, and mixed latency-sensitive.n 3. inject deterministic kernel perturbations: add a synthetic 1050ms delay in the slowest attention kernel and verify scheduler hedging/timeout behaviour.n 4. run stochastic chaos phases: network partitions (0.52s jitter), nvme fault injection (simulated stalls), and transient gpu throttling simulation.n 5. monitor telemetry dashboard (latency, error-rate, kernel-queue-depth, gpu-utilization) and the qualification acceptance checklist.n - artifacts: full benchmark results, crash dumps, kernel traces, and an incident-style summary for any anomaly.nn4) canary rollback validation (production-but-controlled)n - canary window: 2472 hours depending on change size and risk profile.n - traffic steering: start with 1 of traffic, progress to 10 only if all slos and checks pass at each step.n - rollforward rules: automatic at each step if: (a) no p0 signals for 2h, (b) error-rate delta 3x baseline for 15 minutes, p99 latency baseline 50 for 10 minutes, or any kernel watchdog crash.nnbenchmarks and test corpus (what to run)n- baseline corpora:n - small-chat: median length 60 tokens, mostly streaming, latency-sensitive.n - long-completion: median length 1,200 tokens, throughput focused.n - multi-turn-chat: mixes prefix cache reuse patterns to exercise kv cache.n- for each corpus run: record per-token kernel time, scheduler queue metrics, gpu occupancy, and memory high-water marks.n- statistical reporting: p50/p75/p95/p99/p999 for latency mean and 95 ci for per-token kernel micros.nnprofiles and telemetry requiredn- mandatory telemetry emitted during qualification run:n - kernel.exec_time_ms (per-kernel tag), kernel.exec_count, kernel.queue_depthn - request.latency_ms (per-stage: queue, kernel, postprocess), request.path (route tag), request.trace_idn - gpu.utilization_pct, gpu.memory_used_mb, gpu.temp_celsiusn - kvcache.hit_ratio_prefix, kvcache.hot_evictions, kvcache.repopulation_latency_msn- tagging: all metrics for a qualification run must include qualifier_id and experiment_label.nnobservability dashboardsn- create a temporary dashboard for each qualification run that includes:n - time-series for p99 tail latency, request error-rate, kernel queue depth heatmap, and gpu memory pressure.n - a waterfall view (textual) of the top 5 slow requests with kernel traces attached.n- logging: increase kernel-level debug logging only for the qualification run (env var rk_qual_debugtrue) and ensure logs are retained for 14 days in the qualification workspace.nnexperiment catalogue (example matrix)n- the following table (described) maps experiment types to goals and pass criteria:n - kernel-change goal: ensure no kernel-time regressions pass: p99 per-kernel exec_time 10 without 5 memory overheadn - tracing-addition goal: increase observability pass: all traces sampled and attached to traces in the dashboard with /n- observability signals updated and dashboards createdn- regression prompt-set run: human-reviewed failures triagedn- rollback playbook validated in stagingn- security review (if change touches data plane or auth paths)nnoperational notes and common pitfallsn- memory fragmentation: small kernel-side allocator changes can change high-water marks without changing average usage always inspect allocator heatmaps.n- nvme stalls: some lab simulations surface stalls only at longer run durations include at least one 6-hour endurance run for storage-dependent changes.n- telemetry overhead: adding fine-grained per-kernel counters can increase cpu load qualify sampling rate before enabling in canary.nnappendix: example cli snippets and reproducibility tipsn- launch local qualifying harness (docker):n - docker run --rm -e rk_qual_debug1 -v (pwd)/bench:/bench redwood/runtime-qualifier:latest /bench/run --corpus small-chat --out /tmp/qual.csvn- quick telemetry export (prometheus query example):n - prometheus_query histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucketqualifier_idq-202602155m)) by (le))n- replaying production slice to replica cluster:n 1. generate curated trace: tools/trace_slice --start2026-02-01t00:00z --duration1h --patternmixed /tmp/slice.avron 2. replay: bench/replay --targetchaos-qualifier admission controllers. it consolidates requirements from runtime architecture, kernel scheduling, profiling, benchmarking, and release runbooks into a single actionable checklist for engineers and release managers.nnpurpose and audiencenn- purpose: ensure safe, measurable, and auditable runtime experiments with clear release gates and rollback criteria.n- audience: runtime engineers, sres, release managers, experiment owners, and applied ml engineers validating model-serving changes.nnscopennapplies to any change that touches the serving runtime execution path including but not limited to:n1) new or updated kernel implementations or kernel hints.n2) scheduler policy changes (priority, preemption, admission).n3) prefetch/kv cache algorithm changes or cache layout.n4) quantization profile rollouts and mixed-fidelity execution.n5) changes to batching logic and slotting/credit accounting.nnkey concepts and decision modelnn- risk tiering: every experiment must be classified into low / medium / high risk. classification factors: blast radius (cross-tenant potential), slo sensitivity, frequency of affect, and revert complexity.n- canonical metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, errors per 1000 requests, kernel-failure-rate, token-cost (per-1000 tokens), tail-kernel-duration, queue-depth distribution, successful-prefetch-rate, and fidelity-regression-score (from eval harness).n- checklistnn1) proposal and classification (owner creates an experiment rfc with: description, affected services, implementation plan, risk tier, feature flag path, and target metrics).nn2) automated prechecks (ci):n - linting and static safety checks on kernel code.n - unit tests and deterministic scheduler simulation pass.n - performance microbench: baseline vs candidate on representative model snapshot (script provided below).nn3) offline evaluation:n - run the candidate through the benchmarking harness with the same request surface as prod for 1m synthetic tokens or 24h of replay, whichever is earlier.n - record per-token cost and throughput delta.n - run the fidelity suite (prompt set) and capture quality signals: f1, bleu (if applicable), and our fidelity-regression-score.nn4) canary plan:n - canary size: start at 0.5 traffic for high risk, 1 for medium, 5 for low.n - canary duration: minimum 4 hours and until at least 10k live tokens have been served.n - observability hooks: enable detailed tracing (kernel spans), increase sampling of tail traces to 100 for canary cohort.nn5) gate evaluation:n - pass conditions (all must hold):n a) latency: p95 no worse than 10 relative to baseline and p99 no worse than 15 (configurable by risk tier).n b) errors: error-rate increase 25 or p95 40 for high risk experiments.n b) error-rate increase 0.2 errors/1k.n c) any kernel panic/watchdog node hang.n d) model-quality regressions above threshold defined in the rfc.nn6) staged rollout and primary release:n - ramp schedule: exponential ramp doubling every 612 hours with metric-level check at each step.n - final gate: full cluster performance benchmark on a representative mixed-workload shadow for 6 hours with no critical threshold breaches.nnrollback and incident interactionnn- if a fail condition is observed, the oncall or experiment owner must:n 1) flip the feature flag to revert candidate.n 2) notify sre and runtime owners in runtime-incidents with a short post including metrics and trace links.n 3) open a postmortem stub (template below) within 24 hours.nn- for partial degradations (e.g., localized node issues), consider throttling the rollout, isolating faulty topology (node affinity), and running targeted kernel telemetry collection rather than full rollback.nntelemetry and required signalsnnminimum dsid_2a79112d6e7f4ee797aa34f43d6635d2, source_type: confluence, title: slot reservation protocol and deferred warmstart manual, content: overviewnnthis manual documents the slot reservation protocol used by the redwood serving runtime and the deferred warmstart mechanism that reduces first-token latency for interactive requests without excessive pre-warm cost. it is written for oncall engineers, scheduler and worker owners, and product owners who need an operational contract for admission and warmstart behavior.nngoalsn- reduce tail latency for interactive routes by pre-reserving execution slots for requests judged latency-sensitive.n- limit wasted gpu cycles by deferring full warmstart work until a reservation is confirmed and a short pre-execution checkpoint is reached.n- provide clear admission semantics, deadlines, and observable signals for sre runbooks and automation.n- define safe fallback behavior so requests are served cold if warmstart is unavailable, with telemetry to measure impact.nnkey termsn- slot: a single execution unit on a worker that can be bound to one inference request at a time.n- reservation: a soft hold on a slot that can be confirmed, released, preempted, or expired.n- warmstart: preparing kv prefix state and kernel activation so generation can start with reduced latency.n- deferred warmstart or dws: the practice of delaying full warmstart actions until after reservation confirmation and a final readiness checkpoint.nnhigh-level flown1) frontend classifies incoming request into a tier such as interactive, best-effort, or batch.n2) for interactive requests, the frontend asks the admission component to reserve a slot using the srp api. the request includes an affinity fingerprint, sequence length hint, and kernel hints.n3) admission forwards a reserve request to the scheduler with a short deadline the scheduler attempts tentative reservation on candidate workers.n4) workers reply confirmed if they can honor the reservation within the deadline. on confirmation, admission returns a reservation acknowledgement to the frontend.n5) after confirmation, admission starts dws: it sends a compact kv hint and kernel activation request to the assigned worker. dws has a configurable soft time budget.n6) if dws completes before its budget, the frontend sends the request payload to the warmed slot. if dws aborts or times out, the payload is sent to the worker for cold execution and fidelity is recorded.nnreservation states and transitionsn- pending becomes confirmed when the worker accepts.n- pending becomes expired if the deadline is missed.n- confirmed may become released after use or be preempted by higher priority work.nnadmission api summarynthe reserve call carries the following fields in plain text: affinity fingerprint (tenant, model, route), sequence length hint, a deadline in milliseconds, a priority level, and a set of kernel hints. the response includes a status token that indicates confirmed, queued, or expired plus an optional slot identifier and eta.nndeferred warmstart semanticsn- dws is executed only after reservation confirmation and when affinity trust conditions are met. the default trust threshold is one previous affinity hit but is configurable per-customer.n- dws has three logical phases: compact kv hint injection, kernel activation, and a final readiness checkpoint.n- the default dws budget is 30 milliseconds. if the worker cannot finish within the budget the system aborts dws and falls back to cold execution. abort events are recorded.nnrecommended configuration defaultsn- reservation.deadline_ms 15n- warmstart.time_budget_ms 30n- affinity.trust_threshold 1n- preempt.policy preempt-by-priorityn- reservation.max_pending_per_node 64nnoperational runbook: common failure modesn- symptom: elevated dws abort raten 1. inspect metrics: reservation latency percentiles and worker kv prepare latency percentiles.n 2. if admission latency exceeds reservation deadline, investigate control plane saturation and network latency.n 3. if worker kv prepare latency is high, check gpu utilization, kernel unload events, and memory pressure.n 4. short-term mitigation: increase warmstart.time_budget_ms to a conservative value such as 60 milliseconds for affected pools.nn- symptom: confirmations frequently expire for interactive trafficn 1. examine scheduler pending counts per node and the scheduler queue length.n 2. if pending counts approach the per-node maximum, scale worker pools or reduce the per-node pending limit.n 3. review preemption logs if frequent, tune preemption policy or raise priority for critical routes.nn- symptom: preemption causes missing warmstarts and slo missesn 1. correlate request trace ids with scheduler event logs for the preceding window.n 2. if preemptions align with traffic bursts, enable a short holdback window so confirmed slots complete first-token generation before preemption.nntelemetry, metrics and alerts (minimum set)n- counters and histograms to export:n - admission_reservation_attempts_totaln - admission_reservation_confirm_raten - admission_reservation_latency_ms p50 p95 p99n - worker_warmstart_success_raten - worker_kv_prepare_latency_ms p95n - runtime_first_token_latency_ms p95 tagged by fidelity warmstart or coldstartn- recommended alerts:n - reservation_failure_rate exceeds 3 percent over 5 minutes - p1 paging for runtime oncalln - dws_abort_rate exceeds 1 percent over 10 minutes while cost exceeds budget - p2 investigate kernel churn and memory pressurennquality versus cost considerationsn- aggressive warmstarting yields the lowest latency but increases gpu active time and memory pressure. use the affinity trust threshold and per-customer warmstart budgets to constrain warmstarts for cost-sensitive tenants.n- for low-priority traffic, prefer lazy strategies with background prefetchers rather than immediate dws.nnsafety and fallback patternsn- if a worker fails during dws, scheduler marks pending reservations as expired and attempts reseating to an alternate worker under a secondary deadline, default 25 milliseconds.n- for customers requiring strict confidentiality, dws is opt-in and warmth requires explicit permission to prefetch cached prefixes.nnrollout checklistn1. add feature flags: admission.srp.enabled and worker.dws.enabled, defaulting to disabled.n2. canary the reservation api in a single region and enable dws for internal test routes only. monitor confirmation rates and first-token latency.n3. run synthetic traffic with mixed affinity distribution to validate worker kv prepare latency at target load.n4. increment traffic exposure and enable preemption holdback.n5. at intermediate exposure, enable for a small set of low-revenue tenants while collecting cost telemetry.n6. proceed to full rollout after 72 hours stable operation at each stage and absence of sustained alerts.nnownership and contactsn- primary owner: serving-runtime scheduler team, runtime-scheduler-oncall channel.n- secondary owner: serving-runtime worker team, runtime-worker-oncall channel.n- product contact for sla decisions: priya shah.nntroubleshooting commands and examplesn- tail reservation traces for a node in the last 15 minutes: redwoodctl reservations tail with node filter and status filter.n- inspect recent worker kernel and warmstart logs using remote access and the worker inspect tool to show warmstart history.nnengineering test guidancen- unit tests should mock reserve responses for confirmed and expired states and assert admission behavior on timeouts.n- integration tests should replay production fingerprints for at least five minutes and require warmstart success rate above 90 percent for interactive tier under nominal load.n- load tests should use the benchmark harness with affinity skew to verify per-node pending limits and reservation saturation behavior.nnsecurity considerationsn- kv hints must never contain plaintext customer pii admission scrubs hints and rejects any payload that exceeds configured size limits.n- reserve api requires internal mutual tls and scoped tokens with reserve write permission.nnappendix: simplified worker-side behavior pseudocode described in prosen- on tentative reserve, the worker marks a slot tentative and evaluates whether it can confirm the reservation within the configured deadline. if it can, it confirms otherwise it queues or expires the tentative reservation.n- on dws start, the worker checks for memory pressure and may abort early. if resources permit, it prepares kv using hints and activates kernels from idle state. the worker records prepare latency metrics and responds ready or abort.nnexample configuration snippet preempt.policy: preempt-by-priorityn- preempt.holdback_ms: 10nnrelated referencesn- runtime rejection and backpressure sla in the eng-sre space.n- coldstart warmup strategies in the eng-serving-runtime runbooks.nnrevision historyn- 2026-02-15: draft created by asha ramanathann- 2026-02-20: incorporated reviewer feedback on preemption behaviorn- 2026-03-01: published with rollout checklist and alert guidancen, doc_id: dsid_71b6f70a93174517929649d72ba1354f, source_type: confluence, title: fallback synthesis and sla preservation handbook, content: summary:nthis handbook consolidates guidance for synthesizing graceful fallbacks across the serving runtime while preserving customer slas. it covers the decision graph, kernel scheduling considerations, a profiling/playbook for investigating performance regressions that lead to fallbacks, an operational benchmarking protocol to validate fallback behavior, and concrete runbook steps for mitigation and postmortem.nnpurpose and scope:n- purpose: reduce customer-visible sla breaches by providing a repeatable playbook for when fallbacks, degradations, or variant swaps are triggered by runtime anomalies.n- scope: applies to all hosted and dedicated executions managed by the serving runtime (production fleets, canaries, and pre-production mirrors). excludes private on-prem deployments where the customer owns local network/infra.nnintended audience:n- oncall sres and runtime engineersn- runtime product owners and release engineersn- observability/telemetry engineers and performance researchersnnkey concepts and definitions:n- fallback: any automated or manual change that routes a request to a different model variant, region, or degraded execution path intended to preserve latency or error slas.n- sla preservation target: primary slos we attempt to preserve are p99 latency and availability per-customer route.n- variant: model quantization/size/compiled-kernel variant that is functionally compatible.n- eviction vs fallback: eviction is a resource reclaim action on a worker fallback is a traffic-routing reaction at the decision layer.nnslo thresholds and mapping (operational values):n- availability slo: 99.9 over 30 days.n- latency slos: p50 1.5x configured slo for five consecutive 1-minute windows - candidate fallback.n - error rate (5xx) spike 3x baseline for 3 consecutive windows - immediate evaluation.n - gpu kernel queue depth 85 for sustained 30s - trigger conservative admission.nnfallback decision flow (high-level):n1) detect anomaly: telemetry alert fires (latency/error/queue depth).n2) correlate signals: match trace ids, kernel-level metrics (kernel latency, occupancy), and recent config changes.n3) classify cause: kernel regression, model artifact, traffic surge, network degradation, or hardware failure.n4) action selection: pick from the fallback catalog (model variant swap, route-level throttling, regional reroute, or degrade features).n5) apply fallback with canary: route 5 - fallback for 60s, observe p99 and error delta.n6) if successful: gradually ramp to 100 over 10 minutes.n7) if unsuccessful: rollback and escalate to incident channel.nndecision heuristics (rules of thumb):n- prefer model-variant fallback when kernel cpu/gpu stalls or kernel timeout errors are observed.n- prefer region-level reroute when network egress/ingress errors are correlated to region telemetry.n- avoid functional-degrading fallbacks (e.g., remove tool-calls) for routes marked high-fidelity unless explicitly approved by product.n- maintain conservative prefactors: use 1.5x2x thresholds for latency-based fallbacks to avoid oscillation.nnkernel scheduling considerations during fallback:n- preemptive eviction policy: mark fallback traffic as low-priority so kernels initiated by fallback traffic are subject to cooperative preemption.n- kernel selection: when falling back to a quantized variant, ensure the kernel mapper chooses the relaxed-precision kernels with the same attention sharding to minimize kv-cache incompatibilities.n- kv cache handling: ensure session affinity mapping is preserved if kv cache rehydration will introduce large cold-starts, prefer routing to a compatible variant that can share cache where possible.n- admission throttles: apply admission tokens per-gpu to prevent fallback traffic from thrashing host queues.nnprofiling playbook (quick triage):n1) capture trace: enable 100 sampling on impacted route for a 5-minute window using trace tag: fallback-triage-.n2) collect kernel-level histograms: per-kernel execution times, queueing durations, occupancy, and memory allocs for affected hosts.n3) run lightweight reproducer: using the operational workload replayer, mirror a 10s slice of production traffic into a sandbox with kernel debug flags enabled.n4) compare to baseline: use the last-successful-stable profile from the execution-profile-registry and compute delta percentiles.n5) hypothesis checklist: kernel regression, bad kernel rollout, model weight mismatch, gpu thermal/driver regress, or system-level overload.n6) apply mitigations: kernel rollback, model-variant swap, or admission controller limit.nncli examples and snippets:n- mark route for 5 fallback:n redwoodctl routes update --route-id r-abc123 --fallback-variant quant-8bit --canary-percent 5 --canary-duration 60snn- snapshot kernel histograms (host):n curl -ss jq .histograms /tmp/host-23-kernel.jsonnnbenchmark protocol for validating fallback behavior:n- objective: quantify the latency, error, and cost delta when switching to a fallback variant under representative load.n- setup: use the operational-workload-simulator against a mirror stack with the same model catalog and kernel builds.n- steps:n 1) baseline: run 10m at expected steady qps (s) and collect p50/p95/p99 and kernel histograms.n 2) induce fallback: apply target fallback configuration (variant/region/quantization).n 3) ramp workload: run a 30m scenario with 2x momentary spikes to simulate burst behavior.n 4) measure: p50/p95/p99, error budget consumption, per-token gpu time, and per-request memory allocations.n 5) pass criteria: p99 follow ramp plan.n6) if canary fails - rollback and execute isolation steps (drain hosts, cordon, and trigger host repair runbook).n7) open incident with priority p1 and assign owners: runtime-oncall, kernel-author, model-oncall.nnpost-incident checklist and postmortem triggers:n- trigger a postmortem if sla breach 1 hour or customer-impacting errors exceed 1,000 requests.n- include: timeline with kernel-level latency charts, decision rationale for fallback, and action items (e.g., kernel rollback automation).nnrelease notes and known issues matrix (short form):n- release 2026.01.12: introduced conservative fallback orchestrator. known: initial rollout underestimates kv cache rehydration cost for large sessions (mitigation: adaptive kernel selector flag).nnoperational runbook annex (troubleshooting cheatsheet):n- symptom: sudden p99 spike with no deploysn - check kernel histogram for long-tail spikesn - if kernel spikes present - try model-variant fallback to quant-8bitn - if queue depth high and no kernel spike - check admission throttles and increase preemption windownn- symptom: 5xx surge correlated to a recent kernel rolloutn - rollback kernel bundle on affected hostsn - apply route-level canary to fallback variantnnownership and escalation paths:n- runtime oncall: first responder for detection, canary application, and short-term mitigation.n- kernel team: authoritative owner for kernel rollbacks and performance fixes.n- model onboarding: owner for validating functional compatibility of fallback variants.nnreferences and related pages:n- execution-contracts-and-stable-fallbacks-2026 (execution contracts and compatibility matrix)n- dsid_7c221fabe85f41e4b97084b41cdc82ac, source_type: confluence, title: operator economics and fidelity gating manual, content: purposen-------nthis document codifies operator-facing economics and fidelity-gating controls used by the serving runtime. it explains the decision surface between cost, latency, and output fidelity and provides prescriptive operator procedures, telemetry checks, and safe rollback paths. intended audience: sres, runtime engineers, and platform owners.nnsummary and scopen-----------------n- scope: runtime-level controls (scheduler quotas, kernel selection hints, kv cache warmup, model variant fallback) and the observability/benchmark artifacts needed for safe gating.n- goal: keep production slas while minimizing incremental cost and preserving highest-possible fidelity for priority traffic.n- not covered: model training or offline eval pipelines (see /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals).nnkey concepts and definitionsn---------------------------n- fidelity band: discrete levels of model execution quality we expose to the runtime: high, balanced, economical. each band maps to kernel variants, quantization profile, kv cache eviction aggressiveness, and max sequence length.n- cost delta: estimated additional /token or /request when upgrading fidelity band.n- fidelity gate: a runtime policy (per-route or global) that controls which fidelity bands are eligible for a request.n- operator budget: a time-boxed cost allocation (e.g., additional 5000/week) used to permit temporary fidelity upgrades for experiments.nnarchitecture overview (operator view)n------------------------------------nthe runtime exposes a fidelity controller service that synthesizes signals and programs the scheduler/kernels and routing plane. high-level flow:n1) request classification: route-level tags customer tier dynamic qos (latency headroom, token budget).n2) fidelity scoring: small in-rack scorer computes a score (0..100) using historical latency, delta cost, and a lightweight quality estimate from the shadow-eval service.n3) gate decision: score mapped to fidelity band using configured thresholds.n4) program runtime: scheduler receives a per-request execution profile (kernel hints, max tokens, kvcache hint).n5) observability: fidelity decisions are annotated in traces and roll up to the fidelity controller dashboard.nnoperators should understand these contracts before changing thresholds or kernel hints.nnoperator configuration referencen-------------------------------nbelow are the canonical fields and recommended defaults stored in the runtime config service. change via the control-plane api (see cli examples).nntable: fidelity gating fields (canonical)n field description recommended default units owner balanced band 60 score runtime-scheduler n kv_warmup_ms recommended prefetch window to warm kv for high band 1200 ms kv-team n quant_profile quantization profile applied per band q8_0 (balanced), q4_0 (economical) string runtime-optimizer n max_sequence_override hard cap for economical band 512 tokens runtime-scheduler nncli and api examplesn--------------------nto view current gating dsid_2df2d68eefab45ddb30fe5766b5801c2, source_type: confluence, title: runtime fidelity surgeon manual, content: summaryn-------nthis manual describes the end-to-end process and operational discipline we use to change inference fidelity inside the runtime: any deliberate change that affects numeric precision, kernel selection, batching policy, kv-cache warmup, model variant selection, or routing heuristics that we expect to change latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. the document combines architecture rationale, kernel scheduling implications, profiling playbook steps, benchmarking commands, an acceptance gate checklist, and example release-note scaffolding.nnscopen-----n- applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments for production traffic.n- covers automated changes (autotune controller), manual operator interventions, and canary rollouts.n- excludes model training changes, prompt-level a/b experiments, and customer-visible prompt edits.nnwhen to perform fidelity surgeryn-----------------------------nperform a fidelity change only when one or more of the following are true: n1) measurable unit-cost savings (5 projected) with acceptable quality riskn2) latency slo headroom is low and a fidelity change is required to meet tail slosn3) a hardware constraint (gpu memory, thermal ceiling) necessitates an alternate execution pathn4) quality regressions are explicitly tolerated for degraded tiers (e.g., fallback fast path).nnbefore you start (preflight checklist)n------------------------------------n- ownership: confirm an owner from runtime-ops and an owner from applied-ml (names and pagerduty rotation).n- ticketing: create a ticket with hypothesis, target metric delta, and rollback conditions.n- canary targets: identify traffic cohorts and snapshot corresponding request surfaces.n- baseline captures: collect 1 hour of traces for the target cohort including kernel traces, kv-cache hit rates, per-token cost, and example outputs (min 100 sessions).n- evaluation prompts: select at least 200 prompt/test pairs from the eval harness tagged for quality regressions.nnarchitecture considerations that inform changesn----------------------------------------------n- kernel selection is orthogonal to model architecture the runtime maps model ops to kernel families at dispatch time. changes in kernel hints may increase occupancy and change preemption behavior.n- prefetch and kv-cache warmup interact with quantized execution: warmup patterns that assume fp16 cache layouts may be less effective for int8 kernels.n- priority-driven scheduler treats fidelity-change traffic as deferred candidate until canary passes this prevents accidental priority inversion.nnoperator runbook: step-by-stepn-----------------------------n1) prepare canary image/config: increment feature flag and attach a unique trace tag (fidelity-surgeon-).n2) dry-run locally: use the shadow harness to replay captured traces against the new kernel/code path with shadow traffic enabled (no live responses).n - command: n ./bin/shadow-replay --trace-filebaseline-traces.tar.gz --kernel-hintint8-micro --concurrency20 --outputshadow-report.jsonn3) run microbenchmarks on the intended hardware slice (3 runs):n - per-token latency (p50/p95/p99)n - kernel invocation time distribution (collect cuda/nvtx traces)n - memory high-water mark and fragmentation samplen4) canary rollout: begin with 0.5 traffic to a stable pool with increased logging and a non-blocking guard. monitor for 30 minutes.n5) expand canary: if health signals remain green, expand to 5 for 2 hours, then to 25 for 12 hours.n6) full rollout: gradually promote to 100 using the rollout matrix in the acceptance section.nnkey monitoring signals (must be green during canary)n---------------------------------------------------n- slos: request p99 latency relative delta projected threshold.n- kernel health: no new kernel ooms, kernel launch errors, or nvml thermal spikes.nnprofiling playbook excerptsn--------------------------n- sampling plan: stratified sampling across short/medium/long sequences, chat vs. single-call, and top-ten customer tenants.n- tools and commands:n - nvprof/nsight: capture gpu kernel timelines for the benchmark trial. example: n nsight-sys profile --outputnsys-report.nsys --tracecuda,nvtx occupancy at fixed sequence lengths.n- replay benchmarks: replay captured production traffic with preserved inter-arrival timing. this shows end-to-end behavior (queueing, batching).n- shadow a/b: run new path in shadow mode with sampling of produced outputs for offline quality scoring.n- cost simulation: feed kernel-level latencies into the cost model to project monthly delta.nnexample bench admission window for int8 kernels to avoid long head-of-line blocking with high-occupancy kernels. typical knob: runtime.scheduler.admission_ms (default 3ms) - 1.5ms for micro-kernel heavy workloads.n- priority decay: lower priority decay to bias warmup cohorts into prefetch success for cache-sensitive flows.n- cooperative preemption: enable for high-mix pools when deploying new kernels dsid_7482a5d40cfb45d88fec6bb81a37ef81, source_type: confluence, title: runtime experimentation blueprint and hypothesis protocol, content: overviewnnpurpose: this document defines a standardized, repeatable blueprint for formulating hypotheses, instrumenting experiments, and executing cross-layer runtime experiments that span runtime architecture, kernel scheduling, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suites, runbooks and release verification. it codifies guardrails for safety, data collection contracts, and an escalation path for regressions detected during experiments.nnaudience: runtime engineers, sres, performance researchers, release managers, and solutions engineers who run or consume inference experiments.nnscope and high-level principlesnn- keep experiments scoped to a single independent variable wherever possible (e.g., scheduler policy, kernel variant, kv warmup window).n- measure both application-visible metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token cost) and internal kernel signals (occupancy, kernel queue depth, preemption count, batch composition).n- use shadow channels and low-risk canaries for disruptive changes require automatic fallback for any change affecting p99 by 25 or cost by 15 in production-like traffic.n- maintain reproducibility: every experiment must have an id, input corpus, and synthetic traffic profile attached to the run artifact.nnroles and ownershipnn1. experiment owner (single point): responsible for hypothesis, orchestration, runbook, and final report. (typically the engineer proposing the change.)n2. observability owner: ensures traces, metrics and sampled traces are available and annotated with experiment_id.n3. sre reviewer: verifies safety windows, capacity headroom, and rollback plan for production canaries.n4. release manager: gates experiment-to-release handoff and signs off acceptance criteria.nnhypothesis lifecycle (protocol)nn1. formulate hypothesis: 12 sentence statement (e.g., switching kernel-variant x to f32-int8 delta path reduces p50 by 18 for short sequences without increasing p99 by 5.)n2. define primary/secondary metrics: primary p99 tail latency secondary token cost per million tokens, preemption rate, gpu stall time.n3. create experiment specification: include traffic corpus, seed rng, workload mix (inference/generation/chat/embedding), concurrency shape, and warmup steps. use the experiment template.n4. baseline capture: run at least three baseline runs across different cluster nodes (same family) and record statistical distribution.n5. run treatment: execute change with identical traffic collect same signals.n6. statistical test: use non-parametric comparison (e.g., mannwhitney u) for latency distributions and bootstrap confidence for cost metrics.n7. acceptance rules: pre-declared thresholds (see acceptance table). if a treatment fails, follow rollback runbook.nnexperiment handbook, content: summaryn-------nthis handbook describes the operational signal fabric and the cohorted scheduler approach used by redwoods serving runtime to map runtime observability signals to scheduler decisions, incident triage actions, profiling experiments, and benchmarking checks. it is written for runtime engineers, sres, and subsystem owners responsible for scheduler policies, telemetry alignment, and production rollouts.nngoalsn-----n- define a single signal taxonomy (the signal fabric) that is consumed by scheduling heuristics, alerting rules, and profiling experiments.n- describe how execution cohorts are derived, annotated, and persisted for deterministic investigations.n- provide concrete runbooks for common scheduler/resilience incidents and profiling experiments.n- give a rollout checklist for scheduler policy changes that minimizes regressions in latency, cost, and fidelity.nnscopen-----napplies to: all runtime scheduler components (priority governor, admission controller, kernel mapper), kernel plugins that expose telemetry hooks, and the profiling/benchmarking suites that validate scheduling changes. this document does not specify kernel implementation details it focuses on operational mapping between signals and scheduler behavior.nncore conceptsn-------------n1) signal fabric: canonical names, units, and retention for runtime signals consumed by scheduling logic. signals are emitted at three layers: request-surface (api/router), kernel-dispatch (runtime kernels), and infra (node/accelerator).n2) cohorts: deterministic classification of requests into buckets based on stable attributes (model_id, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket, client_tier, route_flags). cohorts allow targeted profiling and rollback.n3) decision bindings: declarative rules that map signal thresholds and cohort identities to scheduler actions (prioritize, throttle, preempt, fallback to variant).n4) fidelity guards: safety checks (quality/eval) attached to any scheduler action that can change model variant/quantization.nnsignal fabric (canonical table)n--------------------------------n signal name layer unit cardinality producer ttl use cases n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------n request.p90_latency_ms request-surface milliseconds per-route router 90d slo monitoring, alerts n kvcache.hit_rate kernel-dispatch fraction (0-1) shard kvcache 30d batching hints, warmup n kernel.queue_depth kernel-dispatch integer shard dispatcher 14d admission control, preempt decisions n node.gpu_util_pct infra percent node node_agent 60d capacity planning, admission n token.emission_rate_per_s request-surface tokens/s tenant runtime_router 30d billing/cost throttles n request.sequence_bucket request-surface enum (s/m/l/xl) per-request router 90d cohorting, kernel hints n kernel.latency_per_op_ms kernel-dispatch ms/op kernel kernel_profiler 90d kernel selection, canary gating nnnote: cardinality indicates the level at which the signal is indexed. keep high-cardinality signals off the hot path unless sampled.nncohort definition and lifecyclen-------------------------------n- cohort keys: model_id, model_variant_id, sequence_bucket, client_tier, route_tag.n- generation: router computes the cohort_key at request admission and attaches headers: x-runtime-cohort: modelv3.1varquant-8bitlenxltiergoldroutechat_inlinen- storage: cohort annotations are copied into trace/span baggage and a lightweight cohort index (redis-backed) max_preempt_per_node: 2, backoff_minutes: 5,n safety_check: fidelity_guard_alphannnn- predicates are evaluated by the decision engine at 10s cadence. keep predicates simple to avoid evaluation (short)n--------------------------------------------------n1) background fairness governor (default): throttle tenants consuming 75 of background credits in 5m window.n2) sequence-length capper: for cohorts with median_sequence_length xl and p99 queue_depth 100, cap to l variant.n3) opportunistic admission: if node.gpu_util_pct batch-aggregatorn- protocol: http/1.1 json body or internal grpc (preferred). required fields: request_id, customer_id, model_variant, priority, max_latency_ms, seq_hint (optional).n- expectations: batch-aggregator will acknowledge receipt within 5ms (p50) and either accept for batching or reject with backpressure with a human-readable reason.n- obligations: if the aggregator accepts, it must surface an accept_trace_id and the estimated enqueue_delay_ms. if rejecting, it must return retry_after_ms if applicable.nn2) batch-aggregator - kernel-executorn- protocol: internal grpc with a binary batch payload and per-request metadata.n- expectations: kernel-executor will either start execution within the configured scheduling window (default 8ms) or return a preemption token explaining why (e.g., memory pressure, higher-priority workload).n- obligations: executor must persistently record kernel_start and kernel_end timestamps for each batch and expose per-kernel memory_high_water_mark bytes.nnscheduling contract (kernel-level)nn- priority levels: system (highest), interactive (default), background (lowest).n- scheduling window: default 8ms for interactive traffic configurable per-deployment. kernels should honor the window and not block longer than window 2ms for integration steps.n- max tokens per scheduling slice: 2048 tokens per gpu slice for transformer-based models unless overridden by model_profile.n- fairness: no single customer may consume more than 30 of kernel credits on a shard unless explicitly reserved.n- preemption semantics: preemption returns preempted status with reason code and a deterministic backoff recommendation. preemption must be idempotent: re-submitting the same request_id within the recommended backoff window must be safe.nnshard isolation invariantsnn- lease model: shard-manager grants a lease token to the kernel-executor to operate a shard leases are renewed every 2s. loss of lease triggers a soft-eviction where the kernel drains active batches for up to 250ms before halting new accepts.n- memory isolation: each shard has a soft_limit and hard_limit (bytes). the soft_limit is 80 of hard_limit and triggers eviction/gc policies. hard_limit must never be exceeded kernel must fault instead of corrupting other shards.n- namespace separation: kv-cache-proxy provides tenant namespaces. cross-tenant cache affinity is prohibited unless explicitly whitelisted.nntelemetry and observability contractnnevery runtime binary must export the following metrics and trace annotations:nn- metrics (prometheus style):n - runtime.request.router.latency_ms.p50/p95/p99n - runtime.shard.lease_renewal_success_raten - runtime.kvcache.hit_ratio_last_5mn - runtime.scheduling.preemptions_totalreasonn- traces: annotate spans with request_id, accept_trace_id, kernel_start, kernel_end, kernel_slice_id, and preemption_reason.nnsuggested alerting thresholds (baseline)nn- alert a1 (request backlog): batch_aggregator.enqueue_depth 1000 for 2m - sev2.n- alert a2 (kernel memory pressure): kernel.mem_high_water_mark 90 of hard_limit - sev1.n- alert a3 (preemption spike): preemptions_total increases by 5x baseline in 5m - sev2.n- alert a4 (lease renewal failures): shard.lease_renewal_success_rate sev1.nnconfiguration catalog (example table)nn config_key purpose recommended_default notes n---------:---n scheduling.window_ms target kernel scheduling window 8 inputs so engineers can reason about per-request unit economics and make configuration decisions that respect latency slos.nnscopen- serving runtime cost components: gpu compute, memory, cpu-side assumptionsn1) costs are additive along a critical path, with caching and batching providing multiplicative reductions for token-level work.n2) latency slos are primary constraints cost optimizations must not increase p95 beyond target without explicit approval.n3) simulations should mirror production traffic mixes (session lengths, model variants, priority classes).nncore cost model (gpu_time(slice) gpu_cost_per_second)n- memorysharecost (allocated_memory_fraction gpu_hour_cost) amortized over active sessionsn- schedulingoverhead context-switch and preemption penalties (measured workaround: warm-fill by routing a small fraction of sessions to a prewarm pool.n- nonlinear quantization interactions: q4-q3 transitions can change kernel selection heuristics, causing unexpected kernel fallout. when evaluating quantization savings, run the simulator with kernel_hint_override to match the kernel mapper.n- edge-case: undersized slice_duration combined with high-priority churn contracts and tuning playbook, content: summary:nspecification and operational playbook for the runtime autotune framework: telemetry contracts, experiment design, safety controls, and oncall procedures for automated kernel and batching parameter tuning.nnbody:noverviewnnthis page documents the runtime autotune framework (raf): an orchestrated system that ingests workload telemetry, runs controlled optimization experiments, and produces validated parameter updates (kernel selection, batch sizing, concurrency caps, and quantization profiles) that can be rolled out to production runtime clusters. the goal of raf is to improve per-token cost and tail latency while preserving correctness and customer-visible slos.nngoals and non-goalsnn- goals:n - automate routine tuning for stable workloads to reduce manual effort and cost by 1030 over time.n - maintain or improve 95/99/99.9 latency slos never trade away slos for cost without an explicit human approval step.n - provide clear telemetry contracts so experiments are reproducible and auditable.n- non-goals:n - raf does not perform model-level parameter changes (weights) or retrain models.n - raf is not intended to replace incident response automated rollbacks exist for safety but oncall intervention is required for complex degradations.nnhigh-level architecturenn1) telemetry ingestion: continuous metrics stream and structured trace events are ingested into the raf experiment service.n2) workload profiler: synthesizes request distributions (sequence length, prompt prefix similarity, token-per-request distribution, function-calls frequency).n3) hypothesis generator: maps workload fingerprints to candidate tuning vectors (e.g., kernel a for short sequences, mixed-kernels for long tails).n4) controlled experiment runner: executes traffic-shaping a/b/canary experiments in isolated slices.n5) validator and safety checker: compares aggregated metrics against acceptance criteria and generates signed decisions.n6) rollout manager: applies changes according to rollout policy (canary - gradual - global) with automatic rollback triggers.nntelemetry contract (required fields)nnevery signal used by raf must implement the following contract. signals are exported as prometheus metrics or annotated traces with the following stable names and labels. table reflects canonical names used across customers and internal deployments.nn- metric namespace: redwood_runtime_autotune_ (prometheus)nn metric name type description required labels collection frequency notes n------------------------------------------------------------------------------n redwood_runtime_autotune_request_seq_length histogram request input token count distribution model, region, shard 1m buckets: 0-32,33-64,65-128,129-256,257-512,512 n redwood_runtime_autotune_latency_seconds summary end-to-end request latency (s) including network kernel exec model, region, shard, priority 10s quantiles: 0.5,0.95,0.99,0.999 n redwood_runtime_autotune_kernel_cpu_ms counter cumulative cpu ms used by kernel selection per request model, kernel_variant, shard 1m reset on process restart n redwood_runtime_autotune_kvcache_hit_ratio gauge kv-cache prefix hit ratio (0..1) model, shard 30s critical for batching decisions n redwood_runtime_autotune_error_counts counter categorized error counts (parse, model-mismatch, oom, timeout) model, error_type, region 10s must increment consistently nnoperational semantics for metricsnn- label cardinality: model and region are required additional labels (customer_id) may be included but cardinality must be capped using the cardinality policy (see related page).n- aggregation window: raf uses sliding windows with configurable length (default 5m for short experiments, up to 30m for conservative validation).n- fidelity: samplers must preserve rare-tail behaviour use stratified sampling when downsampling traces.nnhypothesis passes acceptance, expand to staged rollout: 1 - 5 - 20 with minimum dwell time of 10 minutes per stage.n3) each stage runs with an active control arm (unchanged parameters) and returns pre/post metrics.nnacceptance criteria (validator rules)nn- latency (tail) regression: 95th percentile tail must not increase by more than 5 relative to control.n- error budget: error_counts.total must not exceed control by more than 10 absolute or 2x relative (whichever is smaller).n- cost delta: expected per-token cost must improve or remain within -2 (no 2 cost increase allowed).n- resource safety: gpu memory usage must not exceed 90 of baseline.n- guard for degenerate behaviour: if kvcache_hit_ratio drops by 0.05 absolute in canary, abort.nnautomated rollback triggersnn- instant rollback on any of the following during a stage:n - 99.9 latency regressed 10 absolute.n - oom errors observed in 0.1 of canary requests.n - unhealthy node count increases by 1 per shard.nnexperiment telemetry retained for auditnn- every experiment stores: candidate vector, start/end timestamps, aggregated metrics for control and treatment windows (as json blobs), decision (approve/reject), operator (automated or user id), git sha for runtime binaries, and rollout graph.n- retention: 90 days hot, 2 years archived (compliance requirement).nnsafety and human-in-the-loop controlsnn- any candidate that touches quant_profile or kernel_variant requires an explicit human review for models with customers in restricted compliance tiers.n- tiered approvals:n - low risk: kernel parameter tuning that does not change quant_profile and passes canary - auto-approve.n - medium risk: changes that touch quant_profile but are only conservative adjustments - require 2 engineering reviewers.n - high risk: any change that reduces replication or changes memory layout - product and security review required.nnrunbook: how to launch a manual experimentnn1) create a new experiment record in raf ui or via incident if necessary.nntroubleshooting checklist (first 60 minutes)nn- if canary fails:n 1) check redwood_runtime_autotune_error_counts for error_typeoob/oom/timeout.n 2) inspect per-shard latency histograms to detect skew.n 3) compare kvcache_hit_ratio between control and treatment.n 4) if resource saturation is suspected, run ephemeral profiler (profctl snapshot --target shard-x) and capture gpu kernel traces.nn- if intermittent tail spikes only during peak traffic, abort staged rollout and reopen with a narrower sequence-length targeted candidate.nnoperational responsibilities and of document., doc_id: dsid_220be189b9c34ae986d518b3bf46bef4, source_type: confluence, title: economic fidelity controller and safeguards design manual, content: overviewnnthis document specifies the economic fidelity controller (efc): a runtime subsystem that dynamically balances model fidelity, latency, and per-token cost across hosted and dedicated deployments. the efc is a control plane component embedded in the serving stack that enforces cost and quality guardrails through real-time signals to the scheduler and kernel selection layer.nngoalsn- enforce organization-level cost targets (per-customer and aggregated) while preserving user-facing quality slos.n- provide a transparent, auditable policy surface for degradations and fidelity regressions.n- make runtime fidelity decisions reversible and safe: all changes must be observable, attributable, and subject to automatic rollback.n- integrate with existing runtime scheduler and kernel mapper without adding undue tail-latency risk.nnscope and non-goalsn- in-scope: model variant selection, dynamic quantization profiles, request routing to cheaper device pools, short-lived fidelity steps (e.g., sequence-length bucketing, kv cache hints), telemetry and alerting.n- out of scope: training-time quantization decisions, model architecture changes, long-term contractual pricing.nnhigh-level architecturenncomponents:n- runtime-efc (control loop service) computes per-cohort fidelity actions every 5s by default.n- scheduler-proxy receives efc actions and converts them to scheduler admission rules / kernel hints.n- kernel-guard lightweight in-node agent that applies kernel variant selection and enforces per-request fidelity caps.n- telemetry-bridge aggregates fidelity decisions, token/cost deltas, and model quality signals for dashboards and audits.nndata flows (textual diagram)n1) telemetry - runtime-efc: raw signals (per-route latency p50/p95/p99, per-token cost, embed/call counts, quality regressions from evals) flow to runtime-efc via the telemetry-bridge.n2) runtime-efc - scheduler-proxy: actionable policy (e.g., reduce high-cost customer cohort fidelity to f-2 for 60s route low-priority cohort to econ-gpu-pool).n3) scheduler-proxy - kernel-guard: concrete kernel variant and admission instructions.n4) kernel-guard - runtime (per request): tag request with fidelity metadata enforce runtime caps.nncontrol loop semanticsn- decision cadence: default 5s decision window with exponential backoff on oscillation.n- safety multiplier: every action carries a safety_multiplier (0.01.0) actions with multiplier 512).n- cohort-selector: matches requests to cohorts using route, customer_tier, token_budget, and tags.n- duration: ttl for the fidelity-step (e.g., 30s, 5m, 1h).n- escalation: if action persists escalation_window, efc escalates to an owner and can trigger rollback policies.nntelemetry and signalsnkey signals (ingested via telemetry-bridge):n- checksn- kv_cache_hit_rate and sequence_length_distributionn- kernel_switch_rate and kernel_error_raten- packing_efficiency and batch_size_distributionnnslos and thresholds (examples)n signal target warning critical owner n------------------------------------------n route_latency_p95 550ms 800ms runtime-sre n per_token_cost (30m window) 0.0012 0.0020 finance-eng n quality_score_regression delta experiment efc default.n- kernel hinting: fidelity_step maps to kernel tags (e.g., quant-int8, split-attn-low, kv-prefetch-disabled). kernel-guard translates tags into in-node flags.nnkernel selection pseudocode (simplified)n1) request arrives with cohort_idn2) kernel_tag kernel-guard.lookup(cohort_id) n3) selected_kernel kernel_catalog.best_match(kernel_tag, request.shape)n4) if
