controller scenario.n, doc_id: dsid_aca4da624f3e4c4a8432c797ee68d36e, source_type: confluence, title: async kvcache prefetch and adaptive kernel selection playbook, content: summarynthis playbook describes the design, operational controls, profiling guidance, benchmarking recipes, and incident runbooks for the asynchronous kv cache (kvcache) prefetcher and the adaptive kernel selection subsystem. the document explains how the prefetching pipeline integrates with the request classifier and kernel selector to reduce token-era latency for long-context and multi-shot workloads while preserving cost and fairness slos.nnwhy this existsn- root cause: tail latency often originates from sequential kv loads and conservative kernel choices for requests with uncommon sequence profiles.n- goal: reduce p95/p99 generation latency by prefetching kv segments and selecting kernels tuned to the observed request pattern without increasing average gpu occupancy or costs by more than 8.nnscopen- included: async prefetch coordinator, request classification heuristics, kernel selection policy, metrics and alert thresholds, profiling steps, benchmarking recipes, rollout and rollback steps.n- excluded: model architecture changes, quantization profiles (see quantization-profiles directory), network-level transport changes.nnhigh-level architecture (text diagram)n- ingress - request classifier - routing prefetch coordinator - kernel selector - gpu dispatcher - kvcache (per-shard) - runtime executorn- feedback loop: runtime telemetry - adaptive policy engine - prefetch kernel policy storenncomponents and responsibilitiesn1) request classifiern- tag requests at ingress with a sequence profile: typical length distribution, presence of tool/function calls, streaming flag, and priority class. uses lightweight sampling models (logistic model trained on historical traces).n- responsible for assigning a prefetch hint (none, soft-prefetch, eager-prefetch) and candidate kernel families (a/b) for the kernel selector.n2) prefetch coordinatorn- receives hints and maintains per-session prefetch state. issues non-blocking kv reads to co-locate likely kv pages before the request reaches the hot kernel path.n- uses backpressure-aware dispatch: prefetch requests are priority-0 and are throttled by an adaptive token bucket per-gpu to maintain tail slos.n3) kernel selectorn- maintains a policy table indexed by (model-variant, sequence-profile, priority). each entry contains candidate kernels with expected latency cost vectors.n- uses a bandit-style experiment framework for online exploration (epsilon-greedy by default) with decay windows tied to model version rollouts.n4) adaptive policy enginen- periodically (5m) retrains lightweight policies from telemetry. generates updated thresholds for prefetch aggressiveness and kernel switching.nnkey design tradeoffs and safeguardsn- safety first: kernel switches are allowed only if the candidate improves expected latency without exceeding a configured cost delta (default 8).n- backpressure integration: prefetch-level throttles yield immediately under gpu memory pressure or when per-gpu kernel saturation 85.n- gradual exploration window: exploration rate is capped to avoid noisy regressions in canaries.nnoperational metrics and dashboards (minimum required)n- prefetch hit rate (per model, per region): percent of requests where prefetched kv page satisfied first kv fetch.n- prefetch to primary fetch latency delta (ms).n- kernel selection distribution: percent usage of each kernel family by model-version.n- p50/p95/p99 generation latency (token complete) by kernel family and sequence-profile.n- gpu occupancy and queue length by kernel family.n- cost-per-token delta by kernel family.nnslo guardrails (observable thresholds)n- p95 generation latency: target 120ms, alert if 160ms sustained for 3m.n- prefetch hit rate: target 70 on long-context workloads, warning if 8 sustained 30m, page at 12.nnprofiling playbook (how to investigate quality/latency regressions)n1) initial triagen- verify if latency spike correlates with: recent kernel rollout, prefetch policy change, model-version rollout, or gpu pool capacity event.n- query traces: filter by request classifier tag and kernel family.n2) reproduce with developer sandboxn- use the sandbox driver with the same sequence-profile and batch shape. run microbenchmarks with and without prefetch: ./bench_driver --model vx --profile long-context --prefetch on/off --kernel a/b.n3) telemetry collectionn- capture a full trace set for 5 minutes: kernel dispatch times, kvcache miss/hit events, per-token latency, and gpu occupancy. use the runtime trace sampler: rt-sample --duration 300 --labels kvcache,prefetch,kernelselect.n4) root-cause patterns and fixesn- high kv miss low prefetch hit - increase conservative prefetch window and examine classifier false negative rate.n- kernel family p99 regressed - disable exploration flag for that family roll back canary.n- gpu memory pressure during prefetch - reduce per-gpu prefetch tokens or restrict eager-prefetch to dedicated pools.nnbenchmarking suite (recipes and canonical configs)n- objective: quantify cost/latency tradeoffs for prefetch aggressiveness and kernel families across representative profiles.n- canonical workload set: short-chat (avg len 30), long-instruction (avg len 512), multi-shot session (avg len 800 with kv locality).n- benchmark config table (text):n - test name: long-kv-prefetch-scann concurrency: 200n seq_profile: long-instructionn prefetch: eagern kernels: a-optimized, b-latencyn duration: 30mn - test name: mixed-plg-burstn concurrency: 500n seq_profile: mixedn prefetch: softn kernels: a-optimizedn duration: trace_id, timestamp, model_version, kernel_family, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, kvcache_event, cost_units.nnrelease and rollout plann1) local qa: unit tests microbench suite.n2) canary: enable soft-prefetch each stage the policy engine must show no adverse impact on slos for 30m before advancing.n4) automatic rollback triggers: sustained p95 regression 20 or prefetch hit rate drop 30 vs baseline for 15m.nnrunbook snippets (incident steps)n- symptom: sudden p99 spike for long-context modeln1) check recent policy changes: /ops/deploy-log or policy-store update id.n2) query prefetch hit rate and runtime-observation-enrichment-and-labeling-guidelines-2025, content: overview:nthis document defines the canonical approach for enriching runtime telemetry (traces, kernel events, request metadata) with contextual labels and cost tags so downstream consumers (alerting, billing, profiler, experiments) can reliably join signals. the goal is consistent, low-cost enrichment that enables accurate slo attribution, cost-per-inference accounting, and fidelity-aware debugging across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.nnwhy this matters:n- inconsistent labels are the single largest source of signal fragmentation when debugging tail latency and kernel regressions.n- cost and energy tags let product and finance teams reconcile per-route economics without pulling raw traces.n- enriched, compact traces speed triage for oncall by surfacing the minimum causal set of attributes needed to reproduce or route incidents.nnprinciples:n1) minimal, stable keyset: restrict primary labels to a small set that is unlikely to change (see label taxonomy).n2) schema-first: all labels follow the canonical key names and types in this doc any extension requires a review.n3) cost-aware sampling: enrich higher-value requests at a higher sampling rate inexpensive warmup traces sampled low.n4) privacy minimal pii: do not attach user pii or raw prompt text to traces. use hashes or prompt-ids where needed.n5) low-latency enrichment: enrichment must not add more than 1 ms on the request path in p95. use asynchronous enrichers for non-blocking attributes.nnlabel taxonomy (canonical keys):n- request.id: stable uuid for the user request (string)n- route.name: product route or api path (string)n- model.variant: model name and variant (e.g., gptx-16q8) (string)n- kernel.path: kernel family / variant invoked (string)n- hw.pool: accelerator pool identifier (e.g., a100-pool-3) (string)n- cost.token_estimate: integer estimated token count (stringified integer)n- fidelity.flag: one of full, approximate, degraded (string)n- kvcache.hit_ratio: float (0.0-1.0) represented as stringn- customer.tier: free standard enterprise (string)n- region: cloud region (string)n- trace.version: schema version (string)nnnote: store numeric values as strings for telemetry pluggability and to avoid downstream parsing discrepancies.nntable: retention and storage hints (recommended):n- traces.enriched.retention: 30d (for fully enriched traces used in oncall workflows)n- traces.minimal.retention: 7d (for minimal traces used only for perf sampling)n- aggregated.metrics.retention: 365dn- cold-storage.export: weekly snapshots to s3 for compliance (retention 2y)nnsampling policy (high-level):n1) baseline sampling: 0.5 of all requests capture minimal trace (spans request.id route.name).n2) enriched sampling tiers:n - high-value routes (customer.tierenterprise or routes flagged by product): 20 enriched.n - potential-regressions: traffic flagged by the anomaly-detector (see procedure) gets 100 enrichment for 1h.n - manual oncall escalations: toggle enrichtrue via /api/operator/enrich-toggle for the given route for immediate 15-minute capture.n3) dynamic cost weighting: if cost.token_estimate 10k, escalate enriched sampling by 5x for that request bucket.nnenrichment pipeline (component roles):n- request ingress (lightweight): attaches request.id, content: overview:nthis document defines a pragmatic mapping between runtime observability signals and the cost / slo consequences they imply. it consolidates ownership for each signal, provides concrete alert thresholds, investigative playbooks, and sample queries to accelerate incident triage and cost attribution. the goal is to make cost-impacting signals actionable for oncall, sres, runtime engineers, and product stakeholders without repetitive context-switching.nnwhy this exists:n- we observe recurring incidents where telemetry is present but responsibility and cost mapping are unclear.n- kernel-level events (slow kernels, preemption, fragmentation) generate telemetry that must be translated into cost signals (excess gpu-hours, increased tail-latency retries, failed inference units).n- this doc standardizes naming, ownership, and initial remediation steps so pager fatigue and finger-pointing decrease.nnsignal taxonomy (high level):n1) resource capacity signalsn - gpu_util_pct: instantaneous gpu utilization per noden - gpu_steal_pct: fraction of gpu cycles lost to eviction/preemptionn - host_mem_pressure: os-level memory pressure on serving nodesn2) kernel scheduler signalsn - kernel_latency_p50/p95/p99: per-kernel execution latenciesn - kernel_queue_depth: queued kernel invocations waiting on scheduler slotn - kernel_handoff_count: number of handoffs between kernels/plugins during a requestn3) kv / model caching signalsn - kvcache_hit_rate: ratio of requests served from kv cachen - kvcache_warmup_time: average time to populate cache after model swap or scale eventn4) request surface fidelity signalsn - observed_brevity: fraction of responses truncated due to eviction or timeoutn - model_variant_switch_rate: rate of runtime fallback to lower-fidelity variantsn5) cost-correlated aggregatesn - token_cost_rate: modeled /token over 1m windows (see cost-model section)n - excess_gpu_hours: measured gpu-hours above steady-state baselinennsignal cost mapping (annotated table):nnote: this table is intended to be human-readable. for programmatic mapping, see the appendix sample sql/promql.nn observability signal immediate cost investigation playbook, content: summary:nthis page defines the kernel health index (khi) a composite signal used to detect regressions and degradation in the serving runtimes kernel layer and provides a step-by-step oncall investigation and remediation playbook. the khi aggregates kernel-level telemetry (latency, error rates, kernel queue lengths, preemption events, and gpu memory pressure) into a single, interpretable score per scheduler cohort. the goal is early, actionable detection with minimal false positives and clear escalation steps.nnwhy we need khi:n- kernels are a frequent choke point for tail latency and cross-tenant interference.n- single-signal alerts (e.g., p50 token latency) are noisy when mixed workloads or rolling deploys are active.n- khi provides a stable, cohort-scoped index that surfaces meaningful kernel-level change while preserving correlation to user-visible slos.nnscope and ownership:n- scope: gpu kernel operations and the scheduler/handoff surface inside the runtime (kernel invocation, queueing, preemption, kernel handoff errors, kernel timeouts).n- owning team: eng-serving-runtime (runtime kernel and scheduling subteams).n- oncall escalation: runtime oncall - kernel scheduling rotate - runtime performance owners.nnkhi definition (high level):n- khi is a normalized, weighted sum of standardized component signals for a cohort and 1-minute window:n - latency sensitive kernel tail (k_tail): percentile-based tail of kernel execution time (e.g., 99th percentile of measured kernel time).n - kernel error spike score (k_err): count of kernel-level errors (failed launches, launch timeouts) normalized by request volume.n - queue pressure index (k_q): average queue length / slot capacity ratio in scheduler queues.n - preemption churn (k_preempt): count of preemption events per minute normalized by active kernels.n - memory pressure index (k_mem): fraction of kernels that triggered oom/soft-oom or elevated allocation/reclaim events.nn- simplified score formula (illustrative):n khi 100 (0.35norm(k_tail) 0.25norm(k_err) 0.15norm(k_q) 0.15norm(k_preempt) 0.10norm(k_mem))n where norm(x) maps the raw metric to 0,1 using cohort-specific baseline percentiles (historical 7d median mad).nninterpretation buckets:n- khi 70: high-priority incident. execute mitigation matrix and page kernel scheduling owners.nnpromql and query recipes (examples):n- 99th percentile kernel exec time per cohort (example):n histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kernel_exec_duration_seconds_bucketcohortweb-embeddings5m)) by (le, cohort))nn- kernel error spike (5m):n sum(rate(kernel_launch_errors_totalcohortweb-embeddings5m)) / sum(rate(kernel_invocations_totalcohortweb-embeddings5m))nn- queue pressure (1m avg):n avg_over_time(scheduler_queue_lengthqueuekernel-.,cohortweb-embeddings1m) / scheduler_queue_capacitycohortweb-embeddingsnn- preemption churn (1m):n sum(rate(kernel_preemptions_totalcohortweb-embeddings1m)) / max(1, sum(rate(kernel_invocations_totalcohortweb-embeddings1m)))nn- memory pressure (ratio):n sum(rate(kernel_memory_pressure_events_totalcohortweb-embeddings5m)) / sum(rate(kernel_invocations_totalcohortweb-embeddings5m))nnalerting rules (recommended thresholds):n- khi alert (page): khi 40 for 2m sustained or khi delta 25 in 5m. severity: p2 (first responder), escalate to p1 if sustained 10m or correlated slo breach.n- kernel error rate guide: kernel_launch_error_rate 0.005 (0.5) sustained 5m - generate paging alert.n- queue pressure guide: scheduler_queue_length / capacity 0.7 for 3m - fire warning 0.9 - page.nnoncall investigation checklist (ordered):n1) confirm alert and scopen - look at khi time series and cohort tag. is the spike localized to one cohort or global?n - check related slo dashboards (token latency, request success rate) for correlation.n2) immediately gather fast artifacts (first 2 minutes)n - grep or use trace ui to collect 520 traces that hit altered kernels.n - snapshot kernel metrics: kernel_exec_duration_seconds, kernel_launch_errors_total, scheduler_queue_length, kernel_preemptions_total, kernel_memory_pressure_events_total.n - capture top-10 affected hosts/pods and gpu ids.n3) triage for common fault classes (parallelizable):n - regression in kernel binary/driver: check recent kernel-related rollouts or kernel-variant canaries in the last 30m. command: git rev-list --since30 minutes ago -- kernel/n - resource exhaustion: look at node gpu memory util and host-level oom logs. cli examples: kubectl top pod -n runtime sort -k3 -nr ssh to host and check nvidia-smi --query-gpumemory.used,utilization.gpu --formatcsvn - scheduler misconfiguration: check admission-controller and credit buckets for cohort. query admission metrics and recent config pushes.n - hot-path kernel slowdown due to sequence length change: correlate request sequence_length histogram to kernel latency.n4) apply fast mitigations (choose applicable, run one at a time):n - route affected cohort to safe model variant or lower fidelity model to reduce kernel load. (console route change follow routing rollback checklist.)n - increase scheduler slots or temporarily widen admission (if slo permits).n - abort rollout: revert recent kernel or kernel-config change via canary rollback.n - evict noisy tenant(s) if cross-tenant noise is identified (follow eviction authority policy).n5) if mitigations fail, page kernel scheduling owner and sre with incident severity.nnpost-incident diagnostics and writeup (10 steps):n1) capture full 1h/24h metric windows and annotate the khi spike and mitigations applied.n2) replay sample traces with throttling reproduction harness (use the replay-runbook below).n3) run targeted microbenchmarks against suspected kernels (see section: microbenchmark recipes).n4) check for correlated infra events (network blips, cloud npu maintenance notices, host reboots).n5) extract kernel flame graphs and differential profiles against a pre-incident baseline.n6) if a new kernel variant is implicated, run the compatibility test matrix and kernel-safety smoke tests.n7) update khi normalizers if the baseline has shifted legitimately due to new model mix.n8) produce a short incident summary with root cause, corrective actions, and preventive work.n9) link a follow-up ticket with owners and target dates for any code/config change.n10) verify remediation by validating khi and slos for 4872 hours.nnmicrobenchmark recipes (quick):n- controlled invocation: run the kernel microbench driver with varying sequence lengths and batch shapes to reproduce tail behavior. example command: n ./kernel_microbench --modeldecoder_v2 --batch-shape1x64x512 --sequence1024 --repeat200nn- kernel launch stress: synthetic parallel launch script to exercise launch paths. n python tools/parallel_launch.py --workers128 --ops2000 --cohortweb-embeddingsnnobservability changes to implement (backlog):n- add khi cohort breakdown to the daily perf digest email and console uptime dashboard.n- store 7d sliding baseline histograms per cohort to make normalization robust to diurnal patterns.n- introduce automatic root-cause candidate ranking: link top correlated signals and host/pod lists in alert payload.nnknown limitations and caveats:n- khi can be biased during large deployments or a/b experiments always annotate major rollouts and use rollouts tag to mute alerts during coordination windows.n- the normalization function requires 7d stable baseline newly onboarded cohorts with 85c sustained, nvlink_error_rate baseline, driver-restart events, unexpected gpu offline.n - immediate impact: abrupt token latency spikes, increased tail latency, node removal from pool.nn- kernel-level regression / latency inflation:n - examples: new kernel release with suboptimal tiling for medium sequence length per-kernel code-path takes 2x cycles for specific ops.n - signals: kernel_duration_p50/p95 increase for impacted kernel id, kernel-inflight-queued, kernel-error-ratio.n - interaction: scheduler may increase backpressure, leading to higher queueing latency across tenants.nn- scheduler misconfiguration or policy conflict:n - examples: aggressive fairness policy resulting in starvation of high-priority slos priority inversion with ephemeral plugins.n - signals: queue-depth-by-priority, delayed-scheduler-invocations, starvation-durationthreshold.nn- kv cache evictions cold-start storms:n - examples: bulk tenant requests after model swap cause cache churn and repeated warmups.n - signals: kvcache-hit-rate drop, warmup-requests-per-minute spike, per-request-additional-latency-with-warmup.nn- model-variant oscillation / continuous fallback churn:n - examples: routing policy repeatedly swaps between quantized and full-float model variants under marginal quality regressions.n - signals: model-switch-count, transient-quality-regression-alerts, per-session-inconsistency.nn- control-plane routing instability:n matrix and slo correlation (short):n- sev 1 (customer-impacting steady): sustained 50 increase in tail-99 latency, 5 error rate for 5 minutes.n- sev 2 (degraded but partially functional): 2050 tail-99 kapoor, and the serving runtime on-call rotation., doc_id: dsid_aac5bbb53762465bbc62bd7a4d66de5e, source_type: confluence, title: service surface and scheduler interop playbook, content: overviewnnnpurpose: this playbook defines the service surface contract between the serving runtime and kernel scheduler components, specifies an interop handshake, and provides operational guidance for profiling, benchmarking, and incident response when scheduler/runtime mismatches cause latency or cost regressions. it is intended for runtime engineers, scheduler authors, sres, and platform product managers.nnwhy this existsn- we frequently observe subtle regressions when a new scheduler or kernel mapping is rolled out without a clearly defined contract (e.g., unexpected preemption behavior, missed cache affinities).n- a small, testable interop specification and an operational checklist reduce rollout risk and speed investigation.nnscopen- applies to the primary gpu serving runtime, the kernel scheduling layer, and their integration surface (request admission, priority propagation, kv cache hints, slot accounting).n- out of scope: low-level device driver patches, third-party accelerator sdk internals (these should have their own adapter docs).nnactors and ownershipn- runtime api/serving team: owns the public-facing runtime service surface, telemetry annotations, and stability slos.n- kernel/scheduler team: owns scheduling decisions, admission controller, and kernel hints.n- eng-sre: owns alerts, incident runbooks, and canary gating criteria.nnkey goals and invariantsn1) deterministic metadata: requests must carry a minimal, normalized header bundle (priority, estimated_seq_len, model_variant_hint) so scheduler decisions are reproducible.n2) idempotent handshake: scheduler must acknowledge accepted admission units and provide an opaque allocation token that the runtime will return on completion.n3) observability parity: both sides must emit a matching correlation_id and timestamped lifecycle events for each request path (admit, queue, slice_start, kernel_enqueue, kernel_complete, complete).n4) graceful degradation: when the scheduler cannot honor a request-level quality hint, it must return a structured fallback suggestion that the runtime will act on (e.g., select lower-fidelity variant, apply shorter seq cutoff).nnservice surface specification (compact)n- request headers (required):n - x-runtime-correlation: (opaque, generated by fronting service)n - x-priority: integer (0low .. 10critical)n - x-estimated-seq: integer (tokens)n - x-model-variant: string (optional hint)n - x-cache-affinity: string (optional prefix fingerprint)nn- admission response (scheduler - runtime): json body with fields - status, allocation_token, granted_fidelity_profile, queue_position (nullable), eviction_constraint (nullable), telemetry_tags. example:nn n status: granted,n allocation_token: alloc_9f2a...,n granted_fidelity_profile: vocab-trim-quant8,n queue_position: null,n eviction_constraint: null,n telemetry_tags: kernel-a, slot-42n nnhandshake and admission protocol (textual flow)n1) runtime wraps incoming client request with x-runtime-correlation and normalized headers.n2) runtime sends admission call to scheduler: /admit (post) with request headers estimated_runtime_budget_ms field.n3) scheduler responds synchronously (.n4) run the latency attribution script: tools/latency-attrib --bucket profiling/ --group-by allocation_token, kernel_type.n5) if kernel.exec_ms shows heavy variance tied to allocation_token, escalate to kernel team with attached trace and stripped pcap of scheduling rpcs.nnbenchmarking guidancen- benchmark goals: reproduce production mix of sequence lengths and priority bands. target metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per gpu, preemption rate.n- synthetic benchmark command example (k8s job):nnkubectl run bench-replay --imageredwood/bench-replay:stable -- n --corpus s3://bench/corpus/mix-aug-2026.json --qps 200 --priority-dist 0:10,5:70,9:20 --duration 30mnn- cost-aware bench: run two passes with and without prefix caching enabled and compare tokens/sec and average cost-per-token.nnrelease and canary checklist (integration of scheduler/runtime)n1) unit tests: admission serializer/deserializer (coverage 95).n2) integration tests: local docker-compose full-handshake scenario.n3) canary (10 traffic for 24h) with telemetry gating: if admit.latency_p95 increases 10 or preemption_rate3 pause rollout.n4) run the benchmarking job (above) against canary compare baseline against canary with an automated diff report.nnincident runbook (quick triage)n1) alert triggers: spike in admitted.queue_length or admit.latency_p95.n2) run quick probe: curl /debug/admit?sample100 on scheduler to check policy state.n3) correlate allocation_token churn to runtime kernel_complete events. command: tools/trace-correlate --from now-15m --tag correlation_id --agg by allocation_token.n4) if scheduler is returning fallback fidelity frequently, temporarily toggle runtime to conservative_fallback_mode via feature flag: runtime.fallback.modestatic-low-fidelity.n5) escalation: if issue persists 30m open incident and page kernel and scheduler oncall. attach traces and the benchmark replay command used for repro.nnknown limitations and mitigationsn- limitation: allocation tokens are opaque and prevent cross-cluster visibility. mitigation: add hashed cluster_id in telemetry_tags.n- limitation: scheduler response latency can amplify tail latency. mitigation: local admission cache in runtime with ttl 200ms for frequent identical requests.n- limitation: priority inversion when many low-priority, long-seq requests occupy non-preemptable slots. mitigation: implement aging-based slot rebalancer (see roadmap item).nnappendix: example diagnostic payload (json)nn correlation_id: 6f8d7c8b-2d6b,n and experimentation manual, content: overviewnnthis document defines redwoods recommended practice for failure inoculation experiments against the serving runtime. the goal is to run controlled, measurable experiments that surface weak points in: kernel scheduling, kv-cache consistency, model swap safety, preemption and eviction, cross-tenant interference, and network/service mesh degradations while preserving customer slas and ensuring fast rollback.nnscope and motivationnn- scope: hosted, dedicated, and private runtime topologies. focus area for this manual: experiments that exercise the inference serving stack layers (dispatcher, scheduler, kernel, kvcache, model loader, and network fabric).n- motivation: proactively discover degradations and channel findings into kernel/scheduler hardening, autoscaling rules, runtime admission policies, and fidelity fallback contracts.nndefinitionsnn- failure inoculation: deliberate, controlled introduction of adverse conditions to observe system resilience and recovery behavior.n- experiment runbook: documented steps for preflight, execution, measurement, and rollback.n- safety envelope: pre-declared constraints that must not be violated (slo breach thresholds, impacted tenants, time windows).nnsafety policy and gatingnnbefore any experiment is scheduled the following gates must be satisfied:nn1) business and customer gaten- no running experiments against paid enterprise dedicated clusters without explicit customer approval.n- hosted experiments must restrict to synthetic tenants and test api keys production traffic must not be targeted.nn2) slo safety envelope (hard thresholds)n- global p95 api latency must not exceed baseline p95 30 for more than 5 minutes.n- error rate (5xx) must remain below 0.5 of baseline traffic during the experiment window.n- token-generation fairness: no single synthetic tenant may consume 10 of cluster dispatch capacity unless previously authorized.nn3) operational staffingn- at least two on-call engineers from eng-serving-runtime must be present during the experiment (primary observer).n- sre must be notified and on standby if the experiment could affect cross-tenant routing.nnexperiment types and intentnna. scheduler perturbationn- intent: validate scheduler credit accounting, priority inversion detection and graceful backpressure.n- action examples: artificially throttle kernel dispatch for a priority tier inject slot starvations to simulate device contention.n- key metrics: kernel queue length, per-priority p99 latency, kernel rejection rate, scheduler admission counters.nnb. kv-cache warm/cold transitionn- intent: exercise cache warmup paths and eviction ripple effects during model swap.n- action examples: evict selected tenant shards, simulate cold model swap (flush local cache remote fetch delays).n- key metrics: kvcache miss rate, model load time, tail latency during first 100 tokens after swap.nnc. model swap and fallback orchestrationn- intent: verify canary/rollout safety, fallback to lower-fidelity model variants, and kv consistency post-swap.n- action examples: trigger a staged model push to a small cohort, then force a full-swap while artificially raising checksum mismatch errors in the loader.n- key metrics: successful fallback count, consistency reconciliation time, error surface for model artifact validation.nnd. network fabric degradationn- intent: validate rpc timeouts, grpc retry behavior, and graceful degradation when inter-node latency increases.n- action examples: introduce 50-250ms rtt between dispatcher and gpus inside the test topology, or inject packet loss of 0.5-2.n- key metrics: request retry rate, end-to-end token latency, cpu scheduling spikes attributable to increased rpc stalls.nne. thermal and power throttling simulationn- intent: emulate gpu thermal throttling and observe kernel preemption/backoff reactions.n- action examples: reduce available compute quota to a worker to simulate thermal step-down.n- key metrics: kernel reschedule rate, preemption counts, impact on concurrent tenants.nnexperiment design template (always populate)nn- experiment id: runbook-yyyymmdd-short-namen- owner(s): (name, pager)n- objective: one-sentence hypothesisn- target topology: (hosted/dedicated/private) and cluster ids or labelsn- safety envelope: list of slo thresholds and excluded tenantsn- steps: numbered preflight - inject - observe - withdraw - analysisn- measurement sheet: queries and dashboards to collect (see example observability queries)n- rollback criteria: explicit conditions that trigger an immediate abort and remediation stepsn- postmortem required: y/n (postmortem required for any experiment that triggers a safety-envelope violation)nnpreflight checklist (must be completed and signed off)nn1) create experiment ticket in the experiments board and link the runbook.n2) confirm synthetic tenants and test api-keys are configured validate routing isolation.n3) ensure ttl and billing freezes for synthetic tenants to avoid unexpected charges.n4) record baseline metrics for at least 15 minutes pre-injection: p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, kernel queue depth, kvcache hitrate.n5) notify sre and product ops with time window and pager contacts.nnexecution procedure (sample)nn1) start live observability snapshot: run the collection job to capture high-resolution traces for the next 30 minutes. command: curl -x post -d scope:experiment-run -h authorization: bearer obs_tokennn2) apply failure injection via the chaos service:n- scheduler throttle example:n curl -x post n -h authorization: bearer chaos_token n -d type:scheduler-throttle,target:prioritylow,duration_s:300,params:drop_rate:0.15nn3) monitor critical dashboards: kernel queue depth, scheduler admission logs, per-priority tail latency.nn4) observe for the pre-declared timebox (suggested 5 minutes for initial smoke). if any rollback criteria met, execute rollback (step 6).nn5) withdraw injection: call the chaos service to remove the perturbation.nn6) if rollback criteria met, escalate following the runtime incident process:n- immediate action: cancel injection and run remedial script to re-stabilize dispatchers:n kubectl -n runtime-system rollout restart deployment/dispatcher --selectorclustertest-clustern- notify affected owners in title: runtime resource annotation taxonomy and signal enrichment, content: summarynnthis document defines a canonical taxonomy for resource annotations used across the serving runtime, plus the enrichment pipeline that turns raw telemetry config into scored signals used by the scheduler, admission controller, and autoscaler. the goal is to standardize names, types, semantics, and operational practices so that components can interoperate without brittle ad-hoc mappings.nnmotivationnn- multiple teams (scheduler, kernel mapper, autoscaler, observability) require consistent, machine-readable metadata about model-serving resources (gpus, shards, model variants, containers, and requests).n- inconsistent annotation names caused mismatches in fallback routing and incorrect prefetch decisions during q3 incidents.n- a small, well-documented set of canonical fields reduces cognitive load for owners and speeds rollouts of policy changes.nnscopenn- this taxonomy applies to: gpu nodes, runtime shards, model-variant instances, session tokens (provenance), and request classes.n- out of scope: long-term billing tags (managed by finance) and user-level semantic labels (managed by product teams).nncore principlesnn1) backwards-compatible: existing annotation keys must continue to be supported new keys should have clear deprecation paths.n2) idempotent enrichment: repeated enrichment runs should produce identical signals for the same inputs.n3) typed and validated: each key has a strict type and acceptable value range.n4) explainable scores: any composite score must be reproducible and accompanied by its component weights.nncanonical annotation table (summary)nn key type description primary consumers default/notes n------:---------n resource_type string one of gpu-node, shard, model-variant, session, request-class all required n affinity string affinity class: one of high, medium, low used for co-location heuristics scheduler, autoscaler default: medium n eviction_priority integer 0 (never) - 100 (highest) eviction ranking, lower safer to evict scheduler, runtime default: 50 n kvcache_hotness float 0.0-1.0 locality score for kv cache reuse kernel-mapper, scheduler computed by enrichment pipeline n kernel_hint string preferred kernel execution path (e.g. attention-sliced-v2, fused-mlp) kernel-mapper optional n fidelity_profile string fidelity target: max_quality, balanced, cost_saver autoscaler, rollout impacts quantization and fallback policies n estimated_tps float estimated tokens-per-second capacity for this resource admission, autoscaler derived from microbenchmarks and telemetry n thermal_headroom float 0.0-1.0 available thermal headroom resource_type/gpu_model) using canonicalizer map.n2) join time windows: create sliding windows (default 5m, 1h) for hotness and latency measures.n3) compute primitive signals: mean_ttfb, median_tokens, kv_access_rate, error_rate, thermal_percentile.n4) normalize clamp: scale signals into canonical ranges, clamp outliers (z-score guardrails).n5) composite scoring: calculate kvcache_hotness, estimated_tps, eviction_priority_delta using weighted sums. weights are stored in the scoreconfig repo and are versioned.n6) publish annotated record: write to annotated resource store (a lightweight document store with versioned entries).nnexample enrichment rule (pseudocode)nn kvcache_hotness calculation - pseudocodennwindow last_15_minutes(requests.filter(modelx))nkv_hits sum(window.map(r - r.kv_hit ? 1 : 0))nkv_accesses sum(window.map(r - r.kv_accesses))nhotness (kv_hits 0.5 kv_accesses) / max(1, window.request_count)nnormalized_hotness sigmoid_scale(hotness, scale0.8) clamp to 0..1nnoperational notes on enrichment weightsn- scoreconfig is a git-backed json with simple schema: kv_weight: 0.6, latency_weight: 0.3, thermal_penalty: 0.1. changes require a review and a ci gate that replays enrichment on a representative sample.nnstorage and apinn- annotated resource store: path /annotated-resources/resource_id, json document with last_enriched_at and version tag. the store supports conditional writes (etag) to avoid stomping concurrent enrichments.n- read api: /api/v1/annotated-resources?filter... supports predicates on canonical fields and returns stable snapshots.nnconsumers and contractsnn- scheduler: consumes annotated records and uses affinity kvcache_hotness thermal_headroom to rank placement. contract: annotated record must be eng-sre - platform-eng lead.n- suggested reviewers for changes: diego ramirez runtime telemetry sampling and cost-aware profiling policy, content: summaryn-------nthis document defines redwoods standardized policy for runtime telemetry sampling and cost-aware profiling. it describes which signals to collect, how to sample requests to meet slos while controlling telemetry costs, recommended storage/retention tiers, and an operational runbook for changes or incidents that require higher-fidelity traces. the goal is to preserve diagnostic signal for engineering and sre workflows while bounding observability costs and avoiding unbounded ingestion/ingress spikes.nnmotivation and goalsn--------------------n- reduce observability spend growth while retaining high utility for performance and regression investigations.n- provide deterministic, auditable sampling behavior across runtime components (dispatcher, kernel dispatcher, kvcache, model-handler).n- make profiling decisions workload-aware: bursty clients, tail-heavy routes, canary experiments, and high-cost model variants should get more coverage.n- define safe escalation and rollback paths when increased telemetry is required during incidents or experiments.nntelemetry signals (priority list)n--------------------------------n1) high-value, low-volume (always-on)n - per-request slo metadata: request_id, route, model_variant, tenant, priority_class, latency_ms, status_coden - aggregated token-level counters: tokens_requested, tokens_emitted per model_variant (1s rollup)n2) medium-value (sampled)n - traces for inference lifecycle across runtime components (dispatcher - kernel - device)n - kernel queue times and kernel execution durations (p50/p95/p99 histograms)n3) low-value / expensive (adaptive sampling)n - full step-level gpu kernel traces (ptx/cupti-level) and per-op gpu timelinesn - full request payloads and user prompt text (redaction rules apply)nnsampling strategy overviewn--------------------------nwe use a hybrid deterministicadaptive sampling strategy: a low base sample rate plus deterministic upsampling for classes of requests that historically produce high-value signals.nnbase rates (default global policy)n- trace sampling (end-to-end request spans): 1 in 200 requests (0.5)n- kernel-level detailed tracing: 1 in 10,000 requests (0.01)n- heavy payload capture (prompts 2k tokens): 1 in 500 requests (0.2)nndeterministic upsampling rules (always evaluated before random sampling)n1) canary/experiment routes: 100 tracing for canary cohorts during rollout window.n2) error-class upsampling: any request with status ! 200 is captured at 100 for at least 10 minutes after first occurrence, then decays to base rate over an hour.n3) tail-latency upsampling: requests that exceed route p95 latency are marked for additional traces for the next n100 matching requests.n4) high-cost models: model_variants with per-token cost x (configurable) increase trace sample to 1 by default.nnadaptive, cost-aware throttlingn------------------------------n- observability budget: each runtime cluster (per-region) has a monthly ingestion budget measured in trace-equivalent-units (teus). teu is defined as a weighted unit that normalizes traces, kernel traces, and payload captures.n- when projected weekly teu consumption reaches 60 of budget, the system reduces non-essential sampling rates by 30 and notifies owners. at 85 projected consumption, further reductions occur and only high-priority deterministic sampling remains.n- an emergency override allows sre to enable 100 tracing for up to 2 hours for incident triage this must be logged and tagged to an incident id.nnretention and storage tiersn--------------------------n- hot (7 days): full-span traces and per-request metadata stored in tracing backend (used for immediate triage and dashboards).n- warm (30 days): aggregated histograms and reduced traces (kept with sampling metadata).n- cold (365 days): token counters, aggregate model_variants cost metrics, and sampling logs for audit.nntable: storage and retentionn signal_type retention storage_location downstream_exports n trace_full 7d trace-cluster-hot alerting/dashboards n trace_reduced 30d trace-cluster-warm performance-reports n aggregates 365d metrics-db billing/simulation nndashboarding and alertingn-------------------------n- critical slo dashboards should use sampled-corrected histograms. sampling-corrected estimators must be applied to p95/p99 calculations when sampling ! 100.n- alerts:n - incoming trace teu rate cluster budget_projection_rate 1.2 - paged to eng-sre.n - spike in kernel-level error rate (5 of kernel calls in 10m) - pager.n - sampling configuration drift (any change to deterministic rules) - notify runtime config-owners and security for scrutiny.nnoperational runbook (when more fidelity is needed)n--------------------------------------------------n1) triage phase: validate the failure mode using existing traces and aggregated metrics.n2) if insufficient signal, escalate to temporary upsampling: update cluster sampling override policy to increase trace sampling to 5 for affected routes for a maximum of 90 minutes.n3) if kernel-level detail required, enable kernel-level tracing for a dedicated rolling node pool with isolated teu accounting.n4) after capture: revert overrides, tag traces with incident id, and run cost reconciliation.n5) produce a post-incident note listing why higher fidelity was required and whether sampling policies should be adjusted.nnchange management and rollout processn-----------------------------------n- sampling policy lives in a declarative feature flag repo: repo: infra/observability/sampling-policies, file: runtime-defaults.yaml.n- changes require:n 1) design doc (1 page) describing reason and measurement plan.n 2) pr with unit tests simulation against synthetic workloads (see tools/telemetry-sim).n 3) canaried rollout to 2 of clusters for 24 hours check teu impact and correctness.n 4) gradual rollout with metric-based gates.nnconfig examplesn---------------nyaml example for route-level policy (runtime-defaults.yaml excerpt):nn---nroutes:n - name: /v1/generaten default_trace_sample: 0.005 0.5n upsample_rules:n - name: canary_cohortn matcher: route:generate and cohort:canaryn sample: 1.0n - name: tail_latency_boostn matcher: route:generate content: summary:nthis document defines a reproducible, cross-layer approach for measuring, attributing, and validating execution fidelity (quality of model outputs and execution correctness) against token-level and kernel-level cost accounting. it is intended for runtime engineers, performance sres, and applied ml teams. the manual describes metrics, instrumentation requirements, a validation lab protocol, ci/qa gates, and recommended runbook actions when drift or regressions are detected.nnscope and motivation:n- scope: hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where the redwood serving runtime is responsible for kernel selection, kv cache management, batching, and quantization.n- motivation: teams often treat fidelity (quality) and cost (gpu cycles, token pricing) as separate concerns. engineering changes (kernel updates, scheduler policies, quantization profiles) create cross-cutting effects that can reduce quality while improving cost or vice versa. this manual provides a standard contract for measuring both and for validating regressions prior to rollout.nnkey concepts and definitions:n1) execution fidelity: a composite of functional correctness checks (deterministic outputs for fixed seeds and prompts), quality evaluation (task-specific metrics like bleu/rouge, embedding cosine retention, or user-defined evals), and runtime consistency (kv cache correctness, repeatable logits for pinned rng seeds).n2) cost accounting units:n - token_compute_ms: per-token kernel time measured in wall-clock milliseconds in the kernel execution path.n - host_latency_ms: per-request host-side latency excluding kernel execution (scheduling, serialization, network).n - memory_pressure_score: percentile-based indicator of gpu memory fragmentation affecting eviction rates.n - kernel_credit_units: abstracted unit mapping per-kernel to normalized cost used in cost-allocation reports.n3) cross-layer attribution: mapping from token/response quality deltas to kernel-level events (kernel selection changes, quantization boundaries, batch slice sizes) and to infrastructure events (gpu throttling, nvlink errors).nninstrumentation contract (minimum):n- traces: every request must emit a trace containing request_id, model_variant, kernel_id, kernel_start_ms, kernel_end_ms, batch_size, sequence_lengths, kvcache_hit_ratio, and rng_seed when provided.n- metrics: per-kernel counters for invocations, avg_exec_ms, p50/95/99_exec_ms, gpu_util, and transient_error_count.n- logs: deterministic kernel logs must include stable kernel signature and quantization profile id.n- probes: a lightweight fidelity probe that can be run on a small sample of requests to compute a quick quality score (see validation lab below).nnmeasurement model and schema (example):n- reporting key: date, region, cluster, model_family, model_version, deployment_tier - values: tokens_processed, token_compute_ms_total, host_latency_ms_p50, fidelity_probe_score_p50, kernel_credit_units_total.n- store rollups at 1m, 15m, 1h granularity.nnvalidation lab: reproducible experiment protocolnpurpose: run deterministic workloads (synthetic and live-sampled) through candidate runtime changes and produce a signed report that combines fidelity and cost tradeoffs.nprerequisites:n- canary cluster with same kernel-build-id and same model artifacts as candidate.n- seed corpus: 10k prompt-set with labeled expected behaviours (include edge cases, long-context examples, and hallucination-sensitive prompts).n- eval harness configured to produce both numeric metrics and qualitative examples.nnprotocol steps:n1) baseline capture (24h): collect baseline metrics on current runtime and model_version for 24 hours using production traffic shadowing or synthetic replay. persist kernel traces and fidelity_probe outputs.n2) controlled candidate run (6h): deploy candidate kernel/scheduler/quantization to canary cluster and replay the identical workload. ensure identical seed rng and request ordering when possible to maximize comparability.n3) compute delta report:n - for each prompt in the seed corpus compute: quality_delta candidate_score - baseline_score.n - compute cost_delta (candidate_token_compute_ms_total - baseline_token_compute_ms_total) / baseline_tokens_processed.n - flag any prompt with quality_delta 15 may be accepted if regression cases are triaged and mitigated with fallback policies.nnci/qa gates and automated checks:n- unit tests: deterministic kernel unit-tests must pass for signed kernels.n- integration checks: a lightweight fidelity_probe run (sample size 200) with automated alert if probe_score drops below baseline by 1.n- pre-merge: bundles that change kernel selection logic require an attached canary-compatibility matrix.n- pre-release: performance annex must include token_compute_ms delta and the signed validation lab report.nnexample experiment config (yaml-like inline):n---nexperiment_name: kv-cache-reshard-q3nseed_corpus: s3://redwood-evals/kv-reshard-seed/2026-01ncanary_cluster: canary-eu-west-1-3nmetrics: fidelity_probe_score, token_compute_ms, host_latency_msnrollback_policy: immediate-on-fidelity-dropnduration: 6hn---nnpractical checklist for triage when fidelity regressions appear:n1) confirm measurement integrity: validate that the same seed corpus and rng seed were used, check trace completeness.n2) correlate with kernel_id and quantization_profile: use the top-5 kernel attribution table.n3) check infra signals: gpu thermal and nvlink counters, oom events, or driver resets during the candidate window.n4) if kernel-level cause: annotates the kernel in the kernel registry and tag as suspect. run kernel bisection.n5) if scheduling or batching cause: re-run with reduced batch-size and disabled preemption to compare.n6) action: rollback, deploy per-route fallback to previous model_variant, or apply a targeted kernel patch.nnoperational dashboards and reports (recommended):n- fidelity vs cost heatmap: x-axis fidelity_probe_score delta, y-axis cost_delta_per_token. color incidence count.n- per-model fidelity anomaly stream: streaming alerts when rolling 1h fidelity_probe_score deviates by 2 sigma.n- kernel-level ledger: per-kernel deploy history with quick links to validation lab reports.nnownership and responsibilities:n- runtime sre (oncall): monitoring, immediate triage, runbook execution for infra failures.n- runtime platform: produce validation lab report and maintain the experiment harness.n- applied ml / model onboarding: define seed corpus and acceptance thresholds for each model_family.n- release owner: responsible for including the validation report in the release bundle.nnrunbook excerpts (quick actions):n1) fidelity-alert-fire:n - notify: @runtime-sre, @applied-ml open incident with tag fidelity-regression.n - snapshot: capture 1h of kernel traces and the validation lab delta gradual expansion gates: fidelity_probe_score stability and cost_delta within defined envelope for 6 successive evaluation windows.n- fallback: maintain a per-route automatic fallback policy that can runtime and for running controlled experiments (feature gates, kernel rollouts, scheduler tuning, quantization profiles, and routing policies). it combines a lightweight impact matrix with an experimentation cookbook and the minimal runbook snippets required to triage regressions introduced by change. the goal is to reduce blast radius, speed detection, and make rollbacks predictable.nnscope:n- applies to changes that modify: runtime binary (c/cuda), kernel selection mapping, scheduler policy, kv cache behavior, batching heuristics, and routing/fallback rules.n- excludes purely client-side sdk changes or docs-only updates (those follow a different lightweight process).nnwho should use this:n- release engineers and runtime owners for planned rolloutsn- sres rollback threshold (alert-driven) n----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------n kernel mapping or new kernel binary kernel scheduler, gpu dispatcher, telemetry increased tail latency, oom, kernel hangs p99 latency 350ms for 5m or error 0.5 n scheduler policy change request router, admission control, metrics priority inversion, head-of-line blocking p95 latency 30 n kv cache eviction/format change kvcache, model swap, warm start cold-start regressions, model consistency third-party-accelerator-onboarding-and-runtime-integration-2026, content: overviewnnpurpose: this document defines the engineering process, interface contracts, testing checklist, performance profiling playbook, and runbook steps required to safely onboard third-party accelerator kernels (vendor-provided or community plugins) into redwoods serving runtime. it is intended for runtime engineers, kernel maintainers, release engineers, and partners delivering binary kernels.nnscope: includes abi/handshake, scheduling delegation, telemetry requirements, automated benchmarks, release gating criteria, and emergency rollback procedures. does not cover dedicated/hardware procurement policies or vendor commercial agreements.nnkey goalsn- protect production slos (p95 latency, p99 tail, and throughput) when new kernels are introduced.n- ensure predictable fallbacks and fast mitigation for regressions.n- provide a repeatable onboarding checklist for partner kernels.n- integrate kernel-level telemetry into profiler and benchmark suites.nn1) architecture and contractsn1.1 high-level flown- client request - router - kernel-aware scheduler - accelerator driver - kernel binary - execution - kv cache / memory manager - responsen- the scheduler exposes a lightweight delegation api to accept or decline work based on kernel-reported capacity hints.nn1.2 required contracts (must be implemented by any third-party kernel)n- abi handshake: json manifest exchanged at registration time containing: kernel_id, supported-ops, max_sequence_length, preferred_batch_shape, memory_reservation_bytes, suggested_concurrency, quantization_support (none/int8/fp16), version, and signature (sha256).n- health api: /kernel/health - status: readydegradedunavailable, current_load: int, available_slots: int (grpc or http as configured).n- telemetry hooks: emit tracing span with tag kernel.id, provide per-call token_count and per-buffer memory_usage metrics.n- fallback hints: on degradation kernel must supply a suggested fallback model_variant or indicate graceful-degradation behavior.nn2) scheduling delegation modeln- scheduler roles: admission control, prioritization, and preemption signaling.n- delegation handshake: scheduler sends a probe (100200ms budget) to allow kernel to confirm readiness and advertise capacity. if no response within the probe window, scheduler treats kernel as unavailable for that allocation.n- priority mapping: requests carry route_priority (0system,1premium,2default,3best-effort). kernel must accept or reject based on a priority bitmap advertised in the manifest.n- preemption signal: scheduler may send preempt_with_intent to request graceful early termination of lower-priority in-flight work. kernels must support checkpointing of kv cache state if execution spans 500ms.nn3) profiling playbook for new kernelsn- baseline collection steps (automated pipeline)n 1. deploy kernel in isolated sandbox cluster with synthetic traffic that mirrors target route shapes (short-form-chat, long-sequence-completion, embeddings).n 2. run 3 x 30-minute runs per workload shape at steady concurrency targets: low (10), nominal (100), and burst (300).n 3. capture full traces, kernel internal counters, gpu occupancy, pcie/nvlink bandwidth, host cpu steal, and memory fragmentation metrics.n- key signals to evaluaten - mean_token_latency, p95/p99 token generation latency, kernel_dispatch_time, kernel_queue_wait, kernel_compute_time, kvcache_hit_ratio, memory_alloc_failures.n - cost proxy: tokens/sec per accelerator-hour and estimated /1m tokens using current price model.n- failure modes to flag automaticallyn - sudden increase (20) in p99 with no corresponding cpu or request-shape delta.n - unbounded growth in memory ( 5 per minute over 5 minutes).n - frequent short bumps in kernel_queue_wait correlated with nvlink retransmits.nn4) benchmarking suite integration stepsn- add kernel to perf-registry: a yaml entry in the benchmarking repo with fields: kernel_id, node_type, driver_version, regression_thresholds. example table:n field example description n kernel_id vendorx-int8-v2 unique id used in manifests n node_type g10x-48gb validated hardware profile n driver_version 4.2.1 expected driver / runtime combo n p99_threshold_ms 42 absolute gating p99 for nominal workload n throughput_tokens_per_sec 12_000 expected steady-state throughput nn- bench harness requirementsn - must run the kernel under the same batching and prefix-caching configs used in production.n - mirror request provenance (token lengths, system prompts, function call patterns).n - produce an artifact: annotated trace (.zip) plus a normalized perf json that includes histograms.nn5) release gating and validationn- mandatory checks (all must pass for canary rollout)n 1. unit trust: manifest signature verified and integration tests pass (functional correctness).n 2. canary perf: benchmark harness p99 and throughput within 95 of golden baseline.n 3. telemetry conformity: kernel emits required spans and metrics.n 4. graceful-fallback test: simulated node failure triggers scheduler fallback without client error rate 0.1.n- progressive rollout plann 1. sandbox - internal canary (5 infra) for 24h - expanded canary (25) for 72h - production (100) with 2-week monitoring holds.n 2. automatic rollback if: p99 increases by 25 or error rate increases by 0.5 over baseline within the observation window.nn6) known issues and mitigation patterns (for this kernel onboarding flow)n- issue: kernel reports low available_slots intermittently causing oscillation. mitigation: enable probe backoff to 2s and increase scheduler probe timeout for the node pool.n- issue: memory fragmentation leads to oom on long sequences. mitigation: enable slab compaction on host and tune kernel memory_reservation_bytes in manifest.n- issue: degraded telemetry fidelity (missing token_count). mitigation: fail the canary and require kernel debug build with logging enabled add temporary sidecar to enrich traces.nn7) runbook: emergency rollback (fast path)n- preconditions: alert fires for rolling-p99-regression or 0.2 client errors router by toggling route-level kernel preference to previous kernel_id via feature toggle service.n 3. trigger scheduler-level evict-and-failover: call /scheduler/evict?kernel_idgrace30s on impacted pool.n 4. revert driver-level configuration if driver update applied within last 6h.n 5. roll forward mitigation: re-run perf smoke tests on a mirrored sandbox if passes, perform controlled reintroduce at 5 for 2 hours.n 6. document incident in postmortem with timeline, traces, and kernels artifacts.nnchecklist quick-reference (for on-call)n- is the manifest signature valid?n- are health dsid_5fd71242d1d442ed9636267fa1d6985f, source_type: confluence, title: cohort sampling governor and kernel lifecycle playbook, content: summaryn-------nthis playbook documents the cohort sampling governor (csg) the runtime component that determines how we sample live inference traffic for profiling and fidelity checks and the kernel lifecycle safeguards that control how kernel changes are rolled out against sampled cohorts. the goal is to keep profiling cost bounded while ensuring representative coverage and safe kernel change rollouts that preserve slos.nnscope and intended audiencen- audience: serving runtime engineers, oncall, profiling team, runtime sres, and release engineers.n- scope: live sampling policies, cohort definitions, governor tuning knobs, kernel lifecycle states, rollout/rollback procedures, validation queries, and incident remediation.nnwhy this mattersn- sampling informs quantization, batching and kernel selection decisions. incorrect sampling bias - bad kernel hints - fidelity regressions at scale.n- kernel rollouts must be coordinated with sampling to avoid unobserved regressions impacting production slos.nnkey concepts and definitionsn- cohort: a stable grouping of requests (by client, route, model_version, or token-rate percentile) used for sampling.n- governor: dynamic service that assigns a sampling probability to each cohort based on budgets, recent coverage, and anomaly score.n- kernel lifecycle states: canary, shadowed, gradual, broad, paused, rollback.n- fidelity sample: a captured trace that includes prompt, response, kernel version, and annotations (latency, token counts, cost).nnhigh-level architecturen1. ingress: request classification service tags request with cohort_id (rules: route, model, customer_tier, token_count_bin).n2. csg: computes sample_prob in realtime using policy inputs (budget, entropy, last_seen, anomaly_score).n3. shard router: duplicates requests to profiling pipeline if sampled otherwise normal path.n4. profiler pipeline: stores traces, computes fidelity metrics, runs automated evals.n5. release controller: consults sampling coverage before moving kernel lifecycle forward.nnsampling policy and knobsn- global budget: maximum profiling qps allowed (default 50 qps for hosted clusters).n- per-cohort min/max probability: ensures low-volume customers still sampled and high-volume customers capped.n- entropy-driven boost: increase sample_prob for requests with surprising model output (high perplexity / low confidence).n- decay window: weight recent coverage more heavily (default 24h).nnrecommended baseline policy (table)n cohort_type rule min_prob max_prob rationale n--------------------------------------------------n enterprise-high customer_tier enterprise and sla gold 0.005 0.02 guarantee representation for high impact customers n public-api route startswith /generate 0.001 0.01 common surface area sampling n tail-token request_length_percentile 99 0.02 0.1 capture long-sequence regressions n experimental-model model_tag in alpha,exp 0.05 0.5 prioritize new variants nndynamic adjustmentsn- if global budget saturated, csg reduces probabilities proportionally, maintaining every cohorts min_prob floor.n- if an anomaly detector triggers for a cohort (latency or error spike), sample_prob is boosted by factor (2x by default) for 1h.nntelemetry and metrics to monitorn- sampling qps per-cohort (gauge) expected vs actual.n- profiled-fidelity-lag (histogram): time between request and availability of trace in profiler. target: p95 0.85.n- content: overviewn--------nthis manual describes how the serving runtime components must integrate to preserve predictable inference slas while enabling safe experimentation. it consolidates architecture contracts, scheduler integration expectations, a compact profiling playbook, benchmarking guidance, release checklists, and concise runbook actions. the audience is runtime engineers, platform owners, and sres who operate or extend the inference stack.nnscopen-----ncovers the following subsystems and artifacts: inference-router, kernel-coordinator, kernel-manager, kv-cache, fidelity-orchestrator, batching-service, telemetry-adapter, and the benchmarking harness (op-sim). it intentionally excludes sdk-level api ergonomics and customer console ui.nndesign principlesn-----------------n- observable contracts: every handoff between components must carry an event with correlation_id and causality_trace.n- fail-fast, degrade-safe: fallbacks must preserve api success (200s) with explicit fidelity headers when possible.n- testability: each integration point must be exercised via the op-sim harness before rollout.n- bounded blast radius: experimental scheduler plugins run in sandbox cohorts with quota-limited traffic.nnarchitecture components and responsibilitiesn------------------------------------------n- inference-router: performs tenant routing, request classification, and initial priority tagging. must attach request.metadata.priority and request.metadata.expiry_ts.n- kernel-coordinator: authoritative placement decision-maker returns allocation tokens and kernel_hint (e.g., segmented-attn-v2, quantized-8bit).n- kernel-manager: asserts kernel version compatibility, triggers handoff to the gpu dispatcher, and surfaces kernel telemetry with kernel_signature and kernel_commit.n- kv-cache: manages prefix caches per-session emits cache_warmup events and provides warmup_score (0..1).n- fidelity-orchestrator: maps workload - model_variant with policy evaluation (latency vs cost vs quality).n- batching-service: consolidates requests, exposes queue_depth and current_burst_size metrics.n- telemetry-adapter: normalises and annotates traces for downstream slo dashboards.nnscheduler integration contract (must be implemented on every kernel path)n------------------------------------------------------------------------ntable: required fields on kernel allocation responsen field type meaning example n correlation_id string mirrors router for this request shape 45 n fallback_variants list ordered fallbacks when capacity misses lrg-8q, lrg-4q nnbehavioral expectations:n1) kernel-manager must validate allocation_token within 200ms of issuance.n2) if kernel-manager cannot satisfy kernel_hint, it must return first compatible fallback_variants and set response.header.x-fidelity-degraded true.n3) any allocation that waits 2s must be annotated with queue_backpressuretrue and emit an alert to the slo monitoring stream.nnprofiling playbook (compact)n---------------------------npurpose: enable fast root cause between request-shape, minutes.n3) correlate kernel_signature - kernel_latency_ms histogram and kv_hit boolean.n4) if tail slo (95p 120ms), run microbench: single-tenant kernel warmstart and memory-pressure sweep.nuseful confluence, title: observability adapter sidecar: design manual and onboarding guide, content: overviewnnthis document describes the design, operational contracts, and onboarding checklist for the observability adapter sidecar (oas)a lightweight per-node sidecar that attaches to serving runtime processes and provides production-safe, low-overhead instrumentation for per-request fidelity signals, adaptive sampling, and enriched traces. it is intended for runtime engineers, profiling owners, and sres who will operate and extend the oas.nngoalsnn- provide a stable, low-latency mechanism for enriching requests with fidelity metadata (kernel hints, kv-cache hit/miss, quantization variant).n- support adaptive, policy-driven sampling that balances observability coverage with cost and privacy constraints.n- decouple heavy signal processing from the hot runtime path via asynchronous sinks and backpressure-aware queues.n- offer clear contracts so runtime teams can consume telemetry without coupling to probe implementations.nnscope and non-goalsnn- in scope: sidecar api contract, sampling controller protocol, configuration schema, rollout checklist, security constraints, and troubleshooting playbook.n- not in scope: changes to kernel scheduling heuristics, evaluation algorithms for model quality, or storage-side analytics pipelines (those are handled by telemetry-backend teams).nndesign principlesnn1. non-blocking hot path: sidecar must not add synchronous latency to inference token emission or rpc response paths.n2. bounded memory predictable cost: local queues have strict bounds policies exist to drop or aggregate when saturated.n3. policy-driven behavior: sampling and enrichment governed by remote policy controller with health-fallback to cached defaults.n4. minimal privileges: run with least privilege network egress only to approved telemetry endpoints.n5. observable and debuggable: expose health, queue-length, and sampling-rate metrics for immediate slo correlation.nnarchitecture (text diagram)nn- serving process (runtime) local ipc socket (unix/grpc) observability adapter sidecar (oas) n n oas components:n - ingress listener: small sync layer to accept lightweight event envelopes ( 80 for 5mnoas.sampler.effective_rate gauge observability coverage effective_rate 5snoas.sink.drop_count counter data loss drop_count increase 100/minnndeployment and rollout checklist (numbered)nn1. pre-flight validation:n a. verify unix socket permissions and selinux/apparmor policy.n b. confirm oas container resource limits: cpu 200m, mem 128mi to start.n c. validate policy endpoint reachable from canary nodes.n2. canary (5 nodes):n a. enable oas in observe-only mode (sample_rate0, aggregatetrue) and flow to debug sink.n b. check oas.queue.length and oas.sink.latency_p95 for regressions.n c. confirm no increase in serving p99 latency beyond 1.n3. progressive ramp: 5 - 25 - 100 over 72h observing signals adjust sample rates if sink latency increases.n4. enable adaptive sampling live with conservative initial policies (global sample_rate 99.5 monthly and effective sampling coverage within 10 of policy target.nnchange management and policy reviewnn- all policy schema changes must be reviewed by telemetry-backend and privacy team.n- major behavioral changes (e.g., switching to synchronous enrichments) require a canary plan and sign-off from runtime performance sig.nnappendix: example sampling policy jsonnnn version: 1,n rules: n matcher: model_variant .-quant,action: sample_rate: 0.02,aggregate: false,n matcher: route confluence, title: fractional kernel coexistence handbook, content: overviewnnthis handbook documents the design, operational guidance, profiling procedures, benchmark suite, and incident runbooks for fractional kernel coexistence (fkc) the runtime pattern that allows multiple kernel implementations and fidelity levels to share physical accelerator capacity with fine-grained isolation and graceful degradation. it consolidates architecture intent, scheduler contracts, rollout checklist, and actionable troubleshooting flows so engineers and oncall sres can operate fkc safely in production.nngoalsnn- enable multiple kernel implementations (full-precision, quantized, sparse, optimized attention variants) to run concurrently on the same gpu(s) without violating latency slos for critical routes.n- provide bounded performance isolation: define and enforce resource shares, preemption semantics, and degradation fallbacks.n- make kernel transitions observable and revertible with low blast radius.n- instrument profiling and benchmark workflows that reflect production co-location effects.nnaudiencenn- runtime engineers, scheduler owners, serving sres, release engineers, and applied ml engineers onboarding new kernels.nndesign summarynn1) principle: soft-isolation via fractional allocation and latency budgetsn - we do not rely on hardware partitioning exclusively runtime allocates fractional execution slots and soft-resources (tensor memory caps, tensor-core credit buckets) and enforces latency budgets per request class.nn2) componentsn - kernel registry: metadata store mapping model_variant - kernel_tag, stability_grade, observed_seq_len_profile.n - fractional admission controller (fac): decides admission and slot sizing per incoming request. implements token-accounting (credits) per kernel_tag.n - kernel handshake protocol (khp): short rpc between scheduler and kernel container to request/return fractional slots, handshake includes kernel_hints and kernel_fidelity_flags.n - graceful fallback orchestrator: on admission failure or slo violation, reroutes to compatible kernel variant or reduces fidelity according to policy.nnscheduling model and contractsnn- request classes: realtime-critical, background-batch, best-effort-async. each class has a latency slo, credit refill rate, and eviction priority.n- slot size: logical unit (fraction) representing amortized token throughput and memory footprint. slot sizes are mapped to kernel categories (e.g., fp32-large, q4-small).n- preemption semantics: preemption is cooperative where possible. if kernel cannot yield (long-running large sequence generation), fac will avoid new admissions for lower-priority classes and use fallback routing. immediate preemption (hard kill) is reserved for safety-critical incidents and requires manual approval.nnkernel handshake protocol (khp) - message contractnn- handshake.request request_id, kernel_tag, required_slots, max_latency_ms, kvcache_hint n- handshake.accept allocation_id, granted_slots, preemption_token, expected_release_ms n- handshake.reject reason_code, suggested_fallback_tags n- release allocation_id, actual_duration_ms, observed_peak_mem_mb nnnote: khp messages are carried on the schedulers local rpc bus and annotated in traces. handshake defines fields but transport is protobuf-over-grpc in current implementation.nnadmission controller configuration (recommended defaults)nn parameter default description n------:---n realtime.credit_rate 500 credit/s refill rate for realtime routes n batch.credit_rate 200 credit/s refill rate for background batch n small-slot-mem-cap_mb 512 soft memory cap for q4-small category n large-slot-mem-cap_mb 16384 reserve for fp32-large n preemption.grace_ms 250 time to allow cooperative yield nnsample fac policy (yaml)nnnadmission_policies:n realtime:n min_slots: 2n max_concurrent: 600n credit_rate: 500n background:n min_slots: 0n max_concurrent: 200n credit_rate: 200nkernel_categories:n q4-small:n slot_mem_mb: 512n priority: 30n fp32-large:n slot_mem_mb: 16384n priority: 10nnnprofiling playbook (co-located kernels)nn1) objective: measure interference and performance coupling when two or more kernel variants run concurrently on the same physical gpu set.n2) inputs: production-like request traces (sequence distribution, prompt prefix patterns), representative models for each kernel variant, and noise traffic generator.n3) steps:n a) reserve a test gpu pool with identical hw to production.n b) deploy kernel variants with fac enabled and set deterministic credits (freeze refill rates).n c) start baseline: run single-kernel load for 30 minutes to capture baseline latency p50/p95/p99, gpu sm utilization, power, memory high-water mark.n d) add second kernel mix slowly using traffic ramping (10 increments) until steady state. collect traces.n e) run adversarial microbursts (3x normal qps for 60s) targeting the lower-priority kernel to validate eviction and fallback.n f) run a slot starvation injection where large-slot kernels hold allocations for longer than expected to validate fac backpressure behavior.nn4) telemetry to capture (metric names):n - runtime.admission.granted_slots_totaln - runtime.admission.rejected_by_fac_totaln - runtime.kernel.allocation_duration_ms (histogram)n - runtime.kernel.peak_mem_mbn - gpu.sm_util_pct (per device)n - runtime.latency.route..p50/p95/p99n - runtime.fallback.reroutes_totalnn5) success criteria:n - critical realtime routes: p95 within slo 10 overhead vs baseline.n - no memory ooms observed_peak_mem_mb slo 250ms for 5 minutes and reroute rate 5n- sev2: realtime p99 slo 250ms for 25 minutes or reroute rate between 15n- sev3: deployment or benchmark failures without immediate customer impactnnsev1 quick steps:n1) page oncall runtime/sre and kernel owner.n2) run quick diagnostics:n - curl -s jq .allocations_activen - content: summaryn-------nthis document defines the canonical telemetry schema emitted at the dispatch layer, describes the signal-decision mapping used by the runtime to enact fallbacks, and provides an operational playbook for on-call and engineering teams to diagnose and remediate dispatch-induced degradations. the intent is to ensure consistent instrumentation, make fallback triggers auditable, mattersn-----------------n- dispatch is the first decision point that affects latency, model fidelity, and per-token cost.n- inconsistent telemetry or opaque fallback decisions have caused missed slas and customer surprises in previous incidents.n- this playbook standardizes signals so automated escalation and incident playbooks can be deterministic.nntelemetry schema (dispatch dispatch queue (critical for tail latency).n- kernel_exec_time_ms: wall time of in-kernel execution. excludes queue timen- end_to_end_latency_ms: total time from http ingress to response commitn- prefetch_hit: whether a prefetcher predicted and warmed the kv cache for this sessionn- decision_trace: ordered list of decision checkpoints (useful for replay and audit)nnalerting thresholds and slo mappingsn-----------------------------------nwe maintain per-tenant and global slos. the dispatch layer maps signal anomalies to alerts and automated fallbacks. use the following baseline thresholds fallback policy eng-sre n kernel_queue_time_ms (p99) 50 ms 150 ms increase priority for pinned kernels enable hedging if persists 5m - fallback to compressed variant runtime n dispatch_decision rejected (rate) 0.5 2 backpressure review open incident if sustained 1m eng-sre n fallback_rate (tenant, 1m) 1 5 page product on degrading quality, run triage runtime/product n kv_cache_hit_rate slot-claim-timeout).n2) immediate mitigations (5--20 minutes)n a) if spike is caused by a specific kernel_id and thermal/host issues: mark kernel node as drain-candidate and migrate sessions (cli execution surface manual, content: purposennthis document defines the observability bridge: the cross-cutting contract between the serving runtime execution surface, kernel scheduler, and the observability/benchmarks systems. it is a practical manual for engineers who implement instrumentation, create profiling experiments, debug production slo regressions, and author synthetic terminologynn- execution surface: api boundary between the front-end request router and the per-gpu kernel worker. includes request metadata (route, priority, model-variant), session affinity hints, and requested qos profile.n- kernel epoch: a contiguous sequence of kernel launches that service a single logical request (can include kernel hedges, fallback kernels, and prefetch kernels).n- decision trace: a compact, append-only event bundle attached to each request that records scheduling choices, cache hits/misses, kernel variant selection, and routing fallbacks.n- observability bridge: the canonical set of telemetry artifacts (metrics, traces, event logs, binary samples) and the mapping rules from runtime artifacts to downstream stores (prometheus, jaeger/otel, clickhouse).nnobservability bridge: telemetry contractsnn1) minimal per-request trace model (otel-compatible)nn- required attributes (always present):n - request.id (string)n - request.route (string)n enqueuedispatchkernel_startkernel_endpostprocess)nn- important events (emit as spans or events inside the request trace):n - kvcache.hit / kvcache.miss (include shard_id and approximate latency_ms)n - kernel.selection (selected_variant, heuristics_triggered)n - kernel.hedge (hedge_target_ms)n - routing.fallback (reason_code, fallback_variant)n - admission.control (slot_granted, preemption_note)nn2)
