probabilistic and cost-aware. default policy: sample 0.1 of requests globally, 1 of requests in the 9599.9th latency percentile, and 100 of requests marked as incidents. captured artifacts: full trace, kernel microprofile (cuda cupti / rocm hsa), and model logits snapshot (first 64 tokens).nnmapping and retentionnn- mapping rules: traces - jaeger/otel counters/histograms - prometheus/thanos binary samples - clickhouse s3-backed archive with ttl 90 days for non-incident samples, 540 days for incident samples.nnkernel scheduler observability patternsnnmake scheduling decisions visible without exposing implementation internals:nn- annotate every kernel launch with kernel.metadata tags: slot_type (dedicatedburstpreemptible), kernel_priority, preemptible_till.n- emit scheduling decisions as events in the request trace with reason codes mapped to stable enum values.n- surface per-slot occupancy metrics with 1s resolution and 1m rollups.nnexample kernel decision trace (otel pseudo-json)nnn trace_id: ...,n spans: n name: request.dispatch, attributes: kernel.epoch_id: e-6bd3,n name: scheduler.decide, attributes: slot_type: preemptible, decision: queued, reason: compatibility dependency graph and safety orchestrator, content: summarynnthis document defines the scheduler compatibility dependency graph (scdg) and describes the safety orchestrator that enforces compatibility, graceful degradation, and safe rollouts between kernel variants, scheduler plugins, and runtime subsystems. it combines a static dependency model with dynamic runtime checks and an automation layer that performs remediation and controlled fallback.nnwhy this existsnn- kernels and scheduler plugins are evolving rapidly (new quantization paths, sparse-attention kernels, fractional residency modes). we need a machine-readable compatibility model to avoid accidental unsafe pairings.n- incidents historically involve combinations of kernel variants admission-controller policies that produce deadlocks, soft ooms, or priority inversion. the scdg lets automation surface risky pairings before they reach production.nnscope and assumptionsnn- space: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling and runtime-architecture operational surface.n- assumes per-cluster kernel metadata is available via kernel-manifest service (artifact: /artifacts/kernels).n- not a replacement for unit/interop tests it augments ci and runtime safety checks.nnkey conceptsnn1) node: a component (kernel, plugin, admission-controller, cache-manager). each node has attributes: name, semantic-version, capabilities, resource-profile, affinity-tags.n2) edge: a directional compatibility relation between nodes. edge metadata includes: compatibility-level (compatible advisory incompatible), min-version, known-issues-ref.n3) cohort: a small set of nodes commonly updated together (e.g., tensor-core-kernel-v2, prefetch-plugin-1.4). cohorts are used for canaries and rollback groups.n4) safety orchestrator: runtime daemon that consumes the scdg and enforces policy: rejects incompatible combos, synthesizes safe fallbacks, and coordinates rolling remediations.nndesign overviewnn- authoring: kernel owners publish node descriptors as yaml under kernel-manifest ci validates descriptor json schema.n- graph materialization: a scheduled job (scdg-builder) consolidates manifests from clusters, runs compatibility heuristics, and persists a canonical scdg snapshot to the metadata db.n- runtime enforcement: safety orchestrator subscribes to snapshots. on each model-serving slot allocation, it verifies requested kernel plugin pair against scdg. if advisory or incompatible, orchestrator applies configured policy (block warn-and-audit auto-fallback).n- telemetry: every verification emits a verification event (verif_id) with context: request_id, node-pair, compatibility-level, decision, and matched-cohort. these events feed the scheduler-telemetry pipeline.nncompatibility matrix (example table)nn component a component b min a ver min b ver compatibility action on incompatible cost_weight: 1.0nnn- note: events should be json-encoded when landing in structured logging systems they must also exist as compact binary in the tracing pipeline for high-cardinality sampling.nnrequired fields (text form): request_id, timestamp (iso8601), node (string), decision (string), reason_codes (list), latency_ms (number), cost_weight (number), input_signals (list).noptional but recommended: model_version, kernel_revision, tenant_id, route, sampled_trace_id.nn3. minimal telemetry to support common investigationsnnto triage scheduling issues within 515 playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook documents the predictive slotting and quota orchestration subsystem: an extension of the kernel-level scheduler that enforces per-customer slas while optimizing for cluster efficiency and cost. it is intended for runtime engineers, sres, and on-call responders responsible for scheduling, capacity planning, and incident triage.nngoalsnn- ensure tenant-level latency slos (p50/p95) are met with automated slot allocation and predictive adjustments.n- provide fairness across tenants while honoring reserved quotas (dedicated pools) and burstable capacity.n- reduce cold-start-related tail latency by pre-slotting based on forecasted request patterns.n- offer safe rollout and emergency rollback procedures for scheduler policy changes.nnscope and non-goalsnn- in-scope: kernel scheduling decisions, slot/quota bookkeeping, admission control, eviction policies, telemetry hooks, and runbook actions.n- out-of-scope: long-term capacity procurement, billing integration, and data-plane model weight placement (handled by the placement controller).nnkey terminologynn- slot: a logical reservation of gpu dispatch capacity for a tenant for a time window (e.g., 100ms quantum).n- quota: the steady-state allocation (tokens/sec or slots/min) assigned to a tenant.n- predictive slotting: proactively creating temporary slots based on short-term forecasts.n- soft-reserve: slots that can be preempted with a predefined grace window.n- hard-reserve: non-preemptible slots used by dedicated customers.nnarchitecture overviewnnthe subsystem sits between the admission controller and the kernel dispatcher. flow: request - request-classifier - admission controller (quota check predictive slot lookup) - slot allocator - dispatch queue - kernel.nndiagram (text):n- cluster nodes (gpu pool) - dispatcher clustern- control plane: forecasting service - quota-orchestrator - slot-index (consistent hash)n- telemetry: per-slot metrics - time-series db - anomaly detectornndecision matrix: when to create predictive slotsnn1) input signals:n - recent per-tenant qps (sliding 60s and 5m)n - sequence length distribution heatmap (recent window)n - kv-cache hit ratio trend for tenantn - announcement of scheduled traffic (customer webhooks)n2) heuristics and thresholds (example):n - if 60s qps quota 1.15 and predicted 3-min moving avg quota: create up to min(ceil(excess / slot_capacity), burst_cap).n - if kv hit ratio improving and tail latency stable - prefer soft-reserve slots for better multiplexing.nnpolicies and constraintsnn- hard-reserve tenants always get hard-reserve slots first predictive slotting does not create hard-reserve slots.n- total predictive slots per node limited to 25 of dispatch capacity by default (configurable).n- eviction priority: predictive soft-reserve predictive hard-reserve (if misconfigured) best-effort.n- maximum predictive slot lifetime: default 120s.nnpolicy config example (yaml)nnscheduler_policy: n default_predictive_window: 180 secondsn max_predictive_fraction_per_node: 0.25n slot_quantum_ms: 100n eviction_order: predictive_soft, predictive_hard, best_effortn per_tenant_overcommit_factor: 1.15nnpredictive algorithm (high-level)nn- input: timeseries x_t (qps), kv_hit_t, latency_t, historical pattern templates.n- forecast: use exponential smoothing recent pattern matching to produce 3-minute forecast f.n- decide: required_slots ceil(max(0, (f - quota) average_request_cost / slot_capacity)).n- rate-limit creations: only create n slots per 10s per node to avoid thrash.nnpseudocodenn1. window last 180s samplesn2. f forecast(window)n3. if f slo for 5m and predictive_slots_active 0 and eviction_rate 10/minn- sev3 if predictive_slot_fraction 0.4 on more than 3 nodes for 10mnnoperational runbook: common incidentsnn1) symptom: tenant experiences repeated quota_breach and 5xx errorsn - step 1: check tenant quota and recent qps (dashboard: tenant/overview).n - step 2: inspect predictive slot creation logs (control-plane job: quota-orchestrator).n - step 3: if orchestrator is not creating slots but qps is high - verify forecasting service health (service/forecast-service).n - step 4: for immediate mitigation, increase soft-reserve grace window or temporarily bump per_tenant_overcommit_factor for tenant via runtime flag.n - step 5: if 5xx persists, open incident and attach kernel dispatch traces.nn2) symptom: cluster-wide predictive thrash (rapid slot create/evict loops)n - step 1: disable predictive slotting globally: curl -xpost control/scheduler/flags -d predictive_enabled:false.n - step 2: revert to conservative static quotas and set max_predictive_fraction_per_node0.0.n - step 3: run a slow reenable with a 10 fraction and observe for 30m.nncanary rollout checklist (scheduler policy changes)nn1. code: ship feature gate behind runtime flag.n2. unit tests: synthetic forecast unit tests, eviction scenarios, and fairness invariants.n3. canary: enable on dev cluster - perf test with synthetic burst profile.n4. gradual roll: enable for 1 of production tenants with low-risk label for 1h, then 10 for 4h, 25 for 24h, 100 if metrics stable.n5. metrics to watch during canary: per-tenant p95, eviction_rate, predictive_slot_fraction, sequence throughput, and kernel queue depth.nnbenchmarking scenarios (for the perf-suite)nn- synthetic burst mix: 90 short sequences (1664 tokens), 10 long (512), varying qps spike from baseline to 5x for 60s.n- steady-state overcommit test: run at 120 aggregate quota for 30m and measure tail latency and fairness (jains index).n- cold-start alignment test: simulate cold kv caches to validate that predictive slotting reduces p99 tail by at least 15 compared to baseline.nnprofiling guidancenn- required traces: request timeline (classification - admission - slot allocation - dispatch - kernel start/stop), slot lifecycle events, kernel occupancy samples.n- use lightweight sampling at 1 in production 100 tracing during large canary windows.n- profiling targets: mean slot creation latency wavefront overcommit.n mitigation: add jittered backoff and inter-tenant dampening in the forecasting step cap cross-tenant slot creation rate.nn- issue: predictive slots can increase gpu fragmentation leading to slight throughput loss.n mitigation: enforce a defragmentation window where predictive slots are consolidated every 5 minutes measure via dispatch_utilization.nn- issue: misclassified request classes cause slot misuse (e.g., background eval traffic labeled as interactive).n mitigation: tighten classifier rules and add a sampling verifier that checks top-1 model id and path for mismatches.nnmaintenance and tuning guidancenn- quarterly: review per-tenant eviction trends and update per_tenant_overcommit_factor baseline.n- monthly: run fairness simulation from perf-suite and evaluate jains index target 0.95 for active tenants.n- after detection is ambiguous, the runtime falls back to generic profile selection.nn software stack assumptionsnvalidated on the following baseline (see perf suite artifacts for exact pins):n- cuda: 12.x linen- nvidia driver: 550 linen- runtime: runtime-1.18 (older releases may accept only a subset of keys)nn deployment modesnsupported in:n- hosted (fleet default per-pool overrides)n- dedicated scheduler.continuous_batching.enabled truen- scheduler.batch.max_batch_tokens (balanced: moderate throughput-first: higher)n- scheduler.queue.max_enqueued_requests (hard cap)n- request.output.completions..text, apply redact-patterns for email, phone, credit-card. example regex: (?:bd12,19b)(?:bw.-@w.-.a-za-z2,b).n2. high-cardinality dims: remove or hash values for fields tagged dim.cardinality.high (e.g., session_id, ephemeral_token). keep a 64-bit truncated hash for causal joins.n3. size capping: if span total bytes max-span-bytes, strip non-essential nested structures in this order: stack_traces - raw_payload - metrics_payload. add annotation: pruner.reasontruncated_size.n4. link preservation: when link-preserve-strategycompact-ids, replace (lts) strategy for the serving runtime and the policy for backporting fixes onto lts branches.nnthe lts channel exists to support dedicated and private customers who need a stable kernel scheduling baseline for 612 months with:n- predictable patch cadencen- clear eligibility criteria for backports (security/sev1/sev2)n- strong correctness performance gatesn- reproducible, auditable release artifactsnnthis policy is intentionally conservative: lts prioritizes stability and operational predictability over feature parity with main.nn---nn goalsn- provide an lts branch line (e.g., fork or divergent architecture.n- backporting new features, experimental performance optimizations, or large refactors.n- guaranteeing that lts includes every improvement that lands on main.nn---nn target customers and scopen who lts is forn- dedicated customers requiring predictable throughput/latency and planned change control.n- private (vpc/on-prem) customers with regulated environments, slower upgrade cycles, and audit requirements.nn where lts is consumedn- hosted: lts may be available as an opt-in runtime track for qualifying customers, but hosted generally rolls forward more frequently. release line.n- lts branch: a release branch cut from a mainline minor release and supported for a longer window (example: runtime-1.18-lts).n- patch release: incremental updates on an lts branch (example tag: 1.18.1-lts).n- backport: applying a fix that landed on mainline onto the lts branch via cherry-pick (or minimal equivalent change).n- sev1/sev2: severity definitions aligned with sre debuggable (explicit selection logic, metrics, logs).n- prevent silent drift between runtime defaults and shipped profile packs (normalized defaults compatibility constraints).nnthis is a design reference for implementation in runtime-config and the profile loader.nn---nn goalsn1. define a profile pack format with versioning and a stable schema.n2. support inheritance/overrides to minimize duplication (common base gpu family sku mode).n3. define hardware detection inputs and normalization rules (including mig/multi-gpu edge cases).n4. provide compatibility rules against:n - runtime releases (min/max supported runtime version)n - build capabilities (compiled features)n - driver/cuda constraints (esp. b200 early enablement)n - deployment mode constraints (hosted/dedicated/private)n5. define guardrails (validation, safe ranges, required invariants) and a fallback strategy.nn non-goalsn- introducing new kernels from scratch.n- customer-specific bespoke tuning logic (handled via support/solutions using supported overrides).n- api surface changes to inference endpoints.nn---nn terminologyn- profile pack: a versioned bundle containing one or more profiles plus metadata.n- profile: named set of configuration values for runtime scheduling/kernels/memory behavior.n- selector: rules that determine when a profile is eligible (gpu sku, driver, runtime, deployment mode).n- effective config: resolved runtime config after selection inheritance overrides.n- override sources: fleet default, per-pool, per-deployment (helm), per-route, environment variables (see adr for precedence).nn---nn design principlesn1. explicit compatibility best-effort magicn - profiles must declare the runtime versions and environment assumptions they are compatible with.n2. guardrails are enforced at runtime startupn - invalid profiles must not partially apply.n3. selection is deterministicn - given the same node/runtime inputs and the same pack, selection returns the same profile.n4. safe fallback pathn - if selection/validation fails, runtime falls back to known-safe defaults (or a base profile), and emits actionable logs/metrics.nn---nn profile pack structuren filesna pack is a directory or archive containing:n- pack.json (metadata index)n- profiles/.json (individual profiles)n- optional readme.md (human-readable)nn pack metadata (pack.json)nrequired fields (all strings unless noted):n- schema_version: semantic version of the pack schema (e.g., 1.1.0).n- pack_version: semantic version of the pack content (e.g., 2026.02.0).n- release_channel: stable beta experimental.n- generated_at: iso date.n- profiles: list of profile file names.n- default_profile: name of the safe base profile (e.g., base/default).nnnotes:n- schema_version gates parsing. runtime must reject unsupported schema major versions.n- pack_version gates rollouts/rollback and observability.nn---nn profile schemanprofiles are json documents with:n1) identity documentationn2) selector (eligibility) rulesn3) inheritancen4) config payload (scheduler/kernel/memory/etc.)n5) guardrailsnn top-level fieldsn field type required notes n---------:---n name string yes globally unique within the pack (e.g., h100/balanced). n description string yes human-readable summary and intended workload envelope. n profile_version string yes semver increments when semantics change. n inherits_from list of strings no ordered list later parents override earlier parents. n selector object (json) yes see selector section used to determine eligibility and priority. n compatibility object (json) yes runtime/build/driver constraints. n config object (json) yes actual tuning knobs key-space is versioned by runtime. n guardrails object (json) yes validation rules and invariants enforced by loader. n deprecations object (json) no migration info for keys planned for removal. nnimplementation note: although selector, compatibility, config, and guardrails are structured objects, they remain json objects in-file validation happens via the runtimes json schema custom validators.nn---nn inheritance modelninheritance is intended to reduce duplication and make it obvious which knobs differ by sku.nn rulesn1. inherits_from is an ordered list.n - resolution order: apply first parent next parent this profile.n2. cycles are rejected.n3. a profile may override a key by setting it to a new value.n4. key deletion is supported only via explicit tombstone:n - __delete__ sentinel for specific namespaces (restricted see guardrails).nn recommended inheritance hierarchyn- base/defaultn- gpu-family/hopper (h100)n- sku/h100-sxm vs sku/h100-pcie (only when materially different)n- mode/balanced vs mode/throughput-firstnnwe prefer fewer levels and avoid per-instance-type profiles unless required (hardware variance handled via guardrails and detection normalization).nn---nn selector: eligibility prioritynselection chooses the best eligible profile given node/runtime facts.nn inputs available to selectionn- gpu facts (via nvml / device properties):n - gpu.vendor (must be nvidia for this pack)n - gpu.arch (e.g., hopper, blackwell)n - gpu.sku_normalized (e.g., h100-sxm, h100-pcie, b200-sxm, l40s)n - gpu.memory_gbn - gpu.is_mig and mig slice info (if applicable)n - gpu.countn- software facts:n - runtime.version (e.g., 1.24.3)n - runtime.build_features (compiled capabilities)n - cuda.version, driver.versionn- deployment facts:n - deployment.mode: hosted dedicated privaten - deployment.pool (hosted/dedicated) or deployment.cluster_name (private)n - regionnn selector fieldsn field type required notes n---------:---n match.gpu_skus list of strings yes normalized skus supports only for base profiles. n match.deployment_modes list of strings yes one or more of hosted/dedicated/private. n match.mig string no allowed disallowed required. default: allowed. n priority integer yes higher wins if multiple profiles match. n rollout_tag string no for staged rollouts (e.g., b200-experimental). nn tie-breakingnif multiple eligible profiles have the same priority, select the profile with:n1) more specific sku match (exact family alias wildcard)n2) higher profile_version (semver compare)n3) lexicographic name (stable determinism)nnif still ambiguous, emit profile_selection_ambiguous and fall back to pack.default_profile.nn---nn compatibility rulesnprofiles must declare compatibility the loader enforces it at startup and on reload.nn compatibility fieldsn field type required notes n---------:---n runtime.min_version string yes inclusive semver. n runtime.max_version string no inclusive semver recommended when keys are removed/behavior changes. n runtime.required_features list of strings no build feature flags (e.g., kv_cache_budgeting). n cuda.min_version string no if set, enforce. n driver.min_version string no if set, enforce. n known_incompatible list of strings no human-readable reasons/conditions emitted in logs/metrics when detected. n maturity string yes stable beta experimental. nn enforcement behaviorn- if maturityexperimental, runtime must require an explicit enable (feature flag or allowlist) depending on deployment mode:n - hosted: allowlist by pool/regionn - dedicated: allowlist by pooln - private: explicit helm value runtime flagn- if compatibility checks fail:n 1) loader marks the profile ineligible.n 2) selection proceeds to next best profile.n 3) if none eligible, fall back to pack.default_profile.nn runtime release compatibility strategyn- we pin profiles to runtime minors to avoid silent semantics changes in knobs.n- default stance:n - runtime.min_version is the first runtime minor where the profile keys are fully supported.n - runtime.max_version is optional but should be set for experimental/b200 profiles until stabilized.nn---nn hardware detection and normalizationnprofile matching uses a normalized sku string. detection must be robust across providers and driver string variants.nn detection sources (ordered)n1. nvml device name pci device id (preferred)n2. nvidia-smi -q parsing fallbackn3. cloud metadata (instance type) only as a last resortnn normalized sku strings (current)n- h100-sxmn- h100-pcien- b200-sxmn- l40snn normalization rulesn- trim vendor prefixes/suffixes and normalize separators:n - e.g., nvidia h100 80gb hbm3 h100-sxm or h100-pcie based on pci id / form factor hintn- memory-based disambiguation is allowed only as a guardrail, not as the primary signal.nn mign- profiles may specify match.mig.n- default behavior:n - if mig is enabled and match.migdisallowed, the profile is ineligible.n - if mig is enabled and no mig-specific profile matches, fallback to base.nn multi-gpu nodesn- profile selection is per runtime process (not per device). if a node has heterogeneous gpus, selection is considered ambiguous and must fall back unless:n - a dedicated heterogeneous profile exists with explicit match rules.nn---nn config payload namespacesnconfig is logically namespaced the runtimes config registry defines allowed keys and value types.nn current namespaces (v1.x runtime)n- scheduler.n - continuous batching knobs, prefill/decode fairness, queue limits, backpressure thresholdsn- kernels.n - kernel auto-selection toggles, seq-len bucket boundaries, attention implementation selectionn- memory.n - kv-cache budgets, fragmentation mitigation, admission controln- collectives. (optional)n - nccl/collectives tuning for multi-gpu configurations (only when supported)n- cpu_runtime.n - thread pools, pinning hints, serialization overhead controlsnn key constraintsn- only keys registered in the runtime config registry may appear.n- keys are annotated with:n - supported runtime versionsn - safe rangesn - whether they are freezable (safe to pin per sku)nn---nn guardrailsnguardrails are enforced during profile resolution and again after all overrides are applied.nn guardrails fieldsn field type required notes n---------:---n limits.max_batch_tokens integer yes hard cap prevents runaway batching. n limits.max_concurrency integer yes hard cap per runtime instance. n kv_cache.max_fraction_of_gpu_mem number yes 0.00.95 ensures headroom for activations/fragmentation. n queue.max_depth integer yes admission control. n latency_slo_intent string yes balanced throughput_first latency_first used for dashboards review. n disallow_keys list of strings no keys that must not be set by this profile. n require_keys list of strings no keys that must be set (prevents partially-specified profiles). n invariants list of strings no named checks implemented in code (e.g., prefill_fairness_nonzero). nn examples of invariants (implemented checks)n- prefill_fairness_nonzero: prefill/decode fairness parameter must be 0 for streaming-enabled routes.n- kv_cache_budget_le_activation_headroom: enforce kv cache budget leaves at least x gib headroom.n- queue_limits_consistent: queue depth and backpressure thresholds are consistent and non-negative.nn startup behavior on guardrail failuresn- if a guardrail fails after applying all overrides:n 1) emit profile_guardrail_violation with which key and which source overrode it.n 2) if violation is hard (oom risk / invalid type / negative threshold), runtime refuses to start in dedicated/private and auto-falls back in hosted (configurable by pool policy).n 3) if violation is soft (performance risk), runtime starts but annotates metrics and logs.nn---nn override compatibility (post-resolution)noverrides are a feature they must remain supportable.nn policyn- some keys are pinnable via profile but not overridable by downstream sources (to prevent unsafe customer configs).n- some keys are overridable but bounded.n- some keys are adaptive-only and must not be set in a profile.nnthe runtime config registry carries these annotations the loader enforces them when applying overrides.nn override precedencensee adr: adr-hardware-tuning-profiles-distribution-and-override-order.nnthis docs requirement: override source must be visible in logs/metrics for each effective key that deviates from the selected profile.nn---nn versioning and deprecationn versionsn- schema_version: pack schema (breaking changes only on major bump)n- pack_version: content release version (rollout/rollback unit)n- profile_version: semantics of a single profilenn deprecation strategyn1. mark keys deprecated in the runtime registry with:n - deprecation runtime versionn - suggested replacementn2. loader emits warnings when a profile sets deprecated keys.n3. after 2 runtime minors, deprecated keys become errors (unless explicitly allowlisted for private backcompat).nn---nn observability requirementsnthe runtime must expose the following at minimum:n- metric: runtime_profile_selectedname, pack_version, profile_version, maturity (gauge 1)n- metric: runtime_profile_override_appliedkey, source (counter)n- metric: runtime_profile_ineligibleprofile, reason (counter)n- startup log event: effective compatibility matrix (runtime version, pack version, selected profile, driver/cuda)n- debug endpoint (auth-gated): returns effective config sources guardrail statusnnthese are required for oncall triage and for perf-canary segmentation.nn---nn deployment mode compatibilityn hostedn- profiles are applied by fleet defaults per-pool overrides are supported.n- on incompatibility, fallback to base profile automatically (pool policy) to prioritize availability.nn dedicatedn- profiles are applied by pool defaults customer-specific overrides must remain within bounded knobs.n- on hard guardrail violation, fail closed (do not silently start with unsafe config).nn privaten- profiles shipped either baked into runtime or mounted via helm values (per adr).n- private environments must be able to:n - pin pack_versionn - dump effective confign - disable profile selection and use runtime defaultsnn---nn example (illustrative)nbelow is an illustrative profile showing the intended structure (names and keys are representative).nnjsonnn name: h100/balanced,n description: h100 dsid_783bf49cab374602ae2d7cb4a85d3181, source_type: confluence, title: runtime coordinator and hardware affinity playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook documents the runtime coordinator (rcd) component and the hardware-affinity model used to bind inference requests to physical accelerator resources. it covers architecture rationale, scheduler integration, kernel hinting, profiling recipes, benchmarking guidance, release notes for the coordinator v1.3.0, operational runbooks, and a short known-issues catalog. it is intended for runtime engineers, sres, and performance-focused ml engineers who operate hybrid gpu pools (mixed vram / nvlink topologies) and want predictable latency/cost tradeoffs.nngoalsn-----n- provide a deterministic affinity model that preserves tail-latency slos while improving throughput and utilization.n- make kernel-selection and device placement decisions observable and reversible.n- offer repeatable profiling and benchmarking guidance so changes to affinity heuristics can be validated.n- provide clear runbook actions for common failure modes related to affinity and coordinator decisions.nnquick summary of decisionsn--------------------------n- affinity is scored using a weighted vector: (topological proximity, free_memory_fraction, current_kernel_compat_score, recent_error_rate). we bias toward proximity if expected sequence length 512 tokens.n- the runtime coordinator exposes a declarative affinity-profile per deployment that can be tuned (e.g., latency-first, cost-first, isolation-first).n- kernel hinting metadata travels with the request header (x-runtime-kernel-hint) and is used to pick precompiled kernels fallback path is explicit and logged.nnarchitecture and data flown--------------------------n1) ingress receives request - classifier extracts route, model, latency tier, and expected sequence length.n2) coordinator consults the affinity engine to rank candidate devices.n3) coordinator requests a kernel reservation from kernel broker for the scored device.n4) if kernel reservation succeeds, the request is dispatched if not, coordinator tries the next device or triggers fallback routing policy.nnkey componentsn- runtime coordinator (rcd): decision engine implementing affinity policies, placement scoring, and escalation/fallback logic.n- affinity engine: in-memory topology graph historical metrics (eviction rates, kernel success).n- kernel broker: lease manager for in-memory kernels and residency state (hot / warmed / cold).n- device telemetry adapter: exposes device metrics (mem, temperature, pcie bandwidth) into the affinity engine.nnaffinity model and scoringn-------------------------nscoring vector (each normalized 0..1):n- topology_proximity (0.5 weight): 1.0 for gpu on same numa socket nvlink 0.6 for same server different numa 0.2 for different host.n- free_memory_fraction (0.25 weight): fraction free after reserving estimated kv cache prompt payload.n- kernel_compat_score (0.15 weight): historical success ratio for model-variant quantization combo.n- recent_error_rate (0.10 weight, inverted): recent failure rate (lower is better).nnfinal score weighted_sum ties broken by lru of last_use_timestamp to improve locality.nnaffinity profiles (examples)n- latency-first: topology_proximity0.8, free_memory0.1, kernel_compat0.05, errors0.05n- cost-first: topology_proximity0.2, free_memory0.3, kernel_compat0.3, errors0.2n- isolation-first: prefers devices with low cross-tenant memory usage, adds 0.2 safety bonus to devices with isolation flags set.nnscheduler integration and kernel handoffn--------------------------------------n- the rcd integrates with the global scheduler using a lightweight rpc (grpc) interface: allocatedevice(request_meta) - devicelease. devicelease includes device_id, kernel_hint, lease_ttl_ms.n- kernels are loaded lazily. kernel broker supports two strategies: optimistic prefetch (load on ranking) and conservative (load on assignment). use optimistic for latency-first profiles and conservative for cost-first.n- handshake sequence (simplified):n 1. rcd - kernel broker: reserve kernel on device xn 2. kernel broker - device agent: pin kernel and return success/failuren 3. if success, rcd marks device as reserved and dispatches request otherwise rcd increments kernel_compat_bad counter and retries.nnkernel hinting and contractn--------------------------n- requests may carry an x-runtime-kernel-hint header: format model:variant:quantization. the coordinator uses this to prefer kernels but validates compatibility.n- kernel broker exposes kernel metadata: kernel_id, compiled_for_sm, quantized_bits, expected_workspace_bytes.n- compatibility rules: compiled_for_sm must match device.sm_family or kernel is marked multi-sm compatible. workspace_bytes 95th percentile).n- step 3: if kernel stalls appear on specific sm families, collect ncu --target-processesall to inspect tensor core utilization and register spilling.nn2) pcie / host-side stallsn- step 1: inject a synthetic heavy-kv-evict workload using the benchmark harness (see benchmarking guidance) across co-tenants in a staging cluster.n- step 2: collect perf counters on the host pcie root port: perf record -e pci: and cross-correlate with device telemetry.nn3) end-to-end latency attributionn- use the runtimes correlator to produce a waterfall trace. if kernel handoff retries are 1 of requests, the coordinator is a dominant contributor.nnbenchmarking guidance (how to validate changes)n------------------------------------------------ngoals: validate slos (p50/p95/p99), kernel success rates, and cost per token under representative mixes.nnbenchmark steps:n1. build synthetic workload with sequence-length distribution matching production (we provide a corpus builder tool: workload-corpus-gen).n2. run three profile passes: micro (single-gpu), rack (topology-aware, nvlink present), cluster (mixed types). each pass should run 30 minutes minimum for stable percentiles.n3. metrics to collect: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, device_multiprogramming_index (dmi).n4. validation gates: any change that increases p99 by 7 or kernel_fallback_rate by 0.5pp must be blocked and reviewed.nnsample benchmark command (example)nnbenchmark-runner --corpus /bench/corpora/seq-dist-512.json --parallelism 200 --profile rack --out /tmp/bench-rcd-202609nnnconfiguration table (recommended defaults)n----------------------------------------n config_key default notes n affinity.profile latency-first can be overridden per-tenant n coordinator.max_retries 3 kernel reservation retries before fallback n kernelbroker.prefetch optimistic set to conservative for cost-first experiments n coordinator.lease_ttl_ms 8000 typical request ttl tune for longer generation workloads n affinity.topo_bias_threshold 0.12 minimum score delta to prefer topology nnrelease notes (rcd v1.3.0)n-------------------------n- new: affinity profiles (latency/cost/isolation) configurable per-tenant.n- new: kernel hint header support and explicit fallback logging.n- improvement: kernel broker prefetch heuristics reduce p99 by 6 in mixed nvlink racks (internal benchmark).n- fix: prevented a race where two rcd instances double-reserved the same kernel after a lease renew failure.nnoperational runbook: affinity-related incidentsn----------------------------------------------nincident type a: sudden p99 regression with high kernel_fallback_raten1. detect: alert when kernel_fallback_rate 0.5 for 10m and p99 baseline 7.n2. immediate mitigation: switch tenant to conservative affinity profile (api call: post /v1/tenants/id/affinity?actionswitchprofileconservative).n3. if mitigation fails: drain the affected device pool using the schedulers drain api and route new requests to fallback pool.n4. postmortem: collect traces, kernel broker logs, and device telemetry for the 30 minutes before incident.nnincident type b: device-level oom during assignmentn1. detect: device telemetry shows sudden free_memory_fraction drop and kernel_compat_score falls to 0.n2. mitigate: immediately revoke leases to the device (rcd - kernel-broker revoke) and trigger eviction script: rcdctl evict --device id --grace 120s.n3. recovery: reimage device agent if oom persists after eviction escalate to hw team if host-level memory errors persist.nnincident type c: pcie saturation causing multi-tenant latency spikesn1. detect: host_pcie_util 85 correlated with crostalk in tenant latencies.n2. mitigate: reduce parallelism for co-located tenants via token-based admission: rcdctl set-parallelism --tenant id --value 0.6 (reduces allowed concurrent slots).nnknown issues (short catalog)n---------------------------n- pcie-root-port-saturation-eviction(2026-07): observed when large kv cache flushes are scheduled simultaneously with cross-host prefetch. mitigation: stagger prefetch windows and apply host-level preemption.n- ephemeral-kernel-compile-time-deadlock(2026-03): rare deadlock in the kernel compilation pool leading to stalls when two incompatible quantization requests race. workaround: restart kernel-broker service patch in v1.3.1 planned.n- nvlink-failover-delay(2025-11): nvlink path failover can add 13ms to p95 during hardware link reconfiguration translated into affinity score jitter. we added smoothing in the scoring logic to avoid thrash.nnsignals and slos to watchn------------------------n- slos: p50 pack - execute - commit - cleanup.n- each wave carries a wave id (uuid), priority class (low/normal/high), and waveform hints (expected sequence length, kv-cache affinity, quantization tag).n- waves may be single-tenant or multi-tenant depending on affinity and isolation constraints.nnarchitecture componentsn-----------------------n- wave controller (service): creates and coordinates waves per gpu node. runs in the runtime control plane.n- kernel coordinator (in-runtime agent): local to each gpu process, executes the waveform phases and enforces packing and fairness.n- wave metadata bus (lightweight pub/sub): transports wave lifecycle events (wave-start, pack-complete, exec-complete) to telemetry and tracing.n- admission shim: lightweight hook at request enqueue time that emits waveform hints and slo tags.nnscheduling primitives and contractsn---------------------------------n1. slot promises: a kernel can promise a time-limited slot to the wave controller when it has partial readiness (e.g., token prefix loaded). the promise includes expected slot duration and token budget.n2. cooperative preemption token: short consensus token to allow higher-priority waves to reclaim unused slots during pack phase (fast-path only).n3. quiesce boundary: kernels must implement a quiesce handler to checkpoint the kv cache pointer and return consistent partial outputs on preemption.nnwave orchestration lifecycle (detailed)n-------------------------------------n1) preparen - admission shim validates hints and annotates the request.n - wave controller assigns preliminary wave id and target node(s) based on affinity and slos.n - telemetry: emit wave.prep.wave_id.n2) packn - kernel coordinator gathers ready kernels and evaluates pack candidates using waveform hint heuristics.n - pack decision includes which kernels will run together and estimated duration.n - telemetry: emit wave.pack.wave_id with pack composition and estimated duration.n3) executen - kernels execute with coordinated start. micro-batching may be performed only if all kernels meet packing constraints.n - cooperative preemption may be triggered if a higher-priority wave claims slots.n - telemetry: wave.exec.wave_id including per-kernel timing and kernel ids.n4) commitn - outputs are merged, cache pointers advanced per-tenant quotas updated.n5) cleanupn - memory and ephemeral allocations released pack accounting updated.nnobservability contract (what to emit)n------------------------------------n- required events: wave.created, wave.pack_attempt, wave.pack_commit, wave.exec_start, wave.exec_end, wave.preempt_request, wave.preempt_granted, wave.cleanup_complete.n- each event must include: wave_id, node_id, kernel_id(s), priority, estimated_duration_ms, actual_duration_ms, pack_reason (latency/cost/affinity), and a diagnostic tag.n- correlate with existing traces: append wave_id to the request trace root.nnconfig knobs (table)n--------------------n name default description operator guidance n wave.max_pack_size 8 max kernels in a single pack start at default, tune downward for high tail latency n wave.max_pack_latency_ms 8 max time to wait while assembling a pack lower to prioritize latency increase for better efficiency n wave.priority_strictness medium how strongly controller prefers higher-priority waves set to high for slo-critical clusters n wave.coop_preempt_window_ms 2 time window where cooperative preemption can be claimed during pack keep small to minimize instability n wave.kv_affinity_threshold 0.7 confidence threshold to colocate wave with warm kv cache use 0.8 for latency-sensitive traffic nnexample pack decision pseudocoden-------------------------------nn// simplified pack selection logicncandidates gather_ready_kernels()nscore(candidate) affinity_score0.6 priority_score0.3 - est_duration0.1nselected top_k(candidates, wave.max_pack_size, score)nif max_est_duration(selected) wave.max_pack_latency_ms: fallback_to_singleton()nnnsafe degradation and fallbacksn------------------------------n- if pack assembly time exceeds wave.max_pack_latency_ms, controller falls back to executing available kernels immediately (singletons).n- if cooperative preemption fails repeatedly for 3 waves in 60s for a node, disable pack on that node for 60s (circuit breaker).n- if observed 95th latency increases by 20 after a rollout, rollback the new controller and enable conservative packing config.nnrunbook: investigating long pack timesn-------------------------------------n1. alert triggers: packing_latency.node 99th percentile threshold for 5m.n2. triage steps:n a) query last 10 wave.pack_attempt events for the node: composition, estimated vs actual durations.n b) check node gpu utilization and dispatch queue lengths (node/gpu/id/utilization, dispatch.queue.length).n c) verify kv-cache hit ratio for packed kernels low affinity increases waiting.n d) if packing contention due to small kernels, reduce wave.max_pack_size or increase priority_strictness.n3. mitigation:n - temporarily set wave.max_pack_latency_ms to 3ms for high-priority traffic.n - trigger node-level pack-disable circuit breaker if pack attempts 100 and mean wait 15ms.n4. postmortem: record root cause, pack composition, and correlate with traffic mix.nnbenchmarks and validation strategyn---------------------------------n- microbenchmarks: synthetic mixes of (short, medium, long) sequences at concurrencies 10, 50, 200 measuring p50/p95/p99 for token latency and per-token gpu cycles.n- a/b rollout: shadow ckwo with pack disabled for 24h compare cost-per-token and tail latency. staged rollout matrix described below.nnrollout plan and metricsn-----------------------n1) canary (5 traffic, internal customers): run ckwo controller in parallel mode (no-enforce) for 48h. monitor wave packing ratio and tail latency.n2) limited summary:nnthis playbook describes the adaptive kernel mapper (akm) and associated capacity-scaling procedures used by the redwood serving runtime to dynamically select execution kernels and right-size gpu capacity for diverse llm workloads. the akm is a runtime component that maps model characteristics and live workload signals to a kernel/quantization/placement profile and triggers scale decisions or fallback policies when thresholds are crossed.nnpurpose and scope:n- document how the akm makes decisions (inputs, scoring, policies).n- provide concrete configuration examples and cli commands for ops.n- prescribe runbook procedures for performance regressions and capacity incidents.n- link to profiling and benchmarking artifacts used to tune akm heuristics.nnintended audience:n- serving runtime engineers (primary)n- sre and capacity plannersn- model onboarding and perf benchmarking teamsnnkey concepts (brief):n- kernel candidate: a specific combination of operator implementation (cuda/cublas/cutlass), data type/quantization (fp16/int8), and fusion knobs.n- profile: measured perf/latency/cost numbers for a model sequence length distribution batch shape.n- cost-utility score: composite metric combining tokens/sec (throughput), p95 latency, and estimated cloud cost per token.n- mapping policy: a set of rules that prefer lower-latency kernels for low-concurrency, and higher-throughput kernels for high-concurrency.nnarchitecture overview:n1) telemetry inputs to akm:n - model metadata: architecture family, layer count, head size, weight dtype (fp32/ptq/q4).n - rollouts.nnscoring function example (pseudo):n score w1 norm(tokens_per_sec) - w2 norm(p95_latency) - w3 norm(cost_per_token)nweights (w1..w3) are configurable per customer tier (e.g., enterprise source_type: confluence, title: predictive warmstart and cache-hinting architecture for low-latency serving, content: summary:nthis document defines the predictive warmstart and cache-hinting architecture (pwc architecture) designed to reduce observable tail latency and cold-start variability for multi-tenant model serving. the design couples an inference-side predictive planner with the kv-cache prefetcher and the runtimes kernel scheduler to proactively populate hot state and shape scheduling hints based on traffic predictions.nngoals_and_non_goals:ngoals:n- reduce 95th and 99th percentile request latency for cold or low-traffic model variants by pre-populating kv caches and tensor allocator state before request arrival.n- provide a low-risk canary and rollout path that can be throttled per-customer or per-model.n- expose telemetry for cost vs latency trade-offs and enable automated tuning.nnon-goals:n- this design does not replace hardware-level warmup that requires model weight preloading. it focuses on runtime-level warmstart (kv cache, allocator priming, kernel hints) and workload-level caching policies.nnscope:napplies to: hosted and dedicated runtime pools where multi-tenant scheduling and kv-cache are active.nout of scope: on-prem private deployments with strict air-gapped constraints unless customer opts in deep model weight transformer warmups that require offline preparation.nnbackground_and_motivation:noperational observations (2024-q4 to 2025-q2) showed that mixed workloads with bursty conversational sessions produce repeated cold-like tails: small sessions that skip cache priming cause disproportionate tail-latency spikes and gpu kernel mispredictions. existing approaches (heuristic ttl-based caching, on-request prefetch) either over-provision memory or introduce request-time overhead. predictive warmstart aims to move the decision upstream to a planner that learns short-term traffic patterns and coordinates safe prefetches.nnarchitecture_overview:nhigh level components:n- predictive planner: time-series and event predictor that emits warmstart candidates (tenant, model, session signature, ttl recommendation).n- cache hint broker: lightweight control plane that accepts predictions and converts them into cache-prefetch jobs and kernel-hint annotations.n- prefetch worker (on-node): receives jobs, enqueues kv-cache prefetch, tensor allocator prime, and lightweight kernel micro-benchmarks to touch critical code paths.n- scheduler integration layer: exposes a hint api that the kernel scheduler uses to preferentially schedule warmstart jobs during free slots and to avoid starving priority traffic.n- telemetry and cost estimator: aggregates prefetch effectiveness and cost (tokens, memory, kernel time) for feedback to planners policy optimizer.nndata_flow_and_interactions:n1) runtime telemetry (session arrives, token distribution, model variant) flows to the planner via a time-series ingestion stream (kafka topic: runtime.session.signals).n2) the planner produces candidate warmstart events in the pwc.candidates topic. each event has: tenant_id, model_id, signature_hash, preferred_node_affinity, estimated_score, ttl_seconds. example payload (json): n tenant_id: cust-123,n model_id: redwood-v2-small,n signature_hash: sha256:abcd...,n preferred_node: poola-6,n score: 0.78,n ttl: 120n.n3) cache hint broker validates, rate-limits, and enqueues prefetch worker jobs.n4) prefetch worker issues prefetch calls to the local kv-cache api, primes allocators (page-touch) and runs microkernel invocations with a capped budget.n5) scheduler uses annotation flags on these jobs to schedule during slack periods if server load exceeds threshold, prefetch jobs are evicted gracefully and rescheduled.nnprefetch_and_warmstart_algorithms:ncore heuristics and policies:n- scoring function: score alpha recency_score beta session_prob gamma model_cost_factor - delta mem_pressure_penalty. we empirically set alpha0.5, beta0.3, gamma0.15, delta0.05 for initial rollout.n- signature selection: prefer shortest canonical token prefix that maximizes reuse prefer session-level signatures for chat workloads, request-level signatures for retrieval/embedding workloads.n- budgeting: each node has a prefetch budget (cpu_millis, gpu_ms, mem_mb) and a soft_cost_limit. prefetch jobs are charged to the originating tenants cost center.n- ttl adaptation: if repeated hits observed, ttl is extended multiplicatively up to an upper cap (configurable). if misses exceed a threshold within window w, the planner reduces score for that signature.nnnode_level_components:nprefetch worker responsibilities:n- kv-cache prefetch api call example: post /internal/kvcache/prefetch n model: redwood-v2-small,n signature: ,n context: the users last message summary...nn- allocator prime: touch pages and pre-allocate gpu tensors of expected size. cli helper: runtime-prime --model redwood-v2-small --tensor-shape 1x2048 --budget-ms 20.n- microkernel probe: run a 5-10ms inference warm call with deterministic random seed using quantized path where applicable.nnotes: prefetch operations must be idempotent and safe on repeated application.nnscheduler_integration_and_fallbacks:nintegration points:n- hint api: schedule.hint_register(job_id, priority_hint, preferred_window_ms).n- admission control: scheduler consults node prefetch_budget and current load. if cpu or gpu util 75, hints are deprioritized.nfallbacks:n1) if prefetch failed due to mem pressure, mark signature as expensive and reduce planner score for 10 minutes.n2) if kernel microbenchmark reveals slow path on a variant, the runtime will annotate model_variant as compat_slow and planner will prefer alternative variant ids for warmstarts.nnslo_cost_and_configuration_table:nconfiguration key/value (presented as a table in prose):n- pref.max_concurrent_prefetch_per_node: 8 (integer) - maximum concurrent prefetch jobs on a node.n- pref.cpu_budget_millis_per_min: 5000 (ms) - cpu budget per node per minute.n- pref.gpu_budget_ms_per_min: 300 (ms) - gpu warmstart budget per node per minute.n- pref.kv_prefetch_ttl_default_s: 60 (seconds) - default ttl for prefetch entries.n- pref.score_threshold: 0.6 (0-1) - planner emits only scores threshold.nslo/target metrics to track: 95th token latency (-10 target vs baseline), 99th token latency (-5 target), prefetch success hit rate 70 for emitted jobs, prefetch cost per saved-latency ms under configured cost cap.nntelemetry_and_observability:nrequired telemetry (exported to metrics and traces):n- metric: pwc.prefetch.emitted_total (labels: tenant, model, node, variant)n- metric: pwc.prefetch.hit_total (labels identical)n- metric: pwc.prefetch.cpu_ms_consumedn- metric: pwc.prefetch.gpu_ms_consumedn- trace: pwc.candidate.lifecycle (events: created, broker_validated, dispatched, completed, evicted)n- logs: prefetch-worker info/error with structured fields (tenant_id, model_id, signature_hash, reason)ndashboards to create:n- prefetch efficiency: hit/emit over 1h/24h windowsn- node budget exhaustion confluence, title: tp stability fixes (multi-gpu) design: hang taxonomy, root causes, and runtime hardening plan, content: summaryntensor-parallel (tp) replicas (28 gpus per replica) are now the dominant mode for our largest dedicated clusters and several high-throughput hosted workloads. under sustained mixed load (prefill decode, long context, bursty concurrency, client cancels), we have observed failure modes that manifest as:n- silent stalls (no progress, gpus appear busy or idle, requests hang)n- downstream request timeouts (streaming or non-streaming)n- autoscaling thrash due to inflated p99/p999n- occasional sev1 incidents requiring draining/replacing replicasnnthis document proposes a targeted hardening plan focused on correctness stability (not a tp architecture rewrite), with an emphasis on:n1) a clear taxonomy of stall/hang signaturesn2) concrete root-cause hypotheses mapped to instrumentation and fixesn3) scheduler and comms-boundary changes that reduce the probability of deadlocksn4) safe failure semantics (watchdogs abort/drain) to prevent indefinite hangsn5) a rollout strategy with guardrails and regression coveragenn goals / non-goalsn goalsn- eliminate known hang/timeouts in tp execution under load.n- improve diagnosability: separate compute, comms (nccl), and scheduler starvation.n- add regression coverage (repro harness perf canary fault injection).n- provide safe mitigations: watchdogs, controlled abort/retry paths, operational runbooks.nn non-goalsn- major refactor of tp execution model.n- model quality/evals work beyond using models as workload generators.n- new user-facing product features unrelated to reliability.nn background: current tp execution (high level)nin a tp replica, each request is executed across n ranks (gpus) using:n- runtime scheduler: builds prefill and decode steps and dispatches work across streamsn- kernel comms boundary: nccl collectives (e.g., all-reduce / reduce-scatter / all-gather) are issued on a designated comm stream and synchronized with compute streamsn- kv cache: per-rank allocation eviction/compaction shared scheduling decisions require consistent rank-local statennkey constraint: collectives require all ranks to participate in the same collective sequence with compatible shapes and ordering. any divergence (control flow, scheduling, cancellation paths, memory errors) can lead to indefinite waits.nn taxonomy of tp hang / stall signaturesnthis taxonomy is meant to be operational: each signature should map to measurable signals and specific mitigations.nn signature a collective ordering mismatch (classic deadlock)nsymptomsn- some ranks blocked inside an nccl call others blocked earlier/later in a different collectiven- no forward progress request(s) hang until client timeoutn- often correlated with mixed prefill/decode and high concurrencynnlikely causesn- scheduler creates different step/collective sequences across ranks (e.g., starvation, interleaving differences)n- cancellation path triggers early exit on a subset of ranksn- error path (oom, invalid shape) returns early on a subset of ranks without synchronizing abortnnwhat we need to measuren- per-rank collective sequence number and in-flight collective countn- rank-local step id (prefill vs decode) and batch composition hashn- time since last completed collective per ranknnn signature b stream/event synchronization bug (silent stall)nsymptomsn- nccl is called, but the stream waits on an event that is never recorded (or recorded on a different stream)n- gpu utilization may be low one stream appears stuckn- reproduces more frequently with cuda graphs or conditional graph pathsnnlikely causesn- missing or incorrect cudaeventrecord / cudastreamwaitevent orderingn- using default stream semantics inadvertently (implicit dependencies differ by build/runtime flags)n- graph capture constraints causing unexpected stream dependenciesnnwhat we need to measuren- structured logs for sync points around comms boundaries (enter/exit, event ids)n- optional debug counters for stream waits and event records (sampled)n- nccl debug traces (limited window, safe enablement)nnn signature c scheduler starvation of collectives (fairness / backpressure)nsymptomsn- under heavy prefill, decode progress slows dramatically some ranks continue issuing prefill-heavy workn- collectives required for decode are delayed long enough to trigger timeouts or watchdogn- appears as hang from the client perspective, but may be a starvation-induced stallnnlikely causesn- fairness logic allows prefill-heavy batches to dominate a ranks compute streamn- coordination points (barriers) are not treated as high priority collectives can be queued behind long kernelsn- different ranks observe different queue pressure, producing divergence in which collectives are reachednnwhat we need to measuren- scheduler queue depth by class: prefill vs decode vs collectiven- time-in-queue metrics for collective-ready stepsn- per-rank heartbeat that includes last forward-progress timestamp at step granularitynnn signature d kv cache compaction / memory pressure causing rank divergencensymptomsn- one or more ranks enters compaction/eviction paths while others proceedn- eventually results in collective mismatch or prolonged stalln- often correlated with long context high churn (many concurrent sequences) fragmented kvnnlikely causesn- compaction path changes allocation decisions that affect batch composition or tensor shapes per rankn- an allocation failure causes early-return on one rankn- shared decisions (e.g., which sequences to evict) not consistently applied across ranksnnwhat we need to measuren- kv cache pressure signals: fragmentation score, compaction duration, allocation failuresn- cross-rank agreement checks on batch plan (sampled hash compare)nnn signature e cancelled streaming request leaves collectives waitingnsymptomsn- client disconnect during streaming server cancels requestn- subset of ranks drops the request early other ranks continue and block in a collectivennlikely causesn- cancellation is handled per-rank without a synchronized cancel barriern- cancellation occurs between plan and execute stepsnnwhat we need to measuren- cancel events tagged with request id step id rankn- whether cancel was synchronized (all ranks observed) vs local-onlynnn proposed instrumentation (diagnostics first)nthis project prioritizes actionable signals before (and alongside) fixes.nn 1) tp heartbeat stall reason taggingnadd per-rank heartbeats emitted at key points:n- start/end of prefill stepn- start/end of decode iterationn- start/end of each nccl collectivennheartbeat fields (labels)n- replica_id, rank, tp_world_size, correlationn- maintain a monotonic per-rank collective_seqnon- emit in_flight_collectives gauge per rankn- add tracing span fields (sampled) for collective_seqno, rank, and batch_plan_hashnn 3) boosted over prefill)nnn proposed runtime changesnwe propose changes in three layers: (1) scheduler ordering/fairness, (2) comms boundary sync, (3) safe abort/drain semantics.nn change 1 scheduler guardrails: prevent collective starvation and reduce divergencenproblem: the scheduler can delay collective-requiring work behind long prefill kernels, and ranks can drift in which steps they reach under load.nndesignn1) introduce an explicit priority class for collective-ready work.n2) enforce a maximum prefill run-ahead budget when decode collectives are pending.n3) ensure all ranks use consistent step plan boundaries:n - a step plan is computed once per replica tick and broadcast to ranks (or derived deterministically from shared inputs).n - if a rank cannot execute the step plan router, the scheduler, and kernel instances. it provides a prescriptive matrix of signals and thresholds, sample policy yaml for the admission broker, instrumentation guidance, an operational runbook for admission-related incidents, and a rollout checklist for changes to the admission logic.nnscope and audience:n- audience: runtime engineers, scheduler owners, sres, and reliability-focused product engineers.n- scope: admission decision inputs and outputs, signal definitions, negotiation rounds, safety gates for degradation, and testing/rollout steps.nngoals:n- make admission decisions deterministic and auditable across heterogeneous gpu pools.n- preserve latency slos by prioritizing low-latency cohorts while allowing controlled degradation for best-effort traffic.n- provide a safe negotiation protocol that avoids oscillation when kernel availability fluctuates.nnkey concepts:n1) admission broker: a small, deterministic service colocated with the request router responsible for converting traffic intent into kernel slot requests.n2) signals: typed metrics used in negotiation (see table below).n3) negotiation round: a single exchange in which the broker proposes a slot profile and kernel replies with an acceptance, partial-accept, or reject.n4) slot profile: an immutable descriptor (model variant, max_seq_len, prioritization_token, quality_tier) used to match kernel capabilities.nnsignals and metrics (definitions):n- runtime.admit.latency_ms: time taken by the admission broker to respond to router before handoff.n- kernel.acceptance_rate: fraction of proposals accepted by kernels per 1m window.n- scheduler.queue_depth: number of pending kernel requests.n- kernel.available_slots: sum of free execution slots across matched kernels.n- fidelity.headroom_pct: estimated percentage of quality headroom remaining if requested batch is admitted.n- kvcache.warmth_score: heuristic (0.0-1.0) of prefix cache locality expected for the request.nnadmission decision matrix (human-readable table):n traffic class min slo p50 (ms) max allowed queue_depth min kernel.available_slots kvcache.warmth_score min default action 10s.n- fidelity.headroom_pct is estimated from the latest quality model and is used to decide whether a cheaper quantized kernel can be used.nnpolicy example (admission-broker.yaml):nyamlnversion: prefetch crediting interleaved kernel launches, content: h1. overviewnthis page describes redwood inferences credit-based tensor-parallel (tp) scheduling system that improves overlap between nccl communication and compute by introducing a lightweight flow-control primitive (credits). credits are also integrated with kv-cache prefetch so that expensive host-side prefetch work yields when collective pressure is high, reducing host stalls and tail latency.nnthis document supersedes the implementation notes originally captured in pr-51402. the core design remains the same, but the rollout state, knobs, and a few implementation details have been updated since the initial merge.nnh1. motivationnmulti-gpu tp workloads can experience intermittent host-side stalls when:n kv-cache prefetch threads (host work dma staging) contend with nccl launch/hostbuffer management.n large collectives and large prefetch bursts serialize kernel launches on the host.n a small number of long-sequence requests create head-of-line blocking for mixed traffic.nnprior scheduling overlapped comm/compute but lacked backpressure. credits provide that backpressure while enabling controlled interleaving of smaller compute kernels.nnh1. key conceptsnh2. creditsna credit represents permission to have an in-flight collective window for a tp group. launch paths consume credits completion returns them.n credits are scoped per tp group.n credits are intentionally lightweight to avoid host contention.n credit starvation should result in bounded waiting (no host oom / runaway buffering).nnh2. kv prefetch creditingnkv prefetch requests must acquire credit (or yield) when the system is under collective pressure. this prevents prefetch bursts from amplifying host stalls.nnh2. interleaved kernel launchesnwhen credits permit, the runtime can issue smaller micro-kernel launches (sub-chunked gemm/attention components) to increase comm/compute overlap and reduce serialization.nnh1. architecturenh2. componentsn1) tp credit allocatorn maintains a pool of credits per tp group.n tracks outstanding collective windows.n exposes fast-path apis for launch threads.nn2) nccl launcher integrationn collectives consume credits on launch and return them on completion.n hostbuffer metadata includes a credit token so downstream host work can attribute pressure correctly.nn3) kv prefetcher integrationn prefetch uses a try-acquire pattern.n on low credit availability, prefetch yields and returns a suggested backoff.nn4) kernel interleavern schedules smaller compute chunks when credits are available.n uses conservative defaults to avoid regressions on low-bandwidth topologies.nnh2. token / aba safety (updated)nthe original implementation used a 32-bit composed token (credit_id:epoch) to avoid aba when reusing small credit ids.nupdate since initial merge:n the token is now treated as a 64-bit logical identifier internally (still compact on the wire where possible) to reduce the probability of epoch wrap under long-lived high-qps services.n the debug endpoint presents both the short id and the full token for correlation.nnh1. configurationnh2. feature flag (updated)nthe credit pipeline is controlled by an environment flag:n redwood_tp_credit_pipelinennrollout status (as of 2026-03-12):n hosted clusters: default on for a100/h100 nvlink tiers.n hosted ethernet tiers: default on with conservative autotune caps.n dedicated clusters: default off unless explicitly enabled by the deployment owner.nnh2. primary knobsnthe system supports ethernet)n tp degreen model shape hints (hidden size, head count, typical batch)n historical bandwidth/latency telemetry (when available)nnupdate since initial merge:n autotune now clamps credits more default for dedicated enabled for hosted canaries).nnh1. observabilitynh2. metricsnthe following metrics are emitted:n tp.credit_grantsn tp.credit_waitsn tp.prefetch_yieldsn tp.interleaver.splitsn prototype (short/long prompt-aware) design, content: summarynthis document proposes a scheduler prototype to reduce user-visible p95 tail latency for text generation under mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts), without materially regressing throughput or fairness.nnwe introduce a prompt-aware, class-based scheduling policy that:n- classifies requests into short and long classes using prompt/context length and (optionally) a predicted prefill cost.n- maintains two queues and applies a biased dispatch policy that favors short while guaranteeing progress for long.n- separates prefill and decode scheduling decisions to avoid long-prefill head-of-line (hol) blocking.n- adds guardrails: aging, burst caps, max skew, and token budgets.n- ships behind a feature flag with safe defaults and a staged rollout plan.nnowner: serving runtime / scheduling (tech lead: lena fischer em: sofia ivanova)nn---nn motivation and problem statementn what we see in productionnredwoods continuous batching and kv-cache-heavy decode path performs well for homogeneous workloads. under mixed workloads, we see a consistent pattern:n- a long-context request enters the batch with a large prefill cost.n- prefill dominates the iteration selection for several cycles.n- short requests accumulate behind it (queue time increases).n- result: ttft and p95 latency for short-like requests spike, even when aggregate throughput remains acceptable.nnthis is a classic head-of-line blocking issue amplified by:n- large variance in prompt/context length.n- prefill compute spikes compared to steady decode.n- batch construction heuristics that implicitly favor large, ready-to-run sequences.nn goalnreduce p95 latency for latency-sensitive short prompts (especially chat) in mixed workloads.nn non-goals (prototype)n- no customer-configurable multi-class qos product in this phase.n- no full redesign of admission control/backpressure we only minimally couple to existing mechanisms.nn---nn design principlesn1. prefer predictable tail improvements over theoretical optimality (srpt-like policies can be fragile without accurate remaining-time estimates).n2. guarantee progress for long (no starvation).n3. minimal disruption to runtime invariants (continuous batching, kv cache semantics, kernel selection).n4. feature-flagged observable: new policy must be safe to canary and easy to rollback.nn---nn background: serving pipeline (prefill vs decode)nwe use the terms:n- prefill: first forward pass over prompt/context to populate kv cache.n- decode: subsequent token generation steps using kv cache.nnin mixed workloads, long-context prefill acts like a compute bubble that can block short ttft.nn current (simplified) flown(conceptual details vary by model/runtime config)nn1) request arrivesn2) enqueued into a single scheduler queuen3) scheduler picks a set of requests to form the next batchn4) runtime executes either:n - prefill for new sequences, and/orn - decode for active sequencesnn proposed flow (class-aware)nwe explicitly split selection signals for:n- new-prefill admission (which new requests to prefill now)n- decode continuation (which active sequences continue decoding)nnwe treat these as related but separable decisions, each with class-based guardrails.nn---nn proposed architecturen high-level componentsn- classifier: assigns each incoming request a class short, long and computes a lightweight cost estimate.n- two queues: short_q and long_q.n- dispatcher: selects work each scheduler iteration using class-aware rules.n- aging / starvation prevention: escalates priority for long-waiting long requests.n- token budget guardrails: caps per-iteration prefill and decode work contributed by each class.nn text diagram: queues and pipelinennclient requestsn n vn-------------------n request classify n (short / long) n-------------------n n v vn-------- --------n short long n queue queue n-------- --------n /n /n v vn ------------------- ------------------n class-aware --- batch builder n dispatcher (prefill/decode) n ------------------- ------------------n n v vn ----------- ------------n prefill decode n ----------- ------------nnkey point: dispatcher provides a class-balanced candidate set and budgets batch builder remains responsible for kernel-friendly packing within those constraints.nn---nn classification: short vs longn inputs available at enqueue timen- prompt_tokens (tokenized prompt length)n- context_tokens (if continuing a conversation or multi-turn context)n- max_new_tokens (generation limit)n- model_id / architecture hintsn- optional: a cheap predicted prefill cost (tokens model factor) derived from prior observationsnn default heuristic (prototype)nwe classify as long if any of the following are true:n- prompt_tokens context_tokens long_prompt_threshold_tokensn- or predicted prefill cost long_prefill_cost_thresholdnnotherwise classify as short.nnrationale:n- the simplest signal that correlates with prefill time is context length.n- prefill cost can diverge across models/skus we allow an optional calibrated threshold.nn threshold selectionninitial default thresholds will come from anonymized production trace distributions (see trace analysis sheet) and validated via benchmark sweeps.nnrecommended starting points (to be tuned per sku/model):n- long_prompt_threshold_tokens: 1024 (hosted chat) / 1536 (dedicated mixed workloads)n- long_prefill_cost_threshold: disabled by default (0 off)nn edge casesn- very short prompt but extremely large max_new_tokens: still short by default. this is intentional for ttft focus decode fairness is handled by decode budgets.n- streaming: treated the same class affects scheduling but not token emission semantics.n- tool/function calling: class assignment based on prompt/context only, not tool latency.nn---nn scheduling policy: two-queue with biased dispatch fairnessn goals of policyn- improve p95 for short by avoiding hol blocking from long prefill.n- maintain throughput by not overly fragmenting batches.n- guarantee progress for long with explicit fairness and aging.nn core ideanmaintain two fifo queues:n- short_q: latency-sensitiven- long_q: throughput-oriented but must not starvennon each scheduler iteration, the dispatcher:n1. computes eligible work (requests ready for prefill active sequences ready for decode).n2. enforces per-class token budgets for both prefill and decode.n3. selects a candidate set with a target class share for admission.n4. applies aging to ensure long requests that wait too long are promoted.nn dispatch algorithm (prototype)nthe dispatcher runs every scheduling iteration (or when gpu becomes available):nninputs:n- short_q, long_qn- active_decode_short, active_decode_long (optional conceptual partitions)n- current load signals: queue depths, average prefill time, decode backlogn- config knobs (see below)nnoutputs:n- a set of selected sequences for the next batchn- budget caps for prefill/decode worknnpseudocode (conceptual):n1) determine budgets:n - prefill_budget_tokens_totaln - decode_budget_tokens_totaln - split into per-class budgets using short_prefill_share and short_decode_sharenn2) apply aging:n - for long requests with time_in_queue long_aging_threshold_ms, temporarily treat as short for selection purposes (promotion), capped by aging_promotion_max_fraction.nn3) prefill admission:n - admit from short_q up to prefill_budget_short_tokens.n - admit from long_q up to prefill_budget_long_tokens.n - if one class is empty, allow borrowing within borrow_cap_fraction.nn4) decode continuation:n - continue decode for active sequences with per-class caps.n - if decode backlog is high, reduce new prefill admission via prefill_backoff_on_decode_pressure.nn5) guardrails:n - enforce max_class_skew_ratio between admitted short and long over a rolling window.n - enforce long_progress_min_tokens_per_sec (derived) by ensuring minimum decode/prefill slices.nn why two-queue vs srptnwe considered srpt and remaining-time estimators rejected for prototype due to:n- need for accurate remaining-time prediction across models and sequence lengths.n- high risk of oscillation/thrashing and difficult explainability.n- two-queue gives a stable, controllable behavior with a smaller surface area.nn(see adr for the full decision record.)nn---nn starvation prevention and fairnessnwe define starvation as: long requests experiencing unbounded waiting time under sustained short traffic.nnmechanisms:n1. guaranteed long slicen - ensure prefill_budget_long_tokens and/or decode_budget_long_tokens never go to zero unless long_q is empty.nn2. aging-based promotionn - after long_aging_threshold_ms, a long request is eligible for promotion.n - promotion is bounded to avoid flipping the system entirely to long.nn3. rolling-window skew constraintn - track admitted work over fairness_window_ms.n - if short dominates beyond max_class_skew_ratio, force long admission until back within bound.nn4. burst capsn - short bursts can be beneficial for p95 but harmful for long limit via short_burst_max_iters and short_burst_cooldown_iters.nnnotes:n- fairness is defined at the runtime level (not tenant level) for this prototype.n- interaction with existing per-api-key quotas is unchanged.nn---nn prefill vs decode separation (kernel/runtime interaction)nmixed workloads trigger kernel instability when sequence length distributions swing quickly. we aim to reduce thrash by:n- stabilizing batch composition: keep decode-heavy batches decode-heavy and prefill admission bounded.n- token budgeting: cap prefill tokens per iteration to avoid a single long prefill dominating.n- avoiding rapid alternation: use prefill_backoff_on_decode_pressure so when decode backlog is high, we dont keep injecting large prefill work.nnconstraints:n- batch builder
