confluence, title: tail-latency circuit patterns and kernel-shed strategy, content: executive summarynnthis document defines an operational and architectural pattern to control tail latency in redwoods inference serving runtime by combining request-level circuit breakers, proactive kernel shedding (gpu/accelerator scheduling decisions), and short-lived queue smoothing. it provides concrete thresholds, configuration examples, telemetry keys, and a safe rollout procedure for production. the goal is to reduce p99/p999 latency excursions while keeping overall throughput and request fairness predictable.nncontext and problem statementnn- observed symptom: intermittent p99/p999 spikes driven by a small percentage of long-sequence generation requests, adversarial input shapes, or kernel stalls when heterogeneous accelerators (a100, h100, and llm-optimized tpu-like devices) are mixed in a shard.n- impact: customer-facing latency slo violations, elevated cost during surges as autoscaler spins up nodes, increased error budget burn for downstream services (request-router, console, telemetry-ingest).n- existing gaps: kernel scheduler currently prioritizes throughput there is no standardized circuit contract between request-router and kernel-agent to gracefully shed work or downgrade to degraded variants.nndesign goals and non-goalsnngoals:n1) bound tail latency (p99, p999) for routes with strict latency slos by enabling fast local decisions at the edge of the runtime (request-router) and coordinated shedding in the kernel-agent.n2) maintain predictable unit cost: ensure shedding decisions prefer graceful degradation over dropping or unbounded retries.n3) maintain observability and explainability: every shed/downgrade decision must emit structured telemetry for post-incident analysis.nnnon-goals:n- this doc does not replace higher-level routing policies (policy-service) for multi-region failover.n- it is not prescribing specific model quality fallback prompts model fallbacks are orchestrated elsewhere (model-fallback-service).nnkey components and responsibilitiesnn- request-router: applies client-side and tenant-level slos, issues circuit decisions, maintains per-tenant running counters. owner: request-platform team.n- kernel-agent (per-node): enforces kernel-shed decisions, implements token-budget preemption, and selects degraded execution paths (quantized kernel, shorter kv cache warmups). owner: serving-runtime team.n- admission-proxy: queues and shapes incoming requests, exposes backlog length metric admission.queue_length. owner: edge-team.n- telemetry-pipeline: captures structured decisions under serving.shed_event with tags tenant, route, reason, action. owner: observability-team.nnpattern overviewnn1) two-tier circuit model:n - fast local circuit: decision made in request-router within 50ms based on moving-window metrics (requests/s, queue length, p95 latency). short ttl (1s).n - node-level kernel circuit: longer horizon (30s2m) in kernel-agent that aggregates local kernel health (gpu utilization, kernel stalls, oom counts).nn2) kernel-shed actions (ordered by preference):n a) prefer model-variant downgrade (e.g., switch to int8/4-bit variant) with preserved schema.n b) reduce generation max_tokens for tail-risk requests (mutating request with explicit max_tokens cap).n c) move request to slow-path batching with preemptible background slot.n d) reject (http 429) only as last resort when capacity and fallbacks are exhausted.nnoperational thresholds and slosnn- service slos (example for low-latency route /v1/generate/fast):n - p50 150 or p95(latency) 220ms for 3 consecutive 1s windows.n - kernel circuit enters degraded mode when kernel.utilization_pct 92 for 30s or kernel.stall_count 5 in 60s.n - automatic cooldown: circuits move to half-open after 10s (fast) / 90s (kernel).nntelemetry and metrics (canonical names)nnuse the following structured metrics and events. all metrics must include cluster, node_id, tenant, route dimensions.nn- serving.request_duration_ms (histogram)n- serving.queue_length (gauge)n- serving.kernel_utilization_pct (gauge)n- serving.kernel_stall_count kernel-selection behavior (b200 vs h100)nb200 differs from h100 in two important ways:n1) kernel set: b200 uses a different set of best-performing attention kernels and preferred data types.n2) heuristic thresholds: sequence-length bucket boundaries and switch points differ.nn key differences vs h100n- attention kernel preference:n - h100 profile leans on stable flashattention variants tuned for hopper.n - b200 profile enables blackwell-optimized attention kernels (where available) and is more conservative about fallback paths.nn- datatype / quantization posture:n - h100: common wins with around mid-length prompts (observed thrash in early canaries). the b200 profile pins bucket boundaries and reduces runtime adaptation frequency.nn- prefill vs decode split:n - b200 profile biases toward prefill efficiency when concurrency is high, but caps decode starvation via stricter fairness limits (see scheduler section).nn practical operator implicationsn- if you compare b200 vs h100 and dsid_0e47679a4c5249ce944eaa59e3d67813, source_type: confluence, title: workload-aware batching defaults (fast / standard / cost-efficient) design, content: overviewnthis document defines redwood runtimes workload-aware batching defaults: three customer-facing latency slo tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient) implemented as tiered batching profiles selected automatically by the runtime based on workload signals and policy configuration.nnthe primary goal is to reduce cost per 1k tokens via safer batching defaults while preserving predictable tail latency (especially for streaming) and avoiding starvation under mixed workloads.nnthis is the primary design doc for:n- tier definitions and the contract we uphold for each tier (in runtime terms).n- scheduler knob mapping (continuous batching heuristics, queueing, prefill/decode balancing, admission control).n- workload signals (length buckets, streaming flag, concurrency, overload signals) and selection logic.n- override hierarchy (customer override route/model policy tier default) and explainability (reason codes).n- rollout and rollback plan for hosted and dedicated.nn background and decision summarynwe will ship three tiered defaults rather than per-tenant real-time autotuning (see adr-023). the tiers give customers a stable mental model and enable us to publish and validate recommended profiles per model family hardware class.nnkey principles:n1) tail latency is a first-class constraint (fast tier must protect p99 and streaming time-to-first-token).n2) defaults must be explainable (operators can see the effective tier/profile and why it was selected).n3) behavior under overload must be safe and predictable (backpressure, load shedding, and bounded queues).n4) profiles must work under mixed workloads (avoid starving long prompts, avoid short prompts dominate forever).nn goals / non-goalsn goalsn- provide 3 tiers with validated scheduler knob sets that meet tier slo targets under the benchmark methodology.n- make tier selection workload-aware using a small set of robust signals (prompt length distribution, streaming vs non-streaming, concurrency and queue pressure).n- add observability for tier effectiveness (latency, queue depth, batch size distribution, cache hit rate) and profile selection reason codes.n- support overrides for enterprise/dedicated and safe rollback via feature flags and kill switches.nn non-goals (initial release)n- fully automatic per-tenant tuning in real time.n- introducing new cross-region routing decisions beyond existing smart routing policies.n- changing model quality behavior (we will add guardrails/evals to ensure no meaningful quality regression).nn definitionsn key termsn- prefill: processing the prompt/context portion of a request (often compute-heavy and variable length).n- decode: token-by-token generation (typically more latency sensitive for streaming).n- continuous batching: dynamically packing multiple requests into gpu execution steps over time.n- wait budget: maximum queue time a request may spend waiting to be batched.n- batch tokens: the total tokens processed in a single execution step (prefill tokens decode tokens).nn tier contract (runtime interpretation)nthe slo targets are defined formally in the sre slo tier doc. runtimes contract is:n- fast: prioritize tail latency and streaming responsiveness over throughput. use tight wait budgets, stronger admission control, and conservative max batch sizes.n- standard: balanced default moderate batching with bounded tail latency.n- cost-efficient: maximize throughput and /token improvements while staying within published latency bounds more aggressive batching and larger batch token limits, with guardrails to prevent queue blowups.nnimportant: these tiers are defaults (not guarantees) and are enforced via best-effort scheduling plus overload protections.nn high-level architecturen componentsn- scheduler (runtime): implements queue admission, request classification, batching, and prefill/decode interleaving.n- policy engine (control plane): resolves tier selection configuration at route/model/tenant level.n- telemetry pipeline: emits per-tier metrics and reason codes with cardinality controls.nn data flow (simplified)n1) request arrives with attributes (model, route, region, streaming flag, prompt length, max output tokens).n2) policy engine resolves an effective tier (and optional profile override) based on precedence rules.n3) scheduler tags request with a tier, selects a batching profile (possibly adjusted by workload signals), and applies admission control.n4) runtime executes continuous batching telemetry records latency/cost/queue metrics, plus selection reason codes.nn workload signalsnwe use a small set of signals that are low-cardinality, stable, and available at request time.nn request-time signalsn- streaming (boolean): whether the request is streaming tokens.n- prompt_length_bucket: bucketed prompt tokens (derived from tokenizer estimate or actual token count once computed).n - buckets (initial): 0256, 2571k, 1k4k, 4k8k, 8k.n- max_output_bucket (optional, coarse): 1k.n- model_family / engine_compat_class: derived from model catalog metadata (e.g., llama-style decoder-only moe constraints attention kernel compatibility).nn runtime signalsn- concurrency_estimate: rolling ewma of in-flight requests per model shard.n- queue_depth and queue_wait_ms: per-tier queues (bounded) and current tail of wait.n- kv_cache_pressure: derived from cache occupancy and eviction rate.n- overload_mode: boolean state computed from admission control triggers (see overload section).nn signals explicitly not used (v1)n- tenant identifier (to avoid high-cardinality coupling and fairness issues).n- prompt content (privacy complexity).n- fine-grained per-user/client metrics.nn tier selection logicntier selection happens in two layers: (1) control-plane policy (configured tier), and (2) scheduler-level workload-aware adjustments (within the tier).nn layer 1: effective tier from policy engineninput sources:n- request header/sdk parameter (optional only allowed if enabled for the route).n- route policy (hosted api and dedicated).n- tenant/cluster override (dedicated), plus model constraints.nnoutput:n- effective_tier: fast standard cost_efficientn- effective_profile_id: optional explicit profile overridenn layer 2: workload-aware adjustments (within tier)nwe do not upgrade/downgrade tiers automatically in v1. instead, we adjust a small set of knobs inside the selected tier based on workload shape and overload.nnadjustments include:n- lowering max_wait_ms for streaming-heavy traffic in standard tier.n- tightening max_batch_tokens for very long prompt buckets to prevent head-of-line blocking.n- enabling stricter admission control earlier if queue_wait_ms trends upward in fast tier.nn selection pseudo-code (conceptual)nn// resolved by policy enginentier resolve_effective_tier(request)nprofile base_profile_for(tier, model_family, hw_class)nn// scheduler-level adjustmentsnif request.streaming:n profile.max_wait_ms min(profile.max_wait_ms, streaming_wait_cap_mstier)nnif request.prompt_length_bucket in 4k-8k, 8k:n profile.max_batch_tokens min(profile.max_batch_tokens, long_prompt_batch_captier)n profile.prefill_max_concurrency min(profile.prefill_max_concurrency, long_prompt_prefill_captier)nnif overload_mode_active(tier):n profile apply_overload_policy(profile, tier)nnemit_reason_codes(...)nreturn profilennn scheduler knob mappingnthis section defines the knobs that constitute a batching profile. names are aligned with runtime config schema (eng-18422 / pr-28431), but the table below is the behavioral contract.nn profile knobs (v1)n knob description why it matters n---------n max_wait_ms maximum queue time before forcing dispatch direct tail latency control primary lever for fast n max_batch_tokens upper bound on total tokens per step (prefilldecode) throughput vs tail latency bounds worst-case step time n max_batch_requests upper bound on number of requests in a batch prevents pathological micro-requests from overpacking n prefill_decode_ratio_target target gpu time split between prefill and decode avoids decode starvation (streaming) or prefill backlog n prefill_max_concurrency max concurrent prefills admitted per shard prevents long prompts from dominating compute n decode_max_concurrency max concurrent decodes admitted per shard controls streaming smoothness, ttft, and p99 n queue_max_depth bounded queue size per tier prevents unbounded latency growth enables backpressure n admission_max_queue_wait_ms threshold to start rejecting/throttling predictable degradation under overload n anti_starvation_quantum_ms ensures long/slow requests make progress prevents starvation under mixed length buckets n enable_prefix_cache_preferential prioritize requests with cache hits (bounded) improves /token without harming fairness nnnotes:n- we keep the knob surface area intentionally small. internally there may be additional parameters (e.g., kernel dispatch granularity), but those are not exposed as profile-level knobs.n- profiles are parameterized by model family hardware class where necessary.nn baseline tier profiles (initial targets)nvalues below are initial targets for top model families and are finalized by the benchmark suite. publishable values live in the profile matrix doc / spreadsheet this design doc defines the intended relationships.nn tier intent max_wait_ms max_batch_tokens admission control prefill/decode balancing n---------:---:------n fast protect p99 / streaming 13ms (streaming cap 12ms) conservative early strict decode-biased when streaming n standard balanced 38ms (streaming cap 35ms) moderate moderate adaptive n cost-efficient optimize throughput 820ms (streaming cap 58ms) aggressive (bounded) later, but stronger overload guardrails prefill-biased unless streaming nn streaming considerationsnstreaming is treated as a high-priority latency mode:n- time-to-first-token (ttft) is strongly correlated with prefill queueing prefill step time.n- inter-token latency is sensitive to decode scheduling and decode concurrency.nnrules:n1) for streaming requests, apply a stricter wait cap regardless of tier.n2) when the decode queue for streaming requests is non-empty, enforce a minimum decode service share (prefill_decode_ratio_target shifts toward decode).n3) avoid batching streaming decode into overly large steps that produce bursty token emission.nn queues, fairness, and starvation preventionnwe maintain per-tier logical queues, but fairness is enforced globally per shard.nn fairness designn- requests are tagged with tier and length bucket.n- scheduler uses weighted fair queuing between:n - tier queues (fast standard cost-efficient weights)n - within each tier: length buckets with anti-starvation guaranteesnn anti-starvation mechanismnwe use a quantum-based mechanism:n- each length bucket accumulates deficit credits over time.n- even if short prompts dominate arrivals, long prompt buckets will eventually accumulate enough credit to be scheduled.n- anti_starvation_quantum_ms is tier-dependent (fast smallest, cost-efficient largest).nn head-of-line blocking mitigationn- large-prefill requests (8k) are limited via prefill_max_concurrency.n- long prompts may trigger a lower max_batch_tokens cap to bound step time.nn overload behavior (safe degradation)noverload behavior must be predictable and reversible.nn overload detectionnwe enter overload_mode per tier when any of the following conditions persist for a rolling window (e.g., 515s):n- queue_wait_ms p95 admission_max_queue_wait_ms (tier-specific)n- queue_depth approaches queue_max_depthn- repeated cache eviction spikes correlate with degraded latency (kv_cache_pressure high)nn overload actions (ordered)n1) backpressure: return 429/503 with retry-after (hosted) or propagate backpressure upstream (dedicated), respecting existing policies.n2) tighten wait budgets: reduce max_wait_ms (especially for fast/streaming) to prevent latency spirals.n3) clamp batch size: reduce max_batch_tokens to keep step time bounded.n4) shed confluence, title: kernel credit accounting fairness playbook, content: summaryn-------nthis playbook describes the design, configuration, operational runbooks, and rollout guidance for the kernel-level credit accounting and fairness layer used in redwoods multi-tenant inference runtime. the system ensures predictable throughput and latency slos while preventing noisy-tenant and priority-inversion problems when many concurrent requests contend for gpu kernels and kv-cache resources.nnintended audiencen-----------------n- runtime engineers (owners of kernel scheduler and admission control)n- sres on-call for serving clustersn- capacity planners and product owners for dedicated/private productsnngoals and non-goalsn-------------------ngoals:n- provide stable latency for high-priority routes while allowing best-effort capacity for trial/metered usersn- bound tail latency by limiting long queue accumulation on kernel execution pathsn- offer explainable and auditable per-customer accounting for gpu kernel usagennnon-goals:n- replace higher-level rate-limiters or api quotas (this works below api surface in serving runtime)n- fully eliminate all client-visible variability in extreme overloads we provide graceful degradation strategies insteadnndefinitions and key conceptsn----------------------------n- credit: abstract unit representing entitlement to consume a kernel timeslice. credits are consumed when a request enters a kernel-execution critical section.n- credit bucket: per-tenant (and per-priority) balance tracked in-memory (and periodically checkpointed).n- refill policy: rate at which credits are added to a bucket (tokens/sec).n- debit event: decrement of credits on kernel entry if insufficient credits, request is queued or subject to degradation depending on policy.n- fairness window: configurable sliding window (default 60s) for measuring usage and computing deficits.nnarchitecture overviewn---------------------n1) placement: the credit accounting layer sits in the local serving process before kernel invocation and is enforced per-shard (numa / gpu device). it integrates with:n - admission-controller (global decisions for burst allowances),n - kernel-mapper (selects kernel variant after accounting), andn - request-pool (local queues and backpressure).n2) persistence: buckets are ephemeral but periodically checkpointed to the control plane to enable cross-node rebalancing and debugging. checkpoint sync is best-effort every 30s immediate sync occurs on tenant migration.n3) telemetry: metrics exported as prometheus/otel metrics and traces. see telemetry and dashboards section.nnfairness algorithm (summary)n---------------------------nwe use a hybrid deficit-weighted round robin (dwrr) with a decay term to prefer recent underutilization. highlights:n- each tenant t has a configured weight w_t and min-guarantee g_t (credits/sec).n- deficit increases by w_t quantum on each scheduling round and decays at half-life configured via fairness-window.n- when kernel resources are scarce, tenants with exhausted deficits are deprioritized.n- priorities (system, paid-enterprise, paid-standard, trial) are mapped to weight ranges and short-term burst credits.nnconfiguration reference (example)n--------------------------------n(stored in runtime config: /etc/redwood/runtime/kernel-crediting.yaml per node)nn---n top-level config versionnversion: 1ndefault_fairness_window_seconds: 60nquantum_micros: 5000 scheduling quantum used to bump deficitnpriority_classes:n system:n weight: 100n min_guarantee: 1000n burst_tokens: 5000n preemptible: falsen enterprise:n weight: 50n min_guarantee: 300n burst_tokens: 1000n preemptible: falsen standard:n weight: 10n min_guarantee: 50n burst_tokens: 200n preemptible: truen trial:n weight: 1n min_guarantee: 5n burst_tokens: 50n preemptible: truentenant_overrides: per-tenant config (optional)n tenant-abc123:n weight: 20n min_guarantee: 100nnoperational runbook: high-level flown-----------------------------------n1) admission: incoming request - admission controller - credit check.n2) if credits kernel_cost(request) - debit and enqueue for kernel mapper.n3) if credits check fallback policy:n a) if low-priority and degradation allowed - route to a quantized model variant (lower kernel cost).n b) if burst_allowed (and bucket has burst_tokens) - consume burst tokens and admit.n c) else - return 429 with retry-after or queue with bounded wait (configurable max_wait_ms).n4) on kernel completion, an accounting reconciliation event returns partial credits for short-circuited operations (e.g., cache hit avoids kernel).nnrunbook: incident scenarios and stepsn------------------------------------na. symptom: sudden increase in p99 latency on standard and trial tenants while enterprise remains stablen- likely cause: burst tokens exhausted or noisy tenant consuming more than weight.n- steps:n 1. run quick telemetry queries (below) to identify tenant with spike in kernel_invocations.n 2. inspect credit_balance and deficit for top-10 tenants.n 3. if noisy-tenant found, temporarily set tenant weight to a lower value:n redwoodctl runtime update-tenant-config --tenant tenant-id --weight 5n 4. if more immediate relief needed, toggle preemption threshold to allow enterprise preemption:n redwoodctl runtime set-flag --name preemption_aggressiveness --value highn 5. document incident and add tenant to noisy-tenant watchlist.nnb. symptom: large queue growth observed on particular gpu devicen- likely cause: numa hotspot, slow kernel variant or memory thrashing.n- steps:n 1. correlate queue growth with kernel time/per-kernel-error.n 2. offload trial/standard queues by increasing min_guarantee for enterprise/system or disable burst for low tier.n 3. if kernel is hung, trigger per-device kill and warmstart per runbook: /eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/numa-aware-shard-placement-eviction-playbook-2026.jsonnntelemetry and dashboards (queries and metrics)n--------------------------------------------ncore metrics (prometheus names):n- redwood_kernel_credit_balancetenant,priority (gauge, credits)n- avg_over_time(redwood_kernel_queue_length1m) 50 for 2mn severity: p2n- alert: tenantcreditdepletedhighn expr: increase(redwood_kernel_debits_totaltenant.5m) (tenant_expected_rate 3) and redwood_kernel_credit_balance cost_k (cost in credits). on run, d_t - cost_k.ndecay: d_t d_t exp(-ln2 / half_life_seconds) every second (half-life parameterizable).nnappendix b: troubleshooting confluence, title: cohort eviction and fidelity escalation manual, content: overview:nnthis document defines the cohort-driven eviction and fidelity-escalation strategy used by redwoods serving runtime. it describes the architecture, kernel scheduling interactions, operational runbooks for incidents, and recommended profiling and benchmarking steps to validate policy changes. the guidance focuses on minimizing user-visible fidelity regressions while preserving slos for latency and availability.nngoals:n- maintain 99th percentile latency slos for latency-sensitive routes while maximizing throughput on cost-sensitive routes.n- provide deterministic, observable escalation paths: eviction - quantized fallback - reduced-context variant - full degrade to lower-cost model.n- ensure safe, auditable rollouts of eviction/fidelity policies with canaries and automated rollback triggers.nnscope and components referenced:n- runtime-orchestrator: policy engine that maps requests to cohorts and routes.n- gpu-dispatcher: low-level kernel invoker and per-gpu slot allocator.n- kvcache-manager: session/kv cache lifecycle controller and warmstart hints.n- kernel-allocator: chooses kernel variants (e.g., fused-attn, tiled-attn, quantized path).n- fidelity-adapter: component that surfaces fidelity presets (max_tokens, sampling_temperature, context_prune).nntraffic cohorting model:n1) cohort definition: requests are classified at ingress by route, customer-tier, and latency-sensitivity tag. example cohorts:n - realtime-high (interactive chat, enterprise, latency 95th), kv cache hit rate, and burst concurrency. these signals are normalized per-pool and reported to the runtime-orchestrator.nnkernel scheduling policy interaction:n- kernel selection: kernel-allocator maps model request cohort - kernel variant. preference order (by default): fused-opt - tiled-opt - quantized-path - cpu-fallback. the allocator can be overridden per-cohort.n- batch slicing: gpu-dispatcher slices batches with priority-aware buckets realtime-high requests form a minimum-preserve slice to keep latency low.n- hedging and speculative kernels: for cohorts marked hedge-enabled, the runtime may launch a lightweight quantized kernel after timeout t_hedge_ms (default 40ms). first response wins other kernels are cancelled.nneviction and fidelity escalation ladder:nthe ladder is a deterministic sequence a request can experience under resource pressure. configurable at service-level in the policy manifest.n1) soft eviction: drop queued low-priority requests before dispatch. threshold: queue_length q_soft_threshold (default 250).n2) kv cache eviction: eject less-recent contexts from cache (policy: lru with cohort weights). trigger when cache_mem_util 0.78.n3) quantized runtime path: switch kernel variant to 8-bit or 4-bit quantized execution for eligible models. trigger on node_mem_pressure or sustained tail latency 2x slo.n4) context trimming: fidelity-adapter prunes non-critical tokens (system prompts or long histories) based on prune_policy.n5) model variant swap: route to a smaller model variant with explicit fidelity delta recorded.n6) slow-path fallback: route to dedicated lower-cost pool with higher latency but preserved throughput.n7) circuit-break to return http 503 for clearly out-of-budget requests after grace period.nnoperational marked published.n, doc_id: dsid_4a35f075919f4c13bfe0fb6fd3169e3d, source_type: confluence, title: kernel state redistribution and roll-forward sop, content: overviewnnthis runbook documents the standard operating procedure (sop) for redistributing kernel-managed execution state across gpus and performing a roll-forward recovery when a traditional rollback (reinstating an older model or kernel bundle) is unsafe or unavailable. the focus is on minimizing customer-visible latency and preserving kv-cache / session-consistency while satisfying slo guardrails.nnscope and when to use this sopn-----------------------------n- applies to sharded and single-gpu kernel topologies that maintain volatile execution state (kv caches, per-request scratch, compiled kernel state).n- intended for incidents where:n - a kernel variant becomes unresponsive or corrupt mid-epoch and a rollback would cause unacceptable latency/regression, orn - partial state loss affects a subset of shards but continuing execution with reconstructed state is preferable to global fallback.n- not for: full-node hardware failures with persistent disk loss (see node-replacement playbook).nnownership and escalationn------------------------n- primary owner: serving runtime oncall (team: eng-serving-runtime).n- secondary: kernel/ scheduling squad.n- pager escalation: if the runbook cannot bring request-service back within 5 minutes, escalate to sre lead and declare p1.nnsuccess criterian----------------n- target: 99 of in-flight sessions either complete without user-visible error or are gracefully migrated to a compatible fallback within sla.n- safety gates: token-consistency checks pass, kv cache rehydration success rate 95 for affected sessions, no silent divergence of session outputs after roll-forward.nnprerequisites and fast checks (0-2 minutes)n-------------------------------------------n1) confirm incident classification: kernel corruption vs performance regression.n2) check slo dashboards: tail latency 95/99 quantiles, error-rate spike.n3) run quick telemetry queries:n - kernel_process_healthkernelx over last 2mn - kv_rehydration_failuresshardaffected.n4) if hardware-level alerts present (ecc, nvlink down), consult hardware runbooks do not proceed with roll-forward.nnhigh-level stepsn----------------n1) quiesce new admissions to the affected kernel cohort kernel shards for snapshot extraction.n3) extract consistent snapshots with lightweight freeze and copy protocol (see snippet).n4) verify snapshot integrity and generate redistribution plan.n5) perform state redistribution (shard relocalization) in parallel with live rehydration probes.n6) monitor session consistency checks and release admissions once thresholds met.n7) post-incident audit and write-up.nndetailed procedure (play-by-play)n--------------------------------n1) quiesce and force admissions policy (operator, 0-1 min)n - run: n bashn route new traffic away from kernel-x cohortn rctl set route --cohort kernel-x --policy divert --target-pool fallback-pooln rctl tag cohort kernel-x set redistribute-onlytruen n - expected result: new requests are diverted or annotated so redistribution does not need to handle them.nn2) snapshot extraction (operator kernel-scheduler, 1-3 min)n - goal: capture consistent kv cache and minimal execution metadata without halting in-flight generation.n - implementation pattern (incremental freeze):n - apply per-shard soft-lock: sets frozentrue for snapshot epoch.n - drain micro-batches for 200-500ms to allow deterministic cache flush ratio for migrated sessions should be 5 for 2m, or sustained p99 2x baseline.nn7) cutover and release (finalize, 1-2 min)n - once targets pass probes and metrics are within thresholds:n - promote routing weight to 100.n - remove redistribute-only tags and re-enable normal admission.n - emit event: incident..rollforward.complete to the incident channel.nn8) post-incident and cleanup (10-30 min)n - deallocate ephemeral prewarm slots.n - archive snapshots with retention policy: keep hot snapshots 7 days, cold snapshots 90 days.n - create incident audit: attach snapshot manifests, metric timelines, and decisions.nnemergency roll-forward (when snapshots incomplete)n--------------------------------------------------n- if snapshot extraction fails for a shard but continuing service is publishedn, doc_id: dsid_5273a23b95744289892cc9ad87d3e850, source_type: confluence, title: priority-driven kernel scheduler: design and runbook, content: summary:nspecification and operational runbook for the priority-driven kernel scheduler used by redwoods serving runtime. covers design rationale, scheduling algorithm, configuration knobs, slo mappings, metric instrumentation, rollout steps, and incident mitigation playbooks for latency and throughput regressions.nnbody:npurpose and scopennthis document defines the priority-driven kernel scheduler (pdks) used in the redwood serving runtime. it describes the design goals, algorithm, configuration surface, expected slo behavior, and operational runbook for on-call engineers and release owners. the pdks module is responsible for deciding kernel assignment, preemption, and batching windows for gpu workers (processes: rw-runtime-worker, rw-batching-proxy), and for enforcing tenant and model-level latency/throughput policies.nnwhy a priority-driven scheduler?nn- production goals: meet 95th/99th percentile latency slos for interactive (chat/generation) workloads while maintaining cost-efficient gpu utilization for background/throughput jobs (embeddings, bulk rerank).n- mixed workload environment: hosted api, dedicated pools, and private clusters all run on the same runtime binary scheduling logic must support strict isolation for dedicated pools and best-effort background work for shared pools.n- operational predictability: explicit priority tiers make rollback and mitigation simpler (e.g., throttle low-priority batching windows rather than kill running kernels).nndesign overviewnn1) priority tiersn- p0 (latency-critical): interactive chat/generation requests with sla/enterprise flags. high preemption weight, small batching windows (configurable min_batch 1), kv cache locality pinned.n- p1 (standard): normal api requests. balanced batching and latency.n- p2 (background): embeddings, bulk transforms, scheduled jobs. large batching windows, throttled when p0/p1 backlog grows.n- p3 (best-effort): offline jobs, non-critical re-runs. lowest priority, allowed to be paused or migrated.nn2) key scheduling primitivesn- kernel assignment: map model_variant - kernel_profile. the kernel selection subsystem consults a per-model kernel_profile table (see config table below) that includes preferred cuda/cublas/cudnn kernels and quantized-code paths.n- preemption policy: preemptibletrue on p1/p2/p3 p0 requests set preemptiblefalse. preemption is implemented via checkpointing kv cache and fast context switch (1030ms target).n- fairshare buckets: soft quotas per-customer and per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbor across p1/p2. buckets are refilled every 60s.n- batching window adjustment: dynamic window adjusts between min_batch and max_batch based on measured inter-arrival time and current slo pressure.nn3) observability surfacen- metrics emitted (prometheus names):n - rw_scheduler_queue_lengthpriorityn - rw_scheduler_avg_batch_sizemodel,priorityn - rw_scheduler_preemptions_totalcausen - rw_kernel_kernel_selection_latency_msn - rw_scheduler_kernel_switch_latency_ms (target 10 of worker queue, scheduler will: (a) reduce batching window to min_batch for affected workers, (b) throttle p2/p3 intake by 50, (c) signal autoscaler with priority reason p0_backlog.n- standard (p1): 95th percentile latency 0 for 3mn2) alert: rw_scheduler_gpu_occupancy_percent 5x in 5m windownnfirst-response checklist (page owner: runtime-oncall)n1) acknowledge pager post to runtime-ops with alert details and diagnostics link.n2) run quick health queries (grafana):n - check rw_scheduler_queue_length by priority and modeln - check rw_scheduler_avg_batch_size and gpu occupancy per noden3) if p0 slo violated:n - execute emergency throttle: curl -x post -d action:throttle,priorities:p2,p3,factor:0.5n - scale up dedicated capacity: run infra script: ./tools/scale_pool --pooldedicated-default --delta2 --reasonp0_slo_emergencyn - if preemptions spiking, check kernel_switch_latency_ms: if 150ms, escalate to infra and gpu-firmware teams.n4) if gpu occupancy low across nodes: check driver logs (/var/log/nvidia-installer.log) and dmesg for ecc/pcie errors consider node drain and gc.nnmitigation flows (detailed)nn- flow a: temporary p2 suspensionn 1. verify backlog levels and confirm p0 impact.n 2. use operator api to set intake_allowedfalse for tags matching background_jobs for 15m.n 3. monitor p0 latency when 99p returns to target for 5 minutes, re-enable intake at 50 and ramp.nn- flow b: kernel-path fallbackn 1. if kernel_selection_latency_ms spikes and model fails to launch optimized kernel, fallback to generic_kernel for affected model_variant via: curl -x post -d model:,to:generic_kerneln 2. notify model-onboarding and performance teams to triage kernel build.nnrollout checklist for changes to scheduler (release owner required)n1) design review completed and reviewers signed off.n2) unit and integration tests in ci: scheduler unit tests, simulated traffic harness with p0/p1/p2 mixes.n3) canary deploy to a single dedicated pool (tag: canary-scheduler-1) with traffic split 1 for 24 hours.n4) run perf harness: ./tools/perf-harness --profileinteractive-heavy --duration30m and validate rw_scheduler_ metrics.n5) gradual ramp: 5 - 20 - 50 - 100 across non-critical pools over 4872h with rollback gates after each step.nntroubleshooting examples (commands)n- inspect per-worker queue: curl -s jq .n- force a kernel-selection dry run: curl -x post -d model:llama2-70b,sequence_length:1024n- dump kv cache stats: docker exec -it rw-worker /bin/sh -c rw-kvtool stats --formatjsonnntesting and benchmarking guidancenn- use the benchmarking suite job-profile: interactive-p0-random (available in perf repo). key expectations: 99p latency for small context ( 32k). future: incremental checkpointing and crdt-style partial restore.n- multi-gpu scheduling: current algorithm optimizes per-gpu workers independently and has suboptimal cross-gpu placement for large model sharding. future: global placement optimizer with communication-cost model.n- heterogeneous hardware: cpu fallback paths for quantized kernels are immature expect 2x latency when falling back to cpu.nnappendicesnna. glossaryn- kv auditable, realtime decision layer that monitors kernel/scheduler health, synthesizes signals across layers, and executes preapproved selfheal actions. the goal is to reduce noisy oncall interrupts for transient kernel noise while providing rapid, reversible remediation for deterministic faults that threaten slos.nnaudience:n- oncall sres and runtime engineersn- kernel and scheduler ownersn- runtime observability and automation engineersnnwhy sho: problem statementn- scheduler-level regressions (priority inversion, admission spikes, kernel starvation) often manifest across multiple signals with non-obvious causality.n- manual triage is slow highly-automated remediation must be conservative, observable, and reversible.n- the sho provides a standard decision contract and safe remediation actions so teams can opt-in with clear guardrails.nnhigh-level designn1) signal ingestion: aggregated telemetry from dispatcher, kernel-profiles, kvcache, gpu telemetry, and network layer.n2) feature synthesis: rolling-error rates, kernel latency percentiles, credit-accounting deltas, slot utilization, and memory pressure indices.n3) heuristic and ml tiers: short ruleset-based checks for high-confidence faults an optional ml model to identify correlated multi-signal anomalies.n4) policy engine: maps detected failure modes to approved remediation actions with associated confidence thresholds.n5) actuation/blocking: dry-run, non-blocking notification, or automatic remediation. all actions are logged to the incident trace and can be rolled back automatically or manually.nndetection signals and thresholds (baseline)n- kernel_cpu_latency_p50/p95/p99 (per-kernel): p95 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m buckets medium severityn- scheduler_queue_depth: sustained 85 of configured capacity for 2m mediumn- kernel_preemptions_rate: increase 3x baseline highn- slot_evictions_per_min: 10/min for a node cohort mediumn- kvcache_warmup_failures: 5 failures within 5m lown- gpu_thermal_throttle: any non-transient throttle event logged by nvml highn- cross-signal rule: if p99 latency increase scheduler_queue_depth spike kernel_preemptions_rate rise immediate canary rollback action at confidence 0.8nnpolicy mapping examplesn- high-confidence gpu thermal throttle (nvml): immediate isolate node (cordon drain policy) action: schedule node cordon, redirect new requests, start evacuation.n- kernel preemption storm (rule-based): lower background priority cohort for 2m, enable cooperative preemption mode action: toggle scheduler param preempt_cooptrue for affected cohort.n- latency increase with kv cache misses: enable kv prefetch hints increase warm pool size by 10 for 10m.n- admission overload (queue depth): enable temporary token-based backpressure: audit.nb) confidence between 0.6 and 0.9 gated remediation: perform non-blocking action (e.g., param tweak plus page to oncall) and run 5m watch.nc) confidence create incident page and alert, no actuation.n4. actuation: perform action using orchestration api (see actuation api spec snippet below).n5. observe: track remediation effect via pre and post windows (1m, 5m, 10m).n6. rollback: if metrics do not improve or regress further, automatically revert parameter and mark as failed remediation.n7. postmortem: automatically create an incident skeleton and assign to the owning team if describes the opportunistic scheduling model and the formal eviction contracts used by the runtime to preserve slos while optimizing for cost and throughput. it combines a design overview, scheduling rules, pragmatic implementation details, a profiling checklist, a benchmarking plan, and an on-call runbook for eviction-related incidents.nngoalsn-----n- preserve 99th percentile tail-latency slos for latency-sensitive routes.n- maximize gpu utilization and reduce per-token cost using opportunistic consolidation.n- provide deterministic, auditable behavior when eviction occurs (handoff warm-up).n- instrumentation and regression checks to detect adverse quality or latency impacts.nnscopen-----nthis document applies to: n- multi-tenant inference runtime on heterogeneous gpu pools.n- scheduler components that make per-request placement decisions and kernel handoff.n- eviction/handoff logic used by the kvcache manager and session lifecycle controller.nnnon-goalsn---------n- low-level kernel optimization details (covered separately in kernel-and-scheduling docs).n- long-term capacity planning (covered in eng-sre/capacity-planning).nnhigh-level designn-----------------n1. priority bands: requests are classified into 3 bands latency-critical (band a), economical-high-throughput (band b), and best-effort/background (band c). classification is a deterministically applied function using request metadata (route, customer tier, model variant, deadline hints).nn2. opportunistic packing: when gpus are underutilized, the scheduler will co-locate band b/c work with band a in non-blocking way using: n - kernel slice isolation (time-sliced or slot-based),n - soft admission tokens (credit-based) andn - kvcache partition isolation to avoid eviction storms.nn3. eviction contracts: for every placement decision a compact, three-field eviction contract is recorded: n - keep_until (wall-clock or token-count),n - restore_cost_budget (estimated extra tokens to rehydrate),n - handoff_policy (none live-migrate graceful-evict-and-warmup).nn4. handoff warmup: for live-migrate or graceful-evict-and-warmup, the scheduler triggers an asynchronous warmup path: prefetch key kvcache prefixes, preload attention cache state where available, and bias routing for a short warming timeframe (configurable).nndesign invariants (must hold)n----------------------------n- deterministic fallback: when capacity shifts, the routing policy must produce consistent placement for identical inputs across a 60s window.n- observability-first: every eviction must emit an evictionevent with unique id, contract fields, pre/post metrics.n- cost-clarity: opportunistic packing must never increase the tail latency of band a routes beyond configured slo delta (default: 5ms).nnscheduler algorithms (summary)n----------------------------n- primary: slot-based allocator with soft priorities. each gpu exposes n time-slots per scheduling epoch. band a gets preemptive access to earliest slots. band b/c fill remaining slots opportunistically.n- secondary: kernel affinity engine selects an execution kernel variant per-slot to maximize occupancy while respecting sequence length breakpoints.n- preemption: cooperative preemption used for in-flight lower-priority requests the runtime supports resumable slices for models that implement slice checkpoints.nneviction contract lifecycle (sequence)n------------------------------------n1. allocate - scheduler writes eviction contract in placement store.n2. emit evictionevent (state: planned).n3. if eviction requested, scheduler evaluates handoff_policy: n - live-migrate: initiate memory-transport protocol (only available for co-located shards and compatible kernels).n - graceful-evict-and-warmup: drain active generation, spawn warmup worker on target gpu.n - none: immediate eviction.n4. emit evictionevent (state: executed) post-metrics.n5. when restored, emit evictionevent (state: restored).nnconfiguration table (defaults and recommended ranges)n-----------------------------------------------------n parameter default recommended range notes n----------------------------------------------n scheduling.epoch_ms 200 50-1000 granularity of slot epochs lower finer preemption but more overhead n scheduling.slots_per_gpu 8 4-32 total logical slots to allocate n eviction.rehydrate_token_budget 1200 200-10000 estimated tokens allowed to restore a session used to prioritize restoration n handoff.timeout_ms 5000 1000-30000 timeout for live-migrate attempts n packing.bandb_util_threshold 0.45 0.2-0.9 if gpu utilization 0.5 over 1h for band a routes - pager (sev2).n2. warmup duration median 1000ms for band a - pager (sev3) ticket.n3. post-eviction tail-latency increase 8ms sustained 15m - pager (sev2).nnprofiling and regression checklistn--------------------------------nrun the following when tuning packing or deploying new scheduler variants: n1. baseline profile capturing pre/post tail latency using production-shadow traces for 1h (use 10 traffic mirroring).n2. instrument kvcache hit/miss per-session and tokens_replayed histogram.n3. run synthetic microbursts (10x baseline qps for 30s) and verify preemption does not increase 99th percentile beyond allowed delta.n4. compare kernel occupancy and slot utilization heatmaps across nodes.nnbenchmarking plann-----------------n- bench goal: show cost-per-1000-token reduction and 99th-latency impact for three workload shapes (short-chat, long-completion, embedding-batch).n- bench matrix: vary packing.bandb_util_threshold across 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, epoch_ms across 100,200,500, and measure metrics for 4 hours.n- success criteria: 10 utilization improvement, and per-token cost decrease 8 vs untuned baseline.nnruntime runbook: eviction spike incidentn---------------------------------------n1. detection: alert fires when eviction error rate configured threshold or post-eviction p99 delta 8ms.n2. initial triage (first 5 minutes): n - check evictionevent stream for correlated ids and decision_reasons.n - identify node(s) with spike: rtmctl node tail-events --since 15m.n3. immediate mitigation (if band a affected): n - disable opportunistic packing on affected pool: rtmctl config set packing.enabledfalse --poolpool-xn - increase scheduling.slots_per_gpu to reduce preemption frequency: rtmctl config set scheduling.slots_per_gpu12 --poolpool-xn4. if warmup failures observed: n - check network transport logs for memory-transport errors.n - re-run warmup manually for top 5 sessions: rtmctl warmup replay --session --target-node n5. post-incident: n - run profiling checklist (see above).n - create postmortem with evacuation timeline, root cause, and follow-ups.nnrollout checklist for scheduler changesn-------------------------------------n1. unit tests for slot allocation, eviction contract write/read, and fallthroughs.n2. staging performance bench with shadow traffic (target: p99 within 3ms of baseline).n3. gradual canary (5 traffic, 30m) with automated rollback if alerts trigger.n4. increment to 25, escalation matrix.n, doc_id: dsid_09696d84762e45329b8f2ef4fdd66b20, source_type: confluence, title: observability injection and kernel validation harness, content: summaryn-------nthis page describes the observability injection and kernel validation harness (oikvh): a lightweight, repeatable framework to verify kernel-level execution correctness, safety, and observability contracts under realistic telemetry perturbations. the goal is to detect regressions that only surface when tracing sampling, sidecar proxies, or sdk instrumentation are enabled in production and to ensure kernel safety nets (fallbacks, handshakes, hedging) continue to meet slo-preservation guarantees.nngoalsn-----n- provide an automated harness to exercise kernels and scheduler paths with controlled observability perturbations (sampling, added latency, dropped events).n- validate observability contracts: trace spans, correlation ids, kernel ids, and event sequencing required by debuggers and autotuners.n- assert that runtime slos (p50, p95, p99 token latency, and error budget consumption) remain within tolerance under injected noise.n- surface silent failures caused by instrumentation (e.g., excessive serialization time, blocking i/o) before rollouts.nnbackground and motivationn-------------------------nreal regressions have been observed where tracing sidecars or extended span annotations introduced cpu/gpu stall contention or increased critical-path latency in specific kernels. those regressions are intermittent and correlate with specific sampling rates and sdk backpressure behavior. the oikvh complements existing microbenchmarks by exercising full request lifecycles under observability stressors and validating both functional outcomes and telemetry integrity.nndesign overviewn---------------nthe harness is composed of four cooperating layers:n1) workload generator: replays synthetic and recorded traces with sequence-length and token-branching distributions.n2) kernel driver: invokes runtime kernel entry points (attention, kv-cache operations, kernel handshakes) with deterministic seeds and controlled input shapes.n3) observability injector: programmatically modifies sampling rates, span size, annotation payloads, and simulates sidecar delays or event drops.n4) assertion engine: collects runtime metrics, traces, logs, and performs deterministic checks for ordering, missing spans, slo regressions and resource anomalies.nnharness components and interfacesn--------------------------------n- harnessctl: cli to configure and launch experiments.n- harness-agent: small in-process shim that can toggle sdk behavior (sync vs async logging, sample rate) at runtime.n- replay-corpus: directory of sampled request traces and generated synthetic workloads.n- assertion-library: a set of reusable checks (latency budgets, kernel-signal presence, kv cache warmup checks).nnoperational diagram (text)n-------------------------n1. harnessctl launches a controller (k8s job or local process).n2. controller schedules n parallel kernel drivers against a test runtime cluster or a mocked harness runtime image.n3. observability injector instruments the runtime via harness-agent and network proxies to inject delays or drop events.n4. assertion engine gathers metrics via prometheus, traces via jaeger/otlp collector, and logs from stdout.nnkey test source_type: confluence, title: quota reshaping and graceful priority revocation spec runbook, content: summarynnthis document specifies the quota reshaping and graceful priority revocation feature for the redwood serving runtime scheduler. the goal is to allow the scheduler to rebalance per-tenant and per-route resource allocations under sustained pressure without causing sharp fidelity drops, slo violations, or oscillatory eviction behavior. the doc contains: design intent, scheduling state machine, metrics instrumentation, operational runbook for incidents, config examples, rollout checklist, and ownership.nnwhy this existsnn- problem: sudden quota exhaustion, tenant burst consolidation, or hardware degradation can force hard evictions that break kv cache consistency, invalidate warmstart assumptions, and produce large p95/p99 latency regressions.n- goal: implement a controlled, observable sequence to reshape quotas and softly revoke priority (i.e., gradually reduce slot weights / kernel credits), providing smooth fidelity degradation and clear recovery paths.nndesign overviewnn1) principle: degrade gracefully, prefer admission control and shaping over instantaneous preemptive evictions.n2) surface: extends scheduler admission controller and kernel admission (credit) layer. two coordinated actions: n - quota reshaping: modify per-cohort quotas (gpu slots / kernel share) based on observed usage and backlog.n - priority revocation (soft): decrement per-request priority multiplier and re-evaluate kernel assignment do not forcibly preempt running kernels unless safety thresholds exceeded.n3) safety: hard-eviction remains a last resort behind multiple guarded checks.nnterminologynn- slot: logical allocation unit for gpu kernel execution (existing).n- credit: kernel-level cpu/gpu time accounting token.n- cohort: grouping (tenant-route-model-version) used for quota accounting.n- soft-revoke: transient decrease of effective priority multiplier used by the scheduler when scoring requests.nnstate machine (high level)nn1) detect: async monitor observes backlog growth, queue latency, kernel queue length, and gpu occupancy.n2) candidate selection: pick cohorts with highest excess tail-impact score (see scoring below).n3) reshape proposal: synthesize a target quota delta for each selected cohort. proposal includes: delta_percent, grace_period_s, rollback_condition_expression.n4) soft-apply: apply soft-revoke by reducing cohort priority by x in increments (step size configurable). track the impact for observation_window_s.n5) confirm/rollback: if p95 latency or fidelity metric regresses beyond configured tolerance, automatically rollback the change. if improvement persists and allowed budget used, commit the reshape to quota service.nnscoring and selectionnnuse a weighted score combining: queue_growth_rate (50), p99_latency_increase (30), recent_error_rate (10), coldstart_fraction (10). normalise each signal and compute: score 0.5g 0.3l 0.1e 0.1c. higher score - higher candidate priority.nnkey metrics instrumentation (names are authoritative)nn- scheduler.quota_reshaper.proposals.count (counter)n- scheduler.quota_reshaper.applied.count (counter)n- scheduler.priority_revocation.step_applied (gauge) current step for cohortn- scheduler.priority_revocation.rollback.count (counter)n- runtime.kv_cache.hit_ratio (gauge) use when deciding safe reshaping targetsn- runtime.p95_latency_ms (histogram) per-cohort, per-routen- scheduler.backlog.size_by_cohort (gauge)n- scheduler.soft_revoke_active (gauge boolean)n- alerts: alert if scheduler.quota_reshaper.rollback.count 3 within 30m for same cohortnnconfig example (yaml)nn--8nnoperational runbook: immediate steps summarynthis document defines the security and isolation model for runtime plugins (extension modules), the scheduler contract that governs plugin execution and preemption, and operational guidance for hardening, profiling and benchmarking plugin-enabled runtime paths. it is intended for runtime engineers, sre, and security reviewers.nngoalsn- allow safe, resource-bounded extensions to the serving runtime (e.g., custom token preprocessors, routing adapters, feature gates) while preserving tenant isolation and slos.n- define a clear scheduler contract so plugin authors and kernel/scheduler teams share expectations about cpu/gpu/io budgets, preemption, and observable signals.n- specify profiling and benchmarking methodology for plugin-enabled experiments to avoid blind spots in latency/cost analyses.nnscopen- applies to: ephemeral plugins loaded into the runtime process or per-request sandboxes (wasm, subprocess, container), scheduler hooks that influence kernel selection, and the profiling/canary paths used during deploys.n- excludes: long-lived persistent sidecars with separate process governance (see appendix for cross-process patterns).nndefinitionsn- plugin: a modular extension that executes during various stages of request processing (preprocess, postprocess, routing).n- sandbox: the isolation boundary for a plugin (wasm runtime, seccomp cgroup, or container).n- execution slot: logical budget allocated by the scheduler for a plugin invocation (time cpu gpu hints ephemerality flag).n- kernel: the runtime component that executes model inference.nnsecurity isolation model (high level)n1) default isolation: all third-party or untrusted plugins must run in a sandboxed environment. approved internal plugins may run in-process only after security review and feature-flag gating.n2) resource cgroups: every sandboxed plugin invocation must be instantiated with a cgroup (cpu quota, memory limit, blkio throttle). suggested defaults are in the config table below.n3) syscall filters: use seccomp policies tailored to each sandbox type prohibit network access unless explicitly requested and approved.n4) filesystem access: sandboxes must mount read-only data volumes write access limited to ephemeral tmpfs with size caps.n5) cryptographic keys: plugin code must not receive plaintext customer keys. any kms/hsm access must be proxied by a runtime rpc that performs auth checks and enforces audit logging.n6) network egress: deny by default. egress rules require an allowlist and audit trail (team ticket id).nnrecommended cgroup defaults (table)n parameter recommended default rationale n-------------------------------:----------n cpu_quota 100ms per invocation bounds cpu tail latency when many small plugin calls occur n memory_limit 64mb prevents per-request memory blowups increase only with review n blkio_weight 50 (out of 1000) limits disk pressure from plugins during retries or dumps n pids_max 32 prevents fork bombs from exhausting node resources n ephemeral_tmp_size 8mb prevents uncontrolled temp file growth nnscheduler contract (concise)n- scheduler shall advertise per-invocation execution slots with the following attributes: slot_id, cpu_budget_ms, wall_time_deadline_ms, priority_class, preemptible:true/false, affinity_hint. plugin runtime must accept these attributes at start and enforce budget locally.n- plugins must check remaining_budget_ms on each yield point (documented below) and abort gracefully returning a standardized status: plugin.timeout or plugin.preempted.n- preemption semantics: when the scheduler reclaims a slot, the plugin process/wasm runtime must receive a soft-signal (sigusr1-equivalent) and begin controlled shutdown within soft_shutdown_ms (default 20ms). if soft shutdown does not complete, the hard-kill path triggers after hard_kill_ms (default 150ms).n- affinity and locality: plugins that request gpu hints must annotate affinity_hint the scheduler may reject or remap hints to keep kernel scheduling deterministic.nnplugin lifecycle and api checklistn1. manifest: every plugin bundle must include a manifest.yaml with: name, version, author, declared_api_surface (pre/post/routing), declared_resource_hints, required_capabilities (network, file_write), and signing_checksum. example manifest snippet: nnmanifest.yamln---nname: redwood.token-filternversion: 0.3.1nauthor: internal:token-teamnapi: preprocessnresource_hints:n cpu_ms: 20n memory_mb: 16ncapabilities: network:false, file_write:falsensignature: sha256:...nn2. signing provenance: plugin bundles must be signed by an approved build pipeline. the runtime verifies the signature against a rotation-aware public key list at load time.n3. static analysis: run the plugin through the sandbox-targeted static analyzer (see pipeline job: eng-serving-runtime/plugin-static-check).n4. canary: deploy plugin in a canary with 1 of traffic, run the profiling and tail-latency checks described later, and only escalate to broader rollout after meeting slos for 48 hours.nnyield points and cooperative preemptionn- yield points are the only safe locations where user code may check budgets: after deserialize, after tokenization, and before issuing kernel offload. for wasm plugins, provide a host function check_budget() which returns remaining_budget_ms and allows early return.n- cooperative window: plugin code must assume that a hard preemption may occur at any syscall boundary keep critical sections small and idempotent.nnobservability profiling requirementsn- telemetry emitted per invocation: plugin.id, invocation.id, slot_id, start_ts, end_ts, cpu_ms_user, cpu_ms_sys, memory_peak_mb, decision_trace (max 512 chars), status.n- traces: span naming convention: runtime.plugin... include kernel hint tags when applicable.n- sampling: for production, sample all plugin failures and 0.5 of successful calls during canary increase sampling to 100 for the first 10k invocations or 24h.n- profiling: capture wall time cpu time histograms keep p90/p99 deltas before and after plugin enablement as part of the benchmark report.nnbenchmark canary checklist (step-by-step)n1) baseline: run a 24h synthetic run of the target workload without the plugin. capture per-route p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token.n2) synthetic plugin run: enable plugin on a shadow copy of traffic at 0x cost impact and measure overhead with production kernels.n3) canary rollout: 1 traffic (multi-az). monitor plugin metrics runtime slos for 48h. key thresholds: p99 increase baseline 5 sustained for 2 minutes.n2) immediate mitigation: disable plugin routing flag for affected route (cli: rwdctl runtime plugin disable --route x --plugin name).n3) trace collection: snapshot last 500 traces with trace-ids tagged plugintrue and upload to /var/tmp/plugin-triage/.n4) revert decision: if disabling returns slos to normal within 3 minutes, keep disabled and create p0 incident. if no change, escalate to scheduler oncall.n5) post-incident: run the profiling checklist and attach findings to incident record.nnrunbook: plugin resource runaway (memory or cpu)n1) pager triggers on node-level oom_kill or cpu_throttle 70 sustained.n2) isolate: scheduler should mark node as cordoned_for_plugins and start draining plugin-invocations to new nodes.n3) kill policy: notify plugin owner_team via automated page issue soft-kill to plugin processes and escalate to hard kill after hard_kill_ms.n4) recovery: autoscale replacement nodes if needed and run kernel-level health checks.nnhardening checklist for security reviewn- ensure manifest signature validated and build provenance recorded.n- verify seccomp/capabilities are the minimal set for declared features.n- confirm no direct kms keys are provisioned into plugin environment.n- run fuzzing for 72h using the runtime plugin-fuzz harness (job: eng-serving-runtime/plugin-fuzz-72h).n- confirm telemetry contains at least 8 fields listed in observability section and uses redaction policy for pii.nnexample scheduler-policy fragment (yaml)n---npolicy_name: plugin-defaultsnpriority_classes:n - name: latency-sensitiven cpu_budget_ms: 50n preemptible: falsen - name: backgroundn cpu_budget_ms: 100n preemptible: truenhard_kill_ms: 150nsoft_shutdown_ms: 20nmax_concurrent_plugins_per_node: 64nntesting harness commandsn- build and sign plugin: tools/plugin_builder --build ./pkg --sign --key-id ci-plugin-key-02n- run unit sandbox locally: tools/sandbox_runner --bundle ./out/redwood.token-filter.tar.gz --profile debug --max-invocations 1000n- canary enable: rwdctl runtime plugin enable --plugin redwood.token-filter --route reviews-api --percent 1 --reason canary token-filter v0.3.1nnownership slan- plugin runtime and scheduler teams own the enforcement code and telemetry emitters.n- plugin authoring teams own their manifests, static analysis fixes, and canary configuration.n- slos preserved: no plugin deploy should increase route p99 by more than 5 absolute or add 0.1pp error-rate without explicit senior eng approval.nnappendix a: cross-process plugin patternsnif a plugin requires long-lived resources or external network egress, prefer a separate service with an authenticated, audited rpc. the rpc should be rate-limited and expose a per-request cost budget. this pattern isolates faults and allows independent scaling.nnappendix b: troubleshooting quick referencen- symptom: plugin not starting under and bindings spec, content: overview:nnpurposen- define the translation layer and binding registry that enable safe automatic fallback and translation between heterogeneous accelerator backends and the reference gpu kernel paths in the redwood serving runtime.n- provide operational policies, slo impact modeling, telemetry contract, and rollout steps for enabling the feature across hosted and dedicated pools.nnscopen- applies to kernel dispatch paths that may execute on: nvidia gpus (cuda/cublas/cudnn tensor cores), amd rocm, third-party accelerators with vendor sdks (e.g., habana, graphcore), and cpu-quantized fallback paths.n- includes design for a runtime translation shim, per-accelerator binding manifests, quality gating, and scheduler integration points.n- excludes model training and developer sdks covers inference-only serving runtime and operator interactions.nnbackground and motivationn- our runtime must support a growing set of accelerator types while preserving predictable latency and correctness. different accelerators expose different kernel semantics (data layout, tile sizes, fused op availability).n- rather than maintaining fully separate codepaths per accelerator, the translation layer provides:n - deterministic, validated translations of dispatch descriptors (shard shapes, datatype, op flags) into vendor-specific kernel hints,n - a bindings registry describing capability levels and quality-compatibility for each accelerator, andn - fallback policies the scheduler uses to preserve slos when preferred backends fail or degrade.nndesign goalsn1. safety: never violate model numerical correctness guarantees beyond a bounded epsilon defined per-model/config.n2. observability: every translation and fallback decision must emit structured telemetry for slo attribution and regression detection.n3. locality: translation must be cheap ( cuda-compat shim - quantized-cpu) with clear rollback semantics.nnhigh-level architecturen- components:n - translation-shim: a lightweight service in the serving process that maps canonical dispatch descriptors to backend-specific call signatures and kernel hints.n - binding-registry: static manifests that enumerate per-accelerator capability (supported dtypes, fused ops, effective throughput, fidelity tier).n - bind-manager (scheduler plugin): consults binding-registry at placement time and annotates requests with ordered backend candidates and max-fidelity constraints.n - fallback-orchestrator: runbook-aware state machine that executes recovery sequences (rebind, degrade quantization, divert to regional pool).nnarchitecture diagram (textual):n- client - ingress - request-classifier - bind-manager - kernel-dispatcher - translation-shim - vendor-kernel - acceleratorn- fallback path: translation-shim - fallback-orchestrator - (alternate vendor-kernel quantized-cpu)nnbinding registry format (yaml example)n- purpose: machine-readable capability manifest used by bind-manager and translation-shim.nnbinding_manifest: n accelerator_id: nvidia-a100-80gbn vendor: nvidian capability_version: v1n supported_dtypes: fp16, bf16, int8-quantizedn fused_ops: layernorm_fused, attention_fusedn performance_profile:n - sequence_len: 512n tokens_per_sec: 12kn tail_p95_ms: 5.2n fidelity_tier: highn fallback_compatible_with: cuda-compat-shim, cpu-quantized-pathnncompatibility matrix (samples)n accelerator_id fp16 bf16 int8 fused-attn gpu-kernel-compat n-------------------------------------------------------------------------n nvidia-a100-80gb yes yes no yes native n amd-mi250 yes partial no partial shim n habana-gaudi-2 no partial yes no shim nncapability levels in the registry are annotated with one of: native, shim, partial, none.nntranslation shim responsibilities and apin- input: canonical dispatch descriptor (model id, op sequence id, tensor shapes, dtypes, requested fidelity).n- output: vendor-specific call descriptor (kernel id, workspace bytes, launch grid), plus a quality-estimate score.n- local checks: validate workspace fits memory budget, simulate small representative kernels on a cached microprofile to update per-request latency expectation.n- api (pseudo-cli):n curl -x post n -d model:gpt-small,op:attention,shape:1,512,4096,dtype:bf16nntelemetry contract (events emitted)n- translation.requested model, op, requested_fidelity, bind_candidatesn- translation.resolved chosen_backend, affinity, estimated_latency_msn- fallback.invoked original_backend, fallback_backend, playbook documents the token-aware scheduler (tas) telemetry contract, production safety checks, and step-by-step fallback and mitigation procedures used by the serving runtime. tas is the scheduler layer that considers request token counts, sequence-length distributions, and per-request slo budgets when assigning kernels and shaping batching windows. the goal of this document is to make the scheduler-to-runtime observable, auditable, and safe for rapid rollouts without surprising regressions in tail latency or model fidelity.nngoals and scopenn- define the telemetry signals required by (engineering)n- primary oncall: runtime-sren- secondary: inference-platform-teamn- reviewer group: perf-eng, observabilitynnkey concepts and definitionsnn- request token shape: observed pair prompt_tokens, completion_budget used to pick batching window and kernel hints.n- kernel hint: metadata tag passed to runtime indicating preferred execution variant (float16/quantized/sharded-attn variant).n- batching window: the time horizon tas holds requests to form a batch adaptive to token shape and slo.n- fidelity clamp: policy that gracefully reduces model variant (e.g., smaller model or lower precision) to preserve slos.nnrequired telemetry (contract)nnall signals must be emitted at request decision time and at kernel completion. these are structured as key/value tags in the trace and as metrics in prometheus/otel.nn- request.id (string)n- request.arrival_ts (epoch-ms)n- request.token_estimate (int)n- request.completion_budget_tokens (int)n- request.priority_tier (string) runtime.kernel_handshake_failures counter (labels: reason)n- runtime.fidelity_actions_total counter (labels: action,reason)n- tas.batch_window_ms gaugennsafety thresholds and deterministic rulesnnthe scheduler enforces these safety constraints before committing a request to a batch and emitting the kernel_hint.nn1) kernel compatibility gaten- if runtime reports kernel_handshake_failures 5 in last 1m for chosen kernel_hint, mark hint as degraded and pick next compatible variant. if no variant available, fallback to model-fallback.nn2) token-window slo guardn- if scheduler.predicted_latency_ms slo_target 0.9 for the request.priority_tier, reduce batching_window_ms by 50 for the next 30s for that tenant-model pair.nn3) memory-pressure guardn- if runtime.memory_pressure_levelhigh on the increase preemption priority for critical requests, spin up additional execution slots.n- quantization fallback: switch kernel_hint to a quantized execution path (q4/q8) if the model variant has been validated for the tenant. label action in telemetry: fidelity_actionquantize.n- model fallback: route to a smaller/compatible model variant. must attach a quality-warning header to downstream callers scenarios: design runbook, content: overviewnnpurpose: this document describes the economic priority governor (epg) a scheduling policy component that combines token-cost signals, per-tenant budgets, slos, and priority tiers to make admission, throttling, and graceful-degradation decisions in redwoods serving runtime. it includes design rationale, policy examples, a rollout/test plan, observable contract, and a practical incident/runbook for when degradation modes trigger.nnaudience: runtime engineers, sres, product owners for dedicated/private tiers, and on-call responders.nnsummary of behaviornn- the epg takes as input: request priority, tenant token-budget metadata, model variant cost estimate, current per-gpu/kv cache pressure, and slo health signals.n- it evaluates a scoring function that yields one of: allow, delay (micro-burst queue), degrade (route to cheaper model variant or quantized path), or reject.n- degradation modes are tiered and reversible the governor records decisions and exposes a decision trace for postmortem.nndesign goals and constraintsnn1) slo preservation: keep p95 latency and error-rate slos for high-priority users where feasible.n2) cost predictability: prevent runaway cost from low-priority or uncontrolled workloads.n3) graceful degradation: prefer fidelity stair-step (model-quantize-cached-response) rather than blackholing traffic.n4) observability: each decision must emit a decisiontrace event with inputs and reason codes.nndecision inputs and data modelnn- request.priority: enum (urgent, interactive, background)n- tenant.budget_window_usd_per_hour: numeric (configured per-tenant)n- model.variant.cost_per_ktoken_usd: numeric (runtime catalog metadata)n- gpu_utilization_pct: rolling 30s averagen- resource_pressurenninterpretation: lower score - more aggressive degradation. we tune weights (w_) via a/b simulation experiments documented below.nnpolicy configuration (example table, expressed in temporary per-tenant throttle: redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant-id --qps 10 --duration 15mnn4) deeper diagnosisn - replay decisiontrace logs via the epg simulator (see testing and simulation) to reproduce policy decisions.n - check for model catalog mis-priced variants (cost_per_ktoken drift) and measurement anomalies in cost model.n - confirm kv cache hit-rate low hit-rate may force model summaryn-------nthis playbook describes the capacity safeguard and quality delegation mechanisms the runtime scheduler uses to preserve customer slos while minimizing cost. it is intended for runtime engineers, on-call sres, and product owners responsible for routing and tiering policies. the document covers design intent, concrete admission-control configurations, emergency mitigation steps for spikes and noisy tenants, and a test matrix for rollout validation.nngoals and scopen----------------n- preserve 95th/99th latency slos for paid tiers under bursty traffic.n- minimize unnecessary apply to hosted, dedicated, and private modes (differences noted).nnterminologyn-----------n- slot: logical gpu time window available to a request unit used by admission controller.n- fidelity: an abstraction combining model variant (e.g., base/quantized/ distilled), token budgeting, and sampling temperature.n- quality delegation: controlled, policy-driven decision to lower fidelity for non-critical traffic to preserve slos for higher-tier traffic.n- safeguard pool: reserved slots (percentage of cluster) kept aside for high-priority traffic and emergency backfills.nndesign overviewn---------------n1) two-tier slot accountingn - fast path slots: low-latency, prewarmed kernels with kv cache affinity. targets 12 gpu hops.n - bulk slots: high-throughput, higher-latency buckets for best-effort work (large batches, background embedding jobs).nn2) safeguard pool and soft-reservationn - default: 8 of capacity marked as safeguard pool cluster-wide. this is configurable by offering and region.n - soft-reservation semantics: safeguard pool drains preferentially to fast-path requests when utilization 92.nn3) quality delegation policy enginen - decision inputs: request_priority, customer_tier, model_variant_cost, current_latency_headroom, recent_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate.n - delegation actions: model downgrade (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant), reduce max_output_tokens, switch to cached-prefix generation, or return synthetic fallback.nnconfiguration examplesn----------------------nbelow is a representative admission controller policy (yaml). use
