title: kernel auto-selection v2 design, content: h1. kernel auto-selection v2 designnnowner: yuki sato (runtime kernels)ndesign leads: hiro tanaka (kernels), noah patel (architecture/perf correctness)nprimary stakeholders: sofia ivanova (scheduling), lena fischer (workload regime characterization), omar el-sayed (tail-latency/observability), marcus reed (perf validation), ethan park (control-plane gates)nnh2. 1) summarynkernel auto-selection v2 (selector v2) updates the serving runtime kernel selection logic to be explicitly keyed on:n1) model family/architecture (e.g., llama-family vs mistral-family vs qwen-family vs gemma-family)n2) sequence length regime (prefill/decode characteristics and buckets)n3) gpu type/sku (a100/h100/l40s variants, incl. mig where applicable)nnthe intent is to reduce p95/p99 latency and improve throughput stability across heterogeneous fleets while preserving:n- correctness (no numerical/caching correctness regressions)n- determinism (same inputs - same selection decision)n- operational safety (fast rollback overrides)nnselector v2 ships behind feature gates, with allowlist/denylist controls by model gpu sku region.nnh2. 2) motivation / problem statementnselector v1 has grown organically and primarily selects kernels using a limited feature set (mostly model size a coarse prefill/decode heuristic). this has resulted in:n- mis-selections in long-context workloads (tail latency spikes when a kernel is optimal for short prompts but degrades for large prefill)n- sku sensitivity (kernels that are stable on h100 may regress on l40s some a100 variants differ in optimal kernel choice)n- hard-to-debug incidents (selection decisions are not sufficiently observable per request hard to reproduce in staging)n- rollout friction (lack of targeted controls increases blast radius)nnselector v2 makes feature extraction explicit, selection rules auditable, and fallbacks guaranteed.nnh2. 3) goals and non-goalsnh3. goalsn- performance: reduce p95/p99 latency and reduce variance in decode throughput across mixed workloads.n- stability: prevent tail latency spikes from long-context misclassification.n- safety: safe fallbacks when a kernel is unavailable, unstable, or unsupported for a given gpu sku / driver / model.n- determinism replayability: selection decisions must be reproducible and stable given identical inputs and config.n- observability: emit per-request selection decision telemetry with bounded overhead.n- operational controls: feature-gated rollout and hot-reloadable allow/deny lists.nnh3. non-goalsn- learning-based kernel selection (out of scope for v2 see adr-017 for rationale).n- changing the scheduler policy itself (selector consumes scheduler hints scheduling remains authoritative for batching/placement).n- automatic kernel compilation at request time (selector only chooses among registered kernels / precompiled variants).nnh2. 4) current behavior (selector v1)nselector v1 (simplified):n- inputs: model identifier, estimated prefill length, estimated max output tokens, some runtime flags.n- behavior:n - picks one attention kernel family (e.g., flash-attn vs baseline) and a small set of fused ops if enabled.n - performs minimal hardware branching (h100 vs other) and relies on defaults for most skus.n - has implicit fallbacks spread across multiple call sites.n- gaps:n - no explicit model-family classification model variants can land in the wrong bucket.n - coarse seq-length logic (short/long threshold) does not handle mixed workloads.n - limited per-request traceability.nnh2. 5) proposed approach (selector v2)nselector v2 is a rule-based decision engine with:n- a normalized feature vector extracted from request model metadata hardware metadata.n- a kernel registry mapping (model_family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket, op_set) - candidate kernels.n- a deterministic decision procedure that produces:n - chosen_kernel_set (attention fused ops package)n - fallback_reason (if not using preferred kernel)n - selection_version (for audit/replay)nnh3. 5.1 high-level architecture placementnselection occurs at plan construction time (before execution), after:n- model is resolved (including version pin)n- hardware runtime reports gpu propertiesn- scheduler provides optional workload hintsnnselection result is cached (bounded) by:n(model_id, model_revision, gpu_sku_norm, driver_norm, seq_bucket, selector_config_hash)nnh2. 6) inputs and feature signalsnh3. 6.1 model family / architecture classificationnwe introduce a model-family classifier that produces:n- model_family: llama, mistral, qwen, gemma, othern- architecture_tags: list (e.g., rope_variant, gqa/mqa, kv_head_count, hidden_size bucket)nnprimary sources:n- model manifest (preferred)n- runtime introspection of model config (fallback)nnnotes:n- classification must be deterministic and stable across model aliases.n- for unknown models, familyother and we default to conservative kernels.nnh3. 6.2 sequence length regime and bucketsnwe bucket requests using a combination of:n- prefill_tokens_est (prompt length)n- decode_tokens_est (expected output / max_tokens)n- optional scheduler_hint: observed_workload_seq_histogramnndefine seq_bucket (initial):n- s: prefill 8192nnadditionally define workload_mode:n- prefill_heavy (prefill dominates)n- decode_heavy (decode dominates)n- mixed/unknownnnguardrail:n- if prefill_tokens_est is missing/unknown, bucketunknown and select a safe baseline kernel.nnh3. 6.3 gpu sku normalizationnwe normalize gpu identity into gpu_sku_norm and capability tags:n- gpu_family: a100, h100, l40s, othern- sm_version: e.g., 80, 90n- hbm_gb (rounded bucket)n- mig_profile (if mig enabled otherwise none)n- driver_norm cuda_norm (coarse versions for known-unstable blocks)nnnormalization rules (initial):n- treat a100 40gb vs 80gb as same family but different hbm bucket for memory-sensitive kernels.n- for mig: include profile string (e.g., 1g.10gb) to avoid selecting kernels requiring larger shared resources.nnh2. 7) kernel registry and candidate generationnh3. 7.1 registry structurenthe registry provides candidates per (op, model_family, gpu_sku_norm, seq_bucket):n- attention_kernels: ordered listn- kv_cache_kernels: ordered listn- fused_ops_package: ordered listnneach candidate has metadata:n- supports: model_tags, gpu_tags, seq_constraintsn- stability: ga, canary, experimental, blockedn- constraints: min_driver, max_driver, requires_migfalse, max_prefill_tokensnnh3. 7.2 candidate generationnfor each op category:n1) filter kernels by hard constraints (support version blocks).n2) sort by preference order (rule-based, per gpu family and seq bucket).n3) return candidate list rationale.nnh2. 8) decision logicnselector v2 is deterministic and rule-based. at a high level:nnstep a extract featuresn- model_family, architecture_tagsn- seq_bucket, workload_moden- gpu_sku_norm, driver_norm, cuda_normnnstep b build candidatesn- for attention: preferred list for (model_family, gpu_family, seq_bucket)n- apply denylist blocks (kernel_id, gpu_sku_norm, driver_norm, model_id)nnstep c choosen- choose the first candidate that passes constraints and is not blocked.n- if none pass, fall back to baseline.nnstep d emit selection recordn- selected_attention_kernel_idn- selected_fused_ops_package_idn- candidate_ids (possibly sampled)n- feature vector (redacted/hashed where needed)n- selection_version config_hashnnh3. 8.1 example rule sketch (illustrative)n- if gpu_familyh100 and seq_bucket in s,m and model_family in llama,mistral,qwen:n - prefer attentionflashattn_v2_sm90n- if seq_bucket in l,xl:n - prefer attentionpaged_attn_smxx_longctx (if supported) else flashattn_v2 with longctx parametersn- if gpu_familyl40s:n - prefer attentionflashattn_v2_sm89_tuned (if stable) else baseline_attnnn(concrete kernel ids and tuning parameters are maintained in the registry the selector references them by stable id.)nnh2. 9) fallback hierarchy (safety first)nwe formalize a single fallback hierarchy to remove implicit, distributed fallbacks.nnh3. 9.1 fallback precedencenif preferred kernel is unavailable/blocked/unsupported, fall back in this order:n1) same kernel family, conservative parameters (e.g., disable aggressive tiling)n2) alternate high-performance kernel validated for sku (e.g., flash-attn - paged-attn or vice versa, per registry)n3) baseline attention implementation (reference path) with conservative fused ops disabledn4) emergency safe mode: baseline attention disable non-essential fusions force safe kv cache behaviornnh3. 9.2 reasons for fallback (telemetry enum)n- kernel_not_registeredn- kernel_blocked_by_denylistn- gpu_unsupportedn- driver_blockedn- seq_bucket_unsupportedn- model_tag_unsupportedn- validation_gate_not_passed (e.g., kernel marked canary-only)nnh3. 9.3 guaranteenselector v2 must always produce a valid executable plan if the runtime supports the model at all. if the model is unsupported, fail early with an explicit error (do not loop through kernels).nnh2. 10) determinism guaranteesndeterminism is a hard requirement for debugging and for dedicated/private customers.nnh3. 10.1 deterministic selection definitionngiven the same:n- model_id model_revisionn- request-derived features (prefill_tokens_est, decode_tokens_est) and scheduler hints (if enabled)n- normalized hardware identity (gpu_sku_norm, driver_norm, cuda_norm)n- selector_config (including allow/deny lists)nnthe selector must return the same selection result.nnh3. 10.2 guardrails to enforce determinismn- feature extraction must be pure (no time-based or random inputs).n- candidate ordering must be stable and not depend on hash-map iteration.n- all config inputs used for selection must be captured in selector_config_hash.n- if scheduler hints are used, the hint must be a stable, serialized snapshot value (not a moving pointer).nnh3. 10.3 replaynwe define a selection replay record that can be captured (sampled) and replayed locally:n- feature vectorn- kernel registry snapshot versionn- selector_config_hashn- resulting kernel idsnnh2. 11) observability and telemetrynh3. 11.1 required per-request fields (sampled)n- selector_version (e.g., v2)n- selection_config_hashn- model_id, model_familyn- gpu_sku_norm, driver_norm, cuda_normn- seq_bucket, workload_moden- selected_attention_kernel_idn- fallback_reason (if any)nnh3. 11.2 optional fields (more aggressively sampled)n- candidate_kernel_idsn- candidate_filter_reasons (top-n)n- selection_latency_us (selector evaluation overhead)nnh3. 11.3 sampling and overheadn- default sampling: 0.1 per route/model, with ability to increase temporarily during canary/debug.n- hard cap: do not exceed 1 by default in hosted dedicated/private adjustable via config.n- selector evaluation time budget: p50 pool region globalnnh3. 12.2 allowlist / denylistn- allowlist: enable v2 only for specified model families/models during rollout.n- denylist: block specific (kernel_id, gpu_sku_norm, driver_norm, model_id) combinations.n- hot reload: supported with bounded propagation time (target n- cli/runtime flag: --dump_kernel_selectionnpinning must:n- bypass the selector for the pinned opn- still validate hard constraints (fail fast if truly incompatible)nnh2. 13) performance / correctness validation plan (design-level)nsee benchmark matrix page for full coverage. at a design level, v2 requires:n- microbench: selector overhead and kernel switch overhead boundsn- macrobench: end-to-end p95/p99 latency and throughput across:n - model families: llama/mistral/qwen/gemman - seq buckets: s/m/l/xl with mixed distributionsn - gpu skus: a100/h100/l40s ( common variants)nnpass/fail gates (initial, subject to sre review):n- no correctness regressions (golden output kv cache invariants)n- error rate not worse than v1 (p99 absolute threshold)n- p99 latency regression budget: 3 requires explicit signoff denylist or rule adjustmentnnh2. 14) risks and mitigationsn- risk: long-context misclassification leads to tail spikes.n - mitigation: conservative thresholds xl bucket forced safe kernels add explicit longctx guardrail canary focused on long-context routes.nn- risk: gpu sku normalization misses a variant (e.g., cloud naming mismatch).n - mitigation: normalization unit tests with known sku strings log raw gpu name in debug traces default to safe kernels on unknown sku.nn- risk: telemetry cardinality blow-up.n - mitigation: stable normalized gpu strings sample candidate lists limit tag dimensions review with observability team.nn- risk: nondeterminism due to scheduler hints.n - mitigation: treat hints as optional require snapshot serialization fallback to request-derived estimates.nnh2. 15) open questionsn1) seq bucket thresholds: are the s/m/l/xl thresholds appropriate across our customer mix, especially for summarization and rag workloads?n2) mixed workload handling: should we bias selection toward prefill-heavy safety when scheduler hints indicate a long-tail of xl prompts?n3) mig support policy: do we treat mig as a first-class sku_sublabel in all environments or disallow v2 by default on mig until coverage improves?n4) driver/cuda blocks: what is the minimal safe set of driver_norm blocks at launch (avoid overblocking and losing perf gains)?n5) registry ownership and update cadence: who owns the steady-state updates of kernel preference ordering (kernels vs perf/evals vs release eng), and how do we gate changes?n6) cache key stability: are we comfortable with caching decisions by (seq_bucket) only, or do we need additional bucketing by decode_tokens_est for certain kernels?nnh2. 16) appendix: pseudocode (selector)ncodenfunction select_kernels_v2(request, model, hw, scheduler_hint, config):n feats extract_features(request, model, confluence, title: scheduler policy language (spl) and declarative profile library, content: overviewnnthis page introduces the scheduler policy language (spl): a compact, declarative format for expressing kernel scheduling and resource partitioning intent in the redwood serving runtime. spl is intended for runtime operators and product/infra owners who need predictable slos, multi-tenant fairness, and reproducible rollbackable scheduling changes without modifying code paths in the dispatcher or kernel selector.nngoalsn- provide a human-readable policy dsl that maps to runtime kernel scheduling primitives (priority, batch slicing, preemption windows, kernel selector hints).n- make tenant-level slos, cost tiers, and fallback policies first-class and auditable.n- enable safe staged rollouts via validation, dry-run, and automatic fallback to default profiles.n- support observability mapping: each policy declares the metrics and traces it depends on and the telemetry it will emit.nnquick summaryn- spl is yaml-first (examples below) with a strict type schema enforced by the runtime controller.n- policies live in the configstore (git-backed), validated by the policy service, and pushed to dispatchers as signed bundles.n- key concepts: profile, rule, target, threshold, kernel_hint, preempt_window, admission_bucket.nnwhen to use spln- constraining latency for high-priority endpoints (e.g., chat-completion interactive)n- guaranteeing fair gpu time slices across customers in dedicated clustersn- implementing cold-start soft-limits and warmup prioritiesn- expressing region/instance-specific kernel selection preferences for cost-saving quantized variantsnnspl primitives (human description)n- profile: a named collection of rules and defaults. profiles are versioned.n- target: selector expression that matches request attributes (route, model, customer_tier, region).n- rule: an ordered policy clause (match - action) with a priority and safety guard.n- action parameters: priority_level, batch_cap, preempt_window_ms, kernel_hint, cache_weight, fallback_sequence.n- threshold metrics: p50, p95, cpu_ms_per_token, token_rate, queue_length.nnexample policy (yaml)n enforce interactive-latency profile for platinum customers using gpt-4x variantsnprofile: interactive-platinum-v1ndescription: preserve 99th percentile tail latency for interactive endpoints owned by platinum customersnversion: 2026-02-01nrules:n - target:n route: /v1/chat/completionsn customer_tier: platinumn model_family: gpt-4xn match: truen actions:n priority_level: 1 1highest, larger numbers lower priorityn batch_cap: 8n preempt_window_ms: 12n kernel_hint: fp16-low-latencyn cache_weight: 0.9n safety_guards:n - metric: p95_latency_msn operator: ) valuen- target : attribute: value, ... n- match : boolean or expression combining selectors with and/orn- action : priority_level: int, batch_cap: int, preempt_window_ms: int, kernel_hint: str, cache_weight: float n- safety_guard : metric: string, operator: one-of(, ), value: number nnvalidation matrix (controller checks)n1) schema validation: required fields present, types correct.n2) semantic validation: batch_cap within 1, 256, preempt_window_ms within 0, 2000, cache_weight in 0.0,1.0.n3) slo collision check: if two profiles target same routetier with overlapping windows, require explicit decision (priority or merge).n4) kernel hint compatibility: warn if kernel_hint maps to an unsupported kernel on the target pool.nntable: allowed ranges and default valuesn- priority_level: int, allowed 1..100, default 50n- batch_cap: int, allowed 1..512, default 16n- preempt_window_ms: int, allowed 0..2000, default 100n- cache_weight: float, allowed 0.0..1.0, default 0.5n- admission_bucket: string, allowed interactive, burst, batch, low_cost, default batchnnruntime behavior and mappingn- the dispatcher reconciler converts an spl profile into a policy bundle per node pool. a bundle contains: compiled match tree, action table, and telemetry hooks.n- priority levels are translated to scheduler lanes lower numeric priority is scheduled ahead of higher numbers.n- preempt_window_ms defines the soft window in which a running kernel can be preempted and requeued with cooperative preemption handshake. values larger than 500ms are reserved for long-running batch jobs.n- batch_cap interacts with the kernel-slicer to decide whether to use continuous batching (low-latency path) or slice-per-batch (throughput path).nnoperational concerns and playbook steps (change management)n1) author policy in the policy repo branch. add unit tests using the policy validator harness.n2) open pr and assign eng-serving-runtime and sre reviewers.n3) run policylint and policysim locally: ./tools/policylint policy.yaml then ./tools/policysim --profile policy.yaml --trace sample-trace.jsonn4) dry-run deploy to canary pool: push bundle with tag canary and enable dry-run mode (no active enforcement, emits telemetry).n5) observe metrics for 24-72 hours (p50/p95 latency, queue_length, eviction_rate, preempt_count).n6) if metrics are within expected bounds, promote to staged rollout (10 - 50 - 100) with automated rollback triggers defined below.n7) on rollback, use policyctl rollback --to controller will resume previous bundle atomically.nnautomated rollback triggers (recommended defaults)n- p95 latency increase 15 sustained for 15 minutes.n- preempt_count increase 3x baseline in 10 minutes.n- gpu_memory_util_pct 95 for longer than 2 minutes.nntesting and benchmarksn- each policy should include representative trace inputs in policies/test_traces/. use the benchmarking harness to simulate traffic across sequences (long-form, short-chat, bursty embeddings).n- recommended benchmark matrix:n - short interactive: 8k requests, seqs 32 tokens avg, target p95 5 of dispatched kernels in 1 minute, it will automatically replace kernel_hint with the nearest compatible variant and emit policy.kernel_hint_fallback event.n- a profile can declare a fallback_sequence (ordered list of profile names). when resource pressure triggers, runtime will progressively demote the request to the next profile in sequence.nnsecurity and signingn- policy bundles are signed with the policy service key. dispatchers reject unsigned or expired bundles.n- access to the policy repo is rbac-gated: only owners in infra-schedulers and platform-owners may merge to main.nnmigration notes for existing configsn- the controller will import legacy priority jsons via policyctl import-legacy --source legacy-priorities.json and map top-level fields to a profile with version migrated-. manual review is required for kernel_hint translation.nnownership and contactsn- primary author: aisha patel (eng-serving-runtime)n- operational owner: sre (oncall rotation, contact via pager duty team sre-serving)n- kernel-variant mapping owner: kernel team (kernel-team@redwood.ai)nnappendix: example policysim output (abbreviated)n- summary: 95th latency delta: 4.2 (expected)n- preempt events: 12 per minute - stable under thresholdn- kernel fallback events: 2 (kernel_hint - fp16-fallback)nncli snippetsn- validate: ./tools/policylint path/to/policy.yamln- simulate: ./tools/policysim --policy path/to/policy.yaml --trace traces/platinum-chat-2026.jsonn- deploy (canary): policyctl apply --profile interactive-platinum-v1 --env canary --dry-runfalsen- rollback: policyctl rollback --profile interactive-platinum-v1 --to interactive-platinum-v0nnchange log (high level)n- 2025-11-03: draft created and initial grammar specified.n- 2025-12-14: added safety guards and validation matrix after internal review.n- 2026-01-20: canary support and telemetry contract finalized.n- 2026-02-12: publishing the first stable spl spec and profile library.nnrelated artifacts and repo locationsn- policy repo: git@repo.redwood.ai:infra/scheduler-policies.gitn- validator: //tools/policylint (internal binary)n- simulator: //tools/policysimn- controller service: infra/policy-service (k8s namespace: infra-policy)nnnotes and open itemsn- draft an automated test that injects a kernel_hint mismatch and verifies fallback semantics.n- consider adding cost-aware policy expressions (cost_per_token 0.55 and free_bytes 2 gbn critical: fragmentation_ratio 0.70 and free_bytes 1 gbnnrationale: fragmentation is only actionable if meaningful free space exists otherwise pressure is real and eviction may be required.nnh1. proposed designnwe propose a two-part approach:n compaction: relocate kv pages to reduce fragmentation, performed incrementally with budgets.n eviction: tier-aware eviction when pressure is high and compaction cannot recover sufficient contiguous space quickly.nnthe compaction mechanism is integrated with the scheduler to avoid decode stalls and to allow backpressure/guardrails.nnh2. design principlesn correctness first: relocation must preserve per-seq kv content and ordering.n budgeted work: bound compaction by time and/or bytes moved per scheduling cycle.n avoid tail spikes: do not perform large relocation inside latency-sensitive decode inner loops.n observable: export metrics tracing spans to correlate compaction/eviction with tail latency.n safe-by-default: feature flags kill-switch staged rollout.nnh1. compaction mechanismnh2. what we compactnwe compact at the granularity of allocator pages (or blocks) used for kv storage. compaction moves live pages to earlier (lower) addresses in the arena to create larger contiguous free spans.nnwe do not attempt to change the logical layout of kv within a page we only relocate pages and update indirections.nnh2. preconditions / invariantsnduring relocation we must preserve:n a sequences kv pointer table must not point to freed/moved pages.n reads during decode must see a consistent view of the kv pointers.n cancellation/free racing with relocation must not leak pages or double-free.nnwe enforce these with:n a per-sequence relocation lock (logical lock in scheduler state not a heavy mutex).n a relocation state machine (see kv-cache-memory-layout-overview page).n a two-phase commit for relocation:n 1) copy live page(s) to new locationn 2) atomically swap pointer(s)n 3) release old page(s) back to free-listnnh2. incremental compaction (primary)nincremental compaction runs as a small step each scheduler cycle, bounded by budgets.nnalgorithm sketch:n1) determine if compaction should run:n fragmentation_ratio above thresholdn free_bytes above minimum actionable freen allocator under pressure soon or pressure now signals (see integration)n2) choose relocation candidates:n prefer sequences with pages scattered across many spansn prefer low-priority tiers first (hosted free/dev hosted pro dedicated)n avoid sequences marked as pinned or latency criticaln3) choose destination:n allocate a contiguous target span near the front of the arenan if no contiguous destination exists, compaction step becomes no-opn4) copy pages:n use gpu memcpy/pack kernel as appropriaten update indirectionsn5) update allocator metadata and emit metricsnnbudgets:n bytes_moved_budget_per_tick (default varies by tier)n time_budget_per_tick_ms (hard cap)nna step stops when any budget is exhausted or when scheduler enters a latency-critical boundary.nnh2. background compaction (secondary optional)nwe support an optional background compaction worker thread that can perform additional relocation when:n the scheduler indicates the system is in a low-utilization windown or when a pool is in stabilize mode after a burstnnthis worker is strictly lower priority than request processing and must also respect global budgets. initial rollout will keep background compaction disabled by default incremental compaction is the primary mechanism.nnh2. compaction triggersnwe trigger compaction when any of the following are true:n fragmentation_ratio trigger_thresholdn free_span_count span_count_thresholdn allocator_failures_recent 0 (failed allocations that required fallback/eviction)n tail_latency_guardrail engaged (sre signal see guardrails doc)nnwe also include hysteresis to avoid oscillation:n trigger on threshold_high stop when below threshold_low.nnh2. candidate selection and fairnessnwe maintain a small priority queue of candidate sequences. each sequence is scored by:n scatter_score (number of spans touched)n bytes_to_compact (estimated)n tier_weight (lower tiers more eligible)n pinned_penalty (pinned sequences typically ineligible)nnwe also enforce fairness:n no single sequence can consume x of a tick budget.n round-robin across candidates to avoid starvation.nnh2. kernel requirementsnmost moves can use device-to-device memcpy. for some layouts (paged kv with interleaved head dimension), we may need a lightweight pack kernel to maintain alignment/coalescing.nninitial plan:n start with memcpy for page-aligned moves.n add pack kernel only if benchmarks show significant regression due to misalignment or if page strides require transformation.nnh1. eviction policyncompaction reduces fragmentation but cannot create memory out of thin air. when true memory pressure exists (or compaction cannot quickly produce a contiguous span), we must evict.nnh2. policy summarynwe implement tier-aware lru eviction at the sequence level:n evict whole sequences (freeing all kv pages for that sequence).n prefer evicting:n lower-tier traffic first (e.g., hosted free/dev)n older/idle sequences (lru by last_token_timestamp)n sequences not marked pinnednnwe do not evict partial layers or partial kv for a sequence in the initial release.nnh2. pinned sessions and correctnessnsome sessions are pinned:n dedicated customer pinned sessions (contractual / product requirements)n internal canary/test sessionsnnpinned sessions are ineligible for eviction unless:n emergency_oom_mode is enabled (explicit, off by default)n and sre oncall flips the kill-switch policy (see runbook)nnh2. prefix cache interactionnif prefix caching is enabled for a model profile:n prefix cache entries are separately tracked and are more evictable than active sequences.n under pressure we evict prefix cache entries before evicting active sequences.n compaction does not move prefix cache entries in v1 unless they share the same arena if shared, they participate as low-priority candidates.nnh2. customer-facing behaviorneviction of an active sequence manifests as:n request error (e.g., resource_exhausted) or retryable overload signal depending on caller typen or graceful degradation if routing can retry on a different replica/region (when enabled)nnwe will not silently drop tokens.nnh1. scheduler integrationnthe scheduler is the control point to ensure compaction does not cause tail latency spikes.nnh2. integration pointsnwe integrate compaction into scheduler phases:n end of prefill phase: safe window to do small relocation stepsn decode boundary between token steps: only if budget is tiny and queue depth is lown after completion/cancellation processing: coalesce small compaction stepnnh2. budget enforcementnbudgets are enforced by the scheduler, not solely within allocator code:n the scheduler provides a per-tick budget context:n time_budget_msn bytes_budgetn max_sequences_to_touchn the allocator/compactor must check the context and return early.nnthis is intentional to keep latency control centralized and consistent with other runtime maintenance tasks.nnh2. backpressure and overload signalsnwhen overload is detected:n prefer shedding new work over doing heavy compaction.n compaction should enter stabilize mode:n perform minimal work required to prevent allocator failuren rely on eviction if needednnsignals:n queue_depth_highn decode_utilization_highn p99_latency_risingn allocator_failures_recentnnh2. safety: cancellation and concurrent eventsncancellation can race with relocation. we handle with:n sequence state transitions guarded by scheduler state machine.n relocation epoch per sequence:n cancellation waits for relocation swap to complete or aborts relocation at a safe pointn allocator operations must be idempotent for the old page free after pointer swap.nnwe will add targeted stress tests for cancellation during relocation (see validation plan).nnh1. configuration and feature flagsnall controls are runtime config flags (no console ui in v1).nnh2. feature flags (names are internal subject to config registry constraints)n runtime.kv_compaction.enabled (default: off initially)n runtime.kv_compaction.mode off incremental incremental_plus_backgroundn runtime.kv_compaction.trigger_fragmentation_ratio_high (default: 0.70)n runtime.kv_compaction.trigger_fragmentation_ratio_low (default: 0.55)n runtime.kv_compaction.min_actionable_free_bytes (default: 2gib hosted 1gib dedicated)n runtime.kv_compaction.bytes_budget_per_tick (default: hosted 128mib dedicated 256mib)n runtime.kv_compaction.time_budget_per_tick_ms (default: hosted 0.35ms dedicated 0.50ms)n runtime.kv_compaction.max_sequences_per_tick (default: 2)nneviction:n runtime.kv_eviction.enabled (default: on existing behavior refined)n runtime.kv_eviction.policy tier_aware_lru_v1n runtime.kv_eviction.allow_evict_pinned (default: off)n runtime.kv_eviction.prefer_prefix_cache_first (default: on)nnkill-switch:n runtime.kv_compaction.kill_switch (default: false)n when true: disables compaction immediately and blocks new relocation steps.nnh2. tier defaults (proposal)n hosted free/dev:n compaction enabled after canaryn smaller budgets to minimize latency riskn aggressive eviction permitted (non-pinned only)n hosted pro:n compaction enabled after hosted subset validationn slightly higher budgetsn dedicated:n compaction enabled lastn higher budgets allowed, but stronger guardrails on eviction (pinned sessions common)nnfinal defaults will be set after benchmark canary results (see experiment tracker).nnh1. observabilitynwe add:n metricsn tracing spansn dashboards and alerts (sre-owned)nnh2. metrics (high level)nallocator health:n kv_allocator_fragmentation_ration performance and correctness validationnh2. benchmark plannwe extend the benchmark suite with scenarios designed to induce fragmentation:n mixed prompt lengths (p50 short, p90 long)n high churn stress testsnadd/extend tests:n cancellation during relocation (including repeated cancel/retry)n concurrent completion evictionn long-running sessions with intermittent backpressuren adversarial disable background compaction by defaultn copy overhead increases gpu utilization:n mitigation: limit bytes moved tune thresholds add pack kernel only if neededn pointer swap race leading to incorrect dsid_bc97f9911d9e4cc4bc6efc4db7ca495b, source_type: confluence, title: perf regression canary (prod) design: runtime kernel/scheduler attribution, content: 1. summarynwe will deploy a lightweight, always-on performance canary in production to detect and alert on per-model serving regressions before they broadly impact customers. the canary continuously runs a synthetic, privacy-safe workload against a curated model list in each enabled region/tier and evaluates results against versioned baselines.nnprimary regression signals:n- p95 end-to-end latency and p95 runtime-only latencyn- tokens/sec (throughput)nnsecondary signals used for attribution and fast triage:n- prefill vs decode latencyn- scheduler queueing time and batch size distributionn- kv cache hit rate (where applicable)n- runtime build id, kernel selection id, scheduler config idnnthis document covers the architecture, workload model, metrics, baseline strategy, regression evaluation, attribution, and rollout plan.nn 2. problem statementnruntime performance regressions are often introduced by:n- kernel changes (new fused kernels, attention paths, quantization kernels)n- scheduler/batching heuristic changes (continuous batching decisions, token budget changes)n- model config updates (rope scaling, max context, kv cache settings)n- gpu fleet changes (new driver, mig layout, sku mix)n- release/rollout sequencing and region-specific differencesnncustomer traffic is too noisy and privacy-sensitive to use directly for early detection. we need a controlled, repeatable signal that is:n- low overhead (0.5)n- stable queueing (p95 queueing under defined cap for baseline-quality)nn 7.4 region handlingninitial policy:n- baseline is hardware sku tier scoped, and region is treated as an attribute for monitoring.n- we only split baselines by region when we have evidence of consistent region deltas (driver versions, fleet composition).nnoperationally:n- the evaluator can apply region-specific multipliers if needed (config-based) without exploding baseline cardinality.nn 7.5 baseline updates and driftnbaselines are updated when any of the baseline keys change (new runtime build, new model version, new hardware sku).nnwe avoid continuously rolling baselines in the first iteration because it can hide slow regressions and caused alert storms in prior systems. instead:n- baselines are fixed per release key and explicitly advanced.n- we monitor drift separately via a baseline freshness dashboard panel and a slow drift warning (non-paging).nn(see adr: baseline computation and thresholds.)nn 8. regression evaluation and anti-flap logicn 8.1 windowing and minimum samplesnperf-canary aggregates observations in a rolling evaluation window.nndefaults (per model target):n- evaluation window: 30 minutesn- minimum samples: 80 total requests and at least 15 requests in each of the top 2 buckets by weightn- cooldown: 45 minutes after an alert resolves before re-alerting on the same keynn 8.2 regression definitions (initial)nwe evaluate multiple conditions. a regression is raised if any paging condition is met, otherwise warning if warning conditions are met.nndefinitions use percent change from baseline:n- latency regression: (observed_p95 / baseline_p95 - 1)n- throughput regression: (baseline_tokens_per_sec / observed_tokens_per_sec - 1)nninitial thresholds (subject to calibration):nwarning:n- p95 e2e latency 10 for 2 consecutive windowsn- or p95 runtime latency 10 for 2 consecutive windowsn- or tokens/sec drop 8 for 2 consecutive windowsnnpaging (top models only controlled by target list):n- p95 e2e latency 20 for 2 consecutive windowsn- or tokens/sec drop 15 for 2 consecutive windowsnnguardrails:n- if scheduler queueing p95 increases by 30 and runtime latency is flat ( 90 minutes.nn 8.3 noise controlsn- use histograms and compute quantiles server-side (prometheus/grafana) and evaluator-side using stable quantile estimator.n- apply a small smoothing factor for p95 comparisons (ewma across windows) but never smooth raw metric emission.n- enforce two-window confirm for warning/paging.n- deduplicate alerts by: (model_id, model_version, runtime_build_id, hardware_sku, region, tier, metric_class).nn 9. attribution and triage signalsnwhen a regression triggers, we want immediate evidence pointing to the likely root cause.nn 9.1 kernel-level vs scheduler-level heuristicsnthe alert payload includes a classification based on these decision rules:nna) likely kernel/runtime execution regressionn- runtime_total_latency_ms p95 increases materially ( threshold)n- and scheduler_queueing_latency_ms is flat or minorn- and kernel_selection_id changed recently or correlates with runtime_build_id changennb) likely scheduler/capacity regressionn- scheduler_queueing_latency_ms p95 increases materiallyn- and runtime_total_latency_ms p95 is flat or minorn- and batch size distribution shifts (lower effective batch) or active requests increasesnnc) likely model-config regressionn- regressions are isolated to a single model_versionn- and kernel_selection_id and runtime_build_id unchangedn- and prefill/decode split changes consistent with config (e.g., max context / rope)nnd) likely infra/fleet regressionn- regressions correlate with hardware_sku or a single regionn- increased variability increased queueing increased error ratesn- correlated fleet signals (driver rollout, mig config changes) if availablenn 9.2 required tags for attributionnto support the above, runtime telemetry must expose:n- runtime_build_idn- kernel_selection_id (bounded enum e.g., attn_v3_fp16, attn_v4_flash, int8_decode_v2)n- scheduler_config_id (bounded enum ties back to scheduler heuristics)nnimplementation detail:n- do not emit raw kernel names or dynamic combinations as labels.n- maintain a mapping table in runtime code for stable ids.nn 9.3 what goes in the alert payloadnalert payload fields (sent to incident-bot):n- model_id, model_version, region, tier, hardware_skun- runtime_build_id, kernel_selection_id, scheduler_config_idn- baseline p95 and observed p95 (e2e and runtime)n- baseline tokens/sec and observed tokens/secn- queueing p95 and batch size deltasn- confidence level (based on samples and variance)n- links: dashboards, baseline artifact, recent runtime release notes, runbooknn 10. dashboards (what we expect to see)nfor each model target, the dashboard provides:n- p50/p95/p99 time series for e2e latency and runtime latencyn- prefill/decode/queueing breakdownn- tokens/sec and tokens/requestn- batch size histogram (over time)n- kv cache hit rate (when enabled)n- annotation overlays for runtime releases and kernel flag flipsnndashboards must include a inference read metrics write.n- no access to customer metadata stores.n- config reads are audited.nn 11.2 data handlingn- synthetic prompts only.n- no prompt or completion text is persisted.n- logs are redacted and include explicit assertions:n - never log request payloadn - never log auth tokensn - only log bucket id and token countsnn 11.3 overhead budgetntarget: route to shard-group leadern 2) orchestrator computes micro-batch plan (batch size, slice offsets)n 3) kv indices resolved cross-shard comm plan computedn 4) kernels invoked on each shard with coordinated comm primitivesnnkey scheduling primitives and policies:n- priority lanes: per-tenant/per-route numeric priority (0..7). use lanes to isolate high-slo customers from best-effort workloads.n- deadline-aware slicing: requests with tight latency budgets can be sliced into smaller micro-batches that avoid queueing behind large batches. config knob: scheduler.deadline_slicing.enabled (boolean) and scheduler.deadline_slicing.max_slices (int).n- backpressure thresholds: two soft thresholds (queue_soft_ms, queue_hard_ms). if queue latency exceeds queue_soft_ms the scheduler reduces auto-batched slice sizes by 25 until below threshold. if queue_hard_ms is exceeded the request is re-routed to fallback model variant.n- affinity constraints: pin hot shard leaders to nic/gpu pairs to reduce cross-host comm overhead for latency-sensitive flows. affinity.policy can be set to host-local spread packed.nnkernel selection heuristics (how mapper picks kernels):n- inputs considered: seq_len distribution (p50/p95/p99), effective micro-batch size, quantization profile, active comm topology.n- heuristic examples:n - if p95_seq_len 8 - choose fused-attention-kernel-v2 for stable throughput.n - if quant_profile int8 and there are frequent prefix-cache-hits - prefer int8-kernel-with-cache-optimized-path to reduce decode overhead.n - if all-reduce latency 120us - choose locality-optimized kernels that favor reduce-scatter overlap-compute.nnprofiling and investigation playbook (step-by-step):n1) reproduce on staging with the same model-version and shard-topology. record the exact git commit / runtime image.n2) capture end-to-end traces for 5k requests across representative traffic: use agent tracing (trace level debug) and kernel-level telemetry. commands:n - rwinfctl trace start --model my-model:2026-02-01 --duration 10m --level debug --out /tmp/trace-(date s).zipn - nvprof (for local reproduce) or perf on host capture gpu kernel timelines.n3) produce flamegraphs for the baseline latency (expected 20 of observed latency and comms are under budget, open a kernel ticket and include reproducible microbench steps (see ownership and escalation).nnbenchmarking suite notes protocol and signal handbook, content: summary:na practical handbook describing the protocol and operational guidance for coordinating memory eviction (kv cache, model weights/shards) with kernel scheduling signals to prevent tail-latency spirals and preserve throughput slos.nncontent:noverviewnnthis document defines the evictionkernel coordination protocol (ekcp), a lightweight control plane and operational playbook that synchronizes cache/shard eviction decisions with kernel scheduling hints and backpressure signals emitted by the serving runtime. the goal is to avoid reactive thrashing (concurrent eviction heavy kernel activation) and reduce tail latency regressions when the system rehydrates caches or migrates shards under load.nnscopen-----n- applies to: kv cache eviction, session/sequence eviction, model shard migration, and kernel activation scheduling in the serving runtime.n- excludes: higher-level routing policies (tiered fallback routing) and customer-side session management.nnwhy this mattersn----------------nduring mixed workloads we observed sequences of events that amplify tail latency:n1) memory pressure triggers mass eviction of kv cache and/or lightweight session state.n2) immediately after eviction, the scheduler admits high-priority requests that require cache rehydration and heavy kernel execution.n3) kernel queue saturation and memory reallocation cause long-tail latencies and increased error rates.nnekcp provides a modest coordination layer of signals and policies to:n- stagger and rate-limit rehydration work.n- prefer low-fidelity fallbacks until caches are warmed.n- prioritize small, cheap inference requests during warmup windows.nndesign principlesn-----------------n- backwards-compatible: defaults are conservative behavior toggled via config flags per cluster/pool.n- signal minimal: only a few semantic signals to avoid high cardinality.n- observability-first: emit clear metrics and traces for every decision.n- experiment-friendly: feature flags canary ramp plan included.nnprotocol summary (high level)n----------------------------nekcp uses three coordinated signal channels between eviction manager and kernel scheduler:n- evictionintent: emitted when a tenant/pool plans mass eviction (soft signal).n- warmupwindow: a timeboxed period after eviction where rehydration is rate-limited and scheduler favors cheap kernels.n- rehydrationprogress: incremental reports of cache warm percentage (0-100) and shard residency counts.nnstate machine (per-pool)n------------------------nstates: idle - evicting - warmup - normalntransitions:n1) idle - evicting: evictionintent(true) issued when free_memory warmup: once eviction completes, warmupwindow opens for n seconds (configurable).n3) warmup - normal: when rehydrationprogress warmup_target or warmup timeout expires.n4) any state - idle: manual override or pool drain event.nnmessage formats (examples)n-------------------------nall messages are lightweight json blobs carried over the internal control plane (grpc or internal pub/sub). example payloads: nnevictionintent example:nn pool_id: gpu-pool-23,n initiator: eviction-manager:v2,n reason: memory-pressure,n estimated_evicted_mb: 15360,n timestamp: 2026-06-11t13:22:08znnnwarmupwindow example:nn pool_id: gpu-pool-23,n warmup_seconds: 45,n priority_policy: favor-l2-small-requests,n rehydration_target_percent: 30,n timestamp: 2026-06-11t13:22:18znnnrehydrationprogress example:nn pool_id: gpu-pool-23,n cache_percent: 22,n shard_residency: model-a: 3, model-b: 7,n timestamp: 2026-06-11t13:22:42znnnoperational policy parameters (recommended defaults)n--------------------------------------------------n parameter default description n------:---n memory_threshold_low 0.15 fraction free memory that triggers soft eviction n warmup_seconds_default 30 default warmup window length n warmup_rehydrate_target 25 percent of important cache that should be present to exit warmup n rehydrate_slowdown_factor 0.6 rate limiter: reduce parallel rehydration tasks by this factor during warmup n allow_high_fidelity_during_warmup false whether to allow heavy kernels during warmup nnscheduler integration pointsn----------------------------nthe kernel scheduler consumes ekcp signals and implements the following behaviors while warmup is active: n- admission shaping: lower concurrency for kernels requiring x mb scratch or y streams. n- kernel hinting: prefer quantized or small-batch kernels for a configured percent of early requests. n- soft-fallback: route to cheaper model variant (if available) for non-critical requests until warmup passes.nnobservability contractn----------------------nevery ekcp event must produce:n- trace/span with event tags: pool_id, state, initiator, reason, warmup_secondsn- metrics (per-pool): ekcp_evictions_total (counter), ekcp_warmup_seconds (histogram), ekcp_rehydrate_percent (gauge), ekcp_warmup_blocked_requests_total (counter)n- if cache_percent 90 and warmup is active: reduce admission for heavy kernels.n4) apply quick mitigations (ordered):n a) increase warmup_seconds for the pool by 30s.n b) enable allow_high_fidelity_during_warmupfalse (if toggled).n c) temporarily divert non-critical traffic to cheaper variant or fallback region.n d) if kernel queue remains saturated, scale up ephemeral burst capacity (if available).n5) post-incident: run a targeted replay of representative requests to validate recovery and update the eviction threshold if repeated.nnbenchmarking and validation sandbox (sched-sandbox) used to validate cost-aware admission policies, economic priority governor behaviors, and safe canary rollouts for kernel changes. it is intended for runtime engineers, oncall, and performance owners running safety-limited experiments against production-like traffic.nnpurpose and scope:n- reduce risk when introducing scheduler/econ changes by running them in an isolated traffic. it does not affect real dispatch instead it annotates decisions for comparison.n- kernel-admitter (component): produces observed kernel slot allocations and credits. sandbox mirrors the api and uses the same kernel hints.n- econ-governor (component): configurable economic model (weights for latency vs cost vs fidelity) used by sched-sandbox to synthesize priority.n- profiling-agent: collects trace fragments, kernel timing, and cost estimates for sandboxed requests.nndesign principles:n1) non-invasive: sandbox must never affect live routing or admission. make-change-by-annotation only.n2) deterministic inputs: ensure sampled requests have the same input features (sequence length, model variant, tenant tier, token budget).n3) low-noise sampling: prefer stratified sampling by tenant and route to ensure representation across latency-sensitive and batchy workloads.n4) telemetry parity: capture the same telemetry tags as production (kernel_id, slot_count, credit_charge, model_variant, origin_region).nnoperational slos (for sandbox observability):n- sample coverage: 0.5 of all requests per active route or at least 5 qps per route for 95 of time.n- trace fidelity: 99 of sandbox traces must include kernel_id, kernel_latency_ms, and credit_cost_estimate.n- canary detection latency: sandbox must detect a statistically significant slo shift within 30 minutes for a sustained regression lasting 5 minutes.nnadmission policy and economic model (econ-governor):nthe econ-governor computes a numeric priority score p per request: p w_l normalized_latency_sensitivity w_c normalized_cost_sensitivity w_f fidelity_penalty.n- weights are declared per-experiment and can be tuned in the sandbox ui.n- normalization uses percentiles from a 7-day rolling window (p50..p99.9) per route.nnconfiguration table (canonical knobs):n knob description default safe-range n----------------------------------------n sampling_rate fraction of requests mirrored to sandbox 0.005 0.001 - 0.02 n econ_weights w_l,w_c,w_f vector 0.6,0.3,0.1 each 0.0 - 1.0, sum0 n admission_queue_limit max concurrent sandboxed admissions queued 200 50 - 1000 n drift_alert_threshold relative delta from production decision rate to trigger review 5 1 - 20 n canary_window_minutes sliding window for canary decision aggregation 30 5 - 120 nncanary and experiment lifecycle (step-by-step):n1) plan: create experiment entry in the experiments registry with objectives, owner, and primary metrics (cost per token delta, p99 latency, fidelity rollback rate).n2) baseline capture: run sandbox with current production econ_weights for 2472 hours to capture baseline decision distribution and kernel hints.n3) pilot: deploy modified econ_weights or scheduler policy to sched-sandbox only at sampling_rate 0.5.n4) shadow analysis: run automated comparison job that computes the following per-route metrics every 10 minutes:n a) decision flip rate (fraction of requests where sandbox decision differs from production).n b) delta cost estimate (sandbox_est - production_est) per-token and per-request.n c) slo delta (p50,p95,p99) predicted from kernel_latency models.n5) canary escalation: if metrics within acceptance band for 4 consecutive windows, increase sampling_rate to 2 and repeat.n6) live canary: with approval, route 1 real traffic to new scheduler policy (controlled canary). if safe, scale to 10 then full rollout.nnacceptance bands (default):n- cost per-token increase: 50ms or decision flip rate 25 sustained for two windows.n- drift alert when sandbox decisions diverge from production at drift_alert_threshold this triggers an investigation ticket.nnprofiling and benchmarking protocol for experiments:n1) synthetic fidelity replay: replay a slice of production traffic (stored in request-corpus) through the sandbox with and without the change to compute kernel occupancy differences.n2) microbench patch: run kernel-level microbenchmarks with stress harness to estimate worst-case slot contention and thermal influence.n3) shadow benchmarks: run the bench-suite (bench-run) with the candidate scheduler policy against a mirrored cluster to measure throughput and tail-latency under mixed workloads.nnexample cli snippets:n- enable sandbox for experiment ex-123:n rctl experiments create --id ex-123 --owner aisha --weights 0.5,0.4,0.1 --sampling 0.005n- sweep: export sandbox traces, kernel snapshots, and bench-suite results for the last 60 minutes.n4) rollback any canary routing if in live canary stage.n5) triage with the kernel team: inspect kernel_id distribution and credit exhaustion signals.n6) if root cause is econ weights, revert to baseline weights and re-run baseline capture for 24 hours.n7) produce a postmortem within 72 hours if utilization. it is intended for on-call operators, runtime engineers, and release leads who need to understand how telemetry is translated into scheduler adjustments, how automated and manual controls interact, and how to safely intervene.nngoals and scope:n- keep 99th percentile token latency below slo targets per tier (see slo table).n- maintain per-node gpu utilization in the operational band to avoid thermal or nvlink contention (recommended 6085 during normal traffic).n- limit regression risk by constraining automated changes behind safe guardrails and staged rollouts.n- cover both automated autotune flows and manual operator interventions.nnquick reference slos and thresholds:n slo / metric target operator alert threshold action level n--------------------------------------------------------------n 99p token latency (hosted-prod) 140ms for 5m p1 n 99p token latency (dedicated) 100ms for 5m p1 n gpu thermal throttle events / node 0 per 1h 3 in 10m p1 n gpu memory fragmentation ratio 0.4 p2 n scheduler change fail rate (canary) 2 p2 nnkey concepts:n- feedback loop inputs: aggregated traces (99p latency), kernel queue lengths, per-shard kv cache hit rates, sequence length distribution, per-gpu occupancy, and admission controller reject rates.n- controller outputs: kernel slot allocations, batch slicing targets, priority weight adjustments, per-tenant quota limits, and hint signals for kv cache prefetch.n- guardrails: change rate limit (max 5 of slots per minute), rollback window (10 minutes), and canary sampling (5 traffic by default).nnroles and ownership:n- runtime scheduling team: primary owners for the feedback controller and policy language.n- sre on-call: monitors alerts and executes runbook actions.n- release lead: approves non-automated policy changes and coordinates canaries.n- observability team: owns metric definitions and dashboards used by the loop.nnautomated feedback path (high level):n1. signal ingestion: streaming metrics from the collector (grpc-traces, kernel-metrics-pipeline).n2. signal enrichment: causal attribution service enriches latency spikes with kernel and tenant context.n3. decision engine: policy engine evaluates rules and candidate adjustments.n4. safety checks: simulated dry-run against the simulator and quota check.n5. apply: change is committed to the scheduler with a versioned change id and canary rollout.nnsafety and simulation:n- all automated changes are run through the local decision simulator. the simulator must flag potential 3 expected 99p latency regressions or 5 drop in throughput.n- canary matrix: default is 5 traffic for 10 minutes, 20 for 20 minutes, then full roll. the decision engine will abort if any stage shows alert violations.nnoperator runbook: incident triage and mitigation steps:n1. confirm the alert: check 99p latency, kernel queue backlogs, and recent scheduler change ids. cli: redwoodctl metrics query --range 10m --metric 99p_token_latency --service serving-runtimen2. identify correlated signals: correlate with deployment events, kernel rollout flags, or thermal events. use dashboard: serving runtime / scheduling feedback loop / recent decisions.n3. if automated change is in progress and latency regressed:n a. rollback automated change: redwoodctl scheduler rollback --change-id --reason latency-regression-rollbackn b. pause auto-rollouts: redwoodctl scheduler set-guardrail --auto-rollout falsen c. open an incident and tag the runtime-scheduling slack channel (runtime-scheduling) and page sre.n4. if no automated changes present, apply manual mitigation: reduce admission controller concurrency for affected model variant(s). example:n a. redwoodctl admission update --route /v1/generate --concurrency 8n b. expand canary to divert to fallback model variant if available: redwoodctl routing set-fallback --route /v1/generate --variant small-llm-quant --weight 0.25n5. observe p95 or 5 drop in cache hit ratio triggers oncall.n8) safety and fallback rulesn - ensure fallback model variant available and compatibility table updated.nncommands and diagnostics contention (cpu/gpu throttling or batching misconfig).n2) capture traces - start kernel traces for 60s on affected devices. - collect per-request timing, kernel durations, memcopy times.n3) check scheduling hotspots - look for priority inversion where low-priority bulk jobs starve interactive queues.n4) inspect cache behavior - if cache miss spike correlates with latency spikes, check shard experimenting with quantization, always run automatic evals tied to the prompt set and check ceiling/lower threshold differences.nncommon pitfalls and how to avoid correlator and event reconciliation playbook, content: summaryn-------nthis runbook describes the recommended operational process and commands to correlate end-to-end request traces with low-level kernel dispatch events and gpu timeline samples, detect event mismatches (reconciliation failures), and perform remediation and post-incident analysis. it is intended for sres and runtime engineers responding to tail-latency, unexplained cost spikes, or transient model-swap oscillations where higher-level traces (api/ingress) do not match kernel-level telemetry.nnwhen to usen-----------n- persistent or recurring tail latency (99.9th percentile) with no clear api-level throttling.n- cost anomalies where per-token compute does not match expected kernel time.n- model swap or variant fallback events observed in control plane logs but no downstream kernel activity.n- kernel timeouts, stalled gpus, or delayed kv cache warmups that manifest as opaque request slowdowns.nnowner escalationn------------------n- primary on-call: eng-sre/runtime-sli on-call.n- secondary: runtime-kernel team (pager) if kernel or gpu hang suspected.n- escalate to infra on-call for suspected hardware/driver issues.n- post-incident owner: person who closes the incident must schedule a postmortem in 72 hours.nnprerequisites and telemetryn--------------------------nensure the following telemetry streams are available and not in degraded mode before starting:n- request-traces (sampled via trace-collector trace-id present in headers x-rw-trace-id)n- kernel-events stream (kernel-dispatcher - event bus) with event_id and parent_request_idn- gpu-timeline samples (per-device microsecond timestamps)n- kvcache-metrics and session-affinity logsn- runtime-proxy and model-router logs at info levelnnminimum retention and sampling recommendations:n- request-traces: 1 deterministic sampling for production increase to 10 during investigationn- kernel-events: full capture for at least 6 hours around incident windown- gpu-timeline: rolling 1-hour window, sampled at 100hz aggregation for latency spikesnnquick reference slos and thresholdsn----------------------------------ntable: primary triggers used in the playbook (text table)n signal alert threshold triage priority notes n api p50/p95/p99 p99 2x baseline p1 typical entry signal n kernel queue depth 85 sustained 5m p1 indicates backpressure n gpu utilization vs kernel time gpu util 10 p2 warmup or affinity break nnstep-by-step proceduren----------------------n1) capture incident window and identify a representative tracen - timebox: pick 5 minutes around alert onset and 30 minutes before for baseline.n - query traces:nn bashn increase sampling if possible for live investigationsn curl -s n -h authorization: bearer obs_api_key jq . lessn nn - identify a trace with full path: ingress - runtime-proxy - model-router - kernel-dispatcher. note the x-rw-trace-id and request_id (request-id header).nn2) map high-level trace spans to kernel eventsn - kernel events contain fields: event_id, parent_request_id, kernel_name, start_us, end_us, device_id, reason. use parent_request_id to map to request_id.n - example kernel-events query (elasticsearch/esql):nn sqln select event_id, parent_request_id, kernel_name, start_us, end_us, device_id, reasonn from kernel-eventsn where parent_request_id req-1234 and timestamp between 2025-09-10t12:09:30z and 2025-09-10t12:15:30zn nn - if parent_request_id is missing: search by trace timestamp /- 50ms on same host/slot and correlate by kernel start_us approximate to span.start_timestamp_us.nn3) reconciliation rules and heuristics (event matching algorithm)n - exact-match: trace.request_id kernel.parent_request_id - mark reconciled.n - heuristic match: if exact-match absent, match by host, gpu device_id, and kernel start timestamp within /- 2500us of span boundary.n - unmatched span classification:n - missing-kernel: high-level span present, kernel event absent suspect routing/fallback or kernel dispatch failure.n - orphan-kernel: kernel event with no active high-level trace likely system-level background task or delayed trace sampling.n - delayed-commit: kernel start occurs but no end_us recorded - suspect watchdog or driver hang.nn4) run automated reconciliation query and produce summary reportn - use the provided connector script (trace-correlator) on the runbox:nn bashn ./tools/trace-correlator --trace-id req-1234 --window 30s --output /tmp/recon-req-1234.jsonn cat /tmp/recon-req-1234.json jq .summaryn nn - expected output: counts for reconciled, missing-kernel, orphan-kernel, delayed-commit.nn5) remediation actions by categoryn - missing-kernel:n 1. check model-router logs for no-capacity or variant-mismatch for the affected trace-id.n 2. if routing indicates fallback to another region/tier, verify that cross-region routing is completing and that kernel-dispatcher is reachable.n 3. if model was swapped mid-request, run the model-swap audit:nn bashn curl -s -h authorization: bearer cp_api jq .n nn 4. if routing and control-plane look healthy, raise a kernel-dispatcher debug request to capture next 100 dispatch attempts and escalate to kernel team.nn - orphan-kernel:n 1. check whether the kernel was part of a background eviction, prefetch, or garbage collection by inspecting kernel_name and reason.n 2. if orphaned kernel time is significant (100ms), investigate whether tracing sampling missed the parent due to rate limits. consider increasing request-traces sampling temporarily.nn - delayed-commit / gpu hang:n 1. immediately check gpu watchdog metrics and driver logs on node.n 2. if kernel end_us missing, perform a soft-reset on the dispatcher lane (non-destructive) by toggling lane draining: curl -x post 3. if soft-reset fails, escalate to infra capture a full gpu dump and attach to incident.nn6) short-term mitigations to restore slosn - activate canary fallback: route to pre-warmed smaller variant (model-small-quant) for new inbound requests for the affected customers.n - increase continuous-batching windows for short period to absorb variance if kernel queue depth is high.n - temporarily raise trace sampling to 10 to improve reconciliation signal.nn7) post-incident diagnostics and artifactsn - required artifacts to attach to postmortem:n - representative trace(s) x-rw-trace-id(s) and request-id(s).n - /tmp/recon-.json output.n - kernel-event dump for the incident window.n - gpu timeline sample slice (.timeline.gz).n - control-plane rollout events for model-variants.n - run a delta analysis comparing expected kernel time vs observed kernel time across the 1-hour window around incident. include token counts and model variant in analysis.nnoperational tools and snippetsn----------------------------n- trace-correlator usage: ./tools/trace-correlator --window 30s --sample-rate 10 --trace-id n- timestamp between 2025-09-10t12:00:00z and 2025-09-10t13:00:00zn group by hostn order by reconciled_count ascn nn- kernel dispatch debug mode (non-prod first):nn yamln debug_mode: truen capture_count: reconciliation metric: recon.mismatch_rate (percent of spans that did not reconcile) with 1-minute resolution to use in alerting.nncommon investigation scenarios describes the adaptive cohort probing and handoff process used by the redwood serving runtime to detect per-cohort fidelity degradation, orchestrate kernel handoffs, and safely probe changes under production traffic. it defines telemetry signals, thresholds, automated decision steps, and operator procedures for investigation and rollback. the goal is to allow dynamic handoffs (e.g., between quantized kernel a and fallback kernel b) while preserving slos and minimizing cost impact.nnscopenn- applies to multi-tenant inference pools running heterogeneous kernels (fp16, 8-bit quantized, sparse-aware kernels) on gpu clusters.n- covers automated probing, graceful handoff, telemetry required, manual intervention steps, and validation/benchmarking checklist.n- excludes model packaging and build processes (see model-onboarding docs).nnaudiencenn- oncall sres and runtime engineers responsible for scheduler and kernel rollouts.n- benchmarking and profiling engineers validating kernel variants.nnbackground and motivationnnredwood supports multiple kernel implementations with different performance/cost/quality characteristics. when the scheduler considers swapping a cohort to a new kernel variant (for cost saving or fallback), naive switchovers can introduce regressions (tail latency spikes, token errors) that impact customer slas. adaptive probing lets us sample production traffic for a small and controlled cohort, gather fidelity and latency signals, and make a conservative decision to expand, hold, or rollback.nnkey terminologynn- cohort: a logical group of requests defined by model, route, or customer label.n- probe window: the time-bounded sampling period used to evaluate a kernel change for a cohort (default 5 minutes).n- handoff: the act of routing cohort traffic from one kernel variant to another.n- fidelity regression: any measurable reduction in output quality against a defined prompt-suite (e.g., rouge/bleu/embedding-similarity drop or increased hallucination rate).nnarchitecture overview (textual diagram)nnserving runtime components involved:nn- dispatcher: request classifier and cohort router (policy engine)n- scheduler: allocates kernel slots and performs handoff orchestrationn- kernel registry: metadata and compatibility matrix for kernel variantsn- probe engine: lightweight mirroring and sampling sub-system for probe windowsn- telemetry pipeline: streaming traces, percentile latencies, fidelity probes, error ratesnn(imagine a horizontally stacked diagram: dispatcher - scheduler - kernel instances probe engine forks short-lived shadow requests to probe kernels and emits enriched traces into telemetry pipeline.)nnsignals to collectnncollect these signals at 1s/10s/60s granularities depending on signal type:nn- latency: p50/p95/p99 for token generation and end-to-end request timen- error rates: grpc/http 5xx, codec errors, kernel panicsn- fidelity metrics: embedding cosine similarity to baseline, token-level divergence, special token counts (unk/unk-like), model-specific eval score on a small prompt setn- resource signals: gpu sm utilization, memory pressure, kernel queue depthn- queueing indicators: queuing_time_ms, active_slots, preempt_countnndecision thresholds (defaults)nn- latency: p99 increase 15 for probe cohort compared to baseline fail proben- error rate: absolute increase 0.5 percentage points or relative 2x fail proben- fidelity: embedding similarity drop 0.015 absolute or relative quality delta 5 on validation prompts fail proben- resource: sustained (30s) gpu mem pressure 90 or sm utilization pegged at 98 fail probennconfig table (example values)nn- probe_window_minutes: 5n- probing_fraction_initial: 0.01 (1 of cohort)n- probing_fraction_step: 0.05 (increase to 5 on success)n- max_probe_fraction: 0.20n- telemetry_aggregation_interval_seconds: 10n- required_consecutive_success_windows: 2nnautomated probe lifecycle (high-level steps)nn1) candidate selection: release pipeline marks kernel variant k2 as candidate for kernel k1 on cohort c.n2) canary allocation: scheduler selects a probe subset p (probing_fraction_initial) of cohort c and routes those requests to k2 for probe_window_minutes.n3) shadow probing (optional): for fidelity-sensitive cohorts, the dispatcher sends a non-blocking shadow request to k2 in parallel results are compared against the primary path.n4) aggregation: probe engine aggregates telemetry for p and computes delta vs baseline.n5) decision: if all thresholds are satisfied and required_consecutive_success_windows are met, increase probing_fraction by probing_fraction_step and continue. if probe reaches max_probe_fraction and passes final checks, promote k2 for cohort c. otherwise, abort and revert to k1.nnmanual escalation playbook (when automated probe fails but metrics are borderline)nn1) pager triggers: if failure threshold crossed for production cohort above severity threshold (see slo incident taxonomy), page runtime-oncall.n2) initial triage (5 min):n - confirm the cohort identity and affected customers.n - check recent kernel release events, model version swaps, infra incidents.n - run ktrace for an exemplar request (see commands below).n3) containment (10 min):n - quarantine cohort: change cohort routing policy to pin to stable kernel k1 for all non-probe traffic.n - increase telemetry sampling to 100 for affected cohort for 15 minutes.n4) root cause and remediation (3090 min):n - if kernel bug suspected, open kernel rollback and mark variant as unsafe in kernel registry.n - if resource pressure, expand capacity or move cohort to different node pool.n - for fidelity regressions, trigger a focused validation replay (see benchmarking steps) and notify model quality team.nninvestigation confluence, title: kernel continuity and state reconciliation manual, content: purpose:nthis manual describes the operational controls, instrumentation, and step-by-step runbooks for maintaining kernel continuity across live kernel handoffs, preemptive evictions, and cross-node failover. it focuses on deterministic state reconciliation of kv caches, token-level prefix state, and quantization metadata to avoid model drift, duplicate generation, or silent correctness regressions during runtime transitions.nnscope and audience:n- audience: runtime oncall, runtime engineers, release engineers, and sres responsible for kernel rollouts and incident recovery.n- scope: live kernel swaps, preemption and eviction events, cross-numa/node handoffs, and scripted rollback scenarios. does not cover model-level content validation or developer sandbox experiments (see related pages).nngoals and slo constraints:n- preserve deterministic generation for pinned sessions where possible: session_replay_agreement 99.9 within 2s of handoff under nominal load.n- maintain 99th percentile latency slos within configured degradation targets (see table operational thresholds).n- avoid silent semantic regressions: any handoff that changes generation tokens for 0.1 of validation prompt set must trigger an audit and canary rollback.nndefinitions (quick):n- kernel instance: runtime binary kernel plugins that schedule and execute attention kernels.n- kv state: key/value caches (kv_cache) containing past key/value tensors and session metadata used to accelerate autoregressive generation.n- continuity window: time range where in-flight requests must be consistent across old and new kernel variants.n- deterministic reconcile: process that ensures two kernel instances produce identical logits for an identical prefix.nnarchitecture overview (text diagram):n- ingress - request classification (priority, session pin) - kernel router - kernel pool (gpu shards)n - each kernel has local kv cache shared persistent session index (session index backed by redis/etcd).n - handoff path: kernel a (source) - cooperative drain - state snapshot - kernel b (target) - verify - commit - update router.nnkey invariants to enforce:n1) snapshot completeness: all active kv ranges referenced by sessions must be included in the snapshot (no partial references).n2) sequence monotonicity: session token counters must not decrease across handoffs.n3) quantization metadata fidelity: quantization scale/zero-point and per-layer layout metadata must accompany tensors.n4) observability trace ids must be preserved across gs (gateway) to kernel transitions.nnoperational thresholds (table):n- slo / threshold / actionn- session_replay_agreement 99.9 / auto-verify pass - commit handoffn- session_replay_agreement 95-99.9 / mark as degraded, produce regression diff report, require engineer signoffn- session_replay_agreement 5s then fail fast to fallback poolnninstrumentation and required metrics (minimum):n- kernel.handoff.attempts (counter)n- kernel.handoff.success (counter)n- kernel.handoff.duration_ms (histogram)n- kernel.kv.snapshot_size_bytes (gauge)n- kernel.kv.missing_keys_during_replay (counter)n- kernel.replay.agreement_pct (gauge per session sampled)n- kernel.quant.meta_mismatch (counter)n- trace.session_id preserved (boolean per handoff)nnobservability queries (examples):n- reconciliation failure rate last 1h:n - promql: sum(increase(kernel_replay_agreement_failures_total1h)) / sum(increase(kernel.handoff.attempts1h))n- sessions with missing kv keys:n - promql: sum by (kernel_id) (increase(kernel_kv_missing_keys_during_replay_total15m))n- latency impact of handoff:n - logql: json handofffalse or handofftrue compare percentile(latency_ms,95, kernel)nnpre-check checklist (automated gating before any kernel rollout):n1) canary cohort traffic mirror is configured (mirror ratio 0.02).n2) snapshot size distribution within historical 95th percentile for target model.n3) quantization profile compatibility matrix verified for target kernel version.n4) observability sampling and tracing propagated for all canary requests.n5) canary health probes (see health probe list) passing for 15 minutes.nnhealth probes (example list):n- probe /healthz/kernel - returns ok kernel_version kv_snapshot_epochn- probe /healthz/replay - runs deterministic replay on a synthetic prefix corpus and returns agreement pctn- probe /metrics - prometheus scrape endpointnnrunbook: graceful kernel handoff (cooperative) - for sre / oncalln1) intent: move sessions from kernel a to kernel b for planned upgrade or maintenance.n2) preconditions: b has been validated in staging, gating pre-checks passed, canary mirror warm.n3) steps:n a) mark kernel a as draining in router config: set routing.weight(a)0 over 30s window router will forward new requests to other kernels while allowing in-flight to finish.n b) trigger snapshot: post /internal/kernel/a/snapshot - returns snapshot_id.n c) verify snapshot completeness: get /internal/snapshots/snapshot_id/verify - expect missing_keys:0, meta_ok:true. if missing_keys 0 go to troubleshooting below.n d) transfer snapshot to b: post /internal/kernel/b/ingest-snapshot snapshot_id: ....n e) run local deterministic replay on b for sample prefixes: post /internal/kernel/b/replay-sample - returns agreement scores per prefix.n f) if agreement 99.9 for sampled prefixes, mark commit: post /internal/kernel/b/commit-handoff snapshot_id:.... router update: atomically swap session index pointers to b.n g) monitor for 15 minutes: replay.agreement_pct, kv.missing_keys, 95/99 latency. if any threshold violated, trigger rollback (see rollback flow).n4) post-mortem: record snapshot_id, durations, sample diffs, and link to incident tracker.nnrunbook: emergency handoff (preemptive eviction) - for critical capacity eventsn1) intent: evict and migrate sessions from an overloaded node when cooperative drain not possible.n2) preconditions: immediate capacity pressure, automated graceful drain failed or impossible.n3) steps:n a) select victim kernel(s) using eviction scorer (eviction_score configured_threshold).n b) create partial snapshot including most-recently-used kv ranges prioritized by active sessions. limit snapshot duration to 500ms to bound tail latency.n c) ingest into fallback kernel pool (a pool running conservative kernels that accept smaller snapshots).n d) run targeted replay on highest-priority sessions only (top 1 traffic by token-volume).n e) if replay agreement 10 for any affected session cohort. system will:n 1) re-point router session index back to source kernel snapshot_id (atomic pointer swap).n 2) mark target kernel instance as failed and add to quarantine list.n 3) create incident ticket and populate required fields (snapshot ids, sample diffs, metric deltas).n- manual rollback requires engineer signoff and is used when automated rollback cannot be executed (e.g., persistent index corruption).nntroubleshooting matrix (common failure modes):n- symptom: missing keys during replayn - likely causes: partial snapshot, metadata mismatch (namespace/versioning), or rpc truncation.n - first actions: examine snapshot verification output, check transport logs for truncated payloads (s3/redis clamp errors), check kernel.kv.snapshot_size_bytes variance.nn- symptom: quantization metadata mismatch - scaled logits differn - likely causes: kernel compiled with different quantization layout, per-layer quantization rounding change, or precision-promote in kernel config.n - first actions: compare kernel.build_metadata.quant_profile between a and b. if mismatch, abort commit and roll back.nn- symptom: replay agreement slightly degraded (99.0-99.8)n - likely causes: non-determinism in floating ops at fringe layers, timing differences in fused kernels, or sampling variance in test corpus.n - first actions: increase sample size for replay check, run deterministic microbench on fused kernel path, and if persistent, capture kernel traces for triage.nnreconciliation algorithm (recommended pseudocode):npythonn high level pseudocode for deterministic reconciliationndef reconcile_snapshot(source_snapshot, target_kernel):n 1. validate metadatan assert source_snapshot.model_id target_kernel.model_idn assert source_snapshot.quant_profile target_kernel.quant_profilenn 2. stream keys and apply in deterministic order (lexicographic by session_id, then seq_num)n for session_id in sorted(source_snapshot.sessions):n for ev in sorted(source_snapshot.sessionssession_id.events, keylambda e: e.seq_num):n target_kernel.apply_event(session_id, ev)nn 3. run sampled deterministic forward passes and compare logitsn diffs n for prefix in sample_prefixes():n out_src source_snapshot.simulate_forward(prefix)n out_tgt target_kernel.simulate_forward(prefix)n diffs.append(cosine_similarity(out_src.logits, out_tgt.logits))nn return aggregate_agreement(diffs)nnupgrade and rollout policy (recommended):n1) canary (1 mirrored traffic, 30m) - 2) extended canary (5 mirrored traffic, 2h) - 3) progressive roll (20 - 50 - 100) with health gates at each step.n2) automatic rollback gates for any step if replay.agreement drops below configured threshold for the cohort.n3) all rollouts must include a replay corpus and the snapshot archive stored with provenance tags.nndeveloper guidance for kernel authors (short):n- maintain backward-compatible quant_profile changes add feature flags and opt-in toggles for new fused kernels.n- implement deterministic seeds for any non-deterministic code paths used during snapshot application and replay.n- provide a unit-test harness: unit_replay_suite that can be executed with ./tools/unit_replay_suite --snapshot --kernel .nnpost-incident checklist and artifacts required:n- snapshot_id(s), sample prefixes used, replay diffs, kernel build hashes for source and target, prometheus metric snapshots (15m pre/post), traces (otel) correlated to trace.session_id, and incident timeline.nnappendix a: example cli
