source_type: confluence, title: serving runtime hotfix procedure (hosted api), content: overviewnthis runbook describes how to execute an emergency hotfix or emergency rollback for the hosted api serving runtime. it is optimized for speed while preserving safety (blast-radius control, verification, rollback readiness).nnapplies to: runtime pods (model-server), runtime scheduler, runtime sidecars, runtime config/feature flags, and kernel selection/quant profiles when delivered via runtime image/config.nn preconditionsn- if there is active customer impact: declare an incident session ownership by draining new requests from a source shard, replaying kv as needed, and binding to a destination shard.nnarchitecture overview (concise):n- orchestration layer (orch): issues swap commands, coordinates canaries, and sets routing policies.n- shard controller (sc): enacts bind/unbind, coordinates kv replication, and performs drain.n- kv layer: multi-tiered prefix cache with ephemerality flags and fast-lookup index.n- frontdoor router: routes requests by session token - shard map can be flipped to prefer new shard when canary progresses.nnconsistency models and tradeoffs:n- option a (strong): synchronous kv snapshothandshake with two-phase commit. guarantees no missing keys at cost of higher latency during swap windows.n- option b (eventually consistent): shadow-replication with read-fallback to source shard. lower latency, but requires careful time-bounded fallbacks and observability.nnrecommended default for production: hybrid approach. start with option b during canary periods with strict telemetry for full rollout switch to option a for final cutover when load is predictable.nnpreflight checklist (automatable):n1) validate model artifact checksum and signature: sha256sum and k8s image signature present.n2) confirm destination shard has 1.5x memory headroom for kv warmup.n3) slo budget check: current error budget planned swap budget (default 0.5).n4) open on-call window and post runbook link to runtime-ops.n5) gather baseline telemetry (p50/p95/p99 tokens/latency, error-rates, kv-miss-rate).nnstep-by-step migration playbook (operational steps):n1) prepare canary routing rule:n - orch: create canary route rule (1 traffic) mapped to destination shard with shadow-read: true and write-back: false.n - confirm no destructive flags set.n2) warmup and shadow replication (10-30 minutes typical):n - trigger kv prefetch: sc issues async prefetch for top-10 hottest prefixes via background task.n - monitor kv-warmup-progress: expect 80 hot prefix residency within window.n3) telemetry gating during canary (continuous):n - p50/p95 latency delta 5 - 20 - 50 - 100 over multiple verification steps (15-60m between steps).n - at each step, run automated smoke tests and fuzzed prompt validation against responses to detect semantic drift.n5) final cutover (atomic rebind):n - switch routing map atomically: orch flips session token assignment and marks source shard for graceful deprecation.n - if option a chosen: perform synchronous kv handshake before flipping (blocking window).n - wait 3x observed median warmup latency before marking migration complete.n6) post-cutover validation and tidy-up:n - mark source shard as standby for 1 hour to serve any read-fallbacks and then evict.n - run integrity-check job to confirm no missing session prefixes.n - update catalog/version metadata and notify product/clients if required.nnrollback criteria and steps:n- auto-rollback triggers (any one):n sustained p99 latency 2x baseline for 15m.n error-rate spike 1 absolute for 5m.n kv-miss rate on destination 5x baseline for 10m.n semantic-eval failures (failing 3 out of 20 sampled prompts).n- rollback procedure:n 1) orch reassigns routing map back to source shard (atomic).n 2) destination shard switches to read-only and begins cache eviction.n 3) post-rollback alerting: tag incident and capture traces for triage.nnoperational knobs and configuration examples:n- canaryroute yaml example:n ---n kind: canaryrouten metadata:n name: model-swap-canary-1n spec:n percent: 1n shadow_read: truen write_back: falsen metrics_gates:n - latency_p95_delta_ms: 100n - kv_miss_rate_ratio: 2.0nn- shard binding config snippet:n shard_bind_timeout_ms: 30000n kv_sync_mode: shadow_async options: shadow_async synchronous_two_phasen max_prefetch_prefixes: 2000nnobservability required dashboards:n- canary health panel: p50/p95/p99 latency, ingest qps, kv-miss-rate, error-rate, session-affinity-violations.n- integrity panel: orphaned-prefix-count, prefix-staleness-hrs, fallback-read-count.n- tracing: ensure spans include orch.request_id, shard_id_old, shard_id_new, kv_sync_mode.n- logs: structured event dsid_8dfa8794d51e4bec899fb0c795c9ba8c, source_type: confluence, title: soft failure synthesis and routing playbook, content: summary:nnthis playbook documents the end-to-end design, operational guidance, and engineering procedures for synthesizing and routing soft failures in the redwood serving runtime. soft failures are controlled degradations (reduced fidelity, alternative kernels, fallbacks to smaller model variants, or increased batching/timeout tradeoffs) used to preserve availability and slos when a hard failure or capacity exhaustion is imminent.nngoals and scope:nn- define the runtime-level signals, thresholds, and scheduler policies used to trigger soft-failure modes.n- provide profiling and benchmarking scenarios to validate degradations preserve user-facing slas.n- document concrete runbook steps for detection, triage, mitigation, and rollback of soft-failure events.n- capture release compatibility constraints and known issues related to soft-failure orchestration.nnthis playbook applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments that use the redwood serving runtime. it covers kernel scheduling hooks, routing policies, kv cache behavior, telemetry instrumentation, and operator runbooks.nndefinitions and key concepts:nn- soft failure: a deliberate, well-scoped reduction in fidelity or compute that keeps requests progressing rather than failing hard (errors). examples: reduced beam size, lower-precision kernels (int8), model-variant downgrade, function-call truncation, or increasing allowed latency window.n- fidelity stair-step: an ordered list of degradation modes (tier 0: full fidelity tier 1: quantized kernels tier 2: smaller model tier 3: cached response / static fallback) used for predictable escalations.n- slo-preserving route: a request routing outcome that aims to keep p95 latency and error rate within slo by preferring lower-cost alternatives over returning 5xx errors.nnarchitecture overview (how soft-failure flows through runtime):nn1. signal sources: kernel latency spikes, gpu memory pressure, queue depth, per-tenant error budget depletion, cross-region capacity alerts. each signal is emitted to the runtime decision-plane.n2. decision layer: the decision fabric evaluates rules (slo rules, tenant priority, current fidelity state) and emits a policy action (e.g., apply degradation profile g: quantize-kernel allow-extra-20ms-latency).n3. scheduler kernel mapper: the kernel scheduler receives the policy and maps incoming requests to appropriate kernel binaries/runner pools, adjusting batching hints and preemption windows.n4. routing fallbacks: router chooses between local degraded pool, remote region, or model variant. a weighted hedge (default 80/20) is maintained during progressive rollouts to validate quality metrics before widening.nndiagram (text): decision fabric - scheduler - kernel pool(s) - router - client responses (fidelity stair-step applied at scheduler/router boundary).nnkernel scheduling and routing policy details:nnpolicy units and primitives:n- policydefinition: name, priority, trigger_signals, actions, rollback_window_seconds.n- actions (examples): set_kernel_hintquantized_int8, set_model_variantcompact-1.3b, extend_timeout_ms20, enable_kv_prefetchtrue.n- priority semantics: higher priority policies preempt lower ones within the same tenant cross-tenant isolation enforced via kernel-credit accounts.nndefault production policy (summary):n- trigger: per-gpu queue depth 85 or p95 kernel latency 1.4x baseline for 90s.n- action sequence (applied sequentially every 30 seconds until safe):n 1) hint quantized kernels for non-critical tenants.n 2) increase batching window by 10ms for background routes.n 3) swap to smaller model-variant for new sessions only.n 4) route 10 of traffic to remote region (longer network latency tradeoff).nntelemetry and profiling playbook (what to collect and how to act):nnsignals to collect (minimum):n- kernel dispatch latency histogram (per kernel id, per shard).n- gpu memory headroom gauge per node and per process.n- queue depth and queue wait time per route.n- kv cache hit ratio and reconstruction time.n- decision fabric action logs with correlation ids.n- sampled request traces (1 in 5k for production baseline, 1 in 200 for degraded periods).nnprofiling procedure when a degradation policy fires:n1) increase trace sampling to 1 in 200 for the affected tenant and route.n2) capture 60s of full kernel-level traces and stack annotations.n3) run an accelerated microbenchmark run simulating the observed concurrency shape (see benchmark scenarios).n4) produce a short profiling ticket with attached traces, affected kernels, and suggested mitigations.nnexample cli to collect kernel histogram from node: (shell snippet)nnsudo redwoodctl node-telemetry --node gpu-17 --metrics kernel_dispatch_histogram --window 60s traces/kernel_hist_60s.jsonnnbenchmark soft-fail p95: 700ms, quality drop measured by prompt eval: 65 of baseline and error rate slo threshold 1.5 or total errors 0.5.nntriage checklist (first 10 minutes):n1) acknowledge alert and capture top-of-trace logs: decision-fabric events and kernel histograms.n2) identify scope: tenants affected, routes, kernels, regions.n3) validate if degradation mode is intentional (rollout, experiment). if intentional, skip to monitoring - verification.n4) if unintentional, determine quickest reversible mitigation: temporarily widen rollback_window_seconds to 0 and ask decision fabric to cancel policies via the control plane.nnmitigation recipes (ordered by safety):na) conservative rollback: cancel active degradation policies for the affected tenant and force full-fidelity kernel mapping on a small set of canary nodes.nb) capacity unlock: evict background batch jobs (eviction priority policy) to recover headroom.nc) cross-region spill: route 25 of traffic to a warmed remote region with identical model variant.nd) emergency throttling: apply rate-limiter to low-priority routes only until headroom is restored.nnexample control-plane command to cancel a policy:nnredwoodctl policy cancel workflow: dev pateln, doc_id: dsid_22d5555c480d4f7fade8e9e19ace1bba, source_type: confluence, title: fidelity containment and cost-feedback playbook, content: overviewn--------nthis playbook defines a structured, testable approach for containing output fidelity regressions while responding to cost and capacity signals in redwoods serving runtime. the goal is to preserve customer-visible quality within defined tolerances while allowing the runtime to reduce unit cost and maintain latency slos under stress.nnintended audiencen- runtime sres and oncall engineersn- serving runtime product engineersn- applied ml / model-onboarding engineers responsible for model variantsn- solutions engineers running dedicated/private rolloutsnnscope and definitionsn- fidelity: measurable customer-facing quality of generated text or embeddings (proxy signals include embedding cosine similarity drift, eval-set pass rate, hallucination detectors, and automated eval metrics like rouge/bleu/em/accuracy on canned checks).n- cost signal: per-request (or per-token) cost estimate derived from kernel accounting and model variant price multipliers.n- containment action: an automated or manual change that reduces runtime resource use or switches model variant to a cheaper/less-fidelitous option (examples: quantized variant, shorter max tokens, trimmed sampling temperature, fall back to smaller model).n- allowed fidelity window: policy-defined bounds (absolute or relative) that define tolerable degradation for a given customer tier/route.nnkey principlesn1. prioritize customer-facing quality over short-term cost savings. containment actions must be reversible and accompanied by quality monitoring.n2. make containment decisions observable and auditable: every automated action must produce a traceable event and justification.n3. apply progressive containment: prefer parameter tuning and cache/batching before model-variant switch.n4. keep inexpensive, fast rollback paths and an explicit manual escalation path for high-impact customers.nnobservable signals and thresholdsn- primary signals: p50/p95 latency, p99 latency, tokens/second served, per-token-cost estimate, model variant error-rate on canary prompt set, embedding drift (cosine similarity delta), auto-eval pass rate.n- secondary signals: kernel queue length, gpu occupancy, kv cache hit ratio, request retries, grpc error rates.nnminimum policy thresholds (example defaults)n signal warning threshold containment threshold notes n---------------------------:----------------------:-------n p95 latency (route) 350 ms 600 ms measured at route-level aggregation over 1m windows n p99 latency 900 ms 2s escalation if sustained 5 minutes n per-token cost (moving 5m avg) 15 vs baseline 40 vs baseline baseline is 30d rolling median n embedding drift (cos sim drop) 0.03 0.07 evaluated on route-specific reference corpus n canary eval pass-rate drop 5 ppt 15 ppt ppt percentage points nncontainment matrix (progressive actions)n1. soft tuning (no model change): reduce max_response_tokens by 1030, reduce sampling temperature or top-p, tighten repetition_penalty, enable prefix/kv cache prefetch for hot routes.n2. batch and cache aggression: increase batching window by 1025 for non-interactive routes, enable shared prefix caching when identity-safe.n3. model micro-variants: switch to quantized or 8-bit floating variant of the same model.n4. model downgrade: route to smaller model family with documented fidelity/cost tradeoff.n5. route-based rate limiting: apply slow-path throttle to non-critical traffic classes.n6. emergency low-fidelity fallback: deterministic n-gram based summarization or templated replies for extreme outages.nnautomation policy template (yaml-like example)nn policy_name: fidelity-cost-feedback-2026ntriggers:n - metric: per_token_cost_5mn comparator: n threshold: 1.40 1.0 baselinen window: 300n severity: highn - metric: p95_latency_routen comparator: n threshold: 0.6 secondsn window: 60n severity: mediumnactions_sequence:n - id: soft_tune_1n action: reduce_max_tokensn params: percent: 20 n rollback_on: canary_eval_drop_ppt 10n - id: enable_batching_aggressiven action: increase_batch_window_msn params: add_ms: 15 n - id: variant_quantizedn action: switch_model_variantn params: variant: quant-8bit n - id: variant_downgraden action: switch_modeln params: model_family: redwood-lite n - id: emergency_template_fallbackn action: apply_template_fallbackn params: template_id: low_fidelity_fallback_v1 nnnoperational runbook (play-by-play)n1) detection and initial triage (oncall)- review alert payload: identify affected routes, model variants, and customer tiers.- confirm signal: check p95/p99 windows, per-token cost spike, and kernel-level metrics (gpu queue length, occupancy).- run quick baseline: compare to rolling 30d baseline and to same-window previous day.nn2) canary evaluation (automated/manual)- run the canonical canary prompt set for each impacted route against current runtime and candidate containment variants. canary outputs to be scored by automated eval harness.- pass criteria: no more than x ppt drop in canary pass-rate for standard tier less strict thresholds for internal/beta routes.nn3) apply progressive containment- execute actions in the containment matrix one step at a time. after each step, wait a stabilization window (default 60180s for soft tuning 510 minutes for model variant switches) and re-evaluate canary metrics and the primary signals.- required observability: annotate the deployment/trace with the containment_action id and reason.nn4) monitor and iterate- if metrics recover within thresholds, retain the change for a policy-defined cooldown (default 30 minutes) while running a more comprehensive quality sweep (1030m).- if metrics do not improve or quality regression exceeds rollback_on conditions, immediately roll back the last action and escalate to oncall escalation path.nn5) escalation pathn- pager duty: runtime-sre@redwood.com (primary)n- if repeat-size event or large customer impact: paging product-eng lead and solutions engineering for affected customers.n- for legal/security impact (data exposure): notify security@redwood.com immediately.nnmanual rollback checklistn- identify exact action to rollback (action id and timestamp).n- ensure no upstream automation will re-apply the action during rollback window. use the feature-flag lock: runtime.containment.lock true.n- execute rollback and validate canary and live traffic metrics for 15 minutes.n- note the rollback in incident timeline with justification.nntesting and preflight requirementsn- every containment action must have an associated unit test in the runtime-autotest suite and a canary-run scenario in the benchmark harness.n- poison tests: synthetic low-fidelity queries must be included to ensure fallback templates dont leak sensitive info.n- load test runbook: schedule a weekly simulated event where containment policies are exercised end-to-end in staging using traffic replays.nnobservability and dashboards (minimum set)n- route health dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token-cost trend, request volume, kv cache hit rate.n- canary quality dashboard: rolling pass-rate for canary prompts per route and per-customer-tier.n- containment actions log: chronological view of automated/manual actions, actors, and outcomes (success/failure, rollback).n- kernel telemetry correlation: cross-filter by trace id to observe kernel-level queue depth, gpu occupancy, and active kernel variant.nnaudit and compliancen- all containment decisions (automated or manual) must emit an audit event title: cold-start quality degradation detection and recovery runbook, content: summary:nthis runbook describes how to detect, triage, and recover from quality degradations that are correlated with cold-start events in the runtime (examples: increased hallucination rate, lower qa pass rate, deterministic prompt-prefix regressions after model swap, or output truncation tied to kv cache misses). it is focused on production incidents where client-facing correctness metrics drop following service restarts, model swaps, autoscaler-driven scale-ups, or routing to undersized warm pools.nnscope and intent:n- scope: hosted/dedicated/private deployments running the redwood serving runtime. applicable to model swaps, node restarts, autoscaling events, or any scenario where a high proportion of requests experience cold execution (empty kv/embedding caches, unprimed kernels).n- intent: detect regressions quickly, preserve customer-facing slos, and restore previous-quality behavior with minimal disruption. this runbook prioritizes safe, reversible actions and clarifies ownership.nnwho owns this runbook:n- first responder: serving-runtime oncall (eng-serving-runtime team)n- escalation: runtime-sre lead, model-onboarding owner, customer-success for impacted customersnnkey signals to monitor (detection):n1) behavioral quality metrics (primary):n - qa pass rate on synthetic prompt-sets (rolling 5m and 1h buckets). alert if 1h pass rate drops 20 relative to 6h baseline.n - hallucination indicator: fraction of responses matching negative heuristics (nonsense score, repeated tokens). alert if 5 of responses exceed hallucination threshold and correlated with cold-start tags.n2) telemetry and execution signals (correlated with cold-start):n - kv cache miss rate: per-shard and per-model kv miss rate spike (prometheus: runtime_kvcache_miss_rate). alert if 80 of requests for a cohort are cold for 10min.n - prefix latency spike: token-latency for first n tokens (token_index 2x baseline.n - model swap events: recent model variant switch or kernel rollouts (eventlog entries).n3) sampling-based checks (low-volume but high fidelity):n - shadow evaluation: sample requests shadowed to previous model/variant if shadowed outputs differ on correctness checks by 15 relative to live, flag as regression.nndetection playbook (automated alerts and triage):n- automated alerts to page oncall when any primary signal triggers. alerts should include:n - affected model(s)/variant(s) and cohort idsn - recent autoscaler/node events in last 10 minn - kv cache miss heatmap and per-shard error raten - attached sample of 10 failed responses (anonymized)nninitial triage (oncall checklist):n1) validate alert: confirm metric anomalies using promql and sampling endpoints. quick promql queries: n - qa pass rate: sum(rate(eval_qa_pass_total5m)) / sum(rate(eval_requests_total5m))n - kv cold fraction: increase(runtime_kvcache_miss_rate10m) 0.2n2) correlate with infra events: check cluster events, node restarts, pod reschedules, and model rollout timestamps (kubectl get events, /ops/eventlog).n3) isolate scope: check whether issue affects single model variant, model family, single region, or all customers. use per-route and per-token tagging.n4) collect traces dumps: capture 30s full trace for a failing request pattern (trace-id), and export kernel telemetry and kv warmup state for the affected shard(s). cli snippets below.nnimmediate mitigations (order of preference safer first):n1) route traffic to warm pool or previously healthy variant:n - use routing policy to send impacted percentage to warm pool while keeping the rest on primary for canary validation.n - command (control plane): redwood route update --model --variant prev-stable --percent 30 --reason cold-start-quality-rollbackn2) force kv prefill for high-impact cohorts: schedule an immediate prefill job for affected keys (see prefill command below). prefill avoids cold kv misses that often trigger hallucination in long-context models.n - prefill cli: redwood runtime prefill-kv --shard --keys-file /tmp/prefill-keys.json --priority highn3) temporarily widen quality slo to reduce batching/fusion: reduce concurrency and batching for the affected variant to reduce kernel cold micro-behavior that affects output shape.n - config patch (example yaml snippet):n batcher:n max_batch_tokens: 4096n target_latency_ms: 50n enable_prefill: falsen4) rollback model variant if the degradation coincides with a recent variant rollout and automated canary validation fails. rollback is disruptive prefer routing to warm pool when customer impact is partial.nncommands data-collection recipes:n- capture a full trace (oncall machine with access):n curl -ss -h authorization: bearer obs_key /tmp/trace.jsonn- export kv state for shard:n redwood infra kvcache dump --shard --output /tmp/kvcache-shard-123.dumpn- run batch of synthetic qa prompts against previous-stable variant:n redwood eval run --model :prev-stable --prompt-file qa-failure-sample.json --concurrency 5 --out /tmp/eval-prev.jsonnnoperational controls (threshold table editable):n- this table lists the default thresholds used by the detection engine. operate conservatively and update only after post-incident review.nn signal alert threshold severity default action n------:------n 1h qa pass drop vs baseline 20 absolute drop sev2 page oncall run shadow eval n kv cold fraction (cohort) 80 cold requests for 10m sev1 route to warm pool prefill kv n prefix token latency change 2x for token_idx 15 sev1 immediate rollback or route to prev-variant nnnote: the table above should be managed in the runtime-config repo (config/runtime/coldstart-detection.yaml). sample yaml fields: nnsignal_thresholds:n qa_pass_drop_pct: 20n kvcold_fraction_threshold: 0.8n prefix_latency_multiplier: 2.0n shadow_delta_pct: 15nnrecovery playbook (step-by-step):n1) if kv cold fraction is main driver: run prefill job, validate reduced kv miss rate, then gradually increase traffic to variant.n2) if model swap is root cause and prior variant performs better on shadow eval: route 100 to previous variant and open a rollback change in the deployment tracker.n3) if the issue is due to kernel rollout or scheduling change: pause the kernel rollout, set scheduler to conservative profile, and engage kernel owner to examine kernel changes.n4) if widespread and unknown: enable temporary degradation mode that firms up safety heuristics (shorten response length, add conservative decoding params like top_p0.8) while engineers investigate.nnpost-incident actions (postmortem checklist):n- create a postmortem within 72 hours with: timeline, contributing causes, sampling artifacts, kv dump, traces, rollout ids, and remediation owner.n- update the thresholds table if alert was noisy or too lax.n- add targeted integration tests to the benchmark suite: shadow-evaluation scenarios that mimic the failed cohort shape.n- schedule a follow-up: kernel scheduling replay across recorded traces to reproduce the behavior in the lab.nnrunbook escalation matrix and sla:n- sev1 (customer-impacting correctness): page oncall immediately, 15 min ack, 1 hour mitigation or rollback.n- sev2 (degraded qa but limited subset): page oncall, 30 min ack, mitigation within 4 hours.nnknown gotchas and heuristics:n- small cohorts (low traffic) produce noisy qa signals require a minimum sampling floor of 200 requests/hour before auto-alerting.n- not every kv miss spike implies hallucination cross-check with decoding entropy and repeated token heuristics.n- prefill can be expensive. use prioritized prefill for high-value cohorts only.nnexamples and case studies (short):n- case: model-variant x rollout (2025-08-13) produced a 35 qa pass drop for long-context summarization requests. root cause: optimistic kernel fusion that skipped boundary prefetch for windowed attention. recovery: immediate rollback to prev-stable, patch to prefetch check in kernel 2.1. patch released with canary and shadow checks.nnreferences and links:n- prefill job operator dsid_aeb8dd3f5b744ea0b307954410bd57a7, source_type: confluence, title: runtime fallback graceful degradation playbook, content: summary:noperational runbook and engineering guidance for automatic fallback and graceful degradation behaviors in the redwood serving runtime. covers triggers, architecture interactions, scheduler implications, profiling and benchmarking guidance, and step-by-step incident remediation.nnbody:noverview:nnthis playbook describes the intended behavior and operational steps for runtime-level fallback and graceful degradation across redwood inference deployments. it targets on-call sres, runtime engineers, and platform product owners who must ensure applications meet latency and availability slos under degraded conditions (e.g., spot evictions, model ooms, regional capacity constraints, extreme tail-latency events).nngoals and slo impact:nn- primary goals:n - keep requests successful and bounded in latency by applying controlled degradation rather than failing hard.n - maintain transparency to customers (logs, metrics, traces) when fallbacks occur.n - provide deterministic, testable fallback policies that interact cleanly with kernel scheduler decision-making.n- slo considerations:n - availability slo: keep request success rate 99.9 across primaryfallback flows.n - latency slo: p95 3 in 5m).n2) resource saturation: queue length config.queue_threshold or cpu/gpu utilization sustained 92 for 60s.n3) tail-latency surge: p99 request latency for a model configured model.p99_threshold for 60s.n4) regional capacity shortage: target region has 3 absolute) and defined auto-fallback rule is enabled.nnarchitecture integration (how fallback fits in the runtime):nn- placement: fallback logic lives in the routing and execution orchestration layer (service: runtime-router). the runtime-worker accepts policy decisions (serve, downgrade, cache-hit, reject) returned by router.n- policy store: policies (per-route) are defined in the control plane config-store and propagated as immutable rollout keys. each policy key maps to a fallback strategy bundle.n- execution paths:n - normal path: route - schedule - worker - model - response.n - fallback path examples:n - model-variant downgrade: route - schedule - worker - quantized-or-smaller-model - response.n - cached-prefix reply: route - cache-check - cached-response - response.n - short-circuit: route - runtime-synthesizer - short-summary response (used for long-running synth).n - regional fallback: route - alt-region-router - remote-worker - response.n- observability: all fallback decisions emit a fallback.reason tag and fallback.variant tag on traces and metrics. billing and cost analytics receive a fallback.flag to attribute cost differences.nnfallback strategies and recommended order (policy template):nn1) prefetch cache (least-visibility change)n - serve cached completion or prefix when ttl not expired.n - use for high-qps, low-variance routes (embeddings, re-ranking).n2) quantized / smaller model variantn - serve from a model variant with smaller memory footprint or int8 quantization.n - keep model-variant performance profile available in model catalog.n3) partial-response / synthesisn - return partial tokens up to configured token limit summary flag.n - mark response with metadata: degraded: true, reason: partial-response.n4) cross-region routingn - use only when network latency increase is acceptable vs local unavailability.n5) hard reject / 503 fallbackn - final resort when no compatibility policy exists provide diagnostics link in body.nnkernel-scheduler considerations:nn- prioritization policy: the kernel scheduler should expose preemption hints for fallback flows. for example, models used in fallback (smaller quantized variants) receive lower cpu/gpu priority class so that primary models reclaim resources first.n- eviction thresholds: scheduler must support two eviction windows: graceful and immediate. graceful eviction attempts to flush in-flight kv caches and migrate small models immediate eviction kills the process when node health is compromised.n- continuous batching interaction: when switching to smaller model variant, kernel should recompute batching windows (batch_size, batch_timeout) because per-token latency and throughput profiles change. the runtime must trigger a batching reconfigure hook on model-switch.nnprofiling benchmarking guidance during fallback mode:nn- benchmark plan: run a paired a/b microbenchmark comparing normal variant vs fallback variant across the following axes: cold-start latency, steady-state latency, p99, throughput at target concurrency, memory footprint, and token throughput.n- profiling checklist (oncall):n 1) capture perf traces (nvprof / nsight) and runtime traces (opentelemetry) for both normal and fallback variants.n 2) compare kv-cache hit rate and batching efficiency before/after fallback.n 3) measure syscall and gpu kernel latencies look for stall patterns indicating memory pressure.n- metrics to surface on dashboards: fallback.count, fallback.latency.delta, fallback.impact_pct_of_requests, fallback.model_variant, fallback.trigger_reason.nnoperational runbook (step-by-step):nndetection:n1) alert fires: fallback_policy_triggered or model.p99_exceeded.n2) oncall acknowledges and posts to incident channel (ops/runtime-fallback).nnimmediate triage (first 10 minutes):n1) confirm scope: run queries:n - curl -ss - rtfctl route inspect --fieldsqueue_len,model_variant,uptimen2) check node and scheduler health:n - kubectl get pods -n runtime -l appruntime-worker -o wide n - k8s node metrics: kubectl top nodes sort -nr -k3n3) determine fallback type currently in use via logs/traces (search for fallback.reason tag).n4) if fallback variant is active and correctness is acceptable, follow stabilization steps below.nnstabilization steps (1060 minutes):n1) if queue backpressure is root cause, temporarily increase per-route max_workers or enable short-burst scaling (config: autoscale.bursttrue) for up to 30 minutes. document change and set timer.n2) if model ooms triggered fallback, scale up node group (add nodes) or enable model eviction order: evict large non-critical models first.n3) if degradation due to bad model quality (detected by eval alerts), toggle model.quality_block to stop rollout and enable previously-validated variant.n4) apply temporary route-level policy: set fallback.strategycache-first, max_tokens128, respond_with_degradation_flagtrue.nnrollback and permanent fix (124 hours):n1) if configuration/rollout caused the issue, revert the rollout using the control-plane rollback cli: cpctl rollout revert .n2) if capacity is root cause, schedule a capacity bump and update scaling policy: infra-iac pr to increase gpu_pool.capacity by recommended amount.n3) if kernel scheduler misbehavior suspected, collect scheduler dump and escalate to runtime-scheduler team: runtime-scheduler@redwood.ai. include scheduler dump path and most recent kernel-profile tarball.nncli and debug commands (common):n- rtfctl policy get n- rtfctl model variants n- curl -ss kubectl logs -n runtime -c worker --since15m grep fallbackn- oc promql sum(rate(fallback_total5m)) by (route)nnconfig snippet (example policy - warmup strategies and entropy reduction playbook, content: summary:nthis playbook describes recommended approaches for reducing cold-start latency and request output entropy during model/worker startup in redwoods serving runtime. it consolidates operational patterns, automated warmup recipes, example configs, and runbook steps for diagnosing and recovering from cold-startrelated slo breaches. the guidance applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.nnscope:n- applies to long-lived model workers and ephemeral worker pools (autoscaled gpus).n- focus on first-token latency, tail latency during burst scaling, and early-session output quality variability caused by incomplete kv cache or lazy kernel initialization.n- excludes model training workflows and offline batch workloads.nnbackground and problem statement:ncold starts in the runtime manifest in three measurable ways:n1) high first-byte/first-token latency before kernels and memory paths are hot,n2) increased variance/entropy in early outputs when kv caches or sampled attention layers are empty or not warmed, andn3) transient resource throttling when many warmup tasks coincide with customer traffic.nthese symptoms complicate slos for developer-facing apis and drive poor user experience for plg customers who exercise new endpoints.nngoals and slos:n- bring median first-token latency for a cold worker within 1.2x of steady-state median within the first 60 seconds of start.n- keep 99th-percentile first-token latency below 250ms for dedicated pools and 500ms for ephemeral workers on typical l-inference models (l 512 tokens) during warmup windows.n- ensure early-output perplexity / bleu (where applicable) is within 10 of steady-state model output on canonical prompt sets after warmup sequence completes.nnprinciples:n- make warmup deterministic and measurable. synthetic sequences should mimic real user distributions.n- minimize interference with live traffic: warmup must be rate-limited, backpressure-aware, and preemptible.n- favor progressive warming over wholesale parallel warmup when capacity-constrained.n- prefer cached-prefix warming for popular prompt prefixes and kv cache seeding for chat-style sessions.nnwarmup techniques (catalog):n1) kernel and cuda warmupn- purpose: jit kernels, populate driver memory mappings, load ptx/cu into gpu.n- recipe: run a minimal forward pass with sequence_length32 and batch_size1 across major model ops.n- observability: kernel load time traces, cuda module load events.nn2) kv-cache seeding (chat and long-context models)n- purpose: fill per-shard kv caches with realistic key/value vectors for reused prefixes.n- recipe: replay top-n canonical prefixes derived from traffic analytics (n20 default) at target sequence lengths.n- implementation note: use offline precomputed embeddings for synthetic prefixes to avoid model compute where possible.nn3) token-distribution annealing (entropy reduction)n- purpose: reduce early output variance by briefly constraining temperature/top-k during first few tokens.n- recipe: during warmup requests set temperature0.7 - 0.5 - 0.2 over first 5 tokens, then restore customer-configured sampling.n- guardrail: only apply to internal warmup requests do not alter customer-visible sampling.nn4) layerwise micro-batching for kernel primingn- purpose: exercise large-matrix paths at small batch sizes to prime gemm kernels and memory allocator.n- recipe: run micro-batches of 14 across sequence lengths 8,32,128 in series.nn5) prefix-aware kv prefetching for multi-tenant poolsn- purpose: avoid polluted global kv spaces by quarantining tenant-specific warmup prefixes.n- recipe: allocate transient warmup kv buckets tagged by tenant and promote buckets into the main tenant shard once validated.nnwarmup orchestration patterns:n- passive: warmup triggered on scale-up completion but paused if ingress tps threshold.n- active: proactive warmup before traffic shifts (e.g., scheduled deploys, predictable traffic spikes).n- hybrid: run a minimal passive warmup on boot, then schedule active warmup in off-peak windows.nnconfiguration examples (yaml snippet):nnwarmup:n enabled: truen mode: hybridn prefix_list_source: traffic-analytics/top-prefixes-v2n sequence_profile:n - length: 32n count: 10n - length: 128n count: 5n kvbucket: tenant_quarantinen rate_limit_rps: 5n max_concurrency: 2n sampling_anneal_steps: 5nnnsuggested default parameters:n- rate_limit_rps: 5 requests per worker during warmupn- max_concurrency: 2 synthetic warmup threads per gpun- prefix_list n: 20 top prefixes per model/tenantn- anneal_steps: 38 tokens depending on model sensitivitynnautomated warmup pipelines (implementation notes):n- warmup controller integrates with orchestration service (k8s operator / redwood scheduler).n- controllers must observe the pool slo token bucket before issuing warmup requests.n- warmup requests are flagged at trace-level with tag: warmuptrue for downstream trimming and auditing.n- use per-model warmup manifests stored in the model catalog for reproducibility.nnrunbook: diagnosing a warmup-related incident (slo breach)n1) detectn - alerts: increased first-token latency (p99_first_token threshold) or high early-output perplexity for a small but growing percentage of sessions.n - query: filter traces where trace.tagwarmup ! true to exclude synthetic runs.n2) triagen - check cluster events: scale-up, ooms, gpu driver reloads within last 10 min.n - check warmup controller logs: failures, rate-limit kicks, preemption events.n - inspect kv cache hit rates (per-shard): missing hits indicate improper seeding.n3) immediate mitigation (015 min)n - pause active warmup pipeline (toggle warmup.enabledfalse).n - if high latency correlates with kernel loads, roll back to previous runtime image with known kernel warm state.n - reduce warmup concurrency or rate limits: set max_concurrency1 and rate_limit_rps1.n4) recovery (1560 min)n - perform controlled progressive warmup: one worker at a time with monitoring hooks.n - if kv caches were corrupted, evict and reseed using validated prefix lists.n - re-run synthetic sampling with telemetry to validate output perplexity.n5) post-incident actionsn - collect root cause: automation bug, driver regression, noisy prefix set, or capacity storm.n - update model warmup manifest and increase test coverage in ci for cold-start scenarios.nnscripting and cli examples:n- trigger an on-demand warmup for model mosaic-v2 with protocol begins.n 4. migrating - hot (fast-path) if migration succeeds without loss.n 5. migrating - evicted if migration fails or eviction threshold crossed.n 6. any - closed on explicit session end or ttl expiry.nnkv-cache consistency guarantees and semantics:n- within-shard operations: atomic append semantics for kv-update events. kernels consuming kv must use the latest indicated sequence number stamped by the session coordinator.n- cross-shard handoff: we use a two-phase snapshot-and-ack protocol for handoff: source worker snapshots kv segments, destination worker applies snapshot and acknowledges. only after ack does routing flip.n- best-effort reordering protection: sequence numbers prevent reordering when network duplicate packets occur however, packet loss during handoff can yield partial snapshots that must be detected and retried.nnconfiguration table (default thresholds and rationale):n config_key default unit rationale n--------------------:------:----------n fidelity debt amortization operational playbook, content: summaryn-------nthis playbook describes the elastic fidelity debt amortization pattern: a deterministic, observable procedure to reduce latency/cost slo debt by gradually stepping application fidelity (model variant, quantization, batch sizing, caching aggressiveness) using a staircase profile. the goal is to preserve user-facing availability while amortizing the operational and quality cost of emergency fidelity drops over a controlled time window.nnwhen to usen-----------n- high short-term load or capacity pressure where immediate full-fidelity fallback causes unacceptable cost or instability.n- post-incident recovery when we want to converge back to nominal fidelity without causing new tail-latency spikes.n- release windows for quantization/kernel rollouts where a fast rollback would cause excess cost or churn.nnintended guarantees and slos impactedn------------------------------------n- availability: no more than 1 user-facing errors during transition windows.n- latency: p95 should remain below configured emergency slo (example: 450ms).n- quality budget: aggregated eval-score degradation limited to -3 per 10 minutes during amortization.n- cost smoothing: avoid 2x immediate per-token cost increase when restoring fidelity.nnkey concepts and terminologyn----------------------------n- fidelity step: a named configuration applying a set of runtime knobs (model_variant, quant_profile, batch_max, kvcache_mode, kernel_variant).n- debt window: the time budget to recover (e.g., 30m).n- amortization staircase: ordered fidelity steps applied at deterministic intervals.n- safety gate: quality and latency checks that must pass before launching the next step up.nnexample staircase (recommended baseline)n---------------------------------------n1) emergency-low: small quantized variant, aggressive batch coalescing, kv cache only prefix mode. (immediate)n2) safety-hold: medium quantized variant, conservative batch increase, kv caching warmed, kernel spec fallback. (5 minutes)n3) gradual-restore-1: larger variant with per-tenant token cap lift, reduced quantization. (10 minutes)n4) gradual-restore-2: near-nominal variant, speculative prefetching enabled. (20 minutes)n5) nominal: full-fidelity model variant and runtime knobs. (3060 minutes)nnoperational configuration (policy sample yaml)n--------------------------------------------n- name: elastic_fidelity_amortizationn debt_window_minutes: 30n steps:n - id: emergency-lown duration_minutes: 5n model_variant: gptx-mini-q4n quant_profile: q4-aggn batch_max_tokens: 1024n kvcache_mode: prefix-onlyn accept_quality_drop_pct: 5.0n - id: safety-holdn duration_minutes: 5n model_variant: gptx-small-q4n quant_profile: q4n batch_max_tokens: 2048n kvcache_mode: normaln accept_quality_drop_pct: 3.0n - id: gradual-restore-1n duration_minutes: 10n model_variant: gptx-base-q8n quant_profile: q8n batch_max_tokens: 3072n kvcache_mode: normal-warmupn accept_quality_drop_pct: 1.5n - id: nominaln duration_minutes: 10n model_variant: gptx-basen quant_profile: fp16n batch_max_tokens: 4096n kvcache_mode: fulln accept_quality_drop_pct: 0.2nntelemetry signals to watch (real-time)n-------------------------------------n- runtime.p95_ms (by route and model_variant) target: 1n- runtime.kvcache_hit_ratio (by tenant) expected to increase through steps flag if 2x baseline when moving stepsn- eval_shadow.delta_score (shadow eval harness) must stay within accept_quality_drop_pctnnrunbook: emergency execution (operator path)n-------------------------------------------n1) detect: pager triggers (high p95 or gpu oom alerts). open incident in slack channel runtime-incidents and create an incident stub.n2) immediate action (02 min): set policy to emergency-low. cli: redwood runtime apply-policy --policy elastic_fidelity_amortization --start-step emergency-low --forcen3) observe (27 min): watch runtime.p95_ms, runtime.error_rate, kvcache_hit_ratio. if error_rate 1.5 after emergency-low, escalate to oncall and consider capacity-side mitigations (resume fallback region or scale up dedicated capacity).n4) controlled staircase (530 min): allow policy to advance per configured durations. before each advance, execute safety gate checks (see below). if a gate fails, halt and execute remedial actions (warm caches/evict/prefetch or re-enforce batching).n5) converge to nominal: once nominal step passes all gates for two consecutive intervals, mark incident resolved and create a post-incident note with metric deltas.nnsafety gate checks (pre-step promotion)n--------------------------------------n- promoted if:n - p95 improved or (scheduler, batching, kv cache, gpu utilization signals) and how to apply mitigations safely without causing retry storms or noisy-neighbor regressions.nnthis runbook is used when:n- p95/p99 latency spikes and/or timeouts correlate with runtime saturation.n- error rates increase due to runtime admission rejecting work (shed) or the gateway/routing breaker opening.n- one or more gpu pools show if runtime is overloaded, accepting more work usually makes recovery harder.n2. avoid retry storms. any change that increases 429/503 must ensure stable retry-after behavior at the edge (gateway) and bounded retries in clients.n3. change one thing at a time. apply a single mitigation, wait 35 minutes, then evaluate.n4. preserve tenant isolation. do not globally increase batching to fix one tenant if it degrades others.nn quick decision treenuse this to choose the right mitigation quickly.nn a) queue depth climbing and latency increasing gpu utilization highnlikely compute saturation (tokens/sec bound) or under-provisioned pool.n- first actions: tighten admission / reduce concurrency confirm gateway breaker is protecting.n- secondary: reduce max_tokens caps / streaming concurrency adjust batching caps conservatively.nn b) queue depth climbing gpu utilization moderate memory usage high / oomsnlikely kv cache pressure / memory fragmentation / long-context load.n- first actions: cap max_context or max_prefill_tokens reduce parallelism for long prompts.n- secondary: adjust kv cache policy reduce batch size or prefill concurrency.nn c) queue depth stable latency spikes error reduction that reduces dependency load.n- secondary: coordinate with sre consider draining affected shards.nn d) shed rate high but saturation metrics look normalnlikely bad thresholds or bad signal / instrumentation issue.n- first actions: validate signal freshness and aggregation check if a single shard is bad.n- secondary: roll back threshold changes page runtime instrumentation owner.nn where to interpretnuse these to confirm you are dealing with runtime overload (vs gateway/routing/dependency).nn 1) prefill queue depthnwhat it means: number of requests waiting for prefill (prompt processing).ninterpretation:n- rising steadily with increasing prefill latency indicates prefill saturation (often long prompts).n- if prefill queue grows but decode queue is flat, you are prefill-bound.nn 2) decode queue depthnwhat it means: backlog of decode steps (streaming generation) waiting for compute.ninterpretation:n- rising decode queue with high gpu util indicates tokens/sec saturation.n- rising decode queue with moderate gpu util can indicate scheduler overhead or throttling.nn 3) token/sec saturationnwhat it means: measured throughput approaching pools steady-state ceiling.ninterpretation:n- if tokens/sec is near ceiling and p99 worsens, prioritize shedding / concurrency reduction.n- if tokens/sec is low but queues grow, suspect stalls, memory, or dependency issues.nn 4) kv cache pressurensignals:n- kv_cache_usage_ratio high (near configured limit)n- high kv_cache_evictions and increasing latencyninterpretation:n- high kv usage correlates with long contexts and many concurrent streams.n- evictions can cause performance cliffs prefer limiting long-context concurrency rather than only increasing batching.nn 5) memory pressure / fragmentation proxynsignals:n- increasing allocation failures / reserved but unavailable patternsn- frequent oom recoveries/restartsninterpretation:n- treat as urgent restarts can cause thundering herd if the gateway keeps admitting.nn standard triage proceduren step 1 confirm impact and scope (23 minutes)n1. identify region(s), model(s), and tiers affected.n2. confirm if the gateway breaker is open and shedding is happening at the edge.n3. check whether impact is localized to a pool/shard or systemic.nnrecord in the incident doc (or slack thread):n- start timen- affected region model tiern- current shed rate and p99 latencynn step 2 determine saturation type (5 minutes)nuse the metrics glossary above to classify as:n- compute saturation (decode-bound)n- prefill saturation (prompt-bound)n- memory/kv pressuren- dependency brownout / scheduler stallnn step 3 apply the least risky mitigationnprefer mitigations in this order (lowest blast radius first):n1) tighten admission for the impacted pool/routen2) reduce expensive features (streaming concurrency, tool-calling complexity)n3) reduce max_tokens / max_context caps (tier-aware)n4) tune batching capsn5) drain/cordon bad replicas/shardsnn step 4 validate recoverynafter each change:n- wait 35 minutes (longer for long-context workloads)n- confirm queue depth trends downn- confirm p99 latency improvesn- confirm shed rate stabilizes (not oscillating)n- confirm no new error class/regression is introduced (e.g., missing retry-after at edge)nn mitigation actions (how-to)nnotes:n- exact knobs vary by deployment. when in doubt, coordinate with gateway oncall before changing customer-visible behavior.n- all changes should be logged in the incident timeline with time, actor, knob, previous value, new value.nn mitigation 1 reduce runtime admission / concurrency (preferred first response)ngoal: stop backlog growth and allow queues to drain.nncommon actions:n- reduce runtime_max_inflight_requests for the impacted pool.n- reduce decode_concurrency_per_gpu or streams_per_replica.nnoperational guidance:n- if queue depth is climbing: cut concurrency by 1025 first.n- if ooms are occurring: cut concurrency by 2550 and reduce long-context traffic.nnexample (illustrative) command patterns:n- view current pool config:n - rwctl runtime pools get --region us-east --pool hosted-a10g-1n- patch concurrency cap:n - rwctl runtime pools patch --region us-east --pool hosted-a10g-1 --set decode_concurrency_per_gpu6nnrollback:n- restore previous values after queues stabilize for at least 30 minutes.nn mitigation 2 feature reduction toggles (reduce expensive work)ngoal: reduce per-request cost while keeping service available.nnsupported feature reduction modes (must be policy-guarded):n- lower streaming concurrency (limits concurrent active streams per tenant)n- reduce tool-calling complexity (e.g., cap tool calls or tool schema size)n- apply stricter max_tokens caps during overloadnnwhen to use:n- decode-bound saturation (tokens/sec ceiling)n- tenant with unusually heavy tool-calling causing noisy-neighbor behaviornnhow to execute:n- confirm the feature flag is enabled for overload mode (policy causing latency cliffs.nnactions:n- increase max_batch_tokens slightly (515) if gpu util is high but scheduler overhead is low.n- decrease max_batch_tokens if tail latency is exploding due to too-large batches.nnwhen to use:n- stable traffic with predictable sequence lengthsn- you have clear evidence of batching inefficiency rather than pure saturationnnwarnings:n- over-aggressive batching high.nnsteps (generic kubernetes pattern adapt to your environment):n1. identify unhealthy pods:n - kubectl -n serving-runtime get pods -l pool -o widen2. check logs for repeated oom or crash loops.n3. cordon/drain (if supported via runtime orchestration):n - rwctl runtime replicas cordon --replica --reason oom-loopn4. verify load rebalances and queues recover.nn mitigation 6 coordinate shed rate remains 12 after local mitigationsn- you see a single hot model family saturating a regionnnwhat to provide:n- region/pool/model impactedn- current saturation signals (queue depth, tokens/sec)n- desired action (regional shift vs model fallback)nnconstraints:n- ensure loop prevention and bounded retries are working (routing should not bounce between regions/models).nn common min-open duration.n- reduce concurrency slightly more to create headroom.n- confirm signal is smoothed (avoid reacting to 1030s spikes).nn failure mode: timeouts increase but shed rate is lownsymptoms:n- requests pile up gateway keeps admitting runtime queues spike.nfixes:n- coordinate with gateway to increase edge shedding and set retry-after.n- ensure runtime admission is wired to degraded.nn verification checklist (post-mitigation)n- queue depths trending down (prefill and/or decode)n- ooms stopped restart rate normaln- p95/p99 improved and stable for 15 minutesn- shed rate stable (not flapping) and within acceptable tier policyn- no spike in client retries / upstream request rate amplificationn- correlation ids present in overload responses (spot-check sample logs)nn or inconsistent error payloads observedn- need for new/clearer dashboards or better signal smoothingnncapture:n- peak queue depth, peak tokens/sec, max kv usage ration- time-to-recovery after backoff guide, content: overview:nnthis guide defines the detection, containment, and remediation patterns we use when the llm kv (key-value) cache exhibits consistency or availability problems that engineeringn- notification channels: platform-ops, oncall-pager, paged phone rosternndefinitions and failure modes:n1) missing-kv reads: requests that expect a cached kv entry but receive a cache-miss where a valid entry should exist.n2) stale-kv reads: reads that return older prefix state due to replication lag or divergent leadership.n3) partial-shard-unavailable: a subset of shards return 5xx or time out.n4) consistency-mismatch: divergence between metadata index and stored shard contents resulting in incorrect routing or invalid tokenization offsets.nndetection signals (metrics logs):n- metric/runtime_kv_read_error_rate (per-shard, p95)n- metric/runtime_kv_stale_read_ratio (synthetic checks comparing authoritative source to cache)n- metric/runtime_kv_replication_lag_seconds (95/99)n- alert: kv-shard-error-criticaln - trigger: shard error rate 0.5 for 5m and p95 latency 250msn - severity: p1 (page)n- alert: kv-read-degraded-warnn - trigger: aggregated stale_read_ratio 0.2 for 10m or replication_lag_seconds p99 3sn - severity: p2 (slack)n- dashboard panels to include:n - per-shard read error heatmapn - multi-region canary diff (ratio of mismatches)n - recent leader-change spike or replication_lag configurable threshold andn - model slo indicates a better ux serving slightly stale responses vs 5xx errors.n3) in degraded-read-backoff mode, the runtime will:n - apply exponential read delay/queuing for new requests targeting that shard (config: backoff_base_ms, max_backoff_ms)n - fall back to last-known-good (lkg) prefix state if the request decoder accepts slightly older kv state (config: allow_stale_prefixtrue for non-strict routes)n - stream partial outputs with a header: x-redwood-kv-state: degraded/lkgnthis behavior reduces 5xx storms, prevents cascading load onto healthy shards, and buys time for automated healing.nnconfig table (recommended defaults):n knob description default n----------------------------n backoff_base_ms base backoff sessionn, doc_id: dsid_03a8ab94206346de9272d413bfe6c367, source_type: confluence, title: execution provenance, replay, and hash specification, content: overviewnnthis document defines the execution provenance format, canonical hash scheme, and replay artifact requirements used by redwood inference runtime for deterministic reproduction of inference executions. it standardizes what data to capture at request ingress, kernel selection, kv-cache decision, routing, and final token emission to enable: post-incident forensics, fidelity regression repro, and deterministic replay in the sandbox.nngoalsnn- make a minimal, fixed set of fields that allow deterministic replays at the same or compatible runtime version.n- ensure artifact size is bounded and classified so privacy-sensitive payloads can be redacted before long-term storage.n- provide a reproducible hashing strategy to detect non-deterministic divergence between production and replayed runs.nnscope and non-goalsnn- scope: inference request path from api gateway - runtime-coordinator - kernel-router - gpu shard(s) - response assembly. includes model variant metadata, kernel hints, and runtime decisions.n- non-goal: this is not a full telemetry retention policy refer to observability for retention windows and pii rules.nnspecification: execution provenance artifactnnan execution artifact (e-artifact) is a newline-delimited json (ndjson) file with three reserved top-level records in order: metadata, decisions, events. additional records (log / trace / payload) are optional and flagged. each line is a single json object with primitive values only. nested objects are flattened with dot notation in keys (see examples).nnrequired records (order matters):nn1) metadata record (type: metadata)n- artifact_version: text (current: v1)n- runtime_version: semantic version string (e.g., 2.14.0)n- model_id: catalog identifier (e.g., redwood/open-13b-v2)n- model_variant: text (e.g., int8-fast)n- request_id: global request uuid (x-request-id)n- timestamp_utc: iso8601n- ingress_cluster: region/cluster idn- route_name: api route namen- fidelity_profile: label used by fidelity-orchestrator (e.g., balanced)nnexample metadata line:nn type: metadata,n artifact_version: v1,n runtime_version: 2.14.0,n model_id: redwood/open-13b-v2,n model_variant: int8-fast,n request_id: b6b7e2f2-8a72-4f1a-9c7b-1a2d3e4f5a6b,n timestamp_utc: 2026-01-10t15:34:21z,n ingress_cluster: us-west-2-prod-1,n route_name: /v1/generate,n fidelity_profile: cost-optimizednnn2) decisions record (type: decisions)n- kernel_selection: text (kernel id chosen)n- kernel_flags: comma-separated short flags (e.g., prefetch,kvcache)n- kvcache_hit_bitmap: base64-encoded bitset (optional)n- scheduler_cohort: text (cohort id used by job scheduler)n- routing_path: pipe-separated list of nodes/shards (e.g., coord-3shard-12shard-15)n- batch_size_at_dispatch: integern- quantization_profile: textn- fallback_invoked: boolean string (truefalse)n- fallback_reason: text (if fallback_invoked)nnexample decisions line:nn type: decisions,n kernel_selection: kvm-attn-v2-16,n kernel_flags: kv-prefetch,continuous-batch,n scheduler_cohort: cohort-22,n routing_path: coord-3shard-12,n batch_size_at_dispatch: 8,n quantization_profile: q4_0,n fallback_invoked: falsennn3) events record(s) (type: event)n- sequence of deterministic events with monotonic event_index starting at 0.n- event_type: one of ingress, kernel_enter, kernel_exit, kv_write, kv_read, token_emit, errorn- event_index: integern- elapsed_ms: integer (ms since metadata.timestamp_utc)n- note: short text (max 256 chars)n- checksum_hint: short hex string (optional, used during correlation)nnexample event line:nn type: event,n event_type: kernel_enter,n event_index: 3,n elapsed_ms: 37,n note: dispatched to shard-12nnnoptional record types (flagged via type):nn- payload (type: payload): request prompt and redaction mask. if present, store only after automated pii redaction payloads 8kb must be stripped and replaced with a reference to secure blob store.n- trace (type: trace): block of stack frames/execution markers for kernel base64 compressed.n- log (type: log): supplemental runtime logs, one-per-line semantics.nnhashing and divergence detectionnnpurpose: determine if replay diverges from production execution due to runtime non-determinism or model-level changes.nncanonical hash construction (sha256):n- inputs concatenated in this exact order (utf-8): metadata.request_id runtime_version model_id model_variant decisions.kernel_selection serialized-events-hashn- serialized-events-hash sha256 of the concatenation of event lines exactly as persisted (preserve order and whitespace).n- final hash (execution_hash) sha256 hex of the entire concatenated string.nnstore the final execution_hash in the metadata record under key execution_hash. replays compute their own execution_hash and compare. differences are classified as:n- match: identical hash - deterministic replay successn- kernel_diff: kernel_selection differs (indicates routing or scheduler change)n- event_mismatch: same kernel but serialized-events-hash differs (indicates non-determinism or missing telemetry)n- metadata_mismatch: any other metadata field mismatch (e.g., model_variant change)nnreplay workflow (operational runbook)nnprerequisites: sandbox runtime matching runtime_version (within same minor), model artifact available, kernel plugin versions compatible.nnsteps:n1) fetch e-artifact by request_id from replay job via runtime-coordinator-controller (rcctl):nn start a replay with the archived artifact attachednrcctl start-replay --artifact-id b6b7e2f2-8a72-4f1a-9c7b-1a2d3e4f5a6b --sandbox-profile small --env runtime_replay_mode1nn4) on completion the sandbox computes execution_hash and writes a small replay-summary json to /artifacts//replay-summary.json containing: request_id, original_execution_hash, replay_execution_hash, status (match/kernel_diff/event_mismatch/metadata_mismatch), divergence_hint.nnreplay triage matrix (quick decisions)nn- match - close forensics ticket as reproducible attach summary and annotated trace.n- kernel_diff - escalate to kernel-scheduling owners: include decisions record, compare scheduler_cohort and kernel_flags.n- event_mismatch - run delta-trace analysis: compare event_index sequences and run event-aligner tool (see tools section).n- metadata_mismatch - check rollout history likely model or runtime upgrade caused mismatch.nnretention and privacy guidancenn- e-artifacts for high-severity incidents: retain for 180 days. other artifacts: 30 days by default.n- sensitive fields: payload.prompt and payload.user_text --original orig.ndjson --replay replay.ndjson --out diff.htmln- hash-inspector: prints the canonical concatenation used to compute execution_hash for auditing.n- repro-runner: helper utility that spins a sandbox with model artifacts pinned.nndiagnostic fields and common failure modesnntable: common divergence indicatorsnn symptom likely root cause first action n---------n kernel_selection (trace/span/metric availability).n- exclusions: hardware-level power failures and long-lived data-plane networking partitions (these are handled by infra-chaos).nnsuccess criteria (pass/fail)n--------------------------n1) functional correctness: 100 of golden prompt set must return syntactically valid responses for the active fidelity target, with no malformed tokens or kv desync artifacts.n2) latency preservation: during fallback exercises, p95 must not exceed configured fallback-slo-multiplier x baseline p95 (default multiplier 2.5) for more than 60s continuously.n3) error budget preservation: fallback exercises must not consume 1 of monthly error budget for the affected tenant pool.n4) observability: every fallback action must emit a correlated trace/span and a metric tag (fallback_type reason) within 2s of policy firing.n5) rollback/recovery: automatic rollback to previous stable variant must succeed within 5 minutes for canary rollouts that experience degraded quality.nntest plan overviewn------------------n1) canary/unit tests (ci): validate logic paths with deterministic mocks. run for every kernel-scheduler or fallback-policy change.n2) staging validation (integration): run the full plan against a staging cluster that mirrors production routing and telemetry collection.n3) controlled chaos in canary prod (low-traffic window): short, scheduled experiments that validate production signals and playbook correctness.n4) escalation rehearsals: practice runbook steps with oncall and sre to measure human response and timing.nntest types and proceduresn-------------------------na. kernel unavailability simulationn- purpose: ensure the kernel mapper and admission controller fall back to compatible kernels or model variants without corrupting kv cache or client sessions.n- pre-conditions: baseline throughput at 20 of steady-state golden prompt set loaded and pinned.n- steps:n 1. inject kernel sigstop via test harness on a subset of worker processes (3 nodes) to simulate a hung kernel.n 2. observe: request router should divert new requests away from affected kernels after 3 failed scheduling attempts.n 3. verify: no kv cache corruption events in logs sessions tied to affected kernels are migrated or retried.n 4. metrics to monitor: kernel_failure_count, kernel_schedule_retries, kvcache_migration_events, request_reroute_ratio.n- pass/fail:n - pass if golden prompts succeed within retry policy and no cache mismatches are observed.nnb. model variant fallback and quality validationn- purpose: validate that downgrading fidelity (e.g., 16k-8k context, quantized variant) preserves semantic correctness and that the quality monitoring pipeline will detect regressions.n- steps:n 1. trigger variant swap for a small subset (1 traffic) using the deployment controller to a quantized variant.n 2. feed continuous golden prompt set and synthetic adversarial prompts aimed at edge-cases.n 3. capture outputs and run automatic evaluation (embedding-similarity token-level diff custom assertions).n 4. assert alerts are fired by the quality monitor if quality drop configured threshold (default 6 drop in embedding similarity).n- tools: rollout-cli, quality-eval-harness, embeddings-service, diff-checker script.nnc. regional failover and routing policy exercisen- purpose: verify smart routing and cost-aware fallback preserves slos when a region is slowed or unreachable.n- steps:n 1. simulate increased regional latency by adding artificial delay on the regional egress (tc/netem) in staging.n 2. confirm tiered routing policy triggers (region_fallback_count metric increments) and traffic is rebalanced to alternate regions according to configured policy.n 3. validate that per-tenant token cost does not spike beyond policy limits and that route trace contains fallback annotations.nnd. kv cache warmup and eviction race scenarion- purpose: confirm that when primary shard evicts and fallback uses cold cache, responses are still correct and warmup telemetry is produced for downstream autotune.n- steps:n 1. force eviction on a kv shard by lowering memory watermark through the admin api.n 2. route live sessions and verify fallback returns coherent responses while autoscaler warms new copies.n 3. confirm warmup_latency, kvcache_miss_ratio, and kvcache_prefetch_hints metrics are emitted.nne. admission backpressure and queue-starvationn- purpose: ensure admission controller rejects or queues work as designed and that graceful degradation path (reduced tokens, partial response) is triggered for overload.n- steps:n 1. generate synthetic burst (10x normal p50 throughput) to the cluster.n 2. verify admission decisions, queue lengths, and that the partial-result fallback path returns truncated but valid outputs with a clear header x-redwood-fallback-reason: partial-response.nnobservability telemetry requirementsn--------------------------------------nevery experiment must source_type: confluence, title: execution degradation simulator and recovery procedures, content: summaryn-------nthis document describes the execution degradation simulator (eds) a lab-grade harness and operational runbook for reproducing, characterizing, and automatically recovering from runtime degradation modes that affect execution coordination, kernel scheduling, kv cache warmup, and tail-latency amplification. the guide contains: architecture interactions, supported simulation scenarios, telemetry requirements, step-by-step recovery procedures, benchmark acceptance criteria, and post-test analysis templates.nngoalsn-----n- provide a deterministic, auditable way to inject realistic degradation into the serving runtime so teams can validate detection and recovery logic.n- control) without impacting production.nnscope and intended usen---------------------n- target: internal staging clusters and dedicated canary pools only. never run eds against production clusters unless authorized by sre with a staged blast radius plan.n- components in scope: execution coordinator, scheduler, kernel handoff, kvcache layer, dispatch layer, telemetry collectors, and autoscaler hooks.n- not in scope: third-party accelerator firmware updates and hardware-level electrical faults.nnhigh-level architecture interactionsn-----------------------------------n- execution coordinator: kernel admission and batch composition. injected noise should include burst queueing, priority inversions, and synthetic long-running kernel reservations.n- kernel handoff: emulate slow kernel activation (warm-up latency), deliberate kernel failures, and fallback activation to software kernels.n- kvcache: simulate cold start storms, targeted shard eviction, and inconsistent session lookup latencies.nnprerequisitesn-------------n1. access to staging cluster with labeled nodes: eds-canary-.n2. a snapshot of representative traffic (shadow replay corpus) stored at content: summarynnthis playbook describes the simulation-driven, safety-first approach for introducing and validating asynchronous kernel handoffs in the runtime scheduler. it complements the scheduler contract and kernel handoff design docs by providing step-by-step simulation recipes, invariant checks, telemetry baselines, and an incident recovery checklist for live rollouts.nnintended audiencen- runtime engineers implementing scheduler/handoff changesn- sres validating rollouts and runbooksn- performance engineers and profiling ownersnnscope and definitionsn- asynchronous kernel handoff: transferring control of a kernel or execution slot from one worker / kernel instance to another without blocking incoming requests synchronously may include prefetching of kv cache and lazy state reconciliation.n- simulation harness: an isolated environment that replays production-like traces and injects failure modes deterministically.n- safety invariants: conditions that must hold before, during, and after handoffs (listed below).nngoalsn1. validate correctness: ensure no token duplication, kv cache divergence, or session corruption occurs across handoffs.n2. preserve slos: keep p50 and p99 latency within the rollback guard rails during canonical handoff scenarios.n3. enable deterministic root cause: simulation traces must reproduce handoff failures with 95 fidelity to production traces.n4. provide a concise checklist for safe rollout and emergency rollback.nnsafety invariants (explicit)n- invariant a: no request may be acknowledged to the client more than once.n- invariant b: kv cache consistency: for any session id, post-handoff output must be deterministic given the same prompt and pre-handoff kv state.n- invariant c: memory safety: no kernel may hold references to evicted memory regions after handoff.n- invariant d: backpressure preservation: handoff must not exceed a 10 transient increase in queuing for any request class.nnsimulation harness overviewn- components:n - trace replayer: injects request timeline events (arrival times, priorities, session ids, token budgets).n - fault injector: simulates partial failures (gpu preemption signals, process sigterm, nvlink transient errors, slow kv prefetch).n - kernel proxy: mediates handoff by providing deterministic serialization/deserialization of kernel runtime state.n - metrics collector: exports the same telemetry schema we use in staging (request_timeline, kernel_events, kvcache_diff_ratio, handoff_duration_ms).nnquick start (local staging)n1. provision the harness members.nngoalsnn- provide deterministic, repeatable steps to evaluate scheduler changes and their impact on tail latency, cost, and kernel utilization.n- standardize profiling hygiene for scheduling experiments so results are comparable across clusters.n- define a lightweight benchmark matrix that exercises common production shapes and quantization variants.nnservice component inventorynn- runtime-orchestrator: control plane that composes kernel dispatch plans and routes requests to kernel-dispatcher.n- scheduler-service: admission controller and slot allocator implements priority buckets and credit accounting.n- kernel-dispatcher: gpu-side dispatcher that executes mapped kernels.n- kvcache-service: shared kv cache with warmup and eviction telemetry hooks.n- request-classifier: sidecar component that assigns incoming requests to pre-configured execution cohorts.nnkey performance targets (slos)nn- stability slo (short requests, seq 15 invocation rate variance across active slots for a sustained 10-minute window.n- cost slo: per-token gpu time change 10 at p95 or p99: construct causal hypothesis and search for correlated spikes in kernel_enqueue_delay_ms or priority-rebalancing events.n - check kernel utilization per-gpu and per-kernel type. if a single kernel shows 25 uplift in p99 execution time, tag as kernel-regression.nn6) quality gatesn - block rollout if: p99 regression 15 on short workloads or kernel tail safety slo violated.n - soft rollout allowed if cost delta safe-mode: infra-cli flag set-scheduler-mode safe (falls back to admission-by-cost).n4. re-route new traffic to backup gpu pool (tag: fallback-dedicated) using runtime-orchestrator policy: runtime-orchestrator route --policy fallback-dedicated --reason --keys-file /tmp/top10.json).n- if node thermal: cordon affected nodes and shift batches using runtime-orchestrator node-drain policy.nnpost-incident (3h-72h)n- run the full profiling playbook and protocol to validate mitigations before rollout.nnaudiencenn- runtime engineers (kernel and scheduler owners)n- sres who operate gpu pools and admission controllersn- platform product managers planning fallbacks and slasnncontext and problem statementnncross-tenant failure domains occur when a fault (hardware, thermal, driver, model regression, or noisy neighbor) degrades quality-of-service for multiple tenants sharing a gpu node, a rack, or a scheduler queue. without explicit mitigation, symptoms include elevated p95/p99 latency, kv-cache churn, kernel timeouts, and degraded throughput. traditional single-tenant isolation strategies are expensive instead we use kinetic fallback patterns adaptive, fast-acting fallbacks that proactively reduce fidelity or change routing to preserve slos for unaffected tenants while isolating failure impact.nngoals and slosnn- preserve tenant-facing availability: 99.95 uptime per customer pool (monthly).n- maintain latency slos under degraded conditions: p95 0.5 over 1m).n2) evaluate impact window runtime-scheduler queries kvcache-manager and kernel-agent for eviction rates and kernel latencies.n3) apply kinetic fallback stage a (non-disruptive): increase per-tenant slot circuit cap, enable local kv cache aggressive rewarm, issue kernel preference hints (prefer fused-kernel-lite).n4) if condition persists, stage b (fidelity reduction): fallback-router switches non-critical tenants to quantized model_variant-q8 and reduces max-generation-length to 512 tokens.n5) stage c (isolation): runtime-scheduler enacts tenant-weighted throttling and migrates hot tenants off the degraded node.n6) recovery: reverse stages in order verify telemetry returns below thresholds for 5m.nnkernel scheduling guidancenn- priority buckets: map request classes to 4 buckets (realtime, high, standard, background). realtime and high get preemptible kernel credits standard uses expected latency slotting background is best-effort.n- credit accounting: maintain per-tenant credit ledger (rolling 1m window). trigger preemption when a tenant exceeds 120 of its baseline consumption.n- eviction policy: prefer stochastic gentle-eviction (randomized per-session) for background workloads to avoid synchronized mass evictions.n- kernel hinting: use kernel-agent to supply two orthogonal hints to the scheduler preferred kernel (e.g., fused-attention-v2) and memory-mode (evictable / pinned). these hints are advisory and scoped to the current affinity.nnprofiling and triage playbook (short)nn1. immediate triage (010 driver rollouts).n - hypothesis b: thermal or nvlink degradation (confirm with hvac and nic alerts).n - hypothesis c: noisy neighbor / model with pathological sequence lengths.n3. short-term mitigations (3090 minutes)n - if noisy neighbor: apply tenant-weighted throttling and migrate heavy sessions: runtime-cli migrate-sessions --from-node gpu-xx --to-pool spill-pool-3 --tenant tenant-id --duration 1hn4. post-incident profiling (90m72h)n - capture deterministic replay of representative requests: replay-capture export --tenant tenant-id --window incident --format tar.gzn - run microbenchmarks against candidate kernels and quantization levels. see benchmarking protocol below.nnminimal benchmarking protocol for fallbacksnnpurpose: validate stage b fallback variants (quantized compaction and tier-aware eviction in the serving runtime. it is intended for runtime on-call and sre during canaries and broad rollouts.nncompaction reduces kv allocator fragmentation under mixed
