source_type: confluence, title: request surface replay synthetic corpus builder, content: summaryn-------nthis document describes the canonical process and tooling to produce replayable request surfaces and synthetic request corpora for benchmarking, profiling, and regression tests of the redwood inference runtime. the corpus builder produces privacy-validated payloads, stratified sampling artifacts, and annotated replay manifests that drive the microbench, end-to-end, and kernel-level perf suites.nngoalsn-----n- provide reproducible, representative request sets that reflect production request shape (tokens, context windows, multimodal markers, kv cache patterns).n- enable deterministic replay for latency, tail analysis, and kernel-sensitivity tests.n- produce anonymized synthetic variants for open benchmarking and distributed perf teams.n- integrate with existing perf harnesses and the profiling playbook to link input tokens to kernel execution traces.nnscope and non-goalsn-------------------nin scope:n- extraction and normalization of request metadata from live sampling channels (telemetry/ingress-proxy).n- sampling strategies that preserve per-tenant request distributions.n- tools to synthesize requests that preserve statistical properties while removing pii.n- output formats and manifests consumed by the benchmarking suite and runtime profilers.nnout of scope:n- full conversational session reconstruction (this builder targets single-request / short-session replay).n- long-term storage policy (see data-residency-and-retention policy).nnwhen to use this buildern------------------------n- before kernel rollouts to verify sensitivity across representative inputs.n- prior to model-variant release to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs.n- during incident postmortems where a reproducible input is needed for hypothesis testing.nnhigh-level designn-----------------n1) ingress sampling: live request sampler emits lightweight records to the sampling pipeline (ingest topic: perf-samples).n2) normalizer: canonicalizes fields (prompt, metadata, token counts), computes derived features (prompt_length, kv_hits_est), and marks candidate pii spans.n3) sampler stratifier: chooses records by tenant, model, time-of-day, and sequence-length bucket produces a replay_manifest.json.n4) anonymizer synthesizer: replaces pii using deterministic synthetic replacement can optionally generate paraphrases and temperature variations.n5) exporter: writes artifacts to artifacts/perf-corpora// with a defined structure for the benchmark harness.nndata model and manifest formatn----------------------------nthe pipeline emits two artifact types: raw_sample_records (for internal debugging) and replayable_corpora (used by benchmarks). a sample replay manifest (replay_manifest.json) has these top-level fields (text form):nn- name: string (corpus id)n- created_at: iso timestampn- sample_count: integern- stratification: list of dimension:bucket-definitionn- files: list of path:relative/path.jsonl, compression:gzipnone, record_schema: v1n- privacy_level: noneanonymizedsyntheticn- producer_version: semvernnrecord schema (line-delimited json): each line is a request record with flattened fields to simplify ingestion. example (single line):nn request_id: r-01234, tenant: t-company-x, model: redwood-7b-v1, prompt: summarize the quarterly kpis..., prompt_tokens: 124, max_tokens: 256, response_expected: true, kv_cache_hint: 0.2, metadata: route: /generate, region: us-west-2nnnnote: the manifest and record schema are stored as flat jsonl nested maps in metadata must be stringified to keep ingestion tooling simple.nnsampling and anonymization guidancen----------------------------------n- minimum sample sizes: for per-tenant test corpora aim for 10k requests or 1 of tenant traffic, whichever is smaller.n- buckets: use token-length buckets 0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048, 2049 and priority buckets (real-time, background, batch).n- differential privacy step: for public synthetic exports, apply a dp noise layer to counts (epsilon configurable default 1.0) before publishing aggregate summaries.nnanonymization modes:n1) anonymized: redact or replace email/phone/account ids with deterministic tokens (user_00001).n2) synthetic: generate paraphrases that preserve language features (pos distribution, length) but not original content used for customer-sharable corpora.nnanonymization table (example)nfield action notesn--------------------nemail replace deterministic hash - user_nnphone redact replace with naccount_id token - acc_n preserve stable id mapping for replay correlationnfree_text_prompts pii detect paraphrase optional paraphrase to preserve token shapennpipeline: step-by-step runbookn-----------------------------nprerequisites:n- access to sampling topic (infra role: perf-sampler-reader).n- s3 write access to artifacts bucket: dispatcher topology and stability protocol, content: overview:nnthis document defines the gpu dispatcher topology and stability protocol (gd-tsp) a cross-cutting operational spec for how the serving runtime maps inference requests to gpu execution resources, how we validate topology changes with controlled benchmarking and profiling, and the runbooks to recover from topology-induced instability. it consolidates architecture intent, kernel scheduling implications, profiling playbook steps, benchmark protocols, release notes conventions for topology changes, and a curated list of known issues with pragmatic mitigations.nnintended audience:n- runtime engineers responsible for dispatcher, scheduler, and kernel mappingn- sres and oncall responders for inference fleetn- performance engineers running micro/scale benchmarksn- private deployment engineers planning topology configuration changesnngoals and invariants:n- maintain tail-99 latency slos under mixed workloads (default slo: 99th percentile 100).n- coldpath connector: higher-throughput, preemptible pool used for background or low-priority requests.n- kernel affinity profile: a selected set of kernels (fp16/int8/triton fallback) and launch parameters pinned per gpu pool.n- kv-cache partitioning policy: descriptor for how kv caches are split across shards (range, hash, or lru-slab).nn2) topology design guidelines (high level):n- prefer narrower shards for high-priority low-latency workloads. narrow shards fewer concurrent requests per gpu reduces queuing variance.n- co-locate coldpath workloads on quantized kernels to save memory and throughput avoid mixing with hotpath fp16 kernels on same physical gpu when latency slos are tight.n- use numa-aware placement for on-prem racks: ensure dispatcher shards respect pcie locality and do not cross numa domains for kv-heavy models.n- configure dispatcher to expose a per-shard concurrency cap and a soft-threshold for admission (default soft-threshold 0.75 concurrency_cap).nn3) kernel scheduling implications and constraints:n- kernel preemption cost: long-running fused kernels (e.g., long-sequence rotary attention fused kernels) increase preemption penalty. documented rule: if average kernel_time 12ms, prefer non-preemptive placement for hotpath.n- continuous batching policy interacts with shard width. wider shards yield larger effective batch sizes use batch size caps to avoid oom and increased p99.n- kernel selection ramp: when upgrading kernels, ramp through alpha-canary-general with checkpointed perf baselines. kernels must pass microbenchmarks for latency, tail, and throughput before rollout.nn4) profiling playbook for topology changes (step-by-step):npre-change checklist:n1. record current topology manifest and active dispatcher routing table (cli: redwoodctl dispatcher export --namespace --output json).n2. capture baseline traces for 30 minutes using the standard sample policy (trace-level: request, kernel, and nvml counters).n3. run the lightweight synthetic smoke test for correctness (single-turn, deterministic prompt).nnchange-and-profile steps:n1. apply topology change in a canary shard (apply to 13 gpus) during low-traffic window.n2. start continuous microbenchmark runner against canary for 60 minutes: 5 workload profiles (small-chat, assistant-long, embedding-batch, rerank, multimodal-lite).n3. collect the following telemetry: per-request latency histograms, kernel latency distributions, gpu utilization, memory clocks, power draw, nvlink traffic, kv-cache hit ratios, and preemption counts.n4. correlate sudden p99 jumps with kernel-time percentiles and preemption_count spikes.n5. if p99 delta 20 or average gpu dram rising 10 relative to baseline, automatically roll back.nnprofiling artifacts to produce:n- canary-report-yyyymmdd.csv (rows: timestamp, workload, p50, p95, p99, qps, avg_gpu_mem_mb, kv_hit_ratio)n- flamegraphs for kernel stacks (symbolized)n- nvml time-series segments clipped to incident windownn5) benchmark suite protocol (how we validate topology changes end-to-end):npurpose: provide reproducible, comparable results to gate dispatcher topology changes in ci and pre-prod.nnbenchmark harness configuration (table):n- scenario: small-chat assistant-long embedding-batch rerank mixed-burstn- seq_len: 32 512 512 128 variablen- concurrency: 200 40 16 80 variablen- duration: 10m 20m 10m 15m 30mn- metrics: p50,p95,p99,tail-qps,token-cpu-ms,token-gpu-ms,cost-per-tokennnrun protocol (numbered):n1. provision an isolated pre-prod cluster matching the target topology (exact gpu models, a/b ip ranges, same kernel libs).n2. seed with representative kv-cache warmup traffic for 20 minutes.n3. execute bench harness with the scenario matrix above. 5 replicates per scenario to reduce variance.n4. aggregate metrics and run statistical significance test (paired t-test on p99 across replicates).n5. approve topology change if: p99 delta (e.g., dispatcher topology split hotpath shards for chat-v2).n- body must include: rationale, list of affected clusters, benchmark artifacts links, canary rollout schedule, rollback conditions, owner and oncall rota.n- must attach: canary-report csv, microbench baseline json, and profiler flamegraphs.nn7) runbooks (quick actions for common symptoms):nsymptom a: sudden p99 spike across a single shard- quick triage:n1. verify alert and scope (redwoodctl metrics query --expr p99_latencyshard).n2. fetch latest kernel latency histogram from tracing service.n3. if preemption_count increased 10x, toggle preemption_policysoft for affected shard and re-run microbench.n4. if gpu memory increased abnormally, temporarily shrink concurrency_cap by 25 and initiate kv-cache eviction.n5. if immediate mitigation fails, reassign traffic off shard to fallback pool (cli: redwoodctl dispatcher reroute --from --to ) and open incident.nnsymptom b: ooms observed on mixed workloads after topology change- quick triage:n1. inspect kernel allocations in the last 10 failures (tracing id list).n2. if new kernel introduced (kernel_version mismatch), revert kernel on shard.n3. reduce batch size caps and restart worker process for shard.n4. escalate to runtime-core-owner if oom persists after 2 restarts.nn8) known issues catalog (selection with mitigations):n- issue: kv-cache slab fragmentation causing steady growth of memory usage on long-lived shards.n - symptom: slowly increasing gpu memory footprint (1-2 per day) without workload change.n - mitigation: schedule periodic slab compaction (cron: /opt/redwood/bin/kv_compact --shard --threshold 0.6).nn- issue: nvlink saturation when cross-rack shard affinity incorrectly configured.n - symptom: decreased throughput and increased kernel latency during multi-query kv-syncs.n - mitigation: pin shards to same-rack gpus or throttle kv-sync frequency add nvlink utilization alarms.nn- issue: incompatible quantized kernel scheduler evaluation manual, content: overviewnnnthis manual describes a repeatable process for characterizing production inference workloads, mapping them to appropriate accelerator classes, and evaluating scheduler/kernel policies to meet slos while minimizing cost. it consolidates profiling playbook steps, benchmark harness configuration, acceptance criteria for rollouts, common failure modes, and lightweight runbook actions for operational teams.nngoalsn-----n- produce a deterministic workload fingerprint (latency shape, token density, sequence distribution, kv-cache affinity).n- map fingerprints to a small set of hardware classes (e.g., h100-80gb, a100-80gb, l40s-48gb, t4-16gb) with expected cost and tail-latency envelopes.n- evaluate scheduler knobs (batching, slotting, preemption, kernel hints) and quantify their impact on per-token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, and gpu utilization.n- provide a decision checklist for model-variant selection and fallback policies.nnscope and audiencen------------------nthis doc targets sres, runtime engineers, and applied ml engineers responsible for: model onboarding, canary design, dedicated capacity sizing, and private deployment sizing. it assumes familiarity with the runtime tracing tooling (trace-proxy, kernel-hint annotations) and the benchmarking harness in tools/perf-harness.nnkey definitionsn---------------n- request shape: immutable properties of a request prompt tokens, expected response token cap, streaming vs non-streaming.n- sequence distribution: histogram of inputoutput lengths across a sample window.n- affinity: the probability that successive requests share kv cache entries (session/conv affinity).n- fidelity class: mapping of model/quantization/profile that yields a certain output quality and cost.nn1) workload fingerprinting (profiling playbook)n------------------------------------------------nstep-by-step (safe for production):n1. identify a representative sampling for high-volume routes.nnrecommended capture command:nntrace-proxy capture --router route --write /tmp/captures/route-2026-02-01.jsonl --sample-rate 0.01 --fields title: batching slo tier benchmark methodology, content: overviewnthis document defines the benchmark methodology used to validate the three customer-facing batching profiles (fast / standard / cost-efficient) prior to rollout and on an ongoing basis via perf canary gates.nnthe methodology is designed to:n- prevent benchmark theater by using representative mixes (prompt length, streaming ratio, and concurrency) that approximate real production traffic.n- make regressions actionable by standardizing metrics, run configurations, and pass/fail gates.n- provide apples-to-apples comparisons between tier candidates and existing defaults, while controlling for hardware variance.nnthis methodology is used for:n- pre-merge/per-pr targeted perf checks (limited matrix, fast turnaround)n- daily perf canary (expanded matrix, high confidence)n- release qualification for runtime-1.22 tiered batching defaultsnn---nn scope and non-goalsn in scopen- tier validation for latency slo compliance (p50/p95/p99) and tail stability under concurrency ramps.n- cost/perf characterization: throughput (tokens/s), gpu utilization proxies, and /1k tokens estimates (using redwood metering coefficients).n- mixed workload behavior (shortlong prompts, streamingnon-streaming) including starvation and queue blow-up safeguards.n- overload behavior validation (controlled overload) to ensure predictable degradation.nn out of scopen- per-tenant auto-tuning or customer-specific prompt sets.n- cross-region routing policy comparisons (handled by routing tests) this doc assumes a fixed region per run.n- full quality evals we only run a lightweight correctness/guardrail sanity pass here (see quality smoke checks).nn---nn definitionsn tier labelsn- fast: prioritizes tail latency protection and stable streaming experience.n- standard: balanced defaults for typical production traffic.n- cost-efficient: maximizes throughput with guardrails may accept higher tail latency within tier slo.nntier slo numeric targets are defined in: confluence://eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-definition-fast-standard-cost-efficient.nn request typesnwe benchmark two primary request types because they stress different scheduler paths:n1) chat generation (prefill decode)n2) embeddings are excluded from this suite (separate pipeline and batching semantics)nn key latency metricsn- ttft (time-to-first-token): streaming-only and non-streaming measured separately.n- itl (inter-token latency): decode latency per token (streaming).n- e2e latency: full request completion time (non-streaming) and time-to-final-token (streaming).nn prompt and output lengthsnwe explicitly model prompt and generation length distributions.n- prompt_tokens: tokenized prompt lengthn- max_output_tokens: configured output length capn- realized_output_tokens: actual generated tokensnn---nn workload modelnwe validate each tier against the same workload model, with a tier-specific acceptance gate.nn workload mix (baseline)nbaseline mix is intended to approximate aggregate hosted api traffic while still being stable enough for regression detection.nnworkload mix weights (by request count):n- 55 chat (general assistant / support-agent style)n- 25 summarization / extraction (longer prompts, shorter outputs)n- 20 code assistant (moderate prompts, longer outputs)nnstreaming ratio (baseline):n- 70 streamingn- 30 non-streamingnnrationale:n- streaming dominates customer experience sensitivity (ttft/itl) and is where batching foot-guns are most visible.n- non-streaming is included to ensure throughput and e2e latency behavior remains sane.nn prompt length distributionsnwe use a 4-bucket prompt length model to force mixed-bucket contention and catch starvation issues.nnprompt token buckets (by tokenized prompt length) and target weight (baseline):n- bucket s (0256): 35n- bucket m (2571,024): 40n- bucket l (1,0254,096): 20n- bucket xl (4,0978,192): 5nnoutput length targets (by workload type):n- chat: realized_output_tokens p50 220, p95 650n- summarization/extraction: realized_output_tokens p50 120, p95 250n- code: realized_output_tokens p50 280, p95 900nnnotes:n- output lengths are not forced we cap via max_output_tokens and rely on prompt design temperature to approximate distributions.n- we reject prompt sets that collapse to near-zero outputs, because they under-stress decode.nn concurrency rampsneach benchmark run includes a controlled concurrency ramp to evaluate stability and tail behavior across operating points.nnramp profile:n- warmup: 3 minutes at low concurrency (c_low)n- ramp: step concurrency every 2 minutesn- hold: 6 minutes at peak concurrency (c_peak)n- cooldown: 2 minutes at mid concurrencynnconcurrency points (per model/hardware pair):n- c_low: 0.25x nominaln- c_nominal: 1.0x nominaln- c_high: 1.5x nominaln- c_peak: 2.0x nominalnnnominal is defined as: the highest concurrency where standard tier meets its p95 slo with 0.3 (excluding intentional load shedding responses, which must be labeled)n- timeout rate 0.2n- queue depth shows monotonic growth over 3 minutes at c_nominal or c_highn- starvation: p99 queue wait time for bucket s exceeds 2x the median wait time for bucket s for fast tiern- overload segment causes unrecovered queue growth (does not return to within 20 of pre-overload queue depth within 2 minutes of returning to c_nominal)nn gate d: cost improvement sanity (non-blocking initially)nfor cost-efficient tier candidates, we record throughput and /1k tokens improvement vs standard.n- target: 12 throughput improvement at c_nominaln- if improvement is 15 on p99 ttft from the other two, mark the suite as unstable and rerun once.n- if instability persists, it becomes a perf infrastructure ticket (do not block unrelated releases unless fast tier p99 is impacted).nn---nn benchmark execution (how to run)n inputsn- runtime build: pinned shan- config: tier profile knobs and selection logic togglesn- model: pinned model versionn- prompt set: versioned bundle (see prompt set selection doc)n- region/hardware: specified explicitlynn standard command (example)nthe canonical command is maintained in the perf-suite repo, but the shape is:nn- deploy runtime build to a fixed-size test clustern- run loadgen with:n - mix profile: baselinen - prompt length buckets enabledn - streaming ratio setn - concurrency ramp enablednnexample (illustrative):n- perf-suite run n --model llama-family-70b n --tier fast n --hardware h100-80gb n --region us-east-1 n --promptset slo-tier-v3 n --streaming-ratio 0.70 n --concurrency-profile ramp_v2 n --replicas 4 n --duration-min 17 n --record-reason-codes truenn---nn reporting formatnfor each tier/model/hardware combination, publish a summary block to the perf report:n- slo pass/fail at c_nominal and c_highn- regression deltas vs baselinen- tokens/s and estimated /1k tokens deltasn- key scheduler distributions (batch size, queue depth)n- any guardrail violationsnninclude a short interpretation paragraph:n- what changed (knob deltas)n- whether failures appear tied to prefill congestion, decode congestion, or queue admissionn- recommended next action (tweak profile, adjust safeguards, or treat as infra noise)nn---nn ci / perf canary integrationnthis methodology maps to two execution tiers:nn tier 1: pr-level (fast)n- single model/hardware combo per tier (rotating daily)n- 1 run (no repeats)n- gates: safety guardrails regression threshold (looser)nn tier 2: daily canary (authoritative)n- full canary matrixn- 3 repeats per combon- gates: full (a/b/c) enforcednnif daily canary fails:n1) auto-file a ticket with run id, charts, and suspected culprit (last green sha range)n2) page on-call only if fast tier p99 ttft fails slo at c_nominal for a top modeln3) otherwise route to runtime-perf triage queuenn---nn quality smoke checks (lightweight)nbecause batching changes can surface edge cases (e.g., truncation interactions, streaming chunking), we run a small correctness sanity pass:n- verify token counts and termination reasons are within expected boundsn- check for elevated empty output rate and truncation raten- run a small set of golden prompts to detect obvious formatting regressionsnnthis does not replace the full quality eval suite it is intended only to catch gross failures early.nn---nn updating the methodologynchanges to:n- workload mix weightsn- prompt bucket definitionsn- concurrency ramp profilesn- gating thresholdsnnrequire approval from:n- serving runtime scheduling (sofia ivanova or delegate)n- applied ml/evals (jonas weber or delegate)n- sre (sean gallagher or delegate)nnbaseline refresh:n- baselines may be refreshed only after:n - 3 consecutive green daily canaries on the new build, andn - sign-off recorded in the perf-canary baseline ticketnn---nn known limitations / blind spotsn- customer traffic is more diverse than our three-workload mix niche workloads (extremely long outputs, highly tool-calling heavy patterns) may behave differently.n- network variance can dominate ttft in some regions we minimize but cannot eliminate it.n- nominal concurrency calibration can drift with infrastructure changes we re-calibrate monthly or after major driver/runtime updates.nn---nn appendix: troubleshooting common failure modesn1) fast tier p99 ttft regressionn- check queue wait time and admission control counters.n- inspect batch size distribution: unusually large prefill batches can harm ttft.n- confirm no background model reload or cache eviction storm.nn2) cost-efficient tier queue blow-up under overloadn- check overload segment recovery criterion.n- verify guardrails: max wait budget, max batch tokens, and backpressure toggles.nn3) high error raten- separate load-shedding responses from true errors.n- confirm client timeouts are not too aggressive for standard/cost-efficient.nnowners:n- benchmark harness: rina kobayashin- content: overviewnnthis page defines a set of synthetic stress profiles and a small chaos-harness used by sre and runtime teams to validate kernel scheduling, kv cache behavior, batching heuristics, and degradation/fallback policies under controlled but realistic failure modes. these profiles are used for:nn- pre-release performance gating (release branch canary)n- continuous nightly regression exercise the hot paths across the serving runtime (attention kernels, kv-cache, batching, preemption).n2. surface regressions in tail latency, correctness (token drift), and error modes introduced by kernel changes or scheduler refactors.n3. validate fallback and graceful degradation policies (model variant fallback, region fallback).n4. give a standardized triage playbook and pass/fail criteria tied to slos.nnscope and exclusionsnn- scope: inference path (token generation / chat), scheduler interactions, cache eviction under pressure, batching/packing, network backpressure.n- exclusions: training workloads, model conversion artifacts, client-side sdk correctness.nnownershipnn- primary: eng-serving-runtime / runtime qe (runtime-qe@redwood.com)n- secondary: eng-sre continuous long sequence generation (avg 4096 tokens) to exercise backend memory pressure and attention kernel breakpoints.n- mixed-tenant-thundering-herd: many small tenants with spiky arrivals to validate priority accounting and kernel-credit throttling.n- encoder-heavy-burst: short, high qps encoder-style workloads that produce large batching opportunities but stress kernel queueing (example above).n- ablate-batcher: toggle batcher parameters (max_latency_ms, max_tokens) across runs to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.n- graceful-degrade-path: incrementally reduce preferred model capacity and validate automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variants without correctness regressions.nnpass/fail criteria and slosnnpass conditions are evaluated per-run and are used by ci gating and nightly regression alerts. each profile tie to an action level:nn- green: all slos met and no increase in token-error or hallucination metrics beyond historical baselinen- amber: specific slo breach but within tolerable rollback policy (e.g., p99 up to 1.5x baseline) - alert triagen- red: major degradation (p99 2x or error_rate 0.2) - block merge and trigger incident processnndefault slo thresholds (adjust per workload):nn- p50 latency 10/min during failure, run the cache inspection script to dump kvcache shards and eviction logs:nn benchctl kvcache-dump --node node-12 --shard 3 --out during incidentsnn- scaling: temporarily scale dedicated pool by 20 capacity (if autoscaling not reacting)n- routing: route high-priority tenants to a warm reserve pool (route policy: limit concurrency to 50 of default)n- kernel gate: if a new kernel change is suspected, rollback kernel binary on canaries via the artifact manager and re-run the failing profile.n- fallback: toggle model_variant_fallback to allowed for the route to shift traffic to quantized variant.nnexample commands (ops):nn rctl cluster scale staging-gpu-pool --delta 10n rctl route update --route (kvcache-eviction-surge, longcontext-steady).n- automated gating: ci jobs will annotate prs with benchctl artifacts and link to the profile run result.nnknown issues and workarounds (as of overviewnnsummary:nthe shadow evaluator is a product initiative to provide an automated, prompt-set driven regression detection service that runs shadow (non-production-impacting) evaluations against candidate model variants prior to rollouts. the goal is to catch regressions in real-world prompt patterns and alert product and model owners with actionable diagnostics before customer-facing traffic is exposed.nnthis prd defines user journeys, functional and non-functional requirements, high-level design, rollout plan, success metrics, and operational run/playbook for the feature.nnmotivation and context:n- customers and internal teams increasingly rely on model variant rollouts and automated canaries. existing unit-test and lab evals miss distributional edge-cases embedded in customer prompt-sets.n- we need an evaluation layer that: 1) reuses customer prompt-sets (curated captured), 2) runs candidate model variants in shadow mode, 3) computes fidelity and quality deltas against baseline, and 4) returns prioritized regressions with reproducible evidence.nngoals (what success looks like):n- detect regressions that would have impacted customer-facing traffic with at least 80 precision and 60 recall in pilot customers for top-5 critical prompt-sets.n- provide per-prompt diagnostic payloads (inputs, baseline output, candidate output, diff highlights, metric breakdown).n- integrate with console to surface alerts in the rollout workflow and with optimize to suggest mitigations (roll back, lower-fidelity fallback, quantized variant).n- low operational cost: shadow eval should not increase serving cost for hosted traffic more than 2 at typical canary scales.nnnon-goals:n- this is not a full replacement for offline, human-in-the-loop evaluation for safety-critical models.n- we will not initially support multimodal prompt-sets (images, audio) text-only for v1.nnuser stories:n- as a platform engineer, i want to register a production prompt-set and schedule nightly shadow runs so regressions are flagged before deploys.n- as a product manager, i want to see a ranked list of prompt regressions (with confidence scores, token-level diffs, and sample traces) if capacity is constrained.nnfunctional requirements:n1) prompt-set ingestion:n - support three sources: curated prompt libraries (internal), tenant-provided prompt-sets (customer uploads or pinned invocation parameters).n - bundles must be downloadable via console and accessible via an internal s3 path.nn6) integration points:n - console: alert tile in rollout page with quick actions (pause production serving nodes.n- determinism: where models are deterministic (seeded), runs should be reproducible otherwise, log rng seeds and sampling params.nnsuccess metrics and kpis:n- time to detect payload_checksum failures.n4. register signal in the central registry (link in related_pages).n5. request privacy review if payload contains any user-identifiable metadata.nnoperational examples and dsid_9937e3378aff43a28ab825c5f3f35382, source_type: confluence, title: fidelity vs cost sensitivity simulator: spec and lab guide, content: overviewn--------nthis document defines the fidelity vs cost sensitivity simulator (fcs-sim), a reproducible synthetic experiment platform and accompanying lab guide used to quantify trade-offs between output fidelity (quality), per-token cost, and latency across model variants, quantization profiles, batching configurations, and routing policies. the simulator is intended to produce actionable guidance for: model-variant selection, quantization rollouts, batching/autoscale configuration, and routing fallback strategies.nnmotivationn----------nteams frequently need to answer questions such as: n- how much output quality do we lose if we switch from fp16 to 8-bit quantized kernels at 512-token prompts for my search summarization workload?n- for a given slo (p99 expected fidelity deltas for named prompt-sets (e.g., summarization-v1, search-qa-v2) calibrated by eval harness.n- routing_emulator (rust): simulates smart routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, tiered-fallback), replica pools, and capacity constraints.n- batch_simulator (python): implements batching logic (continuous batching, fixed-window batchers) and models warmstart/warmup effects on kv cache and model state.n- aggregator_and_reporter (notebook cli): aggregates metrics, produces csv/html reports, and generates experiment artifacts for storage in s3://redwood-fcs-sim/experiments/.nndata flow (high level):n1) trace_ingestor - normalized request streamn2) routing_emulator kernel_latency_model batch_simulator - per-request latency cost estimatesn3) fidelity_model_store - per-request fidelity delta (relative to baseline)n4) aggregator_and_reporter - consolidated scenario metrics and visualizationsnnkey metrics producedn--------------------n- latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99 (ms) per route and aggregatedn- cost_per_1000_tokens (usd) and cost_per_successful_response (usd)n- expected_fidelity_delta (e.g., bleu/rouge/embedding-sim delta or custom eval score delta) per prompt-setn- sla_breach_rate: fraction of requests slo threshold (configurable default 250ms p99)n- perceived_degradation_rate: fraction of requests expected to have fidelity delta user-provided thresholdn- fallback_frequency: percent of requests routed to fallback variantsnnexperiment protocol (recommended reproducible steps)n---------------------------------------------------n1) define objective and acceptance criteria. example: allow quantized variant rollout to 20 traffic if perceived_degradation_rate perceived_degradation_probabilityn- data_version: git sha of eval harness run used for fitnnexample fidelity model store for low-risk routes: perceived_degradation_rate acceptance - abort and open rfc with mlops and product.n3) if metrics stable - ramp to 5 over 24h, then 20 over 48h, running a/b evaluation with subjective checks at 20.n4) full rollout only after 7-day stability window and no regression alerts.nnrunbook: when simulator flags an unexpected regressionn----------------------------------------------------n1) confirm input trace and fidelity mapping versions from experiment_manifest.yaml.n2) re-run experiment with seed fixed and increased source_type: confluence, title: multi-tenant noise injection benchmark protocol, content: summarynnthis document defines the multi-tenant noise injection benchmark protocol (mnibp) used by the runtime team to quantify how different types of noisy neighbor behavior and kernel-level jitter affect per-tenant slos, cost-per-token, and model fidelity. the goal is to produce reproducible, comparable results across gpu types and scheduler configurations so we can: 1) validate scheduler hardening and isolation features, 2) estimate degradation risk for customer slas, and 3) generate test vectors for release gates.nnscopenn- applies to runtime clusters supporting multi-tenant inference (hosted dedicated pools).n- tests cover kernel scheduling policies, preemption waveforms, kv-cache eviction, and bursty tenant load shapes.n- not intended for hardware failure injection (use the hardware fault simulation playbook).nnowners and contactsnn- primary owner: eng-serving-runtime / performance finalized release gating language and retention policy., doc_id: dsid_4d84bcfa3cf8467498ee128f69924826, source_type: confluence, title: load sculpting and fidelity certification framework, content: summaryn-------nthis document defines the load sculpting and fidelity certification framework (lsfcf): a cross-team protocol and artifact set for validating runtime behavior, kernel scheduler interactions, and model fidelity under sculpted production-like load. the goal is to provide a reproducible, auditable path to certify that a runtime/kernel change or model variant meets latency, cost, and quality gates before rollout to hosted or dedicated fleets.nnscopen-----napplies to: runtime engineers, kernel/scheduler teams, profiling and benchmarking engineers, qa, and release owners.nincludes artifacts: load sculpting profiles, fidelity acceptance tests, end-to-end scenario harnesses, release-checklist items, and a minimal certification report template.nexcludes: model training/eval-only artifacts (handled by applied-ml-and-evals).nnmotivationn----------nwe frequently observe subtle regressions that only surface when the scheduler interacts with specific request shapes (eg. many short queries with heavy kv-cache churn, or large context continuations causing kernel fallback). the lsfcf standardizes how we: n- compose sculpted traffic that stresses critical kernel/scheduling paths.n- correlate profiling signals (kernel latency, sm occupancy, memory pressure) with end-to-end slos and model-quality regressions.n- produce a certification record with deterministic criteria for progressive rollouts.nndefinitionsn-----------n- sculpted profile: synthetic traffic pattern derived from production traces and parameterized by qps, concurrency, sequence-length distribution, and session affinity.n- fidelity gate: a threshold-based test comparing model output on a canonical prompt set, measured by quality metrics (bleu/rouge/embedding-similarity/regression-count).n- certification run: full execution of lsfcf artifacts across target hardware and runtime configurations includes profiling capture and post-run analysis.nnframework overviewn------------------n1) selection: identify target dimensions to exercise: sequence length tail, kv-cache churn, batch shape skew, priority churn, and mixed tenant interference.n2) build sculpted profile: parameterize generator with distribution seeds, warmup/cooldown windows, and correlated metadata (token budgets, prompt templates, tool-calls).n3) execute harness across three fidelity lanes:n - canary-lab: single-node variant to validate functional correctness and basic perf.n - integration-stable: 1050 node cluster with representative scheduler configuration and simulated multi-tenant noise.n - preprod-mirror: traffic-mirroring of a sampled production window with 1020 production qps (read-only for data plane).n4) capture telemetry: kernel traces, per-kernel histogram, gpu occupancy, allocator metrics, rpc latencies, and request provenance.n5) run fidelity tests: prompt-set pass/fail and quality delta thresholds.n6) produce a certification report with pass/fail verdicts, regression vectors, and rollout recommendation.nnsculpted profiles (example table)n--------------------------------n profile_name qps_peak concurrency source_type: confluence, title: perf canary: synthetic prompt distribution (v0.4), content: overviewnthis page defines the synthetic prompt distribution used by the production performance canary (perf-canary). the canary exists to detect p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops per model (optionally per region/tier/sku) with minimal noise and zero customer data.nnthe prompt distribution is intentionally shape-focused (token lengths, prefill/decode mix, and request patterns) and uses template-generated, non-sensitive content.nnversion: v0.4 (current)nn---nn what changed since v0.3nthis revision keeps the overall design and bucket structure, but updates several workload knobs to reduce variance and improve coverage of newer request paths.nnchanges:n1. request interface mix updated to include a small, strictly bounded tool/function calling shape.n2. bucket weights adjusted to slightly increase mid/long-context coverage (p2/p3) while staying within overhead targets.n3. decode tail weight increased modestly to improve sensitivity to tokens/sec regressions.n4. streaming ratio reduced to limit instrumentation-induced variance in end-to-end metrics (runtime-only metrics remain stream-independent).n5. overhead budget target tightened (see validation checklist).nnbaseline note:n- v0.4 is not baseline-compatible with v0.3 for absolute latency baselines must be recomputed per model family.nn---nn goalsn1. provide a stable, reproducible workload that approximates typical production request shapes:n - short chat turnsn - medium instruction-style requestsn - longer context (rag-like) inputsn2. exercise runtime performance characteristics that commonly regress:n - prefill attention (prompt length sensitivity)n - decode loop efficiency (generation length sensitivity)n - scheduler/queueing behavior (concurrency mix)n - batching behavior (wide distribution of sequence lengths)n3. keep the workload privacy-safe:n - no customer promptsn - no user identifiersn - no training data excerptsnn non-goalsn- measuring response quality (handled separately via eval harness and prompt sets)n- matching every customer domain distribution perfectlyn- capturing multi-turn conversation state beyond 2 turns (initially)nn---nn constraints and safety rulesn- no customer data: prompts are generated from controlled templates and synthetic text blocks.n- no pii: templates must not include real person names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, or account identifiers.n - exception policy: if a template needs proper nouns for realism, use only names from the internal synthetic-name allowlist (non-real, generated) maintained by applied ml evals.n- no secrets: no api keys, auth tokens, or internal incident text.n- content neutrality: prompts should avoid disallowed content categories that might trigger model safety filters unevenly across model versions.n- reproducibility: prompt generator must be seedable canary runs must be replayable.nn---nn workload modelnthe canary uses a mixture of request shapes. a shape is defined as:n- interface: chat, completion, or tool/function callingn- prefill length bucket (input tokens)n- target decode length bucket (output tokens)n- system/user template family (synthetic text)n- generation parameters (temperature/top_p/etc.)nn request interface mixn- chat: 65n- completion (instruct-style): 25n- tool/function calling: 10nnrationale:n- most production traffic is chat-like, but we keep completion coverage for older integrations and to exercise slightly different formatting/tokenization paths.n- tool/function calling is included at low weight to detect regressions in structured-output formatting and the associated serving path, while keeping variance bounded.nn---nn prefill (input) length bucketsninput lengths are bucketed in tokens (post-tokenization). bucket selection uses fixed weights (below), then the generator samples a specific length uniformly within the bucket range.nn bucket id token range (inclusive) weight typical pattern exercised n------:---:---n p0 1664 0.18 short chat turn low prefill overhead n p1 65256 0.34 common instruction/chat requests n p2 257768 0.26 medium context batching interactions n p3 7692048 0.16 rag-like context prefill attention pressure n p4 20494096 0.06 long-context edge kv/cache and kernel thresholds nnnotes:n- these ranges are tuned to keep gpu overhead within the perf-canary budget while still catching regressions in long-context kernels.n- bucket weights are global defaults specific models may override (e.g., long-context models can increase p3/p4).nn---nn decode (output) length bucketsnthe canary targets an output token count the request uses max_tokens and stop conditions such that typical output lands in the intended bucket.nn bucket id target output tokens weight typical pattern exercised n------:---:---n d0 1664 0.22 short answers latency dominated by prefill n d1 65256 0.45 most common generation lengths n d2 257768 0.27 longer responses decode efficiency and scheduling n d3 7691024 0.06 tail decode sustained throughput and thermal stability nnrationale:n- canary sensitivity to tokens/sec regressions improves when decode lengths include sustained decoding (d2/d3), but we cap the tail to control overhead.nn---nn joint distribution (prefill x decode)nwe do not sample prefill and decode independently we use a constrained joint distribution to reflect reality (very long prompts rarely request extremely long generations).nnallowed pairs and weights (normalized within each prefill bucket):n- p0: d0 0.58, d1 0.38, d2 0.04, d3 0.00n- p1: d0 0.26, d1 0.55, d2 0.17, d3 0.02n- p2: d0 0.14, d1 0.48, d2 0.33, d3 0.05n- p3: d0 0.10, d1 0.53, d2 0.32, d3 0.05n- p4: d0 0.14, d1 0.60, d2 0.24, d3 0.02nnrationale:n- keeps the workload realistic and reduces variance from extremely long end-to-end sequences.n- ensures the canary hits both prefill-heavy and decode-heavy regimes.nn---nn template familiesntemplates define the content without introducing variability that would overwhelm performance signals.nn chat templates (65 of traffic)nall chat requests include a system message and a user message.nnsystem message families (selected uniformly):n1. you are a concise assistant. answer with bullet points when appropriate.n2. you are a technical assistant. prefer clear steps and short explanations.n3. you are a helpful assistant. if the request is ambiguous, ask one clarifying question.nnuser message families (selected with weights):n- (0.38) structured extraction: asks to extract fields from synthetic paragraphs (non-sensitive)n- (0.34) summarization: summarize synthetic text blocks (generated lorem-like technical prose)n- (0.16) planning: generate a short plan for a synthetic scenario (no real entities)n- (0.12) light reasoning: simple multi-step reasoning on synthetic facts (bounded)nn completion templates (25 of traffic)nprompt is formatted as an instruct-style completion:n- instruction: ninput: noutput:nninstruction families:n- rewrite/shortenn- create a checklistn- convert paragraph to json-like keys (synthetic fields only)nn tool/function calling templates (10 of traffic)ntool calling requests use a single tool with a small schema and bounded output to reduce variance.nntool family (selected uniformly):n1. extract_fields_v1n2. classify_issue_v1nnschema rules:n- maximum 8 keys.n- values are short strings or small arrays (bounded length), no free-form long text.n- no nested objects in the tool output content (enforced by the generator).nnrationale:n- exercises structured output paths and serialization without turning the canary into a quality benchmark.nn---nn synthetic text blocks (for prefill length control)nto reach the target prefill bucket, the generator appends one or more synthetic paragraphs from a controlled corpus:n- neutral, technical-sounding prose (e.g., abstract descriptions of systems, graphs, scheduling)n- randomized but deterministic token sequences from a whitelist vocabularynnimportant: the corpus is generated internally and reviewed to ensure it contains:n- no proprietary contentn- no customer namesn- no copied documentation textnn---nn generation parametersndefaults (unless overridden per model config):n- temperature: 0.1n- top_p: 0.95n- max_tokens: derived from decode bucket upper bound (upper bound 8 token slack)n- presence_penalty: 0.0n- frequency_penalty: 0.0n- stop: nnend, (template-dependent)n- stream: enabled for 50 of requestsn- seed: derived deterministically from (canary_run_id, model, region, shape_id)nnrationale:n- lower temperature reduces variability in decode length and avoids occasional long rambles that distort tail latency.n- a small max_tokens slack reduces truncation artifacts at bucket boundaries.n- streaming is included because it exercises buffering/serialization paths, but the ratio is reduced to improve stability of end-to-end metrics.nn---nn concurrency and pacingnperf-canary runs continuously with a fixed per-target budget.nndefault pacing per (model, region, sku, tier):n- target request rate: 0.10.8 rps (config-driven)n- concurrency: 16 in-flight (config-driven)nnnotes:n- the scheduler is intentionally exercised with overlapping requests, but we cap concurrency to avoid canary-induced queueing dominating signals.n- if the canary is primarily measuring runtime-only latency, it will also emit queueing time separately so we can attribute regressions.nn---nn what we measure vs what we controlncontrolled by this distribution:n- prefill token countn- target decode token countn- request mix (chat vs completion vs tool calling)n- streaming rationnnot controlled (and intentionally observed):n- batching outcomes (batch size distribution)n- queueing time under normal production loadn- kernel selection outcomes given real hardware runtime versionnn---nn rationale and design notesn why these buckets?n- buckets align to known performance regimes where regressions have historically occurred:n - kernel changes around long-context thresholdsn - scheduler heuristics sensitive to mixed sequence lengthsn - kv cache behavior changes when prefill dominatesnn why not mirror exact customer distributions?n- customer distributions change over time (product launches, region shifts, sdk versions). the canary needs a stable reference to detect regressions in the serving stack itself.nn why include a small amount of tool calling now?n- serving has multiple request pathways with different serialization/validation overhead.n- a low-weight, bounded tool shape increases regression detection coverage without materially increasing noise.nn---nn versioning and change managementn- this distribution is versioned as canary_prompt_dist_version (e.g., v0.4) and emitted as a metric tag and in canary logs.n- any change that impacts token lengths, interface mix, or the joint distribution must:n 1. increment the versionn 2. run the perf-canary validation plan in stagingn 3. recompute baselines (or explicitly document baseline compatibility)nnapproval required:n- runtime perf suite (owner): noah pateln- applied ml evals review (prompt/template safety): rina kobayashin- scheduling review when concurrency/pacing changes: sofia ivanovann---nn validation checklist (for edits)n1. tokenizer sanity: measured token lengths fall into intended buckets (p95 within bucket bounds).n2. decode length stability: measured output tokens are within target bucket 90 of the time.n3. safety/privacy: no pii strings templates pass redaction assertions.n4. variance check: end-to-end p95 variance does not increase materially versus previous version at constant runtime.n5. overhead: canary stays within regional gpu overhead budget (nnendnnchat (structured extraction):n- user: extract the fields component, symptom, suspected_cause, mitigation from the text below. output as key:value lines:nnnnendnncompletion (checklist):n- prompt: instruction: write a 7-step checklist for validating a service rollout in a synthetic environment.ninput: noutput:nntool calling (extract_fields_v1):n- tool name: extract_fields_v1n- user: from the synthetic text, extract service, metric, regression_type, suspected_layer. keep values under 12 tokens each.nnnnendnn---nn faqnq: why include streaming at all?na: streaming exercises buffering/serialization paths and helps ensure that end-to-end instrumentation remains correct across modes. runtime-only latency metrics should remain comparable.nnq: should we add multilingual prompts?na: not in v0.4. multilingual content can change tokenization behavior and output lengths unpredictably across models. we may add a dedicated multilingual shape set once baselines and variance are well characterized.nnq: does tool calling turn this into a quality benchmark?na: no. outputs are schema-bounded and performance-oriented correctness is not scored here beyond basic schema validity and boundedness.nn---nn ownershipn- primary owner: runtime perf suite (noah patel)n- prompt/template safety review: applied ml evals (rina kobayashi)n- runtime source_type: confluence, title: canary sla oracle and benchmark gate specification, content: title: canary sla oracle and benchmark gate specificationnnsummary:nthis document defines the design, operational contract, and runbook for the canary sla oracle a deterministic decision service that evaluates canary releases against a defined set of benchmark gates before permitting progressive rollout. the specification ties release tooling to the benchmarking suite and runtime observability so releases are gated by both fidelity (quality) and operational slos (latency, error budget, cost).nngoals:n- provide a repeatable, auditable gate for canary decisions that combines synthetic benchmark signals with live canary telemetry.n- reduce false positives/negatives by using weighted evidence and time-windowed aggregation.n- ensure fast feedback for small canaries while remaining robust for larger traffic ramps.n- emit human-readable verdicts and machine-readable artifacts for automation (ok/reject/conditional).nnscope:nthis spec covers: canary sla oracle behaviour, benchmark gate definitions, data ingestion and enrichment, verdict calculation, tie-breaking, and required observability hooks. it does not specify ui/console layouts those are product deliverables.nndefinitions:n- canary: a controlled subset deployment of a new runtime component, kernel, or model variant.n- benchmark gate: a single pass/fail criterion computed from benchmark or telemetry data (e.g., p99 0.92 reject embedding/response-similarity check against baseline n cost_per_token_delta perf-suite and billing 0.85 ok 0.6 conditional s reject insufficient/conflicting data inconclusive.nntime windows and sampling:n- live telemetry: rolling windows of 1m, 5m, 15m primary decision window is 5m with 15m as confirmation.n- perf-suite results: treated as single-snapshot evidence with decay function: weight e-age/48h.n- minimum sample floor: for latency/error gates require 500 requests in the 5m window or verdict is marked inconclusive.nndata enrichment and canonicalization:n- normalize percentiles using the runtimes histogram export (openmetrics). convert to ms and apply route-specific knobs (see section on route sensitivity).n- enrich with: model_variant_id, kernel_commit, instance_type, region, traffic_mix (proportion of streaming/chat/embedding).nntie-breaking and human override:n- if aggregation yields inconclusive or conditional, the policy allows a human approver to escalate with justification. the oracle will surface the top three signals that would flip the verdict if they changed.n- overrides are auditable: approver id, timestamp, justification, and a ttl for the override (default 1 hour).nnrunbook: canary release flow (operators):n1) author triggers a canary via the release tool with expected traffic fraction and perf-suite job id.n2) perf-suite runs pre-release benchmarks (synthetic slos) and uploads results to the benchmark-store.n3) release tool marks canary as active the oracle begins ingesting live telemetry automatically.n4) oracle evaluates gates at t5m and emits initial verdict artifact to the release tool and logs.n5) if verdict ok auto-progress to next stage per release policy.n6) if verdict conditional hold, notify on-call and product reviewer with evidence bundle.n7) if verdict reject trigger automatic rollback policy and create incident for postmortem.n8) if verdict inconclusive extend canary for an additional 10m or require perf-suite re-run with larger synthetic load.nnoperational alerts and observability hooks:n- alert: oracle failure (ingest/compute) p1 oncall.n- alert: inconclusive rate 10 across canaries in last 24h investigate metric sparsity or perf-suite health.n- gauges to expose: current_score, gate_pass_rate, evidence_age_seconds, min_sample_count.n- dashboards: canary health (per-release), gate violations (heatmap by route), evidence drift (time series of quality_similarity).nnexample verdict artifact (machine-readable):nnn release_id: r-2026-0104,n canary_shard: canary-eu-7,n verdict: conditional,n score: 0.72,n evidence: n gate:latency_p99_path,status:pass,measured:95ms,threshold:120ms,weight:3,n gate:quality_similarity,status:fail,measured:0.88,threshold:0.92,weight:5n ,n timestamp: 2026-06-10t16:12:03z,n artifact_signature: sha256:...nnnn(that json is illustrative the real artifact must be signed and include schema_version.)nnrollout automation examples (cli snippets):n- trigger a canary and attach a perf job:nnredwoodctl release start --component runtime --sha abcd1234 --canary 0.01 --perf-job perf-2026-06-10-phinn- query oracle verdict:nnredwoodctl release verdict --release r-2026-0104 title: tp stress suite spec (multi-gpu tensor parallel reliability performance), content: summarynthis document specifies the tp stress suite: a set of repeatable workloads and pass/fail criteria used to detect multi-gpu tensor-parallel (tp) regressions in redwoods serving runtime. the suite targets known failure modes under sustained load (mixed prefill/decode, long context, bursty concurrency, cancellation, memory/kv pressure) that have historically produced request hangs, gpu stalls, and downstream timeouts.nnthe suite runs in two modes:n1) ci smoke gating (fast, minimal hardware): catches obvious deadlocks and correctness-breaking changes.n2) perf lab perf-canary (representative gpus, longer burn): catches probabilistic stalls, p99 latency inflation, and throughput regressions.nn goalsn- detect and prevent re-introduction of tp hangs/timeouts (primary).n- provide early, actionable signals that localize stalls to compute vs nccl/collectives vs scheduler starvation.n- establish stable, versioned workload definitions (distributions, seeds, thresholds) to make results comparable over time.n- integrate with existing redwood pipelines:n - benchmark-lab repro harnessn - perf-canary scenariosn - runtime release gating and canary dashboardsnn non-goalsn- model quality/evals (we use fixed prompts purely as workload generators).n- exhaustive hardware coverage (we prioritize the fleet/hot paths full coverage remains a lab responsibility).n- replacing microbenchmarks this suite complements kernel-level microbench tests.nn definitionsn- replica: one runtime instance serving requests.n- tp degree (tp2/4/8): number of gpus participating in one replicas model partition.n- prefill: prompt processing decode: token-by-token generation.n- hang: request fails to complete without explicit error typically presents as streaming stuck, stalled nccl, or scheduler deadlock.n- stall detector: runtime metric indicating lack of progress (heartbeat gap, collective in-flight growth, queue depth growth without completion).nn suite overviewnthe suite is composed of scenario groups, each with a workload generator and pass/fail criteria.nn scenario groups (required)n1) mixed prefill/decode (streaming)n2) long context heavy prefilln3) bursty concurrency backpressuren4) cancellation / client disconnectn5) kv cache pressure compaction edgesnn scenario groups (optional / phased)n6) replica churn during sustained load (drain/restart while traffic continues)n7) fault injection (forced collective timeout to validate watchdog abort semantics)nn workload generatorsnall generators share these properties:n- deterministic by default via seeded randomness.n- pluggable distributions for prompt length, output length, think-time, and request interarrival.n- supports streaming and non-streaming requests.n- emits structured artifacts:n - request timeline summaryn - per-rank progress markersn - runtime metrics snapshot references (prometheus query links)n - trace sample ids (if enabled)nn generator interface (conceptual)neach scenario defines:n- model tp config: model identifier, quantization profile if relevant, tp degree.n- traffic config: concurrency targets, arrival distribution, duration.n- request config: distributions of prompt lengths and max_new_tokens, streaming on/off.n- failure hooks: cancellation rate, replica restart events, memory pressure toggles.n- success criteria: thresholds and required signals.nn standard distributionsnunless overridden per scenario:n- prompt length distribution (tokens): mixture of short medium longn - 60: 128512 (uniform)n - 30: 1,0244,096 (log-uniform)n - 10: 8,19216,384 (log-uniform only on long-context-capable models)n- max new tokens distribution:n - 70: 64256 (uniform)n - 25: 2561,024 (log-uniform)n - 5: 1,0242,048 (log-uniform decode stress)n- interarrival:n - ci mode: fixed-rate to keep variance low.n - perf mode: poisson arrivals with occasional burst windows.nn scenario specificationsnn 1) mixed prefill/decode (streaming)npurpose: reproduce starvation and ordering issues caused by prefill-heavy batches interleaving with streaming decode steps.nnconfig (baseline):n- tp: 4n- duration: 20 minutes (perf), 5 minutes (ci)n- concurrency target: 24 in-flight requests per replica (perf), 8 (ci)n- streaming: enabledn- prompt length: standard distributionn- max new tokens: skewed toward short/medium (to keep decode churn high)nnadditional knobs:n- decode step budget: enforce continuous decode iterations (avoid all-prefill phases).n- prefill burst windows: 30s windows with 2x arrival rate every 5 minutes.nnpass/fail:n- hard fail if any request exceeds timeout:n - ci: 120s wall timen - perf: 300s wall timen- hard fail if stall detectors trigger:n - per-rank heartbeat gap 30s (ci) / 60s (perf)n - in-flight collective counter monotonic growth without completion for 30sn- soft fail (regression) if:n - p99 end-to-end latency increases 15 vs pinned baseline for same hardware/profilen - decode tokens/sec decreases 10 (throughput regression)nnn 2) long context heavy prefillnpurpose: catch long-context issues that amplify nccl ordering sensitivity and scheduler backpressure, and stress kv allocation paths.nnconfig (baseline):n- tp: 4 (required), tp: 8 (lab-only where supported)n- duration: 30 minutes (perf), 8 minutes (ci)n- concurrency: 8 (perf), 2 (ci)n- streaming: disabled by default (focus on prefill correctness) optional streaming variantn- prompt lengths:n - 50: 8k16kn - 40: 16k32k (only for models configured for 32k)n - 10: 32k64k (lab-only)n- max new tokens: 64256nnpass/fail:n- hard fail on any hang / stall detector trigger.n- hard fail if oom occurs when below expected headroom thresholds (see memory expectations).n- soft fail if prefill latency p95 increases 20 vs baseline.nnn 3) bursty concurrency backpressurenpurpose: validate scheduler fairness and load-shedding hooks ensure we dont wedge replicas during sudden spikes.nnconfig:n- tp: 4n- duration: 20 minutes perf, 5 minutes cin- baseline arrival: maintain 50 of steady-state throughput targetn- burst: 3x arrivals for 20s, every 2 minutesn- concurrency cap: latency returning to within 10 of baseline) 90s.nnn 4) cancellation / client disconnectnpurpose: catch deadlocks caused by cancellation paths leaving collectives waiting or ranks diverging.nnconfig:n- tp: 4n- duration: 15 minutes perf, 5 minutes cin- streaming: enabledn- cancellation rate: 2 of requests cancel mid-decode 1 cancel during prefilln- cancellation timing: random uniform over request lifetime, seedednnpass/fail:n- hard fail if any cancellation causes:n - replica wedging (no progress on subsequent requests)n - watchdog abort storm (excess aborts) exceeding rate limitn- soft fail if diurnal effects.nnbenchmarking suite integrationn-----------------------------n- bench artifacts to generate for every experiment:n 1) microbench: per-kernel latency/throughput at multiple sequence correlation between model fidelity (quality) and runtime execution signals (latency, kernel selection, memory pressure, quantization path) across production-like workloads. the goal is to produce actionable correlations that guide scheduler, kernel, and quantization changes without regressing customer-visible quality.nnwhy this doc existsn-------------------n- engineers often optimize for cost/latency and see unexpected changes in output quality.n- quantitative correlation between fidelity metrics and runtime signals helps make safe tradeoffs.n- this playbook standardizes experiment design, telemetry collection, and analysis so that findings can be validated and operationalized.nnscope and audiencen------------------n- audience: runtime engineers, benchmarking owners, sres, model-onboarding team.n- scope: inference workloads for text generation and chat includes model variants, quantized kernels, and multi-tenant scheduling shapes.n- out of scope: training fidelity analysis, dataset labeling methodology outside of our eval harness.nnkey definitionsn---------------n- fidelity: end-to-end task quality measured by an agreed prompt set and evaluation metric (e.g., bleu, rouge, or redwood qa score).n- runtime signal: telemetry emitted by the runtime (per-request latency percentiles, kernel variant id, slot preemption count, kv cache hit rate, accelerator occupancy).n- correlation window: time window used to align telemetry and fidelity observations (default: 1 hour for production mirroring tests, 515 minutes for synthetic load tests).nnrequired network mirror that can replay production traffic into an isolated runtime fleet.n- metrics store: prometheus long-term rollup in clickhouse for hourly aggregates.nnpre-experiment (task-specific) block rollout, start joint triage (runtime model owner)n kv_cache_hit_rate -10 percentage points check cache affinity and warmstart profilesn kernel_fallback_rate 5 evaluate kernel correctness and performance regressionsnnrecommended default fidelity thresholds (examples):n- short-form summarization: delta rouge-l 10 and use median-of-means for robust estimates.n- q: kernel variant tags missing in traces. a: ensure runtime build includes kernel-annotator and that trace sampling for the experiment is set to 100.n- q: correlation but no causal signal. a: run single-factor ablation (hold other variables constant) and verify reproducibility.nnappendix a sample experiment-manifest.ymln------------------------------------------nexperiment_id: fidelity-20260115-aishanowner: source_type: confluence, title: shadowing fidelity convergence lab protocol, content: summarynnthis page documents the lab protocol for running controlled shadow (mirrored) traffic experiments to measure fidelity convergence across model variants and kernel scheduling profiles. fidelity convergence is the process of comparing output quality (task-specific metrics and human-validated checks) between a live production model and candidate variants (quantized, distilled, or alternative kernels) while simultaneously measuring performance and scheduler interactions. the protocol is intended for benchmarking-and-perf-suite engineers, runtime engineers, and applied ml evaluators.nngoalsnn- produce reproducible, comparable fidelity metrics (bleu/rouge/em/accuracy for task datasets embedding cosine similarity for retrieval) between model variants and production model.n- measure kernel-scheduler interaction effects: how different scheduler policies (e.g., preemptive-shepherding, batch-slicing, slotting) affect fidelity under load.n- provide a safe failover and rollback runbook for experiments that impact latency or error budgets.n- deliver a data artifact package that supports triage: latency histograms, per-token cost, kernel trace events, kv-cache hit/miss rates, and sample outputs.nnscope and definitionsnn- shadowing: replicate a proportion p of production requests and send them to a candidate model variant without altering the client-visible response. logging and sampling must ensure privacy and pii handling consistent with data policy.n- fidelity convergence threshold (fct): threshold defining acceptable divergence default: mean task metric drop 0.985. product teams can define stricter thresholds per sla.n- kernel scheduling profile: a named set of scheduler parameters (slot_size, preemption_timeout_ms, batch_slice_limit) used by the runtime.nnpre-requisitesnn1. canary baseline: a validated production canary model id (e.g., model:redwood-v1-canary).n2. candidate artifact: containerized candidate model kernel hints (quantization profile id, kernel hint file).n3. access: experiment-runner service role with read/write to telemetry s3 bucket and the sandboxed runtime namespace.n4. quotas: ensure shadow traffic rate is limited to candidate variant in sandbox pool, with enforced kernel-scheduler profile. if the runtime detects any p99 or error-rate regression beyond thresholds, automatically drop shadow to 0 (see runbook).nn3) kernel schedule matrix (example)n- profile:baseline slot_size: 16, preemption_timeout_ms: 50, batch_slice_limit: 4 n- profile:latency-optim slot_size: 8, preemption_timeout_ms: 20, batch_slice_limit: 2 n- profile:throughput-optim slot_size: 32, preemption_timeout_ms: 200, batch_slice_limit: 8 nnrun steps (numbered)nn1. provision candidate: push candidate model artifact to sandbox registry and register variant in model-catalog under tag experiment/.n2. prepare experiment config (example yaml below).n3. run a dry run against replayed traffic for 1 hour to check for obvious crashes and kernel-level ooms.n4. start shadow with rate cap monitor real-time dashboards and automated gates for 60 minutes.n5. escalate to expanded run if gates pass (see gating criteria).n6. post-process logs for fidelity metrics, kernel traces, and scheduler attribution.nnexample experiment yamlnnexperiment_id: shadow-fc-2026-02nshadow_fraction: 0.05nrouting:n pool: sandboxn kernel_profile: latency-optimndatasets:n - ticket-summarization-testset-v3n - prod-anon-sample-2026-02nmetrics:n - task_accuracyn - embedding_cosinen - p50_latencyn - p99_latencyngates:n p99_latency_regression_ms: 50n error_rate_delta_pct: 0.5n fidelity_drop_pct_absolute: 1.5nnmonitoring and telemetrynnrequired metrics and traces to collect for each request (retention 30 days):n- request_id, route_id, model_variant_id, kernel_profile, token_count, kvcache_hit, batch_idn- latency_ms (end-to-end), compute_ms (kernel-level), gpu_cycles, memory_bytes_allocatedn- scheduler_events: enqueue_time, dequeue_time, preempted_flag, slot_alloc_msn- sampled outputs (1:1000 sampling) with anonymized prompt hash and output hashnndashboards (required)n- fidelity overview: task metric delta, distribution plots, output examplesn- performance overview: p50/p90/p99 latency split by kernel_profile and request_size bucketn- scheduler attribution: preemption counts, slot occupancy heatmap, batch sizes over timenngating criteria (automated)nn- gate fail if p99 latency increases by p99_latency_regression_ms or error_rate increases by error_rate_delta_pct or fidelity_drop_pct_absolute exceeded.n- gate warn if task metric drop between 1.0 and 1.5 or embedding cosine between 0.985 and 0.99.nnsafe stop rollback runbook (quick steps)nn1. if gate fail triggers, experiment-runner will automatically set shadow_fraction0 and mute candidate variant. notify oncall kernel_profile to baseline and re-run dry replay.n4. if regression is fidelity-related, mark candidate as rejected and create an evaluation ticket with sample outputs and diff table.nnownership and content: summary:nnthis document defines redwoods methodology for measuring per-token energy consumption and mapping that to unit cost across common runtime configurations. the goal is to provide reproducible benchmarks that combine power telemetry, token accounting, latency buckets, and scheduler/kernel settings. use these measurements to: (1) guide model/quantization selection for cost-sensitive workloads, (2) set realistic energy-aware slos for dedicated pools, and (3) feed cost-model inputs for the console optimizer recommendations.nnscope and motivation:nn- scope: llm inference cpu/gpu stacks used by redwood hosted and dedicated runtimes. includes: model variants (fp16/int8/q4f16), sequence lengths 82048, batching policies, kv cache hit/miss scenarios, and multi-tenant kernel scheduling modes.n- motivation: token-level unit cost is traditionally driven by time-on-kernel. we complement that with measured power to capture the true marginal energy cost for chargeback and optimization. this matters for large-scale dedicated fleets and green/sustainability metrics.nnowner and contacts:nn- owner: eng-serving-runtime / performance teamn- primary contact: ravi.menon@redwood.ain- secondary: perf-oncall@redwood.ainndefinitions and conventions:nn1) measurement interval: telemetry window aligned to a request or batch lifecycle. default: request submission time - last token emitted 5ms drain.n2) per-token energy (et): measured joules consumed attributable to generating a token. calculation method described below.n3) baseline idle power (p_idle): power draw of the node(s) measured with runtime process up but quiescent (no requests, background housekeeping allowed).n4) attribution unit: single request, or combinable into micro-batches for throughput experiments.nnhardware and software profiles used in this doc:nn- gpu types: a100 80gb (nvml), a10g 24gb (nvml), h100 (nvml).n- node configs: 1xgpu, 4xgpu nccl-sharded nodes.n- runtime: redwood-runtime v2.3.1 (includes kernel scheduler v1.8).n- kernel builds: cuda-12.2 custom attention kernel v6.1.nnmeasurement methodology (step-by-step):nn1) prepare test fleet:n a) reserve 3 identical nodes for each hardware profile.n b) deploy runtime build under test with identical runtime flags except for the variable under measurement (e.g., quantization flag).nn2) calibrate idle power (p_idle):n a) remove user traffic and ensure collector is attached (nvml-exporter or node-power-proxy).n b) collect power for 120s and store median as p_idle_node.nn3) generate traffic workload:n a) use workload runner (perf-runner v1.5) with a representative prompt set. include: small-chat (len 16), search-snippet (len 128), long-form (len 1024).n b) for each request profile, run 10,000 requests for stable averages. use fixed seed for deterministic tokenization.nn4) collect telemetry:n a) power telemetry: sample at 100hz from nvml via node export.n b) runtime telemetry: token counts, kernel invocation timestamps, kernel ids, batch sizes, and kv-cache hit ratio.n c) infrastructure telemetry: cpu utilization, pcie bandwidth counters, gpu memory usage.nn5) compute per-token aggregate across requests to produce mean, median, and 99th-percentile et per workload bucket.nn6) convert energy to cost:n a) input parameters: cost_per_kwh (team finance input), datacenter pue, currency.n b) cost_per_joule cost_per_kwh / (3600 1000).n c) token_cost et_request cost_per_joule pue.nnminimum reproducibility checklist (run before publishing results):nn- node clock sync verified
