confluence, title: cost model inputs from serving runtime metrics (v1), content: overviewnthis document defines the runtime-exported inputs required by the standard cost model (scm) to produce consistent per-request and aggregated cost breakdowns across console, optimize, and finance reporting.nnthe serving runtime is the source of truth for:n- prefill vs decode token accounting (including accepted/emitted vs attempted tokens)n- kv cache behavior (hits/misses, reuse, evictions)n- batching and scheduling outcomes (batch sizes, queue times, gpu occupancy proxies)n- quantization execution path identifiers (what actually ran on-gpu)nnthis page is a contract between serving runtime, telemetry, and the cost model service.nn scopenin scope (v1): metrics emitted per request (or per request stage) that the cost model needs to explain cost deltas driven by caching/batching/quantization and to allocate runtime-attributable costs.nnout of scope (v1): full kernel-level profilers, per-layer timing breakdowns, and proprietary hardware counters. we prefer coarse but stable identifiers and low-cardinality metrics that can be aggregated safely.nn---nn contract principlesn1. deterministic semantics: a metric means one thing across all runtimes and deployment modes.n2. low cardinality by design: values must be bounded raw histograms are preferred over unbounded sets.n3. stage-aware accounting: prefill and decode are first-class stages for both token and time/cost attribution.n4. execution-path truth: the cost model keys off what the runtime actually executed (kernel/quant path id), not what the request asked for.n5. backwards compatibility: new fields are additive. renames require dual-write for 2 releases and a deprecation notice.nn---nn emission modelnruntime emits a single logical record per request with optional stage sub-metrics.nn required record identifiersnthese identifiers must be present on every record so telemetry can join with platform and billing primitives:n- request_id: globally unique within a region uuid stringn- tenant_id: redwood tenant/org identifiern- project_id: project/workspace identifier (if applicable)n- deployment_mode: hosted dedicated privaten- region: e.g., us-east-1n- model_id: catalog model identifier (pinned version)n- model_revision: immutable model revision hash or build idn- runtime_build_id: runtime binary build/versionn- hardware_sku: canonical gpu sku label (e.g., a100-80gb, h100-sxm)nnnote: several of these come from the control plane however the runtime must pass through the identifiers it was scheduled with, so the emitted record is self-contained.nn---nn metrics: tokens stagesnthe scm requires tokens to be attributed to prefill vs decode consistently.nn definitionsn- prefill_tokens: number of prompt tokens processed in the initial forward pass for the accepted prompt.n- decode_tokens_emitted: number of tokens emitted to the client (including streamed tokens).n- decode_tokens_attempted: number of decode steps attempted, including tokens that were later suppressed/rolled back by stop conditions.nnin v1 cost breakdowns, console uses decode_tokens_emitted for customer-visible token counts, while internal performance modeling may use decode_tokens_attempted to explain compute waste. both are exported to allow reconciliation.nn fields (required)n- tokens.prefill.accepted (int, tokens)n- tokens.decode.emitted (int, tokens)n- tokens.decode.attempted (int, tokens)n- tokens.total.accepted (int, tokens) prefill.accepted decode.emittednn fields (recommended)n- tokens.prefill.cached_reused (int, tokens)n - number of prefill tokens for which kv state was reused from cache (see kv cache section).nn---nn metrics: kv cachenkv cache behavior is the most important runtime-only driver for cost differences across otherwise identical requests.nn kv cache semantic modelnwe track cache at the request level in terms of:n- prefix reuse: how many prompt tokens did not require compute because their kv states were availablen- missed compute: how many tokens required prefill computen- evictions: how often we had to evict kv blocks, causing lower hit rates and/or recomputationnn fields (required)nall units and semantics below must be stable across implementations.nn1) kv_cache.enabled (bool)n- true if the request was eligible to use kv caching (even if hit_rate is 0).nn2) kv_cache.lookup_status (enum)n- allowed values: disabled no_key hit partial_hit miss errorn- partial_hit indicates some prefix tokens were reused but not the full eligible prefix.nn3) kv_cache.prefix_tokens_eligible (int, tokens)n- number of prompt tokens eligible for kv reuse (after normalization, templates, and routing decisions).nn4) kv_cache.prefix_tokens_reused (int, tokens)n- subset of eligible prefix tokens whose kv states were reused.nn5) kv_cache.blocks_reused (int, blocks)n- count of kv blocks reused (block size is runtime-defined but must be consistent within a runtime_build_id).nn6) kv_cache.blocks_written (int, blocks)n- new kv blocks written for this request.nn7) kv_cache.evictions (int, blocks)n- number of blocks evicted attributable to this requests execution window.nn fields (recommended)n- kv_cache.eviction_reason (enum): capacity ttl policy fragmentation unknownn- kv_cache.cache_namespace (string, bounded)n - a small, bounded label (e.g., tenant-scoped vs global) used for debugging hit rate differences. must not include tenant ids or unbounded values.nn validation rulesn- prefix_tokens_reused prefix_tokens_eligiblen- lookup_status hit implies prefix_tokens_reused prefix_tokens_eligiblen- lookup_status disabled implies kv_cache.enabled false and all kv_cache. counts are 0nn---nn metrics: batching schedulingnbatching and scheduling outcomes influence effective gpu time per token, and are required to explain unit-cost changes as batching configuration changes.nn conceptsn- request queue time: time from runtime receiving the request until it is assigned to a batch for prefilln- continuous batching: decode steps can be interleaved across requests this affects decode efficiency metricsnn fields (required)n1) scheduler.queue_time_ms (int, ms)n- time from request enqueue to first execution (prefill start).nn2) scheduler.prefill_batch_size (int, requests)n- number of requests included in the batch for the prefill stage.nn3) scheduler.decode_max_batch_size_observed (int, requests)n- maximum number of concurrently active sequences in the decode loop while this request was active.nn4) scheduler.decode_mean_batch_size (float, requests)n- mean active batch size across decode steps for this request.nn5) scheduler.tokens_per_step_mean (float, tokens/step)n- mean tokens advanced per decode step across the batch while this request was active.nn fields (recommended)n- scheduler.prefill_microbatch_count (int)n - if prefill is microbatched internally.n- scheduler.decode_steps (int)n - number of decode iterations observed for this request.n- scheduler.throttled (bool)n - true if scheduler throttling engaged (capacity protection / slo protection).n- scheduler.throttle_reason (enum): gpu_mem queue_depth fairness overload unknownnn cardinality constraintsn- throttle_reason and lookup_status must be enums with a fixed set.n- no per-request lists of batch composition or other request ids.nn---nn metrics: latency runtime time attributionnthe scm uses runtime wall times for reconciliation and drift analysis, and to allocate overhead when configured.nn fields (required)n- timing.request_total_ms (int, ms)n- timing.prefill_compute_ms (int, ms)n- timing.decode_compute_ms (int, ms)nn fields (recommended)n- timing.serialization_ms (int, ms)n- timing.network_overhead_ms (int, ms)n- timing.runtime_overhead_ms (int, ms)nnnotes:n- compute_ms includes time spent executing model kernels and any runtime-managed waits in the execution stream.n- overhead fields are for internal diagnostics the scm may use them for overhead allocation policies depending on adr-022 configuration.nn---nn metrics: quantization execution pathnthe scm must know what quantization actually unknownnndo not omit the fields omission complicates downstream schema negotiation and drift triage.nn---nn request outcome safety signalsnthese are used by scm and console to avoid attributing costs overviewnnthis document defines a repeatable protocol for cross-layer capacity probing and fidelity-aware sampling used by the runtime performance and benchmarking teams. the goal is to produce deterministic, signal-rich datasets that drive scheduling, kernel selection, and model-variant routing decisions while preserving production safety.nngoalsnn- measure usable capacity and safe degradation points across the full stack (dispatcher - scheduler - kernel - kvcache).n- correlate fidelity changes (quantization, sharding, batching) with cost and error surface.n- produce automatable data and thresholds for runtime admission controllers and canary policies.nnscopenn- applies to hosted, dedicated, and private runtime variants that use the runtime-dispatcher and kernel-allocator services.n- focused on core token-generation workloads (chat, standard completion) and embedding workloads where applicable.n- excludes long-running offline training jobs and third-party accelerator tests unless explicitly scheduled.nnterminologynn- probe: a controlled synthetic traffic pattern used to stress a subsystem.n- cohort: a grouping of similar requests (seq_len, prompt shape, model variant).n- fidelity step: a discrete change in model execution (e.g., int8 - int4, kv cache disabled, half-precision - full-precision).n- safe degradation point: the earliest observed point where slos are broken for 5 of traffic in a cohort and recovery is non-deterministic.nnownershipnn- author: jordan kim (runtime performance)n- primary owners: runtime-performance (eng), kernel-schedulers (eng)n- observability steward: priya nair (eng platform)nnrequired signals slosnncollect the following signals for each probe run:nn- request_id (string)n- timestamp (iso-8601)n- cohort_id (string)n- gpu_mem_used_mb (int)n- host_mem_used_mb (int)n- error_class (string null)nnminimum slos to compare against in probing runs:nn- p95 tail latency (generation end-to-end) int4, reduced kv cache capacity, smaller beam size), run the cohort at target utilizations in increasing order: 40, 65, 85.n- each run duration: 20m steady-state after 5m warmup.n- if any run breaches p99 latency target or shows 5 error_class ! null, mark that combination as degraded.nn4) controlled overload probingnn- for candidate safe-degradation points, perform a controlled overload: ramp utilization by 5 per minute until p95 or error thresholds violated or max 100 util reached.n- capture kernel-level traces for 1 minute windows centered on threshold-crossing events.nn5) automated analysis and threshold extractionnn- run the probe-analyze job to extract: usable_capacity_per_cohort, degradation_onset_util, kernel_breakpoint_map (kernel_id - seq_len - latency slope).n- persist outputs to the benchmarking dataset namespace with tags: commit, runtime-image, kernel-bundle, probe-id.nndata collection schema (text table)nn field type description n --- --- --- n probe_id string unique id for exceeded or error_rate_pct rises 5 compared to baseline, and the kernel_breakpoint_map shows non-linear latency slope for critical kernels.n- kernel pin recommendation: if kernel latency slope crosses yaml harness sample.n, doc_id: dsid_30bb036f2254475fbc8278b55c6db87f, source_type: confluence, title: coordinated execution: benchmarks sampling protocol, content: summaryn-------nthis document defines a coordinated execution benchmark and sampling protocol for validating scheduler and kernel interactions across mixed inference workloads. it complements existing per-component tests by providing a reproducible end-to-end measurement harness, standardized metrics, and a lightweight on-call triage flow for anomalies that arise during benchmark runs.nngoalsn-----n- provide an experiment protocol that produces stable, comparable signals for: latency p50/p95/p99, token throughput, per-token gpu time, kernel-switch rate, and kv-cache hit/miss impact.n- standardize sampling, tracing, and aggregation so regression hunts can compare like-for-like across runtime versions and hardware shapes.n- offer step-by-step runbook sections for running, interpreting, and responding to benchmark anomalies.nnscope and non-goalsn-------------------n- scope: multi-tenant mixed inference profiles (chat single-turn generation long-context summarization), scheduler interaction patterns (admission, preemption, handoff), and sampling-based profiling to attribute tail latency to kernel or network layers.n- non-goals: this is not a replacement for microbenchmarks (kernel unit tests) nor for customer-specific capacity planning it should be used as a cross-cutting integration verification and regression detector.nnoverview of the protocoln------------------------n1. define workload cohorts: head (short chat, 864 tokens), mid (generation, 64512 tokens), tail (long-context, 5124k tokens). each cohort has an associated qps target and entropy profile.n2. synthesize request surface: use the workload corpus generator (see appendix) to produce deterministic request sequences for each cohort.n3. run a staged experiment matrix across hardware shapes and kernel build variants. for each cell collect: end-to-end traces (sampled), kernel-level traces (per-dispatch timestamps), and telemetry counters (scheduler signals, admission events, eviction events).n4. apply the sampling and aggregation rules below to produce a canonical report.nnworkload cohort definitionsn- head: 100ms target latency, 864 tokens, qps per-cohort: 100300.n- mid: 200500ms target, 64512 tokens, qps: 1050.n- tail: 500ms5s target, 5124k tokens, qps: 0.55.nnkey metrics (aggregation rules)n- latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 measured end-to-end and kernel-only. kernel-only sum(kernel execution windows on device).n- token throughput: tokens/sec measured per-cohort and aggregated weighted by customer-weighted token shares.n- kernel-switch rate: number of kernel handoffs per request (normalize by sequence length).n- kv-cache hit ratio and miss latency contribution: report absolute and delta vs baseline.n- preemption/eviction rate: events per 1k requests.nnsampling tracing rulesn------------------------n- deterministic seed: all synthetic corpora must be generated with a fixed rng seed per experiment id. record the seed in the run metadata.n- stratified sampling: sample 1 in n end-to-end requests per cohort to capture full trace data. n is chosen so that overhead 15 vs baseline.n- end-to-end p99: fail if 25 increase or absolute 2s for mid cohort.n- kv-cache miss contribution: fail if miss-induced latency increases 30ms average.nninvestigation triage runbookn------------------------------n1. validate inputs: confirm rng seed, cohort mix, and hardware cell match the experiment matrix.n2. compare traces: aggregate top-3 root cause candidates by per-request kernel-only latency contribution.n3. check scheduler signals: are admission delays or preemptions elevated? check admission queue length and priority inversion counters.n4. inspect kernel histogram: look for new long-tail modes indicating kernel stalls or thermal throttling.n5. inspect device metrics: gpu sm utilization, pcie transfer spikes, and nvlink error counters.n6. if kernel-only latency is unchanged but end-to-end regresses, inspect rpc and serialization metrics and network egress congestion.n7. run targeted microbenchmarks: isolate suspect kernel variant on controlled single-tenant run to confirm reproducer.n8. if reproducer found, create an issue with: run id, seed, failing metrics, top traces (compressed), and suggested hypothesis.nnquick mitigations (operational)n- swap scheduler policy to economic-governor for degraded tail pressure scenarios.n- pin cohort-heavy customers to isolation pool (dedicated capacity) if noisy neighbor observed.n- temporarily enable kernel hedging for long tail requests (config toggle, see runtime flags table).nnruntime flags configuration tablen flag name purpose recommended value n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------n runtime.benchmark.sample_rate stratified documents the microbenchmarking suite we run against the redwood serving runtime to capture per-kernel and per-path variance characteristics that inform scheduling, batching, and autoscaling decisions. the document explains the test harness, recommended configurations, analysis steps for variance decomposition, example outputs, and actions owners should take when results indicate regressions.nngoals:n- provide a repeatable, low-noise microbenchmark that isolates kernel execution time, memory-copy overhead, and kv-cache lookup variability.n- produce variance decomposition reports (p95/p99 variance, coefficient of variation) by sampling across seeds, sequence lengths, and batch shapes.n- surface kernel scheduling sensitivity (e.g., small-batch vs large-batch tradeoffs) to influence kernel mapper rules.n- define actionable thresholds and an alerting/playbook for anomalous increases in variance.nnscope and assumptions:n- targets: single-gpu and 2-gpu shard topologies on a100 v4 and h100 hardware in our lab cluster.n- tests are not full end-to-end requests (no network latency) they are focused on runtime hotspots (attention, softmax, kv-cache management, cuda memcpy, decode tokenizer).n- experiments assume stable host load noisy host metrics invalidate runs (see run criteria below).nntest harness and repository:n- harness: redwood/perf/microbench-suite (internal repo). primary cli: rw-microbench run --profile --repeats 50 --out n- supported profiles: small-decoding, long-prefix-atten, kv-lookup-heavy, tiled-attention, quantized-int8-path.n- artifact format: json lines where each line is timestamp,op,duration_ms,gpu_util,memcpy_ms,batch_shape,seed.nnrecommended lab config (table):n key value notes n------:---n os image ubuntu-22.04cuda_12.1 lab standard image n driver nvidia 545.60 pinned for reproducibility n cuda_visible_devices 0 or 0,1 set per-run n numactl preferred bind to local numa when measuring n run_isolation docker --cpuset-cpus cgroups avoid background processes nnrun criteria (pre-flight checklist):n1. no active builds or long-running loads on the target host.n2. gpu temperature --out runs.parquet.n2. produce per-op histograms and summary statistics: rw-microbench analyze runs.parquet --ops attn_forward_fused,kv_lookup --output analysis/.n3. run variance decomposition: rw-microbench variance-decompose analysis/ --group-by op,batch_shape,seed. this produces a csv with columns op,group,mean,stddev,cv,p95,p99,between_seed_var.n4. compare current run to baseline (stored in perf-bench-baselines). if cv increases by 30 for ops with mean 0.1 ms, mark as suspect.n5. if suspect, capture a flamegraph and kernel trace: rw-instrument trace-kernels --target --duration 120s --out trace/ (requires perf-admin role).nnthresholds and alerting rules (sre owners):n- informational: cv 0.15 for op groups with mean 0.2ms.n- warning: cv 0.30 or p99/p95 ratio 3 for any op (mean 0.1ms).n- critical: between-seed variance increases by factor 2 and absolute p99 increase 25 compared to baseline.n- alerts route to runtime-perf and create ticket in perf backlog with label microbench-regression.nncommon failure modes and triage guidance:n- symptom: increased memcpy_ms variance.n - likely causes: noisy pcie bus, concurrent node-level memcpy, or numa misbinding.n - actions: run nvidia-smi topo --matrix, check dmesg for dma errors, rerun with numactl pinned.n- symptom: intermittent long-tail in attn_forward_fused.n - likely causes: kernel fallback path triggered due to unsupported shape or quantization mismatch.n - actions: verify kernel metadata via rw-runtime kernel-inspect --op attn_forward_fused and check kernel selector logs.n- symptom: between-seed variance dominates (seed medians jump).n - likely causes: cache eviction policy, non-deterministic scheduling, or memory page migration.n - actions: increase warmup iterations, run isolating test with only deterministic seeds, capture kernel trace.nnintegration with scheduler/kernel-mapper decisions:n- the variance report should be consumed by the kernel-mapper pipeline: when cv for a kernel under small-batch shape exceeds 0.25, prefer a latency-priority kernel build for that shape in the next kernel release.n- autoscaler: if per-request variance for small requests (batch 1) leads to p99 2x median, autoscale policy should add a latency-priority shard rather than increase batch size.nnrelease notes and historical baseline policy:n- baselines are stored per hardware family and runtime minor version. name format: baseline---yyyymmdd.n- when a kernel or runtime release is proposed, include a microbench variance report as part of the pr checklist. changes that increase p99 by 10 require a mitigation plan.nnreport example (condensed):n op batch_shape mean_ms p95_ms p99_ms cv between_seed_var verdict n attn_forward_fused 1x64 0.45 0.60 1.78 0.28 0.05 regressed n kv_lookup 4x256 0.12 0.14 0.16 0.08 using the same profile and seeds. if not reproducible, mark as intermittent and schedule a 24h watch with repeated runs.n3. if reproducible, capture nvprof/nsight trace and attach to ticket.n4. assign confluence, title: lane gating and quality quota manifest, content: h1. lane gating and quality quota manifestnnshort descriptionnthis document defines execution lanes and the associated quality quota model used by the runtime to enforce per-tenant and per-route fidelity guarantees. it explains interactions with the kernel scheduler, profiling checkpoints, benchmarking guidance, incident runbooks, and rollout controls. the intended audience is runtime architects, scheduler engineers, and oncall sres.nnh2. overviewnexecution lanes are logical channels that group requests by fidelity budget, slo class, and resource claim characteristics. lane gating is the policy layer that decides which lane a request is admitted to and what quality (model variant, quantization, prefix-cache usage) may be applied. quality quotas are time-windowed budgets (tokens/per-minute) that debit based on per-request estimated cost and output fidelity impact.nnh2. key goalsn- maintain 99.95 p50 latency for interactive lanes under normal load.n- bound cost for bursty tenants via short-term quota windows (default 60s) and long-term smoothing (default 1h).n- enable graceful fidelity degradation rather than hard rejects during capacity constraints.n- give operators deterministic knobs to trade latency, quality, and cost.nnh2. definitionsn- execution lane: named string (e.g., interactive-high, batch-economy, slo-critical) with associated admission rules.n- quality quota: numeric budget assigned per tenant/route that decrements on request admission refunds or adjustments happen on cancellation/retry.n- lane lease: ephemeral allocation of kernel credit for a short duration to service a request without additional contention checks.n- fidelity band: descriptor of allowed model variants / quantization / kv cache usage (e.g., v1.1-fp16-kvprefetch)nnh2. lane taxonomy (default system lanes)n1. interactive-highn - slo: 99 of requests gating - scheduler - egress. use ttl-based rollups for cost accounting (recommended ttl: 3h).nnh2. benchmarking guidancen- benchmarks must include mixed-latency workloads that emulate: short-chat (1024 tokens), and multimodal bursts.n- use the lane-mixer harness to reproduce realistic lane admission pressure. parameters to sweep:n - cohort size (1-500 tenants)n - burstiness (poisson lambda with bursts from 2x-20x)n - cache entropy (fraction of unique prefixes)n- primary metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency per lane, kernel_occupancy, debit-leak (delta between estimated and actual debit).nnh2. slos and alertingn- slo matrix (example):n - interactive-high: p95 latency target 500 qps median latency 1 sustained for 5m - page oncall-sren - kernel-pressure-index 0.85 - escalate to runtime-kernel pagern - debit-estimation-drift 30 over 15m - open incident for estimator teamnnh2. runbook: lane-imbalance incident (quick steps)n1. detect: alert fires for lane_throttle_rate 1 and p95 latency degradation.n2. triage: check plan, content: overview:nnthis document defines the observability signals, safety checks, and automated test plan for runtime circuit constructs used across redwoods inference serving stack. it applies to the runtime components that can engage in circuit-style behavior: inference-router, batcher, kv-coordinator, model-worker, fallback-orchestrator, and edge-proxy adapters. the goal is to ensure that circuit transitions (open / half-open / closed), shed decisions, and graceful degradation behaviors are visible, tested, and safe to roll out in production.nnaudience:n- runtime (examples: kernel-shed, variant-fallback, batcher-queue-cutoff, model-quantize-fallback).n- safety check: deterministic assertions executed before a circuit is flipped in production (e.g., minimum healthy model-worker count, kv cache warmness).n- observability signal: telemetry that must be emitted to correlate circuit events with customer-visible impact (latency, error rates, token drop).nnnon-goals:n- design of new circuit types (covered by adrs). this plan describes testing and telemetry for circuits that are already implemented.nnprinciples:n1) explicit, machine-readable circuit events with stable schema for correlation.n2) safe, automated rollback gates driven by slo regressions and saturation signals.n3) deterministic test harnesses that run in ci and as scheduled synthetic checks in staging and canary clusters.n4) single source of truth for circuit metadata to drive dashboards and incident playbooks.nnownership and contacts:n- primary owner: runtime dsid_b875b2c7d7404486832f7cf8b25ed483, source_type: confluence, title: runtime lifecycle provenance and course corrections, content: overviewnnpurpose: this document defines the end-to-end runtime lifecycle used by redwoods serving runtime, the provenance signals we capture at each stage, and a set of operational course-corrections (automatic and manual) for common regressions. it bridges architecture, kernel scheduling policy, profiling playbooks, benchmark requirements, release highlights, known issues, and runbook recipes into a single operational reference.nnaudience: runtime engineers, sres, performance owners, and release managers.nngoalsn- provide a clear, reproducible model of request flow and the observable signals at each lifecycle stage.n- standardize kernel scheduling guardrails and a compact policy language for predictable latency/cost tradeoffs.n- define profiling and benchmarking protocols for validating changes.n- offer concrete runbooks and corrective actions for production incidents.nnscopenapplies to all hosted and dedicated runtime clusters managed by redwood (hosted-api, dedicated pools, private-runtime bundles). does not cover customer-side inference code or sdks.nnkey terminologyn- request timeline: sequence from ingress - classification - routing - scheduling - execute - emit - postprocess.n- execution unit: indivisible actor that maps to a kernel dispatch on a gpu (may span multiple kernels for long-decoder steps).n- kernel-credit: accounting unit used by the scheduler to ensure fairness and protect slos.n- provenance event: structured telemetry record emitted at well-known checkpoints with deterministic keys (trace_id, request_class, model_variant, kernel_shard, kv_hit, latency_ms, cost_token_units).nn1) runtime architecture summarynhigh-level flow (textual diagram):n- ingress - classifier - router - scheduler - kernel-exec - kv-cache - emit - metrics/logs/audit-storennresponsibilities by component (short):n- ingress: rate-limit, authz, initial sampling. emits ingress_provenance.n- classifier: inspects payload size, prompt shape, and model hints sets request_class tag.n- router: maps request_class - pool (region, gpu family, capacity tier). can rewrite model_variant for cost fallback.n- scheduler: performs priority selection, slotting, batching, and kernel credit deduction.n- kernel-exec: runs optimized kernels on device emits kernel_profiling trace for each dispatch.n- kv-cache: prefix and kv hits observable for hit-rate, warm-up slope, and eviction churn.n- emit: streaming vs non-streaming paths with different durability and backpressure modes.nnprovenance signals (minimum set captured at each checkpoint)n- ingress_provenance: trace_id, timestamp, api_key_hash, route_id, request_size_tokens // emitted at ingressn- classification_provenance: trace_id, request_class, expected_seq_len, model_hint // classifier outputn- routing_provenance: trace_id, pool_id, model_variant, fallback_reason? // selected pool/variantn- scheduling_provenance: trace_id, ticket_id, priority_band, credit_before, credit_after, slot_count // before dispatchn- kernel_profiling: trace_id, kernel_id, dispatch_index, duration_us, occupancy_pct, cuda_stream, mem_bytes // per dispatchn- kv_provenance: trace_id, shard_id, hit_bool, warmup_hint // cache interactionn- emit_provenance: trace_id, final_latency_ms, shard_route // end of requestnnall provenance events include service_version and git_commit to make traces usable for regression attribution.nn2) kernel scheduling policy overviewnwe enforce a compact, declarative scheduling policy used by the slot allocator and kernel admission controller. policies are evaluated per-pool and are versioned.nnpolicy language (example yaml snippet)nnpolicy_version: 2npriority_bands:n - name: realtimen min_tokens: 0n max_tokens: 2048n preemption: truen kernel_credit_rate: 10n - name: interactiven min_tokens: 2049n max_tokens: 8192n preemption: falsen kernel_credit_rate: 5n - name: batchn min_tokens: 8193n max_tokens: 131072n preemption: falsen kernel_credit_rate: 2nslot_allocation:n algorithm: proportional_fairn bias_configs:n realtime: 0.6n interactive: 0.3n batch: 0.1nbackpressure:n request_queue_max_ms: 300n sample_drop_percent: 0.05nnnotes on fields:n- kernel_credit_rate: credits per second allocated to a band. higher rate - lower expected latency at cost of throughput fairness.n- preemption: whether a higher band can preempt active lower-band executions (cooperative preemption). use sparingly for gpu kernels that support safe preemption.nnscheduling invariants (must hold across all runtime versions)n- band isolation: observed 99.9th percentile latency of band x must not exceed baseline(1 band_sla_tolerance).n- credit conservation: sum(kernel_credit_rate weight) across bands must be kernel_profiling - kv_provenance - emit).n4) microprofile: enable high-fidelity kernel_profiling for affected pool (510 sample) for 30 minutes.n5) kernel diff: compare kernel dispatch duration distribution against baseline using the kernel-diff tool.n6) act: apply course-correction (see table below).nncourse-corrections (ordered by risk)n- auto: increase slot_allocation bias for realtime band by 10 for 5 minutes (low risk).n- low-friction: temporarily disable batch band preemption in pool (reduces tail spikes).n- medium: roll forward small kernel patch with autotest gated (requires rolling canary).n- dsid_43121733e2a046de930c387c4be58c8a, source_type: confluence, title: adr: composable request contract and fidelity fencing, content: summarynnthis adr defines a composable request contract and a runtime fidelity fencing mechanism for redwood inference apis. the goal is to make the client-to-runtime capability negotiation explicit and minimal, enable safe progressive rollout of lower-cost model variants, and bind fidelity changes to observable slo effects. this document formalizes fields, semantics, runtime decision points, rollout gates, and the test/gating checklist for adoption.nncontext and motivationnnbackground: redwood exposes multi-variant inference (hosted/dedicated/private) where a single request can be satisfied by different model variants (full precision, quantized, distilled, or fallback models). historically, variant selection has been opaque: the server decided based on capacity and heuristics, with limited client signal. this caused surprising output shifts for clients and made quality regressions difficult to correlate to rollout events.nnkey problems we must solve:n- provide a minimal, backward-compatible request surface for clients to express cost/latency/quality preferences.n- prevent silent fidelity reductions that cause regressions for high-value customers.n- make runtime routing decisions auditable and tied to slos and rollout policies.nndecisionnnwe adopt a new composable request contract with explicit fidelity hints and a fidelity_fence field. the server will evaluate fidelity fences before selecting a variant fences act as runtime safety checks that reject or route requests when fidelity cannot be met. implementation details and rollout gating are below. this adr applies to all text/generation and chat endpoints and will be included in future streaming/embeddings contracts via incremental extension.nncontract overview (fields and semantics)nn1) request.fidelity_hint (optional, string): one of high, balanced, low. if omitted, treated as balanced. hints are advisory server may override when capacity or policy requires.nn2) request.fidelity_fence (optional, object represented as nested json string): a short declarative constraint set the server must honor or respond with a deterministic non-200 code. the fence has three orthogonal checks: quality_threshold, max_latency_ms, allowed_variants. example (as json text in the request):nnnn quality_threshold: 0.92,n max_latency_ms: 350,n allowed_variants: fp16-v2,q8_0-v1nnnnsemantics:n- quality_threshold is measured by the model-internal quality score produced by the evaluation hooks or a surrogate quality estimator. it is expressed as a decimal 0,1 where runtime maps to internal thresholds per model family.n- max_latency_ms is a client slo hint: if estimated response tail for candidate variants exceeds this, server must either route to a lower-latency allowed variant or return 409 with a structured error detailing the conflict.n- allowed_variants is an explicit white-list to constrain selection. if empty, all compatible variants are allowed.nn3) request.cost_control_token (optional, string): an account-level token replacing per-request hints in high-throughput clients binds to profile on the account with pre-approved cost/fidelity tradeoffs.nnruntime behavior and codesnn- when fidelity_fence is present, server performs a deterministic check sequence: (a) candidate enumeration, (b) quality estimator evaluation (fast surrogate), (c) latency estimation using recent tail metrics for the account and variant, (d) apply allowed_variants filter.n- if a candidate satisfies all fence checks, serve with that variant. if none satisfy, server returns http 409 conflict with a structured payload including: failed_checks (list), suggested_variants (list), and a request_recommendation (string).n- for advisory fidelity_hint only, server may downgrade gracefully but must add a header x-fidelity-decision: downgradedhonoredrejected and telemetry that links the decision to request id and rollout flags.nnrationale and alternatives considerednnalternatives considered:n- no explicit fence (status quo): allowed opaque decisions but we get regressions and customer confusion.n- full typed schema with many knobs: powerful but too complex for clients increases surface area and coupling.n- server-only capability discovery endpoint with no per-request fence: helpful but does not prevent mid-request fidelity shifts when runtime load spikes.nnwe chose composable fence because it is minimal, client-declarative, and enables short-circuit safety checks early in the scheduling pipeline. it also lays groundwork for automatic telemetry-driven rollback when fences start failing at scale.nnimplementation plannnscope: api contract change, runtime adapter in serving runtime, console exposure for per-account cost_control_token profiles, sdk updates, and e2e tests.nnhigh-level steps:n1) api: add parsing support for fidelity_fence in the api gateway (compatible with existing clients if field absent).n2) runtime: implement fence evaluation in the request admission path before batching. implement a fast surrogate quality estimator and latency estimator (see metrics below).n3) sdks: add helpers to construct fidelity_fence json and cost_control_token plumbing.n4) console: expose account profile editor for cost_control_token and default fidelity_hint.n5) tests: unit, integration, and degradation-sim tests (see test plan).n6) gradual rollout: dark launch - opt-in by selected customers - global default-to-enabled after 8 weeks and metric pass.nnrollout gating and slosnngate thresholds to progress from dark to global enabled:n- telemetry: fidelity_fence accept rate 99 for 72h for opt-in accounts, and failed_fence_rate page on breach.n- correlated quality-revision alert: if fidelity_decision downgraded and customer-eval-failure_rate increases by 1 in 24h, trigger a medium priority alert.nntesting and acceptance criteriannunit tests:n- parser correctness for fidelity_fence json string, edge cases, and invalid fields.n- deterministic mapping of quality_threshold to internal estimator outputs.nnintegration tests:n- full admission pipeline using simulator variants and a reproducible latency model.n- contract test ensuring header x-fidelity-decision present when relevant.nndegradation / chaos test plan:n- simulate gpu capacity exhaustion and verify that requests with strict fences receive 409 and that advisory hints get downgraded with clear telemetry.nnmigration and backward compatibilitynn- clients that omit the new fields experience no change.n- sdks will default to not sending fidelity_fence until explicitly toggled by developer or account profile.n- console profiles allow account admins to opt-in and generate cost_control_tokens.nnsecurity and privacy considerationsnn- fidelity_fence values are non-sensitive cost_control_token should be treated like an api key and stored in kms-backed account metadata.n- telemetry exposes allowed_variants and chosen_variant ensure these fields are scrubbed in public incident reports and redacted when sharing externally.nnownership and rollout contactsnn- feature owner: aisha bennett (serving-runtime)n- runtime implementation lead: lin zhoun- api gateway changes: diego ramirezn- console/account profile: mira patelnnopen questions and future worknn- replace fast surrogate estimator with learned online estimator tied to continuous evals.n- add service-level constraint composition to blend multiple accounts fences in multi-tenant batch contexts.n- extend fence semantics to embeddings and rerank endpoints with embedding-quality proxies.nnappendix: example changelog entry (for release notes)nn- v2027.03.0: introduced optional request.fidelity_hint and request.fidelity_fence. when fidelity_fence is present, server evaluates constraints and returns 409 if they cannot be satisfied. console: account profile and cost_control_token mvp. sdk: helpers for constructing fences (beta).nnreferencesnn- related: title: adaptive kv coordinator and eviction contract, content: overviewnnthis document specifies the runtime contract for the adaptive kv coordinator (akc), the eviction policy interface, and the safety guarantees that downstream services (shard-manager, runtime-executor, request-router) rely on. it is intended for runtime engineers, infra sres, model-serving owners, and private deployment integrators.nngoalsnn- define a minimal, implementation-agnostic api for kv cache coordination across shards and variants.n- provide deterministic eviction semantics under constrained memory pressure to avoid cross-variant nondeterminism.n- specify telemetry, slos, and runtime knobs required for safe rollouts and private deployments.n- outline a migration path and rollback plan for changing eviction strategies.nnscope and non-goalsnn- scope: in-memory kv caches used for model kv caches (attention cache, prefix cache) and request-level prefix caches managed by runtime nodes. applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.n- non-goal: application-level caching (customer caches outside the runtime) and long-term persistent caches.nndesign principlesnn1. deterministic eviction ordering. eviction must be stable given the same sequence of allocation and access signals.n2. isolated fairness. no tenant or model variant may cause starvation of unrelated workloads on the same gpu node.n3. observability-first. every eviction decision emits structured telemetry with reason codes and causal attribution.n4. configurable conservatism. default policy is conservative aggressive policies must be gated and tested.nncontract: api surfacennakc exposes the following endpoints and message types (grpc/http):nn- allocate(request): request tenant_id, variant_id, shard_id, bytes_requested, priority_hint - response grant_bytes, lease_id, expiration_ts n- touch(lease_id, key_hash, usage_weight): updates last_access and weight for eviction rankingn- release(lease_id, key_hash): explicit release when caller invalidates a prefixn- evictionplan(shard_id): returns ordered list of candidate keys and reason codes (soft/urgent)n- setpolicy(policy_name, policy_config_yaml): operator api to set node-local policyn- reportmetrics(summary): push interface for periodic aggregated telemetrynnall endpoints must accept and return a deterministic request_id header for trace correlation. the allocate response must return a stable lease_id that encodes shard and sequencing metadata (opaque to callers but stable for tracing).nneviction semantics and reason codesnneviction decisions carry one of the following reason codes (exact strings):nn- memory_pressure_soft: invoked when usage 70 of configured node cache budgetn- memory_pressure_urgent: invoked when usage 95 and soft eviction failed to reduce memoryn- tenant_quota_exceeded: tenant has passed its soft quota and lower-priority keys are eligiblen- stale_ttl: key ttl expired according to akc-soft-lease semanticsnnpriority ranking formula (default conservative):nnrank alpha lru_score beta (1/usage_weight) gamma tenant_priority_ranknndefault constants: alpha0.6, beta0.3, gamma0.1. policy configs may tune constants within safe ranges documented later.nnsafety and determinism guaranteesnn1. given identical sequences of allocate/touch/release and identical policy configs, the eviction order must be identical across restarts within a shard. implementations must persist minimal sequence markers (e.g., per-shard monotonic counters) to ensure ordering is reproducible during graceful restart.n2. during a split/merge of shards, akc emits a planned migration manifest with: old_shard_id - new_shard_ids, keys_moved_estimate, expected_live_leases. migration must be annotated with a migration_id and planned_cutover_ts.n3. rollbacks: any policy change applied via setpolicy must support an automatic rollback if the per-minute eviction_rate increases by 3x and tail_latency_spike 1.5x within a 15-minute window.nntelemetry requirements (minimum)nnevery node running akc must export these metrics at 10s granularity:nn- akc.evictions.count (labels: reason, shard_id, tenant_id)n- akc.allocations.granted_bytes_total (labels: shard_id, tenant_id)n- akc.leases.active_count (labels: shard_id)n- akc.eviction_rate_per_minute (shard_id)n- akc.tail_rehydration_latency_p95 (shard_id)nnstructured logs for each eviction event must include: event_ts, shard_id, tenant_id, variant_id, key_hash_prefix, reason, rank_score, pre_eviction_memory_usage, post_eviction_memory_usage, trace_id. logs must be json-lines and sparse-sampled at 1 for full detail and 100 for reasonmemory_pressure_urgent.nnslos and thresholdsnn- rehydration latency: 95th percentile rehydration latency for evicted keys should be configured_threshold for two consecutive windowsn b. eviction_rate_per_minute increases 3x baseline and model-quality-regression alert firesn c. tenant_quota_exceeded events affecting 5 of tenants in 30 minutesn4. post-rollback diagnostics: collect snapshot of eviction logs, in-memory lease map, and allocation histogram create postmortem within 48 hours.nnpolicy configuration example (yaml)nnpolicy_name: conservative_defaultnnodescope: node-localnconstants:n alpha: 0.6n beta: 0.3n gamma: 0.1nsoft_threshold_pct: 70nurgent_threshold_pct: 95ntenant_quota_policies:n default_soft_quota_bytes: 1073741824 1gibn tenant_priority_overrides: nnimplementation guidance and pitfallsnn- do persist only compact sequence markers for determinism avoid full key persistence (heavy).n- prefer lease-based short expirations to hard deletes to allow reconstructable state during recovery.n- beware of clock skews when computing expiration_ts use monotonic counters combined with wall-clock epoch.n- during preemption (gpu eviction), akc must admit a transient fudge window: grace_window_ms 5000 where leases remain valid but marked at risk.nnmigration and versioning plannn1. versioned policy schemas: store policy schema version in policy_config_yaml and reject setpolicy requests with unknown schema_version unless force flag is set.n2. two-phase migration for major changes: (a) deploy code with both vn and vn1 algorithm active behind feature flag (b) run canary traffic comparing deterministic eviction ordering (c) flip flag when stability metrics pass.nnchecklist for private/on-prem deploymentsnn- ensure admin exposes setpolicy over authenticated channel (mtls role-based structured error explaining limitation.nnfailure modes and example symptoms:n- mode a: kernel queue saturation on particular shardn symptoms: kernel ticket wait-time p99 rising, throttled dispatch /fanout-orch/v1/tags/update for tenant ids causing 20 of queued tickets.n c) if sustained 30m, escalate to infra-oncall for capacity add or hot-patch kernel flattening.n3) if mode b (kvcache eviction content: summarynthis document defines a practice for tying public service/api contract changes to slo-driven runtime acceptance gates and an operational rollback playbook. it standardizes how we declare the runtime impact of api/model/runtime changes, what telemetry must be collected, automated gate thresholds, and the exact steps engineers must follow to roll back or mitigate when gates fail.nnscopen- applies to changes that alter runtime behavior or the request/response contract for redwood-hosted inference endpoints and to configuration changes in dedicated and private runtime sidecars.n- includes: new streaming semantics, structured response version bumps, batch/quantization profile switches, kernel scheduling changes, fallback routing, and autoscaling policy changes.n- excludes purely ui-only changes and documentation-only edits.nnmotivationnmaking rollout decisions based on signal close to the customer experience reduces blast radius. historically we relied on ad-hoc dashboards and team conventions this playbook enforces:n- a single source of truth for contract impact metadata declared during prsn- automated slo gates enforced in ci/cd and at canary runtimen- a repeatable, fast rollback path with clear ownership.nndefinitionsn- contract change class (cc): small compatible incompatible runtime-affecting. each change must be labeled in the pr.n- runtime acceptance gate: an automated check that evaluates production-canary telemetry against slos for a change window.n- canary window: default 15 minutes for high-risk changes, 60 minutes for low-risk changes (configurable per change).n- primary slos: availability (p99 success rate), latency (p99), error budget burn.nncontract change classification guide (short)n1. small: internal refactor or non-semantic change with no client-visible effect. minimal telemetry required.n2. compatible: adds optional fields or expands schema in a backwards-compatible way. requires structured-response schema validation and unit tests plus canary gate.n3. incompatible: removes fields or changes semantics. requires staged rollout, documented migration plan, and manual approvals.n4. runtime-affecting: changes that alter batching, scheduling, quantization, kernel selection, or fallback routing. requires per-case perf tests, a canary in production with robust telemetry, and an automatic rollback policy.nnslo mapping (examples)n- availability slo: 99.95 successful responses per region over rolling 30d (primary kpi for breaking changes).n- latency slos: small-req p50 2.5 absolute pts for any critical eval.nntelemetry and instrumentation requirements (must be present for runtime-affecting and incompatible changes)n- request-id propagation across edge - router - runtime - cache - model.n- telemetry fields: request_class (shortlongembeddingbatch), model_variant, kernel-path, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, bytes_in, bytes_out, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, trace_id, latency_ms (broken down by stage).n- structured-response validation failures must be returned as a typed error with error_code struct_schema_violation and increment counter telemetry. synthetic canary traffic must be generated with both short and worst-case long-context prompts.nnci/cd gates and automationn- pr checklist must include: change classification, required telemetry list, expected slo impact, rollout plan, automated test matrix (unit, integration, perf), and owner oncall.n- merge is blocked until: required telemetry is present in canary manifests perf harness passes and at least one reviewer with runtime scope approves.n- canary job (pipeline): deploy to canary routing (1-2 traffic), run synthetic tests, evaluate runtime acceptance gate.n- runtime acceptance gate thresholds are codified in a yaml policy attached to the pr (example below). a failing gate triggers automatic rollback.nnexample gate policy (yaml)n---ngate_name: quantization-profile-switch-2026-11ncanary_window_minutes: 15nthresholds:n - metric: p99_latency_msn comparator: 220n - metric: error_rate_pctn comparator: 0 via router-api (atomic).n 2) promote previous stable snapshot as active variant.n 3) if the change updated kernel payloads or node-level packages, trigger node drain redeploy to recover consistent runtime.n 4) emit structured incident draft (title: automated rollback: ) with initial diagnostics.n- rollback cli (example):n rwinfctl rollout abort --change-idchg-2026-1123 --reasonslo_gate_failuren rwinfctl rollout promote --variant previous-stable --instanttruen- manual mitigation when automated rollback is inappropriate: follow the mitigation checklist in the mitigation section below.nnmitigation checklist (when partial rollback or hotfix is preferred)n- immediately route 100 of traffic to regional fallbacks (fallback-model:safe-1) using the router control plane.n- throttle ingress (edge) for aggressive error storms: set global edge concurrency cap to 10k requests/min and backpressure hints to clients.n- push a small configuration patch: e.g., reduce batch size, disable adaptive-kv-prefetch, or lower max_tokens. test in canary then promote.n- if quality regressions present, revert model artifact and run evaluation suite on the previous weights escalate to model steward.nnoncall playbook (summary)n1. acknowledge incident/alert and read automated incident draft.n2. verify telemetry (sums, p99, error rate) across regions using the pre-made dashboard: runtime gate active canary.n3. if automated rollback triggered: validate rollback completed and monitor metrics for 30m.n4. if no automatic rollback: decide immediate rollback vs mitigation using the guidance above.n5. post-action: create postmortem ticket and tag the change pr/adr for follow-up.nnownership and slasn- change owner: person who authored the pr is accountable until change is stable for 72h.n- runtime oncall: responsible for executing rollback and triage during the canary window.n- model steward: accountable for accuracy regressions and for approving re-rollouts after a failed canary.n- sla to customers: incidents that result in lost availability beyond the slo must be escalated to customer-success for affected tenants within 4h.nntesting and validation matrixn- unit tests: required for all changes.n- integration tests: required when request/response schema changes.n- perf tests: required for runtime-affecting changes include 3 synthetic scenarios: best-case (short prompt), worst-case (long prompt), and mixed-batch (80 short, 20 long).n- chaos tests: optional but recommended for multi-node kernel or eviction algorithm changes.nnpost-rollback analysis and preventionn- postmortem must include: root cause analysis, why gate failed to catch the issue (if applicable), improvements to telemetry or gate thresholds, and a regression test to prevent recurrence.n- if the change misclassified the contract (e.g., runtime-affecting classified as small), add an adr documenting the revised classification rule.nnappendix a ci policy template (minimal)n---ncanary_targets: us-west-2, eu-central-1ntraffic_percentage: 1nsynthetic_tests: short-prompt, long-prompt, degradation patterns (kernel stalls, kv cache thrash, numa imbalance, and soft ooms).nnwhy this existsn---------------nnredwoods runtime is highly-optimized but operates in multi-tenant, bursty actions (routing, shedding, kernel rollback, re-quantization, and temporary qos changes) under tight observability contracts.nnscopen-----nnthis manual covers:n- telemetry signals and minimal thermal/power events.n- exposes an ingest api (protobuf over grpc) with 10s aggregation windows by default.nn2) policy engine (self-heal-orch)n- consumes summarized telemetry evaluates policies (sla confluence, title: delta routing and cost-partitioning architecture for request dispatch, content: summary:nnthis document describes the delta routing and cost-partitioning architecture: a cross-cutting design that unifies request dispatch, cost attribution, and kernel scheduling signals across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. delta routing is intended to reduce tenant-visible latency spikes during heterogeneous workload mixes while enabling precise per-route/per-model cost partitioning for billing and autoscaling decisions.nngoals and non-goals:nn- goals:n - provide a deterministic dispatch policy that balances latency slos, per-token cost targets, and gpu kernel efficiency for mixed workloads.n - enable cost-partitioning signals that feed the billing pipeline and autoscaler without adding 1 p99 latency overhead.n - allow graceful degradation: automated fallback to cheaper model variants or cached responses when kernel pressure threatens slos.n- non-goals:n - replace local kernel mappers delta routing complements kernel selection but does not reimplement device-level scheduling.n - solve cold-start model loading for on-prem packages (handled by deployment bootstrap docs).nnhigh-level architecture overview:nn1) ingress and classification:n - incoming request enters the api gateway and is annotated with: model_id, route_id, client_tier, requested_max_tokens, streaming_flag, and idempotency_key when provided.n - the classifier computes a compact workload fingerprint (sequence_length_percentile, prompt_entropy_estimate, streaming_hint) used to consult local routing caches.nn2) delta router (service):n - stateless microservice running in every region/edge that decides: target-serving-pool, kernel-compatibility-tag, and cost-partition-token.n - inputs: runtime telemetry (kernel queue lengths, p50/p95/p99 at pool), model variants matrix (latency/cost profiles), tenant policy (latency slo, cost cap, allowed fallbacks).n - outputs: dispatch_decision pool, kernel_tag, priority_bucket, partition_token, fallback_reason (optional).nn3) cost partitioning and attribution:n - cost partition token is a short opaque id that flows with the request through serving runtime and is appended to usage events.n - the runtime multiplies per-token resource units by a kernel-efficiency factor (table below) before attributing to partition_token.n - partition tokens are rotated per-hour and resolved offline to human-readable cost centers to avoid per-request metadata explosion.nn4) kernel scheduling signal propagation:n - delta router writes (lightweight) scheduling hints to a shared ring buffer consumed by the kernel mapper on the gpu host. hints include priority_bucket and expected_sequence_quantiles.n - kernel mapper uses hints to pick kernel implementations and adjust slice sizes it remains authoritative for final mapping.nnpolicy heuristics and decision rules:nn- priority buckets: real-time (p99 target tenant_cost_cap and a compatible quantized variant exists with 30 and average kernel latency baseline1.5, mark pool as degraded and trigger cross-pool redistribution.nnkernel-efficiency factor table (example):nn- fp16-optimized-kernel: 1.0n- int8-q4-kernel: 0.62n- grouped-attention-shard-kernel: 0.85n- causal-seq-opt-kernel: 0.94nnthese factors are tuned from benchmarking runs and updated monthly. the runtime multiplies raw token counts by the selected factor to produce resource units for billing.nntelemetry and observability requirements:nn- delta router emits the following metrics per route and per-pool:n - router.dispatches_total (labels: route_id, pool_id, decision)n - router.fallbacks_total (labels: fallback_reason, route_id)n - router.latency_ms_bucketed (p50/p95/p99)n - router.estimated_resource_units (sum)n- traces must include the partition_token and a wire-level tracepoint at: ingress - delta-router - pool-proxy - kernel-entry.n- critical logs: any decision that chooses fallback must log tenant_id, route_id, quality_delta_estimate, and reason.nnprofiling playbook / sampling strategy (short form):nn- when deploying a new routing heuristic or updated efficiency factors, enable a 5 sample of production traffic routed to a (control) and b (candidate) for 48 hours.n- collect kernel-level spans for sampled requests with the tag sample.delta-routingtrue. store full spans for up to 7 days aggregated metrics for 90 days.n- use the local profiling cli to extract representative traces from a given pool:nn profile sampler for pool-3 between timestampsn rwt profile --pool pool-3 --from 2026-02-10t12:00z --to 2026-02-10t14:00z --tag sample.delta-routingtrue --output traces.ndjsonnnbenchmarking guidance (workload design):nn- synthesize three canonical mixes for validation:n - mix a (interactive-heavy): 70 short chat (256).n - mix b (embedding-and-batch): 50 embedding requests, 30 text generation (batchable), 20 reranking requests.n - mix c (burst-churn): repeated high-concurrency hotspots with 1s bursts every 30s to emulate plg spikes.n- metrics to record per-run: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, kernel_throughput_tokens_per_sec, gpu_utilization_by_kernel, resource_units_consumed, cold-cache_miss_rate.n- for comparative experiments, keep deploy delta isolated: run a/b for 2m tokens or 24 hours whichever is earlier.nnrunbook: pool-degradation and emergency fallback (operator steps):nn1) detection:n - pager triggers when router.fallbacks_total for a pool 5/min for 10 min or p99 latency for real-time bucket exceeds slo by 25 for 5 min.n2) quick triage (5 min):n - check router.dispatches_total to confirm increased dispatches to fallback variants.n - query kernel mapper metrics: kernel_queue_length, avg_kernel_latency, memory_pressure.n3) immediate mitigations (10 min):n - if kernel queue growth rate 40: toggle pool read-only to new requests and redirect traffic to warm standby pool. command: rwt pool set-accepting --pool pool-x --accepting falsen - if memory pressure detected (swap or oom events): scale down concurrency slots on the pool and enable aggressive kv-cache eviction: rwt pool tune --pool pool-x --concurrency 0.5 --kvcache-eviction aggressiven4) recovery actions (30120 min):n - rolling restart of gpu hosts with drain policy: follow sigterm drain (see sigterm-connection-drain-and-graceful-shutdown-playbook).n - recompute kernel-efficiency factors if a new kernel release was deployed in the previous 72 hours.n5) postmortem and action items:n - create incident with tags: delta-routing, pool-id, fallback. attach sampled traces and resource-unit time series.n - run a benchmark job that replays the incident workload under controlled conditions and propose changes to fallback thresholds.nninterplay with release process and rollout notes:nn- when releasing updates that affect the router decision logic or efficiency factors, attach the following to the release: 1) a benchmark report comparing resource_units for mix a/b/c 2) a toggled rollout plan with 5 - 25 - 50 - 100 gates and automatic rollback on p99 increase 10 3) updated profiling sampler config.nnknown caveats and edge cases:nn- cross-pool affinity churn: if a model has heavy kv-cache affinity to gpu-host a and delta router moves a chunk of concurrent sessions to pool b, cold misses will spike. mitigation: affinity-aware cost of migration is included in projected cost model prefer delayed migration for long-lived sessions.n- partition token resolution delay: offline resolution of partition tokens can lag up to 2 hours in heavy billing windows ensure customer-facing billing ui displays a preliminary estimate with note about reconciliation.n- quality cliffs on low-bit quantization: automatic fallback uses a conservative 8 quality delta threshold for sensitive routes (payment, legal) the policy must be set to disallow quantized fallbacks.nnopen design source_type: confluence, title: kv cache memory layout overview (allocator compaction), content: purposenthis page documents the serving runtimes kv cache memory layout and allocator structures, and describes the compaction-related state machines introduced in runtime 1.22. the goal is to make the kv arena behavior predictable under mixed sequence lengths and bursty churn, while keeping decode throughput stable.nnaudience: runtime engineers, kernel engineers, sres debugging tail latency/oom, and performance engineers updating benchmarks.nn---n terminologyn- kv cache: per-sequence cached key/value tensors for attention, extended incrementally during decode.n- sequence (seq): a single request stream (chat or completion) tracked by the scheduler.n- token position: decode step index within a sequence.n- page: fixed-size allocation unit in the kv arena. pages are the unit of accounting, relocation, and free-list management.n- block: a logical view of kv storage assigned to a sequence for a contiguous range of token positions implemented as one or more pages.n- arena: pre-reserved gpu memory region used for kv pages (per model profile / device).n- fragmentation: free memory exists but is split across non-adjacent page runs, increasing allocation overhead and increasing the chance of opportunistic eviction/compaction at bad times.nn---n high-level layoutnthe kv cache is stored in a gpu-resident arena allocated per device, partitioned into pages.nnkey design constraints:n1. allocation must be fast on the decode critical path (o(1) or small constant factors).n2. relocation (compaction) must be safe during concurrent decode, cancellation, and streaming.n3. the runtime must be able to attribute memory to a seq for eviction decisions and observability.nn diagram (conceptual)nnkv arena (gpu)n--------------------------------------------------------------n page 0 page 1 page 2 page 3 page 4 ... page n n--------------------------------------------------------------n used by seq a free used by seq b freenncompaction moves used pages to form longer contiguous free runs.nnn---n page and block formatn page size and alignmentn- default page size: 2 mib (profile-dependent see configuration section).n- alignment: 256 bytes minimum page base is aligned to 2 mib.n- rationale: 2 mib is a good tradeoff between allocator metadata overhead and relocation granularity it also plays well with large contiguous copies.nn what a page containsna page is a container for kv data plus a small header stored in cpu memory (metadata) and a corresponding lightweight tag stored in gpu memory for debugging/tracing.nncpu-side page metadata (per page):n- page_id (u32)n- state (enum free, allocated, relocatingsrc, relocatingdst, quarantined)n- owner_seq_id (u64 0 for free)n- owner_layer_range (small range or profile id)n- token_span (start_pos, length)n- refcount / pin_count (for pinned sessions / in-flight kernels)n- last_touched_ts (for eviction heuristics)nngpu-side tag (optional, debug builds / sampling):n- page_id, seq_id, generation (to detect stale pointers)nn block view (per sequence)neach sequence maintains a list of blocks describing where its kv lives. blocks are appended as decode progresses.nnblock fields:n- seq_idn- start_pos (token index)n- length (tokens)n- page_run (start_page, num_pages)n- layout_profile (model-specific kv stride and packing)nninvariant: for a given seq, blocks are strictly increasing in start_pos and non-overlapping.nn---n kv tensor packing within a pagenkv storage is model-profile specific but follows a consistent abstraction:nn- kv is stored per layer, per head (or grouped heads), per token position.n- the runtime uses a layout profile (resolved at model load) to compute per-token kv bytes and the page fill factor.nn layout profilesna layout profile defines:n- dtype (fp16/bf16/int8 for quantized kv where supported)n- head_dimn- num_kv_headsn- layers_per_arena_group (some models group layers across arenas)n- kv_stride_bytes (bytes per token position per layer-group)n- pack_mode (contiguous k then v or interleaved kv)nn addressing function (conceptual)ngiven (page_base, token_pos, layer, kv_head, component):n- offset token_pos kv_stride_bytes layer_offset(layer) head_offset(kv_head) component_offset(component)n- component k, vnnnotes:n- the scheduler treats pages as opaque only the attention kernels interpret the layout profile.n- compaction never changes the logical layout it only moves whole pages (or page runs) and updates block metadata.nn---n allocator structuresn arenaneach gpu device maintains one or more kv arenas:n- hosted: typically one arena per (model, quantization profile, device).n- dedicated: may allocate per pool with higher headroom to reduce eviction pressure.nnarena fields (cpu):n- base_ptr (gpu va)n- page_size_bytesn- num_pagesn- watermarks (low/high pressure thresholds)n- feature_flags (compaction enabled, eviction enabled, debug sampling)nn free list managementnwe maintain two complementary indices:n1. run-based free list: tracks contiguous free page runs for fast best fit within class allocations.n2. bitmap / page state array: tracks per-page state for correctness checks and fast scanning.nnallocation path (simplified):n1. determine required pages for requested token_span growth (rounded up).n2. attempt to allocate from a free run of sufficient length.n3. if no run available but total free pages is adequate fragmentation case (signals compaction candidate).n4. if under high pressure and compaction budget exhausted eviction may be triggered depending on tier/policy.nn fragmentation measurementnwe track fragmentation at the arena level.nndefinitions (used in metrics and guardrails):n- free_pages_totaln- largest_free_run_pagesn- fragmentation_ratio 1 - (largest_free_run_pages / max(1, free_pages_total))nninterpretation:n- 0.0 means all free pages are in one contiguous run.n- values approaching 1.0 indicate heavy fragmentation.nn---n compaction: design overviewncompaction reduces fragmentation by relocating allocated pages into lower-address regions, consolidating free space into larger contiguous runs.nnkey properties:n- incremental: bounded by a time/bytes budget to avoid decode stalls.n- safe under concurrency: respects in-flight kernels and cancellation.n- observable: exports bytes moved, time spent, stalls avoided, and correlation exemplars.nncompaction operates at the page granularity (whole pages), not individual tokens.nn---n compaction state machinesncompaction is represented by two linked state machines:n1) arena-level compaction controller (plans work and consumes budget)n2) per-page relocation lifecycle (safe movement and commit)nn 1) arena-level compaction controllernstates:n- idle: no compaction planned.n- armed: fragmentation threshold exceeded waiting for scheduler phase/budget.n- planning: identify candidate runs: destination free run (low address) source allocated pages (high address).n- relocating: execute relocation steps while budget remains.n- rebuildingfreeruns: update run lists/bitmaps for newly freed pages.n- cooldown: brief pause to avoid thrash (hysteresis).n- aborted: stop due to kill-switch, errors, or pressure changes.nntransitions (high-level):n- idle armed when fragmentation_ratio trigger and free_pages_total above minimal working set.n- armed planning at scheduler boundary (prefill end, decode batch boundary) when budget granted.n- relocating cooldown when budget consumed or no safe candidates.n- any aborted if kill-switch enabled or correctness guard triggers.nn 2) per-page relocation lifecyclenrelocation moves a pages contents from a source page to a destination page.nnstates:n- allocated: page is owned by a seq.n- relocatingsrc: source is selected pinned/refcount checked.n- relocatingdst: destination reserved and tagged.n- copyinflight: copy kernel launched (async).n- commitpending: await synchronization point where it is safe to update pointers.n- committed: block metadata updated destination becomes the new owner.n- reclaimable: source has no pins can return to free list.n- quarantined: used if an error is detected (prevents reuse until inspected).nnsafety rules:n- a page can only transition to relocatingsrc if pin_count 0 (or if pins are from known-safe phases with explicit handoff).n- commit is performed at a scheduler-managed quiescent point to avoid kernels reading old addresses.n- cancellation is handled by either (a) finishing relocation then freeing both old metadata and destination if seq ended, or (b) aborting before commit and releasing destination. see bugfix notes in runtime 1.22.1 for edge cases.nn---n scheduler integration pointsncompaction is not allowed to steal unbounded time from decode.nnbudget enforcement (see adr: compaction budgeting):n- budget is granted in bytes moved and wall time (whichever is hit first).n- the scheduler allocates budget at specific boundaries:n - after prefill, before entering steady decode batchesn - between decode micro-batches when queue depth is stablen - during backpressure handling (optional), to reduce future allocation pressurennguideline: avoid launching compaction copy kernels on the critical path when p99 latency is already elevated unless memory pressure is high.nn---n eviction interaction (tier-aware)neviction is separate from compaction but uses the same observability surface.nn- compaction is preferred when total free pages are sufficient but fragmented.n- eviction is considered when the arena is under pressure (low free pages) or when compaction cannot create a sufficiently large run within budget.nntier-aware behavior (summary):n- lower-priority tiers are eligible for eviction earlier.n- pinned sessions (explicit) are protected.n- prefix-cache pages may be marked preemptible depending on profile.nn---n configuration (runtime flags)nthis page documents the shape of configuration exact names may differ by environment.nn flag / setting default (hosted) default (dedicated) notes n------:---:---n kv.page_size_mib 2 2 profile-dependent changing requires validation. n kv.compaction.enabled true (canary-gated) true (pool-gated) kill-switch overrides. n kv.compaction.fragmentation_trigger 0.35 0.45 dedicated often tolerates more fragmentation due to headroom. n kv.compaction.max_bytes_per_step 256mib 512mib upper bound per scheduler-granted step. n kv.compaction.max_ms_per_step 2ms 3ms target to avoid p99 regressions. n kv.compaction.cooldown_ms 50ms 50ms prevent thrashing. n kv.eviction.enabled true true policy is tier-aware lru by seq. nnoperational note: oncall should prefer flipping kv.compaction.enabledfalse before disabling eviction if correctness is suspected see runbook for ordering.nn---n observability hooksnmetrics and trace spans are mandatory for rollout.nncore metrics (names standardized elsewhere):n- kv_fragmentation_ratio (gauge)n- kv_free_pages_total (gauge)n- kv_largest_free_run_pages (gauge)n- kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total (counter)n- kv_compaction_time_ms_total (counter)n- kv_compaction_steps_total (counter)n- kv_compaction_aborts_total (counter)n- kv_evictions_totalreason,tier (counter)nntracing:n- kv.compaction.plan spann- kv.compaction.copy span (includes bytes, src/dst page ids sampled)n- kv.compaction.commit spann- kv.eviction.select spannnrequired dashboards:n- fragmentation ratio over time with p95/p99 latency overlayn- bytes moved steps per minuten- evictions per minute by tier and reasonnn---n correctness invariants and guardrailsn invariantsn- a page is owned by at most one seq at a time (owner_seq_id is single-valued).n- a block references only pages in allocated or relocatingdst state (during commit).n- no page can be freed while pinned.n- commit is atomic from the schedulers perspective: either the seq sees old pages or new pages, never a partial mix for a given token span.nn guardrailsn- quarantine any page involved in a failed relocation until inspected.n- if repeated aborts occur (e.g., n per minute), automatically reduce compaction aggressiveness and alert.n- if p99 latency increases beyond canary threshold while compaction bytes moved spikes, trigger automated rollback (see sre guardrails page).nn---n faqnwhy move whole pages instead of compacting within a page?npage-level movement keeps attention kernels and layout profiles simple and avoids per-token repacking, while still addressing allocator fragmentation (the dominant contributor to tail spikes under churn).nndoes compaction change output quality?nno. it does not change numeric operations it only changes where kv resides in gpu memory.nnwhats the most common operational failure mode?naggressive compaction budgets can introduce additional copy work and scheduling interference, showing up as p99 spikes during bursts. the rollout defaults favor stability tuning should be validated in benchmark-lab and perf-canary.nn---n changelogn- 2026-02-20: updated state machine definitions clarified commit/quiescent worse by 8 absolute or 15 relative.n - throughput (tokens/sec per gpu slot) not worse by 6.n - kernel_error_rate stays below 0.1 and does not increase 2x baseline.n - cost-per-token (in -equivalent) minutes and continuously):n - latency: short-req p95 within allowed delta.n - error counts: kernel_dispatcher_errors_total must be steady or declining.n - cpu/gpu saturation: no node exceeds 92 sustained gpu utilization for 10m.n - kv miss spikes: no jump 3x baseline.n5) rollback policy: immediate rollback if any automated gate fails or on-call requests rollback.nnrelease notes and
