dsid_a457b9210ea3427c923339f822aee6e3, source_type: confluence, title: execution profile registry and live reconfiguration playbook, content: summarynnthis page describes the execution profile registry (epr) a central runtime component that captures workload execution profiles, exposes them to scheduling and kernel-selection layers, and enables safe live reconfiguration of scheduling, batching, and kernel parameters based on telemetry signals. the document is a combined design operational playbook: architecture, data model, decision logic, safety gates, rollout checklist, and incident runbook.nnwhy this existsnn- serving workloads show high variability (sequence length, user-level burstiness, cache hit-rate). static scheduler configs produce avoidable cost and tail latency.n- epr lets runtime components subscribe to a canonical, versioned set of execution profiles derived from production telemetry and experiment signals.n- operators can use epr to perform targeted live reconfiguration (e.g., batch-slice size, kernel variant selection, kvcache-prefetch policy) while maintaining slos and safe rollback.nngoals and non-goalsnngoalsn1. provide a single source-of-truth for workload execution characteristics and policy hints.n2. enable deterministic, auditable live reconfiguration with automated safety checks.n3. allow fast, low-risk rollout of kernel/scheduler parameter changes and targeted rollbacks.nnnon-goalsn- not a full replacement for the offline autotune pipeline used for model-quantization recommendations.n- not intended to perform global topology changes (e.g., replacing a gpu class) epr operates at request-routing scheduler/kernal level.nnhigh-level architecturenncomponentsn- telemetry ingestors: stream samplers that emit signals into trace metric pipelines (per-request timing, kernel durations, kvcache hit/miss, batch sizes).n- profile builder service: periodically aggregates telemetry into candidate execution profiles (eps). runs feature extraction: seq_len distribution, token-per-request histogram, typical kv cache reuse entropy, tail-latency percentiles, priority-mix.n- execution profile registry (epr): versioned store of profiles and policy hints (json documents). supports read-by-name, read-by-tag, and snapshot-by-commit. exposes an http api and a lightweight grpc endpoint for fast reads.n- reconfig controller: evaluates eps against slo rules and rollout policies issues configuration update bundles to the scheduler agent and kernel agent.n- safety evaluator: canary/shadow judge service that tests a candidate bundle against traffic samples in a controlled environment and reports regressions.nndata flow (described)n1. ingestors collect sampled traces and metrics (default sampling 0.1 for full traces 5 lightweight metrics).n2. profile builder produces candidate eps on a configurable cadence (default: every 4 hours).n3. operator or automated policy promotes a candidate ep to active version in epr.n4. reconfig controller creates a rollout plan (canary percentage, duration, rollback triggers) and pushes bundles to a target cells scheduler agent.n5. safety evaluator monitors canary traffic if triggers are observed, the reconfig controller halts rollout and initiates rollback.nnexecution profile model (canonical json fields)nn- profile_id: string (versionable)n- tags: string (e.g., interactive, long-seq, high-cache-reuse)n- seq_len_pct: stringified histogram reference idn- median_tokens: string (number)n- p95_latency_ms: string (number)n- kvcache_reuse_rate: string (0.0-1.0)n- typical_batch_shape: string (e.g., 1,2,1,4)n- kernel_hints: string (ordered list of preferred kernel variant ids)n- scheduler_hints: string (e.g., prefer-small-batches, aggressive-concurrency)n- safe_rollback_signature: string (hash of pre-change probe results)nnnote: the epr json schema is intentionally flat so runtime agents can do cheap json parsing. each field above is represented as strings or arrays of strings to simplify cross-language clients.nnmapping profiles to runtime decisionsnn- kernel selection: kernel agent queries epr with current routeprofile tag. epr returns kernel_hints starting from low-precision fast variants if kvcache_reuse_rate 0.7 and median_tokens 0.5 and p95_latency_ms 10 to accommodate transient spike.n- observability hooks: tracing and metric sampling level bumped to capture an additional 0.5 trace samples for rollout duration.nnsafety evaluator experimentsnnuse two experiment modes:n- shadow-run (no impact): run candidate kernel on shadowed replicas for sampled requests and compare outputs/latency.n- canary-run: route x of real traffic to canary fleet with full observability.nnmanual and automated rolloutsnnrollout policy example (reconfig controller yaml):nnyamlnprofile_id: epr-2026-11ncanary:n steps:n - percent: 1n duration: 10mn - percent: 5n duration: 30mn - percent: 20n duration: 60mn - percent: 100n duration: 10mnrollback_triggers:n p95_latency_increase_pct: 2n error_rate_increase_abs: 0.005n gpu_memory_pressure_pct: 85nmonitoring:n extra_trace_sampling: 0.5n dashboard: /dashboards/epr-rolloutnnnoperational runbook: quick steps to apply a profilenn1. validate candidate ep in the staging profile builder ui (check histograms and kernel hints).n2. run safety evaluator in shadow mode for 2,000 sampled requests.n3. create rollout plan in reconfig controller and set canary steps.n4. kick off canary. monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, gpu utilization, and cost-estimated token-per-second.n5. if any rollback trigger fires, invoke reconfig controller - automated rollback. if not, proceed to next step until 100.n6. after full rollout, schedule a stabilization window (default 24 hours) before allowing further epr changes for the same route.nntroubleshooting and triage matrixnnsymptom: p95 increases by 3 during canaryn- immediate action: rollback to previous epr version.n- investigation: compare kernel duration traces, look for shifts in batch sizes, check kvcache reuse telemetry.n- postmortem items: add a synthetic replay benchmark summarynnthis playbook defines how the runtime produces per-request provenance and cost-attribution records and how teams should use those signals to investigate fidelity regressions, quantify unit economics, and support billing/chargeback for dedicated/private deployments. it bridges kernel scheduling telemetry, kv cache instrumentation, model variant metadata, token accounting, and accelerator utilization.nnscopenn- applies to all requests processed by the inference serving runtime (hosted, dedicated, private).n- covers the attribution pipeline from request start to final token emission (including fallbacks and partial responses).n- excludes offline training/compilation jobs and batch-only offline analytics (those have separate costing).nngoalsnn1. produce a stable, compact per-request attribution record in energy_coeff, base_latency_ms, price_coeff. teams must version updates and include migration notes.nn- example cost coefficients (illustrative):n source coefficient example unit comment n-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------n model_token_prompt 0.00035 micro per token prompt tokens cheaper n model_token_completion 0.00080 micro per token completion tokens more n kernel_price_coeff 0.12 micro per ms multiply by wall_ms n gpu_power_coeff 0.00003 micro per watt-ms used for energy estimatesnnrunbook: investigate a high-cost or fidelity-regression requestnn1. find request: query the attribution index by request_id or tenant/time window. example kibana query:n- request_id:r_01e9yx5j or (tenant_id:t-acme and @timestamp:now-1h to now)nn2. inspect top-level fields: model_id, kernel_profile, gpu_ms, kvcache_hits. if estimated_cost_micros baseline estimate, continue.nn3. check scheduling and admission logs: verify queue_wait_ms and preemption_events. if queue_wait_ms 50ms, escalate to sre (page on-call).nn4. validate model variant: confirm model_version and quantization_profile. if fidelity_taglow or fallback sequence contains distilled or quantized-fallback, open a fidelity regression ticket and attach the attribution payload.nn5. reproduce in sandbox: use the request-replay tool with preserved rng and decision overrides to force the same kernel and cache paths. command example:nn replay tool (developer sandbox)nredwood-replay --request r_01e9yx5j --preserve-routing --force-cache-prefetchnn6. if kernel wall times dominate, run the microbenchmark for the identified kernel on matching hardware (ref: benchmarking/kernel-microbench-runbook).nn7. if kvcache misses are unexpectedly high, follow kvcache warmup checklist: verify shard placement, prefetch hints, and session-affinity.nnpolicies and thresholdsnn- attribution latency: target 1000 records/min over target, open a capacity incident. owner: telemetry-team.n- fidelity alerts: emit an automatic alert when fallback rate for a model-version exceeds 2 for 30m rolling window. owner: runtime-ml-product.n- cost drift: trigger a cost-anomaly signal when tenant-level per-token cost deviates 20 vs previous 72h. owner: billing-ops.nndata retention and privacynn- attribution records are retained 90 days in hot storage, 2 years in compressed cold storage.n- records may contain prompt_token counts but not prompt text in hosted mode private deployments may opt-in to richer payloads.n- sensitive tenant identifiers should be hashed for analytics exports. see /security-and-compliance/data-management for procedures.nnrollout checklist for the attribution pipelinenn1. unit tests for kernel hinting translation and cost math.n2. integration test: ingest 1k synthetic requests across concurrency shapes and validate sum(est_costs) measured billing samples within 5.n3. canary: enable attribution at 1 of traffic with sidecar publish to test index monitor attribution-latency and mismatch-rate.n4. gradual ramp: 1 - 5 - 25 - 100 over 48 hours with manual signoffs.nnconsumer integration patternsnn- billing: consume estimated_cost_micros on a per-tenant aggregation schedule (hourly). keep a reconciliation process between estimated_cost_micros and actual metered gpu-hours (weekly).n- optimize: use per-request kernel footprints to suggest quantization profiles and batching knobs for the tenant.n- sre: correlate attribution records with trace ids and kernel traces for incident correlation.nnoperational ownership and contactsnn- runtime telemetry pipeline: telemetry-team (oncall: contract and runbook, content: summaryn-------nthis document defines the fidelity orchestrator: a small, horizontally scalable control plane that uses live telemetry to decide kernel selection, execution fidelity, and degradation policies for inference requests. it contains the architecture overview, required telemetry contract (metrics/events), a deterministic decision flow, operational runbook for incidents, rollout checklists, and example policy snippets. the goal is predictable slo adherence (latency/cost/quality) while enabling safe, measurable degradation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.nnaudiencen--------n- runtime engineers (owners, oncall)n- kernel/scheduler teamn- sre and observabilityn- product owners for latency/cost tradeoffsnnproblem statementn-----------------nthe runtime must route requests to optimal kernel variants and execution fidelities (full precision / quantized / reduced context / cached) without violating slos. decisions must be based on standardized telemetry so they are auditable, testable, and reversible. historically we saw oscillation when metrics lacked determinism and when fallback policies were underspecified.nncomponentsn----------n- fidelity-orchestrator (service name): stateless control plane exposing a grpc decision api (/v1/decide) and an http health endpoint.n- telemetry-ingest: stream aggregator that normalizes kernel and queue metrics and writes to the telemetry stream used by the orchestrator.n- decision-cache: fast in-memory cache (per-node) to keep recent decision results for identical signatures (ttl 30s).n- policy-store: versioned policy repository (git-backed) with json policy files and canary rollout capability.nnarchitecture overviewn---------------------nflow (simplified):n1) request arrives at request-router with attributes: model_id, route, token_budget, interactive_flag, tenant_tier, seq_len_estimate.n2) router forwards request to serving-runtime and asks fidelity-orchestrator: decide(request_signature, current_node_telemetry).n3) orchestrator evaluates the policy with the telemetry snapshot and returns kernel_hint, exec_fidelity, fallback_chain.n4) serving runtime applies hint and continues decision cached locally for matching signatures.nncontract: required metrics eventsn-----------------------------------nall producing services must emit the following keys (metric names are canonical):nn- kernel_latency_p50, kernel_latency_p95, kernel_latency_p99 (ms) per kernel variant, 10s sliding windown- kernel_qps (rps) per kernel variantn- kvcache_hit_ratio per model-shard, 1m windown- request_queue_depth per node, per queue-classn- outstanding_tokens_per_session gaugen- token_cost_estimate_per_model (nanos) model-level estimate for cost accountingn- recently_throttled (bool/event) indicates prior admission throttles in last 30sn- node_cpu_pct, node_gpu_mem_free_mb node health indicatorsn- model_quality_regressions (event) evaluation flag from optimize that can block aggressive quantizationnntelemetry delivery semantics:n- aggregation window: 10s for kernel latencies, 1m for kvcache and qps.n- max ingestion lag: 5s orchestrator must tolerate up to 10s stale snapshots but should annotate decisions with snapshot_age.n- cardinality: metrics must include labels: model_id, kernel_variant, zone, tenant_tier.nndecision rules (simplified)n---------------------------n1) if request.interactive_flag true and token_budget baseline_min_tokens (default 16) then prefer low-latency kernels if kernel_latency_p99 eviction_threshold (default 800mb).n2) if kvcache_hit_ratio 0.6 and a cached_execution_variant exists, prefer cached path to reduce per-token cost (tie-breaker: if kernel_qps 90), select degraded_fidelity (reduce batch-size, smaller kernel, or quantized variant) and set degrade_reason tag.nnpolicy expressionsn------------------npolicies are stored in policy-store as json. example (illustrative):nnn id: policy/interactive-default/v1,n conditions: n name: is_interactive, expr: request.interactive_flag true,n name: p99_ok, expr: telemetry.kernel_latency_p99 40 for common interactive signaturesnnrunbook: incidents mitigationn--------------------------------ndetection (automated alerts):n- alert a1: decision_api_p99_latency 50ms for 5m (sev-2)n- alert a2: unexpected_jump_in_degradation_rate 5 in 10m (sev-1 when 20 tenant-impact)n- alert a3: policy-validation-failures during rollout 1 per deploy (sev-2)nnimmediate steps for sev-1 (high-impact degradation):n1) pager to runtime-oncall and kernel-owner (see ownership table below).n2) run: curl -ss jq . check last_reloaded_policy and decision_latency_ms.n3) if decision latency is high: switch router to bypass-orchestrator mode (router flag: --bypass-fidelity). this will pick safe defaults and fall back to serving runtime local heuristics. see section bypass mode.n4) if excessive degradation is due to policy change (identified by last_reloaded_policy matching recent commit), rollback policy via policy-store: git revert and post /v1/policies/reload.n5) if telemetry missing/stale: restart telemetry-ingest service and inspect ingestion lag (kafka consumer offset). command: kubectl -n observability logs deploy/telemetry-ingest -c consumer tail -n 200.n6) post-incident: create an incident report with traces (decision_id list), affected tenants, and action items.nnbypass mode (safe default, fallthrough)n--------------------------------------n- behavior: router skips orchestrator and uses serving-runtime heuristics:n - default_kernel: kernel-lowlatency-safe-v1n - exec_fidelity: balancedn - quota_enforcement: unchangedn- safe rollout: bypass is temporary and logged with reason. router automatically re-enables orchestrator if decision api healthy for 3 consecutive 10s windows.nnownership contactsn--------------------n- fidelity orchestrator service owner: runtime-control-plane (team alias)n- primary oncall rotation: runtime-sren- kernel owner (low-latency kernels): kernel-scheduling teamn- observability: telemetry-platformnnconfig table (key, default, description)n---------------------------------------n key default description n decision_api_timeout_ms 25 grpc client timeout for router - orchestrator n decision_cache_ttl_s 30 ttl for local decision cache n interactive_p99_target_ms 150 interactive p99 latency slo n kvcache_cached_variant_cutoff 0.6 min kvcache_hit_ratio to prefer cached path n policy_canary_pct 5 percent traffic to canary during policy rollout nnrollout change managementn---------------------------n- policy changes must be checked into policy-store with a pr and two approvers: one from kernel-scheduling and one from runtime-sre.n- canary rollout: set policy_canary_pct and gradually increase per the automated canary job. metric gates:n - no increase in tenant_error_rate 0.1n - decision_api_p99_latency within 10 of baselinen - degradation_rate 800n action:n kernel_hint: kernel-lowlatency-v2n exec_fidelity: balancednndebugging checklistn-------------------n1) inspect decision trace for the request_id: curl check telemetry snapshot age attached to the decision. if 10s, prioritize fixing telemetry-ingest.n3) validate policy against schema: ./tools/policy-validate missing metric instrumentation.n- add a unit test to policy ci for any edge-case that caused oscillation.n- adjust canary gates to include the newly-observed signal if missing.nnappendix: example trace annotation (json)n----------------------------------------nn decision_id: uuid-xxxx,n policy_id: policy/interactive-default/v1,n snapshot_age_ms: 4200,n telemetry_keys_used: kernel_latency_p99,kvcache_hit_ratio,node_gpu_mem_free_mb,n score_explain: selected lowlatency kernel: p99 120ms preempt_ack - slice_complete.n- hedging windows: for latency-sensitive traffic we allow speculative hedging to a cold-compatible kernel only if the primary dispatch exceeds hedging_threshold_ms (default 60ms). hedged requests are recorded with hedgedtrue tag.n- admission shaping: dispatcher computes an slo delta per request type (normal/interactive/burst) and emits admission hints to the scheduler via a compact admission hint proto. admission hints are soft the scheduler is authoritative.nnprofiling hooks and observability contractn- minimal trace span set per request: front_door - dispatch.enqueued - dispatch.dequeued - kernel.schedule - kernel.exec - model.kvlookup - response.serialize - response.flush. each span must include the following attributes: request_id, tenant_id, model_id, sequence_length, token_count, kernel_variant, kernel_gpu_id.n- sampling strategy: default p01 for full traces, dynamic increase to 10 during degraded signals, and targeted 100 sampling for requests with fallback_count0.n- kernel-level counters required: kernel_dispatch_count, kernel_dispatch_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, kernel_preempt_count, kernel_oom_events, kernel_retry_count.n- continuous profiling hook: every worker exposes a /debug/profile endpoint returning a compact profile envelope (cpu, gpu kernel stats, active batches snapshot) compatible with the runtime lab tooling.nnbenchmarking guidance (how to validate surface changes)n1) local microbench: use bench-runner --profile-kernel to execute synthetic short and long sequence profiles. use provided corpus under /test-corpus/runtime/fidelity/ for realistic token distribution.n2) shadow benchmarks: mirror 10 of production traffic (low-risk tenants) to the canary kernel build. compare p50/p95/p99 and fallback rates.n3) slo regression check: any kernel change must not increase p95 by 5 at target throughput or increase fallback-rate by 1pp.n4) cost envelope: report per-token cost delta using cost-estimator v2 with the same traffic shape.nnrelease checklist for scheduler/kernel changesn1) update scheduler unit tests and deterministic replay fixtures.n2) run local microbench and post artifacts.n3) run shadow benchmark for at least 24 hours against production-shaped traffic.n4) verify observability hooks present and sampled traces are linked to request ids.n5) bump canary to 1 then 10 then 50 controlled rollout with health gates: kernel_dispatch_latency_p95, kernel_oom_events, fallback_rate.n6) document new config knobs with default values and risks in the change description.nnknown issues and mitigations (operationally actionable)n- issue: oscillating preemption chatter when many small interactive requests interleave with large batches.n mitigation: enable preemption_holdoff_ms (default 10ms) that blocks new preemptions for a short cooling window after a preemption event. if oscillation persists, increase preemption_suppression_factor and throttle interactive admission.nn- issue: kvcache warmup races causing model-ready to report false readiness when weights are present but kv warmup incomplete.n mitigation: model-loader must expose two booleans: weights_ready and warmup_complete. the routing policy uses warmup_complete when serving low-latency tiers for best-effort tiers, weights_ready suffices.nn- issue: speculative hedging spikes extra gpu tail usage during sudden p99 latency events.n mitigation: cap concurrent_hedge_runs_per_gpu to a conservative value (default 4) and enable hedging_adaptive_backoff that reduces hedging when gpu_utilization85.nnrunbooks (short, playbook style)n1) slow p95 kernel schedule (oncall guide)n- trigger: kernel_schedule_latency_p95 target for 10m and fallback_rate increased.n- steps: a) check kernel health dashboard (top kernels by latency). b) inspect recent traces for heavy long sequence batches look for kernel_variant mismatch. c) if a new kernel variant was deployed target 1.25 for 5m.n- kernel_oom_events: alert on 1 event per 10m per node.n- fallback_rate: alert if 1 across fleet for runtime-topology-stability-index-and-degradation-simulation-2027, content: overviewn-------nthis page defines our runtime topology stability index (rtsi), the accompanying degradation simulation framework, and operational playbooks for using these signals to guide kernel scheduling decisions, profiling campaigns, and benchmark validation. the goal is to provide a reproducible method for quantifying how a runtime topology (sharding, kv cache layout, kernel variants, and scheduler policies) reacts to progressive stress and to capture early warnings before user-visible slo degradation.nnwhy this existsn - we frequently ship scheduler and kernel changes that affect tail latency and fidelity in subtle ways unit tests and microbenchmarks are insufficient.n - rtsi provides a single, actionable score tied to observability signals and a simulation harness to stress topologies in controlled ways.n - the output informs rollout gating: canaries, weighted rollouts, and automated fallback thresholds in the router.nnscopen - applies to all hosted and dedicated runtime topologies. private deployments should re-run the simulation with local traffic shapes.n - focuses on inference-serving concerns: latency quantiles, error rates, memory pressure, shard-eviction churn, kernel-failure propagation, and kv cache warmup dynamics.nndefinitionsn - topology: placement of model shards, kv cache shards, and scheduler domains across gpus and nodes.n - rtsi: scalar 0100 where 100 is fully stable under synthetic and replayed traffic stress lower scores indicate increasing instability.n - degradation mode: class of graceful-fallback or failure (e.g., soft-fidelity degradation, eviction storm, kernel stall).nnrtsi design and signalsn----------------------nrtsi is computed from a weighted aggregation of normalized signals collected during a simulation run:n1) latency head/tail scores (p50, p95, p99) directionally prioritized to penalize tail shifts.n2) error amplification factor rate of increased 5xx/response-timeouts vs baseline.n3) eviction churn index rate of kv/shard evictions per minute and the time-to-warm (cold-hit penalty).n4) kernel slip events frequency of kernel slow-path engagements and soft-fallback triggers.n5) cross-cohort interference latency correlation coefficient across tenant cohorts.n6) recovery velocity time for metrics to return to baseline after load drop or mitigation (seconds).nnweighting and normalizationn - default weights: tail latency (0.35), error amplification (0.20), eviction churn (0.15), kernel slip (0.15), cohort interference (0.10), recovery velocity (0.05).n - signals are normalized to 0..1 where 0 is worst-case observed in historical incidents and 1 is baseline. rtsi 100 weighted_sum(normalized_signals).n - the weight set is configurable per release changes must be reviewed with sre and runtime leads.nndegradation simulation framework (how to run)n-------------------------------------------npurpose: execute deterministic experiments combining synthetic bursts and replayed production traces to surface interaction effects across layers (scheduler, kernel, cache).nprereqs:n - access to the simulation harness (git: infra/runtime-sim) and a small cluster configured with the topology under test.n - an anonymized request trace (see trace-redaction-playbook) or the synthetic suite.n - baseline golden metrics for the model/sequence distribution.nnquick run (smoke):n1) checkout infra/runtime-sim@stable and configure experiment.yaml (example below).n2) start cluster: ./scripts/sim-cluster up --topology topology.json --nodes 4n3) load baseline: ./scripts/load-baseline --trace traces/golden-corpus.json n4) run progressive storm: ./scripts/run-storm --burst-factor 3 --duration 600 --cohorts 3n5) collect artifacts: ./scripts/collect-artifacts --out /tmp/sim-outputn6) compute rtsi: python tools/compute_rtsi.py --input /tmp/sim-output --weights config/weights.yamlnnexample experiment.yaml:n name value n experiment_name rtsi-sanity-2027 n topology_file topologies/4node-nonuniform.json n trace traces/median-length-100.json n burst_pattern step(1,3,30m) n scheduler_profile econ-priority-governor-v2 n kernel_variants tf32, int8-fallback nnkernel-scheduling interaction checklistn--------------------------------------nwhen scheduling policy changes are proposed, run the following minimal checklist against rtsi:n1) local pressure test: simulate single-node degradation and measure eviction churn and kernel slip.n2) cross-node blast: multi-cohort ramp to expose interference.n3) fallback exercise: intentionally trigger a kernel slow-path and validate graceful fallback latency bound.n4) canary schedule: run weighted rollout simulation with 5/25/70 split and verify rtsi delta 85 for low-risk backports.n - release gates run extended sims (26 hours) on release branches failures (rtsi delta 10 vs baseline) block signoff.n - benchmark artifacts include an artifacts manifest with: topology.json, scheduler_policy.yaml, kernel_build_hash, raw traces, and computed rtsi report.nnrelease notes and versioningn---------------------------nwhen a runtime change modifies scheduling or kernels, release notes must include:n - rtsi baseline and delta observed in extended sim runs.n - kernel variant compatibility table and roll-forward/rollback instructions.n - recommended canary matrix (percentages, duration, slos to watch).n - any config toggles to delay rollout (feature flags) and their default state.nnknown issues and interpretationsn-------------------------------nwe surface deterministic patterns that should not be treated as immediate blockers but require follow-up: n - eviction ripple: small increases in eviction rate that grow over minutes indicate mis-sized kv partitions. triage: re-evaluate shard sizing and prefetch hints.n - kernel slip noise: intermittent slow-path entries isolated to particular tensor shapes. triage: add microbench for the shape and consider kernel specialization.n - inter-cohort correlated tails: events where a small tenant induces p99 increases across unrelated cohorts typically scheduler admission quanta or quota shaping misconfig.nnoperational runbooks (step-by-step)n---------------------------------nrunbook a: rtsi regression detected during cin1) abort the merge and alert runtime-sre@redwood.n2) attach artifacts manifest and full sim output to the ticket.n3) triage: run quick delta profiler (scripts/quick-delta) to localize to scheduler/kernel/cache.n4) if kernel suspected, run kernel smoke on microbench harness and isolate commit.n5) if scheduler suspected, revert policy or reduce canary weight and re-run sim.n6) update the release notice with root cause and mitigation.nnrunbook b: production tail-latency spike suspected to match simulation signaturen1) toggle circuit-breaker: route traffic to fallback model-variant.n2) open incident, tag with simulation label and link to last successful rtsi run.n3) run targeted replay for the last 10 minutes using production trace sampler.n4) if rtsi-like signature reproduced, follow kernel rollback path.n5) if not reproduced, escalate to sre/runtime-engineering for deeper tracing.nnownership and governancen-----------------------n - primary owner: runtime architecture (runtime-arch@redwood).n - sre for policy: eng-sre (oncall rotation).n - profiling and kernel analysis: performance and applied ml teams.n - changes to rtsi formula or default weights require: runtime-arch eng-sre perf signoff.nnappendix a example weight file (config/weights.yaml)n---n weights.yamlntail_latency: dsid_d7bebcab205f4c848593d521a6afacf1, source_type: confluence, title: fidelity taxonomy scheduler interop matrix - operational manual, content: overviewnnpurposenthis document defines a pragmatic fidelity taxonomy (how we describe and measure request/response fidelity in the runtime), and a scheduler interoperability matrix that maps fidelity targets to scheduler behaviors and required telemetry hooks. it consolidates operational runbooks for diagnosing fidelity regressions, guidance for kernel scheduling policy authors, and benchmarking protocols used to validate fidelity-preserving changes.nnscopen- applies to all inference traffic served by the runtime (hosted, dedicated, private).n- focuses on single-request fidelity (decoding fidelity, model variant fidelity, prompt-preserve semantics) and cohort-level fidelity (consistency across canaries, shadow cohorts).n- does not replace model-eval quality pipelines but complements them with runtime-level observability and mitigations.nnwhy this mattersn- we often trade throughput/cost for fidelity. without a shared vocabulary and clear scheduler contracts, teams make inconsistent changes that cause subtle quality regressions. this manual makes those tradeoffs explicit and operationally testable.nndefinitions and fidelity levelsn1) fidelity levels (business-oriented):n - fidelity:high match-to-model output semantics minimal decoding truncation, full kv cache warm, deterministic tokenization path, 99th-percentile quality invariants verified by shadow evals.n - fidelity:standard non-critical latency optimizations allowed (small batch fusion, soft-quantization fallbacks), acceptable for most consumer-facing services.n - fidelity:economy aggressive cost controls (low-precision kernels, higher batching, prefix elision), intended for bulk processing where micro-quality differences are acceptable.n - fidelity:best_effort degraded mode used during capacity pressure or partial failure best-effort fallback to compatible model variant with explicit response metadata.nn2) observability primitives (signals we require)n - fidelity_label (string): one of the fidelity levels above (attached to request).n - kernel_profile (string): kernel variant used (e.g., stable-tc64, quant-r2).n - kvcache_state (enum): warmpartialcold.n - decode_path_flags (set): includes token-truncation, temperature-clamp, sampling-mode.n - quality_shadow_score (float): periodic shadow-eval score (0..1) when enabled.nnscheduler interop matrix (text table)ncolumns: fidelity_label admission_policy kernel_preference prefetch_hint fallthrough_policy telemetry_requiredn- fidelity:high strict admission (single-request slots) prefer full-precision, deterministic kernels pre-warm kv prefix pin fail open with immediate rollback to canary kvcache_state, decode_path_flags, kernel_profile, quality_shadow_scoren- fidelity:standard balanced admission (slot-sharing allowed) mixed-precision allowed with quality gate opportunistic prefetch degrade-by-quantize w/ warning kernel_profile, kvcache_state, admission_latencyn- fidelity:economy aggressive admission (batch aggregation, deferred slots) prefer quantized/low-precision kernels no prefetch, batch-prefetch only fallback to cheaper model variant kernel_profile, batch_size_histogram, cost_estimate_tokenn- fidelity:best_effort best-effort admission (background slots) any compatible kernel no prefetch tag response with fidelitybest_effort and reason kernel_profile, eviction_events, failure_causennscheduling policy author guidancen- fidelity:standardn probability: 0.05nn- policies must include an explicit fallback route or fallthrough policy when the chosen kernel or capacity is unavailable.n- when adding a new kernel variant, update the interop matrix and include a microbenchmark that exercises the fidelity-sensitive prompt set.nnprofiling playbook for fidelity regressionsn1) rapid triage (015 min)n 1. isolate affected routes by checking fidelity_label in recent traces.n 2. pull kernel_profile and kvcache_state histograms for the route over the last 60 minutes.n 3. if quality_shadow_score dropped 5 vs baseline, open a p0 incident and attach the shadow-eval corpus.nn2) deeper investigation (15180 min)n 1. run a targeted synthetic replay of failing prompts against the candidate kernel variants using the replay harness.n 2. compare decoding artifacts: tokenization diffs, truncation flags, and final-length distributions.n 3. check scheduler admission logs for unusual batching or coalescing events.nn3) remediation (post 3 hours)n 1. if a kernel regression is responsible, roll kernel to previous stable via the kernel-rollout tool and execute canary smoke checks.n 2. if admission policy caused harmful batching, temporarily tighten admission mode for the route and schedule a follow-up to analyze long-term capacity.n 3. apply a temporary traffic-split to route a small percentage to a high-fidelity variant while investigation continues.nnrunbook: canonical commands and scriptsn- pull recent traces for route: curl -s console_url/api/traces?route/v1/generate/summaryfrom-1h jq .n- kernel histogram: quality_shadow_score, 95th decode-time, token-length-distribution, perplexity-delta vs gold-model.n 3. pass criteria: quality_shadow_score within 1.5 of baseline for high/std within 6 for economy.n 4. conversational/stateful sessions to survive eviction, migration, and kernel-level preemption while minimizing memory and latency overhead. the spec covers data formats, storage contracts, scheduler interactions, profiling signals to monitor, benchmark tests to prove cost/latency trade-offs, and a runnable incident playbook for recovery.nngoalsn- minimize user-visible latency when reviving an evicted session (target: 95th percentile revival ,n slice_index: ,n model: ,n seq_range: ,,n created_at: ,n kernel_hint: ,n affinity_hint: n n- binary blob: optimized, compressed kv-delta small decoder-state table. blob layout includes a small crc32 and lz4 compression. the revival path validates crc before load.nn3) storage tiers and consistencyn- ephemeral tier (fast): memory-backed lru cache co-located with the slices active host (store name: session-slice-cache). ttl default: 5 minutes.n- durable tier (cold): a regional object store (store name: session-checkpoints), retention default: 30 days for dedicated customers, 7 days for hosted default.n- write policy: write-through to ephemeral tier synchronously, enqueue background upload to durable tier. on background upload failures the slice-manager retries with exponential backoff failures are surfaced to metrics.nn4) eviction and revival policyn- eviction triggers: memory pressure signals, kernel preemption, node decommission, scaling down. when eviction is decided, the slice is pinned and the slice-manager emits a checkpoint creation event.n- revival flow: client request hits routing layer - routing checks session metadata - if session not resident, routing invokes revival agent - revival agent fetches checkpoint from ephemeral tier (fallback to durable) - validates and streams kv-deltas to kernel-dispatcher using the warmstart api - kernel acknowledges reconstructed prefix - request proceeds.n- fallback semantics: if checkpoint not found or corrupted, the revival agent constructs a degraded session with best-effort prefix (last n tokens in user-visible transcript) and annotates the response with a telemetry flag trace.revival.degradedtrue.nnkernel scheduling interactionsn- warmstart handshake: kernel-dispatcher exposes warmstart endpoints that accept a slice_id, kernel_hint, and resume token. warmstart operations are prioritized into a separate scheduling lane with admission limits to avoid blocking new short-lived requests.n- preemption coordination: schedulers must not preempt an in-flight warmstart unless safe-checks pass. safe-checks include ensuring the revived kv-cache has been persisted to ephemeral tier and that no concurrent write is ongoing.n- admission controls and credits: revival lanes consume kernel-credit units at a 2x weight vs steady inference tokens for the first 50ms to reflect the higher gpu work to reconstruct kv-cache. this weight decays after successful warmstart.nnprofiling and observability playbookn- signals to capture for each slice lifecycle: slice.create.latency, slice.upload.duration, slice.fetch.latency(ephemeral), slice.fetch.latency(durable), slice.validation.failures, revival.handshake.latency, revival.fidelity-flag, revival.memory-overhead.n- trace correlation: include tags session_id, slice_index, kernel_id, request_id to enable end-to-end reconstruction of a revival path in a single apm span.n- sampling policy: sample 100 of failed revivals and 1 of successful revivals. for high-sla customers sample 5 of successful revivals.n- profiling recipe (step-by-step):n 1. reproduce a node eviction in the staging cluster with a mix of slice sizes.n 2. collect full traces for the affected session_ids and kernel dispatch logs.n 3. measure revival.handshake.latency distribution and correlate with kernel_hint and slice size.n 4. verify crc and decompression time dominates or not. if crc 20ms, investigate i/o or cpu noise.nnbenchmarking suite and acceptance criterian- bench types: micro (single-slice create/fetch), integration (eviction revival under steady traffic), stress (mass eviction under bursty traffic), fidelity (regression tests against ground-truth conversation transcripts).n- sample test: revival whole-path slo test - setup: 1k concurrent sessions, each with 3 slices in ephemeral tier trigger rolling eviction of 20 nodes replay 1k requests that require revival. - success criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end revival latency 0.98).n- cost benchmark: measure extra tokens and kernel time used during revival and report per-10k-revivals cost delta. target operator-visible cpu overhead v2 migration requires in-place upgrade of slice-manager and revival agent. we support backward-reading: revival agent v2 can read v1 envelopes kernel warmstart must negotiate kernel_hint.n- feature flagging: rollout under feature flag runtime.slice-checkpointing.enabled false by default. canary pool (5 traffic) - 25 - 100 with observability gates (revival latency failure thresholds).n- model compatibility: ensure that quantized or sharded kernels expose a compatible warmstart shim otherwise runtime will fallback to degraded revival. document model whitelist for full-fidelity revival.nnoperational runbook (incident-oriented)n- symptom a: revival failure rate spike (0.5 over 5m) 1. check slice.upload.duration and ephemeral cache saturation metrics. 2. if ephemeral cache ooms: increase ttl on session-slice-cache or scale slice-cache nodes call on-call storage lead. 3. if durable store upload errors: inspect uploader logs, check object-store rate limits and retry queue size. 4. if crc failures: inspect slice-manager cpu load, investigate kernel library version mismatch. 5. mitigation: temporarily set runtime.slice-checkpointing.enabledfalse for the affected pool and trigger live-migration of pinned sessions using migration script: scripts/migrate-pinned-sessions --gracefuln- symptom b: long revival handshake latency (95p 250 ms) 1. correlate with kernel_hint and kernel-dispatcher saturations. 2. if warmstart lane starved: adjust admission control to add 1 revival-worker for 10 minutes. 3. if decompression dominates: offload decompression to dedicated cpu pool or increase ephemeral tier locality. 4. mitigation: set a temporary admission cap and route new sessions to a lower-latency fallback model.n- emergency recovery (checkpoint corruption widespread) 1. flip a global flag to force degraded revivals and annotate requests (trace.revival.degradedtrue). 2. run a recovery job to rehydrate session state from transcript replay for critical customers. 3. post-incident: run forensic profiling, bump checkpoint crc verification and add checksum telemetry.nnknown issues and constraintsn- cross-kernel warmstart divergence: certain experimental kernels change internal kv-serialization layout causing revival crc mismatch. workaround: add kernel_hint mapping table in the envelope and pin those sessions to compatible kernels.n- high write amplification for very chatty sessions: customers with avg token rate 50 tokens/sec will cause many slice writes recommend configuring adaptive slice policy or applying per-session write-rate throttle.n- replay determinism: revival assumes deterministic kv replay non-deterministic model ops (custom kernels with randomized ops) may yield fidelity drift. such kernels must be added to the non-revivable list in runtime config.nnownership, telemetry, and next stepsn- owner: runtime-session-team (primary), kernel-team (warmstart contract), infra-storage (checkpoint storage).n- dashboards to create: revival health (failure rate, latency p50/p95/p99), slice storage cost by customer, revival fidelity regressions by model.n- next work items:n - v2 checkpoint with signed manifests for better integrity checks.n - chunked streaming revival to reduce worst-case tail (prototype q2 2026).n - operator controls for per-customer slice retention policies.nnreferences and standardize telemetry and decision tracing so every flag decision can be reconstructed end-to-end.n4. reduce blast radius with progressive targeting (canary - ramp - percent - full) and deterministic fallback strategies.nnkey definitionsn---------------n- flag: an identifier that toggles behavior in the runtime (e.g., runtime.kv_prefetch_v2).n- kernel capability: a runtime or accelerator property (e.g., async_prefetch, sharded_attention_v2) that a kernel exposes and can negotiate with the control plane.n- decision trace: structured metadata attached to each request that records the flag decisions and kernel choices used to serve the request.n- safety gate: a set of observable constraints (slo/metric thresholds) that must hold before a flag can progress to the next stage.nncontract: capabilities are short tokens: async_prefetch, sharded_attn_v2, quant_fp8_fastpath.n2. dynamic negotiation: at node start, the control plane retrieves the capability vector and stores it with node metadata. flags scoped to kernel-level are only eligible for nodes that advertise the required capability.n3. fallback compatibility matrix: for each flag, authors must provide a fallback kernel variant or a safe no-op. control plane enforces that flag activation never routes traffic to an incompatible kernel.nnexample kernel manifest (single-line json for confluence, title: dependency agreements and shard topology guidance, content: summarynnthis document defines a lightweight, enforceable contract pattern between clients (api consumers, sdks, internal services) and the redwood serving runtime, and it prescribes adaptive shard topology guidance for production inference fleets. the goal is to reduce coupling, make runtime upgrades predictable, and provide operational controls for multi-tenant and mixed-workload environments.nngoalsnn- define clear api/behavioral guarantees the runtime exposes to callers (latency bounds, failure modes, schema expectations).n- establish a minimal contract envelope for versioning, feature flags, and fallbacks.n- describe shard topology strategies (static, capacity-driven, adaptive) and when to apply each.n- provide observability slo requirements to surface contract violations early.n- define rollout and migration procedures for contract changes and shard topology updates.nnscopennapplies to: redwood serving runtime components (frontend gateways, routing layer, shard managers, worker pools) and any internal clients (hosted api, dedicated controllers, private agents) that invoke text-generation, embedding, or reranking endpoints.nnnot in scope: customer-managed models inside private if customer elects fully air-gapped operational model (see private deployment appendix).nndefinitionsnn- contract envelope: json wrapper the runtime and clients agree on that includes metadata (schema version, client intent, hints) and a validation checksum.n- shard: a logical grouping of worker instances that share model artifacts, kv cache adjacency, and placement constraints.n- adaptive sharding: dynamic rebalancing of shard membership and size based on traffic characteristics and tail latency signals.n- client intent: declared properties the client supplies (latency-sensitive, batch-friendly, high-cost-priority).nncontract requirements (runtime - client)nn1) behavioral guarantees (runtime provides):n- success response semantics: idempotent request ids accepted partial outputs are allowed only when explicitly requested via streamingtrue.n- failure taxonomy: will return 4xx for invalid request schema, 429 for client-level throttling, 503 for transient capacity, 500 for internal errors. 503 responses will include retryable: truefalse in the body.n- compatibility guarantee: for any minor service-side patch (no contract schema change), clients on previous minor versions must continue to receive syntactically valid responses for at least 90 days. major schema changes require an adr and a staged migration.nn2) contract envelope (client - runtime):n- every request must include x-rw-contract-version header. if missing, runtime will accept but emit a high-severity trace and increment a metric contract.missing.n- a minimal json envelope in the request body must include: client_id, request_id, intent (optional but recommended), and schema_version. example envelope: nnn client_id: billing-service,n request_id: 6e0f2bd2-...,n intent: latency-sensitive,n schema_version: 2025-11-01nnn3) versioning deprecation rules:n- semantic-ish versions: yyyy-mm-dd schema versions preferred for clarity.n- deprecation window: major schema deprecations are announced at least 60 days prior, with a compatibility shim maintained for 30 days after removal (total 90-day notice).n- runtime will publish a compatibility-report artifact (s3 console link) whenever a non-backwards patch is applied.nn4) client-side validation requirements:n- sdks must validate required fields and fail fast with 400 for missing critical fields.n- sdks should surface retryable and suggested_backoff_ms from responses to upstream callers.nnshard topology guidancennprinciples:n- locality first: keep requests that reuse kv cache or long-lived context routed to the same shard family.n- isolation second: tenant isolation and noisy-neighbor protection trump micro-optimizations.n- observability third: every topology decision must be explorable via dashboards and trace links.nnshard types:n- static shard: fixed membership. use for dedicated tenants, compliance-sensitive workloads, and stateful model variants. pros: predictable performance, easier tracing. cons: lower utilization.n- capacity-driven shard: membership based on pre-allocated capacity and periodic rebalancing (e.g., nightly). use for steady production traffic.n- adaptive shard (recommended for mixed workloads): continually rebalances based on a control loop (traffic, tail latencies, kv-cache hit-rate). use when workload characteristics change diurnally or bursty.nnshard key selection:n- prefer a composite key: tenant_id:model_version:pipeline_variant. this preserves isolation and model locality.n- avoid using user/session id alone as shard key for high-churn workloads.nntopology configuration table (example)nn parameter description example default traffic for rebalancing 15 30 n tail_latency_threshold_ms p99 latency threshold to trigger scaling or split 1200 1000 n cache_hotness_threshold fractional hit rate considered hot 0.65 0.7 nnadaptive sharding control loop (high level)nn1. collect signals: per-shard p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, kv cache hit-rate, queue length, gpu utilization.n2. compute shard health and shard-level cost-efficiency score.n3. trigger action: split, merge, scale-up, scale-down, or migrate tenants.n4. validate via canary (10 traffic) then full rollout.nnautoscaling and placement policiesnn- placement constraints: shards can be tagged with region, hardware-class, tenant-isolation. scheduler respects these when allocating workers.n- prewarming: maintain a pool of prewarmed workers by hardware-class to absorb sudden spikes. prewarm sizing computed from 95th percentile of short bursts.n- graceful draining: when removing a worker, set state draining, stop assigning new requests, wait for max_drain_time_ms (default 30000) or until in-flight0.nnobservability and slosnnrequired metrics (per shard global):n- requests.total, requests.failed, responses.latency.p50,p95,p99, summaryn-------nthis document defines the predictive prefetch orchestrator (ppo): a runtime component that predicts future token or kv-cache accesses and prefetches required kv pages / model artifacts into local memory or a warm cache tier. the goal is to reduce tail latency and cold-kv misses while preserving cost and fidelity slos. it describes architecture, scheduling interactions, configuration, validation tests, rollout plan, and incident runbooks.nnscope and goalsn----------------n- primary goal: reduce 99th/99.9th percentile token latency for long-context and multi-turn workloads by reducing on-path cache-miss stalls.n- secondary goals: keep incremental cost per useful token request classifier - predictor service (async call) - emits n prefetch hints (page_id, score, lookahead_ms) - prefetch coordinator applies policy - enqueues prefetch - kv-cache manager fetches/warms pages - request proceeds using possibly warmed kv/cache.nnpredictor model and signalsn---------------------------n- predictor is intentionally small (few hundred kb parameters) to keep inference cheap and fast. it operates in two modes: deterministic rule-based (fallback) and statistical scoring (ml).n- features used: session token histogram, user agent, route, model variant, recent completion lengths, last-k page access sequence, request timestamp, and cohort id.n- labels for training: subsequent page access within lookahead window (e.g., 200ms) derived from production traces (shadow mode).n- retraining cadence: weekly for high-change routes monthly for stable routes.nnadmission control scheduler integrationn-----------------------------------------nadmission policy is the safety layer that prevents prefetch work from interfering with on-path kernels. key levers:n- prefetch budget per-gpu per-second (pages/sec). default: 50 pages/sec per gpu.n- prefetch priority class: background_low, background_high. background_low is throttled under any kernel contention.n- kernel credit check: prefetch pool only consumes credits from a separate prefetch bucket if runtime kernel load 70 or tail latency slo is threatened, prefetches are suspended.nnconfiguration table (recommended defaults)n-----------------------------------------n key default description n prefetch.enabled true master switch n prefetch.lookahead_ms 200 max lookahead window to consider access relevant n prefetch.max_pages_per_request 6 cap per prediction n prefetch.gpu_budget_pages_per_sec 50 budget enforced by admission controller n prefetch.min_score_threshold 0.55 predictor confidence cutoff n prefetch.priority_mode background_low default priority class n prefetch.shadow_mode true if true, metrics are collected but prefetches arent applied to on-path traffic nnexample runtime yaml confign---------------------------nyamlnprefetch:n enabled: truen lookahead_ms: 200n max_pages_per_request: 4n gpu_budget_pages_per_sec: 50n min_score_threshold: 0.6n priority_mode: background_highn shadow_mode: falsennnobservability kpisn--------------------nminimum dashboards (per-cluster and per-route):n- prefetch hit rate (prefetch_success / prefetch_attempts) target 70 for routes with high sequentiality.n- delta tail latency (p99, p999) before vs after prefetch action target p99 reduction 10ms for targeted routes.n- prefetch-induced kernel wait time should be 0.65 and recall 0.35 for target routes.n2) shadow-mode pilot: prefetch_success 50 and false_positive 25 regression in p99slo and prefetch_cost_delta within budget for 48h.n4) gradual ramp: 5 - 20 - 50 - 100 with 2472h stabilization windows and automated rollback on sla breaches.nnsafety fallback patternsn-------------------------n- automatic suspend: if runtime.p99_latency increases by 10 over 15m or prefetch_eviction_events threshold, suspend prefetch globally and notify oncall.n- degraded planner: switch predictor to deterministic rule-based prefetch (e.g., last-2-pages prefetch) if model confidence drops.n- eviction-aware prefetch: track prefetch-caused evictions and deprioritize prefetches that historically caused cross-tenant memory pressure.nnincident runbook (cache-thrash loop)n------------------------------------ntrigger: sudden spike in cache evictions correlated with prefetch.activity and rising p99 latency.n1) pager routes to ppo-oncall.n2) run quick inspection: check metricsn - pref_attempts curl - evictions curl if evictions / attempts 0.2 and p99 latency slo, execute emergency suspend:n curl -xpost if suspend is successful, monitor p99 for 10m. if stable, adjust gpu budget down (e.g., -50) and re-enable with background_low.n5) postmortem steps: collect traces, predictor inputs, and candidate root causes routing playbook, content: overviewnnpurposenthis playbook defines the design, operational controls, and experiment/runbook procedures for latency-aware, cost-conscious tiered routing in the redwood serving runtime. it connects slo targets, per-tenant economics, and fallback policies so routing decisions preserve customer-facing latency slos while minimizing unit cost.nnscopen- applies to multi-tenant hosted and dedicated pools where requests may be routed across model variants, regions, and capacity tiers.n- not intended to replace per-customer contractual routing written in the control plane (those are higher-level policies implemented using these primitives).nngoals and design constraintsn1) slo preservation: prioritize meeting 99th percentile latency objectives for customer-facing routes.n2) cost sensitivity: route to lower-cost model variants or capacity tiers when doing so will not materially violate slos or degrade quality beyond tolerance.n3) safety: provide deterministic fallbacks and observability to avoid routing flaps and oscillation.n4) incremental deployability: new routing heuristics must be testable against shadow traffic and staged canaries.nnkey concepts and terminologyn- tier: a logical grouping of capacity (e.g., premium-dedicated, shared-hosted, burst-spot).n- model variant: exact model artifact plus quantization/precision profile (e.g., gptx-1.2-int8-v2).n- fidelity: qualitative measure of expected output quality for a given variant.n- cost-per-token (cpt): estimated operator cost for serving a token on a given variant/tier.n- latency budget: per-request remaining time to meet the configured slo.n- route policy: declarative rule combining selectors (tenant, route, weight) and decision predicates.nnrouting decision flow (high-level)n1. admission: validate request metadata, tenant allowances, and route-level constraints.n2. classification: tag request with workload profile (sequence-length estimate, sync/async, priority).n3. candidate generation: list compatible model variants and tiers.n4. scoring: compute score for each candidate: score alpha latency_score beta cost_score gamma fidelity_penalty.n5. selection and reservation: pick highest-scoring candidate that satisfies hard predicates (region affinity, contractual pinning). reserve slot capacity (kernel admission).n6. execution and post-eval: if execution violates latency budget or quality regression, trigger fallback/rollback.nnslo and economics math (practical formulae)n- expected latency per candidate l_c median_kernel_latency(candidate, shape) network_estimate(candidate.region). use histogram-backed estimates.n- cost per request r_c cpt(candidate) expected_tokens(request). for batching, use amortized cost models (see amortized_cost_table below).n- composite utility u_c (slo_headroom(c)/slo_target) - lambda (r_c / r_ref) - mu fidelitypenalty(c). we treat slo_headroom as max(0, slo_target - el_c).n- decision threshold: pick candidate with max u_c subject to u_c u_min else route to fallback (higher tier).nnconfig table (example values)n key description example notes n slo.target target latency (ms) for route 95 ms (p99) route-level override n lambda cost weight in utility 0.8 tuned per product vertical n mu fidelity penalty weight 1.2 fidelity penalty normalized 0,1 n u_min minimal acceptable utility -0.2 prevents overly cheap but slow picks n cost_ref normalization constant for cost 0.0005/token updated by billing team weekly nnoperational rules and safety knobsn- circuit-breaker: if the selected candidates observed p99 exceeds slo.target 20 for 5 mins, route flow is temporarily pinned to next-safe tier and an alert is fired (severity p2).n- dampening window: do not switch routing preference for a tenant more than once per 60s to avoid oscillation.n- shadow testing: new candidate variants must be validated by 1 hour of 10 shadow traffic before being eligible for live routing.n- canary rollout: initial 1 of live traffic with metric-based escalation gates (latency, quality regression).nnrunbook: outage or mass-latency incident (step-by-step)n1. detect: pager triggers from latency slo alert (p99 exceeded for 3m across a route).n2. triage: identify which candidate types account for majority of slow requests (use the routing decisions histogram - see observability queries section).n3. immediate mitigation (fast path): enable route-level override to force-route to premium-dedicated variant or raise u_min to deprioritize low-cost candidates. command-line: nnshnredwoodctl routes override set --route customer.chat --variant premium-gptx-1 --reason p99-latency-spikenn4. validate: watch p99 and token drop rates for 10m. if steady, keep override while root cause investigation continues.n5. permanent remediation: revert to automated routing only after corrective changes (kernel patch, region failover, or cost recalibration) and a successful canary run.nntelemetry observability contractnminimum signals required for safe operation and postmortem:n- per-route, per-variant p50/p95/p99 latency histograms (1s bucketing for 1m window)n- per-route request counts and error counts by variant and tiern- candidate selection reasons (why candidate selected: lowest cost / fidelity / pinned)n- route decision churn metric (switches/min per tenant)n- shadow validation pass/fail rates and quality regression countsn- amortized cost per request and per-token cpi-like metricnnexample observability queries (promql-like pseudocode)n- p99 latency for route customer.chat:nredwood_latency_seconds_bucketroutecustomer.chat,jobruntime - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(...)))n- fraction of requests routed to low-cost tier:nsum(rate(requests_totaltiershared 5m)) / sum(rate(requests_total5m))nnquality safety and fidelity checksn- automatic prompt-level checks: for generation routes with fidelity-sensitive slas, run lightweight rerank/consistency checks in shadow before returning low-fidelity results live. if rerank confidence 10 increase in p99 and fidelity regression 1 live - 5 live - 20 live at each stage validate latency, quality, cost.nnrollout checklist for routing policy changesn- author a policy pr including: policy yaml, target routes, and experiment plan.n- run 1 hour of shadow validation on staging with traffic representative of production (latency and token shape).n- create a canary run for a pilot tenant for 24h with automatic rollback gates for p99 and quality.n- post-canonicalization: add telemetry enrichment and update billing/cost models if cpt adjustments required.nnownership and escalationn- policy author (owner): eng-serving-runtime/routing (primary)n- oncall escalation: runtime sre - runtime platform lead - product owner for routen- sla incident owner: whoever owns the route in the console product mapping table.nnappendicesna. example policy yaml doc_id: dsid_614aa71eb4e342d196c138452cfb4d97, source_type: confluence, title: runtime execution cascades and soft-fail synthesis, content: summary:nnthis handbook defines the execution cascade model we adopted in 2027 for orchestrating multi-tier inference execution, how kernels and scheduler policies participate in graceful degradation, and the operational playbooks for profiling and benchmarking cascade behaviors. it is intended for runtime engineers, sres, and product owners responsible for model rollouts, sla preservation, and incident mitigation.nnwhy an execution cascade?nn- modern inference requires cross-layer coordination: model variants, kernel capabilities, kv cache state, and router-level routing all affect end-to-end latency and quality.n- the execution cascade formalizes ordered fallback steps (fastest/cheapest - compatible fallbacks - degraded modes) and the safety checks and instrumentation needed to avoid quality regression or outage.nnscope and assumptions:nn- applies to redwood hosted dedicated runtime pools.n- assumes models are registered with a variant graph (primary, low-latency quantized, high-fidelity cpu fallback).n- assumes runtime kernel telemetry (kernel_id, slot_id, preempt_count) and request traces are emitted to the observability pipeline.nn1) conceptual modelnnexecution cascade layers (top-down):nn1. serve fast: low-latency gpu kernels (best throughput, quantized).n2. serve fallback-1: compatible kernel variant (slower but high fidelity).n3. serve fallback-2: cpu or remote microservice for short-tail completions.n4. degraded response: length-limited generation structured error with explicit quality flag.nnkey properties:nn- deterministic ordering: cascades are declared per-model and pinned at route level.n- circuit breakers and hysteresis: transition thresholds use smoothing windows to avoid oscillation.n- quality gates: each downgrade step must pass an automated eval suite before being allowed in the graph.nn2) runtime integration: scheduler and kernel interactionnnscheduling primitives used in cascades:nn- slot reservation: short-term exclusive kernel slots are reserved for high-priority fast-path requests.n- soft-preempt windows: kernels expose a preemptability flag scheduler will only preempt if preempt_count 1 fallback.nnroot causes commonly found:nn- credit exhaustion due to aggressive burst traffic from a single route.n- kernel binary mismatch causing deterministic rejection scheduler then routes to fallback.n- subtle latency amplification from slot-slicing under mixed small/large sequence workloads.nn4) benchmark protocol for validating cascade safetynngoal: measure impact of cascading on p99 latency, token cost, and quality relative to baseline.nnbench steps (standardized):nn- baseline: run model on fast-path solo for 30m, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.n- integrated: enable cascade graph and run same corpus for 30m.n- stress: inject a synthetic burst (10x baseline rps) for 2 minutes, observe transition time and hysteresis.nnmetrics to record (csv):nn- timestamp, route, variant, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, kernel_occupancy_pct, kvcache_hit_rate, quality_score_deltannpass criteria for rollout gate:nn- p99 increase 2x baseline for 10mn - kv cache warmup failure (hit_rate 5 failed requests or p99 2x baseline for 30m) alert platform incident manager and set incident severity to sev2.nn10) appendix: templates and helpersnna) incident tag sample (use in issue tracker):nnlabels: runtime-cascade, kernel-fallback, priority-highnsummary: cascade amplification routemy-service-chat observed 4x p99nnb) quick yaml for sequence-aware admission (example):nnadmission:n policy: sequence-awaren buckets:n - max_seq: 128n pool: small-slot-pooln - max_seq: 1024n pool: large-slot-poolnnc) benchmark csv header (copy into bench-scripts):nntimestamp,route,variant,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_sec,kernel_occupancy_pct,kvcache_hit_rate,quality_score_deltannreferences and links:nn- runtime execution contracts and fallback patterns (internal link).n- scheduler policy language specification (internal link).n- profiling playbook: waterfall and trace correlation (internal link).nnchange log:nn- 2027-11-12: initial and canary checklist (sofia alvarez review).n, doc_id: dsid_43dfd9b333bf4fb4b444310398b8254c, source_type: confluence, title: execution stitching and fallback orchestration, content: overviewnnpurpose: this document defines the execution-stitching pattern and the fallback orchestration responsible for providing graceful degradation when the primary execution path (high-throughput gpu kernel pipeline) cannot satisfy a request within slo. it codifies the state machine, scheduling interactions, configuration knobs, observability signals, and an operational runbook for live incidents.nnscope: runtime-gateway, request-router, kernel-scheduler, kvcache-manager, fallback-router, model-variant-proxy. this guide targets on-call sres, runtime engineers, and platform product owners.nnbackground and intentnn- problem: mixed workload bursts, kernel regressions, or cache churn can cause a subset of requests to miss tail-latency slos. uncoordinated retries or naive fallbacks cause thundering cascades, token-cost spikes, and model quality regressions.n- intent: provide a deterministic, observable orchestration that stitches partial progress from the primary path into safe fallback executions while minimizing cost and preserving user-visible correctness.nnarchitecture summarynnexecution paths (logical services)n- runtime-gateway: front-door handling auth, rate limits, and per-token costing.n- request-router: classifies request by latency budget, priority, and required guarantees assigns to execution lanes.n- kernel-scheduler: maps request lanes to kernel execution pools (low-latency, standard, background) and controls kernel handoff.n- kvcache-manager: supplies kv cache state and prefix-hinting exposes warmup metrics.n- fallback-router: executes alternative strategies (quantized variant, truncated-response, stateless re-generation) and merges results.n- model-variant-proxy: serves model variant redirects and handles compatibility checks.nnexecution stitching concept (high level)nn1) progressive execution: a request begins on the primary lane (low-latency pool). the kernel-scheduler allocates slots and attaches a progress token that represents the number of completed token-chunks and current kv epoch.n2) checkpoints: at prescribed kernel boundaries (every n tokens or at decoder-layer boundaries), the runtime emits a stitch-checkpoint event with progress token, partial logits digest, and kv-origin stamp.n3) decision point: if the primary path is delayed beyond budget t_warn (configurable), request-router consults fallback policy to decide: wait, re-route to a compatible curtailed variant, or switch to a stateless fallback.n4) stitching: if a fallback executes, the fallback-router attempts to hydrate the fallback with the latest checkpoint (prefix/kv partial logits) so it continues generation without repeating completed work. if kv state is incompatible, fallback falls back further to truncated restart.nnstate machine (summary)nn- states: accepted - running_primary - checkpointed - fallback_pending - fallback_running - merging - completed failedn- transitions are timebox-driven and signal-driven. key signals: kernel_heartbeat, checkpoint_created, kv_warm, schedule_preempt.nnscheduling interactions and kernel implicationsnn- kernel preemption: kernel-scheduler must annotate preemption reasons (quota, fragmentation, safety-net) in the kernel_heartbeat so stitching logic can choose soft vs hard fallback.n- slice-aware execution: kernels that support incremental slice commits must expose slice boundaries to runtime-gateway via checkpoint_created, otherwise stitching is not possible.n- fairness: scheduler applies a credit-based weight that factors stitchability_score per request low stitchability pushes requests into conservative fallbacks early.nnconfiguration table (recommended defaults)nn config_key description default n---------------------------------n stitch.max_wait_ms maximum time to wait for primary before triggering fallback_pending 80ms n stitch.warn_ms time to emit early warning event to tracing 40ms n stitch.min_progress_tokens minimum completed tokens to allow stitching 8 n stitch.max_merge_attempts number of attempts to merge fallback output with checkpoint 2 n fallback.quantized_variant model variant id for quantized fallback gptq-compat-v1 n fallback.truncate_heuristic apply truncation when kv mismatch ratio x 30 n merge.similarity_threshold threshold for partial-logit merge acceptance (cosine) 0.92 nnoperational runbook: tail-latency incident (step-by-step)nn1) triage signal: alert fires on metric runtime.tail_95_ms 1.5x slo for 5m and stitch.fallback_rate 3. channel: oncall-runtime. pager: primary sre.n2) initial checks (5 min):n a) verify recent deploys: check runtime-gateway and kernel-scheduler release notes for rollouts in the last 30m.n b) query kvcache-manager: kvcache.hit_ratio_1m and kvcache.warmup_queue length.n c) check kernel health: kernel.pool_fragmentation and kernel.queueing_latency.n3) fast mitigation (1020 min):n a) temporarily increase stitch.max_wait_ms to absorb transient jitter (add 2040ms), using /admin/api/runtime/config apply --patch stitch.max_wait_ms:120ms.n b) if kernel fragmentation high, trigger node drain of batch gpus and rebind low-latency pools: /ops/gpu-drain --pool batch-3 --timeout 2m.n c) if fallback rate is too high and causing cost spike, set fallback.quantized_variant to a cheaper model: /admin/runtime/set-fallback --variant gptq-compact-v2n4) investigation (3090 min):n a) correlate checkpoint_created rates with kernel queue depth. low checkpoint frequency indicates slices are too large.n b) inspect traces: look for repeated merge_reject events (merge.similarity_threshold violations). if frequent, raise threshold or disable merging for the affected model.n5) post-incident actions (within 5 working days):n a) run synthetic replay of failing 95th percentile latency pool concurrency), requests are assigned effective weights and admitted according to a proportional fair-share algorithm.n- we assign each customer-route a weight max( min_weight, allocated_commitment activity_bonus ).n- proportional fair-share ensures each budgeted customer receives capacity proportional to their committed units but allows active customers to gain short-term extra share via activity_bonus.nn3) burst tokensnn- each tenant accumulates burst tokens proportional to recent unused reserved capacity and historical burst tolerance. tokens permit exceeding committed throughput for short windows (config default: 30s window up to 1.5x committed rate).n- token refill rate and max balance are tunable per customer tier.nnarchitecture (textual diagram)nn- api gateway - request router - admission controller - fair-share allocator - batcher - model serving pooln- admission controller enforces per-route concurrency caps and consults burst token store (lru with per-tenant counters).n- autoscaler monitors pool-level metrics and triggers scale actions via fleet manager.nnrecommended configuration table (defaults)nn- default slos: p95: 400ms, p99: 1200ms for text generation endpoints.n- activity window: 60s for weight calculation.n- min weight (min_weight): 0.1 of a unit (prevents starvation).n- burst window: 30s, burst multiplier: 1.5, max token balance: 3 intervals.n- admission queue per pool: max backlog 200 requests before shedding.nnexample admission policy (yaml)nn---nadmission_policy_version: v1nroutes:n - name: min_weight: 0.05n burst:n window_seconds: 20n multiplier: 1.2n max_balance: 2n activity_window_seconds: 30n queue_limit: 100n---nnalgorithm outline (step-by-step)nn1. compute per-route demand: recent qps and concurrency sampled over activity_window_seconds.n2. compute base weight committed_units (from billing/commitment).n3. compute activity_bonus f(recent_spike_score) clipped to 0, base_weight 2.n4. effective weight max(min_weight, base_weight activity_bonus).n5. if pool_concurrency capacity: allocate admission slots proportional to effective weights.n7. if a tenant has burst tokens and effective demand configured slo for 3 consecutive 1m buckets - sev2 paging to oncall.n- queue backlog growing: queue depth 50 of queue_limit and increasing for 5m - pager.n- reject spike: rejection rate 0.5 of requests over 5m - slack alert.n- unexpected idle: utilization investigate scheduling/placement.nnoperational runbook (incident flow)nn1. triagen a. confirm alert and scope (pool-level or cross-pool).n b. open incident in incident tracker and annotate with impacted routes/customers.n2. quick mitigationsn a. if p99 spikes and gpus are saturated: increase pool capacity if autoscaler stalled (temporary scale-up command: fleetctl pool scale --pool --instances 2).n b. if queue backlog is the root cause: raise queue_limit temporarily or redirect low-priority routes to overflow pool. c. if a single tenant is noisy: apply per-tenant throttle (cli: rtrctl throttle --tenant --rate ) and notify cs.n3. deeper analysisn a. check logs for admission decisions, token ledger entries, and fair-share allocations.n b. check model server tail latency and kv cache hit-rate (low cache hit can increase p99).n4. post-incident workn a. update the incident runbook with the root cause and follow-up actions.n b. tune activity_window_seconds or burst multiplier for the impacted routes if needed.nntesting and rollout plannn- unit tests: per-algorithm tests for weight computation, token accounting, and queue admission decisions.n- integration tests: synthetic traffic generator (bench/gen-traffic) to emulate mixed tenants with committed and bursty workloads.n- staged rollout:n 1) canary on a single non-production pool for 2 days with 3 synthetic tenants.n 2) gradual increase to 10 of production traffic (shadow admission decisions) for 3 days.n 3) enable enforcement in 25 of requests for 24h and monitor slo burn.n 4) full rollout with rollback window of 1 hour per region.nnsafety knobs and rollback procedurenn- safety knobs: global_fallback_mode (admit-everything), emergency_cap_increase, token_store_disable.n- rollback: flip global_fallback_modetrue to stop fair-share enforcement and allow requests through. after stabilization, revert configuration changes and schedule follow-ups.nncost and capacity considerationsnn- conservative defaults bias toward small over-provision to protect p99s this increases short-term cost. use optimize recommendations to reduce cost after 24 weeks of steady telemetry.n- track cost-per-request and model-inference-p95 normalized metrics to quantify trade-offs when tuning burst_multiplier or min_weight.nnappendix: dedicated and private deployment notesnn- dedicated pools: commit floors are strict. the fair-share allocator still runs but min_weight committed_units and burst_multiplier is lower by default (1.1). bursting may be disabled by contract.n- private/vpc: operator-controlled token refill rates. operators must ensure time synchronization across token-store replicas (ntp).nnappendix: example cli commandsnn- view behaviors at redwood inference. it covers how features are proposed, prototyped, benchmarked, instrumented, staged for rollout, monitored during canaries, and eventually deprecated (sunset). the goal is consistent, slo-aware rollouts that minimize customer impact and preserve reproducible performance baselines.nnscope:n- applies to changes that affect the serving runtime, scheduler/policy language, kernel implementations, kv cache behavior, and any runtime-exposed configuration flags.n- excludes purely client-side sdk changes (see eng-developer-experience) and infra-only capacity changes.nndefinitions:n- feature: any new runtime capability or behavioral change (e.g., continuous batching heuristic, new kernel micro-op).n- kernel variant: a compiled execution path or quantization profile used by the runtime.n- canary: a controlled rollout to a subset of traffic/instances.n- sunset: formal deprecation and removal of a feature/kernel.nnfeature lifecycle stages (high level):n1) proposal designn - owner creates a short design doc with: motivation, invariants, expected perf/cost impact, compatibility constraints, and rollout strategy.n - required fields: feature id (fr-yyyy-), target release, owner, fast rollback plan.n2) prototype microbenchn - implement prototype behind an experimental flag.n - run microbench suite (see benchmarking section). document delta vs baseline for latency p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost.n3) telemetry tracing contractsn - add kernel/feature labels to traces (tag: runtime.feature_id) and metrics (metric: runtime.feature.id.activation_count).n - ensure trace spans have consistent start/end semantics for latency attribution.n4) integration tests stagingn - pass unit integration test matrix including kv cache consistency tests and multi-tenant fairness tests.n - run staged workload replay in staging fleet for 4872 hours.n5) canary rolloutn - canary to 1 of traffic or 5 nodes (whichever is larger) for 24 hours then 5 for 24 hours then 25 for 48 hours before global.n - canary slo gates: latency p95 5 minutes, customer-facing correctness regression. immediate rollback and all-hands page.n- p1:
