surface stability and versioning contract, content: summarynnthis document defines the stability, compatibility, and versioning contract for any extensions to the redwood serving runtime extension surface. extensions in this document include kernel plugins, priority/admission hooks, observability adapters, custom scheduling policies, and lightweight binary-compatible runtime modules. the goal is to enable third-party and internal teams to safely integrate new features while preserving customer-facing slos, rollout safety, and fast rollback paths.nnscopenn- applies to all code and artifacts that are loaded dynamically into the serving runtime process (ld.so, plugin loader, dynamic shared objects), as well as to external modules that register callbacks with the runtime over the internal plugin api (rpc or in-process).n- does not apply to model files, model weights, or user prompts. it does apply to model-serving kernel implementations and dispatch adapters.nngoalsnn1. prevent runtime crashes and silent performance regressions after extension deploys.n2. provide a clear abi/semantic compatibility guarantee across minor releases so teams can plan integration windows.n3. define test and rollout requirements that keep production slos (p50 latency, p99 latency, availability, error budget) within agreed thresholds.n4. provide an explicit deprecation and sunset path for unstable extension apis.nncompatibility modelnnwe use a three-tier compatibility model for the extension surface:nn- strict abi compatibility (patch releases): binary-compatible, no symbol or struct layout changes. backward-compatible behavior guaranteed. extensions built against a patch-level release must run without recompilation.nn- semantic compatibility (minor releases): may add optional fields, new callback hooks, and extension-facing feature flags. extensions built against an older minor release should continue to function with feature-gates disabled. if an extension requires new hooks, it must declare an explicit minimum minor version.nn- breaking changes (major releases): may change core interfaces and require a rebuild of extensions. major releases are accompanied by a migration guide and a six-month opt-in dual-run period (see rollout migration section).nnversioning policy and manifestnnevery runtime artifact (core runtime, kernel plugins, adapters) must ship with a manifest file: runtime-extension-manifest.yamlnnexample manifest:nn---nname: fast-kernel-pluginnversion: 1.2.0nbuild_target: rwinference-x86_64-gpu-v2nabi_hash: 2f7a4b8enmin_runtime_minor: 2ncapabilities:n - kernel:sharded-attentionn - telemetry:streaming-metricsnallowed_flags:n - enable_experimental_prefetchnsignature: sha256:...n---nnrules:nn- version follows semver: major.minor.patch. runtime core only increments major when abi/semantic breaks are necessary.n- abi_hash is a build-time hash of exported symbols and public struct layout. runtime will refuse to load a plugin if abi_hash mismatches unless explicit override is provided and an operator acknowledges risk.n- min_runtime_minor indicates the minimum runtime minor version that provides required optional hooks.nnextension lifecycle and stability labelsnnextensions must be labeled for expected stability in their manifest: alpha beta stablenn- alpha: experimental allowed only in sandbox and canary clusters, never in global production regions.n- beta: allowed in limited production audiences after automated safety tests pass. beta may be promoted to stable after 2 months with no regression signals.n- stable: cleared for general production rollout.nnintegration and preflight checklist (required before canary rollout)nn1. automated build and signature verification:n - build in ci with reproducible output.n - provide signed manifest and signature verification steps.n2. local microbenchmarks:n - run the per-token microbenchmark suite with a representative request corpus (see benchmarking section).n - compare per-token cpu/gpu time threshold: no 5 regression in median token processing time for kernels, and no 10 regression in p99 latency for end-to-end small requests.n3. telemetry smoke tests:n - verify telemetry adapters emit the runtime-defined trace events and do not create cyclical logging.n4. safety fuzz tests:n - run simulated malformed frames, oom scenarios, and sequential plugin unload/reload to ensure stability.n5. slo simulation: n - run the synthetic traffic simulator (operational-workload-simulator) with the extension enabled and confirm p99 latency and availability stay within the attack budget for the target fleet.nnrollout migration procedurenn1. canary: gate to a single canary cluster that hosts 10 vs baseline for 10 minutes,n - error rate increase 0.5 absolute,n - kernel crash or sigsegv in plugin.n3. controlled ramp: 25 - 50 - 100 with progressive verification and a 24-hour hold at each step for stable labels.n4. emergency rollback: operator runbook and an automated controller exist to yank the extension from active nodes and revert kernel routing to a safe fallback variant. see runbook section for cli commands.nnmeasurement and slo impact accountingnn- any extension that modifies request-path kernels must publish an anticipated slo delta in the manifest and in the pr.n- runtime ci will run a differential benchmark comparing baseline and extension to generate a per-route cost and latency delta table. this table becomes part of the rollout ticket and product release notes.nntelemetry and observability contractnnextensions must emit the following minimal signals to integrate with runtime observability:nn- extension.loaded (gauge) with fields: name, version, stability_labeln- extension.hook.latency_ms (histogram) for each registered callbackn- extension.error (counter) with categorized error types (init, hook-failure, oom)n- optional: extension.span (trace) linking to request.trace_id when executing in-pathnnexample tracing header (json):nn extension: fast-kernel-plugin,n version: 1.2.0,n span_id: ...,n trace_id: ...nnnruntime load-time checks and policy enforcementnnat process start and plugin load time the runtime performs:nn1. manifest signature verification (fail-fast if missing and not in debug environment)n2. abi_hash check and capability whitelist enforcementn3. capability vs policy check: certain capabilities (e.g., direct gpu memory management) require explicit operator allowance and are disallowed in shared multitenant fleets by defaultnnpolicy table (operator-managed):nn capability default allowed in shared fleet requires operator consent comments n gpu direct memory false true high risk: can cause cross-tenant oomn telemetry:streaming-metrics true false low riskn kernel:sharded-attention false true requires isolation testsnnrunbook: emergency disable and rollback (quick commands)nn1. mark plugin unschedulable via service registry:n - redwoodctl runtime plugin disable fast-kernel-plugin --cluster canaryn2. trigger rolling restart of nodes that loaded plugin (graceful drain):n - redwoodctl node drain --label plugin:fast-kernel-plugin --grace-period 120sn3. if crash loop persists, flip the runtime feature-flag fallback:n - redwoodctl runtime set-flag --name enforce-plugin-fallback --value truenntesting and benchmark suite guidancenn- use the per-token microbenchmark and the request-surface replay (see benchmarking-and-perf-suite). capture: median token time, p95/p99 end-to-end latency, gpu occupancy, and allocator fragmentation.n- for kernel-level changes, include unit tests that validate kv cache behavior, prefetch ordering, and cooperative preemption interactions.nnexample microbenchmark invocation:nn./bench/run_per_token.sh --plugin ./fast-kernel-plugin.so --corpus small-oral-requests.json --warmup 60 --measure 300nndeprecation and sunset policynn- stable extension apis can be deprecated with at least one minor runtime release notice (minimum 90 days). deprecation must include: migration guide, compatibility shim if feasible, and test plans.n- sunset: if an api is to be removed, provide 6 months notice with automated compatibility checks and an extended canary window.nnownership and escalationnn- primary owner: eng-serving-runtime team (oncall rotation).n- secondary: eng-platform (release automation), eng-infra (operator policy).n- overview:nnthis document describes the tiered fallback routing and eviction architecture (tfrea) used by redwoods serving runtime to meet multi-dimensional slos (latency percentiles, cost budget, and availability) while degrading predictably during capacity pressure or downstream failure modes. tfrea unifies routing policies, candidate model variants, eviction heuristics, and runtime-informed kernel scheduling hints into a single, observable control loop.nngoals:n- maintain 99th-percentile latency slos per route under normal load.n- bound hosted per-token cost within configured customer cost tiers.n- provide deterministic, monotonic quality degradation (higher-quality - lower-quality) with automated rollback when pressure subsides.n- make fallback decisions explainable and traceable per request for post-incident analysis.nnscope:n- applies to hosted and dedicated modes private deployments can enable tfrea via configuration flag.n- covers routing layer, model-variant catalog, eviction/placement heuristics, kernel scheduling hints, and observability integration.nnkey concepts and components:n1) routing policy engine (rpe)n- policy primitives: latency-priority, cost-priority, isolation-priority. each route has a profile: e.g., latency: 0.7, cost: 0.2, isolation: 0.1.n- decision inputs: request metadata (route, token budget, customer plan), node telemetry (utilization, queue depth), model health (regression alerts), and global capacity signals.n- outputs: selected pool (hot, warm, cold), model variant (full, quantized, distilled), and optional dual-write fallback (emit to both selected and fallback model asynchronously for a/b quality logging).nn2) model variant catalog and contractsn- each canonical model version registers 1..n variants with contract metadata:n - quality_score (0.0-1.0) derived from eval harnessn - compute_cost_factor (relative tokens/second)n - warmup_time_secondsn - compatible_kernels (list of kernels / tensor layouts)n- example registration yaml snippet: n id: llama-3-20b:v2026-02n variants:n - id: llama-3-20b_fp16n quality_score: 0.98n cost_factor: 1.0n warmup: 18n kernels: matmul-fused, alpa-attn-optimizedn - id: llama-3-20b_8bitqn quality_score: 0.92n cost_factor: 0.55n warmup: 6n kernels: quant-8q-convnn3) tiered pools (hot / warm / cold)n- hot: low-latency nodes, prewarmed kv caches, continuous batching source used for latency-priority traffic. slo target: p99 0.4, kernel queue growth rate 20 over 30s, and per-tenant cost throttle events.n- heuristic ordering when evicting: least-recently-used variant replicas weighted by (quality_score route_priority) to avoid evicting high-quality routes.n- soft-eviction step: move from hot-warm hard-eviction: terminate replica (cold) and optionally nominate a lower-cost variant.nn5) kernel scheduling hints and interactionn- rpe emits kernel hints: preferred_kernel, concurrency_target, slice_budget. these are advisory fields consumed by kernel-and-scheduling layer to optimize batch slicing and preemption.n- example hint: preferred_kernel: matmul-fused, concurrency_target: 6, slice_budget_ms: 40.nn6) observability and decision tracingn- every routing decision logs a decisiontrace id attached to request spans. trace contains inputs, scoring vector, selected_variant, and fallback_candidates. stored in the decision-trace index for 30 days by default.n- key dashboards: per-route fallback rate, per-variant quality delta (a/b logs), pool occupancy and eviction rate, kernel hint adoption rate.nnslos and thresholds (operative values):n- route-level p50/p95/p99 slos are configured per route. default intent for conversational routes: p50 10 of requests sustained over 5 minutes without triggering operator notification.nnoperational procedures and runbooks:n1) gradual rollout checklist (owner: runtime-release)n1. create canary pool with 5 traffic weight.n2. enable decision-trace sampling at 5 for canary.n3. monitor: fallback-rate, p99 latency, kernel-queue-depth for 15 minutes.n4. if fallback_rate 1 or p99 regresses 15 over baseline, abort and roll back.n5. if stable, ramp 5 every 10 minutes to target.nn2) incident triage playbook: unexpected fallback surgen- pager triggers at fallback_rate 10 sustained for 2 minutes.n- triage steps:n 1. query decision-trace for last 5 minutes (filter by route). cli: redwoodctl traces query --route --since 5m --filter fallbacktruen 2. check pool telemetry: node_util, kv_hit_rate, kernel_queue_growth.n 3. if kv cold-start 50: trigger warmup job for top-5 variants: redwoodctl runtime warmup --variants --target-pool hotn 4. if node ooms or watchdog hits: cordon nodes and spin up replacement nodes (see gpu-fleet-and-capacity runbook).n 5. temporarily set route policy to latency-priority and pin to hot pool for critical tenants while investigating.nn3) performance regression investigation (owner: runtime-profiling)n- collect sample logs and kernel traces with sampler strategy: 1:1000 baseline, 1:50 on regression window.n- use profiling commands: profiler collect --trace-id --duration 30s --output s3://runtime-profiles/.tar.gzn- correlate with batch-slice histograms and kernel latency percentiles.nnbenchmarking and validation suite:n- the tfrea validation harness is a sub-suite in the performance suite: includes mixed-workload load generator, kv-warmup simulator, and variant quality regression tests.n- key scenarios:n - steady-state with mixed short/long sequences (60/30/10 split by request length).n - rapid burst (2x sustained) with concurrent model-variant promotion/demotion.n - engineered wholesale kernel regression: inject a slow kernel variant to ensure sentinel metrics and fallbacks work.n- release gate: tfrea must pass canary e2e smoke and two automated burst simulations without p99 slo breaches before canary ramp.nnrelease notes summary (2026-02-15):n- introduced tiered fallback routing and eviction architecture (tfrea) to reduce tail latency and control cost during capacity pressure.n- added decisiontrace indexing and trace-based runbook utilities.n- new model-variant contract fields (quality_score, warmup_time_seconds) and kernel hint api.nnknown issues and workarounds (as of 2026-03-02):n- issue: under certain mixed-tenant workloads, eviction ranking can bias too heavily toward routes with frequent short requests, causing long-tail quality regressions for background batch routes.n - workaround: set explicit route affinity in route config to protect background batch routes, e.g., affinity: protect_until: 2026-06-01.n- issue: kernel hint adoption sometimes lags on heterogeneous pools where the kernel mapper is updating mismatch can cause suboptimal batch slicing.n - workaround: restart kernel-mapper after variant promotion: systemctl restart kernel-mapper (one node at a time) and allow 60s for re-registration.nnimplementation notes and apis:n- new api: /v1/runtime/route-evaluate (internal) returns decisiontrace and selected_variant. schema: route, inputs, scoring, selected, fallbacks, hints.n- redwoodctl examples:n - query fallback stats: redwoodctl inference mode: reproducibility spec runbook, content: summary:nnthis page defines the deterministic inference mode (dim): a configuration and operational contract that provides reproducible token output and execution traces across repeated inference runs for a pinned model variant and configuration. dim is intended for debugging, eval reproducibility, and regression investigation where bit-for-bit repeatability (within documented tolerances) is required.nngoals:n- provide a single switchable runtime mode (global or per-route) that reduces nondeterminism sources across scheduler, kernels, and model io.n- enumerate required kernel/runtime properties and configuration knobs to enable reproducible outputs for common models (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, multimodal pipelines).n- provide an operator runbook for enabling dim in canary and production, including telemetry, verification tests, and rollback criteria.nnnon-goals:n- dim is not a substitute for formal cryptographic determinism across heterogeneous hardware families (we document hardware compatibility and limits).n- dim does not freeze model weights model version pinning remains required for reproducibility.nndefinitions and scope:n- deterministic inference mode (dim): a set of runtime and kernel settings plus input seeding rules intended to make repeated calls with identical inputs and model version produce the same token sequence and internal trace signatures.n- trace signature: a compact hash synthesized from key telemetry points (request_id, model_version, rng seeds, kernel checksums, kvcache identifiers) used to quickly validate run equivalence.n- tolerance window: allowed floating-point numerical variance range (default 1e-6 relative) documented per-model class.nnrequirements (operator and engineering):n requirement rationale owner n---------n rng seed pinning exposed per-request async subgraph operators and sampling must consume a deterministic seed architecture overview (serving runtime), content: overviewnkernel selection is the serving runtime subsystem responsible for choosing the concrete gpu implementation (kernel plan) for a request, given:n- model identity and architecture/familyn- workload regime (prefill vs decode characteristics sequence length buckets)n- hardware target (gpu sku, driver/cuda capability, mig partitioning)n- runtime feature flags (quantization profile, attention variant, kv-cache layout)nnthis page describes:n1) where selection happens in the execution pipelinen2) interfaces to scheduler and compilation cachen3) how decisions are cached, serialized, and made replayable/deterministicnnthis is an architectural overview. for the v2 decision logic and fallback policy, see adr-017 and the v2 design doc.nn---nn goalsn- ensure correctness-first selection: only choose kernels that are compatible with the request target hardware.n- maintain determinism and replayability: identical inputs must yield identical selection (modulo explicitly versioned policy changes).n- reduce tail latency by selecting optimized kernels per sku and per seq-length regime.n- keep selection overhead low (bounded cpu time, bounded telemetry overhead).n- provide operational controls: allow/deny lists, feature gates, and forced overrides.nn non-goalsn- training or learning a model-based selector (out of scope for v2 we use explicit policy rules).n- deciding cluster placement (region/pool routing is handled by control plane and scheduling layers).nn---nn high-level execution pipeline (where selection occurs)nkernel selection runs inside the per-request runtime execution path after model resolution and before compilation/execution.nn request flow (text diagram)n1. front door / api adaptern - validates request, resolves model alias model_id model_version.n - normalizes request options (max_tokens, streaming, tool/function calling toggles) into requestoptions.nn2. scheduler / batchern - assigns request to a worker process on a gpu.n - produces lightweight workload hints (e.g., observed prefill/decode distribution for the batch queue).nn3. kernel selector (this subsystem)n - extracts features (selectorfeatures) from request model metadata gpu metadata scheduler hints.n - applies feature gate allow/deny rules.n - generates candidate kernels and selects a kernelplan.n - emits selection telemetry (sampled).nn4. compilation cache launchern - checks compilation cache for compiled artifacts matching kernelplan.n - compiles if missing (within guardrails), then launches the selected kernel.nn5. execution metricsn - executes prefill/decode.n - reports latency breakdown, kernel identifiers, and errors.nnselection occurs at step 3, and is designed to be:n- pure with respect to its inputs (no hidden dependence on time or ambient process state)n- versioned via policy version ids and runtime build versionnn---nn component boundariesn kernel selector modulenowner: runtime kernels runtime architecturennresponsibilities:n- feature extraction and normalizationn- candidate generationn- rule evaluation and scoring (v2)n- fallback selectionn- decision caching and serializationn- telemetry emission hooksnndoes not own:n- gpu placement / pool selection (control plane scheduler)n- compilation artifact generation logic (compiler backend owns compilation selector only keys it)nn kernel registryna registry of kernel implementations and their compatibility constraints.nnregistry entries are keyed by:n- kernel_id (stable string)n- model family/architecture compatibility (e.g., llama-like, mistral-like)n- capability requirements (sm version, cuda capability flags)n- supported quantization profilesn- known-bad deny rules (sku/driver specific)nnregistry is loaded from:n- built-in runtime defaultsn- hot-reloadable config overlays (for emergency deny/pin)nn compilation cache interfacenselector produces a compilationkey / plankey used by compilation caching.nncompilation cache uses compilationkey to:n- lookup a compiled artifact (in-process memory on-node disk cache)n- avoid recompiles across requestsnnselector guarantees:n- if compilationkey is identical, compiled artifacts should be reusable.n- if a choice changes any codegen-relevant parameter, it must reflect in compilationkey.nn scheduler hints interfacenscheduler provides optional hints that improve stability for mixed workloads.nnexamples of hints:n- estimated prefill_tokens and decode_tokens for the in-flight batchn- observed queue regime classification (short prompts vs long-context dominated)n- batching parameters currently in effect (max batch size, continuous batching mode)nnselector treats hints as inputs to selection, but the hint schema is:n- explicitly versioned (hints_schema_version)n- safe to omit (selector must fall back to request-derived features)nn---nn data contractsn selectorfeatures (normalized inputs)nselectorfeatures is the normalized set the selector.nn---nn output contractn kernelplannkernelplan is the selectors output. it is a structured record that must fully describe the execution choice.nnkernelplan includes:n- kernelplan quickly.n- compilation cache ensures the chosen plan maps to a compiled artifact.nnimportant: do not conflate same decision with compiled exists. a kernelplan can be cached even if content: summarynnthis playbook defines the product-level contract primitives, slos, billing mappings, and rollout guidance for conversational session contracts (cscs). cscs are the canonical package that encapsulates per-session runtime guarantees, fidelity expectations, billing signals, and automated fallback policies for redwood customers using conversational (chat/assistant) endpoints. the goal is to provide a predictable, auditable surface that aligns product, billing, and infra for low-friction migrations between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.nngoalsnn- provide a small, composable set of session primitives that cover 90 of customer conversational use cases.n- make fidelity cost trade-offs explicit and machine-readable.n- ensure safe rollouts with canarying, auto-fallback, and observability hooks.n- align slos to billing to avoid surprise invoices while enabling predictable economics.nnscopennthis playbook covers: session lifecycle, contract primitives, slo targets and alerts, billing mapping, runtime enforcement strategy, developer ergonomics (api sdk), and operations/runbook steps. it does not prescribe kernel-level serving implementation or third-party model licensing.nndefinitionsnn- session: a logical conversation with an id and bounded ttl that aggregates requests and token usage for billing and fidelity purposes.n- contract: the json-serializable object that customers pin to a session to express slos, fidelity budget, and fallback policies.n- fidelity: the expected quality/per-token compute profile (e.g., high, medium, low) mapped to model/quantization pairs.n- variant: a named modelconfig tuple (example: gptx-2-8q, llama-70b-fp16).nncontract primitives (stable api surface)nn1) contract_id (string) unique customer-visible id.n2) session_ttl_ms (integer string) how long the session id is valid since the last activity. default: 1800000 (30 minutes).n3) fidelity_budget (string) token-budget or compute-budget per session. format: tokens:1000 or compute:0.75.n4) slo_profile (string) interactive transactional batch-like. each profile maps to latency and availability targets.n5) fallback_policy (string) serialized policy with prioritized variants and cost thresholds.n6) billing_mode (string) per_token per_session hybrid.n7) telemetry_level (string) none basic detailed (affects retention cost).nnexample contract (canonical)nnn contract_id: acme-chat-basic-v1,n session_ttl_ms: 3600000,n fidelity_budget: tokens:2000,n slo_profile: interactive,n fallback_policy: gptx-3-8q,gptx-2-8q,n billing_mode: hybrid,n telemetry_level: basicnnnslos and thresholds (product-aligned)nntable: session slo mapping (product surface)nn slo_profile target_p50_ms target_p95_ms availability error_budget/month default_telemetry n interactive 70 250 99.8 0.2 basic n transactional 150 500 99.5 0.5 detailed n batch-like 500 1500 99.0 1.0 detailed nnnotes:n- p50/p95 are measured per single-turn token generation latency (end-to-end) excluding client-side network.n- availability fraction of successful responses not hitting hard-fallback (400/5xx excluded).n- error budget is applied to the contract_id at tenant level and can be traded for credits (see billing mapping).nnbilling mapping pricing primitivesnn- per_token: bill raw generation tokens by model variant rate. session contracts can define a cursor threshold after which a lower-cost variant is eligible.n- per_session: a flat rate per session start suitable for short interactions or high-variance token usage.n- hybrid: baseline per_session marginal per_token above the session token floor.nndefault recommended price bands (internal product guidance only):nn- interactive/hybrid baseline: 0.003 per session start per_token at variant rate after 200 tokens.n- transactional/per_token: per-token rates scaled by 1.0x (high fidelity), 0.55x (medium), 0.18x (low-8q).nndiscounting and creditsnn- error-budget-burn: when a tenant uses 50 of error budget for a billing cycle, offer guided migration suggestions a one-time credit if switched to a lower fidelity variant by the product team.n- commitment: dedicated capacity customers can lock session-floor pricing via monthly commit sku contracts.nnruntime enforcement strategynn- contracts are evaluated at session creation. enforcement points:n - router: maps incoming requests for a session to the current active variant per fallback_policy.n - serving runtime: enforces per-request token caps and telemetry level.n - billing pipeline: aggregates session-starts and tokens into invoicing meters.nn- fallback behavior order: preference-based variant routing - queueing (up to 2s) - degrade fidelity (quant/variant swap) - degrade features (disable tool-calls) - soft-fallback (short response) - hard-fallback (configured error).nndeveloper ergonomics (api sdk examples)nn1) create session (curl example)nncurl -x post n -h graceful restart latency contracts and snapshot synthesis, content: overviewnnthis document defines latency contracts (slos/slo targets) and the operational protocol for graceful restarts of runtime workers, kernel modules, and model shards. it also specifies the snapshot synthesis format we use for resumable execution: what state is captured, how it is validated, and how resume/rollback works. the goal is to provide a concrete, testable, and observable procedure that keeps customer-facing latency and correctness within predictable bounds during maintenance, upgrades, and transient failures.nnaudiencenn- runtime engineers implementing restart semantics and kernel handoff.n- sre and oncall responsible for incident response when restarts impact slos.n- release engineers and qa writing canary tests and fidelity benchmarks.nndefinitionsnn- graceful restart: a coordinated shutdown and resume of a worker (or kernel) that preserves sufficient execution state so in-flight requests can be resumed or rerouted without correctness regressions.n- cold restart: full process restart without preserved execution snapshots requires warmup/synthetic traffic to reach steady-state.n- snapshot: a serialized representation of runtime-required state for resumability (kv cache segments, session token pointers, decoder cache offsets, plugin state checksums).n- resume window: the time window after restart during which resumed requests must meet latency/fidelity guarantees.nnlatency contracts (slos)nnthese contracts are the sla-facing expectations that the runtime operator must meet under planned maintenance (rolling upgrades) and common unplanned restarts (ooms, node reboots, kernel panics). targets are expressed as 30-day rolling metrics and validated through synthetic traffic during canaries.nnprimary slosnn- controlled rolling restart (per-pool, single-tenant): resumed-request p95 resume/serve), kernel handoff events, snapshot-save and snapshot-apply events, kvcache warmness score, model load digest.n- primary metric names: runtime.resume.apply_latency_ms (histogram), runtime.resume.success_rate (ratio), runtime.snapshot.serialize_ms, runtime.snapshot.size_bytes.n- attribution: resumed vs. newly routed requests are tagged with resumetrue/false. slos are measured only on resumedtrue requests for restart contracts and only on resumedfalse requests for cold-start recovery windows.nnsnapshot synthesis: what we capturennsnapshots must be compact, deterministic, and verifiable. they are intended to let a worker resume decoding/generation for an in-flight request or restore a warm execution state for a session cohort. the synthesis procedure produces a snapshot manifest and a binary blob.nnessential snapshot components (per-entity):nn- header: snapshot_version, producer_node_id, sequence_id, timestamp (iso8601).n- kvcache segments: list of (prefix_hash, ttl_ms, compressed_bytes_base64, checksum_sha256).n- decoder cache: token_index_offset, kv_positions, compressed_kv_blob (lz4), kernel_hint_id.n- active invocation metadata: request_id, model_id, config_hash (quantization/profile), prompt_prefix_fingerprint.n- plugin state checksums: list of plugin_name - checksum, and optional plugin blob pointer.nnformat and versioningnn- snapshot manifest is json (text) with fixed keys blobs are base64 strings or object-store pointers.n- versioning: snapshot_version follows semver-like format v... consumers must reject unknown major versions.nnconsistency and safety checksnnbefore accepting a snapshot to resume, the worker applies these gates in order:nn1) model_id and config_hash must match the local loaded model. if mismatch, reject (fail-open routing to fallback model).n2) checksum verification for all blobs. any mismatch - reject.n3) ttl_ms on kvcache segments must not be expired expired segments are pruned.nnif any gate fails during a planned maintenance canary, the runtime must route the in-flight request to a compatible fallback variant and mark the snapshot as incompatible in telemetry.nnoperational protocolsnnplanned rolling upgrade checklist (per-pool):nn1) mark pool as draining in control plane for 30s.n2) for each worker being rotated: capture snapshot for active invocations and attempt to handoff to hot neighbor using snapshot rpc.n3) wait for runtime.resume.apply_latency_ms p95 1 over 60s.n4) post-incident: run snapshot validation test suite (see testing and canary section) and file incident with execution fingerprint.nncanary and synthetic testsnnwe validate restart contracts using two classes of synthetic tests executed in ci and production canary environments:nn- per-invocation resume test: inject 13 active invocations, force a swap of kernel module and assert runtime.resume.apply_latency_ms p95/p99.n- shard snapshot roundtrip: serialize a full shard snapshot, write to object store, read back on a separate node, apply, and run e2e generation verification (exact-match on deterministic seeds).nntesting matrix (example):nn test type snapshot size assertion run cadence owner adr, content: summarynnthis adr defines the accelerator abi (application binary interface) and the runtime-side driver graceful-degradation policy for heterogeneous accelerator fleets (gpu, tpu-like asics, and vendor-provided inference accelerators). the goal is a small, well-specified handshake and capability set that: 1) allows the runtime to negotiate performance/precision tradeoffs with device drivers 2) exposes a deterministic degradation path when an accelerator cannot satisfy requested guarantees and 3) provides operational signals for capacity, thermal, and error states so higher layers (routing, fallback) can make policy decisions.nncontext and motivationnnredwoods serving runtime runs across mixed hardware: cloud gpus with different memory/compute, vendor inference chips with quantization-aware runtimes, and experimental on-prem asics for private deployments. historically each driver exposed a different surface (promises about sequence-length limits, supported quantization, kv cache semantics), which led to fragile fallbacks and silent quality regressions. operations has observed incidents where a node reported healthy but silently served half-precision tensors, creating subtle hallucination regressions in downstream evals. we need a minimal abi and a deterministic downgrade model so the orchestration and routing layers can react before customer-visible quality drops.nndecision (what we are adopting)nnwe adopt a two-part contract:nn1) accelerator abi (driver runtime surface)n- a json capability manifest returned during driver handshake with these required fields: vendor, model, memory_bytes, peak_fp32_throughput, supported_precisions (list), max_sequence_length, kv_cache_model (nonekeysegsegmented), supported_quant_modes (list), fail_modes (list of canonical failure codes).n- a grpc control channel for health telemetry that emits structured events: thermal_warning, memory_pressure, driver_degradation(start/end), artifact_errors. events include numeric fields (temp_celsius, available_bytes, eviction_count).n- deterministic downgrade functions exposed by drivers: get_degradation_path(requested_precision) - ordered list of fallback precisions and a max-acceptable-seq-length for each step.nn2) graceful-degradation policy (runtime orchestration expectations)n- if a driver indicates driver_degradation or memory pressure that will affect p of requests in next t seconds, the runtime must:n a) mark node as degrading and emit a metric (accelerator.node.degradationreason).n b) for new requests, consult degradation path and either re-route to compatible node, fall back to a quantized variant, or invoke a lower-fidelity model per client policy.n c) for in-flight requests, attempt best-effort kv-preserving re-execution (see runbook) but avoid silent precision demotion unless explicitly allowed by the tenants model policy.nnrationalenn- small manifest events provide actionable signals without locking in per-vendor rpcs.n- centralizing downgrade logic in drivers avoids guessing behavior and ensures the runtime can reason about end-to-end effects (e.g., seq length vs precision tradeoff).n- separating allowed by tenant policy from automatic demotion prevents silent regressions for customers with strict fidelity requirements.nnalternatives considerednn1) do nothing / keep vendor-specific surfacesn - pros: no immediate engineering costn - cons: repeated incidents, unpredictable fallbacks, poor observability for quality regressions (rejected).nn2) full feature-rich driver rpc (rich schema for every kernel)n - pros: maximum expressivityn - cons: long vendor integration time, brittle across versions (rejected).nn3) runtime-only heuristic demotion (runtime interprets raw metrics and decides)n - pros: driver-agnosticn - cons: wrong assumptions across devices drivers have the ground truth (rejected).nnimplementation specificationnn1) manifest schema (json example)nn vendor: string,n device_model: string,n memory_bytes: 68719476736,n peak_fp32_throughput: 12000.0,n supported_precisions: fp32,fp16,int8,n max_sequence_length: 4096,n kv_cache_model: segmented,n supported_quant_modes: static8,dynamic8,awq,n fail_modes: oom,thermal,driver_faultnnn2) control channel: grpc proto (summary)n- service: acceleratorcontroln- rpcs: getmanifest(), streamevents(stream event) - ack, setthrottle(level) - ackn- event structure: timestamp_ms, node_id, code, numeric_map, textnn3) degradation api (driver-side function)n- get_degradation_path(requested_precision: string, requested_sequence: int) - list of precision, max_sequence_length, estimated_throughput_rationnoperational runbook (short)nntriggers and immediate actions:n1) event thermal_warning with temp_celsius 85 for 30s - put node into read-only drain and notify sre.n2) driver_degradation with predicted_available_bytes mark degrading, reduce offerable concurrency by 50 and trigger rescheduling.nnmanual recovery steps:n1) for transient thermal events: verify cooling system, evict long-running ephemeral jobs, restart driver process if required.n2) for persistent artifact errors: collect driver logs / dmesg, escalate to vendor with manifest and event stream.nnrouting api implicationsnn- api layer must include these fields in the request envelope: preferred_fidelity (strictbest-effortcost-optimized) and allow_demote boolean.n- default tenant policy: preferred_fidelitybest-effort, allow_demotefalse. allowing demote requires explicit opt-in by the customer and is surfaced in console settings.nntesting and acceptance criteriann- unit: manifest parsing, event handling, degradation-path evaluation.n- integration: simulate driver events (thermal, oom) in testbed and assert runtime re-routes or rejects per tenant policy.n- quality regression: run prompt-suite ci (refer to prompt-suite-ci-contract-testing-guidelines) before and after simulated demotion metrics: bleu/rouge analogs and hallucination rate must not regress beyond tenant thresholds.nnmetrics to monitornn- accelerator.node.degradation.count by coden- accelerator.request.demoted.count by tenant and modeln- end_to_end_quality_regressions.per_model (linked to evals)n- routing_fallbacks.per_minutennrollout plannn1) stage 0: spec review and vendor alignment (2 weeks).n2) stage 1: driver shim implementation for two vendor drivers and testbed integration (6 weeks).n3) stage 2: runtime support (handshake, event processing, routing changes) in canary (4 weeks).n4) stage 3: tenant opt-in on dedicated and private (2 weeks).n5) stage 4: full launch for hosted (after 8 weeks of canary stability).nnowners and contactsnn- design author: michael chen (runtime team)n- driver integration lead: nadia alvarez (kernel drivers)n- sre contact: priya singhn- product liaison: daniel romeronnopen questions and future worknn- how to represent approximate numeric fidelity (e.g., awq variants with mixed blocks)? we propose a small extension to the manifest to include per-layer fidelity profiles in a later adr.n- should the runtime be allowed to force demotion for system safety (e.g., to avoid cascading ooms)? current decision: only when system_safety flag present in tenant policy (requires legal/product sign-off).nnappendix a: example document defines the integrated runtime safety gate and benchmark gate used by runtime, kernel scheduling, and release teams to evaluate changes to the serving stack (kernels, scheduler policies, routing/fallback logic, and runtime control plane). it describes the architecture of the gate, the required benchmark suite, profiling and sampling playbooks, release checklist integration points, runbooks for common degradation scenarios, and known issues that should block an automated gate.nnscope and intent:n- scope: prs that touch runtime execution kernels, scheduler policy code, model microbenchmark profile (see bench/profile.yaml artifact).n2) shadow validation: candidate commits are mirrored to a shadow pool for a configurable period (default: 2 hours) using a sampled production trace. shadow runs produce a per-request delta bundle (latency, tokens, kernel-selection, cache-hit, memory residency).n3) gate evaluator: centralized job that runs the benchmark suite (see benchmark suite section) and computes pass/fail per threshold matrix.n4) release gate: if the gate passes, an automated canary rollout is permitted failing gates require triage and a blocking label.nnsafety gates and thresholds:n- latency: p50/p90/p95 (in ms) vs baseline. gate fails if p95 increases by 10 and absolute p95 200ms for interactive tiers.n- throughput: end-to-end throughput drop 8 under the same synthetic shape fails gate.n- kernel regressions: any kernel that increases median per-token gpu time by 12 fails gate unless mitigations are documented.n- fidelity: for eval prompt-sets (representative prompt set), generation quality drop 3 (measured by configured metric e.g., semantic-similarity or-task-specific metric) fails gate.n- resource usage: gpu memory usage increase 6 or sustained nvlink saturation delta 10 fails gate.nnscheduler interaction and failure taxonomy:n- decision points: admission controller, preemptive-shepherd, kernel-mapper, fallback-orchestrator.n- failure modes handled by the gate: priority inversion (detected via queueing-delay skew), handoff oscillation (rapid model-swap churn), kernel-starvation (dispatcher blocked by a slow kernel).n- allowed degradations: short-lived p99 spikes during warmstart with clear warmup profile and documented mitigation.nnprofiling playbook (step-by-step):n1) reproduce locally with microbench: run tools/microbench --model --shape and collect profile.json.n2) capture kernel traces: enable kernel-tracer (env: kernel_trace1) and run the synthetic shape for 1k requests.n3) generate the delta tokens).n5) run targeted sampling: for each bucket, select 500 representative requests using the stratified sampler to produce stable medians.n6) validate fallback behavior: for a subset, force an artificial kernel disconnect and assert fallback semantics (should succeed within configured t_fallback 150ms).n7) annotate and upload to gate: produce a gate artifact that includes delta.json, kernel traces, an experiment note, and the bench/profile.yaml file.nnbenchmark suite (tests and minimal pass criteria):n test name purpose key metrics pass criteria n------------------------------------------------n shadow-trace-replay validate end-to-end delta on sampled production traffic p95 latency delta, throughput delta, error-rate p95 5 - 20 - 50 over a minimum of 30m per stage.nnrelease checklist integration:n1) pr author attaches bench artifact and bench/profile.yaml with test shapes.n2) ci runs microbench and attaches artifacts to the pr.n3) gate evaluator runs shadow replay and benchmark suite results recorded in the pr gate/result.json.n4) on pass: auto-merge allowed when other approvals are satisfied.n5) on fail: label gate-failed applied and owners paged according to ownership table below.nnrunbooks (short actionable steps):n- runbook: shadow gate fails with p95 regression:n 1. stop the shadow feed (tools/shadowctl pause).n 2. collect delta bundle and kernel traces.n 3. run binary search: revert recent micro-optimizations or toggle quantization flags (e.g., kernel_quantizeoff) to isolate.n 4. if isolatable to a kernel, open urgent bug with severity:high, attach traces, set assignee to kernel owner.nn- runbook: canary rollout p99 spike detected:n 1. immediately scale canary back to prior weight.n 2. enable extended tracing for affected cohort.n 3. if spike correlates with kernel-change, rollback kernel rollout via the kernel-release roll-back job.nnknown issues (current triage list):n1) interleaved-batch memory safety: under certain interleaving patterns, temporary soft-gc occurs and can show higher memory high-water marks. workaround: reduce interleaving window (scheduler flag max-interleave4).n2) nvlink saturation aliasing: when a multi-socket job runs two large attention kernels concurrently, nvlink counters show aliasing spikes mitigation: stagger activation with kernel-waveform-spread2.n3) shadow replay determinism: occasional seed drift in tokenizer causes small fidelity deltas. note: canonical mitigation is to pin tokenizer version in profile.yaml.nnownership and escalation:n- gate owner: runtime prefix cache telemetry: runtime architecture overview, content: summarynthis page describes how prefix cache and kv cache telemetry is produced inside the serving runtime, how signals map to the request lifecycle (prefill vs decode), and how telemetry flows to the ingestion pipeline with controlled overhead and label cardinality.nnaudience: runtime engineers, telemetry/platform, sre/observability, and pms validating cache hit-rate and wasted prefill recommendations.nnnon-goals: this is not a cache policy/eviction algorithm spec. it focuses on instrumentation and data flow.nn---nn terminologyn- prefix cache: reuses computed prefill artifacts based on canonicalized prompt prefixes. primarily reduces prefill work.n- kv cache (decode cache): reuses key/value tensors across decode steps within a sequence (and, depending on policy, across closely related requests in multi-turn chat when safe).n- prefill: forward pass over the prompt/context to initialize attention state.n- decode: token-by-token generation after prefill.n- reuse depth: the number of tokens reused from a cached prefix (or effective reused prefill tokens).n- wasted prefill: prefill tokens computed that did not contribute to subsequent decode due to cache miss, eviction, policy, mismatch, or retry semantics.nn---nn high-level architecture (signals - ingestion)nthe runtime emits cache telemetry at two levels:n1) request-scoped event counters/histograms recorded in the hot path with bounded labels.n2) span annotations (tracing) for deep debugging and correlation with latency without adding metric cardinality.nn data flow (text diagram)n1. gateway / control plane sets request context (tenant, route, model/version, deployment mode, region) and passes a bounded tag set to the runtime.n2. runtime request lifecycle (admission - prefill - decode - completion) records cache events:n - prefix lookup result reused tokensn - kv reuse effectiveness during decoden - evictions / pressure signalsn - wasted prefill accountingn3. local runtime aggregator batches metric updates and enforces runtime-side sampling/rate limits.n4. telemetry ingestion applies allowlists and cardinality guards drops/aggregates forbidden labels.n5. storage query layer supports dashboards and batch aggregation for recommendations.nn---nn where telemetry is emitted in the runtimentelemetry is emitted in three primary components:nn 1) request context tag binding (early lifecycle)nlocation: request admission / request context constructionnnwhat happens:n- the runtime constructs a cachetelemetrycontext from request metadata.n- only allowlisted label values are accepted (e.g., model family or normalized model id rather than raw model string if needed).nnkey point: all downstream metric calls use this pre-baked context to avoid repeated tag assembly overhead.nn 2) prefix cache instrumentation (prefill stage)nlocation: before prefill begins, during prefix lookup/validationnnsignals recorded:n- prefix lookup attempts and outcomes (hit/miss/partial).n- reuse depth / reused tokens histogram.n- miss reason (bounded enum).nnwhy here: this is the earliest point where we know whether we can avoid some prefill compute.nn 3) kv cache instrumentation (decode stage)nlocation: decode loop and/or scheduler hooks around decode step executionnnsignals recorded:n- kv reuse effectiveness (e.g., percent of decode steps with valid kv reuse, or reused kv blocks).n- miss reason events when decode cannot reuse expected state.nnwhy here: kv cache effectiveness impacts throughput/latency and can diverge from prefix cache results depending on batching, retries, and scheduling.nn 4) evictions memory pressure (continuous)nlocation: cache allocator / eviction policynnsignals recorded:n- eviction counter (by eviction reason enum).n- pressure gauges (e.g., bytes used, eviction rate proxy).nnwhy here: hit-rate drops are often a symptom of pressure these indicators are needed for triage and recommendations.nn 5) wasted prefill accounting (prefill completion decode correlation)nlocation: request completion (or first-decode checkpoint) where we can attribute whether prefill work yielded reuse/benefitnnsignals recorded:n- wasted prefill tokens histogram/bucketed counter.nnkey nuance: we avoid logging any raw prompt content wasted prefill is computed from token counts and reuse indicators.nn---nn mapping telemetry to the request lifecyclenthis section ties the metrics to lifecycle points. this mapping is important for correctness (no double counting) and for interpreting dashboards.nn lifecycle timelinen1. admissionn - bind deployment_mode, region, route_id, model_id, model_version_id (bounded/allowlisted), and request-shape buckets.nn2. prefix lookup (start of prefill)n - emit: prefix_lookup_totalresulthitmisspartial, miss_reason?n - emit: prefix_reuse_tokens_bucket histogram (reuse depth)nn3. prefill executionn - emit: prefill_tokens_bucket histogram (request shape)n - no prompt content is recorded.nn4. decode loopn - emit: kv_reuse_events_totalresulthitmiss, miss_reason?n - emit: decode_tokens_bucket histogramnn5. completion / finalizationn - emit: wasted_prefill_tokens_bucket (derived)n - emit: end-to-end counters (request count, retry count if applicable, with retry-safe semantics)nn streaming retriesn- metrics must be retry-safe. when a stream retry occurs, the runtime must not double-count prefix/kv events from the original attempt.n- the runtime tags a request attempt with a stable request id and attempt index and uses first successful attempt wins semantics for counters that should be once-per-logical-request.n- tracing spans may include per-attempt annotations for debugging, but metric emission stays bounded.nn continuous batching (batched prefill)n- when multiple requests share a continuous batch prefill, hit attribution must be per-request (not per-batch), while shared compute should not inflate hit counters.n- the instrumentation uses request-local reuse accounting derived from the cache lookup outcome and per-request token ranges in the batch.nn---nn signal taxonomy (what we emit)nexact names and label sets are governed by the observability standards and the adr. this section describes the classes of telemetry and how they should be interpreted.nn a) hit/miss countersnpurpose: track cache effectiveness over time.nn- prefix cache hit-rate: did we reuse prefill artifacts for this request?n- kv cache hit-rate/effectiveness: did decode reuse expected kv state efficiently?nnpartial hit semantics:n- a partial hit occurs when some prefix tokens are reused but the full desired prefix is not reusable (e.g., hash mismatch after n tokens, or version mismatch).n- partial hits should be visible as separate result class so operators can distinguish completely cold from almost warm.nn b) reuse depth histogramsnpurpose: hit-rate alone is not enough reuse depth shows whether hits are meaningful.nn- reused_tokens bucketed by prompt length bucket and model.n- enables: detecting regressions where hit-rate stays flat but reused tokens collapse.nn c) evictions and pressurenpurpose: root-cause hit-rate regressions and support recommendations.nn- eviction count by reason (bounded enum).n- pressure indicator gauges (bytes used, high-watermark , or eviction rate proxy).nn d) wasted prefillnpurpose: identify compute that didnt pay off and is often fixable (routing locality, ttl, policy flags, canonicalization).nn- wasted prefill should be interpreted alongside evictions and miss reasons.n- high wasted prefill with high eviction pressure typically indicates insufficient cache capacity or ttl mismatch.nn e) trace annotations (low cardinality alternative)npurpose: correlate cache events to latency and scheduler behavior.nn- spans annotate cache lookup outcomes, reuse depth, and eviction/pressure snapshots.n- traces are sampled separately from metrics and are not required for baseline dashboards.nn---nn join keys and label strategy (how we slice without cardinality blowups)ntelemetry must be actionable by model/route/deployment mode/region and request shape while staying within budgets.nn required dimensions (bounded)n- deployment_mode: hosted dedicated privaten- region: canonical region code (bounded)n- model_id: normalized model identifier (bounded set)n- model_version_id: allowlisted stable id (bounded, rollover-safe)n- route_id: internal stable route identifier (bounded not raw url paths)n- request_shape: buckets (e.g., prompt length bucket, total tokens bucket)nn explicitly not allowed in metric labelsn- raw tenant ids, user ids, raw prompt hashes with high uniqueness, request ids, or free-form strings.nn tenant slicingn- tenant-level views are provided via:n 1) dedicated/private deployments where tenant count is naturally small and allowlisted.n 2) analytics tables / batch aggregates where controlled rollups are computed off-metrics.nn---nn sampling, rate limiting, and overhead controlsnthe runtime must keep instrumentation overhead near-zero (especially at p95/p99). controls:nn1. metrics aggregation: use in-process counters/histograms with periodic flush avoid per-token metric emissions.n2. event sampling: high-volume events (e.g., decode reuse) use probabilistic sampling, then are scaled at query time where appropriate.n3. local rate limiting: if a component produces unusually high event volume, the runtime clamps emission and increments a dropped_by_ratelimit counter.n4. feature flags: all new telemetry is behind runtime config flags so we can canary and roll back quickly.nnoperational guidance:n- prefer measuring reuse at request boundaries (prefill completion, request completion) instead of per decode token.n- use histograms/buckets rather than raw counts by unique values.nn---nn privacy and data handlingn- no raw prompt text is emitted.n- prompt-derived features are restricted to coarse buckets (prompt length) and cache-safe canonicalization outcomes (hit/miss/partial), not raw hashes.n- tracing annotations must not include prompt content only bounded enums and counts.nn---nn ingestion pipeline expectations (runtime - telemetry backend)nthe runtime assumes the ingestion pipeline will:n- enforce label allowlists and drop unknown/unsafe labels.n- apply cardinality guards (e.g., cap series per metric per time window).n- preserve monotonicity expectations for counters handle process restarts and counter resets.n- maintain consistent mapping for model/version identifiers so dashboards can join across gateway logs and runtime metrics.nnfailure detection:n- a metric drop should be distinguishable from a true hit-rate change.n- the pipeline should publish a health indicator metric (ingested series count, drop count by reason).nn---nn common failure modes and how the architecture mitigates themn1) double counting due to streaming retriesn- mitigation: emit once-per-logical-request counters at completion track attempt index only in traces.nn2) incorrect hit attribution under continuous batchingn- mitigation: compute per-request reuse from request-local token ranges add integration tests that simulate batched prefill.nn3) cardinality explosion from route or model labelsn- mitigation: route_id/model_version_id allowlists, normalization, ingestion-side guards.nn4) hit-rate regressions caused by workload mix changesn- mitigation: always break down by request shape buckets and model use guardrail alerts that consider mix.nn5) telemetry overhead regressionn- mitigation: perf canary gates and sampling defaults ability to disable high-volume sub-metrics independently.nn---nn validation checklist attributed to version mismatch.n - ttl expiration produces misses attributed to ttl_expired.nn2. overhead:n - p95/p99 latency regression is within the perf-canary budget.n - cpu overhead from metric filters.nn4. cardinality:n - series count stays within budget after enabling all breakdowns.n - ingestion drop counters remain near zero.nn---nn ownership and change managementn- runtime decompression kernel handshake manual, content: summarynnthis document defines redwood inferences official escape hatch strategy for handling sustained congestion and kernel saturation: a coordinated congestion decomposition and kernel-handshake protocol that (1) reduces tail-latency exposure, (2) preserves critical slos by controlled fidelity degradation, and (3) provides a clear operator runbook for diagnosing and recovering from congestion events. the guidance spans runtime architecture trade-offs, scheduler/kernel interactions, profiling checks, benchmark validation, release notes for v0.14 of the handshake protocol, and a known-issues appendix.nnwhy this existsnn- congestion is multi-dimensional: cpu/host networking, gpu kernel throughput, kv cache pressure, and admission-controller throttles interact and can amplify tail latency.n- previous ad-hoc mitigations (global queue cuts, blunt shedding) risked client-visible errors or large quality regressions.n- this manual codifies a minimal, observable, and reversible path the escape hatch that runtime and operations can use without full-scale rollback.nnscope and ownersnn- scope: serving runtime (request orchestration, scheduler/kernel admission, kv cache warmup), telemetry contracts between runtime and scheduler, operator runbook.n- owners: runtime-scheduler (primary), kernel-engineering (secondary), eng-sre (oncall runbook), observability (telemetry contract).nnkey concepts (short)nn- congestion decomposition: break an incident into orthogonal stressors (kernel queueing, kv miss storm, network slope) and treat each with targeted mitigations.n- kernel handshake: a lightweight per-request negotiation between dispatcher and kernel to confirm admission and a fidelity/priority token.n- escape hatch stages: 1) soft-cohort shaping, 2) priority-aware fidelity staircasing, 3) kernel offload (batch-eviction fallback model), 4) emergency rejection (last resort).nnarchitecture overviewnn1) dispatcher - scheduler - kernel handshake flownn- dispatcher issues a pre-admit probe to scheduler with metadata: model_id, sequence_length_est, client_priority_tier, kv_prefetch_hint, trace_id.n- scheduler responds with a handshake token: admitted: bool, expected_wait_ms: int, fidelity_profile: string, kernel_slot_hint: id, trace_flags.n- dispatcher attaches token to the request and routes to the claimed kernel node. kernel validates the token (nonce timestamp) before binding resources.nnbenefits:n- avoids blind offload: kernels only begin expensive work once token validated.n- enables admission-time decisions (expected wait) surfaced to callers and observability.nn2) congestion decomposition surface pointsnn- kernel queueing: long kernel start latency despite short network and dispatch times.n- kv cache miss storm: many cold sessions with repeated kv-prefetches causing memory pressure and eviction churn.n- dispatcher/multiplex contention: overloaded event loop or slow grpc channels.n- network backpressure: transient nic saturation or cross-az variance.nntelemetry contract (required signals)nn- required per-request fields (exported to traces/metrics): pre_admit_ts, handshake_issue_ts, handshake_response_ts, kernel_bind_ts, kernel_start_ts, kernel_complete_ts, kv_miss_count, admitted_fidelity_profile, kernel_slot_id, tv_cpu_ms, gpu_busy_ms.n- aggregates/alerts: 95/99/99.9 kernel_bind_time kv_miss_ratio over 2-minute windows admission_reject_rate per-model fidelity-downgrade-rate.nnescape hatch stages (detailed)nnstage 0 detectionn- triggers (any one): 99.9 kernel_bind_time 500ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows or kv_miss_ratio 0.25 and error_rate increase 0.5.n- action: escalate to oncall, annotate traces with incident_id, and enable enhanced sampling for affected models.nnstage 1 soft-cohort shaping (fast, reversible)n- goal: reduce inflow rate using priority-aware shaping and client-visible hints.n- steps: 1) scheduler flips cohort-shaped admission (80 of low priority requests are moved to a rate-limited queue). 2) emit a 429-with-hint response that instructs sdk to backoff optionally switch to smaller max_tokens.n- expected impact: 2040 kernel queue reduction within 30s.nnstage 2 priority-aware fidelity staircasing (controlled quality tradeoff)n- goal: reduce per-token kernel work for non-critical requests.n- steps: 1) for affected kernels, inject fidelity_profile override via handshake token (e.g., quantized-8b-fast, llm-lite-summary). 2) scheduler ensures canary a/b percentages for fidelity change (default 5 - 25 - 50 per 2-minute steps). 3) monitor quality regressions using sentinel prompt set evaluation (see profiling section).n- rollback: automatic if quality alert threshold or error rate increases.nnstage 3 kernel offload and fallback routingn- goal: preserve slos by moving some load off saturated kernels to compatible fallback variants (smaller model, different gpu class, cpu-based short-run).n- steps: 1) router consults fallback_matrix for model compatibility. 2) for in-flight requests with long expected wait, router reissues handshake to fallback kernel with incremental fidelity. 3) upgrade path: when capacity returns, tokens expire and dispatcher resumes original routing.nnstage 4 emergency rejection (last resort)n- goal: prevent catastrophic cascade and maintain control plane stability.n- steps: 1) admission controller returns structured rejection with exact reason code and safe duration. 2) operators run immediate remediation (kernel drain, node reboot, capacity surge via dedicated burst policy).nnoperator runbook (step-by-step)nn1) triage (first 5 minutes)n- open incident and tag affected models.n- run quick decomposition checklist: check kernel_bind_time, kv_miss_ratio, dispatch loop latency, nic metrics.n- if kernel_bind_time is primary, apply stage 1. if kv_miss_ratio is primary, apply stage 1 and enable kv-prefetch backoff.nn2) apply stage 2 (if stage 1 insufficient)n- use admin cli to apply fidelity overrides for model x in zone y:nn- cli example:n rwdctl runtime handshake override --model xlarge-1 --zone us-west-2 --profile quant8-fast --fraction 0.25 --reason incident-nn3) escalate to kernel-engineering if kernel_busy_ms continues 90 for 5 minutes. provide trace ids and sample payloads.nn4) recovery validationn- monitor sentinel prompt set regression suite (see profiling checks below).n- gradually remove overrides once 95/99 kernel_bind_time back within slo for 10 consecutive 1-minute windows.nnprofiling benchmark verificationnn- purpose: ensure any fidelity changes do not create unacceptable quality regressions, and that kernel handshake yields expected latency improvements.nn1) sentinel prompt set (operational)n- a curated set of 200 prompts per model capturing worst-case sequence lengths, kv dependence, and multi-turn. run with fidelity variants and compare: exact match rate, bleu-like similarity, and latency distribution.n- baseline run command (local harness):n python perf_harness.py --model xlarge-1 --profile quant8-fast --concurrency 50 --duration 5m --tracingnn2) microbenchmarks for handshake overheadn- expectation: pre-admit handshake roundtrip adds n- apply soft shaping: rwdctl runtime admission shape --model --cohort low --rate-limit 20rpsn- apply fidelity override: rwdctl runtime handshake override --model --profile quant8-fast --fraction 0.25n- validate sentinel suite: python perf_harness.py --model --profile --sanitynnpost-incident follow-up (rca template)nn- description: short summary of what triggered the escape hatch and which stage was used.n- root cause decomposition: kernel-binding vs kv-miss vs dispatch.n- evidence: traces, metrics, cli actions taken, timestamps.n- remediation: code change, scheduler tuning, capacity adjustment.n- preventative experiments: shadow runs, benchmark expansion.nnappendix: json handshake token examplennn token: rwd-tn-1234abcd,n admitted: true,n expected_wait_ms: 48,n fidelity_profile: quant8-fast,n kernel_slot_hint: k-az3-7,n issued_at: 2026-10-03t15:12:22z,n nonce: f3b9a2,n sign: sha256:...nnnappendix: quick signal glossarynn- kernel_bind_time: time between handshake_response_ts and kernel_bind_ts.n- kv_miss_ratio: fraction of requests that encountered at least one kv miss in the warmup window.n- admitted_fidelity_profile: the effective fidelity the kernel will run.nnrelated pages and referencesnn- see runtime-decision-graph-and-observed-behaviour-catalog dsid_076faead3b9a40d08587c1c253ff2865, source_type: confluence, title: fidelity adaptation: evaluation, rollback backstop, and simulation manifest, content: overviewnnthis document defines the fidelity-adaptation evaluation manifest and the operational backstop policies used when runtime adapts model fidelity (quantized variants, model variants, or batching/caching induced fidelity changes). it specifies: goals, evaluation metrics and thresholds, a canary/simulation protocol, rollback/backstop criteria, required observability signals, and example configuration snippets used by latency) and allow rapid operator intervention.n- scope: applies to hosted, dedicated, and private runtime deployments where automatic fidelity adaptation is enabled. does not replace model-level release qa.nndefinitions and acronymsn------------------------n- fidelity adaptation: any runtime action that may change perceived output quality (e.g., switching to a quantized kernel, using a smaller model-variant, applying aggressive kv-prefetching that truncates context).n- rar (relative acceptance rate): production a/b style metric estimating fraction of responses accepted by downstream classifiers or human raters relative to baseline.n- delta-q: normalized quality delta computed from a weighted combination of evaluation metrics (embedding cosine, task-specific metric, and rar). expressed in percentage points.n- backstop policy: an automated control that pauses rollouts and reverts routing when a delta-q or other trigger exceeds thresholds.nnkey slos and thresholdsn-----------------------n- latency slo (p50/p95/p99): must not regress by more than 10ms / 30ms / 75ms relative to baseline variant during canary.n- cost target: expected per-token compute cost reduction 7 (measured over 24h sample) for the candidate to be considered.n- delta-q backstop: immediate rollback if delta-q 1.5 percentage points relative to baseline).n- rar backstop: immediate rollback if production rar delta 0.985 for small quant changes), task-specific accuracy (e.g., exact-match), rouge-l / bleu where applicable.n- shadow traffic comparison: mirror 2 of live traffic for 48 hours compute latency quantiles, rar, and token-cost.n- live canary: gradual traffic ramp 0.5 - 2 - 10 over 2472 hours with active monitoring windows.n- synthetic surge test: run 2x expected peak minutes.n4. validate: at each stage validate: 1) delta-q -0.5, 2) latency p99 within threshold, 3) kernel failure rate 0.1 over 10 minutes.n- soft stop: pause ramp and notify on-call if delta-q between -0.5 and -1.5.n- manual backstop: operator can enact a targeted routing policy that pins affected customers to baseline model-variant for up to 30 days while investigation occurs.n- for dedicated/private deployments: follow local operator rollback steps in addition to control-plane backstop see deployment-guides for customer-specific rollback playbooks.nnobservability and telemetry latency, per-token cpu/gpu time, kernel invocation count, kernel error code histogram.n- quality signals: embedded cosine distribution, rar estimate, sampled human feedback tags (if available).n- resource signals: gpu occupancy, gpu memory high-water, numa imbalance score, nvlink error counters.n- control traces: request provenance tag including canary-id, variant-id, kernel-subtype, and sampling decision.nnalerting rules (examples)n------------------------n- canary-deltaq-critical: delta-q pager - auto-rollback.n- canary-latency-tail: p99 increase 50 compared to baseline for 10m - signals (export semantics), content: purposenthis page defines the runtime-level backpressure and saturation signals used by hosted circuit breakers load shedding. it documents:n- what signals the serving runtime emits (queues, throughput, kv cache, memory pressure, fragmentation proxies).n- exact semantics and units.n- export pipeline (metric types, sampling, aggregation, and cardinality constraints).n- how upstream systems should interpret the signals without creating feedback loops.nnthis is a reference for runtime, sre, gateway/control plane, smart routing, and observability.nn---nn scope and non-goalsnin scopen- signals emitted by the gpu-serving runtime at admission/scheduling boundaries.n- metrics intended for near-real-time overload decisions (seconds).n- metrics intended for dashboards/alerting (minutes).nnnon-goalsn- per-request tracing details (handled by tracing pipeline).n- model-quality or output correctness signals.n- fine-grained per-gpu/per-process troubleshooting metrics with high cardinality (those live in restricted debug endpoints and are not used for load shedding).nn---nn runtime architecture context (where backpressure happens)nat a high level, the runtime splits work into:n1) admission: request accepted by runtime process (after gateway/routing). some requests may be queued locally before scheduling.n2) prefill: prompt encoding kv cache population.n3) decode: incremental token generation using the kv cache.n4) streaming: tokens flushed to the upstream response stream.nnthe runtime enforces backpressure at two points:n- runtime admission: applies concurrency caps and queue limits (soft/hard), returning overload signals upstream when exceeded.n- scheduler: dynamically reduces effective concurrency when saturation is detected (e.g., memory pressure, kv cache exhaustion), and can mark the instance as degraded for routing.nnthe signals below are designed to be robust under:n- prompt-length variance (prefill heavy vs decode heavy workloads)n- streaming-induced tail amplificationn- noisy-neighbor patterns (single tenant sending long prompts / high max_tokens)nn---nn signal taxonomynwe classify runtime saturation into four categories:n1) queueing saturation: backlog is growing and/or wait time is increasing.n2) compute saturation: tokens/sec is at or near sustainable peak marginal load increases latency sharply.n3) memory / kv cache saturation: kv cache capacity or allocation efficiency is limiting throughput oom risk increases.n4) health degradation: dependency or internal faults (allocator errors, repeated cuda errors) impacting capacity.nnupstream policies should prefer early, stable signals (queue depth queue wait) over late symptoms (timeouts).nn---nn export contract (how we emit signals)n metric transportn- primary export: prometheus (scraped) and mirrored into our metrics backend.n- secondary export: opentelemetry metrics for long-term correlation (not used in admission decisions).nn resolution and update cadencen- breaker-grade metrics update every 1s (rolling window) where feasible.n- most gauges/counters are exported at 5s resolution.n- percentiles (e.g., queue wait p95) are computed using runtime-side histograms and exported as prometheus histograms.nn cardinality constraints (hard requirements)nto avoid metric blowups:n- no per-request ids.n- no per-customer dimensions.n- labels are limited to: region, cluster, runtime_pool, model_family, route_class (small finite sets).n- optional label model is only allowed when the catalog size is bounded in that pool otherwise prefer model_family.nnimportant: if a team needs high-cardinality breakdowns for a live incident, use the restricted debug endpoint (see debug-only signals), not prometheus.nn---nn core signals (required)n 1) scheduler queue depth (prefill / decode)nthese are the primary early-warning signals.nnmetricsn- runtime_scheduler_queue_depthstageprefill (gauge, requests)n- runtime_scheduler_queue_depthstagedecode (gauge, requests)nnsemanticsn- number of requests currently waiting to be scheduled for the given stage.n- excludes requests actively running on gpu.nninterpretationn- sustained non-zero decode queue depth correlates strongly with rising p95 latency for streaming workloads.n- prefill queue depth spikes are common during bursty long-prompt traffic use queue wait to differentiate transient bursts vs persistent saturation.nn 2) scheduler queue wait timenmetricsn- runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucketstageprefill (histogram)n- runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucketstagedecode (histogram)nnsemanticsn- time from enqueue start of gpu execution for that stage.nninterpretationn- queue depth without wait time can be misleading (e.g., many tiny tasks).n- for overload decisions, queue wait p95 is preferred.nn 3) effective tokens/sec and saturation rationwe export both actual tokens/sec and saturation ratio relative to a calibrated baseline.nnmetricsn- runtime_tokens_generated_total (counter, tokens)n- runtime_token_throughput_tps (gauge, tokens/sec runtime-computed over rolling 10s window)n- runtime_compute_saturation_ratio (gauge, 0.02.0)nnsemanticsn- runtime_token_throughput_tps is derived from the counter and a stable rolling window.n- runtime_compute_saturation_ratio is observed_tps / sustainable_tps_baseline.n - the baseline is poolmodel_family specific and shipped via config it is periodically recalibrated from load tests.nninterpretationn- ratio 0.95 sustained indicates compute saturation additional load should be shed/queued.n- ratio 0.9 correlates with admission stalls and/or forced evictions.n- under kv pressure, prefill may look healthy while decode queue wait grows (decode needs kv residency longer).nn 6) kv cache eviction / reclamation pressurenmetricsn- runtime_kv_cache_evictions_total (counter)n- runtime_kv_cache_reclaim_failures_total (counter)nnsemanticsn- evictions occur when the runtime must reclaim kv blocks earlier than ideal to admit new work.n- reclaim failures indicate allocator could not free sufficient contiguous blocks (often fragmentation-related).nninterpretationn- rising eviction rate during steady traffic is a strong signal for load shedding or reduced max_tokens caps.nn 7) gpu memory headroom and allocator pressurenwe avoid exporting raw per-gpu memory usage by device id (cardinality and privacy concerns). we export pool-level aggregates.nnmetricsn- runtime_gpu_memory_bytes_used (gauge, pool aggregate)n- runtime_gpu_memory_bytes_total (gauge, pool aggregate)n- runtime_gpu_memory_headroom_ratio (gauge, 0.01.0)nnsemanticsn- aggregate across devices in the pool (sum used / sum total).n- includes model weights runtime allocations kv cache arena.nninterpretationn- headroom ratio 250ms for 30sn - compute saturation ratio 0.95 for 30sn - kv utilization 0.92 for 30sn - allocator retry rate 1/s for 30sn- enter overloaded when (any):n - decode queue wait p95 750ms for 20sn - gpu headroom ratio 0.5 for 60sn- exit criteria require the signal to remain below threshold for a longer interval (typically 60120s) to avoid flapping.nnnote: these thresholds are defaults policy engine can override per pool/model_family with guardrails.nn---nn debug-only signals (restricted not for general dashboards)nfor deep performance work we also maintain:n- per-gpu device utilization, memory, and kernel timingsn- per-model exact tps baselinesn- per-batch sizes and microbatch timingsnnthese are available via:n- runtime-admin endpoint (restricted network rbac)n- short-lived incident capture bundlesnndo not build automated shedding rules on debug-only signals.nn---nn how upstream systems should use these signalsn gateway / admission controlnrecommended order of evaluation (fast to compute, stable):n1) runtime runtime_overload_state (overloaded reject early)n2) decode queue wait p95 and queue depth (protect p95/p99)n3) kv utilization eviction rate (protect memory stability)n4) compute saturation ratio (protect throughput)nnguidance:n- prefer consistent, explicit overload errors over timeouts.n- avoid retry storms: only shed with stable retry-after contracts (see adr-014 for semantics).nn smart routingn- use overloaded state to avoid routing new traffic into an already-saturated pool.n- use degraded as a hint to prefer alternate pools/regions for latency-sensitive tiers.n- do not rapidly oscillate between regions based on 15s spikes require sustained state changes ( 30s) or use the routing systems built-in damping.nn sre dashboards and alertsn- alerts should be based on sustained signals and correlated with customer-visible impact metrics (5xx/timeouts/latency), not on single gauges.nn---nn example promql snippets (for dashboards)ndecode queue wait p95 by regionn- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, region) (rate(runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucketstagedecode5m)))nnkv utilization ratio (pool aggregate)n- avg by (region, runtime_pool) (runtime_kv_cache_utilization_ratio)nncompute saturation ratio (p95 across instances approximated by max)n- max by (region, runtime_pool) (runtime_compute_saturation_ratio)nnallocator retries raten- sum by (region, runtime_pool) burst may not require shedding if decode remains stable.n3) kv pressure can masquerade as compute saturation. when kv utilization is high, throughput may drop while gpus look busy.n4) sampling noise: 1s gauges will be spiky. use 3060s windows for state changes.n5) metric delays: scrape pipeline delays are typically 210s. runtime state gauges help reduce dependency on downstream aggregation.nn---nn
