manifest, content: overview:nnthis document defines a deterministic replay pipeline and the operator safety contract used to validate kernel/operator changes before and during runtime rollouts. the goal is to enable repeatable repros for latency/correctness regressions, reduce time-to-diagnosis for oncall, and provide a standardized canary rollback procedure for experimental kernels and scheduler policies.nnscope:n- deterministic capture and replay for text-generation and chat request surfaces (hosted dedicated pools).n- canary orchestration for kernel/operator binary changes and scheduler policy updates.n- safety checks and telemetry contract required for any kernel-level change deployed to production.nnnon-goals:n- full deterministic replay of external tool/plugin side-effects (these are captured best-effort).n- replaying privacy-sensitive payloads outside of secure reproducer environments.nndesign summary:n1) capture: lightweight per-request snapshot containing request proto, sequence tokens (first n tokens), model variant, session kv hints, scheduler decisions, and kernel hints. captures are sampled at adjustable rates (default 0.1). all captures are salted and stored in an encrypted replay store with access controls.nn2) canonicalization: a reproducible normalization step strips reorder-insignificant metadata (timestamps, trace ids) and pins kernel-versioned artifacts so that the replay input deterministically maps to kernel behavior.nn3) replay harness: an isolated, deterministic executor that replays a captured request on a pinned model binary with seeded rng, fixed batch shapes, and a frozen scheduler policy. replays run in a shadow environment that mirrors runtime kernel flags used in production.nn4) diffing triage: replay output (token stream timings kernel trace) is diffed against the original recorded output. differences are classified with signatures (content-drift, timing-regression, soft-failure, hard-failure).nndeterministic capture schema (summary table):n field description retention n---------n capture_id uuid for replay artifact 90d n trace_version schema version 90d n request_proto sanitized request payload (pii removed) 90d n seed_state rng/initial-state for model runtime 90d n kernel_hints kernel invocation metadata (flags/kernels used) 90d n scheduler_decision assigned slot, priority bucket 90d n sample_metrics timing, memory usage summary 90d nnoperator safety checklist (required before any kernel/operator rollout):n- preconditions:n - unittest suite coverage for changed operator 95 of modified code paths.n - microbenchmarks for tight loops created and committed to perf-suite.n - static analysis asan/tsan pass for proposed patch.n- canary plan:n - canary cohort definition (tenant list or synthetic traffic) n - canary duration: minimum 72 hours real traffic 24 hours synthetic stress.n - acceptance thresholds defined (see slos table below).n- observability telemetry:n - kernel must emit the agreed telemetry keys (kernel.execution_time_ms, kernel.exec_count, kernel.error_code, kernel.fidelity_tag).n - trace sampling rate for capture increased to 1 for canary window.n - alert hooks configured for anomaly conditions (automated rollback triggers).n- rollback strategy:n - immediate circuit-breaker if any hard-failure signature observed in 0.01 of canary requests.n - staged rollback (canary - cohort - global) via policy manager.nncanary runbook (step-by-step):n1. prepare artifacts:n 1.1 build kernel binary with embedded build-id and deterministic metadata.n 1.2 publish to artifact-repo with tag: canary/-.n 1.3 create canary deployment in test cluster with replica_count2, isolate networking.n2. pre-flight checks (automated):n 2.1 run unit microbench pipelines (must pass).n 2.2 run golden replays for 50 representative captures (zero content deviation allowed).n3. start canary (rolling):n 3.1 route 0.5 production traffic to canary cohort and enable replay capture at 1 sampling.n 3.2 monitor kpis for the first 30 minutes: tail-99 latency, kernel.exec_time_ms p99, error_count.n4. escalation and rollback policies:n 4.1 if any of the automated checks trigger (see thresholds) perform immediate rollback and mark change blocked.n 4.2 if degraded but within tolerance, expand to cohort-controlled ramp and continue data (sophie chen) - tightened canary gating thresholds, added chaos scenariosn, doc_id: dsid_295ecf5d80084e6bbebfba0f029619f3, source_type: confluence, title: granular eviction and adaptive execution patterns for mixed inference workloads, content: summarynnthis document describes the design, operational controls, and runbook for the granular eviction and adaptive execution patterns (geaep) subsystem in the redwood serving runtime. geaep is a set of runtime techniques that: (1) reduce unnecessary kv-cache evictions, (2) enable per-request execution path selection (fast path vs. accuracy path), and (3) smooth contention across heterogeneous kernel families in the gpu pool. the guidance here is intended for runtime engineers, sres handling inference incidents, and product teams evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs.nnwhy this doc existsnn- prior problems addressed: eviction storms during traffic spikes, oscillation between quantized and full-precision kernels, and sudden tail-latency increases for mixed short/long sequences.n- goals: lower tail latency for short-prefix requests, reduce unnecessary recompute, expose safe knobs for cost-vs-accuracy routing, and provide clear operational steps for triage and rollback.nndesign principlesnn1) local, demand-driven granularity: evictions and prefetches are controlled per-shard and per-session rather than globally. this avoids thrashing when a single tenant (or bursty bot) requests long sequences.n2) execution adaptivity: requests carry an execution-hint header that lets the scheduler choose a lightweight kernel (quantized, truncated context, prefix-cached) or the accuracy path (full-precision, full-kv materialization). default policy is conservative (favor accuracy) unless overridden by explicit cost profile or model-variant rules.n3) cost-safety guards: automated budget limits and soft-fallbacks prevent runaway cost when adaptivity picks expensive paths.nnkey concepts and terminologynn- shard-eviction-window: configurable time window used to compute per-shard eviction score.n- per-request execution-hint: request metadata field (execution_hint) with values: fast_path balanced accuracy_path.n- eviction-stabilizer: smoothing function that delays eviction decisions when churn is detected.n- kernel-ladder: ordered family of kernels (e.g. q4_8_fast, q8_0_balanced, fp16_full) that the dispatcher may move through for a request.nnconfiguration reference (example yaml)nnruntime_geaep:n enabled: truen shard_eviction_window_sec: 60n eviction_score_threshold: 0.12n eviction_stabilizer_alpha: 0.6n execution_hint_defaults:n short_prefix: fast_pathn long_prefix: balancedn kernel_ladder:n - q4_8_fastn - q8_0_balancedn - fp16_fulln cost_safety_budget_tokens_per_min: 20000n per_tenant_hard_cap_tokens_per_min: 100000nnexplanation of important keysnn- eviction_score_threshold: a normalized value 0,1 shards with score threshold become candidates for eviction. we tune this to balance memory pressure against recompute cost.n- eviction_stabilizer_alpha: smoothing parameter for exponential moving average used by the stabilizer. higher more inertia.n- cost_safety_budget_tokens_per_min: safety budget applied to adaptivity decisions once exhausted, adaptivity falls back to balanced or fast_path depending on flags.nnobservability and metricsnninstrument the following metrics (already emitted by ri-runtime v3.8):n- runtime.geaep.eviction_rate.per_shard (gauge, evictions/min)n- runtime.geaep.eviction_candidates (gauge)n- runtime.geaep.prefetch_hits (counter)n- runtime.geaep.execution_path.countpathfast_pathbalancedaccuracy_path (counter)n- runtime.geaep.kernel_switches.count (counter)n- runtime.kvcache.recompute.tokens_cost (counter)n- runtime.geaep.adaptivity_budget_remaining (gauge)nnalerting thresholds (suggested)nn- p0: runtime.geaep.eviction_rate.per_shard 0.5 for more than 2 minutes and 99th_latency.service 800ms for a modeled short-prefix route - pager.n- p1: runtime.geaep.adaptivity_budget_remaining page to oncall if impacting cost or slos.n- p2: kernel_switches.count rate increases 5x baseline over 10 minutes with increased tail latencies - slack alert to serving-runtime.nnoperational runbook: common incidentsnn1) eviction storm (symptoms: sudden spikes in doc_id: dsid_c85ce50397ba4060941e5ba19ae72890, source_type: confluence, title: adr-0147: prefix kv cache hit-rate definitions, partial-hit semantics, and attribution, content: summarynthis adr defines the canonical semantics for prefix/kv cache hit-rate in the redwood serving runtime, including:n- what counts as a hit vs miss (token-level and request-level)n- how to represent partial hits (reuse depth)n- how hit/miss is attributed across multi-turn chat, streaming, and retriesnnthe goal is to make cache telemetry consistent across runtime, ingestion, dashboards, and the recommendations pipeline, while remaining privacy-safe and avoiding cardinality blowups.nn---nn statusnaccepted (effective for cache telemetry v2 rollout).nn---nn context and problem statementnhistorically, teams used cache hit-rate to mean different things:n- was there a cache entry? (lookup-level)n- how much of the prompt was reused? (token-level)n- did we avoid most prefill? (latency/compute-level)nnthese diverging definitions produced inconsistent dashboards and false positives during incident response (e.g., streaming retry double-counting, batched prefill mis-attribution, and model version mismatch being treated as generic misses).nnwe need a definition that:n1) reflects actual compute avoided (prefill reuse),n2) works for chat where prompts grow each turn (partial reuse is normal),n3) remains stable under streaming/retries and continuous batching,n4) can be aggregated safely by model/route/region/deployment mode.nn---nn decisionn decision 1: hit-rate is defined as token-weighted reuse of cacheable prefill tokensnthe primary hit-rate is token-weighted, computed over a window:nnhitrate sum(reused_prefill_tokens) / sum(eligible_prefill_tokens)nnwhere:n- eligible_prefill_tokens are prompt tokens that the runtime would have had to prefill if no cache reuse occurred, restricted to the portion of the prompt considered cacheable (see definitions).n- reused_prefill_tokens are prompt tokens whose kv states were reused from cache (prefix cache / kv reuse) instead of recomputed.nnthis hit-rate is not a lookup success rate, and it is not a boolean per-request metric. it is designed to answer: how much prefill compute did caching avoid?nn decision 2: partial hits are represented by reuse depth (reused tokens), not a separate partial hit-ratenpartial hits are expected for chat and any workload with shared prefixes.nwe represent partial hits by reporting reused_prefill_tokens (and optionally reuse_depth_bucket) so dashboards can show reuse distributions.nn decision 3: request-level classifications are derived (full_hit / partial_hit / miss) but are secondarynfor triage and recommendations, we also derive request-level outcomes for sampled traces and low-cardinality counters:n- full_hit: reused_prefill_tokens eligible_prefill_tokens and eligible_prefill_tokens 0n- partial_hit: 0 0n- not_eligible: eligible_prefill_tokens 0 (e.g., caching disabled by policy)nntoken-weighted hit-rate remains the source of truth.nn decision 4: streaming retries must not double count hit/missnfor streaming retries (client reconnects, gateway retry-on-timeout), the runtime must ensure cache hit/miss counters are emitted once per logical request, not once per transport attempt.nimplementation guidance is included below.nn---nn definitions and terminologyn request lifecycle termsn- prefill: processing the prompt/context to produce initial kv states.n- decode: iterative token generation after prefill.nncaching impacts prefill compute decode is not part of the cache hit-rate denominator.nn cache types (as used in telemetry)n- prefix cache: reuse keyed by a stable hash of a canonicalized token prefix, returning a handle to cached kv states.n- kv cache: the underlying key/value state used during attention. in practice, prefix cache hit results in kv reuse.nntelemetry uses the terms prefix cache and kv reuse to distinguish lookup/entry behavior from reuse depth and compute avoided.nn token countsnall token counts are expressed in model tokens (post-tokenization).nn- prompt_tokens_total: total tokens in the request prompt/context.n- prompt_tokens_cacheable: tokens in the prompt that are eligible for reuse under the active policy.n - this explicitly excludes non-cacheable segments if/when we introduce them (e.g., policy-based exclusions). if no exclusions exist, this equals prompt_tokens_total capped by policy limits.n- eligible_prefill_tokens: the number of prompt tokens that would require prefill compute absent cache reuse.n - in v2, eligible_prefill_tokens prompt_tokens_cacheable when caching is enabled otherwise 0.n- reused_prefill_tokens: number of eligible prefill tokens reused from cache (i.e., kv states loaded/referenced).nn cache enabled vs eligiblena request is considered eligible for cache hit-rate if:n- cache policy is enabled for the route, andn- the runtime has caching enabled (feature flag), andn- the request uses a model variant that supports caching (all standard decoder-only llms exclusions must be explicit).nnif caching is disabled (policy or runtime), we record separate counters but do not include these requests in the hit-rate denominator.nn---nn metric semantics (normative)nthis adr defines semantics naming is governed by the cache metrics naming/cardinality policy.nn required counters (semantics)n1) eligible_prefill_tokens_totaln- increment by eligible_prefill_tokens for each logical request.nn2) reused_prefill_tokens_totaln- increment by reused_prefill_tokens for each logical request.nn3) requests_total (optional but recommended for consistent rates)n- increment once per logical request.nn4) requests_not_eligible_totaln- increment once per logical request where eligible_prefill_tokens 0.nn derived time-series (query-time)n- hit_rate sum(reused_prefill_tokens_total) / sum(eligible_prefill_tokens_total)n- mean_reuse_depth sum(reused_prefill_tokens_total) / sum(requests_with_eligibility_total) where requests_with_eligibility_total counts requests with eligible_prefill_tokens 0.nn request-level outcome counters (optional)nif implemented, these must be derived from the token counts above:n- requests_full_hit_totaln- requests_partial_hit_totaln- requests_miss_totalnn---nn partial-hit semantics (examples)nassume cache enabled and prompt is cacheable.nn prompt tokens (eligible) reused tokens outcome notes n---:---:------n 800 800 full_hit entire prompt kv reused (rare outside repeated identical calls). n 800 600 partial_hit common for chat history reuse last user turn is new. n 800 0 miss no matching prefix, or valid entry not found (reason recorded separately). nnfor dashboards, token-weighted hit-rate will reflect the 600/800 reuse even if request-level outcome is partial_hit.nn---nn miss reason attribution (normative taxonomy)nwhen eligible_prefill_tokens 0 and reused_prefill_tokens 0, the runtime should emit a miss reason from a stable low-cardinality enum.nnapproved miss reasons:n- policy_disabled: route or tenant policy disabled caching (counts as not_eligible in v2 if emitted, must not be included in denominator)n- capacity: cache had no available capacity / admission rejectedn- ttl_expired: matching entry existed but was expiredn- evicted: entry was evicted prior to use (often correlated with memory pressure)n- hash_mismatch: prefix hash mismatch (includes canonicalization differences)n- version_mismatch: model version/variant mismatch (includes quantization profile differences)n- unknown: reserved for unexpected paths (must be monitored not a permanent bucket)nnnotes:n- evicted vs capacity: capacity is could not admit/allocate now evicted is was present, then removed.n- if multiple reasons apply, emit the most actionable reason in the order: policy_disabled version_mismatch hash_mismatch ttl_expired evicted capacity unknown.nn---nn attribution rules (labels/dimensions)n primary slicing dimensions (approved)nhit-rate must be attributable by the following low/controlled cardinality labels:n- deployment_mode: hosted dedicated privaten- region: cloud region / on-prem site identifier (allowlist)n- model_family and/or model_id (allowlist)n- model_version (bounded see naming policy for how we bucket/shorten)n- route_id (bounded must use stable route identifiers, not raw urls)nn tenant / customer attributionntenant-level labels must not be added to raw metrics by default. tenant slicing should be done via:n- dedicated/private environment isolation, orn- sampled analytics tables / batch aggregation with strict budgets.nn request shape attributionnto support actionable recommendations without prompt logging, request shape must be bucketed:n- prompt_len_bucket: fixed bins (see naming/cardinality policy)n- optional: input_tokens_bucket if prompt_len is ambiguous in some modalitiesnnno raw prompt hashes, user ids, or session ids in metrics.nn---nn multi-turn chat semanticsneach chat turn is treated as a separate logical request with its own token counts.nnrules:n1) eligible_prefill_tokens is computed from the full serialized prompt sent to the runtime for that turn (after canonicalization / templating as implemented by the product layer).n2) reused_prefill_tokens is the length of the longest reusable prefix of that serialized prompt for the active model version.n3) because chat prompts typically grow, partial hits are the expected steady state. dashboards should therefore focus on:n - token-weighted hit-rate trendsn - reuse depth distributions by prompt_len_bucketnnnon-goal:n- we do not attempt to attribute reuse back to a prior turn or conversation id in metrics (cardinality privacy). conversation-level analysis belongs in sampled traces or offline analytics with explicit approvals.nn---nn streaming and retriesn streamingnstreaming does not change cache semantics: reuse is determined at prefill start.nn retries (normative)na logical request may experience multiple transport attempts (e.g., stream reconnects). to prevent double counting:n- the runtime must only increment eligible_prefill_tokens_total and reused_prefill_tokens_total once per logical request.n- if prefill is re-executed due to retry, that additional compute should be tracked separately (e.g., via wasted-prefill metrics) but must not inflate hit/miss.nnimplementation guidance:n- use a stable request_id (propagated from gateway) and an attempt field.n- emit cache hit-rate counters only when attempt 1.n- if the runtime cannot reliably detect attempt1, it must implement local de-duplication keyed by request_id over a bounded time window (in-memory, best-effort).nnrationale:nthis ensures hit-rate reflects caching effectiveness, not network instability.nn---nn continuous batching / shared prefillnwith continuous batching, prefill work may be scheduled in a way that obscures per-request boundaries.nnnormative rule:n- eligible_prefill_tokens and reused_prefill_tokens are attributed per request, regardless of batching.nnif a batch-level prefix lookup is performed, reuse depth must be computed per requests prompt, not per batch. any shared prefill accounting must be reconciled back to per-request increments to avoid:n- over-crediting one request for anothers reuse,n- inflating reuse tokens when multiple requests share a batch.nn---nn edge cases and clarificationsn model/version scopingncache reuse is only valid when:n- model_id matches, andn- model_version matches (includes quantization profile / weights revision), andn- any runtime-internal compatibility keys match (tokenizer revision, prompt template version if applicable).nna mismatch should be recorded as version_mismatch (not miss).nn not eligible requestsnrequests where caching is disabled must not dilute hit-rate.nwe track them separately so recommendations can still surface: enable caching on route x rather than showing low hit-rate.nn lookup success vs reusena prefix cache lookup hit with reused_prefill_tokens 0 is treated as a miss for hit-rate purposes (because no compute avoided). if lookup-level metrics are emitted, they are separate and must not be conflated with hit-rate.nn---nn consequencesn positiven- dashboards become comparable across models/routes and across time.n- recommendations can safely use token-weighted hit-rate miss reasons reuse depth to propose actions (canonicalization, routing locality, ttl, cache bytes).n- sre can distinguish workload-driven changes (prompt mix shifts) from regressions (miss reason spikes).nn tradeoffsn- token-weighted metrics may under-emphasize small prompts request-level derived metrics should be used alongside hit-rate where needed.n- conversation-level attribution is intentionally excluded from metrics (privacy cardinality).nn---nn rollout and validation requirementsnbefore enabling cache hit-rate v2 metrics broadly:n1) perf overhead: instrumentation must not regress p95 latency beyond agreed canary thresholds.n2) correctness tests:n - repeated identical prompts produce full_hit after warmupn - chat-like prompts produce stable partial-hit reuse depth patternsn - streaming retry does not change counters for a logical requestn - version mismatch produces version_mismatch miss reasonn3) data quality checks:n - denominators are non-zero only for eligible trafficn - no unexpected spike in unknown miss reasonnn---nn appendix: reference computation (pseudo-code)ninputs per logical request:n- cache_policy_enabled (bool)n- runtime_cache_enabled (bool)n- prompt_tokens_total (int)n- max_cacheable_prompt_tokens (int, policy/runtime)n- reuse_prefix_tokens (int, computed by runtime lookup)nncompute:n1) prompt_tokens_cacheable min(prompt_tokens_total, max_cacheable_prompt_tokens)n2) if not (cache_policy_enabled runtime_cache_enabled):n - eligible_prefill_tokens 0n - reused_prefill_tokens 0n - increment requests_not_eligible_totaln - stopn3) else:n - eligible_prefill_tokens prompt_tokens_cacheablen - reused_prefill_tokens clamp(reuse_prefix_tokens, 0, eligible_prefill_tokens)n4) increment counters:n - eligible_prefill_tokens_total eligible_prefill_tokensn - reused_prefill_tokens_total reused_prefill_tokensn5) if eligible_prefill_tokens 0 reused_prefill_tokens 0: emit miss reason from taxonomy.nn---nn ownersn- runtime semantics and implementation: omar el-sayed (runtime)n- metrics schema ingestion conformance: nadia rahman content: summarynthis document defines the dynamic request orchestration layers in redwoods serving runtime and the fallthrough/fallback behaviors used during capacity degradation, model mismatch, or resource pressure. it covers design goals, component responsibilities, kernel scheduling heuristics, profiling and benchmarking guidance, release checklist items, known issues and mitigations, and runbook steps for common incidents.nngoals and non-goalsn- goals:n - keep tail latency (p95/p99) stable under mixed workloads and autoscaling events.n - ensure deterministic graceful degradation with measurable cost impact.n - make fallback policies transparent and debuggable for sres and platform customers.n- non-goals:n - this doc does not define model quality thresholds (see evals docs).n - it is not a user-facing api spec see api-standards for public endpoints.nnhigh-level design overviewnthe orchestration stack is layered as: request ingress - policy router - scheduler - kernel manager - executor. a dedicated fallthrough engine runs alongside the router to evaluate compatible fallbacks (model variant, quantized profile, region). key principles: policy-first routing, cost-awareness, and observable decisioning.nncomponent responsibilitiesn- ingress (proxy): tls termination, auth checks, request enrichment (customer metadata, route tags). emits request_id and ingest_timestamp.n- policy router: policy engine that chooses target model family, region constraints, and candidate fallback set. inputs: route config, customer tier, current capacity fingerprint.n- scheduler: converts chosen target into a scheduling decision (immediate, queued, preemptible) and assigns a priority class. enforces per-model qps windowing and per-customer concurrency caps.n- kernel manager: chooses kernel variant and memory layout (bfloat16 / int8 / fused kernels) based on model architecture and sequence length distribution. provides expected token cost estimate.n- executor: runs the kernel, streams tokens, reports metrics and caches kv state.n- fallthrough engine: cross-checks capacity and policy triggers model variant fallback, regional failover, or synthetic short-circuit response (graceful degrade).nnrequest flow (annotated)n1) ingress receives request - adds metadata (customer, route_id, prompt_size).n2) router evaluates policies: if primary model is saturated, produces candidate set primary, quantized-variant, smaller-family, safer-response-fallback.n3) scheduler accepts router candidate set and current node capacity fingerprint. it computes: priority_score latency_weightlatency_sensitivity cost_weightcost_sensitivity fairness_penalty.n4) if priority_score threshold_immediate - dispatch else - enqueue in fair-shared queue or assign to preemptible slot.n5) kernel manager picks kernel path it consults per-model profile table.n6) executor runs and returns tokens post-run metrics are published to observability.nnkernel scheduling heuristicsn- priority classes: realtime (interactive p50/p95 slo), batch (throughput optimized), background (eviction-safe).n- kernel selection order: exact-optimized - fused-attention - int8-quantized - fallback-single-cpu. selection chooses first kernel with estimated latency --output /tmp/trace.jsonn3) profile gpu kernels (on node):n nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys --samplenone --tracecudakernel --duration120s --pid n4) map kernel timings to model layers using the per-model kernel map: /etc/redwood/models/kernel_map.yamln5) if disparity between estimated and observed latency 15, open a profiling ticket and tag with kernel_hash, node_type, and workload_label.nnbenchmarking suite integrationn- benchmark targets: median token latency, p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens.n- standard workloads: chat-mixed, long-context-summarize, single-turn-completion, embedding-batch.n- running distributed benchmarks: use bench-orchestrator to schedule across a representative fleet slice:n bench-orchestrator --suite production-2026 --targets fleet-slice-a --variation quant-profilesn- expected outputs (table-like text):n workload, model, concurrency, p50(ms/token), p95(ms/token), tokens/s, cost/1kn chat-mixed, rdx-v1-13b, 200, 12, 48, 21000, 0.42n- use the benchmark canonicalizer script to normalize results and upload to the perf dashboard:n python tools/benchmark_normalize.py --input results.json --tag release-2026-02nnrelease checklist (runtime binary and kernel map updates)n1) update kernel_map with new kernel_hash - add compatibility metadata.n2) run full regression benchmark suite (3 days on canary slice).n3) create rollout plan: 5 - 25 - 100 with 30m observation windows and automatic rollback if p95 increases 12 or errors increase 1.5x.n4) announce release to oncall and platform channels with telemetry queries for quick assessment.n5) post-release validation: run smoke bench and 1-hour golden traffic replay.nnknown issues and mitigations (selection)n- issue: ephemeral kernel queue overflow during cross-region failover (inc-2025-491)n symptoms: sudden p99 spike for affected region, kernels queued 2s.n mitigation: throttle regional ingress by 30 and trigger fallback to quantized-variant. long-term fix: increase pre-warming policy for region failover.n- issue: int8 kernels producing occasional catastrophic oom on 80gb a100 nodes (kern-2025-77)n symptoms: host oom kill, kernel crash logs include vectorized-alloc failure.n mitigation: apply temporary memory cap via kernel manager (max_workspace0.8node_avail). integrate with kernel scheduler hooks so scenario fidelity is preserved when testing scheduler changes.n- produce traceable profiling artifacts consumable by the benchmarking suite and the profiling playbook.nnscope and audience: engineers owning runtime architecture, kernel-and-scheduling, profiling, and sres running performance experiments or incident triage.nndesign goalsnn1) determinism and provenance: every scenario is a small, self-contained script with a hashable manifest and metadata (model version, quantization profile, hardware fingerprint).n2) scheduler-aware playback: the orchestrator can attach scheduler context (priority, tenant-id, kernel-hint) to each request so the runtime executes the scenario as intended.n3) observability-first: scenario runs automatically capture structured traces, kernel attributions, and per-token cost deltas and upload to the central perf store.n4) lightweight chaos vectors: the orchestrator supports controlled perturbations (evictions, forced preemption, simulated nvlink degradation) to surface degradation modes.nncomponent overviewnn- scenario dsl (yaml): declarative description of request series, injected events, and expected assertions.n- runner: controller that materializes requests and submits them to a chosen endpoint (local sandbox, canary cluster, full production mirror).n- scheduler adapter: library that translates dsl affinity/priority fields into scheduler annotations and kernel hints.n- collector: post-run artifact collector (traces, kernel telemetry, raw responses, golden diffs) with upload to perf-bucket.nnscenario dsl (conceptual example)nn a minimal scenario manifest in yaml. fields must remain flat (no nested objects with unknown keys) for deterministic hashing.nnmanifest_version: stitching protocol between shadow evaluations and production telemetry and provides a canonical manifest format for synthetic probes. the goal is to ensure that shadowed traffic, synthetic probes, and production traces can be correlated end-to-end so that hallucination, latency, and quantization-sensitive regressions are attributable to concrete inputs and runtime conditions.nnscopen- applies to all shadow deployments for hosted, dedicated, and private modes.n- applies to evaluation harnesses that generate synthetic probes, load profiles, and edge-case fuzzing.n- does not replace per-model onboarding acceptance criteria it augments traceability during continuous evaluation and rollouts.nnowner and stakeholdersn- owner: applied ml eval harness (team: eval-harness)n- primary stakeholders: model onboarding, serving runtime, observability, sre, customer successn- review cadence: quarterly or after any major tracing/telemetry pipeline changenndefinitionsn- shadow eval: a non-production model or model variant that receives mirrored or forked traffic for evaluation without affecting the user response.n- synthetic probe: a scripted or generated input designed to exercise a specific prompt family, long-context behavior, or quantization corner case.n- stitch key: a deterministic identifier included in all telemetry and probe payloads used to correlate traces across systems.nndesign goalsn1) deterministic correlate-ability: each synthetic probe or shadowed request must carry a stitch key that maps to a single probe manifest entry.n2) low-cardinality telemetry: stitch keys should be hashed/namespace-limited to avoid high-cardinality explosion in observability backends.n3) privacy-preserving: manifests must not contain pii and must obey probe-privacy budgets defined in quality guardrails.n4) robustness across networks: support for cross-region routing and fallback to local tracing when cross-region headers are stripped.nnhigh-level architecturen- probe generator (eval harness) emits probe payloads with: probe_id, stitch_key, probe_family, version, expected_behavior_tags, and telemetry_hints.n- shadow router mirrors production requests and injects stitch_key when present if missing, a deterministic derivation is applied and logged.n- inference runtime attaches runtime metadata (model_variant, kernel_profile, quant_profile, kv_cache_hit) to the same stitch_key in spans.n- observability pipeline (traces, logs, metrics) indexes stitch_key and materializes a composite view for investigations.nnprobe manifest format (canonical)n- the manifest is a line-oriented jsonl catalog where each entry is a single synthetic probe specification. fields: probe_id, probe_family, created_by, intent, payload_snippet, expected_assertions, tags, sampling_rate, privacy_tier, ttl_days, anchor_seed.nnexample manifest entry (jsonl line):nn probe_id: sp-2026-0007,n probe_family: fewshot-instruction-clarity,n created_by: aisha kapoor,n intent: verify few-shot instruction-following under q4_8 quant profile,n payload_snippet: instruction: summarize the following conversation in one sentence...,n expected_assertions: contains_summary, -- (example: rwd-sp-0007-9f3b).n2) deterministic derivation: if a request contains an anchor_seed or client_request_id, derive the stitch key by hmac_sha256(anchor_seed client_request_id) and truncate to 12 chars.n3) observability retention: store stitch_key as a low-cardinality tag index exact mappings in a separate probe-index service for lookups.nnobservability schema additionsn- tracing span attributes to include: stitch.key, probe.id, probe.family, model.variant, quant.profile, kernel.profile, kv_cache_hit (truefalse), prompt.slice_id.n- metric labels: probe_family, stitch_bucket (hashed namespace), quant_profile.n- log enrichment: every error log emitted during a probe evaluation must include stitch.key and model.variant.nncorrelation and debugging playbook (step-by-step)n1) alert fires on a fidelity or latency regression slice (observability dashboard or eval gate).n2) open the probe dashboard and locate top failing probe_family and top probe_id list for the time window.n3) use stitch_key to gather spans across frontend, router, runtime, and metrics ingestion.n4) confirm runtime metadata: model.variant, quant.profile, kernel.profile, and kv_cache_hit.n5) if quant.profile differs from expected in manifest, tag as quant-mismatch and escalate to quantops team.n6) if kv_cache_hit is false for a probe designed to exercise cache-sensitive behavior, mark as cache-warmup-mismatch and add to cache-priming queue.n7) if sample_size insufficient for triage, bump sampling_rate for those probe_id entries in the next manifest push (see manifest release procedure).nnmanifest release and rollout proceduren1) author creates a manifest branch in the probe repo and adds new jsonl entries.n2) run local manifest-lint (scripts/manifest_lint.py) that enforces privacy_tier, ttl, and tag whitelist.n3) create a pr and request reviewers: applied ml observability.n4) merge to main triggers ci that: uploads full-payload artifacts to secure storage, assigns probe_id - artifact mappings, and emits a manifest release blob versioned by semver (e.g., v1.14.0).n5) canary rollout: release to 1 of shadow capacity for 24h, monitor the stitch_key-indexed fidelity and latency dashboards.n6) full rollout: expand to target sampling_rate across shadow fleets.nnrollforward / rollback triggersn- rollforward: failing probes that are noisy but reveal root cause should be promoted to model-onboard tickets and retained for 180 days.n- rollback: any probe that causes production impact (rare but possible via middleware bug) triggers immediate manifest rollback and revert pr sre incident process applies.nnsecurity and privacy controlsn- probes labeled privacy_tierredacted must not include user-generated content those labeled anonymized may include hashed user ids only.n- access to the full payload artifact store requires audit-enabled acls all accesses are logged.n- synthetic probes that interact with third-party connectors must be approved by security and compliance.nntracing and storage cost mitigationsn- use stitch_bucket (namespace-truncated value) as a lookup key to avoid high-cardinality tags in metrics.n- aggregate span counts by probe_family hourly for 90-day retention drop raw spans older than the probe ttl unless flagged for active investigation.nnoperational runbook: common triage scenariosn- scenario a: sudden spike in doc_id: dsid_bc7de72802db442684945f260589eaf6, source_type: confluence, title: slo adaptive guardian and capacity playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook defines the slo adaptive guardian a decision and automation layer that protects critical slos by combining predictive telemetry signals, tenant-aware fairness controls, and capacity commitment policies. the document covers signal definitions, decision logic, automated actions (soft and hard), owner responsibilities, verification steps, and example configuration snippets for redwoods operational tooling.nnpurpose and scopenn- purpose: reduce mean time to safe-degradation and preserve overall customer experience when capacity stress or quality regressions threaten slos.n- scope: applies to the model-serving tier and associated request-routing proxies for hosted and dedicated clusters. excluded: private/on-prem where local policies override central automation unless explicitly opted in.nnkey conceptsnn1) guardian signal types (inputs)n- slo burn-rate: rolling 1h and 6h burn-rate for primary slos (p99 latency, availability).n- synthetic canary divergence: canary generation error/quality regressions measured by eval sentinel suite (daily).n- queue pressure: per-cluster queue depth and tail-quantile queue time (90/95/99).n- token headroom: available gpu token capacity vs reserved capacity (in token/sec).n- tenant imbalance score: short-term deviation from expected fairness share (0-100).n- telemetry fidelity indicator: percentage of requests with full traces/telemetry degraded fidelity reduces automation confidence.nn2) action tiersn- advisory: non-blocking notifications to oncall and product owners (email/slack).n- soft degradation: policy changes that preserve functionality but reduce per-request resource cost (e.g., reduce max_tokens, disable heavy-tooling, shorten context window).n- throttle shed: tenant-level soft throttles (rate limits) and request shedding (reject with 429 or queue-drop) per priority lane.n- capacity commit: trigger dedicated pool warm-ups or request provisioning (subject to procurement guardrails).n- hard fallback: automatic model variant switch (to smaller quantized or cheaper model) or region-level reroute.nndecisioning matrix (high level)nnthe guardian evaluates signals on three axes: severity, certainty, and tenant impact. the decision sequence is deterministic and aims to minimize customer-visible errors while restoring slos quickly.nn1) severity assessmentn- low: 1h burn-rate 20 - advisory only.n- medium: 1h burn-rate 2x5x or headroom 1020 - soft degradation advisory.n- high: 1h burn-rate 5x or headroom throttle capacity commit advisory.n- critical: sustained 6h burn-rate 10x, telemetry shows correlated queue saturation - runtime-aware-probe-synthesis-and-quant-compatibility-manual, content: summary:nprocedure and operational manual for generating eval probes that reflect runtime behavior and for tagging probes with quant-compatibility signals used by onboarding and rollout gates.nncontent:noverview:nthis page describes the end-to-end process for runtime-aware probe synthesis and for establishing quant-compatibility signals that feed model onboarding, shadow evaluation, and rollout gating. the goal is to produce probes that represent real service traffic and to label those probes with explicit compatibility metadata for quantized artifacts and kv-cache behaviors.nnscope and audience:n- scope: eval probe generation, runtime telemetry mapping, quant-compatibility tagging, acceptance thresholds, triage flow for probe failures.n- audience: evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, runtime sres, quantization engineers.nnwhy runtime-aware probes?n1. synthetic probes that ignore runtime distribution (seq lengths, concurrency patterns, cache-hit profiles) miss edge-failure modes introduced by batching, kv-cache and quantized kernels.n2. runtime-aware probes enable earlier detection of quant-induced coherence degradation, streaming/functioncall instability, and tail-latency regressions.nndefinitions:n- probe: a single input (or small set) used by the eval harness to exercise model behavior.n- quant-compatibility flag: metadata on a probe indicating likely sensitivity to quantization (high/medium/low).n- runtime fingerprint: vector summarizing request features observed in production (avg_seq_len, prefix_reuse_rate, kv_cache_hit, streaming_fraction, avg_tokens).nnownership and slas:n- probe fabrication service (team: eval-fabric) owns the probe generator code and templates.n- model onboarding owns mapping rules used by promotion gates.n- runtime sre owns telemetry signals (latency p95/p99, cache hit rate) and ensures feeds are available.n- sla: daily refresh of runtime fingerprint feed probe generator should produce a new candidate set within 4 hours of a fingerprint change.nnhigh-level workflow (numbered):n1. collect runtime fingerprints (see telemetry feeds below).n2. synthesize a stratified probe set honoring fingerprint strata (e.g., 0-32 tokens / 33-128 / 129 cache_high/cache_low).n3. annotate each probe with quant-compatibility heuristics and an uncertainty score.n4. run fast micro-shadow eval against baseline non-quantized model.n5. run quantized artifact sweep (parallelized) and compute fidelity deltas per probe slice.n6. produce a compatibility manifest (json) used by the deployment gate.nntelemetry feeds (signals to collect):n- avg_seq_len (rolling 24h)n- prefix_reuse_rate (fraction of requests with repeated prefixes in last 7d)n- kv_cache_hit_rate (per-service)n- streaming_fraction (percent of requests that used streaming or functioncalls)n- batch_size_distribution (histogram)n- p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_msn- model_variant_ratio (fraction of traffic hitting each variant)nnprobe synthesis rules (bulleted):n- stratify by sequence length: sample proportions should match runtime fingerprint /-10.n- cache-sensitive probes: include at least 20 with high prefix_reuse_rate when runtime shows reuse_rate0.3.n- streaming/functioncall probes: preserve original turn boundaries and function calling sequences.n- adversarial edgecases: synthesize 5 of probes with high-entropy/noise perturbations for robustness checks.nnquant-compatibility scoring (table as text):n- high: long sequences (512), high prefix_reuse, many functioncalls. (score label: quant-sensitive-high)n- medium: moderate seq lengths (128-512), mixed cache patterns. (label: quant-sensitive-medium)n- low: short responses ( ci triggers quant-sweep job across latest probe manifest.n2. sweep computes per-probe deltas and flags slices where thresholds are breached.n3. if any high-sensitive slice breaches, fail gate and notify onboarding@redwood.com.n4. if only medium/low slices breach, auto-create triage ticket with classification and attach diff artifacts.n5. auto-generate a remediation suggestion: (a) increase quant-precision for embedding/kvcache kernels, (b) add targeted probes to cover failing prompt family, (c) fallback to non-quant variant for rollout.nntriage playbook (when sweep fails):n- immediate checks (515 minutes):n 1) re-run sweep with a different random seed to rule out sampling noise.n 2) verify artifact was built with expected params: quant_bits, group_size, kernel_patch_id.n 3) check runtime cache-change events in last 24h.n- diagnostic steps (15120 minutes):n 1) compare top-10 probes by failure magnitude and annotate shared features.n 2) re-run only those probes against a mixed-precision artifact.n 3) if differences persist, schedule human-in-the-loop evaluation and mark model onboarding as blocked.nntelemetry queries (prometheus / timeseries examples):n- avg_seq_len: sum(rate(request_tokens_total1h)) / sum(rate(requests_total1h))n- kvcache-hit: increase(kvcache_hit_total24h) / increase(kvcache_lookups_total24h)n- p99 latency per-variant: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket5m)) by (le, variant))nnrollout and mitigation strategies:n- canary policy: deploy quant artifact to 1 traffic with canary probes duplicated from production traffic for 24h.n- auto-fallback: if fidelity delta threshold or p99 latency 1.2x baseline for canary, automatically shift canary to non-quant variant and open rollback ticket.n- gradual ramp: 1 - 5 - 25 - 100 with checks at each stage computed from probe-sweep metrics.nnrelated pages:n- /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026n- /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024nnchange log:n- 2026-02-10: initial draft and validation with eval-fabric team.n- 2026-03-05: updated acceptance thresholds and added cli examples after sre feedback.nnappendix: quick-check checklist (one-line bullets):n- confirm fingerprint feed freshness 0.85 for high-severity regressions (policy target).n- maintain mean probe cost per model per day below configured budget (default 250/day).n- reduce low-signal alerts by 60 versus fixed-threshold gating.nnkey conceptsnn1) confidence funnel (cf): a tiered decision flow that assigns probes to bands based on model response confidence, recent drift, and slice criticality. bands:n- band a (investigate immediately): low confidence ( 0.90 and no telemetry anomalies sparse sampling (0.5x baseline).nn2) dynamic probe gating (dpg): runtime policy that adjusts sampling fraction and probe routing based on cf band, slo deficit, and available eval budget. dpg enforces:n- minimum detectability: ensure a slice has at least n30 probes in the last 24h if it is band a or critical customer slice.n- budget-aware throttling: if daily budget burn rate 90, reduce band d sampling first.n- hedged sampling: for ambiguous slices (confidence 0.450.55) route duplicated probes to two different model variants to increase signal fidelity.nnwhen to usenn- new model promotions, quantized rollouts, a/b experiments, or customer-facing feature changes.n- ongoing continuous monitoring where probe volume and slice cardinality are moderate-to-high.nnroles ownershipnn- eval-orchestrator team: implements dpg runtime and provides metrics. defines a repeatable evaluation protocol, harness components, workload recipes, and triage playbook for measuring stability and fidelity of interactive streaming responses when the model invokes function/tool calls. the protocol is specifically targeted at cross-cutting failure modes introduced by quantization, kv-cache interactions, and continuous-batching in production serving. it is intended for applied-ml engineers, runtime owners, and sres validating model promotions and platform changes that affect streaming or function-call behavior.nnscopen-----n- model families: decoder-only encoder-decoder topologies used in redwood hosted/dedicated/private serving.n- modes: streaming token-by-token output with optional function/tool call markers, non-streaming baseline for comparison.n- interventions: quantization changes (8/4-bit paths), kv-cache warm/cold patterns, batching policy changes, streaming buffer/window tuning.n- excludes: offline embedding-only workloads and strictly batch, non-interactive evaluation.nngoalsn-----n1) detect and quantify stability regressions introduced by runtime changes that affect streaming partial outputs or function-call boundaries.n2) measure end-to-end fidelity (intent and argument correctness) of function-call outputs across quantized/float variants.n3) provide deterministic triage steps and thresholds for blocking promotions or triggering rollback.n4) produce actionable artifacts (diffs, heatmaps, replay bundles) that developers can use to debug.nndefinitionsn-----------n- partial-stream divergence: token-level levenshtein distance between prefix streams produced by baseline and candidate at matched prefix lengths.n- call-boundary shift: a change in the token index where the model emits the function_call start token (or structured marker). measured as delta in tokens.n- argument fidelity: semantic equivalence score for the structured arguments in function calls (using domain-specific equality rules).n- streaming latency slos: p50/p95 of time-to-first-byte and time-between-chunks measured at the api gateway.nnmetrics and thresholdsn----------------------nuse these primary metrics in the evaluation dashboard and for automated gating:n- partial-stream divergence (median per-example): acceptable 98 for deterministic argument schemas semantic-score 94 for freeform args.n- streaming latency regressions: p95 time-to-first-byte regression 0.6 or argument fidelity 5 tokens must fail automated promotion.n- canary window: require a minimum 7-day rolling run of the streaming canary with no blocking regressions before promoting quantized runtime to dedicated clusters.n- auto-fallback rule: when argument_fidelity ).n- any real telemetry used to derive distributions must be aggregated/sanitized before fixture construction.nn replay methodologyn execution modesn- ci (pr gating):n - runs a small, fast subset: 50100 fixtures total across key datasets.n - enforces determinism and strict correctness checks.n - runtime budget: 3 minutes wall-clock.n- nightly (extended):n - runs full datasets.n - computes drift metrics and trendlines posts summary to eng-platform.n - runtime budget: 3045 minutes.nn pinning and reproducibilitynto make comparisons stable, the runner must pin:n- schema_version (e.g., cost-model/v1)n- pricing_snapshot_id (e.g., 2026-02-01)n- model_catalog_snapshot (e.g., catalog-2026-02-10)n- runtime-metrics-contract version (for derived fields)nnany change to a pinned artifact requires an explicit update pr to the harness with:n- rationalen- expected diff summaryn- reviewer sign-off from owning teamnn calling surfacenpreferred: validate via cost model api endpoints used by console/optimize (to catch serialization/auth/bounds behavior). fallback: library compute for unit-level invariants.nnthe harness supports two call patterns:n1) per-request estimate endpoint (single fixture estimate)n2) synonyms, misspellings, nested requests, and numeric edge cases.n2) structural fuzzing: include syntactic noise that commonly breaks parsers: mismatched punctuation, truncated sentences, and nested json in text blocks.n3) multi-step sequences: for function chains (tool a - tool b), model must demonstrate correct ordering under simulated session state.n4) latency-sensitive probes: tiny-context and long-context variants measure p50/p95/p99 for both token-generation and post-processing (parse time).n5) quantization sensitivity: for each probe, run on floating-point baseline and at least two quantized variants to capture divergent behavior.nnsample prompt matrix (short table represented as text):n- schema: search_file probes: 200 categories: exact-match, fuzzy-query, truncated-path, the expected function/tool. target slo_targets.correct_tool_selection.n- semantic correctness (semantic_score): automated heuristics small human annotation sample. thresholds depend on product (default 0.85 for conversational tool workflows).n- latency slos: token-generate parse 2 of probes.n- medium-severity: parsable but semantically incorrect params (e.g., wrong file id).nnquantization versions, tokenizers, and quant artifacts to isolate change.n4) if parse errors only in quantized artifact, tag as quant_failure and escalate to infra-quant team.n5) for semantic failures response correction orchestrator, content: overview:nnthis document describes the multi-granularity response correction orchestrator (mg-rco): an automated system and operational runbook for detecting, synthesizing, validating, and rolling out corrections to model outputs at different granularities (token, turn, and conversation/session). mg-rco is designed to integrate with the eval harness, prompt catalog, model onboarding flows, quantization profiles, and regression triage processes so fixes are safe, measurable, and reversible.nnwhy we built mg-rco:n- persistent long-tail quality issues require targeted repairs at different levels (e.g., tokenization errors vs. conversational context drift).n- manual patching is slow and risky a reproducible orchestrator enables faster mean-time-to-fix while preserving production slos.n- corrections must be validated across quantized variants and shadow fleets to avoid regressions introduced by performance optimizations.nnscope and definitions:n1) granularity levels:n - token-level: fixes that alter prompt encoding, tokenization, or scoring of a small lexical pattern (e.g., punctuation handling, unicode normalization).n - turn-level: fixes that affect a single exchange (prompt immediate response) such as hallucination suppression or instruction tightening.n - session-level: multi-turn stateful repairs (context window trimming, memory anchors, persona resets).nn2) correction types:n - prompt rewrite: automated or templated prompt modifications applied at request-time.n - post-filter/heuristic: deterministic filters that modify or suppress outputs (e.g., remove pii patterns).n - model artifact patch: small model re-ranking weights or delta weights applied in runtime (rare, requires rigorous rollout).n - eval-driven synthetic label: generated training/eval examples used for model fine-tuning or on-the-fly re-ranking.nndesign principles:n- minimal blast radius: prefer prompt rewrites and post-filters before considering model artifact patching.n- evaluability: every correction must be covered by an automated eval suite (unit-level slice-level mixed-slo shadowing).n- quant-compatibility: corrections must be probed against quantization profiles and kv-cache behaviors.n- observability: clear telemetry for candidate impact, rollback triggers, and slos.nnsystem architecture (textual diagram):n- detection layer: anomaly detectors, probe triggers, and incident inputs (sentry alerts, eval regressions, customer tickets).n- orchestrator core: stores correction recipes, coordinates patch generation, runs validation workflows, and coordinates rollouts.n- evaluator adapters: run correction-aware eval harness jobs (shadow, canary, full-fidelity replay).n- synthesis engine: template-based rewrite generator small llm-based rewriter used with caution (sandboxed).n- safety guardrails: static checks, cost budget checks, quant-compatibility checks, and approval gates.nnkey integrations:n- eval harness: mg-rco registers a validation job type correction-validation that runs the candidate against the canonical probe set plus a targeted slice.n- prompt catalog: correction recipes are linked to prompt-set ids canonicalized templates are versioned in the prompt registry.n- model onboarding: when a correction requires model artifact changes, mg-rco triggers a model-onboarding check including preflight probes and shadow promotions.n- quantization profiles: mg-rco runs candidate corrections across the active quant profiles for the target model (e.g., int8, q4_0) and fails candidates that show coherence or hallucination regressions beyond thresholds.n- regression triage: every correction generates a traceable incident ticket containing hypothesis, test matrix, and blame candidates for regression investigators.nnoperational runbook: detection to production (numbered steps)n1) detection intake:n - trigger sources: automated regression alert, probe-sentinel, slo breach, customer-reported case.n - create mg-rco intake with: input example(s), tldr of failure class, target service/model, urgency level.n2) preliminary triage (human-in-loop):n - triage engineer assigns granularity and correction preference (prompt rewrite, filter, model patch).n - if evidence points to quant or kv-cache interaction, mark quant-sensitive and notify runtime team.n3) candidate generation:n - for prompt rewrites: run template synthesizer 3 llm-variant rewrites (sandboxed) and canonicalize.n - for filters: author a deterministic rule with unit tests.n - for model patches: create a small re-ranking delta and schedule offline evaluation (requires cross-team pre-approval).n4) automated validation:n - launch correction-validation job in eval harness with matrix: n baseline model (prod variant) candidate correction (shadow)n quantized variants (all active quant profiles)n long-context session replay (if session-level)n adversarial prompt suite for the affected slicen - pass criteria: no regression on anchor slices, x improvement on failure slice, latency increase 5 relative within a 30-minute window, auto-rollback.n- if failure-slice regression reaches 10 relative compared to baseline at canary stage, auto-rollback.n- if cost per 1k tokens rises above the configured cost budget for the route, rollback and notify finance-runbook.nntroubleshooting checklist (common failure modes):n- candidate passes offline but fails in-shadow: check for telemetry mismatch (tokenization differences, header prompts), verify request canonicalization.n- quant regressions: run quant-shadow replay harness, inspect kv cache alignment and attention kernel fallbacks.n- drift reappearance after promotion: schedule probe refresh consider session-level anchors rather than brittle rewrites.nngovernance and change control:n- low-risk corrections (prompt rewrites filters) are auto-approvable with two reviewers.n- medium-risk (synthetic label changes, llm-generated rewrites) require cross-team approval from applied ml and safety.n- high-risk (model artifact deltas) must go through full model-onboarding acceptance, sre performance sign-off, and security review.nnhow mg-rco complements existing playbooks:n- eval harness: runs the canonical correction-validation jobs and contributes new job types and example seeds.n- prompt sets: canonical prompt templates are versioned and mapped to correction recipes to preserve provenance.n- model onboarding: when a patch crosses into model artifacts, mg-rco invokes the onboarding acceptance matrix (preflight probes, shadow promotion).n- quantization profiles: mg-rco requires per-profile passes and stores results in the correction artifact.n- regression triage: every failed candidate generates a triage artifact that is consumable by the regression huntbook team.nnownership and contacts:n- runbook owner: priya nair (applied ml)n- runtime / quant contact: jonah baker (serving runtime)n- evaluator and probe infra: alex chen (eval infrastructure)n- emergency rollback pager: eng-sre oncall (see internal pager rota link)nnappendix a example cli commands:n- create intake: redwood-mgro models, caches, and serving runtime state before or during rollout. it covers objectives, probe types, probe generation, quantization-aware warmups, monitoring signals, and a regression triage fast-path for warmup-induced failures. use this doc for: model onboarding, canary rollout preparations, private/dedicated deployment warmups, and automated preflight checks in the eval harness.nngoals and scopenn- reduce first-request tail latency and token p99 inflation during traffic ramp.n- stabilize kv cache and attention-key/value layout effects so price/quality regressions are reproducible.n- provide reproducible probe suites that exercise: short-context generations, long-context kv growth, streaming function-calls, and quantized kernel paths.n- applicable to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.nnowner and escalationnn- primary owner: serving runtime - warmup telemetry team (eng-serving-runtime).n- secondary owners: applied ml (evals) and platform qa.n- on-call escalation: runbook page: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-warmup-oncall (triage leads: marcus lee).nnwarmup concepts and terminologynn- warmup probe: a deterministic or sampled request sequence designed to bring runtime state (threads, gpu kernels, kv cache, cuda context) into steady state.n- priming prompt: a short contextual preamble appended to user prompts to normalize the models tokenization/attention behavior during initial requests.n- cold-to-warm window: time range after an idle period where performance metrics are expected to improve as warmup completes.n- quant-aware warmup: warmup sequence that routes through the same quantized kernels and precision paths as production traffic (e.g., int8 kv ops).nnwarmup probe taxonomy (recommended probe types)nn1) micro-latency probes (short-turn generation)n- purpose: measure token p50/p95/p99 before and after cache prime.n- example: 3x single-sentence generation (max_tokens16) with streaming enabled.nn2) kv growth probes (increasing context length)n- purpose: exercise kv cache allocation growth and eviction behavior.n- example: 5 requests with cumulative context 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 tokens.nn3) long-coherence probes (multi-turn)n- purpose: validate long-context coherency and attention matrix stability across cached segments.n- example: 10-turn qa where each turn appends 250 tokens.nn4) function-call streaming probesn- purpose: ensure segmented token streaming, function-call triggers, and chunked flushes operate under warmed conditions.nn5) quantization-path probesn- purpose: verify low-precision execution yields no major quality drift after warmup.n- example: compare logits/top-k distribution before/after warmup on representative prompt set.nngenerating and scheduling probesnn- probe source priorities (in order): 1) production sample replay (privacy-filtered), 2) annotated long-tail probes from prompt catalogue, 3) synthetic adversarial probes.n- schedule: run micro-latency probes immediately after deployment, kv growth and long-coherence probes during canary stage (0-5 traffic), quant-probes in parallel for dedicated/private.n- frequency: baseline probes every 10 minutes for first 2 hours then backoff to hourly for first 24 hours.nnprobe configuration reference (table)nn probe_name request_pattern tokens stream expected_metric_delta run_stage n------:---:---:---:---:n micro-latency single-turn short 8-32 true p99 0.88 canary n function-stream short multi-chunk 32-128 true stream-stability 99 immediate n quant-path representative set 16-512 false bleu/metric delta (blocking): run micro-latency quant-path probes against shadow model. fail if p99 threshold or semantic delta limit.n2) canary gate: run kv growth long-coherence probes continuously for canary window. fail and rollback if error spike or quality regressions observed.n3) progressive ramp: continue probes and only advance traffic when hourly checks pass for 3 consecutive samples.nnrollout and rollback procedure (numbered runbook)nn1. create warmup probe suite referencing the release quant-profile and probe seed set.n2. deploy canary (0-2) and trigger immediate micro-latency probes.n3. evaluate probe outputs and metrics dashboard for 30 minutes.n4. if pass, expand to 5 and start kv growth probes long-coherence probes.n5. if fail at any stage, execute automatic rollback: mark model non-promotable, scale down canary, notify on-call and create regression ticket.n6. post-failure: collect probe logs, store reproducible seeds, and run the regression triage checklist (see next section).nnregression triage fast-path for warmup failuresnn- triage checklist (first 60 minutes):n 1) confirm probe seeds and quant artifact match the deployed model.n 2) check for kernel/fusion model artifact id and quant-profile checksum.n - p99 and semantic-similarity deltas (baseline vs observed).n - attach scheduler logs and gpu kernel version.nnbest practices and prompt priming patternsnn- keep priming prompts minimal: prefer a 1-2 sentence neutral context to avoid shifting task semantics.n- use deterministic priming for micro-latency probes use randomized sampling for long-coherence probes to capture variation.n- for multilingual models, include language-balanced prime samples in probes.nnoperational checklist for private/dedicated deploymentsnn- ensure kms keys summaryn-------nthis document defines a reproducible protocol and decision matrix for evaluating throughput vs. fidelity tradeoffs for candidate serving configurations (model variants, quantization profiles, batching policies, and routing tiers). it provides acceptance gates used by model-onboarding, infra, and sre to decide whether a configuration can be promoted to: hosted baseline, dedicated pool, or private rollout. the goal is to make acceptance deterministic, measurable, and automatable.nnscope and audiencen------------------n- scope: llm inference configurations tested in the redwood eval-harness and serving-simulation environments. includes hosted, dedicated, and private serving modes.n- audience: applied ml engineers, serving runtime owners, sre, and product owners conducting promotions and rollouts.nnwhy this protocol existsn------------------------nteams frequently make tradeoffs (e.g., int8 quantization increased batch size) that increase system throughput and lower per-token cost but may reduce output fidelity. without a consistent accept/reject rulebook, rollouts cause regressions or unnecessary conservatism. this protocol standardizes:n- a throughput/fidelity taxonomyn- measurement methodology (inputs, metrics, statistics)n- promotion gates and rollback triggersn- automation knobs for ci/cd integrationnndefinitionsn-----------n- throughput (t): tokens/sec or requests/sec measured end-to-end under the target serving config and arrival pattern. we report tokens/sec at stable-state and 95th percentile request throughput.n- fidelity (f): application-level quality signals computed against the production prompt set. typical signals: semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), exact match (em) for extraction tasks, bleu/rouge for summarization, and a response stability index (rsi) used across redwood.n- baseline: the currently-promoted configuration (model quant batching) used as the reference for delta calculations.nnthroughput buckets and fidelity budget below).ntable: bucket target throughput (req/s) allowed fidelity delta (vs baseline) example use-casesn- low 2,000 req/s delta_f bucket lower-bound for 90 of runs.nnprompt set selectionn--------------------n- use the production prompt catalog slice with stratification over slices that represent different behavior modes: short completions, long-form, instruction-following, extraction, and embeddings.n- minimum sample sizes: 2,000 examples for single-task workloads for multi-slice workloads, ensure each slice has 500 examples.nnpromotion gates (automated)n---------------------------n1) smoke gate (automated ci):n - run a 5-minute smoke harness with a small canonical prompt set (n200). pass criteria: no p99 latency regression 2x baseline and median fidelity delta 3x baseline for 10 minutes.n3) full promotion gate:n - full 20-minute stable run as defined in measurement methodology. pass if fidelity, throughput, and latency requirements satisfied and no new anomalies in logs/traces.nnrollback and regression triage triggersn-------------------------------------n- immediate rollback triggers (automated):n - production fidelity alert: continuous monitoring detects an alert where a rolling 1-hour fidelity metric deviates by more than the allowed delta with p 2x slo for 15 minutes.n- triage playbook summary:n 1. capture failing sample set (use the fidelity-alerting hook to store inputs and outputs).n 2. run replay in the eval-harness with both baseline and candidate configs. produce diffs (token-level and embedding diffs).n 3. if the issue is traceable to quantization/precision (see quantization sensitivity checklist below), treat as high priority for rollback to previous quant-profile.n 4. open a regression investigation issue with tags: regression, fidelity, rollout-id, model-version. assign owner from oncall rotation.nnquantization sensitivity checklist lengths some activations are length-dependent.n- if tokenizer-sensitive failure: compare tokenization deltas and map to prompt failure modes.n- fallback option: promote with mixed precision (e.g., int8 for attention fp16 for mlp) and re-evaluate.nnautomation and ci integrationn-----------------------------n- ci job: eval-throughput-fidelity (parametrized by candidate-id, baseline-id, bucket)n- adaptive eval budgeting and sample allocation framework (aebsaf), a prescriptive system for distributing limited evaluation budget (tokens, runs, annotator-hours) across prompt slices, models, and stages (shadow, canary, production). aebsaf unifies eval harness scheduling, prompt-set prioritization, onboarding readiness checks, quality guardrails, quantization safety sampling, and regression triage triggers.nnpurpose and scope:nn- introduces a lightweight policy and reference implementation for dynamic allocation of eval resources.n- covers allocation across: prompt slices, failure modes, languages, quantized variants, and production routes.n- applies to continuous evaluation pipelines, pre-promotion model-onboarding, and post-release regression scans.n- does not replace per-eval bespoke analysis it provides a default, auditable baseline for most workloads.nnmotivation and goals:nn- real-world constraints: eval compute and annotator time are finite naive uniform sampling wastes budget on low-risk slices.n- objectives: maximize early detection of quality regressions, provide stable statistical power on high-impact slices, and reduce false negatives when promoting models or quantization profiles.nnkey principles:nn1. risk-weighted allocation: allocate more samples to slices with higher business impact or higher historical volatility.n2. multi-stage budgeting: split budgets into smoke (10), focused (60), and exploratory (30) phases to balance coverage and depth.n3. feedback-driven reallocation: increase sampling on slices where variance or failure rates rise above thresholds.n4. cost-awareness: include token, inference latency, and annotation cost into per-sample cost model.nnroles and ownership:nn- eval owner: responsible for configuring aebsaf for a model or workload (owned by applied ml or model onboarding).n- platform: implements scheduler and enforces quotas (eng-harness).n- sre/observability: publish metrics and alerts (eng-platform).n- customer-facing product or cs: define business-impact weights for customer-specific slices.nnterminology:nn- slice: a coherent subset of prompts (e.g., long-context, biomedical, spanish, multi-turn).n- sample: one model invocation annotation (if applicable).n- budget unit: normalized unit combining inference token cost and annotation time (see cost model).nnallocation algorithm (high-level):nn1. ingest metadata for each slice: impact_score (0..10), historic_failure_rate (0..1), recent_variance (sigma), avg_token_cost, avg_latency_ms, sample_capacity.n2. compute a base_weight for each slice:n base_weight 0.5 normalized(impact_score) 0.3 normalized(historic_failure_rate) 0.2 normalized(recent_variance)n3. convert base_weight into budget proportion using softmax with temperature t to avoid extremes:n budget_prop_i softmax_t(base_weight_i)n4. enforce minimum per-slice floor (min_samples) and maximum cap (max_samples).n5. split the allocated samples into stages: smoke/focus/exploratory and dispatch to eval harness queue with priorities.npractical parameter defaults (reference):nn- overall budget: defined in budget units (default for medium workload: 10,000 budget units).n- temperature t: 0.8 (empirically balanced).n- min_samples per slice: 30 (to detect medium effect sizes at alpha0.05 for binary pass/fail metrics).n- max_samples per slice: 2,000 (prevents budget capture by extremely large slices).n- stage split: smoke10, focused60, exploratory30.nncost model (normalized budget unit):nn cost component example value notes n--------------------------------------------n per-sample token cost 0.002 normalized to usd-per-1000-tokens converted to budget unit n annotator-minute 0.05 cost per human minute (crowdsourced) n latency penalty per sample 0.0001 ms small multiplier to deprioritize slow/expensive routes n infrastructure surcharge 1.0 multiply budget for private/onprem runs nbudget_unit token_cost token_weight annotator_minutes annotator_weight latency_penalty latency_weightnnconfiguration example (yaml):nnscheduler:n budget_units: 10000n temperature: 0.8n min_samples_per_slice: 30n max_samples_per_slice: confluence, title: ci eval determinism and flake mitigation, content: summarynour evaluation harness previously produced intermittent metric drops (e.g., 0.04 bleu on a single run) for the quantized-v2 onboarding suite that disappeared on rerun. this page documents the current (2026) standard for reducing nondeterminism, preventing ci flakes, and making regressions actionable.nnthe root causes we have observed include:n- stochastic decoding (temperature/top_p sampling) without per-example rng control.n- rng state not consistently propagated to all relevant libraries/ops.n- gpu-level nondeterminism (kernel selection, atomic ordering), especially in quantized/int8 paths.n- cross-hardware differences (e.g., a100 int8 kernels vs legacy fallback paths).nn what changed since the initial investigationnthe original debugging thread identified sampling parameters and missing explicit generators as primary contributors. the current harness incorporates the same core ideas, with the following updates:n- we now treat deterministic decoding as the default for per-commit ci gates for onboarding suites.n- the determinism flag is implemented as --deterministic / deterministic: true in eval config, and it hard-enforces decoding parameters (see below).n- the runner always constructs and passes an explicit torch.generator for generation, derived from a root seed plus a stable per-example index.n- ci gating moved from single-run metrics to median-of-repeats, and flakiness is measured explicitly.nn definitionsn deterministic (harness-level)na run is considered deterministic (for ci purposes) if repeated executions on the same hardware container image model revision produce identical decoded token sequences for the same prompts.nnnotes:n- hardware drift (a100 vs k80) is not expected to be bitwise identical.n- some quantized kernels may still be nondeterministic even when framework-level deterministic flags are enabled.nn flakena flake is a ci failure caused by nondeterministic variation rather than a real change in model/code.nn recommended ci strategy (current)n 1) per-commit (pr) gate: deterministic quick evalnpurpose: prevent random sampling jitter from blocking merges.n- environment: standardized runner image target gpu class when available (a10 preferred for cost a100 acceptable).n- mode: deterministic: truen- repeats: --repeat 3n- decision rule: gate on the median metric across repeats also fail if output hashes differ across repeats (for suites that require bitwise stability).nn 2) nightly: multi-seed tolerance-based comparisonnpurpose: catch real regressions and quantify expected variance.n- environment: target infra (a100 for quantized-v2)n- mode: deterministic: false (sampling allowed when the eval is designed to measure sampled behavior)n- seeds: 3 seeds (default: 13, 37, 101)n- decision rule: compare against the golden baseline using metric tolerance thresholds alert on sustained shifts (median across seeds).nn 3) on failure: auto-trigger repro debug jobnpurpose: make investigations fast and data-rich.n- auto-collect artifacts listed in the logging and artifacts section.n- include a run summary that states whether variance is:n - decode-level (different token sequences)n - metric-only (same outputs but metric computation drift)n - environment-level (hardware/container mismatch)nn deterministic decoding mode (required behavior)nwhen deterministic: true, the harness must enforce:n- do_sample falsen- temperature 0.0n- top_k 1n- top_p 1.0n- num_beams 1 (unless the suite explicitly tests beam search)n- explicit generator passed into generation apisn- stable batching order (no data-loader shuffling stable sort by example_id)nnrationale:n- simply setting a global seed is insufficient when generation draws randomness in parallel or across different batch shapes.nn rng handling (current standard)n root seed and per-example seedsn- the runner accepts a --seed root seed.n- for each example, derive a stable per-example seed:n - example_seed root_seed example_indexn- construct a generator on the active device and pass it explicitly to generation.nnoperational guidance:n- ensure example_index is stable across runs (do not use worker-local indices unless they are globally consistent).n- if sharding is used, include shard_id in the seed derivation only if shard assignments are stable across runs.nn framework flagsnwe enable deterministic flags when deterministic: true:n- torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(true)n- torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic truen- torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark falsenncaveat:n- quantized/int8 kernels may not fully respect these flags. treat the flags as best-effort rather than a guarantee.nn hardware notes (quantized-v2)n- a100 int8 paths can differ from legacy gpu fallbacks.n- ci determinism requirements are scoped to a single target hardware class per suite.n- the quantized-v2 onboarding suite is pinned to a100 for nightly baselines.nn metric gating rulesn per-commit deterministic gaten- compute metric per repeat.n- report: median, min, max, and standard deviation.n- fail conditions:n - any repeat differs in output token hash (for deterministic suites).n - std dev exceeds threshold (default threshold: 0.005 bleu-equivalent suite owners may override).nn nightly tolerance-based gaten- compare nightly medians to golden medians.n- default tolerances (may be tuned per suite):n - bleu: 0.03 absoluten - chrf: 0.02 absoluten - task accuracy: 0.5 percentage points absolutenn logging and artifacts (required)neach eval run must emit the following into the run artifact directory:n- run_metadata.json: model revision, container digest, gpu type, torch version, eval suite name, config snapshotn- rng details:n - root seedn - per-example seed derivation schemen - torch.get_rng_state() (hex or base64)n - torch.cuda.get_rng_state_all() (per device hex or base64)n- generation parameters:n - do_sample, temperature, top_p, top_k, num_beams, max_new_tokensn- outputs:n - outputs_run_i.jsonl for each repeatn - include decoded text and decoded token idsn- summary:n - metrics_run_i.jsonn - summary.json with median/std and output hash comparisonsnn runner cli (current)nrequired runner options for reproducibility testing:n- --repeat n : runs the same suite n times with the same config and seedn- --deterministic truefalse : enforces deterministic mode when truen- --seed seed : sets the root seednnexample:n- evals/onboarding --suite quantized-v2 --repeat 3 --deterministic true --seed 42nn troubleshooting playbooknif you see nondeterminism with deterministic: true:n1) confirm the run is on the expected hardware class and container digest.n2) confirm output hashes differ (decode nondeterminism) vs metrics differ (metric computation drift).n3) if decode nondeterminism:n - verify generator is passed explicitlyn - verify stable ordering of examples and stable batch shapen - check for any remaining sampling knobs
