behavior, seed derivation, gating thresholds) requires review from applied ml evals serving runtime., doc_id: dsid_ad3ffc015eea431685135cc36e83de00, source_type: confluence, title: hybrid probe ttl prioritization and recovery playbook, content: overview:nthis playbook defines a hybrid orchestration strategy for evaluation probes that combines time-to-live (ttl) semantics, priority scoring, and fast-recovery policies. the goal is to keep continuous coverage of critical prompt slices while bounding eval cost and minimizing probe-induced noise on production-like systems (hosted, dedicated, private). it is intended for the eval platform team, model-onboarding engineers, and oncall responders.nnwhy this exists:n- long-running probe farms can waste budget on stale probes and mask regressions if probes are not aged out intelligently.n- sudden regressions require rapid amplification of high-value probes and automated recovery actions.n- hybrid ttl priority approach ensures freshness, provable coverage, and predictable cost.nnscope and audience:n- scope: eval harness scheduling, probe lifecycle, probe ttl policies, recovery escalation, observability, and example configs.n- audience: eval platform, applied ml, serving runtime, sre.nnterminology:n- probe: a single evaluation input (prompt context) executed against a model variant.n- probe ttl: elapsed wall time after which a probe is considered stale and eligible for retirement or reseeding.n- priority score: numeric value used by the scheduler to order probe execution.n- fast recovery window: short period (default 30m) after a regression signal where high-priority amplification is applied.nnprinciples:n1) freshness over redundancy: prefer reseeding semantically similar probes that are ttl rather than repeatedly running the same slot.n2) cost-aware amplification: limit concurrent amplification to an adjustable budget percentage to avoid overloading infra.n3) observability-first: every probe carries provenance telemetry and must be linkable to eval alerts and regression investigations.nnpriority scoring formula (recommended):npriority w_slice sliceimportance w_recent recencyboost w_sev failurescore - w_cost costpenaltynwhere:n- sliceimportance: integer 1..10 assigned by owners (critical user flows have 8-10).n- recencyboost: 1.0 if probe was not run in last 24h, 0.5 if 624h, 0.0 if 3 or semantic drift threshold.n- reseed strategy: small lexical perturbation (synonym swap), context shuffling, temperature variation for sampling probes.n- reseed limit: at most 2 reseeds per original probe before demotion to cold tier.nnfast-recovery amplification protocol (triggered by regression signal):n1) detection: regression alert fires (see observability section) and is labeled with suspected slice(s).n2) prioritization: scheduler increases w_sev by factor 2 for affected slices, moves associated probes to hot tier.n3) amplification: create n parallel executions for top-k priority probes where n min(amplifybudget, 20). amplifybudget default 10 of probe-farm concurrency.n4) short-circuit fallback: if amplification shows degraded output quality degrade_threshold for 3 consecutive runs, trigger automated rollback/whitelist depending on rollout policies.n5) triage handoff: notify oncall_eval with initial triage summary and links to top failing probes.nnexample amplification cli (illustrative):n amplify top 5 probes for slice onboarding-checks for 30mnredwood-eval amplify --slice onboarding-checks --top 5 --window 30m --budget 0.1nnobservability and alerting (recommended):n- per-probe telemetry: run_id, model_version, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, semantic_similarity_score, failure_flags.n- dashboard: active probes by tier, avg token cost per tier, recent reseed rate, amplification concurrency.n- alerts (prometheus-like pseudo-rule):nalert evalproberegressionhighn if increase(eval_probe_failed_totalslicecritical.10m) 50n for 5mn labels severitypage, teameval-platformn annotations summaryhigh failure rate on critical eval slicesnnslos and thresholds for eval platform health:n- probe execution success rate: 99.5 (daily) for hot/warm probes (failure non-terminal or missing telemetry).n- max amplification-induced excess token cost: 12 of daily probe budget.n- reseed churn (reseeded probes / total probes): keep 24 else (0.5 if last_run_hours 6 else 0.0)n cost_penalty tokens / 1000.0n return w_slice slice_importance w_recent recency w_sev failure_rate - w_cost cost_penaltynnndata retention and privacy:n- probe-level telemetry retained for 90 days for hot/warm, 30 days for cold.n- sensitive customer prompts must be redacted and handled using the privacy-first-shadow-eval pattern (see related page).nntesting and rollout plan:n1) canary: deploy scheduler change to eval-harness/canary pool for 48 hours with amplification disabled.n2) shadow mode: enable amplification calculations but do not change execution order for 7 days compare priority distributions.n3) limited rollout: enable amplification with budget_fraction0.02 for 72 hours and monitor costs.n4) full rollout: increase to target budget_fraction budget guidance and rollout checklist., doc_id: dsid_ba05099cbef74303a6bf6d0ba9b0744a, source_type: confluence, title: prompt failure inventory and annotator contract: scenario taxonomy labeling protocol, content: summarynthis document defines a reproducible taxonomy of prompt-level failure modes, a recommended scenario-driven inventory format, and a labeling contract for human annotators and automated heuristics. it is intended for evaluation teams, model-onboarding engineers, and regression triage owners who need consistent, high-quality labels that link prompt characteristics to observable model behaviors.nngoals and scopen- create a small, stable set of failure categories that cover production-relevant errors (not every linguistic edge case).n- standardize the prompt context metadata we store for each failure (the inventory manifest).n- provide a clear annotator contract and decision rules so labels are consistent across raters and over time.n- enable automated triage heuristics to bootstrap labels and prioritize human review when confidence is low.nnintended audiencen- applied ml engineers running eval harnessesn- model onboarding reviewers who must certify promotion readinessn- regression triage teams performing root-cause analysisn- annotation leads and quality control managersnnhigh-level taxonomy (first-class categories)n1) incorrect factual response (facterror)n- model asserts verifiably false facts about current or historical reality.n- example triggers: wrong dates, wrong numerical facts, incorrect entity attributes.nn2) hallucinated entity or citation (hallucination)n- model invents an entity, citation, or document that cannot be substantiated by the provided context or a reasonable external check.nn3) instruction misinterpretation (instructionmismatch)n- model fails to follow explicit instructions in the prompt (wrong format, omitted fields, reversed order).nn4) safety policy violation (safety)n- model produces content that violates safety constraints: disallowed instructions, harassment, pii leakage, or actionable wrongdoing.nn5) degraded semantic relevance (relevancedrop)n- output drifts off-topic, becomes generic, or ignores context dependencies (e.g., ignores prior chat turns).nn6) tokenization/formatting breakage (formaterror)n- output contains broken json, truncated code blocks, or malformed special tokens causing downstream parser failures.nn7) quantization/artifact degradation (quantartifact)n- output shows artefacts consistent with quantization or kv-cache instability: repeated phrases, tokenization hallucinations, or inconsistent scalar outputs across repeats.nn8) latency/partial-output fallbacks (latencyfallback)n- model response indicates it timed out, returned partial content, or used fallback model variant with degraded quality.nninventory manifest: required fieldsnuse this manifest layout for every logged failure. store as a row in the failure catalog (csv/parquet/jsonl).n- prompt_id: unique stable id for prompt fixture (example: pf_2026_00021)n- source: origin of prompt (prod/bench/manual/synthetic) (example: prod:search-assist)n- seed_text: the raw prompt text (truncated to 8k chars) (example: summarize the following...)n- context_snapshot: short context hash or description of conversation state (example: chat:session_241)n- model_version: exact model flavor used (example: gpt-redwood-v2-quant8)n- hardware_profile: deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private) instance (example: dedicated:p4d-32gb)n- timestamp_utc: iso8601 of the run (example: 2026-01-12t20:34:22z)n- failure_category: one of taxonomy labels (example: hallucination)n- severity: low/medium/high (see severity guidelines) (example: high)n- repeatability: always/sometimes/rare (example: sometimes)n- annotator_id: human rater or automated heuristic id (example: annot-v2-17)n- confidence_score: 0.0-1.0 (string for json flatness) (example: 0.82)n- reproduction_steps: minimal steps to reproduce include seeds and flags (example: see reproduction_notes)n- related_run_ids: other run ids for cross-comparison (example: run_123, run_124)nnseverity guidelinesn- high: visible user harm or complete feature break (safety, pervasive facterror that changes user action).n- medium: materially degrades ux or model correctness but has a straightforward workaround (relevancedrop, formaterror).n- low: cosmetic or rare issues tolerated by product (minor hallucination on non-critical content).nnannotator contract: decision rules and proceduresn1) single-pass automated triage (pre-labeling)n a) run deterministic heuristics: entity-checker against knowledge base, json-parse validator for formaterror, safety classifier.n b) if heuristics produce confidence 0.9 and unanimous category, set label automated value and set annotator_id auto:.n c) otherwise, queue for human review.nn2) human annotation workflown 1) read the prompt and produced output verbatim, then consult the context_snapshot if provided.n 2) apply the taxonomy: choose the single best category. if multiple categories apply, select primary by impact to user (safety fact relevance).n 3) write a one-sentence justification in the free-text justification field for auditability.n 4) assign severity and repeatability using the guidance above.n 5) if unsure, mark label needs_discuss and add required evidence (e.g., external fact links).nn3) adjudication rules (when annotator disagreement 2 raters disagree)n- triage to an adjudicator pool. adjudicator applies evidence-gathering protocol: web lookup, cross-model comparison, and consults model-onboarding lead. final label must include a short evidentiary note.nninter-annotator agreement (iar) targets and samplingn- initial onboarding target: cohens kappa 0.6 on a 500 example calibration set.n- production maintenance: sample 1 of daily labeled items (min 50) for iar monitoring investigate drift if kappa drops below 0.55.nnautomation heuristics and feature checklist for bootstrap labelingn- exact-match referent check (kb lookup): flags facterror/hallucination.n- json/markup health check: flags formaterror.n- safety classifier (ensemble of policy and regex): candidate safety.n- n-gram repetition and perplexity delta tests: candidate quantartifact.n- context similarity score: candidate relevancedrop if low similarity.nndata retention and privacy notesn- do not store full pii in the manifest if prompts may contain pii, store a redacted_seed_text and reference to secure vault for retrieval under approved workflows.n- retention default: 90 days for full text in the eval environment, 3 years for redacted manifest entries. follow security-and-compliance/data-management policies for customer data.nnintegration with eval harness and trace_id, cost_metrics (tokens, latency), and model-runtime snapshot to the manifest.n- provide a stable api endpoint for the triage dashboard to stream new manifest entries (schema url: /internal/eval-manifest/v1).nnoperational playbook: from failure detection to remediationn1) detection: auto-heuristics mark candidate failures and assign confidence.n2) prioritization: failures are ranked by severity x user-impact metric (e.g., active sessions affected).n3) human review: annotators label top n for the day where n is set by sre/product trust thresholds.n4) root-cause analysis: triage uses model_version diffs, quant profiles, and workload fingerprints to hypothesize cause.n5) remediation: roll forward/rollback, quant profile adjustments, prompt-template patches, or dsid_80623c804901452ba9c4854cccc1ebde, source_type: confluence, title: quantization shadow fidelity simulator and regression hypothesis bundle, content: overviewnnthis document describes the quantization shadow fidelity simulator (qsfs) a lightweight, modular evaluator used by the eval-harness to predict behavioral deltas introduced by quantized model artifacts before production rollout and the accompanying regression hypothesis bundle (rhb) for structured triage if the simulator surfaces risk. qsfs is intended for use during model-onboarding, quantization-profile generation, and pre-rollout canary design.nnwhy we built qsfsnn- reduce time and cost: simulate large-scale quantized behavior deterministically on small reference workloads rather than running full shadow fleets.n- improve triage velocity: provide prioritized hypotheses and signal extraction to accelerate root cause identification for regressions tied to quant artifacts.n- standardize handoffs: produce an artifact (rhb) consumed by regression teams, sre, and model owners with uniform fields and triage runbooks.nnscope and non-goalsnn- in-scope: sequence-level fidelity simulation for text generation and reranking models (causal and encoder-decoder), token-level divergence metrics, prompt-conditioning sensitivity, and kv-cache interaction emulation.n- out-of-scope: full gpu kernel performance estimation, detailed latency/throughput microbenchmarks, or end-to-end production traffic replay (use shadow-fleet or production mirror for that).nnhigh-level architecturennqsfs consists of three coordinated modules:nn1) probe fabricator: selects and prepares workload slices (priming context, few-shot examples, edge-case seeds).n2) quantized emulator: runs a quantized-inference deterministic emulator that applies quant noise models and cache-decay approximations to a floating-point baseline.n3) analyzer hypothesis composer: produces fidelity metrics, diffs, and structured hypotheses (rhb).nneach module can be executed independently in the eval-harness pipeline or as a single command. ownership: eval-harness team owns the code applied-ml stewards the probe catalog.nnprobe fabrication and selectionnn- inputs: workload fingerprint, slice definitions, probe budget, and tenant constraints.n- strategy: stratified sampling across context lengths (short/medium/long), priming density (0/1/5 shots), and token-entropy buckets.nnprobe types generated:nn- baseline-stability probes: produce deterministic seeds used for consistency checks.n- quant-stress probes: perturbations (token swap, suffix truncation, numeric precision stressors).n- edge semantic probes: adversarially generated prompts targeting critical functionality (e.g., code generation, instruction-following).nnsimulator configuration (table)nn parameter description default notes n---------:---n quant_profile identifier for quant recipe (e.g., q4f, q8a) q4f-default maps to quantization-profiles catalog n seed_set probe catalog id small-core-100 use larger for release candidate n kv_cache_modeling none approximate options: none, approximate, exact-sim n temperature sampling temp for stochastic probes 0.0 0.0 forces deterministic sampling n rerun_count number of emulator passes per probe 3 aggregate variance budget n divergence_threshold alert-level for token-level divergence 0.06 used to generate rhb alerts nnexecution procedure (step-by-step)nn1. prepare context: map service-level workload fingerprint (from eval-mesh) to seed_set and override priming where necessary.n2. run floating-point baseline (fp32 or bf16) to generate canonical outputs and internal trace (logits, top-k tokens per step).n3. run quantized emulator against the same probes. if kv_cache_modelingexact-sim, emulate cache reads/writes else apply cache-decay model.n4. compute fidelity metrics: token-divergence (kl and token-mismatch rate), response-syntactic-distance (bleu/rouge heuristics), and functioncall-structure-delta (for tool-calling).n5. if any metric breaches configured thresholds, auto-generate an rhb and escalate per policy.nnfidelity metrics and thresholds (examples)nn- token mismatch rate: fraction of sample tokens not in fp baseline top-1 (alert if divergence_threshold).n- kl over logits: mean kl across steps (alert if 0.18).n- response structure flip: of probes where functioncall schema or json validity changed (alert if 0.02).n- latent-behavior drift: embedding cosine drift of final states (alert if 0.12).nnregression hypothesis bundle (rhb) schemannthe rhb is a standardized artifact produced as a json-ld (consumed by issue trackers and triage dashboards). the key fields listed below must be present in the bundle simplified here for human review.nntable: rhb fields and triage actionsnn field example triage owner action on fail n------------n title q4f - q4f-v2: functioncall fidelity regression on payments prompts model-owner assign model regression ticket n probe_ids seed-123,seed-54 applied-ml reproduce locally n primary_signal token-mismatch-rate applied-ml run targeted stress probes n delta_snapshot /artifacts/q4f/v2/compare-2026-02-10 sre pull logs kernel traces n top_hypotheses quant-rounding-bias, kv-cache-loss applied-ml prioritize by score n suggested_mitigations increase precision for attention kernels, use cache-stabilizer rewrite model-owner patch re-run qsfs n impact_estimate 0.6 requests downgraded for payments flow product decide rollout delay n blocker_flag true release_coord block rollout if true nnhypothesis scoring and prioritizationnn- each hypothesis scored by: signal-strength (01), reproducibility (01), surface-risk (01). composite score weighted sum (0.5signal annotation credit allocation and entropy stewardship framework, content: overviewnnthis document defines the annotation credit allocation and entropy stewardship framework: a policy and lightweight algorithm for (1) budgeting human annotation credits across probe classes, (2) prioritizing probes by information gain (entropy) relative to unit annotation cost, and (3) integrating these signals into the eval-harness scheduling and probe-rotation systems used by redwood inference evaluation teams.nnwhy this mattersnn- annotation budgets are finite and shared across many eval initiatives (shadow validation, production-sampled sentinels, regression triage).n- not all probes produce equal information: low-entropy probes rarely surface new failure modes but can consume substantial annotation dollars.n- quantization, caching, and model variants change response distributions we need an adaptive allocation that preserves coverage while minimizing annotation spend.nngoals and success criteriann- increase per-dollar entropy captured (bits per usd) by 20 within the first quarter of rollout.n- reduce annotation spend on low-yield probe classes by at least 30 while maintaining minimum coverage thresholds for critical slices.n- ensure the eval-harness scheduler can enforce per-tenant credit allocations and emergency top-ups with minimal human intervention.nnprinciplesnn1) entropy-first prioritization: prioritize probes ranked by expected information gain (entropy delta) normalized by annotation cost.n2) minimum safety coverage: critical safety slices always reserve a fixed credit floor independent of entropy ranking.n3) rotational freshness: include a percentage of low-entropy probes in every batch to detect distribution drift that entropy estimators may miss.n4) transparency auditability: every credit allocation decision is logged and inspectable budgets and heuristics stored in the eval config.nnkey definitionsnn- probe: a single input sent through the eval-harness (synthetic or production-sampled).n- entropy score: estimated shannon entropy (or surrogate) of model responses for a probe family before annotation.n- annotation credit: unit of human labeling budget configurable per-label type (binary, multi-class, multi-annotator).n- cost per credit: usd-equivalent based on vendor rates and internal labor overhead.nnmetrics trackednn- bitsperdollar: total estimated information gain (bits) collected divided by usd spent on annotation.n- yieldrate: fraction of annotated probes that triggered new actionable findings (regression, safety alert, calibration failure).n- coveragefraction: percent of critical slices that have at least n annotated probes in 30-day window.n- driftsignalrate: rate of probes where entropy estimator disagreed with human labels by threshold (used to tune estimator).nnallocation algorithm (operational procedure)nn1) daily probe cataloging:n - the eval-harness aggregates candidate probes into families and computes a running entropyestimate for each family. entropyestimate uses a lightweight ensemble of predictive models (softmax entropy, edit-distance diversity, and embedding-dispersion).n2) cost normalization:n - map label types to creditunit and usd cost (example: binary1 credit0.60, 3r consensus multi-class3 credits2.10).n3) priority score computation:n - for each family: priority (entropyestimate familyweight) / expectedcostperprobe. familyweight encodes product impact, regulatory sensitivity, and sla exposure (see table below).n4) apply hard floors and ceilings:n - reserve criticalfloor credits: all families with label safety or regulatory get at least 5 of total daily credits.n - cap per-family spend to maxpercent (default 20) unless emergency flagged.n5) sampling and rotation:n - select probes for annotation by sampling in proportion to priority, but inject rotationlowentropyfraction (default 10) of low-priority families uniformly to maintain freshness.n6) dispatch and logging:n - send selected probes to annotation backend with metadata and expected adjudication policy. write allocation decisions to the probe-allocation ledger (timestamp, family_id, priority_score, credits_allocated, owner).nntable: default family weights and thresholds (example)nn family label familyweight critical? minimum daily credits notes n-------------------------------------------------------------------------n safety 3.0 yes 50 regulatory and user-safety slices n user-facing 1.2 no 20 high product exposure n backend-parser 0.8 no 10 non-critical but useful n long-context 1.5 no 15 historically high entropy n rare-edge 1.8 yes 25 low frequency but high impact nnembedding the framework in eval-harnessnn- config integration: add a new top-level field in eval-recipe yaml: annotation_allocation:n - total_daily_credits: intn - rotation_low_entropy_fraction: floatn - critical_floor_percent: floatn - family_weights: mapn - cost_map: mapnnexample yaml snippet:nnannotation_allocation:n total_daily_credits: 2000n rotation_low_entropy_fraction: 0.10n critical_floor_percent: 0.05n family_weights:n safety: 3.0n user-facing: 1.2n backend-parser: 0.8n long-context: 1.5n rare-edge: 1.8n cost_map:n binary: 0.6n multi_class_3: 2.1n multi_annotator_consensus: 3.5nnoperational runbook: emergency top-up and regression triagenn1) trigger: regression triage or p1 production incident requires immediate re-labeling of a suspect probe family.n2) immediate action:n - owner toggles emergency_flag for family_id in eval console. this bypasses maxpercent cap and bumps familyweight to emergencyweight (default 10x).n - system allocates emergencycredits from a reserved pool (configurable).n3) post-mortem allocation reconciliation:n - annotators spend is reconciled to real budget. if reserve used, product manager reviews the spend and approves rebalancing of future daily credits.nnintegration with quantization profiles and model variantsnn- when a model variant or quant-profile is promoted to staging, run a calibrationsweep: sample n probes from top-priority families and recompute entropyestimate under the variant. if bitsperdollar drops below variantthreshold, flag for extended human review and delay rollout.n- for quantized models that reduce response diversity, the entropyestimate should include kernel-aware priors (we store a small per-model variance multiplier in the model catalog).nntelemetry and dashboardsnnexpose the following dashboards in the eval console:n- bitsperdollar over time (by family, by model variant)n- annotationspend vs budget (rolling 7d)n- coveragefraction heatmap (slices x tenants)n- driftsignalrate and top families with estimator-human disagreementnnownership and teamsnn- document owner: aisha patel (applied ml)n- primary implementer: eval-harness team (eng-applied-ml)n- annotation operations: dataops / labelopsn- product stakeholder: feature reliability pmsnnrollout plan (phased)nn1) pilot (2 weeks): enable for 3 families (safety, long-context, user-facing) with a 10 of annotation volume and manual review of allocations.n2) beta (6 weeks): expand to 25 of families and integrate with annotation backend automatic dispatch. measure bitsperdollar and yieldrate.n3) ga (quarterly cadence): full rollout with slos on bitsperdollar and coveragefraction and automated emergency top-ups.nnaudit and governancenn- ledger retention: allocation ledger retained 2 years.n- monthly review: annotationops and applied ml review allocation patterns and update family_weights if needed.n- approval process: any change to criticalfloor or emergencyreserve requires sign-off from product reliability and security.nnappendix: sample sql for bitsperdollar calculationnn-- pseudocode sql (for analytics team)nselectn family_id,n sum(entropy_bits) as total_bits,n sum(usd_cost) as total_usd,n case when sum(usd_cost) 0 then null else sum(entropy_bits)/sum(usd_cost) end as bits_per_dollarnfrom probe_annotation_resultsnwhere annotated_at date_sub(current_date, interval 30 day)ngroup by family_idnorder by bits_per_dollar descnnnotes, known limitations, and future worknn- entropy estimates are approximations early tuning required per-family. track driftsignalrate closely during the pilot.n- this framework assumes stable annotation unit costs vendor churn can invalidate thresholds quickly.n- future: integrate active learning models for per-probe annotation decisioning and experiment with variable consensus (dynamic annotator counts) to further optimize cost-per-bit.nnrelated pages and linksnn- probe telemetry compression and scheduling (see: ../eval-harness/probe-telemetry-compression-scheduling-playbook-2026).n- probe confluence, title: promotion readiness: cross-stage synthetic simulation quantization safety playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook defines a combined evaluation and safety protocol used to decide when a model artifact can be promoted from evaluation (canary/validation) into production routing. it coordinates three corridors of checks: 1) synthetic user simulation to validate behavioral and distributional stability, 2) quantization kernel-sensitivity safety checks for performance-preserving transforms, and 3) lightweight runtime smoke and canary procedures to exercise operational invariants. the goal is deterministic, reproducible promotion decisions tied to explicit pass/fail signals and rollback criteria.nnscope and use casesnn- applies to any model promotion that will be served by redwood runtime variants where quantized or variant kernels (fp16/int8/qlora-style) are in the promotion path.n- intended for models with expected production throughput above 1 qps/customer or with regulatory/data-sensitivity constraints (customer pii handling).n- not required for experimental sandbox promotions under 24h unless flagged by product as critical.nndefinitionsnn- promotion: the act of moving a model from staging/canary to a production route where customer traffic is served.n- synthetic actor: a deterministic user-simulation profile used to exercise prompts and contexts representative of production usage.n- quant safety check: a set of deterministic tests that validate output fidelity and kv-cache integrity across quantized kernels.nnownership and rolesnn- model owner (primary): ml engineer who produced the model artifact and is responsible for test bundles, prompt sets, and baseline metrics.n- eval owner: engineering squad responsible for running the synthetic actor harness and interpreting results.n- runtime owner: infra/runtime team responsible for quantization tooling, kernel selection, and performance baselining.n- release approver: product or platform pm with final sign-off for non-emergency promotions.nnacceptance criteria (summary table)nn- for each criterion below the format is: criterion pass threshold primary signal escalationn - behavioral stability delta regression-triagen - semantic drift embedding cosine shift 95 (rouge-l or bleu for fixed tasks), and human-annotated quality delta 1024 tokens) - 25 weight.n 3) multi-step instruction with tool-calls emulation - 10 weight.n 4) edge adversarial variants (typos, hallucination probes) - 15 weight.n 5) rare-entity and numeric reasoning - 10 weight.nn- execution: run 3 independent seeds per actor with deterministic rng to allow diffs. collect full traces including prompt, logits (sample), kv-cache checksums, and returned tokens. store artifacts in the eval artifact bucket with the tag: promotion/:.nnquantization kernel safety checksnn- purpose: verify that quant transforms and kernel selections do not induce unacceptable semantic/functional regressions.n- automated checks:n - layer-wise output delta: run a 500-sample micro-batch and compute per-layer l2 and cosine delta vs baseline fp32. thresholds: median l2 0.999.n - end-to-end behavioral delta: use the synthetic actor prompt set, compute pass-rate deltas and embedding shifts.n - kv-cache replay: for long-context runs, serialize and replay kv-cache through quantized kernels and validate checksums.n - failure-mode detector: fuzz a subset of kernels with perturbed inputs to detect nans/inf or divergence outliers.nn- tooling commands (example):n - quant bake: n redwood-quant bake --model model.tgz --profile int8-s90 --output quantized/model-int8.tgzn - layer compare: n redwood-compare-layers --base model_fp32 --candidate model_int8 --samples 500 --out report.htmlnnruntime smoke test suitenn- purpose: exercise operational invariants (metrics, logs, tracing) before opening production traffic.n- keys:n - load profile: synthetic actors at 1x, 5x expected qps for 10 minutes each.n - observability checks: ensure traces propagate, token-level billing counters accurate, request ids preserved.n - telemetry asserts: no more than 0.2 errors, p95 latency regression 10 - 50 - 100 by automated policy, each stage gated by acceptance criteria evaluation window (30m for small models, 60m for l8k contexts).n6) monitoring guardrails: automated rollback triggers include: behavioral stability fail, kv-cache parity fail, p99 latency threshold, or error rate spike configured delta.n7) post-promotion audit: collect artifacts, diff reports, and human spot-check on 200 sampled prompts.nnautomated alerting and rollback rulesnn- alert channels: pagerduty to runtime on severity1 (kv-cache corruption), slack runtime-ops for severity2, email to model-owner for degraded quality signals.n- auto-rollback thresholds (examples):n - behavioral pass-rate drop 2 absolute in sliding 10m window - automatic rollback.n - kv-cache checksum mismatch (any) during canary - immediate rollback and incident start.n - p99 latency baseline_p99 1.5 for 10 minutes - gradual throttle and rollback if persists.nndata and artifact retentionnn- all synthetic-run artifacts and diff reports for a promotion must be retained for 90 days under eval-artifacts// with ttl tags.n- human annotation records from the spot-check should be stored with reviewer id and comments.nnfailure triage processnn- if automated checks fail, create a regression ticket with: title, failing signals, links to artifacts, investigator assignment. use label: regressions/promotion.n- regression triage steps:n 1) reproduce in isolated environment (runtime owner model owner).n 2) run layer-diff and kernel-fuzz tests.n 3) if quant-related, attempt quant-profile fallback (e.g., int8-int8-s95 or int16) and re-run harness.n 4) if behavioral, escalate to applied-ml for annotation and root-cause.nnauditability sign-offnn- each successful promotion must include the following artifacts in the promotion ticket: artifact sha, synthetic-run summary report, quant-compare report, smoke-run telemetry snapshot, human spot-check results, release approver signature.n- the release approver records the promotion decision and any exceptions in the promotion ticket.nnappendix: example eval command sequencenn1) bake quant candidaten redwood-quant bake --model s3://models/foo/sha.tgz --profile int8-s90 (must include golden answers).n- actor prompt set: 10k produced prompts across actor catalog.n- long-context replay corpus: 2k sequences 3k tokens each.n- kernel fuzz harness: 5000 micro-batches dsid_5cf28151bea84f5b9736145cc853cf83, source_type: confluence, title: evaluator onboarding and certification curriculum - 2026, content: purposennthis page defines the official redwood evaluation team curriculum for onboarding, certifying, and re-certifying evaluators who operate the eval harness, curate prompt/probe suites, and run shadow/federated experiments across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. the curriculum is designed to: 1) shorten time-to-productivity, 2) reduce annotation and probe creation variance, 3) ensure consistent use of quantification and regression triage tools, and 4) codify the certification gates that allow an evaluator to approve production shadow runs.nnaudiencenn- new evaluators joining the applied ml group.n- ml engineers responsible for shadow validation and probe orchestration.n- cross-functional reviewers (sre/product) who sign off on production gating.nnoverview and outcomesnnat the end of the curriculum, an evaluator will be able to:n- operate the eval harness cli and submit reproducible probe runs (eval-mesh).n- compose probe families that cover calibration, drift, long-tail, and quant-sensitivity slices.n- run a shadow-to-prod migration with the probe migration checklist and pass the certification exam.n- diagnose regressions using the regression investigation playbook and bootstrap a quant-fallback experiment.nnstructurennthe curriculum has three phased tracks that must be completed in sequence:nn1) foundations (2 weeks) orientation, tooling, safety basicsn2) applied labs (3 weeks) hands-on probe design, shadow runs, annotation calibrationn3) certification and audit (1 week) exam, live run approval, pairing auditnneach phase contains lectures, reading, a set of hands-on tasks, and acceptance criteria. evaluators are paired with a steward (senior evaluator) for at least one full shadow lifecycle.nnphase 1: foundations (2 weeks)nngoal: ensure the evaluator understands the platform, core telemetry, and quality guardrails.nnmandatory reading and videos:n- eval harness primer (internal video, 35m)n- quality guardrails: sqc mapping (doc)n- kv-cache behavior and quant sensitivity (paper summary)nnaccess setup checklist:n1. request access to eval-mesh and probe-fabricator via internal ticket (tool-access-202).n2. verify rbac: membership in group redwood-evaluators dsid_4a039d2fdaad492e804567fc58c5baf4, source_type: confluence, title: multi-seed aggregation and variance budgeting for eval stability, content: purposen-------nthis document defines the multi-seed aggregation and variance budgeting protocol (mavb) used by redwoods eval harness to quantify output stochasticity, attribute variance to sources (prompting, model nondeterminism, quantization, runtime caching), and set actionable variance budgets for production rollouts and regression triage.nnscopen-----n- applies to all internal evaluation runs that influence model promotion, quantization decisions, or production rollouts (hosted, dedicated, private).n- intended for use by applied-ml, model-onboarding, runtime, and sre teams.n- covers generation (chat/text), reranking, and embedding stability analyses where multiple random seeds or sampling strategies are relevant.nndefinitionsn-----------n- seed run: one execution of an evaluation workload with a single rng seed and fixed runtime settings.n- seed ensemble: a set of n seed runs used to measure variance for a given workload slice.n- variance budget: a pre-defined acceptable range (σ or interquartile range) for metric fluctuation attributable to nondeterminism.n- attribution buckets: prompt variance, model stochasticity, quantization impact, runtime cache/batching.nnroles ownershipn-----------------n- evaluation owner (applied-ml): defines workload slices, target metrics, and baseline model.n- runtime owner (serving runtime): provides reproducible runtime configs and documents non-deterministic behaviors.n- onboarding lead (model onboarding): approves variance budgets for model promotion and signs off on triage.n- regression lead (regression triage): coordinates bisecting and blames assignment when variance exceeds budgets.nnhigh-level protocol summaryn---------------------------n1. define workload slices (by prompt-type / user-slice / sequence length / language / quantization profile).n2. for each slice, run a seed ensemble of n runs (default n7 n minimum 5 for preliminary checks).n3. compute per-metric aggregation (mean, median, stdev, iqr, bootstrap ci) across seeds.n4. compare against the variance budget table if exceeded, run attribution steps and trigger triage.n5. record all raw seed traces, rng seeds, runtime config, and kv-cache state hash in the eval store.nndetermining ensemble size (n)n-----------------------------n- small slices or quick smoke tests: n 35 (informational only).n- standard production slices: n 7 (balance of power and cost).n- high-sensitivity slices (legal, safety): n 15 and use stratified sampling across rng engine settings.n- guidance: choose n such that 95 bootstrap ci of the primary metric width 60 of excess variance, fail quantization promotion and open a quant-triage ticket.n4. if runtime cache/batching contributes 30, create a runtime investigation with traces and gpu scheduling logs.nnregression triage playbook (short)n----------------------------------n1. tag the failing eval run and mark related traces as p0 for triage.n2. run an automated bisect across commits and model checkpoints using the eval harness (see cli below).n3. for suspected infra/runtime causes, reproduce on a minimal dedicated node with identical runtime config.n4. if model change suspected, request an annotated diff of token-level outputs across seeds and an error-slice report.n5. document conclusion in the regression tracker with blame attribution and corrective action (rollback, quant-tune, prompt-harden).nnpractical examples contract between evaluation owners (model teams, product teams, and the eval platform) for probe prioritization, sampling budgets, and the per-probe cost accounting model used by the redwood eval harness. it codifies: how probes are scored for execution priority, how budget allocation works across workloads (hosted/private/dedicated), and the runbook for triaging cost-driven failures or regressions that originate from probe scheduling and sampling.nnscopenn- applies to all probes scheduled through the eval harness (shadow, continuous, and targeted stress probes)n- covers cost evaluation (input prompt expected checks metadata) run against one or more model variants.n- probe cost: an estimated usd cost for executing a probe in a specific mode (hosted / dedicated / private), including token compute, io, and annotation overhead.n- priority score: numeric score used by the scheduler to rank pending probes for execution.n- sampling contract: a signed agreement (documented here as config) that specifies the target sample rate and sla for a probe family.nnprinciplesnn1) transparently measurable economics: every scheduled probe must attach a probe_cost estimate and cost_breakdown metadata (compute_tokens, warmup_tokens, annotation_minutes).n2) workload-aware fairness: priority score should reflect both customer-facing impact (severity) and marginal economic utility (information gain per dollar).n3) safety-first triage: probes that are safety or compliance critical always have a higher base priority and an independent execution budget.nnpriority scoring model (operational formula)nnpriorityscore base_factor severity_weight lambda (info_gain_estimate / probe_cost) - penalty_adjustmentsnnwhere:n- base_factor: 100 for safety/compliance probes, 50 for production regression probes, 20 for exploratory/ad-hoc probes.n- severity_weight: integer 1..5 assigned by the owning team (must justify)n- info_gain_estimate: expected fraction (0..1) of new failure modes discovered derived from historical probe novelty and slice coveragen- probe_cost: estimated usd cost for the probe in target execution moden- lambda: scaling constant (default 25) tuned quarterly by the eval platform teamn- penalty_adjustments: negative modifiers for duplication, recent failures with no new signal, or owner throttlesnnoperational sampling contract (yaml config rulesnn- contracts are evaluated at the start of each scheduling epoch (midnight utc). if run queue demand exceeds capacity, probes are ranked by priorityscore subject to monthly_cost_cap_usd.n- if a probe_family exceeds its monthly_cost_cap_usd, the scheduler will: 1) pause exploratory probes, 2) reduce sampling rate proportionally for non-safety probes, and 3) notify the owner via email and slack.n- owners may petition for temporary burst capacity by opening a ticket with the evaluation platform approval required from platform finance for 5k burst.nntelemetry, dashboards and slisnnminimum telemetry emitted per probe run:n- probe_id, probe_family, execution_mode, model_variant, start_ts, latency_ms_median, tokens_consumed, warmup_flag, run_cost_usd, result_status (pass/fail/error), info_gain_signal (0..1)nnkey dashboards and slos:n- probe-cost burn rate (daily / monthly) alert if projected monthly spend budget by 10 (pager duty: eval-finance)n- sampling fairness index gini coefficient of executed probes per family alert if gini 0.6 for 72 hoursn- critical-probe-latency slo 95th percentile exec latency 10): owned by evaluation platform (alerts to eval-finance and owner team)n- safety probe failure spike ( 5x baseline in 1 hour): owned by sre safety lead immediate mitigation: pause model rollout and notify product securityn- scheduler backlog summary:nnthis standard defines the metadata, process, and automated checks required to ensure evaluation datasets and synthetic prompt collections used in redwood inference evaluation harnesses are traceable, auditable, and reproducible. it applies to all evaluation artifacts consumed by the eval-orchestrator and offline evaluation pipelines (interactive, batch, and shadow).nnscope and goals:nn- scope: ground-truth datasets, prompt playlists, synthetic generators, sampled mirrors of production traffic, and any derived evaluation artifacts used for model promotion, regression triage, or quality guardrails.n- goals:n - produce a minimum provenance record for every eval artifact that permits exact rehydration in ci and on private/dedicated deployments.n - provide a reproducibility score and gating rules for model promotion and rollout.n - automate metadata capture, enforcement, and lineage visualization.nndefinitions:nn- artifact: any dataset, prompt set, synthetic generator output, or evaluation manifest.n- dataset_id: stable identifier for the upstream source (e.g., redwood/datasets/intent-probes-v2).n- snapshot_sha: git or object-store sha for the exact file(s) used.n- manifest_uri: location in object storage or dataset registry.n- schema_hash: deterministic hash of the record schema (order field names types).n- provenance_level: lowstandardstrict (see provenance levels below).nnprovenance levels and requirements:nn1) low (ad-hoc experiments)n- required fields: dataset_id, created_by, timestamp, manifest_urin- recommendation: include seed when samplingn- not allowed for promotion or production guardrailsnn2) standard (typical evals and benchmark runs)n- required fields: dataset_id, snapshot_sha, manifest_uri, schema_hash, sample_strategy, seed, eval_suite_version, creator_contactn- metadata must be stored in the central data-catalog entry and linked from the eval runn- automated lint must pass (metadata-lint v1.3)nn3) strict (promotion and safety-critical checks)n- all standard fields plus: lineage (upstream datasets used), annotation_guides_version, annotator_ids (or k-anonymized certificate), access_control_audit_uri, differential_privacy_parameters (if applied), reproducibility_scoren- required to use reproducibility_score 0.90 for model promotion to hosted or dedicated clustersnnminimal metadata schema (required keys):nn field description example n-----------------------------n dataset_id canonical dataset name in data-catalog redwood/datasets/intent-probes-v2 n snapshot_sha sha of the gzipped manifest or git tag sha256:2a4b... n manifest_uri s3 or gs uri pointing to the manifest s3://redwood-evals/manifests/intent-probes-v2/2026-01-08.jsonl n schema_hash deterministic hash of field names and types hsh:8f12... n sample_strategy fullstratifiedrandomproduction-mirror stratified:user_segment n seed integer seed for sampling/synth 42 n eval_suite_version semantic version of eval suite used 2026.01.1 n creator_contact owner email or oncall nadia.chen@redwood.ai n provenance_level lowstandardstrict standard nnmandatory fields must be present as top-level keys in the artifact manifest and also as labels in the data-catalog entry. implementations that fail to populate these keys should be rejected by eval-ci pre-submit checks.nnreproducibility score and computation:nnthe reproducibility_score is a number in 0.0, 1.0 that represents the confidence that an artifact pipeline can be deterministically re-executed and yield equivalent evaluation outputs (accounting for known non-determinism). it is computed as a weighted average of:nn- metadata_completeness (30): fraction of mandatory keys present and valid.n- binary_stability (30): whether binaries (evaluator, model surrogate) used are pinned with shas or immutable container digests.n- sample_determinism (20): sampling seeds present and non-random components pinned.n- environment_pin (20): runtime environment pinned (e.g., python packages, cuda driver, runtime container digest).nnthresholds:nn- 0.90: eligible for promotion to canary/dedicated and for use in safety guardrails (strict artifacts require 0.90).nnautomation and enforcement:nn- metadata-lint (cli): runs on any manifest changes. usage:n - metadata-lint validate manifest.json --schema eval-provenance-v1n - metadata-lint compute-score manifest.jsonn - exit codes: 0 pass, 2 warnings, 3 failuren- eval-ci (github/gitlab integration):n - pre-merge hook validates manifest presence and reproducibility_score 0.6 (project config may raise this)n - promotion pipeline requires reproducibility_score 0.90 and provenance_level strictn- data-catalog (service: redwood-data-catalog): automatic registration apin - post /v1/artifacts register payload - returns artifact_id and visual lineage graph linkn- lineage-visualizer: internal service used by sre and qa to render upstream/downstream dependenciesnnpromotion and gating workflow (numbered steps):nn1. author creates or updates evaluation manifest and pushes to the repo or uploads manifest to s3 with manifest_uri.n2. metadata-lint runs locally author fixes schema or missing keys.n3. on pr, eval-ci explainable trust scoring, content: summaryn -------n this playbook describes a standard, reproducible pipeline for (1) calibrating evaluator ensembles, and (2) producing an explainable per-response trust score used by downstream routing, canary gating, and alerting. the document covers terms, data and probe requirements, model-agnostic calibration recipes (temperature scaling, isotonic regression), ensemble aggregation strategies, explainability primitives (feature contributions, provenance tokens), verification tests, and operational runbook items.nn why this existsn ----------------n as redwood supports heterogeneous model variants (full precision, quantized, kv-cache-optimized) and multiple evaluator models (ml-based quality predictors, heuristics, human raters), teams need a single canonical scoring contract that:n - produces well-calibrated probabilities that map to real-world error rates (e.g., p(failure) observed failure frequency).n - is robust across workload slices and domains (multilingual, multimodal, long-context).n - yields explainable signals that can be surfaced in dashboards and used for triage/rollback decisions.nn scopen -----n - applies to evaluator ensembles used in shadow-eval, canary gating, and automated rollback pipelines.n - not intended for training production generation models only for downstream evaluators and meta-decision systems.nn key termsn ---------n - trust score: calibrated probability in 0,1 that an evaluated response meets the acceptance criterion for a slice (higher more trustworthy).n - ensemble: logical combination of multiple evaluators (model-based, heuristic, human label) producing one trust score.n - calibration: post-hoc transform to align predictive probabilities with empirical frequencies.n - slice: workload partition defined by intent, language, prompt family, or tenant.nn acceptance contractn -------------------n for an ensemble to be promoted to production gating, the following targets must be met on the holdout probe set for each critical slice:n - brier score 0.86 for binary failure detectionn - 95 bootstrap ci on predicted failure rate width 0.7 against anchor gold set.n 2) feature telemetry recordedn - evaluator_scores: raw per-evaluator logits/probabilitiesn - input_metadata: model_variant, context_length, client_tier, tenant_id (redacted if required)n - provenance_tokens: contiguous token ranges identified as high-influence by the evaluator (optional for privacy-sensitive slices)nn ensemble architecture patternsn ------------------------------n we recommend the following logical patterns depending on use-case:n - weighted mean (fast, interpretable): trust sum(w_i p_i) / sum(w_i). use when evaluators are independent and have stable per-slice reliability.n - calibrated stacking (meta-learner): train a small logistic/regression stacker on holdout probes to combine outputs and covariates (context length, language). use when evaluators have complementary strengths.n - conservative gating (safe-by-default): if any evaluator reports p_failure 0.95, force trust threshold (store as start:end indices)n - calibration_bucket: one of 0.0-0.1,...,0.9-1.0n example json payload (trimmed):n trust_score: 0.12, top_contributors: e10.05,heuristic-mismatch0.03, highlight_spans: 12:27nn verification testsn decomposition (calibration vs refinement) and automated triage rules:n - if calibration component 60 of brier score, prioritize calibration-focused fixes (more probe data or isotonic).n - synthetic adversarial sweep: apply 3 perturbations per prompt family and assert trust delta store raw telemetry in eval-fs.n 2) run per-evaluator scoring (batch) - persist logits/probs.n 3) fit calibration transforms per-slice - save artifacts to model-registry under namespace eval-calib/ensemble/date.n 4) recompute ensemble scores on validation probes and produce report (automated pr to owners).n 5) if acceptance contract passes, mark artifact as promotable and publish trust scoring config to routing service.nn monitoring alertingn ---------------------n dashboard widgets (redwood console):n - slice-level mean trust and 7d trendn - calibration drift metric (kullback-leibler of bucketed histograms) per slicen alerting rules:n - p1: calibration drift 0.08 over 24h for any slice - pagerduty to eval-oncalln - p2: drop in predictive-auroc 0.07 vs baseline - slack to eval-notifynn rollout checklist for promotionn -------------------------------n - holdout probes archived and checksums recordedn - calibration artifacts uploaded to model-registryn - explainability artifacts validated on 200 examplesn - runbook entry created linking to ensemble config and owner contactsnn troubleshooting common failure modesn -----------------------------------n - low brier but high false negative rate on minority slice:n - action: increase probe representation, retrain slice-aware stacker, or use conservative gating.n - high calibration component (isotonic overfitting):n - action: switch to temperature scaling or regularize isotonic with monotone bin merging.n - annotator dsid_038086c2041043ddb619843d47a7c601, source_type: confluence, title: probe pruning and adaptive sampling playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook defines the probe pruning and adaptive sampling system used by the eval harness to keep continuous evaluations cost-effective while preserving signal for regression detection. it formalizes: probe scoring, pruning thresholds, an adaptive sampler that reallocates budget to high-variance slices, scheduler policies for burst/steady modes, and a safe rollout path for any changes.nnmotivationnnlarge-scale continuous evaluation produces a long tail of low-value probes (very stable slices, duplicated semantics, or highly correlated prompts) that consume budget and increase noise in alerting. by pruning probes and adaptively sampling, we achieve:n- 3060 reduction in probe execution cost for stable workloadsn- faster regression detection on volatile slicesn- lower false-positive alert rates from noisy low-variance probesnnscopennthis document applies to:n- the eval harness scheduler (service: eval-sequencer)n- probe catalog artifacts (probe registry and metadata)n- continuous monitors and alerting rules tied to eval-sentinelsnnnot in scope: manual one-off experiments, offline research-curated benchmark runs.nndefinitionsnn- probe: a single stimulus (prompt context) executed against a model variant and recorded with outputs and telemetry.n- slice: logical grouping of probes (e.g., language, intent, length bucket).n- stability score: running statistic (0..1) where 1 perfectly stable across n recent runs.n- importance score: business-weight multiplier (0.1..10) assigned by owners.nnhigh-level architecturenn1) probe registry enriches probes with base metadata (slice, created_at, owner_team, importance).n2) eval-sequencer assigns probes to worker queues according to adaptive-sample policy.n3) pruner service periodically marks probes as prune_candidate based on scoring rules and retention config.n4) audit logger records all prune actions and supports rehydration for 90 days.nnkey metrics and thresholds (recommended defaults)nn- metric: stability score (rolling 30-day window)n - thresholds: stable if 0.98, semi-stable if 0.950.98, unstable if 0.995 to a higher-ranked probe in same slicen- minimum retained probes per slice: 50 (unless slice cardinality 0.995 and keep the highest-importance/most-recent item.n2) stability floor: for probes with stability 0.99 and age 21 days, mark prune_candidate.n3) low-importance culling: importance 0.97 - prune if slice has minimum retained probes.n4) manual holdouts: probes with flag do_not_prune are preserved.nnadaptive sampling algorithm (overview)nnthe adaptive sampler reallocates probe budget per scheduling epoch (default 24h) based on per-slice signal. steps:n- compute per-slice priority mean(importance max(1, variance_score 10)) recent_violation_factorn- normalize priorities to available budget (tokens / probe cost estimate)n- ensure hard floor: every slice must receive 1 of epoch budget unless explicitly disablednnpseudocode:nnfor each epoch:n load slices sn for s in s:n compute importance_s, variance_s, violation_factor_sn priority_s importance_s max(1, variance_s 10) violation_factor_sn scale priorities so sum(priority) epoch_budgetn assign probes to queue respecting per-slice minimums and per-probe dedup constraintsnnscheduler policiesnn- steady mode: evenly distributed probes across 24h with jitter used for baselining.n- burst mode: directed execution for top-k priority slices when on-call triage requests immediate re-eval or after new model rollout. burst windows capped at 2h and require sre approval.n- canary mode: small fraction (default 2) of new probe templates are exercised for 72h before being added to main catalog.nnconfiguration example (yaml snippet)nn eval-sampler-config.yamlnepoch_period: 24hnmin_slice_budget_pct: 0.01nmin_probes_per_slice: 50nstability_window_days: 30ndedup_cosine_threshold: 0.995nburst_mode_max_window: 2hncanary_fraction: 0.02nprune_scan_interval: 48hnprune_retention_days: 90nnrollout and change controlnnany change to pruning thresholds or adaptive sampler weights must follow this path:n1) draft change proposal in the eval-harness repo with benchmarks (description, config diff, expected savings/risks).n2) submit pr and tag reviewers from applied-ml-and-evals and eng-sre.n3) run controlled experiment (a/b) for 7 days: 10 traffic on new config vs 90 control. record: detection latency for seeded regressions, cost delta, alert noise.n4) if experiment meets pass criteria (10 cost improvement, no increase in high-severity alerts), schedule staged rollout: 10 - 30 - 60 - 100 over 7 days with monitoring gates.n5) post-rollout retrospective and update playbook if necessary.nnpass/fail gate checklist for a/bnn- regression detection latency: no more than 5 worse than controln- alert precision on top-10 slices: not decreased by 3 percentage pointsn- cost per epoch: 10 improvement expected if less, require product sign-offn- no increase in customer-facing incidents attributed to eval changesnnoperational runbook (quick actions)nn- if critical slice goes missing from schedule:n 1) query pruner audit logs: pruner.events?probe_idn 2) rehydrate probe from archival store (rehydrator cli): rehydrator restore --probe --reason emergencyn 3) temporarily mark slice as holdout in probe registry and set min_slice_budget_pct to 0.05n- if adaptive sampler is starving a high-importance slice:n 1) pause prune job: kubectl scale deployment/pruner --replicas0 -n dsid_ffeaaf6110814d89aa7a43398a93426a, source_type: confluence, title: baseline telemetry anchoring and eval seed management, content: overviewnnthis document defines redwoods baseline telemetry anchoring approach and a standardized eval seed management lifecycle. it is intended for ml engineers, sres, and applied ml owners responsible for evaluation stability, promotion gating, and regression triage. the goal is to reduce spurious variance in continuous evals and make failure modes easier to diagnose by controlling seed sources, telemetry baselines, and anchoring strategies across private/dedicated/hosted targets.nnwhy this mattersnn- small changes in rng seeds, tokenization seeding, and probe sampling can inflate perceived variance and trigger false positive regressions.n- anchored telemetry provides a persistent baseline that is resilient to benign nondeterminism while still surfacing meaningful quality regressions.n- standardized seed management enables reproducible replays for triage and quantization regression investigations.nnscope and assumptionsnn- applies to production-facing eval harnesses, long-running shadow evals, and nightly synthesis jobs used for model promotion decisions.n- does not replace deterministic unit tests or model-level determinism efforts it complements them by controlling sampling and anchoring at the eval orchestration layer.n- assumes eval platform can accept explicit rng seeds and deterministic dataset shuffling parameters.nnkey concepts and definitionsnn- anchor set: a small, curated subset of probes used as a stable reference point (typical size: 5002,000 probes depending on workload).n- seed manifest: a versioned file that enumerates rng seeds, shuffle salts, and the indices used to sample anchors and dynamic probes.n- telemetry anchor vector: the vector of baseline metric values (e.g., bleu, rouge, semantic-similarity, latency median) computed over the anchor set for a given model artifact and promotion point.n- seed rotation window: controlled cadence for refreshing the seed manifest (default: quarterly for anchors, weekly for synthetic probes).nnguidelines and requirementsnn1) anchor set creation and stewardshipn - ownership: each product or workload team must nominate an anchor steward (primary backup).n - composition: anchors must cover: n 60 high-frequency, high-impact real traffic slicesn 25 edge / long-tail / adversarial seeds identified from incidentsn 15 synthetic stress probes (long context, function calls, multimodal where applicable)n - annotation: each anchor must have a metadata row (probe id slice origin rationale sensitivity flag). use the anchor manifest template in the examples section below.nn2) seed manifest format and storagen - format: jsonl or csv with columns: manifest_version, seed_id, rng_seed, shuffle_salt, probe_indices, created_by, created_at, role (anchordynamicsynthetic).n - storage: manifests are stored in the eval bucket under path: s3://redwood-evals/manifests/team/workload/manifest_version. lock each manifest with an immutable tag once used for a promotion gate.nn3) telemetry anchoring calculationn - metric computation: compute telemetry anchor vector using the exact seed manifest and the same model runtime config (quant, kv-cache policy, batch config).n - aggregation: report median and 10/90 percentiles for latency mean and std for quality metrics where meaningful.n - baseline window: maintain a rolling baseline history for the last 6 promotion points. use ewma with alpha0.2 to smooth short-lived fluctuations.nn4) seed rotation and freshness policyn - anchor rotation: rotate anchor indices no more frequently than every 90 days unless a triggered incident requires emergency replacement. document reason and vote in the rotation changelog.n - dynamic seed refresh: dynamic probe seed manifests may be refreshed weekly for sampling diversity each refresh must have a different manifest_version and be recorded in telemetry.nn5) promotion and gating protocoln - promotion gate input: automated promotion jobs must reference an immutable manifest_version. the gate compares the new candidate telemetry anchor vector against the preserved baseline vector.n - acceptance criteria: candidate model must not show a statistically significant degradation on more than n slices in the anchor set (n defaults to 2 for 500-1k anchor size). use bootstrap resampling (b1,000) and require p 0.05 for no-regression.n - quality-coverage check: if a candidate improves aggregate metrics but worsens a high-sensitivity anchor (sensitivity flag set), require a product sign-off.nn6) reproducible replay for triagen - repro command: provide the exact cli and environment file to replay an anchor run. example: n n eval-run --manifest s3://redwood-evals/manifests/vision-team/recommendation/v3-manifest-2026-01-12.jsonl n --model-ref model-registry://prod/recommendation/v2.3.1 n --runtime-config runtimes/quantized-gpu.yaml and kernel revision.n 4. record and compare seed hash between original and replayed runs.nnoperational playbooksnn- daily smoke: the eval platform posts a daily anchor vector summary to eval-telemetry. on-call evaluator checks for any drift 2x ewma sigma on critical anchors.nn- regression triage fast path:n 1. triage engineer compares candidate anchor vector to baseline and runs reproducible replay using the manifest_version.n 2. if replay reproduces regression, attach replay artifacts to a regression issue and assign to model owner.n 3. if replay does not reproduce, escalate to platform sre to check runtime/kernel/version mismatch, quant artifact mismatch, or nondeterministic rng sources.nn- emergency anchor replacement: when anchor probes are found compromised (pii leak, invalidated by product change), the steward can replace up to 10 of anchors outside regular rotation. log a post-hoc review within 48 hours.nnmetrics, slos and alertsnn- anchor stability slo: 99 of daily anchor vector differences must be within the ewma 3-sigma band across a 30-day window.n- alerting: create pagerduty alert when:n a single critical anchor drops by 5 absolute in quality or increases latency by 50 p95, orn more than 3 anchors cross the statistical regression threshold during a promotion attempt.nnexamples and templatesnn- anchor manifest snippet (jsonl row):n evaluation pipeline (csep): a reusable, ci-integrated eval harness designed to catch safety regressions, distributional drift on prompt sets, and quantization-induced failure modes across model rollouts and runtime changes. csep unifies prompt selection, metric computation, alerting thresholds, and triage handoffs so that model owners and infra teams can act quickly and reproducibly.nngoalsnn- provide a lightweight, actionable pipeline that runs on prs and nightly schedules.n- surface both absolute safety violations and relative regressions against a pinned baseline.n- make triage deterministic: every failing run produces a standardized artifact bundle for forensics.n- integrate with release gating (canary/rollout) and the model onboarding checklist.nnwhen to use this guidenn- new model onboarding (quantized variants included).n- model or runtime upgrades (e.g., kernel changes, new batching).n- prompt set expansions or production prompt redistributions.n- regression investigations triggered by monitoring alerts.nnhigh-level designnncsep is composed of four stages:nn1) prompt selection and shardingn- use the prompt catalog (see prompt-sets directory) to pick: safety-critical prompts, high-frequency production prompts, and targeted adversarial cases.n- by default: 60 safety suite, 30 prod-sampled, 10 adversarial.n- shards are created deterministically using a seed tied to pipeline run id so reruns are idempotent.nn2) execution harnessn- runs requests against specified model variants (float32, int8/quantized, and fallback variants).n- supports hosted api and dedicated/private endpoints via a unified runner cli.n- tracks timing (p95/p99), token counts, and the raw responses.nn3) metric aggregation and regression testsn- safety metrics include: toxic-span rate, disallowed-instruction triggers, hallucination proxies (entity-mismatch rate), and policy-classifier score distributions.n- quality metrics include: bleu/rouge-style comparisons when references available, embedding-distance drift (cosine), and length-conditioned perplexity proxies.n- two comparison modes: absolute thresholds and relative delta to baseline.nn4) artifact generation and alertsn- pipeline produces a triage bundle: run metadata, raw responses, diffed examples (baseline vs candidate), prompt shards, and a reproducible run config (yaml).n- if checks fail, the pipeline opens a ticket in our tracker with severity and attaches the bundle.nnslos and thresholds (recommended defaults)nn- safety-critical trigger rate (absolute): 30 versus baseline - fail.n- prod prompt acceptance drop: mean acceptance (automated classifiers sample human check) drop 10 - warn.n- token-latency regression: p95 increase 20 - warn p99 increase 30 - fail.n- quantized variant hallucination proxy: relative increase 15 - fail.nnnote: thresholds are tunable per-customer workload the pipeline should set the thresholds from the model certification profile stored in the model registry.nnci integration and flownn1) pull request checks (fast mode)n- runs a lightweight shard (48 safety prompts, 8 prod-sampled) against candidate and baseline short-circuit.n- time budget: 5 minutes.n- outcome: pass/warn/fail comment on pr with summarized metrics and links to full artifacts.nn2) merge/pre-release (full nightly mode)n- runs full safety suite production set quantization sweep.n- schedules on the release branch failure blocks canary rollout.nn3) canary gatingn- canary deploy accepts traffic at 1 if csep green. canary monitored with production telemetry and small quick re-run of csep against live traffic-sampled prompts.nnconfiguration examplesnnexample pipeline yaml (simplified):nnyamlnpipeline: csep-nightlynversion: 1.2nseeds: prompt-subset, and hardware-variant. use the deterministic seed to guarantee consistent sharding.nn4) patch/mitigation optionsn- immediate rollback to pinned baseline (automated option in deployment pipeline).n- deploy model with safety filters enabled (policy classifier / response sanitizer) as a temporary mitigation.n- adjust rollout to 0 and run debugging harness with debug logs (with pii redaction).nn5) postmortem and remediationn- owner files a short rca within 72 hours with attachments from the bundle and a remediation plan.n- if root cause is quant/compilation related, schedule a kernel/infra retro and flag the runtime owner.nnquantization-specific checksnn- include paired runs: quantized vs fp32 with identical seeds and input order.n- compute per-example drift score: embedding cosine drop and policy-score deviation.n- flag examples where policy score crosses the safety threshold in the quantized model but not in fp32.n- maintain a per-model quant-tolerance profile title: longtail continuous scan playbook for production evals, content: summarynnthis playbook describes the longtail continuous scan (lcs) process: an automated, prioritized, and privacy-conscious approach to running small, frequent, and broad-spectrum evaluations of models in production-like conditions. lcs targets tail distributions and low-frequency prompt slices that commonly surface quality regressions after deployments, quantization, or major prompt/handler changes.nnscopenn- applies to redwood studio-managed models and verified open-model variants used in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.n- covers evaluation orchestration, slicing, scheduling, metric thresholds, alerting, and first-response triage for long-tail failures.n- excludes heavy offline human-labeling efforts (those are handled by the annotation pipeline documented separately).nnobjectives and slosnn- detect regression signals originating from: model updates, quantization changes, routing fallback, kv-cache invalidation, and prompt-surface changes.n- time-to-detect: median 6 hours from the first anomalous tail observation.n- time-to-triage (initial owner assignment): 2 hours after a severity-2 alert.n- false-positive rate target: 0.12 triggers a warning 0.25 triggers an incident.n- semantic recall (sr): fraction of ground-truth keyphrases present in model outputs for structured tasks. threshold: drop 6 (relative) triggers a high-priority alert.n- safety-trigger rate (str): rate of policy-flagging tokens per 1k responses. threshold: absolute str 4 and increase 2x baseline triggers immediate review.nnsecondary metrics (profiling):n- median latency (ms), 95th percentile latency, kv-cache hit ratio, and truncated-output rate.nnregression detection heuristicsnn- multi-evidence consensus: an alert requires at least two metric classes to exhibit degradation (e.g., rsi sr), unless the metric is a safety hit.n- rolling-window confirmation: short blips are suppressed using a 3-sample exponential smoothing prior to alerting.n- model-variant correlation: anomalies that correlate only with a single variant (e.g., quantized-int8) tag the alert as quant-suspect.nntriage playbook (first 6 steps)nn1) alert enrichment: the aggregator appends last-known rollout id, model-commit, quant-profile id, and route config.n2) owner assignment: pagerduty integration assigns the alert to the model-owner rotation.n3) immediate checks (automated):n a) verify model-commit changed in the last 24 hours.n b) check kv cache flush events or recent cache eviction logs.n c) examine autoscaler events and pod restarts for the model cluster.n4) canary rollback: if the regression aligns to the canary rollout id and the rollback window is open, trigger automated rollback to prior canary snapshot.n5) shadow replay: launch focused shadow-run against previous known-good variant for 200 seeds. compare diffs and attach to the ticket.n6) human review: if automated checks are inconclusive, assign to applied-ml for semantic review and label impacted slices.nndetailed triage checklist (owners should follow):n- verify reproducibility using the seedset with deterministic rng.n- re-run with and without quantization to isolate numeric sensitivity.n- re-run with cached kv disabled to test cache-sensitivity regressions.n- if safety flags increased, run the safety-deep-eval (1000 synthetic adversarial prompts) before public rollback.nnobservability, alert templates, and runbook snippetsnnalert template (slack / pagerduty summary):n- title: lcs alert: metric regression on route (severity 123)n- body: one-line summary, metric deltas, affected model-variants, last rollout id, link to aggregator graph, and link to reproduction job.nnsuggested grafana panels:n- rsi time-series with slice decomposition (lines per locale/token-length).n- sr per variant as bar-chart with error bands.n- top-10 diffs in token-probability mass as a table.nnautomation
