dynamic-slice-creation-and-priority-scheduling-2026, content: summary:noperational playbook for automatically generating evaluation slices from telemetry and assigning dynamic priorities to each slice for scheduling in the eval harness. reduces manual slice engineering, improves coverage of regressions in long-tail traffic, and integrates with existing promotion and rollback gating.nnbody:noverviewnnthis document defines the dynamic slice creation and priority scheduling system used by the eval harness. the goal is to automatically synthesize actionable evaluation slices from production telemetry, score them by risk/impact, and schedule them into the evaluation queue with appropriate cadence and resource allocation. this complements static slice catalogs and reduces time-to-detection for regressions appearing in the long tail.nnmotivationn----------n- static prompt slice catalogs are brittle and require continuous manual maintenance.n- many regressions surface first in telemetry hotspots or newly emerging user behavior.n- we need a reproducible, auditable pipeline that:n - translates telemetry signal into candidate slices,n - ranks candidates by an explainable priority score,n - schedules slices to the eval harness under capacity constraints, andn - surfaces actionable reports for triage and remediation.nnscopen-----nthis playbook covers:n- slice candidate generation (signals, heuristics, constraints)n- priority scoring function and weighting defaultsn- scheduler rules for the eval mesh/orchestratorn- integration steps for model onboarding and promotion gatingn- monitoring, alerts, and troubleshootingnit does not cover human annotation workflows or label pipelines beyond basic sample labeling used for slice verification.nndefinitionsn-----------n- candidate slice: a compact selector describing a subset of requests (e.g., metadata prompt signature token-length bucket).n- slice fingerprint: deterministic string used to deduplicate candidates.n- hotspot: continuous telemetry region exceeding configured thresholds (e.g., error-rate 2x baseline or latency p95 slo).n- priority score: numeric 0-100 determining scheduling urgency.nndata sources and signalsn------------------------nprimary signals used to generate candidates:n1. error telemetry: response errors, function-call failures, safety sentinel hits.n2. latency anomalies: p50/p95/p99 shifts per model/route/region.n3. semantic drift indicators: embedding drift, response embedding distance to historical buckets.n4. volume surges: sudden increase in request share for a specific route or customer.n5. customer-reported incidents and support tickets (ingested via tag).n6. canary eval deltas: small canary sets that exhibit performance regressions.nncandidate generation algorithm (high level)n-----------------------------------------n1. ingest normalized telemetry windows (default: 24h, configurable).n2. identify hotspots by applying per-route baselines and outlier detection (median absolute deviation).n3. for each hotspot, extract candidate selectors:n - route_id, model_family, customer_tier, locale, device_type, prompt-template-hash, token-length-bucket, top-3 tokens prefix.n4. generate fingerprint: sha1(route_id model_family template_hash token_bucket).n5. deduplicate candidates by fingerprint keep top-n variants per hotspot (default n10).n6. enrich candidates with sample examples and initial lightweight labels (if available).nnpriority scoring (explainable formula)n-------------------------------------nwe use a linear combination of normalized signals to produce a 0-100 priority score. default weights (tunable):n- impacted volume weight (w_vol) 0.30n- error severity weight (w_err) 0.30n- model divergence weight (w_div) 0.20n- customer sla sensitivity weight (w_sla) 0.10n- freshness / growth weight (w_growth) 0.10nnscore computation (pseudocode):nnscore round(100 clamp( w_vol norm(volume_percentile) w_err norm(error_z) w_div norm(embedding_shift) w_sla sla_flag w_growth growth_rate, 0, 1))nnwhere:n- norm(x) maps a signal into 0,1 using historical percentiles.n- error_z is z-score relative to model-route historical error mean.n- sla_flag is 1 for enterprise customers with sla, 0 otherwise.nnpriority tiers (operational):n- 80-100: critical schedule as high-frequency slot, notify on-call triage.n- 60-79: high schedule daily batch, include in weekly regression digest.n- 30-59: medium schedule weekly with lower resource priority.n- 0-29: low schedule opportunistically, aggregated sweeps.nnscheduler rules and quotasn--------------------------n- eval mesh capacity is expressed as concurrent slice slots per hour.n- by default, 40 of capacity reserved for critical/high tiers, 40 for medium, 20 for low.n- per-customer cap: no more than 10 of total slots to a single customer unless approved by cs.n- model-family cap: prevent majority of slots going to a single model family (default 50).n- aging policy: slices that do not surface issues within 4 weekly runs are downgraded automatically.nnscheduler pseudo-workflow:n1. pull prioritized candidate queue, sorted by (priority_score, recency, uniqueness).n2. apply quota constraints and backpressure.n3. allocate to eval runners with appropriate resource profile (e.g., long-context - larger gpu mem).n4. launch evaluation with attached telemetry replay or synthetic generator.n5. capture artifact: eval result, failure trace, example requests, and metrics.n6. if eval triggers regression gates, escalate via regression triage (see triage handoff).nnintegration with model onboarding and promotion gatesn----------------------------------------------------n- new model versions should be shadowed for 72h with an elevated slice sampling weight to detect early regressions.n- promotion requires no critical-tier slices failing and 0 block promotion, immediate triage n high slices failing 10 hold promotion, require mitigations and re-eval n medium slices failing 25 require justification for promotion n regression severity (avg) 0.7 (on 0-1 scale) block and open priority incident nnmonitoring, alerts, and dashboardsn----------------------------------nkey dashboards to build and monitor:n- candidate generation volume by route/model (24h, 7d)n- priority distribution histogram and slot utilizationn- recent failing slices table (with links to artifacts)n- time-to-detection for newly created slicesnalerting thresholds (examples):n- new critical-tier slice created with error_rate 5: page on-call (p1).n- 3 critical slices fail within 24h for a single model family: open incident.nnownership and rolesn-------------------n- ownership: applied ml (owner) maintains heuristics, scoring weights, and integration.n- on-call: eval platform sre handles scheduling failures, runner capacity issues.n- triage: model quality team receives failing slice artifacts and coordinates fixes.n- product/cs: notified for customer-impacting slices.nnrollout plann------------n1. prototype phase (2 weeks): run candidate generator in read-only mode produce candidates and scored outputs to a review queue.n2. pilot (4 weeks): enable scheduling for non-critical tiers and a small model subset.n3. gradual ramp (6 weeks): expand to full model fleet and enable high-priority scheduling.n4. ga: enable promotion gating and integrate with release pipelines.nnoperational slos for the systemn-------------------------------n- candidate latency: new candidate discovered and scored within 15 minutes of telemetry window close (slo 90).n- scheduling success: scheduled candidates start running within 10 minutes of allocation (slo 95).n- artifact availability: evaluation artifacts available for triage within 10 minutes of job completion (slo 99).nntroubleshooting and runbook (quick)n----------------------------------nproblem: candidate queue is empty despite high telemetry volumen1. check ingestion pipeline latency: kafka_consumer_lag 0?n2. confirm hotspot detector thresholds were not misconfigured (path: /config/slicing/hotspot-thresholds.yaml).n3. verify fingerprinting service is healthy look for rate-limiting errors.nnproblem: scheduler failing to allocate slotsn1. inspect the eval-mesh capacity dashboard check for node drains.n2. verify per-model caps are not saturated.n3. check runner pod logs (/var/log/eval-runner/).nnauditing and safetyn------------------n- every candidate and scheduling decision is logged to the audit index with: fingerprint, input signals, score breakdown, scheduled-run-id, and owner.n- slice fingerprints that involve customer pii are redacted if redaction removes determinism, use deterministic surrogate keys.n- security review required for any change that increases sampling for customer data beyond a configured threshold.nnappendicesn---------na. example candidate json (simplified)njsonnn fingerprint: sha1:abc123def,n route_id: chat-completion:v2,n model_family: redwood-rlf-13b,n selectors: dsid_39e95dd057f948c69f01bf24bc925339, source_type: confluence, title: runtime shadow rehearsal and localized probe synthesis playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook defines the runtime shadow rehearsal pattern: an operationalized workflow that (1) synthesizes localized evaluation probes targeted at tenant cohorts, locales, and latency bands (2) runs those probes in a low-risk shadow mesh against quantized and mixed-precision artifacts and (3) performs cost-aware rehearsal passes that validate quality, latency, and coherence before a real rollout. the goal is to detect regressions and quant-induced degradations earlier while bounding evaluation cost and preserving tenant privacy.nnscopenn- applies to model promotion and quantized rollouts for text generation and multi-turn chat services (service names: eval-orch, shadow-mesh, rehearsal-runner).n- covers probe generation, seed selection, rehearsal execution, gating metrics, and rollback triggers.n- intended for on-prem, private vpc, and hosted dedicated deployments.nnwhy this patternnn- longtail and locale-specific regressions often escape coarse global evals. localized probes increase sensitivity to per-tenant failure modes.n- running rehearsals against quantized artifacts in a shadow mesh simulates production mixing without impacting production traffic.n- cost-aware caps and staged rehearsal passes allow teams to validate risk under budget constraints.nnhigh-level componentsnn1) probe fabricator (probe-fabricator)n - responsible for localized probe synthesis: locale-aware lexical meshes, few-shot priming templates, and context anchors.n - inputs: seed traffic fingerprints, tenant taxonomy, priming registry, localization lexicons.n2) shadow mesh (shadow-mesh)n - lightweight runtime that replays probes against quantized variants and the nominal fp32 baseline.n - provides instrumentation (response_coherence, fidelity_delta, q_loss, latency_p95, token_emissions).n3) rehearsal runner (rehearsal-runner)n - orchestrates rehearsal passes, enforces cost caps, aggregates metrics, and writes rehearsal artifacts to eval-orch ledger.n4) gating enginen - applies slos and guardrail rules. produces pass/fail verdicts and recommended rollout decisions.nnlocalized probe synthesis strategynn- taxonomy partitioning: split the tenant base into cohorts along three orthogonal axes: locale (en-us, en-gb, fr-fr, de-de, ja-jp), intent surface (support, search, compose), and latency band (fast p95 500ms).n- for each cohort generate probes across these buckets:n - 40 anchor probes (real user anonymized seeds sampled from last 90 days)n - 40 synthetic perturbations (paraphrases, tokenization edgecases, punctuation/noise injection)n - 20 adversarial variants (contrastive prompts designed to stress hallucination and instruction-following)n- probe counts per rehearsal pass are configurable default targeted sample: 1k probes per cohort for small services, 10k for high-volume services.nnprivacy and provenancenn- anchor probes must be redacted and hashed before leaving telemetry storage (hash-salt per rehearsal job). raw pii is never exported.n- provenance metadata attached to each probe includes cohort_id, seed_hash, probe_type, and priming_template_id.nnrehearsal execution modes (staged passes)nn1) dry-run (low-cost smoke)n - run: 12 of full probe set, quant variants only, no baseline comparison.n - purpose: surface obvious failures and infra incompatibilities. cost cap: x/day (set by team).n2) contrast-passn - run: 20 sample, run against fp32 baseline and quant variant(s). compute fidelity_delta metrics and delta-significance tests.n3) full-rehearsaln - run: 100 probe set, cohort-balanced. includes heavier metrics (token-level divergence, functioncall stability).nngating metrics and thresholdsnnwe compute both statistical and decisionable thresholds. primary signals:nn- fidelity_delta (kl-style scoring templated semantic similarity): fail if cohort mean fidelity_delta 0.12 and throughput-corrected ci excludes zero.n- response_coherence (annotator-simulated score 01): fail if cohort p90 0.08.n- q_loss (quantization artifact score): fail if absolute q_loss increase 0.05 and correlated with token_emission anomalies.n- latency_p95: fail if latency_p95 increase 2x and exceeds target slo band for that cohort.n- embedding_stability (for retrieval/rerank): fail if cosine shift 0.06 on average for critical slices.nndecision matrix (simplified)nn- if any cohort fails fidelity_delta and response_coherence - abort rollout for that cohort and open regression ticket.n- if only latency_p95 regression observed but coherence preserved - engage ops throttling capacity reroute and run narrow replay.n- if q_loss is high but coherence preserved for anchor-probes - schedule quant-tuning pass and run targeted micro-rehearsal.nnrunbook: step-by-step rehearsal for a scheduled quant rolloutnn1) preflight (owner: modelonboard team)n - create rehearsal job in eval-orch: include cohort list, probe budget, quant-variant ids, and expected cost cap.n - run quick smoke locally with rehearsal-runner dry-run mode: run command below.n2) dry-run review (owner: release lead)n - confirm no infra errors in shadow-mesh logs, check instrumentation counters (request_e2e_errors proceed to phased production rollout.n - if some cohorts fail - open triage (link created) and either rollback quant artifact or schedule micro-tunings.n6) post-rehearsal monitoring (owner: sre)n - enable rehearsal-derived sentinels for 72 hours post-rollout and maintain elevated sampling of failed cohorts.nncli examplesnn start a dry-run rehearsal (example)nrehearsal-runner start --job-id rjr-20260712-01 --cohorts en-us:support:fast,de-de:compose:medium --mode dry-run --probe-budget 200 --quant-variant qv-2.1 --cost-cap 200nn run contrast-pass and upload reportnrehearsal-runner start --job-id rjr-20260712-02 --mode contrast --probe-budget 2000 --quant-variant qv-2.1 --baseline mv-1.0 --report-bucket s3://eval-orch/reports/rjr-20260712-02nnyaml rehearsal job manifest (example)nnjob_id: rjr-20260712-02nowner: model-onboardncohorts:n - id: 1000nquant_variants:n - qv-2.1nbaseline: mv-1.0nmode: contrastncost_cap_usd: 1500nretention_days: 30nninterpretation and reportingnn- reports include cohort-level summaries, ranked failure slices, example failing probes, and suggested remediation actions. attachments include raw witness tokens (hashed) and aggregated diff visualizations.n- use the provided report template (report-template-v2) dsid_03945652609045ed841cb7f09902de02, source_type: confluence, title: evaluator backpressure and priority fairness playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook documents the design and operational procedures for the distributed evaluator backpressure subsystem and priority-fairness scheduler used by redwoods eval mesh. it targets evaluator-sidecar and orchestrator components responsible for running probes, scoring outputs, and returning telemetry while respecting product slas and evaluator resource constraints.nngoalsn- prevent evaluator overload during spikes in probe load or slow downstream services.n- ensure tenant and slice priority classes receive fair shares of evaluation budget.n- provide deterministic and observable behavior for on-call engineers.n- make graceful degradation decisions (deferred probes, sampled execution, degraded fidelity) explicit and reversible.nnscopen- applies to: eval-orchestrator, evaluator-sidecar, probe-priority-agent, and the probe-queue services running in the eval mesh.n- not in scope: probe generation policies and annotation pipelines (handled by probe fabrication).nnbackground and motivationn- we run heterogeneous probes (shadow traffic, synthetic seeds, long-context functioncall tests) across a fleet of evaluators. peaks (e.g., model rollouts, heavy shadow validation) can saturate cpu/gpu and cause unexpected increases in latency and cost.n- previous incidents (see incident-2025-eval-thundering.json) showed cascading failures when thousands of long-context probes simultaneously retried after transient kv-cache warmup failures.nndesign principlesn1) observable decisions: every backpressure action must emit an event with reasoning tags (reason, affected_slice, priority_class, resource_util).n2) predictable fairness: priority classes map to weight buckets allocation follows weighted fair queuing with bounded latency targets.n3) multi-tier degradation: prefer fidelity reduction (e.g., use draft evaluator config - sample fewer seeds) before dropping high-priority probes.n4) recovery-first rollbacks: automated scaling/backpressure policies must be paired with an explicit rollback and a health-check gating policy.nnkey termsn- priority_class: gold, silver, bronze, infra.n- probe_token: logical unit charged against a probe budget.n- soft_limit: policy threshold that triggers degradation not an immediate reject.n- hard_limit: reject threshold requiring immediate shedding.nnarchitecture and componentsn- eval-orchestrator: central controller that assigns probes to evaluator pools and updates policies via /api/v1/policy-sync.n- evaluator-sidecar: local agent on evaluator hosts that enforces per-host queueing, backpressure decisions, and emits telemetry to eval-metrics-service.n- probe-queue: redis-backed sharded queue used for short-lived probe bursts.n- probe-priority-agent: service that converts business priority into scheduling weights and budgets.nnslos and operational thresholdsn- probe completion slo (p95): 2.5s for short probes (4096 tokens) in gold class for hosted evaluation.n- queue wait soft_limit: host cpu util 70 or queue length 250 - trigger soft degradation.n- queue wait hard_limit: host cpu util 92 or queue length 1000 - reject non-infra probes.n- backpressure event emission: 100 of decisions must emit to eval-metrics-service with keys: decision_type, priority_class, queue_len, cpu, mem.nnpriority class weights (default)n- gold: weight 8n- silver: weight 4n- bronze: weight 1n- infra: weight 12 (reserved for infra-critical probes)nnbackpressure strategy (high level)n1) admission control: evaluator-sidecar applies per-priority leaky-bucket admitting tokens at rate base_rate weight.n2) soft degradation: when soft_limit hit, execute in this order:n a) reduce sample rate by 50 for bronze/silver probes.n b) convert 1k-token long probes to trimmed probes (context pruning rules applied).n c) de-prioritize functioncall-heavy probes by requeueing with lower routing priority.n3) hard reject: when hard_limit triggered, reject bronze probes first, then silver gold and infra should remain unless host is dangerously saturated.n4) circuit breaker for downstream dependencies: if downstream scorer latency 2x baseline for 30s, temporarily pause new probes that require that scorer and route to fallback scorer.nndetailed procedure: host-side enforcement (evaluator-sidecar)n1) monitor: collect per-host cpu, gpu util (if present), queue_length, avg_probe_latency (sliding 1m).n2) evaluate thresholds in order: if cpu 92 or queue_length 1000 - hard_limit path. else if cpu 70 or queue_length 250 - soft_limit path.n3) soft limit actions (atomic):n - emit event: post /telemetry/backpressure with payload: host,reason,queue_len,priority_sampled.n - apply adaptive sampler: for priority_class in bronze, silver, set sample_rate max(0.1, current 0.5).n - trim contexts: call local priming microservice to apply configured context_trim_rules (see config table).n4) hard limit actions (atomic):n - reject policy: return http 429 with x-backpressure-reason header.n - requeue infra probes to dedicated infra pool when possible.n - trigger autoscaler webhook: post /ops/autoscale-requests with reason evaluator_hard_limit.nnconfiguration matrix (reference)n config_key default description contextual slice replay orchestration and anchoring playbook, content: summary:nthis playbook describes the orchestration pattern we use to reliably replay workload slices through the eval harness and to anchor slice-level baselines across model promotions, quantization changes, and serving runtime updates. it combines deterministic replay, stochastic resampling, and anchor scoring so teams can detect, localize, and triage regressions with high signal-to-noise and consistent instrumentation.nnpurpose:n- provide a reproducible, operationalized pattern for slice extraction, replay orchestration, and anchor creation.n- ensure slice baselines are portable across environments (shadow, dedicated, hosted) and model variants (float, quantized).n- reduce regression triage time by surfacing causal candidates and providing pre-baked diffs for human review.nnscope:n- applies to: interactive generation and chat workloads, embedding batches with context metadata, and reranking pipelines where per-request context affects outputs.n- not in scope: low-level kernel tuning, hardware provisioning, or privacy-incompatible datasets (see privacy-first-shadow-eval page for those).nnkey definitions:n- slice: a named subset of traffic defined by metadata predicates (intent, language, client_id, prompt_template, context_window).n- replay job: an orchestrated execution of a slice through a target model/config combo in the eval harness.n- anchor: a compact summary of prior-run outputs and metrics used as a stable baseline for monitoring and comparison.n- anchor score: multidimensional metric vector (accuracy proxy, semantic drift, response-stability-index, token-cost) used to detect changes.nnownership and responsibilities:n- slice owner: product/feature team that defines the slice semantics and acceptance criteria. (primary contact required)n- eval harness owner: eng applied-ml team maintains replay infra, scheduler, and artifact storage.n- regression triage owner: model reliability squad drives investigation workflows and rollbacks.nndata and artifact requirements:n- inputs: canonicalized request objects (jsonl), tokenizer metadata, kv-cache seeds for long-context tests, and deterministic rng seeds where sampling is allowed.n- outputs: model responses (text/structured), logits or top-k token distribution (when available), embedding vectors, and per-request telemetry (latency, cost, route).n- storage: run artifacts are persisted in the eval-artifacts bucket under /slices/slice_name/run_id/ with an index.json manifest.nnslice definition matrix (example):n slice name predicate purpose min sample owner n critical-invoice-phrases languageen and intentinvoice and prompt_templateinvoice-summarize business-critical nlu checks 500 billingfe n low-resource-lang-zh languagezh and client_tierfree coverage for low-resource tokens 200 i18n n long-context-chats context_tokens2048 and interaction_typechat kv cache and attention stability 300 conversationalai nnreplay orchestration procedure (step-by-step):n1. slice registration: feature team registers slice in the slice registry with predicate, sample window, and ttl. include a canonical prompt set (30200 examples) and an acceptance rubric.n2. sampling and seeding: the harness sampler pulls n requests according to the slice window and injects deterministic rng seeds and kv-cache seeds. for stochastic anchors, include m resamples per request (default m3).n3. environment mapping: map the target run to a model artifact (sha or model-id), quant-profile (if any), runtime image, and routing policy.n4. dry-run validation: run a small pilot (1020 requests) to validate tokenization parity and that no privacy flags are triggered.n5. full replay: schedule the replay job on the eval cluster. use priority queues for critical slices. capture raw outputs, metadata, and system telemetry.n6. anchor computation: compute anchor vectors (see anchoring baselines) and persist alongside run artifacts.n7. diff and alerting: compute delta vs. anchor and run automated checks. if thresholds exceeded, create a regression ticket with pre-populated findings.nnanchoring and baseline procedures:n- anchor types:n - snapshot anchor: full-run anchor created at release cut and stored permanently.n - rolling anchor: windowed anchor computed over the latest x runs (default x7) for stable slices.n - synthetic anchor: for small slices, generated by augmentation and weighted sampling.n- anchor content: for each request store response hash, embedding centroid, top-5 token distributions, stability score, and cost per request.n- anchor scoring (example calculation):n - response-stability-index (rsi) fraction of requests with normalized similarity 0.85 (cosine for embeddings, bleu/rouge/semsim for text)n - semantic-drift 1 - average cosine(embedding_current, embedding_anchor)n - token-cost-delta (tokens_current - tokens_anchor)/tokens_anchorn- anchor retention policy: snapshot anchors retained indefinitely. rolling anchors retained 90 days. synthetic anchors retained 30 days.nnmetrics, thresholds, and automated checks:n- primary alarm triggers (per-slice):n - rsi drop 0.10 create p2 regression ticket.n - semantic-drift increase 0.08 auto-run triage (bisect by model and quant-config).n - token-cost-delta 0.20 and rsi drop 0.05 flag for cost-quality tradeoff review.n - latency increase 25 p50 or p95 breach route to infra runbook.n- evaluation metrics to compute per-run: rsi, semantic-drift, top-token-shift (kl divergence), fidelity score (task dependent), and end-to-end correctness (if labeled).nnintegration with quantization profiles and runtime variants:n- label each replay job with quant_profile_id and runtime_image. store quantization metadata (bit-width, per-channel/per-tensor, calibration dataset id).n- recommended workflow when testing quantized variants:n 1. run float baseline anchor (if not present).n 2. run deterministic quantized replay with identical seeds.n 3. compute paired diffs and generate per-request failure indicators.n 4. if divergences exceed thresholds, run targeted per-layer micro-benchmarks and create a quant-failure case.n- crossworkload guidance: for heterogeneous slices (e.g., embeddings generation), anchor each signal type separately and compute a composite anchor score.nnregression triage fast-path (operational playbook):n1. auto-classify: harness computes candidate root causes using heuristics (config mismatch, tokenizer drift, quantization delta, prompt template change, model version).n2. automated bisect: run binary bisect across commits or model snapshots to narrow to a 12 commit window.n3. localize to dimension: use per-request diffs to determine if failure is concentrated in prompts, languages, or client ids.n4. escalate: if auto-classify confidence p1 thresholds, perform rollback to last snapshot anchor and notify sre.nncli / api examples:n- create replay job (curl):n curl -x post -h authorization: bearer token -h content-type: dsid_f4bd6dad16384ff09f6de106c6ebc795, source_type: confluence, title: workload-mirroring-fork-and-eval-scenario-library-2026, content: overview:nthis document defines a curated library of workload mirroring and synthetic fork scenarios, the process to synthesize them for offline and shadow evaluation, and the acceptance criteria used during model onboarding and quantization qualification. the goal is to provide a consistent, repeatable set of adversarial and production-proximate scenarios to validate latency, correctness, cache behavior, token economy, and regression risk across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.nnmotivation and scope:n- motivation: many regressions and cost surprises arise from rare workload interactions (prefix-skew, irregular kv-cache reuse, long-context fragmentation, or mixed function-calling loads). a compact scenario library reduces surprise by exercising these corner cases during promotion and before rollouts.n- scope: this playbook covers generation, execution, metrics, and triage for: production traffic mirroring, synthetic forks of sessions, quantization-aware shadow runs, latency/failure injection, and multi-tenant noise stress. it does not replace end-to-end customer integration testing rather it complements field tests and unit-level evals.nnkey concepts and terminology:n- mirror: a passive copy of production requests routed to a non-production endpoint without affecting responses to users.n- fork: a diverging variant of a mirrored request where inputs are perturbed (e.g., prompt rewrite, tokenization noise) to create stress cases.n- shadow-run: active execution of models in parallel to production that can run expensive computations (e.g., quantized variants) and collect trace/outputs for offline comparison.n- fidelity-weighted score (fws): composite measure combining semantic similarity, token delta, and downstream metric impact to rank regressions.nnscenario taxonomy (summary table):n id name primary risk vector intended use run mode n s001 prefix-skew chaining prefix reuse kv eviction shadow-run offline diff mirroring/fork n s002 long-context fragmentation (l-16k) memory blowup, kernel change performance and latency slo test shadow-run n s003 mixed-stream tool-calls function call-heavy interleaving correctness structured output mirroring/fork n s004 quantized-roundtrip stress quantization numerical drift compare quant profiles to fp16 quant-aware shadow n s005 burstcold-cache sudden traffic burst with empty kv autoscaling and throughput mirroring with traffic shaping n s006 tokenization adversarials unusual unicode / whitespace model stability and token economy fork synthetic perturbations n s007 multi-tenant interference noisy co-tenants, rate limit backpressure isolation and fallback behaviors mirroring in dedicated pools n s008 latency injection retry storms network lag client retries fallbacks and idempotency mirroring with fault-injection neach scenario in the library includes: a description, input perturbation recipe, traffic shaping parameters, collection hooks, and acceptance thresholds.nnhow to synthesize a forked workload (step-by-step):n1) documented.n- fws threshold: any scenario with fws 0.35 requires blocking investigation 0.200.35 is warning and needs owner signoff.n- error amplification: increased downstream error-rate (e.g., malformed json tool call) by 0.5 must be triaged.nnintegration with model onboarding and quantization profiles:n- promotion gates: for a model or quant profile to be promoted to dedicated/private, it must pass the scenario set mapped to the workload tier (see promotion matrix below).n- promotion matrix (text):n - tier: critical-customer routes - must pass s001, s003, s004, s008 and have fws must pass s002, s005, s006, s007 with latency/p99 criteria.n - tier: internal tools - must pass s001 and s006 with semantic drift checks.n- quant-aware shadow runs: run quantized profile side-by-side with fp16 for at least three independent seeds and compute token-level divergence and downstream metrics. automate this in ci with eval-harness run-quant-shadow --seeds 3 --compare-tofp16.nnexecution narrow to perturbation combinations. use eval-harness bisect --scenario s001 --split perturbation to automate.n4) localize: identify whether drift is due to tokenization, sampling, quantization, or requests., doc_id: dsid_80a0d6a8d1574c4fa0b6fa7ec134b499, source_type: confluence, title: tokenization robustness testbed and operational procedures, content: overviewnnthis page documents the tokenization robustness testbed: a repeatable, automated evaluation harness and operational playbook for detecting, triaging, and preventing tokenization and byte-level drift across model onboarding, quantization, and runtime upgrades. the testbed focuses on mismatches between expected token sequences and runtime tokenization behavior, errors introduced by tokenizer-regression after merges, and failure modes that cause silent semantic changes (e.g., whitespace-sensitivity, unicode normalization, byte-order-mark handling).nnwhy this mattersnn- tokenization changes are a frequent, low-signal source of downstream quality regressions (classification label shifts, hallucination triggers, changed prompt completions).n- quantized kernels and low-level runtime changes can subtly change token boundary behavior these are often missed by standard semantic-only evals.n- for enterprise customers operating in regulated domains, tokenization determinism is part of certification and audit.nnscope and non-goalsnn- in scope: tokenizer behavior across model variants and runtime kernels, tokenizer quantizer interactions, cross-locale unicode normalization, and token-level privacy filters.n- out of scope: overall semantic evaluation (covered by regular eval harness), dataset labeling policies, and user-facing prompt rewriting features.nnarchitecture and componentsnn- eval-orchestrator: schedules runs, stores artifacts to s3-compliant storage (service: eval-runner).n- token-fuzzer: generator of edge-case input (emoji sequences, zwj clusters, bidi text, bom prefixed inputs, mixed normalization).n- tokenizer-checker: deterministic reference tokenizer (pinned to model-catalog version) used as ground truth for token sequence comparisons.n- runtime-prober: executes tokenization emergency mitigation, and long-term prevention for cascading failures in the eval harness probe pipeline. we define failure modes that commonly cause large-scale evaluation regressions, provide an emergency runbook to restore safe continuity, and list durable design changes and configuration standards to prevent recurrence.nnscopen- applies to the eval-harness execution plane (probe generator, sequencer, shadow router, and annotator ingestion queue).n- includes interactions with: quantized shadow artifacts, kv cache warmup probes, and external annotator workers.n- does not cover model training pipeline bugs or user-facing product incidents unless they are caused by an eval probe cascade.nnwhy this mattersn- a single overloaded probe generator or stalled annotation queue can amplify into systemic false-positive regressions, wasted compute, and production instability for private/dedicated shadowing.n- detecting and containing cascades early preserves evaluation fidelity, reduces noise for oncall, and keeps rollout gates (canaries, quant rollbacks) actionable.nnsymptoms (observable metrics)n- probe-failure-rate (probe.errors / probe.total) 5 for 30m.n- sequencer queue latency (p95) 10s or steady growth for 15m.n- annotation backlog 10k unprocessed items and ingestion rate falling 30 vs baseline.n- spike in duplicate probes / replays (indicates retry storm).n- sudden divergence between shadow and synthetic control probes (indicates quantization or cache mismatch).nncommon root-cause patternsn1. backpressure amplification: downstream annotator lag triggers probe retry policy which pushes more load upstream.n2. retry storms: aggressive retry policy (low jitter, high concurrency) transient infra failure - exponential traffic.n3. quantization-induced behavioral skew: quantized model variant returns unexpected tokens and triggers extra post-processing or longer traces.n4. sequencer scheduling inversion: priority inversion where low-priority bulk probes starve critical control probes.n5. resource exhaustion: ephemeral node oom or gpu out-of-memory causing probe workers to exit repeatedly and restart.n6. telemetry blindspots: missing sampling of failed probe payloads, preventing root-cause attribution.nnemergency mitigation runbook (fast path)nrun this immediately when alerts indicate a spike matching the symptoms above. the goal is to stop amplification and buy time for a careful rollback/repair.nnownership: eval-platform oncall (primary), model-onboarding (secondary), infra-sre (escalate when node-level ooms are present).nnimmediate steps (015 minutes)n1) acknowledge pager and post incident stub in eval-incidents with tags: cascade, severity:high.n2) throttle probe ingestion: flip the sequencer rate-limit toggle to 20 of normal via the source_type: confluence, title: synthetic user simulation and long-tail eval protocol, content: overviewnthis document defines the synthetic user simulation (sus) framework and the long-tail evaluation protocol (ltep) used by redwood inference to validate model behavior and serving correctness across rare, compound, and emergent input patterns. the intention is to produce repeatable, auditable simulations that exercise production routing, caching, kv behavior, quantized execution, and fallback logic.nngoalsn- provide a reproducible harness for generating realistic long-tail user slice: a labeled subset of sessions sharing attributes (e.g., nonstandard tokenization, mixed languages, deep-turn 40).n- perturbation: synthetic modification applied to inputs (typos, injection tokens, sentence shuffling, prefix truncation).nnhigh-level architecturen1. seed catalog: canonical prompt templates, persona generators, and locale distributions.n2. perturbation engine: applies deterministic/noisy transforms to seeds with reproducible rng seeds.n3. session mixer: composes multi-turn sequences, optional tool calls, and stateful kv cache interactions.n4. runner: executes dsid_9b131522e77946fcbcafa68ac3ddcf50, source_type: confluence, title: probe dependency graph and orchestration manifest, content: overviewnnpurpose: define the probe dependency graph (pdg) concept, data model, orchestration manifest, and operational procedures for coordinating evaluation probes across shadowing, quantization migration, and regression triage. the pdg ensures probes run in dependency-aware order, minimizes redundant work, and encodes quality/latency constraints for mixed-slo workloads.nnscope: this doc covers the pdg schema, node/edge semantics, orchestration priority rules, example manifests, runtime integration points with the eval harness, and a step-by-step runbook for probe incidents and migrations. it applies to: evaluator teams, model-onboarding engineers, and the runtime/ci owners.nnwhy a pdg?n- probes increasingly depend on the outputs of other probes (e.g., priming templates, cached kv artifacts, quant-safety classifiers). without explicit dependency management, we see wasted compute, nondeterministic scheduling, and triage complexity during regressions.n- pdg centralizes dependency metadata so the eval engine can reuse intermediate artifacts, schedule co-located runs, and generate clear blame paths for regressions.nnkey conceptsnn1) node types (table)n node_type purpose critical_fields owner n probe primary evaluation probe (promptseedslice) id, slice_id, cost_estimate, expected_latency_ms evaluator n transformer artifact producer (priming template generator, tokenizer shim) id, image, cache_key evaluator n quant-job quantization candidate run (per-model/per-profile) id, profile, quant_level applied-ml n kv-cache generated cache snapshot used by downstream probes id, model_version, ttl_sec infra n aggregator combines probe outputs into metrics (e.g., coherence, fidelity) id, metric_list, window_size applied-ml nn2) edge semanticsn- depends_on: downstream node must wait for upstream to complete successfully.n- uses_cache: downstream can reuse upstream artifacts orchestration may skip run if cache is fresh.n- optional_if_failed: if upstream fails, downstream can run a degraded flow (e.g., fallback prompt) but must be tagged in manifest.nn3) contract rulesn- each node declares slo tags: latency_budget_ms, budget_tokens, fidelity_min (0-1).n- orchestrator enforces a soft-deadline nodes that miss latency_budget_ms are flagged and the scheduler may deprioritize their dependents.n- cost_estimate is required (usd/minor_units) to support eval budgeting and probe eviction.nnpdg manifest: yaml examplen example pdg manifest (annotated)nversion: v1nmanifest_id: pdg-example-card-promotion-2027ndescription: pdg for card-promotion ranking probe set with quant shadowingnnodes:n - id: tkn-priming-v1n type: transformern image: gcr.io/redwood/primers/tkn-priming:202701n cache_key: primer/tkn-v1/sha256:abcdn owner: evaluatorn outputs: kv-cache:primer-tkn-v1n - id: probe-ranking-an type: proben slice_id: ranking-promo-an depends_on: tkn-priming-v1n expected_latency_ms: 120n cost_estimate: 0.003n fidelity_min: 0.85n owner: evaluatorn optional_if_failed: truen - id: quant-shadow-lown type: quant-jobn profile: int8-dynamicn depends_on: probe-ranking-an owner: applied-mln expected_latency_ms: 500n cost_estimate: 0.02nedges:n - from: tkn-priming-v1n to: probe-ranking-an relation: uses_cachen - from: probe-ranking-an to: quant-shadow-lown relation: depends_onnnintegration pointsn- eval orchestrator api: post /eval/orchestrate with manifest_id and run_policy (immediate scheduled canary). the orchestrator returns run_id and a plan with task-level eta estimates.n- cache registry: pdg nodes that declare outputs must register artifacts into the central cache service under the manifest namespace. the registry stores artifact provenance and ttl.n- telemetry hooks: each node emits standardized spans (pdg.node.start/stop) and a final overviewnnthis document describes the synthetic mosaic evaluation pattern: a composable approach that combines localized priming, canonicalization, and quant-fallback probes to produce robust, cost-aware onboarding signals for edge and mixed-precision llm services (multilingual, function-call capable). the goal is to detect quality regressions and quantization sensitivity across low-frequency slices while keeping eval cost bounded.nnwho this is forn- ml engineers running model onboarding and quant migration for production services.n- evaluation owners responsible for probe portfolios and telemetry contracts.n- sres operating mixed-precision fleets and canary rollouts.nnwhy we need a mosaic patternn- rare-intent and multilingual slices often fail silent quality checks because synthetic probes dont capture priming/context artifacts.n- quantization and kv-cache interactions cause subtle coherence regressions only visible under particular priming and canonicalized inputs.n- running exhaustive full-fidelity evals is cost-prohibitive we need a low-cost hedging strategy that surfaces high-risk slices for deeper inspection.nnkey concepts and definitionsn- mosaic probe: a small, intentional bundle of related probes for a target slice combining (a) primed variants (localized priming), (b) canonicalized transformations (standardized inputs), and (c) quant-fallback comparisons (float baseline vs quantized variant).n- localized priming: repeatable short-context priming patterns representative of real user prompts (e.g., product-specific examples, local date/time formats, code snippets).n- canonicalization: deterministic normalization applied to inputs (token-level normalization, whitespace/casing rules, function-call structure canonicalization) to reduce noise and isolate model changes.n- quant-fallback probe: paired evaluation where the same probe is executed against a float baseline and the intended quantized runtime to measure fidelity delta and emergent failure modes.nnscope and applicabilityn- target services: any text-generation or function-call endpoint that will run mixed-precision or quantized models. works for multilingual and few-shot scenarios.n- not intended for: high-frequency ad-hoc prompts (use live telemetry probes instead) or purely embedding-only services.nndesign componentsn1) probe family compositionn - for each service slice, synthesize 612 mosaic probes grouped into three cohorts: primed (4), canonical (4), edge-variants (2).n - primed cohort: same prompt stem with 3 distinct priming templates (e.g., product example, short narrative, structured list).n - canonical cohort: normalized transformations (strip extraneous punctuation, standardize dates to yyyy-mm-dd, canonicalize function-call json ordering).n - edge-variants: long-context and truncated-context variants to stress kv-cache behavior.nn2) lightweight fidelity scoring (cost-aware)n - use a two-stage scoring pipeline: (a) cheap lexical/semantic heuristics (bleu-lite, token overlap, function-call schema match) and (b) selective human or heavy automated eval for flagged probes.n - flagging thresholds are configured in the rollout table below.nn3) quant-fallback delta measurementn - execute mosaic probes against float-baseline (f32 or established gold) and quant-target (q4/nn) and calculate: token-level edit distance, function-call schema delta, hallucination indicator score, and perplexity ratio.nnonboarding checklist (step-by-step)n1. identify service slices for coverage: list top-50 rare-intent slices by traffic fraction 0.12 mark probe flagged detailed human review n function-call schema mismatch rate 2 mismatches / 10 probes block function-call rollout annotate and escalate to model-owner n hallucination indicator (heuristic) 0.15 alert on slice pair with semantic eval n latency delta (quant vs float) 20 increase flag perf regression sre triage n cost delta (tokens/response) 30 increase evaluate batching/priming tweak cost-owner review nn- notes: thresholds are intentionally conservative for canary stages and can be relaxed for low-risk slices.nncommands eval harness snippetsn- example invocation (local evaluator cli):nn ./evalctl run --suite mosaic --slice-id auth-email-rare --model baseline-f32 --model-compare q4a --seeds 42 --out results/auth-email-mosaic.jsonnn- minimal yaml config (mosaic probe family):nn suite: mosaicn slice_id: auth-email-raren probes: 8n priming_templates:n - you are a helpful assistant. example: product handles ...n - short explain: questionn canonicalization:n date_format: yyyy-mm-ddn strip_whitespace: truen quant_targets: q4a, q8_0nnmonitoring and alerts (metric - alert rule)n- alert: mosaic_flag_highn condition: flagged_probes(slice) 2 within 1hn severity: p2n runbook: follow troubleshooting section, escalate to model-owner and sre if function-call mismatch present.nn- alert: quant_fidelity_regressionn condition: aggregate_token_edit_ratio 0.10 over 1k probesn severity: p1n runbook: immediate rollback candidate and postmortem.nntroubleshooting and typical failure modesn1) many canonical probes flagged but primed probes okn - likely: canonicalization rules overly aggressive re-check tokenization boundary handling. re-run with less aggressive normalization.n2) primed probes fail but canonical passn - likely: priming artifacts interact with decoding policy. test with temperature0 and deterministic seeds. consider priming rewrite to shorter anchors.n3) function-call semantics diverge after quantizationn - run schema-preserving canonicalization (stable key ordering) and increase float baseline sample size. if mismatch persists, block rollout for function-call routes.n4) high latency delta with quant targetn - confirm execution backend uses optimized kernels check kernel selection logs and hardware affinity. if hardware mismatch, route to dedicated capacity.nnoperational responsibilitiesn- probe synthesis and maintenance: applied ml (probe-stewards) primary: priya nair.n- eval executions and scoring pipeline: eval infra team primary: lucas kim.n- rollout decisions and business impact signoff: service owners and product manager.n- sre on-call for perf regressions: eng sre rotation.nnacceptance criteria for promotionn- zero p1-flagged rollout thresholds and yaml snippets., doc_id: dsid_543ca6caa93c4591a882241c9e22b8c6, source_type: confluence, title: test amplification and latent failure detection, content: summary:nthis document describes our standard for generating amplified test collections from a small set of real failures (latent or observed) to uncover related regressions and emergent failure modes across model variants, quantization profiles, and serving configurations. it bridges the eval-harness, prompt set curation, model onboarding and regression triage processes by describing a repeatable pipeline, danger taxonomy, recommended mutation strategies, and concrete ci / runtime checks to catch latent failures earlier in the lifecycle.nnwhy we need test amplification:n- hand-labeled or in-field failures are often sparse. small seeds may hide families of correlated failures that only appear under slightly different prompts, context truncation, or kv-cache conditions.n- amplification reduces expensive human annotation by generating prioritized synthetic variants that trigger edge behaviors.n- it helps map failure surfaces across deployment axes: model family, sequence length, batch size, quantization format (int8/4/fp16), and routing fallbacks.nnintended audience:n- applied ml engineers owning eval harness integration and model onboardingn- runtime engineers validating quantization/latency trade-offsn- sre and qa teams running pre-release gating suitesn- solutions engineers investigating customer-exposed regressionsnngoals and acceptance criteria:n- a documented amplification pipeline that converts a seed corpus (n gt 5 failing examples) into a prioritized test bundle of 2002,000 variants within 24h.n- amplified tests must include metadata: mutation type, expected failure signal (classification/semantic divergence/unsafe output), trigger conditions (seq_len, kv_cache_percent), and reproducibility flags.n- ci gates must detect statistically significant degradation at pre-defined thresholds (see slos table).nnslos and alert thresholds (recommended):n- latent failure coverage: amplification should increase unique failure triggers by 3x relative to seed set in a single run (target: 3x10x).n- regression detection sensitivity: if model a model b causes a mean response-stability-index (rsi) drop gt 5 on amplified bundle, block promotion and raise p1 review.n- quantization amplification check: any amplified test that flips a safety classifier label (safe unsafe) or changes top-1 intent should be flagged as a critical regression.nnfailure taxonomy (for labeling amplified tests):n1) semantic drift generated variant changes desirable intent despite surface similarity.n2) safety flip content becomes policy-violating after transformation or quantization.n3) hallucination spike previously factual response is now fabricated or inconsistent.n4) truncation sensitivity longer or shorter context changes answer in unacceptable ways.n5) cache-dependent nondeterminism responses diverge when kv cache reuse is simulated.n6) tokenization edgecases whitespace/punctuation/emoji changes tokenization and triggers an error or change in behavior.nnamplification strategies (ordered by priority):n1. orthographic and punctuation perturbationsn - add/remove punctuation, swap hyphens vs em-dash, normalize unicode.n - example: state-of-the-art state of the art, add zero-width space.n2. context slicing and prefix variationn - prepend neutral sentences, repeat tokens, truncate at common tokenization boundaries to simulate windowing.n3. shot/anchor perturbationsn - insert or remove few-shot examples, scramble example order, or substitute placeholders with semantically-similar distractors.n4. numeric and unit transformationsn - convert units, change date formats, replace numbers with words, shift magnitude (e.g., 1,000 1000).n5. adversarial paraphrasing (semantic-preserving)n - use templated paraphrasers with controlled diversity (e.g., back-translation only when quality score gt 0.85).n6. kv-cache and incremental decoding simulationn - re-run prompt with parts of previously generated tokens pre-filled into cache to surface cache-boundary bugs.n7. mixed-mode quantization togglesn - simulate int8/int4 artifacts on candidate models using fast emulator or sliced inference harness to reveal quantization-specific failures.nnautomated pipeline (high level):n1) seed selection: accept seed failures from bug tracker, field telemetry, or offline evals. seeds must include failing_response, expected_response, trace_id, and context snapshot.n2) mutation generation: apply amplification strategies producing labeled variants and collect provenance.n3) filtering scoring: run lightweight filters (toxicity, token-length bounds, trivial duplicates). score variants according to novelty (embedding distance from seed), syntactic variance, and model sensitivity (probe with a fast model).n4) prioritization: select top-k for full-run depending on test budget and desired coverage.n5) full-run evaluation: execute amplified bundle across target matrix (model versions, quant profiles, serving configs). capture metrics: rsi, safety_class, topk_intent_changes, latency, token_count.n6) triage and triage metadata: generate triage deck with failing examples grouped by failure taxonomy and suggested root causes (quantization, prompt-windowing, prompt-template mismatch).nnrunbook: amplify-to-triage step-by-stepn1. create a ticket in the regression board with seed examples and desired open a regression triage session, attach the generated triage deck, and assign owners.n6. for high-severity safety flips: immediately block promotion and notify security/policy via the escalation pre-filter expected unsafe variants unless the seed is unsafe.n- budget allocation: 50 orthographic/context, 25 paraphrase, 25 cache/quant tests by default. adjust per workload.nnintegration points with existing systems:n- eval harness: amplified bundles are a first-class artifact. use the eval-harness runner with --amplified flag and provide matrix yaml.n- model onboarding: require amplified-bundle smoke tests before promotion to staging. add an entry to the model promotion checklist: amplified test run (k500) with zero critical safety flips.n- quality guardrails: wire amplified failure counts into the response-stability-index dashboard and create an alert when growth rate gt 2x/week.n- quantization profiles: add a per-profile amplification pass to detect quant-specific content: summarynnthis document defines a prioritization and budgeting framework for running slice-driven evaluations in redwoods eval harness. it describes a deterministic scoring function for slice prioritization, recommended resource budgets for common evaluation classes (smoke, micro-canary, full-slice, long-tail scan), integration points with quantization profiles and onboarding, and a triage fast-path for regression detection and mitigation.nnwhy this existsnn- eval budgets are finite: the eval harness runs thousands of slices across many models and releases. uncontrolled execution causes high cost and slow feedback.n- we need consistent signal for promotion and regression triage while minimizing gpu/cpu spend.n- quantization changes and heterogeneous deployments (private/dedicated) require different resource profiles this doc standardizes budgeting and prioritization so teams follow predictable least-cost-first patterns.nnscopenn- applies to all automated and scheduled evaluation jobs executed via the eval harness (interactive, scheduled, and triggered by model promotion pipelines).n- does not cover human labeling budgets or external a/b experiments (separate playbooks exist).nndefinitionsnn- slice: atomic workload segment (e.g., subset of prompts with a common characteristic).n- eval class: smoke, micro-canary, full-slice, long-tail scan.n- cost unit: gpu-hour equivalent at redwood internal rate (example: 1 a100-80gb hour 1.0 cost unit 1 t4/8gb hour 0.08 cost units).n- priority window: timeframe within which a slice should be executed relative to model event (e.g., within 2 hours for micro-canary).nnpriority scoring algorithm (deterministic)nnwe compute a score s for each slice to decide execution order when demand exceeds capacity. higher s runs first.nnformula: s w_i i w_r r w_m m w_c (1 / (1 c))nnwhere:n- i (impact) in 0,1: business/feature impact heuristic (0 low, 1 high). set by owning team in slice metadata.n- r (regression-signal) in 0,1: recent historical alert density for this slice (0 none, 1 frequent).n- m (model-change): binary 1 if model architecture/quantization variant changed since last passing run, else 0.n- c (cost-estimate): predicted cost in cost units for full slice run.n- w_i, w_r, w_m, w_c weights default 0.45, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10. weights are tunable via eval-harness config.nnscore interpretation:n- s 0.7: high priority (run immediately consider parallelization).n- 0.4 0 eval cost estimator 0.10 normalized to cost units inverted in score to prefer low-cost slices nnresource budgeting (default budgets)nnthese are guidance values. teams may request overrides for high-value flows override requests go to eng-applied-ml with cost justification. budget values assume redwood internal cost unit convert per-region via pricing table in runbook.nn eval class target wall-clock max concurrent workers max gpu-hours per run example use-cases n------:---:---:---:n smoke 5m 1 0.02 pre-commit/quick sanity checks n micro-canary 30m 2 0.6 canary of new model variant on top 10 slices n full-slice 2-6h 10 8.0 promotion gating for model families n long-tail scan 24h 4 24.0 rare-case stress and drift detection nnbudget enforcement rulesnn1. each eval job must declare eval_class and estimator.cost_units in job yaml. the scheduler will reject jobs exceeding per-team daily caps.n2. peak concurrency throttles: when global cost consumption in last 1 hour 80 of pool capacity, only high-priority (s 0.7) slices are scheduled until consumption drops below 60.n3. quantized runs count as a separate cost bucket and may require additional shadow runs treat them as model-change (m1) for initial prioritization.nnyaml: minimal eval job examplenn---n eval-job.yamlnjob_name: email-intent-full-sliceneval_class: full-slicenowner: nlp-teamnpriority_metadata:n impact: 0.8n model_change: truenestimator:n cost_units: 7.5n gpu_type: a100-80gbn expected_wall_minutes: 240n---nnscheduling procedure (step-by-step)nn1. when a model-promotion event occurs, the promotion orchestration writes a scheduling request for the required slices. include eval_class, owner, and priority_metadata.n2. the eval-scheduler computes s for each slice and places slices into priority queues.n3. the scheduler enforces daily budget caps per team if cap exceeded, scheduler downgrades non-critical slices with an annotation and notifies owners.n4. for micro-canaries, the scheduler ensures runs complete within the priority window (default 2 hours). if a micro-canary fails (see acceptance thresholds below), the pipeline pauses and triggers the regression triage fast-path.nnacceptance thresholds and sample sizesnn- smoke: qualitative checks failure on runtime error or 5 invalid responses.n- micro-canary: run n100 samples acceptance if metric delta baseline - epsilon.n- full-slice: sample size determined by slice variance profiling baseline formula: n min(5000, ceil( (z2 sigma2) / d2 )), where z1.96 (95 ci), sigma is observed stddev from historical runs, d is acceptable absolute difference. default n1000 if no history.nnintegration with quantization profiles and model onboardingnn- onboarding pipelines must tag any change to quant_profile_id. that tag sets model_changem for the first subsequent eval run and prioritizes slices accordingly.n- for quantization-induced runs, run two lanes in parallel (float baseline shadow quantized variant) for the micro-canary. cost estimation should account for both lanes.nnregression triage fast-pathnnwhen a micro-canary or full-slice run exceeds failure thresholds, the following fast-path is executed:nn1. pause promotion and mark model as blocked.n2. snapshot telemetry and store a prioritized subset: top 100 failed prompts, token-level traces, kv-cache rollback events, and runtimes.n3. run automated bisect across variants: kernel selection, quant profile, model weights (if multi-version) limit to 3 parallel bisect branches.n4. if bisect isolates a single cause with confidence 90 (see bisect spec), auto-open a regression incident with severity determined by impacted slos.n5. if cause not isolated within 60 minutes, run fallback: promote earlier verified model variant and schedule detailed offline triage with ml owners.nntelemetry and observability requirementsnneval runs must emit the following fields at 1-minute granularity:n- eval_job_id, slice_id, model_version, quant_profile_id, worker_id, gpu_type, tokens_generated, latency_p50/p95/p99, error_count, failed_prompts_count, metric_values (primary/secondary), cost_units_consumed.nndashboard and alertsnn- a dedicated dashboard eval cost priority lists active jobs, s scores, and cost burn rate.n- alert: when per-team cost consumption 90 of daily cap - page on-call for that team.n- alert: micro-canary failure - slack model-promotions and create incident-tmp channel via api.nngovernance and ownershipnn- owning team: declares impact and maintains slice metadata responsible for justifying budget overrides.n- platform: eng-applied-ml operates scheduler, maintains cost model, and reviews monthly budget exceptions.n- sre: enforces pool concurrency caps and adjusts rate-limiting during global incidents.nnoperational runbook (quick actions)nn- if a slice is consuming unexpected cost (2x estimate):n 1. cancel active job via evalctl: evalctl cancel .n 2. inspect estimator outputs: evalctl inspect --fields estimator..n 3. if estimator was stale, file a ticket to eng-applied-ml with the job snapshot.nn- triaging a micro-canary regression:n 1. lock promotion and run automated bisect: evalctl bisect --job --variants quant,kernel,weightsn 2. if bisect identifies variant: rollback quant profile via model-registry ui and rerun micro-canary.nnexample cli commandsnn schedule a micro-canarynevalctl schedule --job-file eval-job.yaml --priority nown cancel a running jobnevalctl cancel --job-id 2026-ab12n fetch diagnostics for a completed runnevalctl fetch --job-id 2026-ab12 --artifact traces/.jsonnnsecurity and cost accountingnn- all eval artifacts containing customer prompt examples must be labeled pii/tos compliant at creation. the scheduler will reject runs labeled customer-sensitive unless confidentiality override is granted.n- cost attribution is exported daily to finance with the following dimensions: team, owner, model_family, quant_profile_id, region.nnchange lognn- 2026-02-12 (ava chen): initial publish.n- 2026-03-01 (ava chen): weight defaults tuned from internal pilot added triage active.nnprecision budget manifest (recommended schema)nthe manifest is a small yaml saved alongside model artifacts and eval reports. the manifest must be generated during the onboarding pipeline and summarynnthis document defines the specification for the evaluator cli (evalctl) and the sidecar plugin contract used by redwoods eval harness. it formalizes command semantics, plugin manifest fields, telemetry expectations, failure modes, and rollout guidance for both hosted and private (dedicated/vpc) evaluator deployments. the goal is to enable consistent, auditable, and pluggable evaluators across teams and tenants while minimizing operational surprises during onboarding and mixed-precision/quant shadowing.nngoalsn- provide a single, stable cli for running local, ci, and on-host evaluations.n- define a minimal sidecar plugin api so third-party or customer-supplied evaluators can integrate with our shadow mesh.n- surface required telemetry and artifact outputs for traceability, reproducibility, and automatic triage.n- specify failure semantics and a safe rollback/stop mechanism for high-risk eval sweeps.nnscope and non-goalsn- scope: token-level and prompt-level evaluators, synthetic probe runners, function-call validators, and compact shadow probes.n- non-goals: ui/console integrations (visualization details live in product docs) and heavy-weight dataset catalog formats (these remain in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).nnterminologyn- evalctl: the evaluator command-line tool consumed by ci, local dev, and on-host runners.n- sidecar plugin: an executable or http service that implements the plugin contract to run evaluator workloads in a given environment.n- probe: a single test case or input used by an evaluator.nncontract overviewn- protocols supported: stdin/stdout json lines http/json rest (v1) and grpc proto v1.n- manifests: plugins must provide a plugin manifest file (yaml) describing capabilities, resource hints, and artifact outputs.n- outputs: all evaluators must emit a standardized results envelope and an artifacts index.nnevaluator cli (evalctl)n- primary commands and semantics:n 1. evalctl init --manifest : validates a plugin manifest and performs a dry-run capability test. exit codes: 0ok, 2validation error, 3permission/fatal.n 2. evalctl run --manifest --workdir --slice --mode localcishadow --concurrency n --telemetry-level minimalstandardverbosen 3. evalctl collect --workdir --artifact-index out/index.json --output n 4. evalctl stop --run-id --graceful/--forcenn- example usage:n evalctl run --manifest ./plugin.yaml --workdir /tmp/eval-123 --mode shadow --concurrency 4n evalctl collect --workdir /tmp/eval-123 --artifact-index out/index.json --output semver used for promotion gating. new minor versions require in_review and a rollout plan.n- protocols: enumerates supported ipc forms. plugins must support at least one protocol.n- capabilities: free-form tags that the eval mesh uses for routing (e.g., functioncall-validation, kv-cache-sensitive, quant-aware).n- resource_hints: best-effort hints used by the orchestrator for capacity decisions.n- outputs: relative file paths in the workdir that the plugin must produce. see outputs and artifact index below.nnsidecar plugin api (http json v1)n- endpoints and expected payloads:n get /healthz - 200 status:ok,version:0.3.1n post /run - 202 accepts a runspec json, returns run_id:uuid-v4,eta_seconds: intn post /stop - 200 accepts run_id: ... , signal: gracefulforcen get results): considered severity p1 for shadow runs. automated triage will escalate to eval-oncall when the results rate 99.5 successful runs on representative slices during a 72-hour shadow window.n- metric selection heuristics and a compact, explainable slice signature format for describing and tracking behavioral slices used across our eval harness. the goal is to make metric choices auditable, stabilize alerting, and speed regression triage by attaching human-readable signatures and automated fingerprints to each slice used in continuous and shadow evals.nnintended audiencen- applied ml engineersn- evaluators and data scientistsn- sres and oncall reviewers handling model regressionsnnmotivationn- many regressions are surfaced by noisy metrics or improperly scoped slices. we need a lightweight, reproducible contract that encodes what a slice measures, why the metric matters for product quality, and how to interpret alerts.n- slice signatures make it quicker to determine whether a signal is a data/telemetry problem, a model-level behavioral change, or an infrastructural artifact (e.g., quantization/kv cache interaction).nnscopen- applies to: shadow and continuous eval pipelines, canary validations, and longtail probe runs.n- not covered here: complete annotation processes (see probe annotation charters) or privacy-preserving aggregation techniques (see privacy-first-shadow-eval).nnkey conceptsn- slice: a targeted subset of traffic or synthetic probes defined by input predicates (e.g., contains code block, non-english answer request, multi-turn 5 steps).n- signature: a short, human-readable descriptor machine-friendly fingerprint that encodes the slice predicate, primary metric, baseline window, and guardrail tolerances.n- explainability payload: text describing the rationale and expected failure modes for the slice used by triage playbooks and alerting.nnslice signature format (compact)neach slice signature is a single-line descriptor and a 16-character fingerprint (sha-1 truncated) emitted into telemetry. example format: nn nnexample: n code-block-clarity rouge-l@avg 14d -5/8 3f1b8c7a2d9e5f1annthe explainability payload stored in eval metadata (long text) includes: human rationale, common false positives, recommended mitigating probes, and ownership.nnmetric selection heuristicsn1) start with alignment to user-visible outcomes. prefer metrics that map to product kpis (e.g., exact match for code synthesis snippets, rouge-l for summarization fidelity, embedding cosine for retrieval relevance).n2) match metric family to slice behavior. use n-gram/overlap metrics for surface fidelity, token-level perplexity for fluency-related slices, and embedding distances for semantic drift checks.n3) prefer robust statistics for noisy slices: median or trimmed-mean over arithmetic mean report interquartile range (iqr) and 95 bootstrap ci.n4) use delta-based thresholds anchored to a baseline window (14 days default). always include both relative and absolute deltas in alerts.n5) composite metrics: for complex slices combine primary metric quality guardrail. example: retrieval-safety (embedding-sim 0.78) and (toxicity-score 0.05), trigger immediate pager routing.n- noise filters: ignore changes explained by traffic composition shift 20 for core demographic slices unless accompanied by metric degradation within the subgroup.nnsignature examples and table (text representation)n short-id predicate (human) primary metric baseline tolerance sample size min owner n code-block-clarity input contains fenced code blocks or triple backticks rouge-l@avg 14d -5/8 2k probes applied-ml-evals n short-chat-context 3-turn multi-turn conversational prompts coherencescore@median 30d -7/7 5k sessions chat-eval-team n retrieval-qa-fact user asks factoid with linked doc url embsim@mean 14d -4/6 1k probe-doc pairs rtr-team nnhow to construct a useful slice signature (step-by-step)n1) define the user-visible failure youre trying to detect (1 sentence).n2) pick the smallest predicate that isolates the behavior prefer syntactic predicates (tokens, tags) over semantic heuristics when possible.n3) select a primary metric per heuristics above and a secondary guardrail metric.n4) decide on baseline window and minimum sample size for stable ci.n5) draft the explainability payload (who, why, false positives, known mitigations).n6) publish signature to eval registry and link to product/sli docs.nnexample explainability payload (text)nrationale: fenced code block answers require higher token exactness rouge-l correlates with executable snippet fidelity for our code-completion customers.ncommon false positives: code formatting changes only (whitespace/clang-format) mark as surface-only if uast parsing indicates identical ast.nmitigations: add ast-normalization probe, include canonicalization step in annotation pipeline.nowner: applied-ml-evals / sofia patelnntelemetry baseline_window, sample_count, quant_mode (int8/float16/none), cache_hit_rate.n- recommended sampling cadence: daily aggregates for high-volume slices, hourly for slo-critical slices.n- retention: source_type: confluence, title: anchor primer compact benchmark and production probe suite, content: overviewnnthis page describes the anchor primer compact benchmark (apcb): a small, production-focused probe suite designed to measure and track priming/anchoring robustness across model variants, quantization profiles, and kv-cache behaviors. apcb is intended as a low-cost continuous probe that can run in shadow and canary lanes of the eval harness to catch early regressions in few-shot priming fidelity and primer decay across contexts.nnpurpose and goalsnn- provide a repeatable, small-footprint benchmark (50200 probes) suitable for continuous runs.n- measure anchor retention (how long a primer continues to influence outputs) and primer-channel isolation (whether the primer leaks into unrelated generations).n- surface interactions between priming, quantization, and kv-cache reuse that could cause semantic drift or hallucination.n- produce actionable signals with clear triage steps and remediation recommendations.nnscopenn- applied to text-only and single-turn few-shot prompts (15 examples). not a multimodal benchmark.n- runs against: hosted model variants, dedicated instances (representative instance types), and quantized shadow artifacts.n- intended for both offline eval harness scheduling and lightweight in-production shadow sampling.nndesign principlesnn1. compact: keep the probe set small (100 probes) while covering key failure modes.n2. anchored: each probe explicitly includes an anchor section (highly directive text) and a neutral test segment to check anchor spill.n3. diversity: include multiple prompt styles (instruction, qa, roleplay, function-call templates).n4. deterministic scoring when possible: use token-level and semantic similarity metrics plus human-calibrated thresholds.nnprobe taxonomynn- anchor-retention probes: measure how many tokens/turns the primer continues to influence when context length increases.n- anchor-leak probes: detect primer words or intent appearing in unrelated outputs.n- function-call anchoring probes: check parameter name/value adherence after priming.n- stochasticity probes: measure variance across seeds and streaming starts.nnprobe synthesis and datasetnn1. seed corpus: 250 canonical seeds derived from real workloads (support, search snippets, chat intents). seeds are anonymized and stripped of pii.n2. primer types: directive (always answer in bullet points), persona (you are a helpful historian), safety (do not provide legal advice), and structural (function call scaffolding).n3. for each seed, generate 34 probe variants combining primer type and prompt style.nnsampling rulesnn- shuffle probes per run and cap to n100 per continuous run.n- include deterministic random seed for reproducibility in the eval harness.n- run both cold-start (no kv cache) and warm-start (kv cache primed with a short history) variants.nnmetrics and scoringnnprimary metrics (numeric):n- anchor retention index (ari): fraction of probes where the primary anchored instruction persists at specified context offsets (0, 50, 200 tokens). values 0.01.0.n- anchor leakage rate (alr): percent of probes where anchor tokens or anchor intent appear in a mismatched output segment.n- function-call fidelity (fcf): percent of function-call probes that return the correct parameter structure and canonical values.n- seed variance (sv): standard deviation of ari across 5 seeds (captures stochastic instability).nnauxiliary signals (diagnostic):n- token overlap counts between anchor and output.n- edit distance to expected canonical answer.n- embedding cosine similarity to anchored answer (for semantic retention).nnacceptance thresholds (example table)nn metric acceptable warning fail n------:---:---:n ari (0 token offset) 0.92 0.800.91 0.78 0.650.77 0.10 n fcf 0.95 0.850.94 0.08 nnnote: thresholds should be tuned per-model family and per-quantization profile. use this table as a starting guardrail rather than absolutes.nnintegration with eval harness and cinn- harness job: a lightweight job runner named apcb-compact-runner. it supports parallelism8 and artifacts exported as json l2 summaries.n- schedule: run every 4 hours in shadow for high-traffic models nightly for low-traffic.n- ci gate: failing the fail thresholds for two consecutive runs triggers a blocking ticket and auto-notification to model-onboarding and serving-runtime on-call.nncli example (eval harness adapter)nn run apcb against a model variantnapcb-runner --model redwood-gptx-1b-qa --profiles cold,warm --seed 42 --limit 100 --output s3://apcb/artifacts/run_id.jsonnnsample eval job yaml (for harness scheduler):nnjob_name: apcb-compact-nightlynschedule: nightlynparallelism: 8nprofile: cold, warmnseeds: 42,43,44nlimit: 100nnotify_on: warning, failnnartifact schema (short):n- run_idn- model_variantn- profilen- probe_idn- metrics: ari, alr, fcf, svn- raw_output_textn- tokens_for_anchornn(artifacts must remain json lines compliant for downstream triage tools.)nntriage flow and remediation playbooknn1. automated triage: the harness computes delta against baseline (previous stable variant).n2. if fail thresholds hit: open regression ticket with tags apcb, regression, model:. attach full run artifact and delta summary.n3. quick manual checks (owner: model-onboarding):n - re-run failing probes with 5 different seeds and both cold/warm profiles.n - compare against unquantized reference to isolate quantization impact.n - inspect tokenization differences (special tokens, subword splits).n4. escalation matrix:n - if isolated to quant profile - engage quant team and apply rollback to previous quant profile.n - if isolated to kv cache behavior - route to serving-runtime with run_id and capture trace.n - if model variant-regression across all profiles - open rollback and coordinate release blocking.nnremediation suggestions (common fixes)nn- primer rewrite / anchoring strengthening: add explicit delimiting tokens or anchor markers to primers.n- quant fallback: temporarily route production traffic to unquantized or higher-precision variant for affected route.n- kv-cache priming hygiene: truncate reused context and inject anchor sentinel tokens at start of primed sections.n-
