source_type: confluence, title: compact prompt synthesis and latency-aware eval playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook documents the compact prompt synthesis workflow and a latency-aware evaluation protocol designed for production inference pipelines (hosted, dedicated, and private). the goal is to produce a reproducible, measurable process that reduces token budgets while preserving semantic fidelity and meeting latency slos across quantized and cached runtime variants.nnwho should use this docn- evaluation engineers running large-scale latency/fidelity sweeps.n- model-onboarding teams preparing prompts for quantized or on-device deployments.n- platform owners validating rollouts where token budgets map directly to cost.nngoals and success criterian- reduce prompt token counts by 2050 on high-volume templates without 2 drop in targeted downstream accuracy metrics (intent classification, exact-match, bleu/rouge where applicable).n- maintain 95th-percentile latency within configured slo when using compacted prompts under production batching and kv cache priming.n- provide an automated eval harness stage that flags regressions by prompt family and quantization variant.nnscope and non-goalsn- scope: multi-turn templates, function-call priming, and instruction-style prompts used by core product flows. includes integration guidance for kv cache-primed sessions and quantized model variants.n- non-goals: ad-hoc user messages (free text from end users) and manual prompt-writing guidelines for ux copy.nndefinitionsn- compact prompt: a syntactically and semantically equivalent prompt reduced in token length by applying deterministic transformations (slot squeezing, canonicalization, named anchors, and stop-word compression) while preserving model-facing signal.n- fidelity budget: allowable delta on one or more eval metrics (e.g., intent-f1, function-call correctness) used to accept compact prompts.n- latency-aware eval: an evaluation pass that measures prompt impact under realistic batching, kv cache hit rates, and mixed-precision / quantized kernels.nnhigh-level workflown1. prompt family identification and baseline collectionn - assemble representative prompt set: 5002,000 samples per family, stratified by context length and tenant.n - record baseline metrics: mean tokens, 50/95/99 latency (end-to-end), downstream quality metrics relevant to the product (intent, slot-fill f1, code execution accuracy, etc.).nn2. candidate compact synthesisn - run deterministic transformations in the order below to produce candidate variants:n a) slot collapsing: convert verbose slot descriptions to short canonical keys (e.g., user location - loc).n b) anchor compression: replace repeated instructional anchors with single token markers and reference mapping.n c) stopword trimming in protected contexts: only when paraphrase-preserving heuristics score 0.9.n d) template reflow: re-order clauses to reduce overlap and repeated context tokens.n - each step must output a provenance tag appended as a json comment (see examples).nn3. latency-aware evaluation (automated harness)n - run for each candidate variant across runtime matrix: full-precision float16 fp16, int8/4 quantized variants, and mixed-kernel fallbacks.n - emulate production kv cache states: cold, warm (50 hit), and hot (95 hit) by pre-injecting priming requests.n - measure latency under production batching distributions (use real traffic histogram or synthetic distribution).nn4. decisioning and rolloutn - apply fidelity budget checks (per-family): if downstream metric delta promote to canary.n - canary: 25 traffic with telemetry hooks that compare compact vs baseline responses for semantic drift (paired sampling).n - full rollout only if canary holds for 4872 hours and no actionable regressions detected.nnacceptance criteria (example table described)n- the harness will enforce these thresholds per prompt family (presented here as a table):n metric: intent-f1 baseline: 0.91 max delta allowed: -0.02n metric: function-call-accuracy baseline: 0.985 max delta allowed: -0.01n latency: p95 end-to-end baseline: 210ms absolute max: 250msn token savings: baseline mean tokens 58 - target 35 (40 savings)nnconfig and cli examplesn- harness invocation (example):nn rdinfer-eval --suite compact-synthesis --prompt-family user-onboarding --matrix fp16,int8_4,mixed --kv-states cold,warm,hot --batch-dist real --output ./results/user-onboarding/2025-11-07.jsonnn- example compact prompt representation (json comment style for provenance stored as newline-delimited jsonl in the asset registry):nn id:family-user-onboard-4721,variant:slot-collapseanchor-compress,provenance:slot-collapse:v1anchor:short-v2,prompt:anchor_anuser: locseattle goalsetup account prefsnonenassistant: provide a step-by-step checklist.nnbest-practice synthesis heuristicsn- preserve explicit named entities and function-call schemas (do not compress schema keys used by source_type: confluence, title: probe correlation matrix and explainability playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook documents the standard process, tooling, and interpretation guidance for computing probe correlation matrices and producing probe-level explainability artifacts. the goal is to accelerate root-cause triage for multi-probe degradations, make correlations auditable, and produce human-friendly explanations that feed into regression triage, quantization decisions, and rollout gating.nnmotivationnnwhen multiple probes or slices begin to degrade simultaneously, on-call and evaluation engineers need a systematic way to: 1) measure how probes co-vary, 2) identify probe groups likely driven by the same upstream cause, and 3) generate explainability signals (feature importances, counterfactual probes) that guide mitigation. ad-hoc correlation checks and scatterplots slow investigations and produce inconsistent conclusions. this playbook standardizes the pipeline, thresholds, and remediation handoffs.nnscopenn- applies to automated probes and hand-curated slices used in evaluation harness and continuous shadow validation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.n- focused on categorical and numeric probe outputs, classifier scores, embedding distances, and metadata dimensions (tenant, model_variant, quant_profile, kv_cache_hit).n- excludes raw model logits analysis that is covered in runtime-profiling runbooks.nnownershipnn- primary owner: evaluations applied ml (evaluation-harness team)n- secondary consumers: model-onboarding, oncall/eng-sre, product qan- pager handoff: if correlation analysis returns a causal hypothesis with confidence 0.8 (see scoring below), notify the oncall channel eval-triage and open an incident with tag probe-correlation.nnkey definitionsnn- probe: a named test or metric (e.g., fewshot-coherence-english, longcontext-kv-dropout, financial-entity-redaction).n- correlation matrix: nxn matrix reporting pairwise spearman rho, pearson r, and kendall tau between probe signals over an anchored time window (default 1h / 24h for production triage).n- explainability artifact: per-probe contribution vector (feature importance) computed by a lightweight surrogate model (tree-based shap or permutation importance) that uses telemetry and context features.nndata pipeline and inputsnn1) input windows: default windows are 1 hour (fast triage) and 24 hours (stability analysis).n2) signals ingested: probe_score, probe_count, stderr_of_score, median_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, quant_profile, model_variant, tenant_id, request_size_tokens, top_k_entropy.n3) aggregation granularity: 5m buckets higher fidelity available on request.nnstandard procedure (step-by-step)nn1. kickoffn - trigger: automated alert (multi-probe degradation or sqc breach) or manual triage request.n - command to start pipeline (ci runner):n n ./eval-tools/compute_correlation.sh --window 60m --granularity 5m --probes probea,probeb,probec --out /tmp/corr_run_(date s).tar.gznn2. data extractionn - pull probe telemetry from eval_telemetry_v2 (bigquery) using the provided sql template.n - sql snippet:n selectn bucket_start,n probe_name,n avg(probe_score) as mean_score,n sum(probe_count) as total_count,n avg(latency_ms) as mean_latency,n any_value(model_variant) as model_variantn from eval_telemetry_v2n where probe_name in (@probe_list)n and bucket_start between @start and @endn group by bucket_start, probe_namenn3. matrix computationn - for each pair of probes compute: pearson r (for normally-distributed numeric signals), spearman rho (rank correlation for ordinal signals), and kendall tau (robust rank correlation).n - also compute p-values via permutation tests (n2000). title: probe fusion, entropy stewardship, and rollforward manual, content: summarynnthis manual documents the probe fusion pattern used by the eval harness to consolidate redundant probes, manage probe entropy budgets across tenants and slices, and run safe rollforward steps when probes interact with quantization or kv-cache changes. it is intended for evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, and sres responsible for continuous evaluation and regression triage.nnwhy we created this patternnn- large-scale eval fleets accumulate overlapping probes (same logical intent, small perturbations) that increase cost and noise.n- quantization and kv-cache changes amplify signal variance naive probe deduplication can hide edge regressions.n- we need a reproducible, auditable procedure to consolidate probes while preserving statistical power for regressions and supporting safe rollforwards for mixed-precision rollouts.nnwhen to use this manualnn- when probe duplication rate 30 in a tenant or slice and eval costs rise above target.n- before a quantization rollforward or mixed-precision rollout that will change tokenization or kv cache behavior.n- during regression hunts where probe noise obscures root-cause signal.nndefinitions and key conceptsnn- probe fusion: algorithmic consolidation of similar probes into a canonical probe plus synthetic variants, reducing execution cost while retaining coverage.n- entropy budget: per-slice budget (in bits) limiting allowable perturbation diversity included in fused probes.n- hash-stability signature: short deterministic fingerprint computed from normalized promptcontext that remains stable under non-semantic formatting changes (used for deduplication).n- fidelity hedge: a small set of higher-fidelity probes executed alongside fused probes to detect fusion-induced regressions.nnownership and rolesnn- eval platform (owner): implements fusion engine, metrics, and rollout tooling.n- model onboarding (review owner): approves probe-fusion profiles for a model during promotion.n- sre / cost ops: validates budget targets and enforces throttle rules.nnprobe fusion pipeline overviewnn1. ingest and normalize: trim whitespace, canonicalize timezones, replace non-semantic tokens, and compute hash-stability signature (hss).n2. precluster by hss and metadata (tenant, language, slice).n3. compute entropy score for each precluster: sample prompts - compute response embedding variance and lexical edit distance distribution.n4. apply fusion rules: if precluster_entropy threshold, collapse into canonical probe with up to n synthetic variants.n5. add fidelity hedge probes: select a stratified subset (28 probes) across the original cluster to run un-fused for each evaluation epoch.n6. execute fused probes through eval harness and compare to hedges route anomalies to regression-triage queue.nndetails and parametersnn- default thresholds (configurable per-tenant/slice):n - redundancy threshold: 0.30 (clusters with 30 overlap eligible)n - slice_entropy_budget: 4.0 bits (default)n - max_synthetic_variants: 5n - fidelity_hedge_fraction: 0.05 (5 of original cluster)nnhash-stability signature algorithm (high-level)nn1. normalize prompt: unicode normalize, lowercase (unless slice requires case sensitivity), collapse repeated whitespace, remove punctuation tokens marked as non-semantic.n2. canonicalize examples (replace entity tokens with type markers if present).n3. compute sha256 over normalized string, return first 12 hex chars as hss.nnentropy scoring (procedural)nn1. sample up to 50 examples from precluster.n2. for each example, call a fast (cost-limited) evaluator with fixed seed and collect top-1 token distribution and 128-d embedding.n3. compute: response diversity average pairwise cosine(embeddings) lexical variance average normalized levenshtein distance across outputs.n4. final entropy score weighted(sum) of normalized measures. weights: response_diversity 0.7, lexical_variance 0.3.nnoperational runbook: fuse-and-observe (for a single tenant-slice)nn1. pre-checks (automated):n - ensure eval-harness version 4.3.2.n - confirm current quant-profile label for model (if quant-profile changed in last 7 days, require manual approval).n2. dry-run: compute precluster hss and entropy, run simulated fusion (no execution) and surface expected cost savings and estimated coverage loss.n3. approve in ui: model-onboarding owner reviews dry-run report and chooses profile: conservative / balanced / aggressive. default: balanced.n4. execute fusion epoch: run fused probes fidelity hedges for 24 hours.n5. compare hedges - fused outputs using the following metrics (see metrics section).n6. if any metric breach: escalate to regression-triage and revert fused probes to shadow mode (fused recorded but only hedges count toward alerts) until root cause resolved.nnmetrics and alertingnn- probe-level stability slo: hamming-stability 0.95 over 24h for canonical probes (definition: fraction of hedges that match fused canonical output within allowed edit distance for the slice).n- embedding drift delta: average cosine change between hedges and fused , hss: a1b2c3d4e5f6, variants: , , metadata: slice: intent-refactor, language: ennnnote: the above snippet is illustrative the true manifest lives in the eval-asset-registry and is signed by the eval platform service account.nnquantization interactions and safety guardsnn- when a quantization-profile change is in scope, the fusion engine must:n 1) pin a rollback shadow of pre-fusion canonical probes (persist hss-response mapping).n 2) increase fidelity_hedge_fraction to 10 for the first two epochs.n 3) run targeted adversarial priming probes (10 of hedges) designed to stress tokenization and kv expiry paths.n 4) if embedding_drift_delta crosses critical: automatically open regression incident and block rollout.nnregression triage integrationnn- if hedges indicate a breach, create a triage ticket using template: regression-fusion-alert. required fields: model, epoch_id, hss sample, hedges vs fused diffs, embedding snapshots, last quant-profile version, recent infra changes.n- triage steps (short list):n 1. reproduce with hedges only in isolated staging.n 2. run ab test: fused vs unfused with matched traffic for 1000 samples.n 3. if regression confirmed and pinpoints to fusion heuristic: mark fusion rule as disallowed for that slice and schedule a rule update.n 4. if regression correlates with quantization: trigger quant rollback.nnrollforward decision matrix (high-level)nn- preconditions for rollforward: 3 consecutive epochs with warning-level deviations or 2 epochs with non-actionable anomalies plus manual review.n- emergency rollback: single critical threshold breach - immediate block and rollback to pre-fusion shadow.nndata retention and provenancenn- keep canonical probe manifests, hss mappings, and fidelity hedge outputs for 90 days by default.n- all fusion decisions must be recorded in the eval-asset-registry with: who approved, profile used, dry-run report id, and cost delta.nnappendix a: example troubleshooting checklistnn- symptom: sudden drop in hamming-stability but embedding drift small.n - check: slice tokenizer changes, locale normalization, punctuation filtering rules.n - action: temporarily disable canonicalization predicates that remove punctuation.nn- symptom: high false-suppression rate after quant rollout.n - check: seed determinism, fast-evaluator version mismatch, kv-cache warmup differences.n - action: increase fidelity hedges and run targeted primality probes for kv-cache behavior.nnappendix b: implementation notes for engineersnn- fusion engine should be a sidecar to the evaluator with the following apis: compute_hss(normalized_prompt) - hss, score_entropy(precluster_id) - float, propose_fusion(profile) - manifest. all api calls must be idempotent.n- lightweight local simulator must exist that can replay fused vs original probes deterministically for offline verification.nnrelated readingnn- see eval-harness operational manifest and eval-metrics playbook for metric definitions and alerting wiring.n- see quant-shadow-cohort strategy doc for coordinated quant rollouts.nncontributorsnn- primary author: maya chen (eval platform)n- reviewers: arjun patel (model onboarding), lucia gomez (applied safety)nnchange lognn- 2025-09-15: initial draft and prototype fusion rules.n- 2026-02-03: added quant-safety section and hardened fidelity hedge mean-time-to-resolution (mttr) for regressions by standardizing triage signals and escalation steps.nnscopenthis document covers:n- probe authoring and ownership (prompt sets, priming templates).n- eval manifest and artifact registry.n- deployment gating: shadow - canary - staged rollout.n- quantization compatibility tests and hedging policies.n- telemetry, alerting, and regression triage runbook.nnprinciplesn1. treat evaluation assets like code: immutable artifacts (sha), changelogs, and owners.n2. keep cost transparency: every scheduled eval run must include a cost estimate and chargeback tag.n3. fail open for safety-critical checks (safety sentinels), but fail closed for fidelity gates tied to production slos.n4. for quantized deployments, require a declared quant-hedge 0.5)n- global budget: max 3 of total qps can be shadowed into any single eval-cluster to avoid resource interference.n- adaptive throttle: sample rates are dynamically lowered if the eval-cluster and fallback policies, content: summary:nthis document describes the evaluation protocol used to measure and qualify model variants and serving configurations for latency-sensitive workloads. the goal is to produce an operational signal that directly informs traffic routing and automatic fallback policies in redwoods smart routing layer. it covers metric definitions, workload synthesis, test harness configuration, pass/fail thresholds, and an incident triage runbook for latency regressions.nnbackground and motivation:n- many customer-facing features require a sub-100ms median response time or predictable tail latency to maintain ux.n- model choices (size, quantization), runtime kernel selection, kv-cache hit patterns, and batching behavior all interact to create latency regressions that are invisible to token-count-only evaluations.n- automated routing and fallback should be driven by a reproducible eval signal that closely mimics production request characteristics.nnscope:n- applies to: model variants intended for low-latency endpoints (chat-completion, single-turn generation with short context), runtime tunables that affect single-request latency (batching, prefetch, kernel/path selection), and routing/fallback policy parameters.n- excludes: large-batch throughput-only benchmarks, long-context ( 8k) full-document generation stress tests (covered by separate bench).nnkey definitions and metrics:n1) per-request p95 latency: end-to-end time from api ingress to first-byte-of-response (ms).n2) cold-start latency: latency when no warm worker has the model loaded or kv cache is empty (ms).n3) steady-state latency: median and p95 after warmup period (ms).n4) amplification factor (af): ratio of p95 under production-mixed traffic to p95 under synthetic single-client baseline. used to quantify sensitivity to interleaving workloads.n5) slo delta: change in slo attainment compared to baseline model/config (percentage points).nnminimum slos used by this protocol:n- target median (50th): 1.5 triggers investigation 2.0 blocks rollout.nntest corpus and traffic profiles:n- primary prompt set: 1k anonymized short-turn prompts sampled from production (max tokens: 64). prompts are stratified by client product, region, and token distribution.n- adversarial prompt subset: 200 prompts with long-token prefixes, syntactic noise, and content that stresses decoding loops.n- synthetic client mix: a multi-client interleaving generator with 50 concurrent virtual clients, configurable think-time distribution (exponential mean 200ms).n- background noise profile: 10 of requests are long-context ( 2048 tokens) to simulate multi-tenant interference.nnharness configuration (example yaml):n---nharness: latency-sensitivity-v1nclients: 50nthink_time_ms_mean: 200nprompt_set: s3://redwood-evals/latency/short-chat-1k-v2.jsonnmodel_variant: rwinf-7b-q8nbatch_policy: continuousnkv_cache_mode: enablednwarmup_requests: 500nmeasurement_window_sec: 600ncollect: p50, p90, p95, p99, mean, throughput, cpu, gpu_util, memoryn---nnexecution steps (numbered procedure):n1. provision test cluster matching the target deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private). use the infra profile documented in /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/test-cluster-profiles.n2. pre-load models and warm kv caches using warmup_requests. confirm worker processes are up and the model is resident in gpu memory.n3. start the synthetic client generator with the primary prompt set and background noise profile.n4. run for measurement_window_sec (recommended 10 minutes for small variants, up to 30 minutes for larger configs).n5. aggregate metrics and compute af relative to baseline. baseline is the currently promoted modelconfig for the route.n6. if metrics cross thresholds defined under pass/fail criteria, mark the run as failed and trigger the triage workflow.nnpass/fail criteria and gating rules:n- hard fail: p95 200ms or af 2.0 or cold-start 600ms.n- soft fail (requires engineering review): p95 between 180-200ms or af between 1.5-2.0 or median degradation 10.n- canary gating: for canary rollouts, combine this harness signal with production real-user telemetry for 1 hour before advancing traffic if any soft-fail metrics present.nnhow latency signals map to routing and fallback policies:n- if hard fail: route traffic away from the model variant immediately (automatic rollback) and mark variant unhealthy in the routing registry.n- if soft fail: reduce traffic to variant by 50 and add a retry fallback (fast-path to baseline variant) for requests with strict latency budget.n- if af indicates susceptibility to multi-tenant interference: set conservative batching knobs and enable per-customer qos isolation in dedicated deployments.nnquantization and kernel interaction notes:n- always run the harness for both float and quantized builds. quantization may improve median latency but can worsen p95 due to kernel path mismatches.n- record kernel selection logs (kernel_id, torch/llvm path) and include in eval artifact. use the profiling-playbook to map slow paths back to kernel candidates.nnartifact and reporting requirements:n- each run must produce a single artifact tarball with: harness-config.yaml, raw-metrics.jsonl, aggregated-summary.csv, kernel-selection.log, and reproducer-script.sh. upload to s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/latency//.n- create a confluence run summary page using the template in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/run-summary-template. required fields: run-id, cluster-profile, model-variant, pass/fail, owner, link to artifacts.nnincident triage runbook (when a promoted variant shows a latency regression in prod):n1. immediate mitigation (first 5 minutes): increase routing weight to baseline model if autos-rollback is enabled, the router will reduce traffic automatically. notify on-call via slack channel prod-latency.n2. collect traces: enable request tracing for affected route and collect first-byte timing, kernel selection trace, and kv-cache hit logs for a 5-minute window.n3. re-run harness with identical cluster profile and collect af. if af reproduces: escalate to serving-runtime oncall.n4. if af does not reproduce: capture production request samples (privacy-preserving sampling redact pii) and run through the harness with identical concurrency/think-time distribution.n5. postmortem: owner creates a postmortem page including root cause hypothesis, timeline, and remediation (config change, kernel patch, model rollback). link to regression triage playbook and schedule a follow-up regression test after remediation is applied.nnownership and responsibilities:n- eval owner: applied ml evaluations team replay orchestrator (qro): an eval-harness component used to replay production or synthetic traffic against quantized model variants in a controlled, auditable manner. the qro is intended for: deployments.n- run triggers (choose one or more):n 1. before promoting a quantized build to staging/dedicated pools.n 2. after kernel or runtime changes that affect attention/kv cache.n 3. on regression alerts flagged by continuous evals or field reports.n 4. weekly longtail scans on a stratified subset of traffic.nnarchitecture (text diagram):n- components:n - ingress: replay-worker fleet (containerized) that pulls traces from replay store.n - replay store: s3-backed event store with schema-ed traces (request metadata, tokenization, deterministic rng seed).n - controller: qro-controller (orchestrates batches, model mapping, quant profiles).n - normalizer: request normalizer that ensures identical tokenization and prefix padding between baseline and variant.n - metrics collector: emits qa metrics to /internal/metric/v1 and detailed artifact storage to replay store (per-example diff blobs).n - comparator: post-process job that computes deltas and significance tests.nnoperational slos and targets:n- correctness: replay determinism 99.95 (same tokenized input and rng seed produces matching deterministic non-deterministic ops when configured).n- coverage: scheduled scan should process 95 of target trace sample within target window (default 24h for weekly scans).n- latency: single-example replay time not an slo (batch throughput target: 300 examples/s doc_id: dsid_9dea02f226d74983a3b58c0c9d85cd60, source_type: confluence, title: synthetic seed generation and resampling protocol for eval stability, content: overviewnnthis document specifies redwoods canonical protocol for generating synthetic seeds used by eval harnesses and for performing repeatable resampling during stress, stability, and regression tests. the goal is to reduce nondeterministic noise in eval results while preserving representative diversity across workloads and model variants. this protocol is intended for all eval-related automation (ci evals, nightly stress runs, private/dedicated shadowing, and benchmark suites).nnwhy we need a standardized seed/resampling protocolnn- eval instability is a major root cause of false positives in regression alerts and wasted developer time.n- synthetic seeds and resampling policies control two orthogonal factors: reproducibility (exact-repeat debugging) and statistical representativeness (variance in distributional tests).n- without standardization, teams use ad-hoc rngs and sample sizes that lead to inconsistent f-score drift, noisy a/b comparisons, and fragile quantization verification.nnscope and applicabilitynn- applies to: eval-harness pipelines, prompt-set generators, synthetic workload producers, and model-onboarding testbeds.n- out of scope: production request routing, customer data sampling (handled by data-management policies).nnkey definitionsnn- seed: a 64-bit integer used as the root for deterministic prng chains.n- deterministic run: an eval execution that, given the same seed and config, must produce byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs and stable metric computations (modulo model stochasticity when sampling is enabled).n- resample window: the policy time interval after which new synthetic seeds are introduced into continuous evals (e.g., daily, weekly).nnownership and responsibilitiesnn- eval platform (team): maintain the seed service, canonical rng libraries, and automation for resampling. owner: @eval-platform.n- applied ml / evals (team): define per-workload seed distributions, target sample sizes, and required statistical tests. owner: @applied-ml.n- model onboarding engineers: request additional deterministic seeds for debugging and certify new seed sets during model promotions.nnprotocol: seed generation and catalogingnn1) canonical rng and formatn - use the platform canonical prng: xoshiro256 initialized from a 64-bit master seed. implementations exist in redwoods eval-sdks (python and go) at git:redwood/eval-sdks (module: redwood.eval.rng).n - seed metadata record (stringified json) must include: seed_id, seed_value (decimal), created_by, created_at (iso-8601), tags (list), and checksum. example: seed_id:sd-20260214-17,seed_value:9571623412341234,created_by:eval-platform,created_at:2026-02-14t17:23:00z,tags:nl-fewshot,stress,checksum:sha256:....nn2) seed catalog servicen - all seeds must be registered in the seed-catalog (internal http api: seed-catalog.redwood.svc.cluster.local).n - seed records are immutable if a seed is revoked, mark statusdeprecated with a deprecation_reason.nn3) namespacing and tag scheman - use a three-part tag schema: workload-type (e.g., nl-classification), purpose (e.g., canary, stress), and geography/locale (optional, e.g., en-us).nn4) entropy and diversity constraintsn - for each synthetic workload generator, maintain a mapping of entropy budgets (percentiles of prompt template parameterization). the eval team must define minimum coverage constraints (e.g., template coverage 95 over canonical prompt set).nnresampling policy and cadencenn- static evals (on pr): use fixed seed sets pinned in the pr config file. re-run behavior must re-use the same seeds until the pr author updates the config.n- ci nightly/every-24h stress: rotate n seeds per workload where n depends on workload variance (see table below).n- weekly/canary pool: refresh 20 of the pool every week full pool refresh every 12 weeks or when prompt-set changes exceed a threshold.nnresampling cadence tablenn eval type pool size (min) refresh policy rationale n-------------------------------------------------------n pr/unit (deterministic) 8 pinned per pr fast short runs reproducibility prioritized n ci/nightly stress 128 rotate 8 seeds/day capture diversity limit noise per run n production shadow 512 rotate 64 seeds/day extensive coverage for real traffic emulation n long-tail detection suite 2048 stratified monthly resample find edge-case regressions nnstatistical guidance and thresholdsnn- minimum effective sample size (ess): each eval-run must compute ess for weighted metrics ess threshold, trigger triage flow.n- regression alerting: require both (a) metric delta critical_delta and (b) p-value flags. deterministic runs use the same rng chain and template parameterization, ensuring byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs.nnintegration with other eval concernsnn- quantization tests: tag seeds used for quant-eval as quant-sanity keep a small dedicated pool (min 64) that is never rotated during a quant certification run to isolate numeric instability from sampling noise.n- regression triage: link seed_id in regression tickets. the triage playbook should include steps to re-run failing workloads with the exact seed and with a nearby neighborhood of /- 10 seeds to determine whether the failure is seed-specific or systematic.n- prompt coverage: every resample must compute prompt-template coverage delta and fail if coverage falls below 90 of the canonical set.nnfailure modes and runbook pointersnn- symptom: high day-to-day metric variance without code or model changes.n - quick checks: verify seed-catalog returned the expected pool check for unintended stochastic sampling flags confirm prng library version.n - if seed drift suspected: pin to earlier seed_id and re-run. see runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook-2026nn- symptom: single-seed outliers causing regression alerts.n - triage: re-run with deterministic seed run neighborhood of seeds (/- 10) if only one seed fails, mark seed as flakey and deprecate in seed-catalog, then expand pool to maintain coverage.nnmonitoring, dashboards, and slosnn- dashboards to create:n - eval stability overview: per-workload rolling variance, ess, seed-pool utilization.n - seed health: seed success rate, flakiness per-seed_id (failures/total runs), average runtime impact.nn- slos:n - per-run ess 50 for nightly stress (target) and ess 30 (minimum).n - per-workload 7-day variance under threshold defined in workload config (default 0.03).n - seed catalog api 99.9 availability with 200ms median latency.nnrollout and updatesnn1) new seed sets must go through a staged rollout: n - stage a (canary): 5 of nightly runs for 7 days, monitor variance and coverage.n - stage b (gradual): 25 for 14 days.n - stage c (full): 100 after no significant anomalies.n2) if any monitoring alert fires during canary, rollback to previous seed pool and open an incident with applied-ml and eval-platform.nnappendix: quick checklist for model-onboarding engineersnn- request private deterministic seeds for debugging (include seed_id in pr).n- verify that quant-eval tag pool is used for numeric regressions.n- run neighborhood resamples when investigating flaky failures.n- record seed_id in the promotion ticket and note any deprecations.nnreferences and related docsnn- content: summary:nnthis page describes the probe resynthesis budget simulator (prbs): an operational tool and set of procedures used by applied ml to synthesize realistic probe sets from live telemetry, simulate evaluation budget allocation, and surface candidate probe-resynthesis strategies that minimize cost while preserving slice coverage and detection power. prbs is intended to reduce manual probe curation overhead, accelerate probe replenishment for drifting slices, and provide an auditable simulation trail for budget-driven prioritization during onboarding, shadow validation, and regression triage.nnwhy prbs exists:nn- we observe expensive manual annotation cycles when longtail prompt slices drift or when quantization/timeout changes require fresh probes.n- teams need to reason about trade-offs between probe volume, annotation cost, and detection latency for regressions.n- prbs provides deterministic simulations using historical telemetry a workload-cost model to recommend resynthesis policies.nnscope and applicability:nn- applies to: eval harness teams, model onboarding, regression triage, and the quality guardrails workflows.n- not for: production inference routing, customer-facing a/b decisions, or one-off handwritten benchmarks.nnhigh-level workflow (operator view):nn1) ingest: pull telemetry fingerprint snapshots from eval-mesh (daily/weekly cadence).n2) fingerprint synth: cluster pockets of drift and generate seed anchors using the inkling heuristic (see config table).n3) resynthesize: produce candidate probes for each slice using the selected synthesis policy (seeded paraphrase, adversarial-noise, or hybrid).n4) simulate: feed synthesized probes into the cost simulator with target annotation rates, expected annotator agreement, and quantization noise models.n5) score prioritize: output ranked actions (resynthesize x, retire y, escalate z), with estimated cost, expected recall improvement, and detection latency.n6) promote: selected probe batches are committed to the probe registry and scheduled for annotation.nnkey concepts and definitions:nn- probe: an input-record (prompt metadata) used by eval harnesses to exercise model slices.n- slice: a semantically grouped set of probes (e.g., financial-instruction, multi-turn-customer-support, low-resource-language).n- resynthesis policy: algorithmic rule used to generate new probes from seeds (paraphrase, noise-perturbation, translation-backtranslate).n- budget simulation: deterministic calculation of annotation cost and expected detection performance given probe set composition.nnoperational slos and thresholds:nn- probe coverage slo: 95 of active high-priority slices must have n_min probes (n_min depends on slice criticality see table).n- detection latency slo: median time to detect a 5 fidelity regression for high-priority slices 1200 and slice traffic defer resynthesis.n2) if detection latency expected 72h and slice is critical escalate to eval leads and request emergency annotation credit.n3) if quant_noise_factor 0.05 and slice shows coherence-sensitive tokens prefer paraphrase backtranslate hybrid (higher diversity).nnprocedure: from simulation to production promotion (numbered steps for operators):nn1. run prbs simulate with the latest snapshot.n2. review sims//summary.csv and open the top-n predicted actions.n3. validate 3 representative synthesized probes per candidate batch via the human-in-the-loop qa quickcheck (2 annotators).n4. approve or reject candidate batches in the web ui approved batches are automatically enqueued for annotation.n5. after annotation, wait for the annotation-completion webhook and run prbs reconcile --batch to update the registry and cost ledger.n6. if the annotated batch triggers a regression detection improvement mitigation: tighten seed-selection (higher similarity threshold) and increase human qa sample size to 5 per batch.n- mode: simulator underestimates annotation latency - mitigation: add per-region latency slack and tie annotation sla to live queue metrics.n- mode: excessive churn in probe registry - mitigation: apply retire-after policy for probes older than 540 days and introduce probe-stability gating.nnauditability and reproducibility:nn- every simulation run produces an audit bundle: snapshot-id, policy-id, seed-rng-seed, scoring-hash. store audit bundles in s3 and attach to regression board tickets.n- use prbs replay --audit to reproduce the exact candidate set.nnquality guardrail interactions (short):nn- prbs must be run against the same eval contracts used by quality-guardrails (fidelity thresholds, sentinel tests). candidate probe batches that reduce sentinel coverage by 5 are auto-rejected.n- if quantization profiles are in play, prbs will simulate quant_noise_factor effects and surface batches with high sensitivity for manual review.nnobservability and dashboards to monitor (owners):nn- prbs-run-rate (ops) - how frequently sims run per week.n- probe-recommendation-accept-rate (product) - percent of recommended batches approved.n- sim-vs-actual-cost-delta (finance) - monthly reconciliation metric.n- slice-detection-latency (sre) - median detection time for top-50 slices.nnownership and escalation contacts:nn- tool owner: applied ml - eval orchestration (team alias: applied-ml-eval).n- primary oncall for prbs failures: eval-harness oncall (see oncall rota).n- budget escalation: eval pmo (eval-budget@redwood.ai).nnappendix: quick triage checklist for regression incidents related to probe gaps:nn1) confirm whether the failing slice has recent prbs recommendations (search audit bundles).n2) if yes, check whether recommendations were approved/enqueued for annotation and whether annotation completed.n3) if annotation incomplete and slice is critical, escalate for emergency annotation credit and run an interim limited-synthesis with max_perturb0.05.n4) if annotation complete but detection power did not improve, open a root-cause with hypothesis: (a) seed selection bias, (b) insufficient diversity, (c) quantization collapse.nnreferences and related docs:nn- eval budget ledger: overviewnnthis document defines the persona bias probing and anchor eval framework (pbaef), an evaluation harness designed to: 1) detect persona-conditional bias and safety regressions, 2) provide stable anchor baselines for longitudinal calibration, and 3) integrate with redwoods eval orchestration for automated triage and alerting. it combines structured persona variants, targeted adversarial perturbations, and anchor-controlled scoring so that changes in model weights, quantization, or serving configuration can be attributed precisely.nngoals and scopenn- primary goals:n - surface persona-dependent failure modes (bias, toxicity, hallucination) across representative workloads.n - provide anchor baselines that remain stable across model promotions and deployments to detect relative regressions.n - integrate with regression triage playbooks to shorten mean time to detect and resolve quality regressions.n- scope:n - focused on text generation and instruction-following models used in customer-facing chat and assistant flows.n - applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments quantization-specific guardrails included.n - not intended for large-scale safety certification alone complement to safety sandbox.nndefinitionsnn- anchor prompt: a fixed stimulus (prompt context) selected to be stable, low-variance, and semantically neutral used as a baseline to detect drift.n- persona variant: systematic rewrites of a core prompt that inject persona cues (age, occupation, dialect, religion, gender presentation) while preserving informational intent.n- bias delta: relative change in a bias metric between current run and anchor baseline (reported as percent).n- calibrated score: metric value adjusted for known sampling variance using the anchor population.nndesign principlesnn1) anchoring: each report contains both (a) a set of anchor prompts and (b) the active persona-variant suite. anchors are rerun at every promotion and on nightly pipelines to control for infrastructure-induced variance.n2) orthogonality: persona attributes are varied orthogonally to content intent (e.g., same question phrased for different persona labels) to isolate persona effects.n3) parsimony: test suites are compact (100500 examples per workload) to enable frequent runs without large compute cost.n4) explainability: every flagged regression provides diffs, exemplar generations, and likely causal signals (quantization change, kernel switch, batch-size change).nnsuite composition and generation procedurenn1) core intent corpus: 250 canonical prompts covering common product intents (summarization, code generation, customer support, policy clarification). prompts are stored in the canonical prompt repo.n2) persona matrix: 10 persona attributes x 5 values each (50 variants). each core prompt is paired with 8 persona variants sampled with stratified coverage.n3) adversarial perturbations: for each persona-variant pair, apply 3 perturbations from the adversarial prompt suite (lexical noise, sarcasm marker insertion, indirect question phrasing).n4) anchor set: 40 prompts chosen for low semantic ambiguity and historical stability. anchors include deterministic seeds and fixed tokenization to reduce runtime nondeterminism.nnmetric definitions and thresholdsnn- safety toxicity rate: percent of outputs flagged by safety classifier 0.5. threshold: regression if increase 0.4 percentage points and bias delta 25 relative.n- demographic parity difference: absolute difference in positive/negative sentiment across persona groups. threshold: alert if 6 points (0100 scale) relative to anchors.n- hallucination rate: percent of outputs containing fabricated named facts (verified by reference extractor). threshold: regression if increase 3 points and persists across 3 consecutive nightly runs.n- response divergence score (rds): kl-style divergence between persona-conditioned token distributions and anchor distribution. threshold: alert if rds increases by 0.15.nnanchoring and calibration methodologynn- anchors are executed in the same job as the active suite and are used to compute a calibrated score: calibrated_score observed - anchor_mean historical_anchor_mean.n- for short-lived infra variance (noisy gpus, quant kernel jitter) we apply a rolling 7-run median to anchor_mean before raising alerts.n- when calibrating across quantized variants, anchors include both float32 and quantized runs to produce per-precision baselines.nnintegration with eval orchestration and cinn- orchestrator job: eval-orchestrator:run-persona-pbaef triggers pbaef. job parameters:n - model_id (string)n - precision_profile (enum: fp32, q4_0, q8_0)n - run_type (smokenightlypromotion)n- execution schedule:n - confluence, title: adaptive probe stewardship and debt catalog, content: overviewnnpurpose: this handbook defines the policy, operational playbook, and metadata catalog design for adaptive probe stewardship and a formalized probe debt register. the goal is to maximize signal-per-cost from automated and human-in-the-loop probes used by the eval harness while preventing annotation debt, stale probe drift, and runaway evaluation spend during model promotion and quant-fallback rollouts.nnscopen- applies to all probes (synthetic, shadow-captured, and user-sampled) executed by the eval harness and associated annotator pipelines.n- covers lifecycle stages: creation, prioritization, scheduling, annotation, retirement, and debt remediation.n- integrations: eval orchestrator, probe fabricator, telemetry ingest, annotation queue, cost ledger, and model onboarding dashboards.nndefinitionsn- probe: a single workload stimulus (input metadata) intended to exercise model behavior for quality/regression detection.n- probe steward: role responsible for a probe set (assignment lives in probe catalog).n- probe debt: any measurable liability tied to a probe (high annotation cost, stale label, mis-specified slice, privacy/legal flag).n- signal density: normalized ratio of labeled-failures-per-usd for a probe or probe slice.nnprinciplesn1) signal over volume: prefer probes that increase detection power per annotation dollar.n2) explicit debt accounting: treat probes like assets with amortized cost and ttl.n3) automation with human oversight: enable automated reclamation but require steward approval for high-impact actions.n4) cross-stage portability: probes should be tagged for suitability across hosted/dedicated/private runs.nnprobe metadata schema (required fields)n- probe_id (string)n- owner_team (string)n- steward (string)n- creation_date (yyyy-mm-dd)n- last_labeled_date (yyyy-mm-dd)n- workload_origin (enum: shadow, synthetic, corpus_sample)n- slice_tags (list of strings)n- cost_estimate_per_label_usd (float-string)n- expected_frequency (enum: continuous, periodic, one-off)n- signal_density_est (float-string: failures_per_usd)n- privacy_level (enum: public, internal, pii_restricted)n- ttl_days (integer-string)n- debt_flags (list of strings)n- promotion_gate (enum: pre-canary, canary-only, post-canary)nnexample probe manifest (yaml style for human consumption)n---nprobe_id: prb-2026-0643nowner_team: applied-mlnsteward: maya.chen@redwood.comncreation_date: 2026-01-10nlast_labeled_date: 2026-02-14nworkload_origin: shadownslice_tags: long-context, billing-intentncost_estimate_per_label_usd: 1.25nexpected_frequency: continuousnsignal_density_est: 0.007nprivacy_level: internalnttl_days: 180ndebt_flags: high-cost, low-recent-failuresnpromotion_gate: canary-onlyn---nnpriority scoring and budget allocationn- priority score (signal_density_est importance_weight) / sqrt(cost_estimate_per_label_usd epsilon)n- importance_weight is a configurable integer per product-steward mapping (default: 1..5).n- monthly probe budget is allocated by a two-tier allocator: 70 reserved for high-priority probes (score top-10 globally), 30 for exploration/low-frequency probes.nndecision rules (automated)n1) if signal_density_est mark probe for archival.n2) if cost_estimate_per_label_usd 5 and signal_density_est open debt remediation ticket and throttle scheduling.n3) if last_labeled_date ttl_days - flag for relabel or retire.n4) privacy_level pii_restricted requires steward approval for human labeling and must route to the redwood-pii-annotator queue.nnprobe debt catalog (structure)n- debt_id: dtc-yyyy-nnnnn- probe_id(s): list of probe_ids involvedn- debt_type: annotation_cost, stale_labels, privacy_hold, coverage_gap, flakey-assertionn- impact_estimate: short text (e.g., high: may block canary promotion)n- created_by: user/emailn- created_at, status: open, in_progress, mitigated, dismissedn- remediation_plan: short text and ownersnnoperational playbook: lifecycle stepsn1) creation: probe created by fabricator or manual entry. must supply schema fields above and a one-line detection hypothesis.n2) pre-scheduling check (automated): scoring, privacy gate, budget check. if fails, log to backlog.n3) scheduling: high-priority probes go to continuous shadow/execution path periodic probes are slotted into off-peak windows.n4) annotation routing: label queue selection based on privacy_level and cost bucket.n5) signal ingestion: evaluation results are persisted to eval store and fed to probe metrics with these baseline metrics: label_latency, label_cost_total, failures_detected, signal_density_actual.n6) steward review cadence: weekly for active probes, quarterly for low-frequency probes.n7) retirement: an automated archival pipeline can retire probes, but retirement of probes with active debt requires steward sign-off.nnrunbook: when a probe set rapidly increases costn1) alert: cost ledger emits an alert when 7-day spend 3x forecast for a probe set.n2) triage owner: probe steward and applied ml oncall.n3) immediate actions (first 30 minutes):n - pause scheduling of the affected probe ids (eval-orchestrator cli: evalctl probe pause --probe prb-xxxx)n - snapshot recent labels and telemetry to /eval-archives/cost-spikes/probeid/yyyymmdd.logn - open debt ticket auto-populated with key metrics and assign to stewardn4) containment (first 4 hours):n - re-route to low-cost annotators (if quality permits) or to synthetic heuristics for triagen - run signal_density_recalc job to confirm whether detection power justifies spendn5) remediation (2472 hours):n - either retire, reduce frequency, change annotator queue, or re-tag as exploration. update debt catalog and close ticket when mitigated.nnintegration apis and cli snippetsn- schedule a single probe (example):n curl -x post n -h authorization: bearer eval_api_token n -h content-type: confluence, title: evaluator sdk: adapter patterns for private and dedicated eval integrations, content: summarynnthis document describes the evaluator sdk adapter patterns and operational guidance for integrating redwoods eval harness into dedicated and private deployments. it covers design patterns for pluggable adapters, runtime requirements, telemetry mapping, privacy safeguards (dp-friendly workflows), quantization-aware evaluation hooks, and a recommended rollout checklist for operators. the target audience is applied ml engineers, platform engineers, and sres responsible for operating eval pipelines inside customer-isolated environments.nngoalsnn- provide repeatable adapter implementations that minimize changes to the central eval harness while allowing environment-specific integrations.n- ensure consistent telemetry and metric semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private eval runs.n- surface quantization and kv-cache artifacts in eval results to enable safe model promotion.n- maintain privacy-preserving defaults when running shadow/recorded traffic in customer-controlled networks.nnwhen to use this docnn- you are integrating redwoods eval harness into a dedicated cluster or a private (vpc/on-prem) control plane.n- you need consistent metrics and artifact collection between hosted and private evals.n- you need a privacy-preserving shadow evaluation pipeline for customer traffic.nndesign overviewnnthe evaluator sdk is split into three layers:nn1) core harness: evaluation logic, scoring, sample orchestration, and result aggregation.n2) adapter interface (stable): a thin shim that implements environment-specific behaviors (persistence, rpc, telemetry, secrets).n3) runtime plugins: small, replaceable modules that adapt to local infra (s3 vs. minio, prometheus pushgateway vs. remote write, hsm vs. kms).nnadapter responsibilitiesnneach adapter must implement the following logical responsibilities (interface-level):nn- storage_put(key, payload, metadata): persist artifacts (responses, token traces, kv cache snapshots).n- storage_get(key): read artifact for replay or analysis.n- telemetry_emit(metric_name, value, labels): emit evaluation metrics with canonical labels.n- secret_get(secret_ref): fetch credentials (wraps kms/hsm call if needed).n- request_send(endpoint, payload, timeout_ms): invoke a runtime endpoint (used for shadow-routing or live model probes).n- sanitize_input(input): enforce privacy filters (pii redaction/zeroization) before storing.nnpattern 1 file-backed adapter (recommended for private evals)nn- use case: on-prem or air-gapped evals where object stores are available via posix or s3-compatible apis.n- implementation notes: adapter writes to local object store under /var/lib/eval/artifacts/ and emits a manifest.json. use atomic renames for finalize.nnexample config snippet (confluence-style table represented in text):nn key value notes n --- ----- ----- n storage.type s3 minio endpoint for private deployments n storage.bucket eval-artifacts-prod per-customer bucket n auth.kms hsm:/slot1 optional hsm uri nnpattern 2 prometheus-bridge adapter (telemetry-forwarding)nn- use case: dedicated deployments push eval metrics into customers prometheus (pull) or centralized remote_write endpoint.n- implementation notes: provide two modes pushgateway for short-lived runs or remote_write for confluence, title: federated shadowing privacy-bounded probe synthesis playbook, content: summaryn-------nthis playbook defines a repeatable, privacy-bounded approach for running federated shadowing across redwoods hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and for synthesizing probes that approximate tenant workloads without leaking sensitive data. it codifies safe sampling, local privacy transformations, orchestration patterns, monitoring contracts, and regression triage tie-ins. use this playbook when a model or serving change requires cross-environment validation with tenant-level privacy guarantees.nnwhy this existsn---------------n- many production issues only surface when the combination of client prompts, kv cache state, and quantization interact in a target environment.n- full traffic mirroring is often disallowed by privacy or legal constraints. federated shadowing aims to provide coverage with provable privacy limits and bounded telemetry while preserving fidelity for regression detection.nnscope and applicabilityn-----------------------n- applies to: eval-mesh shadowing (on-hosted eval mesh), dedicated clusters, and private deployments where local privacy controls are required.n- not for: investigative human review of raw customer pii do not use this playbook when retention or data export rules would be violated.n- primary owners: applied ml (probe-fabricator), eval orchestration (shadow-orch), and privacy compliance.nndefinitionsn-----------n- federated shadowing: orchestrated execution of synthesized or sampled probes across multiple deployment tiers (hosted/dedicated/private) under a shared evaluation contract.n- probe synthesis: programmatic generation of evaluation inputs derived from anonymized telemetry anchors and service schemas.n- privacy budget (ε): target local differential privacy epsilon assigned to a probe population or tenant slice.n- fidelity score: automated metric comparing probe responses to baseline reference (range 0-1).nnpreconditions (must satisfy before starting)n-------------------------------------------n1) legal data: a signed data-handling attestation for the target tenant class and confirmation from privacy compliance that federated shadowing is permitted for the planned probe class.n2) infrastructure: shadow-orch and evaluator-sidecar deployed to the target dedicated/private clusters.n3) observability: redwood-console route and a telemetry pipeline path created (trace, per-probe metadata, fidelity metric ingestion).n4) baseline: reference model artifact and golden probe-set stored in eval-asset-registry with hash and version.nnhigh-level proceduren--------------------n1. define objective and success criterian - example objectives: detect regression in dsid_89fb08a2730b4db981fae7ccc45b0770, source_type: confluence, title: prompt sharding and cache-aware stability evaluation protocol, content: summary:nnthis document defines a repeatable evaluation protocol for measuring prompt-level output stability when prompts are sharded (split across segments), when prefix and kv caches are active, and across quantized model variants. the protocol is intended for applied ml engineers onboarding new models into redwoods serving fleet and for regression triage when a change in runtime (kernels, batching, quantization) correlates with output drift.nngoals:n- provide a deterministic, low-noise benchmark to compare semantic stability across model variants and runtime configs.n- surface regressions caused by caching differences, prompt segmentation, and quantization.n- produce actionable diagnostics (delta examples, attention/kv-dumps, similarity matrices) to guide model/runtime remediation.nnscope and applicability:n- applies to autoregressive text generation and chat-style models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder where applicable).n- not intended for pure embedding-only workloads (see embedding stability spec).n- routine use: onboarding new model version, validating quantization profile, or triaging a regression flagged by qa or customers.nnkey terms and definitions:n- prompt sharding: splitting a single prompt into multiple chunks that are sent as separate requests or streamed segments to the runtime. common for very long contexts or when prefix caching is leveraged.n- cache-aware mode: evaluation runs where the runtime is configured to populate and reuse prefix/kv cache between segments or across repeated requests.n- stability: measured as semantic agreement between outputs given equivalent intent metrics described below.nnhigh-level protocol (steps):n1) candidate selectionn - pick a representative prompt set (n 200 recommended). use a mix of short, medium, and long prompts and include edge cases: multi-turn chat fragments, code blocks, bullet lists, and html fragments.n - label prompts with modality tags and expected length bucket (short 2048).nn2) baseline generation (canonical run)n - run prompts end-to-end on the reference model variant with cache disabled (cold start) to obtain baseline outputs. record seeds, tokenizer, model hash, runtime version.n - cli example: python eval_runner.py --config configs/ps_stability_baseline.yaml --run-id baseline-2026-02-14nn3) sharded runsn - for each prompt, generate outputs under two sharding strategies:n a) segment-by-sentence: split on sentence boundaries (try to keep segment sizes 256512 tokens)n b) fixed-window: split into equal token windows with 25 overlapn - for each strategy, run in: cache-disabled and cache-enabled modes. capture per-segment outputs and final assembled output.nn4) quantization and runtime variantsn - repeat sharded runs on each model variant of interest (fp16, int8, quantized-llm-configa). ensure identical decoding parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop tokens).n - record kernel/runtime version, kernel flags (use_batched_kv, fused_attention), and hardware type.nn5) deterministic decoding and sampling controlsn - for stability-focused comparisons prefer deterministic decoding (temperature0, do_samplefalse). if sampling is required for downstream fidelity tests, run an additional sampled pass with fixed rng seed.nn6) metrics and thresholdsn - surface-level metrics (per-prompt):n token-level edit distance (levenshtein) normalized by output lengthn n-gram overlap (bleu/rouge) between baseline and candidate assembled outputsn semantic similarity: cosine(sim(embed(baseline)), embed(candidate)) using the reference embedding model (thresholds defined below)n structural agreement: alignment of stop tokens, list lengths, json schema conformance (where applicable)n - aggregate metrics (recommended reporting): mean, median, 95th percentile of normalized edit distance fraction of prompts with semantic similarity 0.03 compared to baseline - warningn 5 prompts with semantic similarity needs-investigationn any prompt with structural break (json invalidation, or missing required fields) - p0 triagenn7) diagnostics produced per failing promptn - raw outputs for baseline and each variant (per-segment and assembled)n - token alignment visualization (side-by-side diff)n - attention/kv dump (where supported) for segments showing divergence (save to /mnt/evals/kv-dumps/run-id/prompt-id)n - embedding similarity heatmap across prefixes and segmentsnnconfiguration examples (yaml):nn configs/ps_stability_baseline.yamlnrun_name: prompt_shard_stability.baselinenmodel: gptx-7b-fp16nmax_tokens: 256ndecoding:n temperature: 0.0n do_sample: dsid_026bbc0fbb97423ab9de20d8f99402d6, source_type: confluence, title: cohort-driven shadow validation playbook, content: overview:nnthis playbook describes a repeatable, cohort-driven approach to shadow (non-production) validation that combines traffic mirroring, cohort stratification, and statistical evaluation to detect drift, regressions, or qoe degradations before a model rollout. it is intended for use by ml engineers, product reliability, and sre when validating model variants (quantized models, finetunes, or new topologies) against real traffic slices.nngoals:n- expose subtle, slice-specific regressions that aggregate metrics miss.n- provide deterministic acceptance gates with clear thresholds and statistical tests.n- keep validation cost-bounded by adaptive sampling and prioritized cohorts.nnscope and non-goals:n- scope: live shadowing and replay for text-generation and embedding endpoints cohort metrics for latency, token cost, response-stability, and semantic fidelity.n- non-goals: synthetic adversarial fuzzing (see separate fuzz playbook) and complete production failover automation.nndefinitions:n- shadow traffic: duplicated requests sent to a candidate model without impacting production responses.n- cohort: a named subset of traffic defined by request attributes (customer_id, route, prompt-template, language, token_count, session_age).n- response-stability-index (rsi): composite metric measuring output drift against baseline using embedding cosine similarity, edit distance, and semantic score.nnwhen to run a cohort-driven shadow validation:n- before a model promotion that affects 5 of production request volume.n- when introducing cross-workload optimizations (e.g., new quant profile, kv-cache changes, batch scheduling).n- after detecting slice-specific degradations in continuous telemetry.nnownership and roles:n- requesting owner: feature/model owner (creates cohorts and success criteria).n- shadow operator: sre / infra (sets up mirroring, monitors resource usage).n- evaluator: applied ml / quality (runs statistical tests, interprets slice failures).n- approver: product owner or reliability lead (approves promotion or rollback).nnhigh-level workflow (stepwise):n1) define cohorts (310 per run):n - use historical telemetry to choose meaningful slices (high-value customers, long-context, multimodal inputs).n - example cohort definitions: high-long-context-english (tokens 2048), enterprise-integration-route (route /api/v1/generate customer_tier enterprise).n2) choose sampling policy and budget:n - default: mirror 10 of cohort traffic for 72 hours or until 5,000 requests per cohort are collected, whichever comes first.n - for sensitive cohorts, reduce to 12 with extended duration.n3) configure shadow routing (example manifest):n - provide network-level mirroring rules and candidate endpoint. see appendix for json/yaml snippets.n4) instrument telemetry and tagging:n - ensure every mirrored request is tagged with: cohort_id, shadow_run_id, baseline_model, candidate_model, sample_rate.n - log raw prompts, token counts, latency, final cost estimate (tokens model_cost_rate).n5) compute per-cohort metrics (real-time and batch):n - latency p95 and p99 (ms).n - token cost delta ().n - rsi (median per cohort) and drift fraction (percent responses with rsi baseline p99 20 and p baseline median - 0.03 and two-sided mann-whitney u test p 0.05.n - for categorical regressions (required fields missing): fisher exact test, require failure rate delta baseline 20 (p 15 cost review, consider quant profile finance/feature owner n rsi median median similarity 0.005 absolute immediate rollback for critical routes product nnsampling and budgeting guidelines:n- minimum sample per cohort for significance: 500 requests. if unavailable, mark cohort as insufficient data and schedule an extended run.n- budget cap per run: token budget defined in run config (default 10m tokens). operator may truncate tests if budget exhausted and annotate results.nndata privacy and redaction:n- always redact pii before storing mirrored requests. use the pipeline redaction rules: replace emails, ssns, api keys, and long identifiers with deterministic tokens.n- for enterprise customers with confidentiality flags, request explicit authorization before mirroring otherwise exclude those cohorts.nnoperational playbook (quick steps):n1) create run ticket with cohort definitions and success criteria.n2) request sre to enable mirror manifest with run_id and sample_rate.n3) confirm telemetry tags are present in the mirror stream.n4) validate that baseline and candidate endpoints are reachable.n5) monitor dashboards (per-cohort) for first 6 hours. if any hard fails occur, follow hard-fail incident checklist.nnpromotions, canary integration and rollout path:n- if all cohorts pass: promote candidate to canary (510 production, canary duration 4896 hours) with continuous cohort monitoring.n- if a small number of low-impact cohorts fail: consider targeted mitigations (prompt templates, per-route fallback) and rerun shadow validation.nnappendix a example shadow routing limited to the target cohort patterns.n- high resource usage on candidate host: coordinate with sre to throttle mirror throughput or scale candidate pool prioritize critical cohorts.n- inconsistent telemetry tags: stop the run, patch instrumentation, and restart to ensure validity of per-cohort aggregates.nnaudit and reporting:n- every shadow run must attach an artifact containing anonymized examples ( 0.8 for p1 regressions in production-like shadow runs).n- bound evaluator spend to a configurable daily budget while maximizing expected information gain.n- smooth probe churn to avoid bursty load on the eval fleet and model-serving clusters.n- provide transparent, auditable priorities and deterministic replay for postmortem triage.nnwhen to use this documentn- onboarding new probe families into the evaluation mesh.n- operationalizing continuous shadow or canary evals against a new model variant.n- implementing cost-constrained, risk-focused probe sampling for private/dedicated deployments.nnscope and non-goalsn- scope: scheduling, scoring, and integration hooks into eval-orchestrator and probe-queue. includes telemetry contract and rollout steps.n- non-goals: model-side instrumentation, long-term labeling workflows, or annotator economics (see separate docs).nnarchitecture summaryn- components:n - probe-fabricator: generates and mutates probe candidates from seed sets and telemetry anchors.n - probe-priority-service: computes a score for each probe based on curriculum rules, risk signals, and cost model.n - probe-queue: a tiered queue (hot, warm, cold) enforced by the scheduler.n - eval-orchestrator: consumes probes from probe-queue and dispatches to evaluator workers.n - backfill-manager: maintains probe budget and triggers historical replays.nnscoring function (design)n- score(probe) alpha ig(probe) beta risk(probe) - gamma cost(probe) delta freshnessboostn - ig(probe): estimated information gain (expected reduction in uncertainty for target slices). derived from historical detection rates and slice entropy.n - risk(probe): production telemetry signal (e.g., 95th-response-lag, error-rate spike probability, semantic-failure-probability).n - cost(probe): expected evaluator compute cost (tokens model_cost_per_token quant_penalty).n - freshnessboost: a small time-decay bonus for recently observed production anomalies.n - alpha/beta/gamma/delta are tunable per-curriculum profile.nncurriculum profilesn- defensive (slo-first): maximize risk, high gamma to constrain cost. use for mission-critical services.n- exploratory (coverage-first): maximize ig, moderate gamma. use for new-model onboarding.n- cost-limited (budget-first): strong cost penalty and aggressive batching suggestions. use for low-cost shadow environments.nnoperational parameters (table)n- the table below lists default parameters used in prod rollout. operators can override per-tenant or per-model.nnparameter default notesn------:---ndaily_eval_budget_usd 1200 soft budget backfill-manager enforces a hard cap with graceful pause.nhot_queue_capacity 5k probes highest priority targets p0/p1 signals.nwarm_queue_capacity 20k probes for ongoing coverage and re-eval.ncold_queue_capacity 200k probes low priority, best-effort sampling.nmax_batch_tokens 25k aggregation target used by probe-queue to group probes for efficient eval.npriority_decay_window_days 7 after this window, freshnessboost - 0.nreplay_retention_days 90 how long synthetic/historical probes are kept for deterministic replays.nnprobe lifecycle (numbered procedure)n1. fabrication: probe-fabricator creates candidate probes from seeds, telemetry anchors, and adversarial mutators. each probe is annotated with metadata: seed_id, slice_id, telemetry_anchor, estimated_tokens, provenance_hash.n2. scoring: probe-priority-service computes score(probe) and assigns a ttl and suggested batch affinity.n3. enqueue: probe is placed into hot/warm/cold tier according to score thresholds.n4. dispatch: eval-orchestrator pulls from hot first, respecting batch and slo constraints warm as capacity allows cold when spare budget exists.n5. result ingestion: evaluator workers emit structured results (labels, evaluator_metrics, cost). backfill-manager updates cost ledger and recalculates ig for related probes.n6. retire or recycle: probes are retired after exceeding retries or after replay_retention_days. reuse is allowed for high-ig probes under a different model variant.nnpriority thresholds (example)n- hot: score 0.72n- warm: 0.35 3 minutes for 10m window.n - action: throttle warm/cold dispatch, enable aggressive batching, and spin up ephemeral evaluator workers (runbook: eng-sre procedure).n3) priority inversion (low-risk probes running before high-risk)n - trigger: audit logs show score misassignment for 100 probes in 1h.n - action: ingest audit logs to simulate scoring, run deterministic replay, roll back priority-service to previous release.nnfailure modes and mitigationsn- overconfident ig estimates: enforce conservative floor to reduce weight on ig during first 48 hours of a new curriculum.n- cost underestimation for quantized artifacts: add quant_penalty per model and monitor cost drift metric: quant_cost_ratio 1.25 triggers mitigation.n- probe duplication loops: dedupe by provenance_hash if 3 duplicates in 1h, mark probe family as noisy and reduce fabrication rate.nnrollout plan (canary - ramp)n1. internal canary (week 0): enable pcaps in eval-staging rewrites.n- well-calibrated annotators reduce false-positive regression alerts and speed up triage in the regression playbooks.nnscopenn- applies to internal and partner annotation vendors used for the conversation prefix up to the turn, the partial response (possibly streaming), and the intended evaluation prompt instructions.n- iaa (krippendorffs alpha for ordinal labels cohens kappa for binary): target 0.7 for ordinal 3 labels, 0.8 for binary pass/fail for production slices.n- annotator latency: median annotation time per judgment unit u003c 75s for full 8k-token session fragments (instrumented).n- drift window: 7-day rolling metrics. significant drift if metric moves 2.5 standard deviations from baseline.nnprep: tooling and data setupnn- create streaming judgment tasks in the judgment units across the top 10 production slices (mix of short, medium, long contexts).n b) each candidate annotator labels the full seed set.n c) compute iaa and per-slice confusion matrices.n d) pass criteria: overall iaa 0.7, no production slice iaa u003c 0.6. those who fail receive focused retraining and re-test on 100 new seed units.nn2) anchoring-phase (daily run, ongoing) keep annotators anchored to golden examples:n a) inject 510 anchor probes each day (randomized) with previously adjudicated labels.n b) track anchor agreement by annotator (daily) and by slice (rolling 7-day).n c) auto-suspend annotator from live tasks if anchor agreement u003c 85 in a rolling 48-hour window.nn3) drift detection and triage (weekly):n a) compute per-slice metrics: label distribution, average annotator confidence, median annotation time, anchor-agreement, and iaa.n b) flag slices with any of:n - iaa drop u003e 0.1 absolute vs baseline,n - anchor agreement u003c 85,n - median annotator latency increase 2x baseline (could indicate task confusion).n c) triage steps (ordered):n 1. re-run a 100-probe adjudication on the flagged slice.n 2. if adjudicated labels disagree with current anchors, create a re-anchoring batch and notify steward.n 3. if disagreement is between annotators only, schedule focused retraining and a 50-probe retest.nn4) continuous quality regression guardrail (integration with eval harness):n - for every model promotion or quantization change, require a shortform shadow evaluation against an anchored probe set (min 1,000 units) where annotator anchor agreement must remain within /-2 of baseline.nnguidance for long-context specificsnn- context trimming: provide explicit priming guidelines to annotators on how to mark relevance when past context exceeds 16k tokens allow annotators to mark earliest token ranges they used when judging.n- streaming partial-response judgments: use a 3-stage label flow: preliminary-pass (after first n tokens), mid-pass (after chunk m), final-pass (full response). capture timestamps and final label must be used for scoring.n- function-call fidelity: expose function-call traces inline ask annotators to rate (02) fidelity of function semantics and argument completeness.nnexample task template (json snippet)nnn task_id: stream-annot-0001,n session_id: s-53042,n prefix_tokens: 6200,n stream_chunks: chunk-1,
