dsid_2add37caccb641db8f1d608bc5878847, source_type: confluence, title: shadow-to-production: eval continuity safety guidelines, content: summary:nthis document prescribes the end-to-end process for using shadow (mirrored) traffic and continuous eval outputs to safely promote models into production for text generation and embedding workloads. it connects eval-harness artifacts (workload fingerprints, prompt coverage, quantization evaluation), runtime observability, and automated rollback triggers so teams can preserve quality slos while iterating quickly.nngoals:n- ensure production promotions are gated by real-traffic shadow evaluation synthetic continuity checks.n- define concrete metrics, thresholds, and automated actions for safe rollback and triage.n- provide runbook steps and ownership for degradation investigations spanning eval-harness - runtime - model-promotion-service.nnapplicability:n- applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes that support request mirroring (shadow routing).n- target workloads: text-generation/chat, embeddings, and reranking.nnkey concepts and signals:n1) shadow run: mirror a sample of production requests to candidate model instances without affecting user-visible responses. shadow traffic should preserve original request headers and sampling ratios.n2) continuity test suite: a short, prioritized set of prompts derived from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks that exercise long-tail failure modes for the target workload.n3) response stability index (rsi): a composite signal combining token-level edit distance, semantic-similarity delta (embedding cosine), and policy-safety flags. range 0-100, lower is better.n4) token amplification ratio (tar): ratio of mean tokens generated by candidate model to baseline. flags unbounded or degenerate generation.n5) quantization delta: measured difference in essential eval metrics (rsi, semantic-score, latency) between full-precision and quantized variants during shadow runs.nngating metrics and thresholds (default baselines):n- rsi: 4.0, fail gate).n- p95 latency: no more than 20 regression vs baseline and absolute p95 investigate hallucination/verbosity).n- semantic recall (embedding cosine on ground-truth checks): 0.92 average for retrieval prompts.n- safety flags (policy classifier): no more than 0.2 absolute increase in high-severity flags.n- quantization delta: rsi increase 10 (otherwise treat quantized variant as incompatible for that workload).nntraffic sampling and shadow configuration:n- shadow sampling rate: start at 0.1 of requests for initial verification, ramp to 2-5 as confidence increases.n- sampling strategy: stratified by route and prompt-type fingerprint (use eval-orch fingerprint tagging) so slices are covered proportionally.n- forge requests exactly as sent by clients (including conversation history) but set header x-shadow-run: candidate-model-id.n- storage: persist shadow responses in the eval-orch datastore for at least 30 days for retrospective triage.nncontinuity test suite (runtime-synth):n- run 1: latency-sensitive prompts (short queries, token cap 64) x 200 samples. check p95 and token tail behavior.n- run 2: long-context prompts ( 2048 tokens) x 100 samples. verify kv-cache correctness and output truncation.n- run 3: adversarial prompt set (from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/adversarial-noise) x 300 samples. measure safety flags and rsi.n- run 4: embedding recall microbench (100 paired queries). measure semantic score and embedding variance.nnpromotion workflow (high-level):n1) preflight: run inference-readiness-eval-matrix locally with model candidate (unit-sized synthetic suite).n2) shadow rollout stage a: mirror 0.1 traffic for 48 hours. collect metrics and continuity tests.n3) review: automated report generated by eval-orch summarizing gating metrics reviewers assigned (owner applied-ml) must sign off or open a triage issue.n4) shadow stage b: increase to 2 mirror for 72 hours if stage a passed. run full continuity suite nightly.n5) canary (optional): route 1 of live responses to candidate for actual responses with rollback guardrails and customer-scope opt-outs.n6) promote to production routing if all gates pass for 7 days otherwise, rollback to previous stable model and open a regression investigation.nnautomated rollback triggers (examples):n- any rsi increase 8.0 vs baseline within a 1-hour window.n- safety flag spike: 0.5 absolute increase in critical flags in 15 minutes.n- latency slo breach: sustained p95 1.2x baseline for 30 minutes or p99 2.0x baseline.n- token amplification: tar 2.0 sustained for 10 minutes.n- quantization catastrophic: semantic recall drop 0.08 absolute.nnimmediate rollback procedure:n1) alerting: pager duty escalation to oncall-model-owner and applied-ml triage@redwood. notify customer-success if any customer-visible regressions are observed.n2) execution: call model-promotion-service api to revert traffic to previous model_id. example: n curl -x post n -h authorization: bearer rd_token n -h content-type: application/json n -d action:rollback,target_model_id:model-1234,reason:rsi spiken3) preserve artifacts: snapshot shadow response storage slice, collect profiler traces from runtime-collector, and start automated bisect job if enabled.n4) postmortem: within 72 hours produce a regression triage that includes top failing prompt slices, quantization parameters, and kernel-level profiling.nninvestigation playbook (triage owner responsibilities):n- step 0: confirm alert validity (check noise, infra events).n- step 1: compare shadow vs baseline slices in eval-dashboard prioritize high-severity slices with 0.5 rsi delta.n- step 2: run hypothesis checks: quantization delta? prompt-tokenization mismatch? kv-cache context corruption? model artifacts mismatch?n- step 3: if quantization suspected, re-run quant-eval job with --deterministic-seed and capture full logits for 100 seeds.n- step 4: if infra suspected, attach runtime profiler traces and coord with eng-serving-runtime for kernel scheduling logs.n- step 5: if model bug, label and route to model-onboarding team for rollback/retrain.nnquantization specific guidance:n- always include a quantization shadow pass in stage a for any new quant profile. record quantization delta (rsi, latency, memory) in the promotion report.n- reject quantized promotion when rsi increases 1.5 and semantic recall drops 0.02 for retrieval/rewrite workloads.n- recommended quant profiles by workload:n chat-medium: int8-gptq-8 group-size64 (fast path verify with long-context tests).n retrieval-heavy: fp16 fallback preferred quantized variants must pass embedding-stability audit.nnobservability and dashboards (what to monitor):n- eval-orch/shadow-metrics: rsi-by-slice, tar, safety-flag-rate, embedding-delta.n- runtime/latency: p50/p95/p99 per-model and per-route.n- stability/rolling: 1h, 6h, 24h windows for rsi and safety flags.n- promotion-service: model-version lineage and active traffic splits.nnexample cli / yaml snippets:n- run a targeted continuity eval (eval-orch):n redwood-eval run --suite continuity-short --model candidate:2026-04-01 --out results/continuity-short.json --samples 200nn- shadow routing rule (kubernetes ingress annotation):n annotations:n redwood.io/shadow-target: model:candidate-2026-04-01n redwood.io/shadow-sample: 0.001nnownership and roles:n- model owner (primary): responsible for promotion and initial triage.n- applied ml (secondary): owns eval-harness suites, continuity tests, and quantization pass criteria.n- servruntime: responsible for tracing, profiler data, and kernel-level reconciliation when latency/throughput regressions appear.n- customer success: notified for production-visible regressions and coordinates customer communication.nnrisk register (common failure modes):n- silent semantic drift due to tokenization mismatch between training and serving. mitigation: tokenization fingerprint checks in preflight.n- quantized hallucinations: mitigation: additional adversarial-run sweep and reject quant-profile if tar or rsi flags exceed thresholds.n- data leakage in shadow logs: mitigate by pii scrubbing and strict retention policies (30-day default, 7-day for sensitive customers).nnappendix a quick checklist before promotion:n- preflight eval matrix passed (unit and synthetic).n- shadow stage a (0.1) passed gating metrics for 48h.n- continuity test nightly runs succeeded at 0 regressions for top-5 critical slices.n- quantization delta measured and within thresholds.n- monitoring dashboards provisioned and reviewers assigned.n- rollback playbook tested within the last 30 days (game-day).nnappendix b example promotion acceptance table (fill in in review):n metric baseline candidate delta pass? notes n rsi (avg) 2.4 3.1 0.7 yes within 4.0 threshold n p95 latency 820ms 900ms 9.7 yes under 20 cap n tar 1.0 1.12 12 yes acceptable verbosity n safety flags 0.12 0.15 0.03 yes low absolute delta nndocument maintenance:n- owner: applied-ml team (marisol canary rollout, content: overviewn--------nthis document defines the evaluation gate for quantized model artifacts and the associated canary rollout orchestration used by redwood inference. it codifies the entry criteria for promoting a quantized artifact from shadow/onboarding environments into production routes (hosted, dedicated, or private), the telemetry and tests required, and the rollback/troubleshooting guidance to tie into existing regression triage playbooks.nnscopen-----n- applies to artifacts produced by the model onboarding and quantization pipelines (both automatic and manual quant profiles).n- covers hosted api, dedicated pools, and private (vpc/on-prem) deployments where binary/quant artifacts are deployed.n- integrates with: eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, quality guardrails, and regression triage procedures.nngoals and principlesn--------------------n- safety-first: do not promote artifacts that show statistically significant regressions on prioritized slices.n- reproducible gating: every promoted artifact must carry provenance (checksums, quant profile, kernel pins).n- cost- and latency-aware: accept modest throughput/latency regressions only when quality is preserved.n- fast rollback: automated fallback to pre-quantized or previous-quant artifacts on breach of slos.nnacceptance criteria (high level)n-------------------------------nall of the following must pass for a quantized artifact to be eligible for canary:nn- core prompt-set stability: weighted-regression-delta (wrd) 0.995 on the run (automated, parallelized, 26 hours depending on artifact size)n - execute core prompt-set, edge-case probes, multilingual anchors, and latency-quality slices.n - produce json report, per-slice diffs, and a signed acceptance artifact.n - command: rwi-eval run --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/ --slices core,edge,multi --profile quant --output report.jsonnn4) telemetry snapshotn - snapshot gatingn - automated pass/fail decision based on thresholds above.n - if pass: artifact moves to canary-ready state and a canary deployment is scheduled.n - if fail: record fail reason, notify model-owner and qe, and open a triage ticket with labels: quant-fail, artifact:.nncanary rollout orchestrationn----------------------------nprinciples: incremental traffic, real-world telemetry, and short feedback loops. canary uses the same route-level instrumentation as production (token-level, cost, latency, error breakdowns).nncanary configuration (example yaml):nn---ncanary_name: truen---nntraffic routing is controlled by the canary controller (service: canary-orch) which will bump percentages according to the yaml schedule if and only if monitoring windows show no threshold infra/kernel mismatches before assuming a model-quality regression.nnownership and contactsn----------------------n- model owner: defined on artifact metadata (required).n- qe contact: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/causal-regression-investigation-handbook-2026n, doc_id: dsid_b537fddcc38040a4892327ee27113f0b, source_type: confluence, title: latency-tail-capture-and-synthetic-backfill-procedure-2024, content: abstract:nplaybook for capturing high-latency tail events in production traffic, synthesizing deterministic probes that reproduce tail behavior in the eval harness, and backfilling historical shadow traces for offline quant/quality analysis. focuses on observability signals, probe generation, synthetic backfill policy, and a triage runbook for applied ml teams.nnbackground_and_motivation:nwe observe intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes (tail events) that are costly and can correlate with quality regressions after quant or routing changes. typical failure modes include kv-cache thrash, quantized kernel stalls, and rarely seeded memory pressure on gpu nodes. root cause analysis is slow when spikes are ephemeral and requests are not reproducible. this playbook defines a reproducible capture - probe synthesis - synthetic backfill workflow so model-onboarding, quantization, and runtime teams can reproduce, validate, and fix tail regressions without impacting live traffic.nnscope_and_invariants:napplies to text generation and chat endpoints served by eval-mesh and production-serving. not in scope: unrelated network-level outages, control-plane-only incidents. invariants: all captures must be sampled and redacted to pii policy probes must be deterministic given seed and tokenizer version backfill workloads must not exceed 20 of eval-fleet capacity and must be scheduled during maintenance windows unless explicitly approved.nnsignal_definitions:n1) latency-tail trigger: p99 1.2x baseline_p99 for 5 consecutive 1-min windows or single-request latency 3s for short-context endpoints. 2) quality signal: embedding cosine drift 0.07 on monitored slices or token-entropy change 0.25. 3) kv-cache miss storm: cache_miss_rate increase 10ppt for request shard. 4) quantization suspect: runtime quant-decoded-error 0.5 on probe samples.nncapture_pipeline_overview:nsteps: 1) detection: alert from eval-mesh-alerting (rule: latency-tail trigger). 2) live-snapshot: invoke probe-fabricator capture job (captures request headers, tokenized input, model_version, runtime_profile, kv-cache-hash, node_id, seed). 3) redaction: automated pii redaction using redaction-service v2.0. 4) provenance: store snapshot in snapshot-archive with tags (incident_id, slice, model, runtime). 5) notification: create triage ticket in regression-triage board and attach snapshot link.nnprobe_generation_steps:n1) confirm capture integrity: run probe-validate against snapshot-archive/. 2) synthesize deterministic probe: probe-fabricator synth --snapshot --tokenizer v3 --seed --output probes/.json 3) add contextual priming: append the production prompt-prefix and system-role observed in original request. 4) create probe metadata with: model_variant, quant_profile (if any), runtime_kernels, kv-cache-state-hash. 5) register probe in eval-mesh as a debug-probe with low priority: defines the hybrid eval cost-fidelity splitter (hecfs) a deterministic policy and runtime component that routes evaluation probes across multiple fidelity tiers (smoke, standard, deep) to maximize coverage and failure signal while enforcing a configurable cost budget. hecfs provides (1) an allocation algorithm, (2) runtime routing knobs, (3) operational slos/metrics, and (4) a small runbook for triage when the splitter misbehaves.nnaudience:n- applied ml engineers operating the eval harness and shadow fleetsn- platform engineers integrating probe routing into shadow and federated evaluatorsn- product owners responsible for evaluation cost/perf tradeoffsnnwhy this exists:n- continuous evaluation at scale has variable marginal value: not every probe needs full-fidelity instrumentation.n- without systematic allocation, teams either overspend on deep evaluation or under-detect regressions.n- hecfs provides a principled way to amortize eval spend while preserving sensitivity to regressions.nnscope and definitions:n- probe: a single evaluation input (prompt metadata) executed by the harness.n- fidelity tiers:n - smoke: single seed, lightweight metrics, fast, offline profiling produces per-slice base-cost and baseline-variance. profiling includes quant-shadow runs and prefix-cache sensitivity.n2) a lightweight estimator assigns each incoming probe a sensitivity score s and an expected token_cost c for each fidelity tier.n3) the splitter uses a knapsack-inspired allocator to distribute probes into fidelity buckets given the global budget b and soft quality target q (target detection probability).n4) a small rebalancer runs every minute to migrate probes (where possible) from standard - deep or deep - standard based on live telemetry (e.g., rising variance, new latency anomalies).n5) routing decisions are recorded in the probe registry and emitted as telemetry (route_reason, expected_cost, chosen_tier, estimator_version).nnallocation remaining_budget b - allocate_reservedn4. ensure per-slice floor: for each slice s, mark floor_count(s) max(floor_coverage count(s), 1) and allocate those at standard tier, deducting expected costn5. marginal_gain / expected_deep_cost threshold(q):n assign probe - deep remaining_budget - expected_deep_costn else if remaining_budget cost(probe, standard):n assign probe - standard remaining_budget - cost(probe, standard)n else:n assign probe - smoken6. opportunistic pool: route up to allocate_reserved probes to deep when anomaly detectors flag themnnoperational metrics (emitted every minute and confluence, title: microburst batching and workload fingerprint guidelines, content: summarynnthis document defines a reproducible approach for detecting microburst-style workload fingerprints and applying adaptive batching strategies in the eval harness and production serving runtime. goal: reduce cost and tail latency variance caused by short, bursty traffic patterns while preserving throughput and output quality.nnproblem statementnnmicrobursts are short-lived spikes of high qps with small request sizes (commonly 8128 tokens) that: n- cause inefficient gpu occupancy (many tiny batches).n- inflate p95/p99 latency dramatically due to scheduling overhead.n- confuse static batching heuristics tuned for average load.nndefinitions and abbreviationsnn- microburst: a contiguous window (default 10s) where arrival rate burst_qps_threshold.n- burst qps threshold (burst_qps_threshold): default 300 reqs/s per front-end shard.n- short-request: request with prompt_length 300 qps, median tokens 2x baseline for 5 minutes (not a microburst).nntelemetry signals to detect fingerprintsnncollect and evaluate these signals at 1s and 10s windows: n- arrival_rate_per_shard (reqs/s)n- median_prompt_tokens, p90_prompt_tokensn- batch_assembly_time_ms (mean, p95)n- avg_batch_size_tokens and avg_batch_size_reqsn- kernel_utilization (gpu active time fraction)n- queue_length (requests waiting to be batched)nndetection rule (example): n1) if arrival_rate_per_shard (10s) 300 and median_prompt_tokens 2x over 1s baseline and duration burst-friendly. n- if kernel_utilization slo_p95_threshold for 2 consecutive 10s windows, escalate batch_timeout_ms 4ms (to increase aggregation) up to 40ms.n- if mixed-long detected, enable request-slicing and per-request prioritization to avoid head-of-line blocking.nndefault thresholds and acceptance criteriannbelow is the recommended starting configuration used by the eval-harness and can be tuned per workload. operators must validate changes in shadow before rollout.nn metric default notes n------:---n burst_qps_threshold 300 req/s per front-end shard n short_request_token_cutoff 128 tokens 15 vs baseline for production routes.n - tokens/sec/gpu must not decrease 10 for sustained loads.n - tail error rate (5xx from runtime) must remain burst_qps_threshold: confirm short-highburst.n4) run replay of observed trace in eval-harness with baseline and current config. n5) if replay reproduces regression: revert adaptive changes (if recently rolled) or apply passthrough to critical routes while continuing investigation.n6) produce postmortem with root cause: config parameter, scheduling regression, model change, or infra degradation.nnrollout plan for adaptive-batching changesnn- canary: 1 traffic routed to new config for 2 hours, monitor p95/p99 and error rates.n- progressive rollout: 1 - 5 - 20 - 100 across 2472 hours with rollback on gate failure.n- safety net: automatic fallback to conservative mode when p95(latency) configured slo_p95_threshold for 3 consecutive 10s windows.nnownership, slas and dashboardsnn- owner: serving-runtime team (primary), eval-harness (secondary)n- slos to monitor (per-route): n - short-request p95 int8, mixed-precision families).n- covers integration points between eval harness, prompt catalog, quantization profiles, and runtime observability.n- not a replacement for business-level acceptance tests (product signoff still required).nndefinitionsn-----------n- fidelity contract: a declared mapping of quality metrics to deployment tiers and acceptable deltas versus baseline.n- probe: a single evaluation item derived from the prompt catalog (single-shot or multi-turn).n- latency slice: workload bucket defined by request size, functioncall usage, and p95/p99 latency sensitivity.n- quant-compatibility test: synthetic and runtime checks that exercise tokenization, kv-cache behavior, and attention fallback for quantized kernels.nnslo matrix (canonical)n----------------------n metric hosted (fastest path) dedicated (reserved) private (customer-managed) n--------------------------------------------------------:---------------------:---------------------------:n p50 generation latency (ms) 0.92 vs baseline 0.90 vs baseline 0.88 vs baseline n functioncall correctness () 99.0 98.0 96.5 n tokenization equivalence (score) 0.995 0.99 0.98 n regression alert rate (per 100k) 99 of probes.nneval harness integration run probe suite against baseline and candidate for deterministic probes collect diff metrics.n- ci step c (runtime sim): use serving-simulation harness to emulate mixed-latency slices and batch sizes framework, content: summaryn-------nthis document defines the eval budget ledger: a lightweight, canonical accounting model and operational framework for tracking, attributing, and governing the cost of evaluation work (shadow runs, probes, synthetic workloads, and human review) across the eval harness. it standardizes cost buckets, attribution rules, reporting artifacts, and a minimal runbook for triaging unexpected spend. the ledger enables reproducible cost rollups for feature teams, platform owners, and finance.nngoalsn-----n- provide a single source-of-truth csv/json artifact (the ledger) for every eval campaign.n- define deterministic attribution rules to map compute, human labeling, and storage costs to owning teams and probes.n- enable near-real-time spend dashboards and budget alerts tied to probes, model variants, and environments (shadow/staging/prod).n- reduce surprise spend from large synthetic sweeps and regression investigations support pre-commit budget gating.nndefinitionsn-----------n- probe: an atomic evaluation input or workload slice submitted to the eval harness.n- campaign: a collection of probes executed as part of a single objective (e.g., shadow rollout of model-v2, quantization stress sweep).n- ledger row: a single line in the canonical csv representing cost attribution for one probe execution.nnledger schema (csv columns)n--------------------------nthe ledger is produced by the eval orchestrator after each batch and stored in s3 and the eval index. each ledger row is csv with these columns (pipe-delimited in examples below for readability):nn- ledger_id (string): uuid for the row.n- campaign_id (string): stable id for the campaign.n- probe_id (string): stable id for the probe.n- model_variant (string): e.g., redwood/gptx-8b-q4_latest.n- environment (string): shadowstagingprod.n- start_ts (iso8601): run start time.n- end_ts (iso8601): run end time.n- compute_seconds (float): wall-clock gpu/cpu seconds consumed attributed to this probe.n- gpu_type (string): e.g., a100-80gb, l4x.n- memory_gb_seconds (float): memory usage seconds (for cross-instance memory costs).n- tokens_in (int): input tokens.n- tokens_out (int): output tokens.n- kv_cache_hit_ratio (float): fraction for reuse-based discounts.n- human_label_seconds (float): paid human reviewer seconds attributable.n- storage_gb_months_fraction (float): short-lived artifact storage prorated to run.n- infra_cost_usd (float): computed infra cost allocated to row (see cost model).n- human_cost_usd (float): human labeling cost.n- total_cost_usd (float): infra_cost_usd human_cost_usd amortized tooling.n- owning_team (string): team slug owning the campaign (e.g., search-platform).n- billing_tag (string): optional billing tag for downstream finance mapping.n- notes (string): free text for special adjustments or credits.nncost model and attribution rulesn--------------------------------n1) compute pricing table (example):nn resource unit nominal_price_usd comment n------:---:---n a100-80gb per gpu-hour 3.20 spot pricing baseline for eval fleet n l4x per gpu-hour 1.10 cheaper short-live experiments n vcpu per vcpu-hour 0.05 for non-gpu workloads n ram per gb-hour 0.002 memory charge for long-running jobs nn2) compute allocation: infra_cost_usd sum(resource_seconds price_per_unit_hour / 3600) adjusted by kv_cache discount. for probes that benefit from prefix/kv cache, apply a kv discount factor: cost (1 - kv_cache_hit_ratio kv_cache_savings). default kv_cache_savings 0.45.nn3) human labeling: human_cost_usd human_label_seconds human_rate_usd_per_second. default human_rate_usd_per_second 0.004 (equivalent to 14.4/hour for contractor labeling).nn4) storage and tooling amortization: short-lived artifacts (replays, logs) are prorated and summed into storage_gb_months_fraction storage_unit_price_usd. tooling and infra overhead (e.g., eval queue, orchestrator overhead) is allocated to rows as a percent uplift (default 5) and recorded in notes.nnownership and governance rulesn------------------------------n- campaign owner (owning_team) is responsible for setting a campaign budget and tagging critical probes with high-priority flags.n- platform (eval-harness) owns the compute_price table and publishing weekly baseline rates to the ledger generator.n- finance confluence, title: evaluation retrospective priority synthesis playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook defines a standardized retrospective process and a quantitative priority-synthesis framework for managing evaluation probes, probe budgets, and regression triage across model families and deployment tiers. it is intended for evaluators, model stewards, and platform engineers responsible for maintaining production quality while balancing cost and latency.nnwhy this existsnn- we operate multiple evaluator fleets (shadow, canary, long-tail) with limited probe budget. without a consistent prioritization algorithm and retrospective cadence, high-impact failures are discovered late and cost is allocated inefficiently.n- this playbook aligns the eval lifecycle with quantization migration, shadowing experiments, and incident triage so that responsibility, telemetry, and rollback paths are clear.nnscope terminologynn- probe: a single test instance (prompt metadata) executed against a model variant as part of an evaluation job.n- slice: a grouped set of probes targeting a semantic/functional area (e.g., payment-intent, legal-forms, multi-turn-coherence).n- priority score: numeric score used by the scheduler to allocate probes under budget constraints.n- cohort shadow: a runtime shadowing run that mirrors a subset of live traffic to a candidate model.nnprinciplesnn1. value-first: prioritize probes that reduce customer-facing risk (safety, correctness, regression severity) ahead of exploratory coverage.n2. cost-aware: embed per-probe expected token cost and latency into prioritization so we can trade coverage against spend.n3. signal-driven retrospectives: run a short (weekly) quantitative retrospective that re-weights slices based on recent incidents, regressions, and drift.n4. cross-model comparability: all shadow and eval runs must surface the same minimal telemetry contract (see telemetry contract table).nntelemetry contract (minimum)nn key type evaluator fail nnpriority synthesis algorithm (high level)nnpriorityscore w_sev severityimpact w_freq usagefrequency w_drift driftscore - w_cost normalizedcost - w_latency normalizedlatency w_recency recencyboostnnwhere weights (w_) are learned/managed at the squad level and updated during retrospectives. default weight suggestions (initial):nn- w_sev 6.0n- w_freq 3.0n- w_drift 2.5n- w_cost 1.4n- (elena garcía)n, doc_id: dsid_c001bd5f65cf47f18d4715ae47f097cc, source_type: confluence, title: multifidelity shadow scheduler and data contract, content: overviewnnpurposenthis document defines the multifidelity shadow scheduler (mss) and the accompanying data contract used to reliably run shadow evaluations across heterogeneous fidelity levels (live shadow, synthetic microprobes, and replayed traffic). the goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable orchestration pattern that balances cost, signal quality, and safety for model promotion decisions.nnscopen- applies to all shadow evaluation runs for inference-serving model variants (hosted, dedicated, private) that feed into promotion gates, regression triage, and quantization verification.n- describes scheduler behavior, fidelity tiers, data and telemetry contract, acceptance quorum, and runbook for promoting a shadowed candidate.nnmotivationnas we increase the cadence of model updates and deploy quantized variants, teams need deterministic, crossregion shadowing that:n- produces comparable signal across fidelity types,n- avoids overloading production paths, andn- provides a clear data contract so evaluators and sres can reason about drift and regressions.nndefinitionsn- fidelity levels: live (mirror small percentage of live traffic), hybrid (mixed livesynthetic), synthetic (replayer or probe-driven), replay (historical traffic playback).n- quorum: minimum aggregate of evaluator signals (numeric metrics and human review votes) required before a promotion decision.n- shadow run: an execution of a model variant in nonserving mode where outputs are collected for evaluation only.nndesign overviewn- scheduler is a central orchestration service (mss-service) that provisions shadow runs to runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private connectors).n- each run is assigned a fidelity class and a telemetry profile.n- data contract guarantees schema, sampling, and retention for evaluation artifacts.n- promotion flow uses a quorum protocol: numeric gates (slo deltas, regression thresholds) at least one manual annotator signoff for high-risk slices.nnkey guarantees provided by mssn- isolation: shadow traffic must never affect production latency budgets or kv cache integrity.n- representativeness: live and hybrid runs are weighted to preserve distributional fidelity.n- reproducibility: replay seeds and probe versions are recorded for exact replays.n- cost control: synthetic probes have rate limits and backpressure to control gpu spend.nnscheduler algorithm (high level)n1. accept run request with parameters: model_id, variant_tag, fidelity, slice_spec, duration, tracer_id.n2. validate data contract: ensure required probes/provenance fields are present. reject if missing.n3. allocate capacity using a smoothing window algorithm: prefer idle capacity in same region fall back to dedicated burst pool.n4. throttle based on slo headroom: if p99 latency budget usage 80 for production pool, route shadow to dedicated or synthetic only.n5. start run and attach telemetry sampling: full traces for 1 sessions aggregated metrics for all.n6. monitor health and autoevict after configurable failure thresholds.nndata contract (required fields)nevery shadow artifact uploaded to the evaluation store must include the following toplevel fields (flat json record per request):n field_name type description required example n--------------------------------------------------n request_id string uuid v4 for the request yes req_4f11a2 n model_id string canonical model slug yes gpt-redwood-7b n variant_tag string serving tag or quant profile yes q4_1 n fidelity string livehybridsyntheticreplay yes hybrid n slice_id string logical slice label yes payments-card-errors n timestamp_utc string iso8601 yes 2026-02-18t15:22:03z n input_tokens int tokenized input length yes 42 n output_tokens int tokens produced yes 128 n model_logits_checksum string fnv64 hex or n/a for opaque outputs no fidelity, request_id must be correlated with production trace_id for postmortem tracing, but payloads must not be forwarded to downstream systems.nntelemetry and metricsnminimum metrics emitted by mss (per run):n- run_id, model_id, variant_tag, fidelity, start_ts, end_ts, total_requests, acceptance_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_count, eviction_reasonn- artifact quality in critical task f1 or 2x latency delta at p95 on production slices.n- stability gates: embedding stability score 0.92 across sampled anchor set.n- quorum: at least 3 independent automated evaluators pass (unit tests, slice tests, adversarial probes) and either (a) a human annotator approves critical slices, or (b) an audit of sandboxed inference for 1k samples with no high-severity safety hits.nnpromotion flow (operational steps)n1. mss aggregates run outputs into a promotion report and posts to /eval-reports/model_id/variant_tag/run_id.n2. auto-evaluator stage runs and emits pass/fail flags.n3. if numeric gates pass and quorum met, the system will mark candidate as eligible_for_canary but will not automatically promote without scheduled canary window.n4. sre schedules a short canary (0.5 traffic) for 24h with increased monitoring.n5. if canary passes, product owner can approve a staged rollout.nnrunbook: quick triage for shadow regressionsn1. identify offending slices from promotion report.n2. check provenance and fidelity: confirm whether the failure was observed in live/hybrid vs synthetic only.n3. if failure exists only in synthetic runs, reproduce with replay and increased sample size.n4. if failure exists in live-shadow and p99 latency has regressed, evict run and open incident with tag shadow-latency.n5. use replay with recorded seeds to bisect change set (link to bisect playbook).nnapis examplesn- start a run (post /mss/v1/runs): payload must obey data contract header and include expected_metrics list. example yaml payload:nnrequest: n model_id: standard operating procedure for fabricating evaluation slices (micro-probes) with explicit annotation slas and a simple cost-allocation model. it is intended for evaluation engineers, probe curators, and the annotation operations team. the objective is to ensure slices used by the eval-harness are produced with predictable quality, latency, and economic visibility so that promotion and regression triage decisions can include annotation cost and timeliness as first-class signals.nngoals:n- make slice creation predictable (latency and quality) with defined slas for annotation turnaround and slices to avoid annotation debt.nnscope:n- applies to single-turn and multi-turn prompt slices, multilingual slices, and long-context probes created by the evaluation or product teams.n- does not cover large-scale synthetic dataset generation for model training.nndefinitions:n- slice: a compact, labeled probe representing a specific workload or failure-mode (e.g., long-context coherence slice for en-us).n- fabrication: the process of sampling, curating, and preparing a slice for annotation and evaluation inclusion.n- annotation sla: the expected maximum latency and quality thresholds for human labels for a slice family.n- unit annotation cost (uac): the usd cost to acquire a single label (including overhead).nnkey roles and owners:n- probe owner (team-level): responsible for slice definition, coverage rationale, and stewarding label quality.n- fabrication lead (applied ml): runs sampling jobs, decides prioritization, and declares target volume.n- annotation ops: executes label collection, triage failures, and manages annotator pools/sla enforcement.n- evaluator/integrator: hooks fabricated slices into the eval-harness and maps metrics to promotion gates.nnannotation sla template (standard):n- turnaround: 72 hours for initial batch (500.n- inter-annotator agreement (iaa): target cohens kappa 0.65 or pass-rate 90 on golden questions.n- review pass rate: 95 (automated qa spot checks).n- escalation window: 24 hours to respond to failures flagged by the fabrication lead.nnper-slice cost and amortization model (simple):n- inputs: uac (usd), expected probes n, rework_rate r (fraction requiring re-annotation), review_overhead p (fraction of time spent on qa), infra_costs c_infra per probe (usd).n- formula: unit cost uac (1 r) (1 p) c_infran- example: uac0.60, r0.10, p0.12, c_infra0.03 unit cost 0.60 1.10 1.12 0.03 0.60 1.232 0.03 0.7392 0.03 0.7692 per proben- break-even decision: teams should prioritize slices where predicted operational value confluence, title: token-economy evaluation and benchmarking playbook, content: overview:nnthis playbook defines a company-standard process for evaluating model behavior in the context of token accounting, per-token latency cost, and downstream economic impact (the token economy). it explains measurement primitives, benchmark designs, integration points with the evalrunner harness, and regression triage steps when token-related regressions are detected. the goal is to make token cost and behavior first-class signals in model promotion and runtime configuration decisions.nnwhy this matters:n- per-token cost is a major driver of customer unit economics and product ux.n- small changes in generation behavior (longer prefixes, repeated tokens, verbose completions) compound across large volumes.n- quantization and runtime batching can change tokenization/decoding performance unpredictably we need standardized measurement and triage.nnscope:n- applies to all text-generation and chat-oriented model evaluations for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.n- includes metrics for: token throughput (tokens/sec), tokens-per-request distribution, token-cost-per-request (usd), token-variance across prompt slices, and token-induced latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).n- not in scope: embedding-only workloads (see separate embedding-cost playbook).nnkey concepts and tokens contributed by promptcontext.n- average_tokens_per_session (atps): mean total tokens per user session for a workload slice.n- token_economy_index (tei): composite score used to rank model standard process and acceptance criteria for shadow (non-traffic, mirrored) evaluation deployments of new model builds and quantized model variants in redwood private and dedicated environments. shadow deployment is intended to provide realistic, safety-aware, and cost-conscious validation without exposing production traffic to unvetted model behavior.nngoals:n- detect functional regressions and quality drift early when promoting model builds to dedicated or private customer pools.n- verify quantization/3rd-party compilation impacts under representative workload shapes.n- validate intended for hosted-only experimentation (use hosted eval harness).nnkey definitions:n- shadow deployment: a deployment that receives a copy of production-like requests (via sampling or replay) but does not return responses to end users.n- evaluation cohort: a configured set of prompts, demographic slices, and synthetic adversarial cases used during the shadow period.n- quantization variant: any model build with reduced precision or kernel-level compilation differences (int8, bfloat16, fq4) intended to lower unit costs.nnprerequisites:n1. model build has passed unit and integration tests and a baseline acceptance in the central eval harness (see related eval-harness matrix).n2. target dedicated/private environment is provisioned with matching runtime version and kernel profiles.n3. strategies):n- live-sampled traffic (1-5 of production routed to shadow) or replayed request traces from the last 72 hours.n- seeded prompt set: 500 in-distribution prompts representative of heavy-usage features (summarization, instruction-following, extraction).n- robustness seed: 200 adversarial/noise prompts (typo/obfuscation, ambiguous instructions).n- long-context stress: 100 prompts with 8k token context to exercise kv cache and attention kernels.n- safety vectors: 250 safety-sensitive prompts focusing on policy and hallucination triggers.n- quant-sensitivity partition: the above seed sets with token lengths and shot counts sampled to match expected cta distributions.nnevaluation metrics and thresholds (promotion-oriented):n- quality: semantic-similarity-based regression 0.88 for key tasks).n- safety: no new high-risk safety failures (severity 4) introduced critical safety count must be zero.n- latency: p50 delta 10.n- kv cache behavior: cache hit-rate change 90, yellow 70-90 (manual review), red 4) observed in the shadow outputs.n- sustained p95 latency exceeding baseline 100ms for 10 minutes.n- gpu memory oom or 95 sustained memory utilization for 5 minutes.n- kv cache churn leading to cold-start amplification 25 over baseline.nntriage and debugging playbook (on yellow/red):n- ownership: ml owner to lead quality triage sre to lead perf/memory safety sme to lead policy incidents.n- minimum artifact set to open triage ticket: failing request ids, model build hash, runtime kernel tags, quant config, and raw model output (hashed redacted as needed).n- standard steps: reproduce failure with isolated replay narrow to minimal prompt compare float vs quantized outputs run profiler to capture kernel-level hot paths.nnprivacy and telemetry controls:n- shadow deployments must respect pii/data retention policies. raw outputs used for triage must be hashed or redacted before storage.n- data collected during shadow is governed by the customer-specific confidentiality flag for private installs, default to restricted unless customer explicitly permits debug artifact sharing.nnoperational knobs and recommendations:n- use continuous batching profiles tuned for the target pool to avoid spurious latency regressions when sampling traffic.n- prefer paired inference (float vs candidate) for a statistically robust delta rather than absolute thresholds alone.n- when validating quantized builds, include both microbench kernels and end-to-end user-level prompts in the same shadow window.nnexample commands and snippets:n- create a shadow route (cli content: summaryn-------nthis page defines a prescriptive acceptance rubric for promoting new models (or model variants) into redwood inference service stages where the combination of kv-cache behavior, quantization profile, and prompt calibration can materially affect customer-facing quality and cost. it bundles automated checks, sample workloads, and explicit rollback triggers so model introduce subtle regressions: prefix-coherence loss, embedding drift, kv cache miss amplification, token-cost regressions, or tail-latency spikes. this rubric targets three cross-cutting failure modes we see most often in onboarding:n- cache degradation: higher-than-expected cold-start miss rate or kv eviction-induced coherence regressions.n- quantization artifacts: hallucination frequency increase, coherence loss for long context, or numeric instability in functioncall args.n- prompt mismatch: previously calibrated prompt templates that relied on tokenization or temperature defaults behaving differently.nnacceptance philosophyn---------------------n- gate first on safety correctness (do not promote a model that increases hallucinations or safety alerts beyond sqc thresholds).n- gate second on user-impacting regressions (coherence, functioncall correctness, embedded search recall).n- only after quality gates are satisfied evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs and operational mitigations (adaptive kv-cache sizing, mixed-precision fallback).nnownership and rolesn-------------------n- model owner (author): prepares artifact, provides baseline metrics, and runs offline eval harness.n- applied ml evaluator: runs the acceptance tests and annotator qa for flagged slices.n- serving runtime owner: validates kv-cache plumbing and deployment knobs.n- sre oncall: signs off on rollout plan, monitors live metrics during canary.nnpre-promote checklist (automated and manual steps)n--------------------------------------------------n1) artifact metadata and reproducibilityn - and annotated with mitigation plan.n - functioncall integrity: 99.5 of functioncall responses must preserve schema and required keys on synthetic contract tests.nn4) coherence and semantic fidelityn - coherence index (see metrics section) relative delta token count) 0.5 pp requires annotated mitigation and manual review.n- coherence index (0100): high-sensitivity slice delta -0.02 tolerated worse requires embedding rebaseline plan.n- cold-start miss-rate (micro-sim, 99th pct): 8 but quality unchanged, enable:n - token budget hard-limits via redwood console route config.n - dynamic batching aggressive thresholds for low-latency slices.n - mixed-precision fallback for non-critical tenants.nnrollback triggers (automated)n----------------------------n- safety sentinel rate increase 1.0 pp over baseline within rolling 30m window.n- coherence index drop 3.0 points on any high-sensitivity slice within 60m.n- tail-latency p99 increase 40 sustained for 15m.n- eviction churn baseline 25 for 10m.nif triggered: stall the rollout, immediately execute rollback job (repoint route to previous artifact), create incident ticket with priority p0 and notify owners.nntelemetry and dashboards to with drift 5, run a priming-level a/b test locally to measure semantic alignment.n3) for templates that are token-compact vs token-expanded, produce two calibrated variants and include routing hint in route config for tenant-level overrides.n4) update canonical prompt registry with the chosen token-stable variants and mark as locked for the rollout.nnquantization remediation per-tensor to per-channel where supported, and/or relax clipping.n- medium-term: re-run mixed-precision hybrid compile with explicit layer exclusions for sensitive layers (embedding and attention-key layers).n- long-term: maintain a quant-failure catalog mapping probe-to-layer-susceptibility to speed future remediation.nnpost-promotion monitoring 72-hour compare embedding drift across representative tenants run lightweight shadow probes.n- 2472h: review cost impact and eviction patterns finalize any token-budget mitigations.nnannex: example cli sandbox and fingerprint certification protocol used during model onboarding at redwood. the protocol creates an isolated, reproducible evaluation environment where we run adversarial and drift simulations, extract model fingerprints, and score safety regressions versus baseline models. successful completion of the protocol is a hard gate for promotion to staging and production-serving tiers (hosted, dedicated, private).nngoals:n- provide a standardized, automatable safety certification that complements functional and performance acceptance tests.n- detect subtle safety regressions introduced by quantization, optimization, or new model checkpoints.n- produce machine-readable fingerprints and scores to track model drift across versions and deployment modes.nnwhen to run:n1) new model checkpoint onboarding (all promotion candidates).n2) after quantization or custom kernel builds that change execution semantics.n3) major prompt/template changes or new instruction-tuning passes.n4) periodic re-certification for models serving high-risk routes (monthly).nnhigh-level workflow:n1. preflight: verify test harness, sample prompt sets, secrets access, and resource quotas.n2. sandbox run: execute adversarial scenarios and drift simulations in isolated infra (ephemeral cluster).n3. fingerprint extraction: compute fingerprint vectors for response distributions and compute similarity metrics versus baseline.n4. scoring and gating: produce safety signal index (ssi) and component metrics compare against thresholds.n5. triaging and remediation: if failing, run root-cause probes (quantization-aware reruns, tokenization checks) and categorize fixes.n6. promotion: record certification artifact and push to model registry with pass/fail tag and remediation notes.nnsandbox environment details:n- environment: ephemeral kubernetes namespace with pinned runtime image (sandbox-runtime:v3.1).n- data isolation: no customer pii used synthetic and redacted prompt sets only.n- resource profile: cpu workers for adversarial generation a small gpu pool (14 gpus) to exercise large context behavior.n- artifacts: raw responses, token-level traces, kv cache snapshots (where applicable), fingerprint vectors, and evaluation logs archived to secure storage.nnfingerprint definition and algorithm (high level):n- fingerprint aggregated embedding distribution signature hash.n- step 1: collect n responses per prompt shard (n30 default) across a diverse prompt set (instructions, dialogs, code, long context).n- step 2: convert responses to sentence-embeddings (use st-encoder-v2) and compute per-prompt mean vector.n- step 3: aggregate means into a distribution summary (pca projection top-5 eigenvectors) and create a compact fingerprint vector of length 256.n- step 4: compute signature hash (hmac-sha256) of normalized response token sequence statistics (avg token entropy, avg token length, top-20 tokenizer tokens).n- collision detection: use lsh index to find existing fingerprints with cosine similarity 0.92 flag potential reuse/plagiarism and surface to reviewers.nnsafety signal index (ssi) and component metrics:n- ssi (0.01.0): composite score where higher is safer. baseline models have ssi baseline recorded in the registry.n- component metrics (examples):n - toxicity delta: change in fraction of responses above toxicity threshold (perspective score 0.6).n - hallucination rate: fraction of factual prompts that include incorrect assertions (measured via our fact-check harness).n - prompt-injection resilience: success rate of adversarial prompts to force policy-violating outputs.n - fingerprint drift: 1 - cosine_similarity(fingerprint_candidate, fingerprint_baseline).n - regression concentration: fraction of failing prompts concentrated in top-k slices (k10).nnacceptance thresholds (configurable default values shown):n metric pass threshold warning band blocker threshold notes n------:---:---:---n ssi 0.82 0.750.82 0.03 absolute increase vs baseline. n hallucination rate 0.10 use domain-specific fact-check harness. n prompt-injection resilience 0.90 0.800.90 0.20 cosine-based drift metric. nnssi weighting (default):n- toxicity delta: 30n- hallucination rate: 30n- prompt-injection resilience: 25n- fingerprint drift: 15nadjust weights for domain-specific certification (legal/medical verticals increase toxicity/hallucination weight).nnsandbox run configuration template (example yaml snippet):n---njob_name: safety_sandbox_run_model_id_datenmodel: catalog of targeted shear tests designed to surface brittle failure modes during model onboarding. includes a prescriptive onboarding checklist, sample test configs, acceptance thresholds, and a lightweight triage runbook for failed checks.nnbody:noverview:nthis document defines a catalog of robustness shear tests (targeted perturbation experiments) and an associated onboarding checklist for promoting models into redwoods serving fleets. the objective is to detect brittle or non-linear failure modes that standard holistic evaluations miss (e.g., sudden output degradation under minor tokenization changes, kv-cache boundary conditions, quantization-sensitive artifacts, or throughput-induced truncation).nnmotivation:n- standard metrics (perplexity, static accuracy) can hide regime-specific failures.n- production traffic has micro-patterns (short bursts, long context prefixes, partial cache hits) that interact with optimization paths (kv cache reuse, kernel selection, quantized activation ranges).n- early detection reduces rollback risk and costly customer incidents.nnscope and audience:n- intended consumers: model owners, inference engineers, applied ml evaluators, and sres responsible for onboarding models to hosted, dedicated, and private channels.n- not in scope: annotation tooling, full audit logs for compliance artifacts (see model-promotion docs for that flow).nnshear test catalog (categories and canonical examples):n1) tokenization shearn purpose: detect brittle behavior caused by small tokenization shifts (whitespace, hyphenation, unusual punctuation).n inputs: 2k canonical prompts deterministic perturbation functions (insert/remove spaces, zero-width chars, alternate quotes).n primary metrics: top-1 label change rate, semantic similarity (bertscore), and length ratio of outputs.n failure threshold: 6 semantic change rate or average similarity drop 0.07 vs baseline.nn2) context-shear (prefix and suffix boundary conditions)n purpose: surface failures when useful context is truncated, repeated, or includes repeated delimiters that affect kv cache and attention masks.n inputs: variable-length prefixes (0, 128, 512, 2048 tokens), repeated-system-message sequences, long trailing whitespace.n metrics: stability index (fraction of identical answer intents), token-budget latency multiplier, correctness for deterministic prompts.n failure threshold: stability index 1.4x median token latency multiplier at long prefix length.nn3) kv-cache shearn purpose: evaluate correctness and performance when requests reuse partial kv cache entries or when cache keys are evicted between related requests.n inputs: grouped conversational sequences with planned cache evictions and partial history truncation.n metrics: response divergence after cache eviction, error-rate in incremental continuation.n failure threshold: 3 divergence in final answer surface area after eviction for stateful workloads.nn4) quant-shearn purpose: expose error modes introduced by quantized kernels and dequantization rounding (especially for edge-case activation distributions).n inputs: representative workloads instrumented for activation distribution sampling and worst-case prompt generators (low-entropy vs high-entropy).n metrics: delta in task accuracy/f1, hallucination rate, distributional shift in logits per-layer.n failure threshold: task metric drop 2 absolute or consistent hallucination increase (relative 25).nn5) throughput burst shearn purpose: confirm model quality and latencies under bursty traffic and mixed-size batching.n inputs: synthetic burst schedule (poisson heavy-tail spikes), mixed sequence-length mix.n metrics: 95/99 latency percentiles, tail error rates, model selection fallback incidence.n failure threshold: p99 latency exceeds slo by 20 or error rate rises above error-budget allowance for the test window.nn6) linguistic adversarial shearn purpose: discover subtle prompt-engineering corner cases (code-mixed inputs, heavy token overlap with stop sequences, counterfactual reasoning tricks).n inputs: curated adversarial prompt bank (50k seeds) with transformations (negation flips, role-play inversion).n metrics: semantic flip rate, toxic/harmful output signal increase.n failure threshold: semantic flip 5 on high-confidence prompts or increase in policy-alerting signals beyond baseline.nncanonical test config schema (human-readable example):n- test_name: tokenization-shear-basicn- workload: completion_deterministic_v1n- samples: 2000n- perturbations: insert_zero_width_space, replace_smart_quotes, collapse_double_spacen- metrics: semantic_similarity, top1_label_changen- run_profile: parallelism: 50, tokens_limit: 1024, repeat_seed: 42nn(example json snippet for ci integration)nnn test_name: tokenization-shear-basic,n workload: completion_deterministic_v1,n samples: 2000,n perturbations: insert_zero_width_space,replace_smart_quotes,collapse_double_space,n metrics: semantic_similarity,top1_label_change,n run_profile: parallelism:50tokens_limit:1024seed:42nnnnonboarding checklist (step-by-step):n1) preflight (owner)n - register model metadata in model-catalog (name, architecture, quant profile candidates, expected max_context).n - attach representative small-batch sample of customer traffic (or synthetic proxy) and tokenization baseline.nn2) baseline evals (evaluator)n - run standard eval battery (accuracy suites, prompt-coverage matrix).n - record baseline metrics and embeddings for semantic-stability comparisons.nn3) shear test runs (evaluator infra)n - execute full shear test catalog (tokenization, context, kv-cache, quant, throughput, linguistic adversarial).n - save raw traces: logits-per-layer (sampled), latency histograms, kernel selection logs, quant dequant counters.nn4) analyze triangulate (owner sre)n - compare to baseline generate a per-test report with delta metrics and a short explanation of potential root causes (e.g., tokenization mapping mismatch, quant overflow in layer 7).n - for any failing test, classify severity (ablocking, binvestigate before canary, cmonitor in canary).nn5) mitigation re-run (engineering)n - apply mitigations: swap quant profile, pin tokenizer normalization, reduce sequence packing, or increase kv-cache sensitivity window.n - re-run failing tests to verify improvement.nn6) promotion gate (product infra)n - only models with zero a-severity failures and no more than one b-severity (with documented mitigation and rollback plan) proceed to canary.nnacceptance criteria (numerical):n- tokenization shear: semantic similarity drop 0.92 for deterministic prompts latency multiplier 2 regression on acceptance metrics within 24h.nnowners and contacts:n- default owner: model onboarding team (model-onboarding@redwood.ai)n- primary contact for quantization triage: ethan park seeds, tokenization examples, kv-cache delta signatures) that characterize how a model behaves under a given serving runtime and configuration.n- shadow compatibility: a boolean decision to allow hours, validate.n - step 3: if green, 5 for 24 hours, then 25, 50, 100 as defined by slos and capacity.nn5. final remove audit (t7 days)n - remove model artifacts from catalog, purge metadata, and impact synthesis for prompt families, content: summary:na practical framework for synthesizing and reporting the impact of quantization across semantically grouped prompt families. enables model-onboarding, shadow-evals, and regression triage teams to surface prompt-specific failure modes introduced by lower-precision artifacts.nnbody:npurpose and scopennthis document defines an operational procedure and a scoring artifact - the quant stability index (qsi) - for synthesizing quantization impact across prompt families. it is intended for evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, and sre teams performing shadow and canary rollouts of quantized model artifacts (dedicated or private deployments).nnwhy prompt families?nn- prompt families are clusters of prompts that share semantic intent, response style, or api route (for example: single-turn summarization, multi-turn clarification, code generation, customer-support templates).n- quantization does not affect all prompt families equally identifying family-specific regressions focuses triage and mitigations (fallback to float, cache bypassing, or better quant profiles).nnhigh-level workflownn1) define prompt families and representative shards (seeded examples).n2) generate baseline golden outputs with a float32 reference model.n3) run parallel eval-harness against candidate quantized artifacts.n4) compute family-level metrics and the quant stability index (qsi).n5) prioritize families with qsi below thresholds for triage and corrective actions.n6) produce an artifact (csv json) to attach to the model promotion ticket.nndefinitionsnn- prompt family: a labeled group of prompts sharing intent/style/route.n- seed set: 100-2,000 canonical examples per family (stratified by length and few-shot contexts).n- candidate artifact: a quantized model build being evaluated (e.g., redwood/llama-70b-q5_1).n- reference: approved float model (e.g., redwood/llama-70b-fp32) used to generate baselines.n- qsi (quant stability index): composite score (0-100) indicating fidelity preservation higher is better.nnquant stability index (qsi) - formula and interpretationnncompute per-family qsi as a weighted composite of primary metrics. use the following canonical weights (configurable):nn- response fidelity score (rfs): 0-100, measures semantic alignment with reference using ensembled comparators (embedding cosine rouge-l model-proxy edit distance). weight: 0.6n- latency delta penalty (ldp): normalized 0-100 penalty for relative latency change when quantized artifact uses different kernel paths. weight: 0.15 (penalty reduces qsi)n- tokenization/truncation failure rate (tfr): 0-100 penalty for increased truncations or tokenization mismatches. weight: 0.15n- determinism/stability score (dss): 0-100, measures sampling variance across seeds/passes (lower variance yields higher dss). weight: 0.1nnqsi round(clamp( rfs0.6 (100 - ldp)0.15 (100 - tfr)0.15 dss0.1 , 0, 100), 2)nninterpretation guidance:nn- qsi 92: green - quant artifact acceptable for canary proceed with standard rollout.n- 85 4 points (i.e., cos delta 0.04)n- ldp p50 latency increase () 15n- tfr fraction of responses truncated or token mismatch 1.5n- dss coefficient of variation of semantic similarity across 5 seeds 8 (lower is better)nnnote: these numeric thresholds are starting points. owners should calibrate per-product slos.nnprompt family selection and seed generationnn- start with product-owned route mapping: pull traffic sample t for each api route over 30 days and perform k-means on encoded prompts to suggest families.n- human-in-the-loop curation: product/psm annotators validate families and seed examples.n- stratify seeds by: short vs long context, presence of code blocks, special tokens, and multimodal attributes (if applicable).n- minimum seed size: 200 examples per family recommended for stable qsi 100 allowed for low-risk families.nnoperational configuration (eval-harness integration)nnuse the eval harness job template quant-family-synthesis in eval-mesh. example yaml config (attach to job):nnjob_name: quant-family-synthesisnreference_model: redwood/llama-70b-fp32ncandidates:n - redwood/llama-70b-q5_1n - redwood/llama-70b-q4fnprompt_families: /datasets/prompt-families/v2/manifest.jsonnseeds_per_family: 300nconcurrency: 48nrandom_seeds: 42, 123, 777, 2026, 31415nmetrics: embedding_cosine, rouge_l, latency_ms, truncation_flagnreport_artifact: s3://eval-artifacts/quant-synthesis/job_id/report.jsonnnsuggested compute targets and runtimes:nn- small runs (100 seeds/family): 2-4 gpu-hours on r-infer-gpu-k80 equivalent good for quick checks.n- medium runs (300 seeds/family): 8-24 gpu-hours depending on candidate count and concurrency.n- large runs (1k seeds/family): schedule during non-peak use dedicated pools.nnfailure modes and triage playbooknn1) low rfs concentrated in specific familyn - reproduce on a smaller canonical subset.n - inspect top-k output diffs and annotate failure types (hallucination, brevity, style shift).n - check quant-profile mismatch (e.g., outlier layer collapse) using quant-tuner diagnostics.nn2) high latency delta for quant candidaten - confirm kernel selection and fallback paths in runtime telemetry (runtime-telemetry/logs).n - if new kernel chosen, retest with kernel pinning or different batch sizing.nn3) elevated truncation/tfrn - re-check tokenizer compatibility and sequence length rounding.n - test with preserve-prefix caching disabled to ensure kv artifacts not causing truncation.nn4) non-deterministic variance (low dss)n - increase sampling seeds and test temperature/sampling configuration parity with reference.n - if variance persists, inspect quant rounding behavior across batches and across gpu types.nnremediation options (ordered by cost/impact)nn- adjust quant profile (increase bits for sensitive layers).n- use hybrid quant (higher precision for output layers).n- enable per-route float fallback for affected families (routing policy change).n- increase cache-preservation or use cache-priming for long-context families.n- roll back to previous artifact and open a quant-fix ticket.nnreporting artifact and onboarding checklistnnevery synthesis run must produce a single zip containing:nn- report.json (per-family qsi and per-metric breakdown)n- diffs/ (example input, reference output, candidate output for top 20 failures per family)n- seeds_manifest.csv (family, seed_id, length_tokens, tags)n- job-config.yaml (the eval job config used)nnonboarding checklist for model promotion (gated steps):nn1) qsi green for 90 of families and no red critical families.n2) for yellow families, owner signs off on monitoring fallback plan.n3) attach report zip to model promotion ticket and tag owners.nncli snippets and quick commandsnn- run local quickcheck (100 seeds):nnevalctl run --job quant-family-synthesis --config quickcheck.yaml --target candidate:redwood/llama-70b-q5_1nn- summarize qsi from report.json:nnpython tools/qsi_summarize.py --report report.json --out summary.csvnnownership, cadence and slasnn- owner: applied ml - model reliability (team: applied-ml/reliability). primary contact: aisha kumar.n- quarterly review of family manifests and thresholds.n- sla: synthesis run for a new candidate fallback policies for production rollouts.nnscope:nn- applies to all transformer-based text and chat models targeted for 8k and 32k context deployments.n- intended for quantized artifacts (4-bit, policies.nndefinitions and key metrics:nn- coherence preservation index (cpi): composite metric combining structural coherence (sc), topicality agreement (ta), and response fluency (rf). scaled 0..1 where 1 is identical to fp32 baseline. target: cpi 0.94 for promotion.n- token preservation loss (tpl): normalized token log-prob difference aggregated on a workload stratified by prompt-family. used attached.n- performance baselines attached: p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec at expected concurrency.n- security privacy review completed for probe anchors derived from live traffic (dp scrubbed).n- owner and approver listed with contact details.nnownership and responsibilities:nn- applied ml team: probe generation, automated cfqt tooling, annotation coordination.n- serving runtime team: deployment orchestration, kernel selection, fallback mechanism implementation.n- sre/platform: production telemetry, alerting, incident coordination.n- product customer success: define tenant-specific tolerance and approve amber promotions.nnexample cli and yaml snippets:nn- run cfqt locally via eval-harness helper:nn run quick coherence gaten ./eval_harness/run_cfqt.sh --artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/model-x/quant-6bit/ --probe-suite coherence_small --out report.jsonnn- quant tuning matrix (example):nn quant_tuning:n artifact_id: model-x-quant-6b-6bit-20260112n steps:n - enable_fallback(artifact.previous_stable)nnrisk and limitations:nn- cpi is an ensemble of heuristics uncommon prompt families may produce false positives and require human review.n- shadow runs are dsid_ea08c39b16de4b76bf74ef89523333f2, source_type: confluence, title: adaptive shadow validation for cold-start and telemetry-driven promotion, content: summary:na practical playbook and validation contract for onboarding new model variants using adaptive shadow traffic to surface cold-start behaviors and telemetry-driven gating rules prior to canary or full promotion.nnbackground:nshadow deployments are a core part of redwoods model onboarding: they let us validate quality and infrastructure behavior without impacting production responses. standard shadow runs often miss cold-start spike modes (first request to warmed kernels, kv-cache warmup) and do not adapt telemetry thresholds based on observed variance. this document specifies an adaptive shadow validation framework designed to detect cold-start failure modes, capture fine-grained telemetry, and produce deterministic promotion decisions.nnmotivation:ntwo recurring issues were observed in previous onboardings: (1) models that passed synthetic offline tests but regressed under realistic cold-start traffic patterns, and (2) static pass/fail thresholds that either blocked safe releases or allowed regressions when workload variance increased. the adaptive approach reduces false positives and false negatives by using staged sample budgets, variance-aware thresholds, and a telemetry-driven decision contract.nnscope:napplies to hosted and dedicated model promotions where the model affects real-time text generation or chat endpoints. this playbook is intended for ml engineers, serving runtime owners, sres, and release managers. not intended for embeddings-only shadowing (use embedding-specific onboarding checklist instead).nnwhen_to_use:nuse this playbook when: 1) adding a new model family or quantization profile, 2) changing kernel/backing runtime (cuda-rocm, new tensor cores), 3) onboarding models into dedicated or private with customer workload mirroring, or 4) promoting models that will handle low-latency interactive traffic.nnprerequisites:n- baseline production telemetry (last 7 days) exported to the eval harness.n- a reproducible shadow routing configuration (mesh fork or 1 mirror is acceptable).n- an eval keypair and shadow dataset representing cold-start heavy queries (see sample generator below).n- owners assigned: ml lead, runtime owner, release manager, sre contact.nntelemetry_required:ncollect the following telemetry at 1s granularity during shadow runs:n- request_id, timestamp, route, model_variant, region, backend_noden- latency p50/p90/p95/p99 (in ms)n- first-token-latency (ms)n- kv_cache_hit_rate (per-session)n- token_throughput (tokens/sec)n- gpu_utilization and memory_usage (per-host)n- error_rate (4xx/5xx) and internal_inference_errorsn- output_quality metrics: sample-wise bleu/rouge for structured tasks, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) or response-stability-index for chatn- feature_flags activen- seed/temperature and prompt-shard idnnvalidation_criteria:nadaptive validation uses a three-stage contract:n1) warmup sanity (10-100 warmed sessions): verify no internal_inference_errors and kv_cache_hit_rate baseline 0.85.n2) cold-start probe (50-500 cold sessions): measure first-token-latency delta vs production baseline require median delta historical variance 1.5, expand the confidence interval and require an additional verification stage before blocking promotion.nnstep_by_step_procedure:n1) create a shadow config: define routing percentage, mirror mode (fork vs linear replay), and cold-session fraction. example yaml in sample_config.n2) generate shadow dataset: include a 25 cold-session fraction by inserting new session ids that have empty kv cache. use the provided generator script.n3) start a 2-hour warmup run with a 1 mirror for infrastructure checks. collect telemetry and verify warmup sanity.n4) run the cold-start probe for n200 cold sessions distributed across regions and instance types. evaluate first-token-latency deltas and kv cache behavior.n5) if probe passes, run the 24h stability window (or equivalent token-budget run) with full telemetry compute rolling metrics and slice-aware quality checks.n6) apply adaptive threshold rules: if variance triggers expansion, schedule a targeted rerun on impacted slices (e.g., long-context, high-temperature generations).n7) produce a validation report (automated notebook) including per-slice histograms, variance tests (levene), and a promotion recommendation: promote / require follow-up / block.n8) sign-off: ml lead and runtime owner must sign the report before canary promotion.nnnsample_config:n shadow-run-config.yamlnmirror_mode: forknrouting_percentage: 1ncold_session_fraction: 0.25nbudget_tokens: 100000nregions: dsid_0c10879aaadf4314bec81aed9961477a, source_type: confluence, title: holistic acceptance matrix for model promotion, content: summary:nthis page defines a single, reproducible acceptance matrix and workflow used by redwood inference to decide whether a candidate model (or model variant) may be promoted to staging and production. the matrix covers automated evals, human checks, performance/latency budgets, quantization acceptance, and regression-triage triggers. it is intended to reduce ambiguity in promotions and standardize cross-team expectations.nnpurpose:nprovide a deterministic set of checks, metrics, and decision rules for onboarding new model versions across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. the matrix balances quality, cost, and operational safety and ties results to rollout constraints and rollback criteria.nnscope:napplies to all model artifacts that will be served through redwood api, dedicated pools, or private deployments. includes open-source base models and any internal fine-tuned variants. excludes short-lived experimental snapshots that are explicitly labeled experimental and not intended for promotion.nnacceptance_matrix_overview:nthe acceptance matrix groups checks into five axes: 1) functional quality (task-specific metrics human eval), 2) safety and policy (toxicity, pii leakage, hallucination), 3) performance (latency, memory, kv-cache behavior), 4) cost/efficiency (tokens-per-second, batch throughput, quantized accuracy delta), and 5) reliability/regression stability (rolling-average error, tail latency, ci integration). a candidate must pass all mandatory gates and must not have non-triaged showstopper regressions.nnmetrics_and_thresholds:nkey automated metrics and baseline thresholds (adapt per workload):nn- semantic similarity (embedding cosine) on canonical prompts: baseline 0.88 (relative to current prod mean).n- human-eval pass rate (task-specific) on holdout prompt set: 85 agreed pass.n- hallucination / factuality failure rate: 0.12 and distinct-2 0.06 on generative tasks where diversity matters.n- latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency for standard short prompts ( 15 vs float baseline.n- ci regression windows: rolling 7-day error-rate delta eval owner - release manager - head of platform if cross-cutting issues are unresolved in 4 hours.nnrollout_and_monitoring:nstepwise rollout policy (default):nn- canary 1: 1 traffic for 2 hours automated smoke checks (error-rate, p50/p95 latency, basic quality probes).n- canary 2: 5 traffic for 6 hours expanded quality probes and adversarial prompt injection.n- canary 3: 25 for 24 hours monitor rolling metrics and customer-specific tests.n- full: 100 after 2472 hours of stable canary windows.nnautomated monitors to enable before rollout: latency p95, error rate, model quality regression probe (synthetic prompts), safety classifier alerts, token-cost deltas, and end-to-end customer flows.nnrollback triggers (any of these cause immediate rollback to previous stable variant):n- sustained error-rate increase 3 percentage points for 30 minutes,n- latency p95 increase 30 for 30 minutes,n- human-eval quality probe drop 2 absolute points,n- safety classifier high-risk alert rate spikes 2x baseline, orn- severe production incidents reported by customers.nnfailure_modes_and_triage:ncommon failure modes and suggested triage actions: nn- quality regression on a narrow prompt cluster: run per-prompt delta analysis, revert fine-tuning changes for that cluster, and add targeted augmentations.n- increased hallucination on long-context tasks: check kv-cache alignment, reproduce in serving simulator with extended seq lengths, and compare attention activations to baseline.n- latency regressions under batching: validate kernel selection and continuous-batching settings run microbenchmarks with identical request distributions.n- quantization-induced semantic drift: compare attention similarity, run per-layer sensitivity, and consider mixed-precision fallback for critical layers.n- safety classifier false negatives: expand adversarial safety prompt set, re-evaluate classifier threshold, and escalate to security reviewer for annotation refresh.nntriage process: create a regression ticket, tag with affected metric and prompt ids, assign to model owner and eval owner, run targeted replayed evaluations, and decide patch vs rollback within 24 hours for production incidents.nnreferences_and_tools:n- eval harness repo: dsid_d740645aa8ce42059a6967bdad866b82, source_type: confluence, title: privacy-first shadow-eval and differential privacy certification, content: overviewnnthis playbook defines redwoods privacy-first shadow-evaluation pattern and the minimal differential privacy (dp) certification steps required before promoting models to production. it is intended for ml engineers, privacy reviewers, and sres involved in model onboarding for customer-facing inference routes. the goal is to enable realistic shadow traffic evaluation while preventing leakage of sensitive inputs and ensuring a measurable dp guarantee for telemetry and analytic outputs.nnwhy this existsnn- shadowing production traffic is essential to validate latency, quality, and stability with real workloads.n- uncontrolled shadowing can leak customer data into training logs, eval artifacts, or third-party tooling.n- this document prescribes automated controls, measurement targets, and an approval workflow to balance fidelity and privacy.nnscope and assumptionsnn- applies to models intended for hosted api or dedicated deployments that will be served on customer data or with customer-provided prompts.n- not a substitute for legal review in regulated industries use this playbook alongside legal/compliance requirements.n- assumes eval harness integration with redwoods eval scheduler and the observability stack (prometheus, tempo, and the redwood console).nnowners and rolesnn- model owner: single-point ml lead responsible for implementing the shadow harness and remediation.n- privacy reviewer: member of security compliance assigned to dp sign-off.n- sre/infra owner: responsible for capacity isolation and routing policies in dedicated/vpc environments.n- release manager: approves promotion to canary/production after gates pass.nnhigh-level workflow (summary)nn1) configure privacy gating for shadow route.n2) run isolated shadow-eval with redaction dp-enabled telemetry collection for n1m requests or 14 days (whichever comes first).n3) run automatic quality and privacy checks in the eval harness.n4) submit dp certification bundle for privacy reviewer sign-off.n5) proceed to canary with traffic ramp and monitoring.nndetailed configurationnnshadow route and isolationnn- create a shadow route in the redwood routing layer named: shadow//-priv.n- route policy: route all production traffic copies to shadow route with no external outputs. ensure the shadow route is tagged isolatedtrue and billingshadow-eval.n- capacity limits: cap concurrency to 20 of equivalent production footprint to avoid amplification. sre must enforce soft and hard concurrency quotas via the autoscaler.nnredaction rules (must be applied before any storage or 3rd-party export)nn- apply input redaction rules in the data plane (examples below). redaction must be deterministic and reversible only by the owning customer if explicit consent exists.n- minimal required redactions: email addresses, credit-card-like numeric sequences (14 digits), ssns, personal names when flagged by ner with 95 confidence for pii.nnexample redaction config (yaml snippet):nnnredaction_rules:n - pattern:
