hash_salt: env:shadow_eval_saltnnndifferential privacy telemetry policynn- all telemetry derived from shadow traffic (metrics, embeddings, gradients, token-logs) must be collected under a dp mechanism prior to being persisted or exported.n- target dp parameters: epsilon 5 absolute on service-critical metrics compared to baseline model (baseline defined in the models onboarding issue).n- latency gate: p95 99.9 coverage of configured pii patterns on sampled dataset.nn- if any gate fails, follow the regression and remediation steps below.nnregression and remediationnn1) owner triages failing tests and classifies as: false positive (audit tuning), implementation bug (redaction or dp exporter), or model-induced leakage (model outputs pii).n2) for implementation bugs: patch and re-run content: summarynnthis document specifies the live probe harness and feedback ingest pipeline used to collect, transform, and surface targeted production probes for model onboarding, continuous evals, and regression detection. the harness balances three priorities: (1) safe, privacy-preserving capture of representative real-world prompts (2) rich telemetry and annotation plumbing for automated triage and human review (3) deterministic routing into eval, retraining, and rollback workflows.nngoalsnn- provide a low-friction mechanism to collect small, labeled probe samples from live traffic without impacting customer request latency or privacy guarantees.n- enable automated tagging and scoring of probes for: quality regressions, quantization sensitivity, function-call/structured-output stability, and latency-cost profiling.n- ensure probes can be replayed deterministically across model variants and quantization profiles in the eval harness.nnscope and non-goalsnn- in scope: probe capture sampling rules, ingestion schema, basic enrichment (metadata, anonymization), downstream routing (storage, eval queue, labeler), and slos for pipeline availability and freshness.n- out of scope: labelling ui ux design, long-term annotation storage beyond retention window (see data retention), and ml model training pipelines (those consume outputs from this pipeline but are documented separately).nnterminologynn- probe: a single captured request/response example plus telemetry and anonymized context used for evaluation.n- probeset: a curated group of probes assigned to an eval campaign or model onboarding job.n- ingest agent: lightweight capture component running in the request path (hosted or private) that emits probe events.nnarchitecture overviewnn1) ingest agents: deployed as a sidecar/edge filter within the request path. agents sample requests according to policy, redact pii client-side, and emit compact probe events to the ingest bus.n2) ingest bus (kafka / pubsub): durable, ordered buffer. events are partitioned by customer_id and model_family to support deterministic replay.n3) enrichment and privacy stage: stream processors that apply static enrichment (token counts, language detection, conversation-turn mapping), pii scrubbing (regex, model-based redaction), and differential-privacy noise injection for customer-sensitive fields when required.n4) classification and routing: deduplication, heuristic tagging (latency outlier, function-call, multi-turn), quality-scorer (fast ml model), then route to one or more sinks: eval queue, probe lake (s3 bucket for long-ish retention), or immediate alerting for severe failures.n5) eval harness integration: probes routed to eval queue are materialized into deterministic jobs (seeded rng, fixed tokenizer) for cross-model replay and scoring.nnprobe lifecycle (high level)nn1. capture: ingest agent captures request and response snapshot (configurable sample rate, default 0.1 of requests).n2. local redaction: agent applies pii redaction rules and annotates redaction level.n3. emit: event pushed to ingest bus with minimal payload (see schema).n4. enrich: stream jobs add telemetry and quality signals.n5. route: classifier decides sink(s).n4. consume: eval harness or labeler consumes event and produces labels/metrics.nnsampling and capture policiesnn- default global sampling: 0.1 uniform across requests.n- adaptive sampling: increase for new/under-evaluated prompt clusters, error responses (http 5xx), rate-limited token spikes (response tokens 2048), or flagged feature usage (function-call).n- customer opt-out: honor per-customer privacy flags. agents must not capture when customer config disables live probes.nningest event schema (compact json example)nnjsonnn probe_id: uuid-v4,n captured_at: 2026-03-05t14:22:10z,n customer_id_hash: sha256:xxxxx,n model_family: gptx-8k,n prompt_tokens: 42,n response_tokens: 128,n lang: en,n redaction_level: pii-scrubbed,n latency_ms: 132,n 200,n metadata: route:chat-completion,feature_flags:function_call,n payload_ref: s3://probe-lake/2026/03/05/probe-uuid.jsonnnnnnote: for this confluence doc we show payload_ref rather than embedding full text to limit bus bandwidth. the payload stored in probe lake is encrypted and access-controlled.nnprivacy and safety controlsnn- pii redaction: on-agent regex model heuristics. redaction policy documented separately in privacy-playbook.n- customer opt-out: honor explicit per-customer settings default is opt-in for accounts created after 2025-06-01.n- dp noise: for high-sensitivity customers tagging, the enrichment stage can apply laplace noise to numeric telemetry fields when flagged.n- access controls: rbac enforced for probe lake (read restricted to sre/applied ml/product with justification).nnslos and metricsnn- ingest availability: 99.95 monthly.n- end-to-end freshness (capture - eval queue readiness): p99 2048 or high perplexity).n2. offline eval jobs replay probes across: baseline model, candidate model, quantized variant(s). comparison outputs are stored and scored by automated metrics: semantic-similarity, prefix-consistency, function-call fidelity, hallucination score.n3. if automated pass, probe set moves to a human labeling batch for edge-case review.n4. pass/fail gates feed into a promotion decision: green promote variant to canary amber create targeted retrain or prompt-rewrite red reject.nnoperational playbook (fast triage steps)nn1. alert: probe.enrich.failure spike or pipeline.latency.p99 breach.n2. page on-call for ingest pipeline.n3. run diagnostics: check ingest bus consumer lags, inspect last successful offset, run sample enrichment job locally against sample payload_ref.n4. if corruption found in payloads, isolate offending partition and trigger synthetic replays.n5. if pii redaction failure rate increased, suspend live capture (flip config flag) and notify privacy on-call.nnexample cli recipesnn- re-run enrichment for a batch of probes:nnbashnprobe-tool reprocess --from 2026-03-01t00:00:00z --to 2026-03-01t01:00:00z --topic ingest-enrich --dry-runnnn- create probeset manifest for label schema: flat list of tags and numeric calibration scores. example fields: coherence: 0-1, hallucination: 0-1, function_call_correct: truefalsen/a, severity: p0p1p2p3.n- label provenance must include labeler_id, label_timestamp, and probe_snapshot_ref.nndata retention and accessnn- probe lake retention default: 90 days. business justification required for extensions.n- probe metadata in event store retained for 365 days.n- audit logs for access to probe lake retained for 1 year.nnfailure modes and mitigationsnn- upstream high-volume customer producing many probes: apply per-customer sampling caps and backpressure at ingest agent.n- enrichment pipeline consumer lag: autoscale consumers and open an investigation runbook that includes backlog replay steps.n- privacy regression (pii escapes): immediate suspend capture for affected clusters, initiate privacy incident playbook.nnownership and contactsnn- primary owner: applied ml probe infrastructure (team: applied-ml-probe).n- fidelity mismatch between shadow evals and runtime (quant, kv-cache, batching).n- we need a reproducible bridge that: (a) preserves safety quality slos, (b) automates conservative fallbacks, and (c) gives clear triage fast-paths for regressions.nnscopenthis playbook applies to: model onboarding for text and multimodal function-call services, any model variants with quantization profiles in our registry, and services that use the redwood eval-harness for shadowing. it is not prescriptive about exact quant kernels but standardizes the decision surface and operational controls.nnkey definitionsn- fidelity tier: label for runtime equivalence class (gold / near-gold / budgeted).n- quant-fallback: automatic runtime substitution to a higher-fidelity variant when safety/quality checks fail.n- shadow cohort: a controlled set of traffic mirrored to a candidate model during validation.nndesign principlesn- conservative promotion: require multi-signal pass (eval harness metrics shadow telemetry human review) before production route cutover.n- observable rollouts: every onboarding includes per-probe sli dashboards and an auto-fail policy.n- fast rollback: automated circuit that returns live traffic to last-known-good variant within 60s for critical slo breaks.nnonboarding checklist (step-by-step)n1. prepare assetsn - register model artifact in the model registry with explicit fidelity_tag and quant_profile_id.n - produce a prompt-set subset (min 500 probes for the service slice) covering core intents and long-tail slices (see prompt conditioning below).n2. shadow validation (27 days)n - launch in a 1025 shadow cohort via eval-harness shadower with telemetry capture (tokens, latency, functioncall integrity).n - run full eval suite: semantic fidelity, hallucination probes, tokenization edgecases, functioncall unit tests.n3. quant safety scann - execute the quant-safety suite (see quant safety table). candidate must meet per-slice fidelity thresholds.n4. human review gaten - product ml reviewer inspects top 200 divergent probes and signs off.n5. micro-canary (26 hours)n - canary to 0.52 live traffic with tight alerting.n6. gradual rolloutn - 2x per hour increases with stability checks until target weight.n7. post-promotion monitoringn - retain probe sampling, automatic regression scoring, and 24h annotated review.nneval-harness prioritized by slo risk (functioncall billing-critical ui-text).nnprompt set conditioning and localizationn- create a seed prompt family per service slice attach locality tags (lang, region, regulatory).n- for quant-sensitivity, generate a localized perturbation set: tokenization edgecases, truncated context, slot-value permutations.n- prompt mutation rules (applied during shadowing):n - deterministic augmentation: synonym substitution preserving slot types.n - stochastic noise: apply 13 char/word-level perturbations for robustness checks.n - context aging: test with prefix drop (25, 50) to emulate trimmed context.nnquant safety and fallback profiles (table)n profile id fidelity tier allowed kernels max expected token delta required pass rate fallback target actions or data corruption. an incremental probe-driven approach lets us exercise these surface areas under controlled load and detect regressions early.nnscopen-----n- applies to models used for dsid_d32ccb4332484e4b97af2f687a713045, source_type: confluence, title: contrastive probe assembly and sweeping guidelines, content: overviewnnthis guideline defines a contrastive, instrumented approach to assembling probe families and sweeping them through the eval mesh so we can detect subtle regressions, quantization sensitivity, and prompt coverage gaps before promoting model artifacts to production. it ties together probe fabrication, priority-led scheduling, quantization-aware sampling, and rapid regression triage hooks into a single operational playbook.nnwhen to use this documentnn- new model onboarding where prompt families are large or heterogeneousn- quantization or mixed-precision migration projects that require targeted sensitivity checksn- routine sweep windows expected outputs designed to exercise a behavior classn- conductor: the service that assembles and schedules probes (service name: probe-conductor)n- sweep: a single pass of a probe family across one or more model variants and runtime configurationsn- anchor set: small, stable sub-sample used as baseline for absolute deltasn- fidelity gate: a quantitative rule that must be satisfied before promotionnnprinciplesnn- contrast-first: always include at least one contrasting probe per family to expose symmetric failure modesn- telemetry-driven: scheduling and priority are driven by recent source_type: confluence, title: cohort-based embedding drift reconciliation playbook, content: summarynnthis playbook defines a repeatable, low-risk procedure to detect, triage, and reconcile embedding drift at the cohort level. it is targeted at product teams, ml infra, and sres who operate embedding services (search, semantic retrieval, recommendation) and want to maintain semantic parity across model, quantization, and data drift events.nnscope and motivationnn- scope: production embedding services (hosted dedicated) that provide vector embeddings to downstream search/recall pipelines.n- motivation: global drift signals can be noisy cohort-level monitoring isolates affected user segments and reduces false positives. reconciliation aims to restore utility (precision/recall, nearest-neighbor stability) with minimal user-facing regressions.nndefinitionsnn- cohort: a stable grouping of traffic by attributes (tenant, locale, client-version, feature-flag). cohorts must be defined in the cohort registry (see operational configurations).n- drift signal: a statistically significant change in embedding distribution or downstream retrieval performance relative to baseline.n- reconciliation: interventions to bring cohort behavior back within sla (can include prompt rewriting, model rollback, re-embedding, quant-profile change, or routing to fallback model).nndetection and alertingnn1) telemetry to collect per-request:n - embedding vector summary stats (l2 norm, mean, std)n - cosine similarity to pinned baselines and per-cohort centroidn - retrieval metrics: top-k precision@k, rerank delta, latency, token countn - cache hit ratio and kv-cache invalidation eventsnn2) aggregation cadence and windowing:n - primary aggregation: 15m windows for high-volume cohorts, 1h for low-volume.n - baseline comparison windows: 7d rolling baseline and 28d seasonal baseline.nn3) statistical tests and thresholds (configurable defaults):n - embedding distribution shift: wasserstein distance 0.12 and mean l2 change 0.08 warning.n - similarity shift: median cosine-to-centroid drop 0.06 warning.n - downstream signal: precision@10 drop 4 absolute critical.nn4) alerting rules:n - warning alert: any single metric breach on 2 consecutive windows.n - critical alert: any downstream precision or recall breach or three distinct metric classes breached in single window.n - alert destinations: cohort-owner slack channel, eval-oncall rotation, and incident ticket created in p1 queue.nncohort triage workflow (high level)nn1) triage intake (automated):n - auto-attach cohort telemetry snapshot (last 3 windows), baseline diffs, and representative probe queries to the incident ticket.nn2) initial human validation (520 min):n - owner verifies cohort definition and checks recent deploys, quantization promotions, routing changes, and data schema changes.n - if a deploy or quant promotion correlates to the first breach timestamp, tag the deploy-id and escalate to rollout lead.nn3) quick impact check (1545 min):n - run cohort smoke eval: sample n200 representative queries and compute precision@10, mrr, and embedding similarity distribution.n - if precision@10 drop 6 and reproduced locally, proceed to reconciliation plan.nnreconciliation plan (ordered by risk and time-to-restore)nnthe reconciliation plan provides a prioritized list of mitigations. always prefer low-risk, reversible actions first.nnlow-risk / fast (minutes):n- route cohort to warm fallback model (same architecture but previous model version) using routing policy: route 100 traffic for cohort to fallback.n- increase caching ttl and enable cohort-specific prefix caching to preserve previous embeddings while rollback is underway.n- apply prompt-layer (client-side) soft rewrite to reduce sensitive tokens known to cause representation shifts.nnmedium-risk / moderate (tens of minuteshours):n- quantization rollback: revert quant profile for cohort to previous profile and promote via canary rule for cohort traffic.n- re-embed a short tail of recent documents (select 4872h window) observed in the cohort with the baseline model.n- apply feature flag to use hybrid nearest-neighbor scoring (combine new embeddings score 0.7 persisted-score 0.3).nnhigh-risk / heavy (hoursdays):n- full model rollback for cohort (requires sla signoff).n- recompute corpus-wide embeddings for cohorted data and run data consistency verification pipeline.nnexample reconciliation decision matrix (text table)nn symptom immediate action escalation threshold confluence, title: experiment quality evals integration (route experiments), content: overviewnthis document defines how redwood attaches quality evaluation (eval) signals to route-level experiment variants and surfaces them as first-class metrics in console rollouts.nnthe goal is to make quality a measurable guardrail alongside latency, cost, and errors, without requiring customers to bring custom metrics in the initial release.nnthis design covers:n- how we generate and attribute eval score streams to route, experiment_id, variant_id.n- sampling and prompt-set execution strategy so variant comparisons are meaningful.n- score normalization so metrics are comparable across prompt sets and over time.n- quality regression guardrails (detection alerting optional auto-stop integration).nn goalsn1) provide an attributed, near-real-time quality score time series for each experiment variant.n2) enable guardrails for quality regressions with clear defaults, and make them configurable per experiment.n3) keep operational overhead bounded (compute cost, metric cardinality, and on-call burden).n4) ensure auditability and reproducibility: prompt sets, scorer versions, and normalization method must be recorded.nn non-goals (ga)n- a full statistical significance engine.n- customer-defined custom metric ingestion.n- cross-region population rebalancing beyond deterministic assignment.nn definitionsn- experiment variant: a named routing target in a route experiment (e.g., control, treatment-quantized).n- eval prompt set: a curated set of prompts used for automated quality scoring (redwood-managed for ga).n- quality score stream: a compact stream of scored eval results (scalar scores metadata) that can be aggregated by variant.n- normalization: converting raw scores into a comparable scale across prompt sets and scorer versions.nn high-level architecturenwe support two complementary signal paths:nna) online shadow eval sampling (near-real-time)n- sample a small fraction of production requests per variant.n- execute a lightweight eval scorer on the sampled request/response.n- emit per-sample eval events with experiment attribution.n- aggregate into variant-level quality metrics.nnb) offline prompt-set eval runs (batch / scheduled)n- run predefined prompt sets against each variants configured model/settings.n- score outputs using redwood eval harness.n- emit a compact score stream attributed to the experiment variant.n- aggregate to time-windowed quality metrics used by console.nnwe will ship ga with (b) as the primary supported signal, and (a) as an optional beta capability for select workloads where scoring is safe and low-latency.nn data contracts and attributionn canonical dimensionsnall eval events emitted for experiment quality must include:n- route_id (normalized template id not raw url path)n- experiment_idn- variant_idn- model_id (resolved model version actually served)n- regionn- eval_prompt_set_idn- eval_run_id (unique id for a batch run)n- eval_scorer_id eval_scorer_versionn- started_at, completed_atnnnotes:n- these match the attribution principles in adr-048. where cardinality risk exists, we keep route_id as a normalized route template identifier (e.g., route chat.completions.v1) rather than raw paths.n- for safety, we do not attach customer-provided prompt text to telemetry by default only hashed identifiers and aggregate metrics are stored unless the account opts in to eval trace retention (separate feature).nn event typesnwe use two event types emitted to telemetry ingestion:n1) eval.sample_scored (one row per scored prompt)n2) eval.run_summary (one row per eval run, contains aggregates and metadata)nnwe strongly prefer aggregating from eval.run_summary for console dashboards to limit cost/cardinality.nn prompt-set execution design (offline path)n when prompt sets runnfor each active experiment:n- on experiment start: run baseline prompt sets for all variants.n- during the experiment: run on a schedule (default every 6 hours).n- on variant config change (e.g., model version update): trigger a run for that variant.nndefault cadence is configurable per experiment, with bounds enforced by policy:n- minimum: every 2 hoursn- maximum: every 24 hoursnn what prompt sets runnprompt sets are selected by route type and model family:n- chat routes: instruction-following, refusal safety, structured extraction, summarization.n- embedding routes: retrieval relevance probes (where applicable).n- rerank routes: ranking consistency probes.nnat ga we will support redwood-managed prompt sets only, organized into suites. the suite is chosen automatically with an option to override:n- suite: general-chat-v1n- suite: extraction-json-v1n- suite: summarization-v1nn minimum sample sizeneach eval run must meet minimum prompt coverage per variant for the run to be considered valid:n- default: 200 prompts per suite per variantn- hard floor: 50 prompts per suite per variant (below this, console shows insufficient data)nnif the configured suite has fewer than 200 prompts, we execute the full suite and flag the run with run_qualitylow_sample_size.nn versioning and reproducibilityneach eval.run_summary includes:n- prompt_set_versionn- scorer_versionn- model_id (exact served model version)n- runtime_profile (e.g., quantization profile id)nnconsole must display these in the run details drawer for auditability.nn online sampling design (optional / beta)n sampling objectivenprovide near-real-time signals for fast-moving rollouts (especially guardrails) without waiting for scheduled prompt-set runs.nn sampling strategynwe apply deterministic sampling based on a stable key to avoid bias:n- sampling_key sha256(experiment_id variant_id sticky_key)n- include sample when sampling_key modulo 10,000 10,000 requests or 2 million prompt tokens in the lookback window.n- latency coverage: p50 and p95 latency available (server-side, end-to-end).n- traffic stability: at least 6 distinct hours with non-zero traffic (to avoid single-burst artifacts).nnif any are missing, do not emit suggestions return insufficient telemetry state to the console.nn data quality exclusions (hard)ndo not emit suggestions for a suggestion unit if:n- the route is in an incident/mitigation state (e.g., active rollback, elevated error rate) as signaled by platform incident flags.n- observability indicates telemetry corruption (e.g., missing model_id/model_version, negative durations, non-sensical token counts).n- the model_version is in canary/experimental state not intended for broad optimization (flagged by model lifecycle service).nn environment restrictions (hard)n- suggestions are generated only for production and pre-prod environments. do not generate for dev/sandbox where traffic is not representative.n- tenant isolation: suggestions must never aggregate across orgs/projects. (also applies to any caching recommendationssee security/privacy guardrails.)nn global safety guardrails (apply to all suggestions)n slo and route criticality (hard)ndo not emit any suggestions for a route if any of the following is true:n- the route has an explicit p95 latency slo 0.25, orn- timeout/cancel rate 0.5, orn- recent regression flag is active (latency or error slo burn within last 6 hours).nnrationale: optimization estimates assume steady-state behavior recommending changes during instability reduces trust and can worsen incident recovery.nn confidence gating (hard)nif the system cannot compute a confidence band (due to missing inputs, insufficient samples, or extreme variance), do not emit the suggestion.nnoperational rule:n- if confidence is unknown, block.n- if confidence is computed but below minimum threshold for the suggestion type (see below), block.nn change magnitude limits (hard)nsuggestions must remain within conservative bounds:n- never recommend a parameter change that exceeds 2 the current setting in a single step (e.g., max_batch_size from 8 32 is blocked must be staged).n- never recommend reducing max_batch_delay_ms below safe minimums (to avoid cpu churn / scheduling overhead):n - streaming routes: min 1 msn - non-streaming routes: min 2 msnnif a larger change is theoretically optimal, emit no suggestion in beta (we prefer no suggestion over unsafe guidance).nn rollout safety posture (soft copy deep link)nif a suggestion is emitted, the details drawer must include:n- a recommended rollout approach (canary and duration) and a link to rollouts tooling.n- a note that savings are estimates and not guaranteed.nn(ux enforcement is tracked in console design spec generation must provide the necessary fields: recommended_canary_percent, recommended_hold_minutes, and primary_risk_factors.)nn batching-specific guardrailsnbatching can materially improve cost/throughput, but it increases queueing and can amplify tail latency under bursty traffic.nn batching eligibility (hard)nemit batching suggestions only if all are true:n- concurrency/qps:n - average concurrency 4, andn - p50 qps 2 req/s over at least 6 hours in the lookback.n- batchability: tokenization and model execution path supports continuous batching for the model family (runtime capability flag).n- traffic shape: coefficient of variation (cv) of per-minute qps 3.0, orn- p95 total_tokens / p50 total_tokens 2.5nn queueing sensitivity (soft risk up-label)nif the route already shows queueing sensitivity, we may still emit a suggestion but must increase risk:n- if (p95 - p50) latency is large ( 400 ms) and gpu utilization is high ( 85) escalate risk by one level.nn multi-region and routing complexity (soft emit fewer suggestions)nif traffic is split across regions and the lookback window per-region is below volume minimums, do not emit region-specific batching suggestions.nnrule:n- require minimum telemetry per region for region-scoped suggestions otherwise block and fall back to global messaging (need more regional data).nn caching-specific guardrailsncaching is most effective when prompts share a stable prefix. incorrect scoping or oversubscription can create reliability issues.nn cache safety (hard) tenancy, privacy, and scopingncaching recommendations must respect the following invariants:n- cache keys must be scoped at minimum to: org_id project_id environment region route_id model_version.n- no cross-tenant cache sharing is allowed, including global caches.n- the platform must not store raw prompts in cache metadata. use hashed/normalized keys per runtime standard.nnif the runtime configuration for the target deployment cannot guarantee these properties (capability flag), block caching suggestions.nn caching eligibility (hard)nemit caching suggestions only if all are true:n- repeatability signal: estimated reusable-prefix rate 8 of prompt tokens (conservative threshold for beta).n- observed cache behavior:n - if cache is currently enabled: cache hit rate 15 with acceptable confidence.n- sufficient volume: same minimum volume as global prerequisites (do not relax).nn cache thrash and oom risk (hard)nblock caching increase capacity or enable caching suggestions if memory pressure is likely to cause instability:n- evictions per 1k requests 25 and cache memory usage is already 80 of allocated cache budget.n- any cache-related oom/eviction storm signal in the last 24 hours (platform reliability flag).nnin these cases, do not suggest turn it on more instead, emit no suggestion in beta (future work: remediation suggestions).nn latency regressions (hard)ncaching suggestions must not predict latency regressions above:n- p50 latency increase 0.7 qps (most prompts are unique).n- high entropy in the first n tokens (runtime-provided proxy metric).nnui requirement when this triggers:n- include this route has high prompt variability expected gains depend on stable prefixes (e.g., system prompt and templates).nn tool calling / function calling (soft generally safe)ntool calling often shares a stable system prefix caching can help, but request payloads may include volatile tool outputs.nnrule:n- do not use tool outputs as cache keys.n- treat tool outputs as part of the non-cacheable suffix do not assume reuse.nnif telemetry cannot separate prefix vs suffix reuse, block (confidence unknown).nn guardrails for estimate presentation (to preserve trust)nthese are generation-time constraints to avoid too-good-to-be-true outputs.nn savings caps (hard)nfor beta, cap displayed savings for any single suggestion unit:n- cost savings percentage: max 35n- /day savings: max 25,000/daynnif the raw model exceeds these caps, clamp and add a note in explanation: capped for conservatism in beta.nn assumptions disclosure (hard)nevery emitted suggestion must include the minimum assumption fields so the console can display a consistent disclaimer block:n- pricing_basis (token price version)n- lookback_window_hoursn- traffic_volume_summary (requests, tokens)n- stale_as_of timestampn- key drivers (e.g., concurrency, reusable-prefix rate)nnif any are missing, block the suggestion (avoid partial/opaque suggestions).nn known edge cases and how we handle themn 1) bursty traffic with periodic spikesnsymptom: batching looks great on averages but causes p95 blow-ups during spikes.n- current handling: block batching suggestions when qps cv 1.2 (hard).n- future: spike-aware modeling and separate peak-hour suggestions.nn 2) mixed workloads under one route (multiple prompt patterns)nsymptom: aggregates hide a low-latency sub-route.n- current handling: if telemetry indicates multi-modal latency distribution (bimodal p50/p95 across segments) and we cant segment, orchestration and ops playbook, content: overview:nthis playbook defines the design, orchestration, and operational procedures for synthetic sentinels lightweight, deterministic probe workloads used to continuously validate model behavior across quality, latency, and quantization boundary conditions. the document targets applied ml engineers, sres operating inference fleets, and product owners responsible for slas.nngoals:n- detect regression candidates earlier than customer-visible signals.n- provide deterministic, reproducible probes that exercise model prompts, function calls, and kv-cache-sensitive flows.n- tie sentinel failures to automated routing/fallback actions and alerting so incidents are actionable.nnscope:n- applies to hosted and dedicated model serving tiers.n- includes probes for: generation quality, function-call formatting, embedding drift, latency-tail, and quantized fallback validation.n- excludes full human-in-the-loop evaluations and long-run a/b experiments (see related pages).nnkey concepts:n- sentinel: a synthetic probe (single-turn or multi-turn) with an expected assertion (exact/patterned/metric threshold).n- assertion types: equality, semantic-similarity (embedding threshold), structural (json schema), and performance (p95/p99 latency).n- probe buckets: smoke, hourly-critical, daily-comprehensive.n- determinism tags: seed, tokenization-version, quant-profile-id, kernel-version.nndesign principles:n- prefer compact probes that isolate single failure modes (e.g., function argument serialization) over monolithic end-to-end prompts.n- label probes with a minimal context vector: workload, tenant-sensitivity, resource-profile.n- keep synthetic probes idempotent and stateless at the sidecar level.nnsynthetic sentinel types and examples:n1) format sentinel (function-call correctness)n- purpose: detect serialization/format drift that breaks downstream parsers.n- example assertion: response conforms to schema /user/profile (required fields: id:string, email:regex).n- probe example prompt (pseudocode):n input: get minimal user profile for idsynthetic-0001, include created_at in iso8601n assertion: json schema validation passes.nn2) coherence sentinel (generation stability)n- purpose: detect semantic regressions and hallucination spikes on anchor questions.n- assertion: embedding(response_anchor) cosine_sim 0.86 vs baseline.nn3) latency tail sentineln- purpose: capture p95/p99 regressions under typical prefix sizes.n- config: tokens_prefix128, tokens_generate64, expected_p95 200ms for 3 consecutive runs increase capacity / route to low-latency pool n quant-fallback 30m structure-diff 2 failover to fp16 variant ticket to quant team nnoperational orchestration architecture:n- sender: sentinel-runner service (k8s job sidecar) schedules probes according to cadence and tenant isolation.n- collector: sentinel-ingest pipeline (kafka topic: sentinel-events-v1) normalizes probe events, enriches telemetry, and stores artifacts in the sentinel-store (s3 prefix).n- evaluator: sentinel-evaluator (stateless service) applies assertions, computes deltas vs baseline, and emits alerts to pagerduty and alertmanager.n- feedback: failing sentinels automatically create issues in the regression-triage board with reproduction artifacts, golden baseline, and suggested blame hints.nnoperational runbook guideline documents how redwood evaluates, monitors, and promotes embedding model versions with a focus on representation stability, backwards compatibility, and the interaction between quantization and downstream retrieval/semantic search behavior. it applies to vector models used for search, deduplication, ranking features, and clustering.nnscope: applies to hosted, dedicated, and private procedures for embedding regressions.n- document experiment and offline eval harness steps to ensure parity across environments.nnkey definitionsnn- embedding drift: statistical shift in embedding-space relationships between two model variants measured on a representative probe set.n- representation fidelity: preservation of semantic neighbor relationships measured via recall@k and mean reciprocal rank (mrr).n- quantization delta: change in cosine similarity distributions introduced by weight/activation quantization measured per workload.nnrepresentative metrics and how to compute themnn1) pairwise similarity change (median and 90th percentile):n - for each probe vector x from baseline model m0 and candidate m1, compute cosine(m0(x), m1(x)). report median and 90p.n - python snippet:nn pythonn import numpy as npn from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similaritynn sims cosine_similarity(emb0, emb1).diagonal()n median np.median(sims)n p90 np.percentile(sims, 90)n nn2) retrieval fidelity (recall@k, mrr):n - use a representative retrieval workload (see probe sets section). query with the same prompts/documents against both models and measure recall@1/5/10 and mrr of ground-truth items.nn3) neighbor rank drift:n - for each item, compute the rank position of its top-k neighbors under m0 and m1. report the distribution of rank displacement.nn4) cluster stability (ari / silhouette change):n - when embeddings are used for clustering, compare adjusted rand index (ari) between cluster assignments from m0 and m1 on the probe corpus.nngating thresholds stratification: default n5,000 with stratified buckets: 50 high-frequency queries, 30 mid-tail, 20 long-tail/edge cases. for multilingual workloads ensure language parity in each bucket.n- include labeled ground-truth nearest neighbors for at least 2,000 items for recall and mrr calculations.nnpromotion checklist (pre-canary)nn1. automated offline eval: pass all gating thresholds on probe set prompt/context distribution shift, snapshot distribution and escalate to product/analytics.n4. remediation: rollback candidate or hotfix preprocessing/model code.nnownership and rolesnn- model owner: confluence, title: multi-probe-failure-classifier-and-automated-mitigation-manifest, content: summarynnthis document specifies the multi-probe failure classifier (mpfc) and the accompanying automated mitigation manifest. mpfc is a lightweight, explainable classifier that aggregates heterogeneous probe signals (functional, coherence, latency, token-economy, and quant-sensitivity probes) to categorize degradations and drive deterministic mitigation actions. the goal is to reduce time-to-recovery for production quality incidents while limiting blast radius for safety and customer-facing regressions.nnscopenn- applies to all model-serving promotion targets (hosted, dedicated, and private) where probe telemetry is ingested into the central eval mesh.n- focused on runtime performance and output quality regressions that can be observed via probe families (see definitions).n- not intended for manual labeling pipelines, data privacy incidents, or infra-only failures (see exception list).nndefinitionsnn1. probe: an automated query or synthetic interaction designed to exercise a specific slice of behavior (e.g., few-shot instruction consistency, long-context coherence, embedding similarity).n2. signal: a numerical or categorical feature emitted by a probe (e.g., pass/fail, perplexity delta, embedding cosine, token delta).n3. failure class: high-level category assigned by mpfc (coherence-drift, hallucination-spike, latency-tail, quant-artifact, behavioral-flip, routing-fallback).n4. mitigation: an automated operational action (e.g., rollback, throttle, route-to-variant, degrade-quant, increase-batch-window, open-chan).nnfailure taxonomy and classifier designnn- coherence-drift: multi-turn context coherence drops, measured via turn-level coherence score delta 8 and increase in repetition metric.n- hallucination-spike: increased factually-incorrect outputs flagged by synthetic fact-check probes (false positive rate increase 5 absolute).n- latency-tail: p95 latency 800ms or p99 2s for gen endpoints serving slo-sensitive routes.n- quant-artifact: sudden rise in token-level inconsistency between float and quant shadow runs (disagreement ratio 3).n- behavioral-flip: deterministic change in a labeled prompt family where label accuracy drops 7.n- routing-fallback: increased fallback-to-secondary-model events 4 of traffic.nnclassifier inputs and feature engineeringnn- inputs (examples): p95_ms, p99_ms, coherence_delta_pct, repetition_score_delta, fp_rate_delta, token_disagreement_pct, fallback_rate, embedding_shift_cosine, kvcache_hit_rate.n- time windows: compute short (5m), medium (1h), and trend (24h) aggregates. classifier uses delta between short and trend windows to detect sudden shifts.n- explainability: mpfc outputs a top-3 contributing signals per classification for operator triage.nnalerting and thresholdsnn- severity levels: p1 (customer-impacting, auto-mitigation allowed), p2 (degrades slos, require review before mitigation), p3 (informational).n- example thresholds (configurable per-service):nn metric p1 threshold p2 threshold note n------:---:---n p95 latency (ms) 1200 800-1200 slo-sensitive routes only n coherence_delta_pct 10 5-10 measured on prioritized slices n fp_rate_delta 6 abs 2-6 abs applies to fact-check probes n token_disagreement_pct 5 2-5 comparing quant vs float nnautomated mitigation flow (high level)nn1. detection: probe mesh emits a trigger event when classifier score configured severity threshold.n2. enrichment: mpfc fetches recent traces, model version tags, rollout state, shadow cohort metrics, and last-deploy commit.n3. scoring: compute confidence and top-3 reasons determine allowable mitigations based on service policy.n4. action: execute mitigation (examples below). actions are conditionally gated by safety checks and cooldown windows.n5. post-action evaluation: run focused sanity probes (micro-slice) against mitigated traffic and hold for 10 minutes. if metrics reference that defines allowed priming patterns (the priming safelist), a categorized catalog of lightweight sanity probes to run during onboarding and rollout, and concrete monitoring thresholds for detecting priming-induced fidelity regressions across quantized and cached serving environments.nnbody:nsummarynnpurpose: this document codifies a repeatable operational approach to validate that prompt priming (templates, system messages, and few-shot exemplars) does not introduce brittle behavior when models are deployed across mixed-precision, kv-cached, and prefix-cached runtime variants. it provides: a priming safelist (allowed patterns and constraints), a catalog of sanity probes grouped by failure mode, an onboarding checklist for model/prompts, and measurable alert thresholds for automated triage.nnscopen- applies to: model onboarding for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments eval harness shadow runs and rapid canary rollouts that include mixed-precision or kv-cache fallbacks.n- excludes: deep safety content audits (see safety-sandbox) and longtail human-in-the-loop annotation processes.nnkey definitionsn- priming: any fixed text injected into context prior to user input (system prompts, instructions, exemplars).n- priming-induced drift: reproducible change in task fidelity attributable to priming text interacting with model variant (quantized kernels, sequence-length changes, cache shards).n- sanity probe: a small, deterministic or semi-deterministic example used to detect regressions early in rollout.nnmotivationnpriming patterns that pass on a full-precision baseline can fail subtly when a model is quantized or served from a warmed kv cache. failures range from hallucination rate increases on factual probes to function-call argument corruption and response truncation. operational teams need a compact, automatable checklist and a short suite of probes that run quickly during shadow or micro-canary stages to avoid noisy rollouts.nnpriming safelist (operational constraints)n1) system-message length: prefer 1024 tokens in any onboarding evaluation. rationale: kernel dispatch decisions and cache priming penalties increase with system length.n2) exemplars: at most 3 exemplars per prompt for interactive routes prefer single-turn compact examples (max 60 tokens each).n3) structured instructions: when emitting json or function calls, include an explicit schema line (e.g., return a single json object matching schema:...) as the final priming line to anchor tokenization.n4) temperature-sensitive segments: avoid mixing high-entropy creative instructions inside the same priming block used for deterministic extraction tasks.n5) token budget anchors: reserve at least 20 of average route token budget for model output during micro-canary runs to detect truncation.n6) disallowed patterns: do not use dynamic time/date placeholders in priming text that mutate between shadow and prod runs (these create false positives).nnsanity catalog (fast probes to include in automation)ngroup a deterministic fidelity probes (run first 95 canonical-answer match on baseline model.n- json-schema emission (4 seeds): exact-match on keys and types for all seeds.nngroup b interaction/ordering probes (detect cache/priming order sensitivity)n- reordering sensitivity (5 seeds): prompt set where ordering of exemplars should not change discrete classification output.n- prefix collision probe: verify that inserted priming suffixes dont collide with tokenized user anchors.nngroup c quantization stress probes (detect precision-induced drift)n- numeric stability (6 seeds): arithmetic or numeric comparator tasks that historically regress under 4-bit quantization. threshold: median absolute error increase 80 of baseline flag if 98, group b pass rate 95, no group c probe exceeding severityhigh.nnrollout fallback policy (practical knobs)n- canary duration: default 48h with minimum 2000 routed inference calls or 2,000 probe samples, whichever comes first.n- auto-fallback triggers (automatic rollback to baseline variant):n - any group a probe regression 3 standard deviations over baseline for two consecutive windows (15m each).n - any group c numeric drift median 0.05 (mae) or functioncall structural failure rate 1.n - streaming/truncation alerts: if 0.5 of long-output probes return below 60 length for two consecutive hours.nnmonitoring alert thresholds (concrete values)n- probe pass-rate slo: 99.5 (monthly) for group a on production-critical routes.n- short-term alert: probe pass-rate drop 1.0 percentage point within 30 minutes triggers p1 review.n- numeric drift threshold: mae increase 0.03 triggers p2.n- functioncall schema mismatch rate 0.5 triggers p1 escalation.nnautomated triage playbook (quick steps for oncall)n1) confirm alert: open the associated probe run artifacts in eval-mesh and capture the diff heatmap.n2) check rollout stage: if canary, pause traffic and expand shadow sampling to increase probe density.n3) isolate vector: toggle quantization fallback to baseline (one click rollback) and re-run failing probes if failures stop, tag as quant-fidelity.n4) if toggling cache solves the issue, document cache-priming keys and apply prefix-shrink mitigation.n5) if unresolved, escalate to applied-ml oncall with artifacts and hypothesis matrix.nnownership and communicationn- primary owner: applied ml - model quality (team: applied-ml-quality).n- secondary owner: serving runtime (team: eng-serving-runtime) for kernel/quant issues.n- communications: any p1 must generate a one-paragraph status on the public incident channel and a retrospective doc within 7 days.nnexample quick commands and config snippetsn- run the priming safelist linter locally:n ri-eval lint-priming --file my_template.txt --ruleset safelist-2026n- run the compact sanity catalog against a candidate model (shadow):n ri-eval run --catalog sanity-catalog-compact --model candidate-v2 --variant quant-4bit --output artifacts/candidate-v2/sanity.json --parallel 8nnexample probe manifest entry (store as a one-line json in the eval-asset-registry):n probe_id:priming_json_schema_01,intent:json,seeds:4,expected_assertion:keys: id,items,total,severity:high,run_time_budget_ms:1200nnbest practices and mitigations (operational recommendations)n- keep priming texts compact and descriptive prefer a single final anchoring sentence that defines output format.n- when migrating to a quantized runtime, run numeric-stability probes with increased seed diversity to reduce variance.n- maintain a small stable set of group a probes mapped to each customer-critical route these provide the earliest warning for regressions.nnrelated pagesn- suggested remediationsn- hallucination spike paired with prefix-caching: shrink system prompt or whitelist caching for the route.n- functioncall key truncation under streaming: add explicit trailing document defines the eval sentinels framework: a set of lightweight, automated gates that run alongside the eval harness and model-onboarding flows to protect production-facing deployments from liveness failures, safety regressions, and unexpected cost spikes. sentinels are intentionally narrow, fast checks that synthesize telemetry across runtime, eval, and billing signals and provide deterministic gate outcomes (pass/warn/fail) used by promotion pipelines, canary controllers, and on-call routing.nngoals:n- provide a common taxonomy and configuration model for liveness, safety and cost sentinels used during model promotion and continuous evaluation.n- specify signal sources, thresholds, and action mappings (e.g., block promotion, notify sre, throttle traffic).n- describe integration points with the eval harness, ci/cd promotion rules, and console dashboards.n- define owner responsibilities and an operational runbook for sentinel trips.nnscope and non-goals:n- scope: model promotion (shadow - canary - prod), continuous eval jobs, lightweight preflight checks before production rollouts, and automated rollback triggers.n- non-goals: deep offline evaluation (full evaluation suites remain separate), model-level fairness certification (handled by safety team processes), or exhaustive cost forecasting (this complements cost recommendations in optimize).nnsentinel taxonomy (summary):n1) liveness sentineln - purpose: detect runtime regressions likely to cause application-visible timeouts or high error rates (o(100ms) checks).n - key signals: p50/p95/p99 token latency, request errors (5xx), kv-cache-miss-rate, stream fragmentation events.n - primary action: fail promotion or trigger immediate canary rollback if above failure thresholds.nn2) safety sentineln - purpose: detect sudden increases in unsafe outputs for high-risk prompt sets or instruction categories.n - key signals: safety-score delta on anchor prompt set, number of responses exceeding policy thresholds, classifier confidence drift.n - primary action: prevent rollout and open an assessment ticket optionally mark model as restricted for certain routes.nn3) cost sentineln - purpose: catch unexpected per-token cost increases or throughput inefficiencies that would materially affect unit economics.n - key signals: tokens-per-request rise, average gpu-seconds per request, batching efficiency drop, quantization fallback events.n - primary action: mark promotion as blocked with guidance to apply quantization/serving config or route to lower-cost variant.nn4) composite sentinelsn - purpose: infer correlated failures across categories (e.g., a safety classifier causing timeouts). composite rules combine multiple simple sentinels into higher-confidence gates.nnsignal sources and scoring, content: summarynnthis page defines a standardized failure taxonomy, a reproducibility-aware severity scoring rubric, and the downstream actions that link evaluation signals to regression triage and model-onboarding gates. the goal is to provide a common language for annotators, evaluators, sre/pl, and product owners so that incidents and degradations are prioritized consistently across the platform.nnwhy this mattersnn- diverse failure modes (factual errors, hallucinations, safety regressions, format breaks, latency spikes) are currently triaged inconsistently between teams.n- a shared taxonomy numeric severity score makes automated routing, alerting thresholds, and rollback decisions deterministic.n- this enables global dashboards, historical trending, and reproducible postmortems.nnscopenn- applies to: eval harness outputs, production shadow tests, quantization verification, canary reports, and manual annotator findings.n- not in scope: infra-only outages (use eng-sre runbooks) or billing anomalies (finance).nn1) high-level taxonomy (canonical tags)nneach failure must be labeled with one or more canonical tags from the list below. tags are ordered for human readability triage systems treat them as independent booleans. use these exact tag keys in metadata and telemetry: nn- factualityn- hallucination (content invented with no source)n- safety (policy-violating or toxic)n- privacy-leak (pii or secret exfiltration)n- semantic-mismatch (intent vs. response mismatch)n- formatting-error (structured output / json / code malformed)n- repetition (undesired verbatim repetition or looping)n- latency-regressionn- tokenization-anomalyn- embeddability-regression (embedding stability / drift)n- rerank-degradation (ranking ordering quality drop)n- incoherence-multi-turn (short-term state drift across turns)n- quant-artifact (errors correlated with quantized artifacts)n- coverage-gap (missing support for a language/slot/context)nn2) severity dimensions and scoring inputsnnseverity is derived from three orthogonal dimensions: impact, incidence, and reproducibility. each dimension is scored 04 and then converted to a combined severity band (s1 - s5). the dimensions are defined as: nn- impact (04): how customer-visible and harmful the failure is. 0 negligible ui noise 4 data loss, privacy breach, or dangerous advice.n- incidence (04): fraction of requests/samples that exhibit the failure in the measured slice. 0 rare (20).n- reproducibility (04): how reliably a human/automated replay can reproduce the failure. 0 non-deterministic single-flaky outputs 4 deterministic on replayed inputs or deterministic in production telemetry.nnscoring guideline table (for annotators):nn- impact: 4 (severe) explicit privacy leak / potentially harmful instruction / data corruption 3 strongly customer-facing incorrectness or major format break 2 visible but recoverable error 1 minor phrasing/fluency regression 0 cosmetic.n- incidence: 4 (20), 3 (520), 2 (15), 1 (0.011), 0 ( 48 or any privacy-leak with impact 3.n- s2 (action: block model promotion urgent hotfix sprint): numeric_score between 24 and 47.n- s3 (action: triage within 48h, create focused eval/metric): 1223.n- s4 (action: track in backlog, monitor): 411.n- s5 (action: informational, low priority): 03.nnnote: thresholds are intentionally conservative for safety and privacy tags any safety or privacy tag with impact 2 automatically elevates band by one.nn4) annotator and evaluator contract (step-by-step)nn1. when an evaluator or annotator encounters a failing sample, they must assign at least one canonical tag.n2. for each tag, score impact, incidence, and reproducibility according to the guidelines above.n3. provide a short evidence snippet ( 0.12 for the slice.n- latency spike detector: flag latency-regression if 95th percentile increases by 30 vs baseline for the model version.n- quant-artifact heuristic: compare full-precision vs quantized answer divergence on seeded prompts if bleu/rouge drops threshold or hallucination rate increases, flag quant-artifact.nneach heuristic must emit structured evidence (e.g., diffs, parsing errors, index links) to support reproducibility scoring.nn6) mapping tags and bands to runbooks ownersnn- s1 (privacy-leak or safety severe): page oncall (eng-sre primary, security secondary) and follow security incident procedure: /oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.n- s1/s2 quant-artifact or factuality widespread: product applied-ml (owners: model-onboarding) must open a promotion-blocker issue and run rapid shadowed replay.n- s2/s3 formatting-error or rerank-degradation: eng-platform and sdk teams own rollout mitigation (schema-linting, input sanitization).n- s3s4 incoherence or repetition: ml research/applied-ml to schedule a focused eval and candidate mitigating prompts.nn7) dashboards and derived metricsnnminimum dashboard surfaces (slos and kpis):nn- top-10 tags by weekly occurrence (normalized by request volume).n- mean severity band per model version (30-day rolling).n- time-to-triage (median days from detection to owner assignment). target: 0.8 for s2 incidents.nn8) integration with model onboarding gatesnn- graduation block: any s1 or repeated s2 within a promotion candidates shadow-eval period blocks promotion.n- quantization check: require a quant-awareness test suite that runs the automated heuristics above and enforces no net increase in hallucination rate 0.5 for production-critical slices.nn9) example workflowsnna. automated detection - annotator - s2 casen1. heuristic flags 2 of support-chat samples with new citation hallucinations.n2. samples route to annotators via the eval-harness queue.n3. annotators confirm tags and scores (impact3, incidence2, reproducibility3).n4. numeric score maps to s2. automated policy creates a promotion-blocker ticket and notifies owners.nnb. canary anomaly - rapid triage - s1 escalationn1. canary telemetry shows 95th pctl latency spike 40 with correlated formatting-error in responses.n2. runbook recommends immediate canary rollback if slo breach plus formatting-error confirmed in 5 of canary traffic.n3. after rollback, run secondary diagnostic to determine whether model change or infra degradation caused the break.nn10) operational notes and caveatsnn- human judgment is intentionally part of the process: the scoring rubric guides but does not replace expert escalation.n- avoid double-counting: when multiple tags apply, use the highest-impact tag for policy decisions but retain all tags in metadata for analytics.n- periodically (quarterly) review the tag set add new tags when recurring failure modes are observed.nnownership and maintenancenn- primary owner: applied ml (evals) anjali rao.n- secondary owners: eng-platform, eng-sre, security (for privacy/safety tags).n- review cadence: quarterly taxonomy review after any major s1 incident.nnappendix: quick reference cheat sheetnn- privacy leaks and safety always elevate severity.n- impact score drives urgency reproducibility multiplies confidence.n- use tag keys exactly as listed when storing metadata.n- if in doubt, escalate to model-oncall do not promote models that have s1 or repeated s2s in their shadow probe privacy budget and annotation retention playbook, content: overviewnnthis playbook defines redwood inferences operational approach to (1) managing privacy budgets for live and synthetic probes, (2) retention policies and purge workflows for annotations and raw probe artifacts, and (3) cost-control guardrails for probe-driven evaluation pipelines. it is intended for ml engineers, evaluators, sre, and security/compliance reviewers.nngoalsnn- protect customer data and limit privacy risk from probes while preserving evaluation fidelity.n- maintain a clear, auditable retention lifecycle for probe artifacts and annotation datasets.n- constrain evaluation costs by enforcing budgeted probe storage and annotation spending.n- provide an operator runbook for retention changes, emergency purges, and privacy incidents.nnscopenn- applies to all probe sources used in the eval harness: shadow traffic probes, synthetic probe farms, and field-captured debug probes.n- covers raw inputs (payloads, transcripts), derived artifacts (tokenized inputs, embeddings, model outputs), human annotations, and evaluation metrics/telemetry.n- integrations: probe ingestion pipeline (probe-ingest), annotation service (annotate-v2), eval-orchestrator, telemetry-warehouse (events-db), and kms-backed storage.nnkey concepts and definitionsnn- probe: any request/record used to evaluate model behavior. includes synthetic seeds, mirrored production calls, and targeted adversarial probes.n- privacy budget: a quantified allowance (dp epsilon or equivalent policy) used to bound cumulative privacy exposure for a dataset or customer. we track budgets per-customer (when applicable) and per-probe-catalog.n- annotation ttl: time-to-live for label data and raw artifacts before automatic purging.nnpolicy summary (defaults)nn1) privacy budget regime:n - live customer-shadow probes: treat as customer data default policy: do not retain raw payload beyond 72 hours without explicit opt-in. apply aggregation/minimization and register to customers privacy budget.n - production-mirrored probes (anonymized): retain for 30 days by default, subject to dp noise injection if aggregated exports leave the secure environment.n - synthetic probe farms: no customer pii expected default retention for raw probe generation seeds is 365 days.nn2) annotation retention and classification:n - raw artifacts (audio, full request bodies): default ttl 30 days for non-sensitive probes, 7 days for any probe marked sensitive.n - transcripts, tokenized inputs: ttl 180 days.n - human labels and annotation metadata: ttl 540 days (annotations are more expensive to reproduce).n - aggregated metrics/counters: retained indefinitely in compressed form but with no per-request identifiers.nn3) storage protections:n - all retained artifacts must be encrypted at rest with customer-specific kms keys when tied to identifiable customers.n - access requires iam-based approval and just-in-time ephemeral credentials for annotators.nnretention table (defaults)nn artifact type default ttl encryption notes n------:------n raw request body (sensitive) 7 days customer kms marked when payload contains sensitive pii or is customer-linked n raw request body (non-sensitive) 30 days platform kms e.g., synthetic probes with no ids n transcript / tokenized input 180 days platform kms useful for debugging and model regression triage n model outputs (per-request) 180 days platform kms strip request identifiers before export n annotations (human labels) 540 days platform kms consider snapshot and archiving before purge n aggregated metrics indefinite (compressed) n/a no per-request linkage stored in telemetry-warehouse nnoperational controls and enforcementnn- probe catalog registration: every probe set must be registered in the probe-catalog service with metadata: owner, sensitivity flag, expected ttl, privacy budget owner, and estimated storage footprint. the eval-orchestrator rejects scheduling for unregistered probe sets.nn- automated ttl enforcement: the retention-worker runs daily and performs three actions: (a) mark items for deletion, (b) publish deletion plan to audit-log, (c) execute deletions in batch during a low-cost window (02:0004:00 pt). deletions are soft by default (tombstone) for 48 hours to allow emergency recovery via a documented approval flow.nn- privacy budget accounting:n - for datasets touching live customer data we maintain per-dataset cumulative epsilon as a metadata field in probe-catalog. the privacy-accountant job increments budget when probes are stored or exported. exports that would exceed configured epsilon are blocked.n - for dp mechanisms, annotate operators must add the dp parameters used (epsilon, delta) and attach the proof-of-noise job id to the dataset metadata.nncost guardrailsnn- storage caps: each probe-catalog entry must include a storage cap. if a catalog exceeds 80 of cap, alert to probe-owner and auto-halt new probe ingestion for that catalog.n- annotation spend slo: annotation projects must include a budget and estimated cost-per-label. if monthly spend reaches 90 of the project budget, the annotation pipeline pauses new assignments and notifies the owner.n- archival policy for cold artifacts: artifacts older than 90 days and below access thresholds are moved to cold-backed storage (lower cost) with a 30 day retrieval window and an additional retrieval fee applied to owners cost center.nnexamples (commands and sql)nn- register a new probe catalog entry (cli snippet):nn probe_catalog, artifact_type, count() as objects, sum(size_bytes)/pow(1024,3) as size_gbn from probe_artifactsn where created_at date_sub(now(), interval 365 day)n group by 1,2nn- soft-delete workflow (operator steps):n 1) retention-worker marks items and emits deletion_plan:id to /audit-log.n 2) probe owner has 48 hrs to request recovery: redwood-probe recover --plan-id id --approval-token ticket.n 3) after 48 hrs, deletion-job executes and emits deletion_complete to /audit-log.nnrunbook: emergency purge (data breach or legal takedown)nn1) trigger: security or legal escalation with ticket and owner confirmation.n2) action: run emergency-purge job with provided filters (customer_id or request_id).n - cli: redwood-probe emergency-purge --filter customer_id12345 --reason legal-takedown-2024-11 --urgentn3) the job runs immediate hard delete (no soft tombstone). all changes recorded to audit-log and retention-audit s3 bucket.n4) post-action: notify compliance legal rotate kms keys if keys were suspected compromised perform snapshot for incident review and then shred it per evidence retention policy.nnmonitoring and alertsnn- metrics to emit:n - probe_artifacts.total_size_gb (by catalog)n - probe_artifacts.objects_marked_for_deletion_countn - annotation.monthly_spend_by_projectn - privacy_budget.remaining_epsilon (by dataset)n - retention_worker.run_latency_secondsnn- alert rules (examples):n - storage cap exceeded: fire if probe_artifacts.total_size_gb storage_cap 0.9 for 5m.n - annotation budget near limit: fire if change to default ttls or privacy-budget defaults must go through: (a) proposal (adr template) - (b) security review - (c) staging rollout for 2 weeks - (d) production rollout with 7-day observation window.n- owners must update probe-catalog entries when ttls change retention-worker supports versioned retention policies so older artifacts respect the policy that was active at creation time unless safety contract, content: overviewnthis page defines the safety contract and operational playbook for rolling quantized model artifacts into production using a probe-first approach. the contract is intended for model onboarding, release engineers, and the eval-harness team. it applies to: per-layer and end-to-end quant conversions mixed-precision fallbacks and token/kv-cache-sensitive variants.nngoalsn- ensure user-visible quality regressions are constrained within an agreed fidelity budget.n- provide deterministic, observable gating for canary and progressive rollouts.n- minimize blast radius by coupling probes, telemetry, and automated fallback logic.nnscope and risk modeln- scope: inference artifacts served via redwood runtime (hosted, dedicated, private) where a quantized binary replaces a floating-point baseline. includes customer-facing endpoints, internal eval shadows, and long-context workloads.n- not in scope: offline batch scoring jobs (separate migration policy), model architecture changes.n- principal risks: semantic drift, hallucination rate increase, latency regressions on small-batch/interactive tails, kv cache incompatibilities.nndefinitionsn- baseline: the currently promoted (non-quant or prior-quant) model artifact used for comparison.n- probe: a curated test case (automated or human-labeled) representing slices of production traffic used to measure quality metrics.n- fidelity budget: numeric thresholds of acceptable deltas (see acceptance criteria).nnownershipn- model owner: product/ml engineer who requests quant rollout. responsible for probe set curation and initial evaluation artifacts.n- eval-harness team: implements probes, schedules shadow runs, and computes metrics.n- runtime/sre: configures rollout routing, caching policies, and automated fallback triggers.n- release engineer: executes promotion steps and signs off on exceptions.nnacceptance criteria (safety contract)nall conditions must be satisfied for promotion from validation - canary - staged - ga.n1) functional correctness: intent-preserving metrics must remain within the fidelity budget compared to baseline on the production-proxy probe suite:n - semantic similarity (sbert cosine) baseline - 0.02 or absolute 0.90n - task accuracy (where labeled) baseline - 1.5 percentage pointsn - safety/suppression tests: no new high-severity safety failures introduced (severity 1)n2) latency resource:n - median token latency 0.05 across 10k long-context probesn - determinism seeds: identical prompts under deterministic setting must match baseline behavior with baseline) with health-check cooldown of 30sn - telemetry events emitted for quant_migration_probe.result, quant_fallback.triggered, quant_rollout.progressnnprobe design guidelinesn- maintain a prioritized probe portfolio:n - hot slices: 50k daily samples for latency-sensitive prompts (short, api-driven paths).n - long-context: 20k probes with 2k token histories to stress kv cache and attention speedups.n - function-call and structured-output probes: 5k examples covering common schema shapes.n - safety and red-team seeds: 10k fuzz/adversarial probes maintained by security applied ml.nn- labeling and thresholds:n - each probe includes: prompt, expected intent, baseline response fingerprint (hash), and reference metric values.n - use aggregated metrics with confidence intervals (95 ci). accept if ci upper bound meets acceptance criteria.nnrollout plan (procedure)n1) local quant validation (model-owner)n - run local quant conversion and unit tests. generate local evaluator report (artifact: quant_local_report.json).n - quick checks: shape/ops parity, seed determinism smoke tests, sample inference on 100 probes.n2) shadow validation (eval-harness)n - schedule 48h shadow against production-proxy probe suite. compare metrics to baseline.n - generate runbook comments and open pr to promote to canary if pass.n3) canary (1 traffic or 0.5 depending on tenant sensitivity)n - duration: 4 hours minimum. monitor metrics over 5-minute windows.n - automatic abort conditions:n - runtime error rate increase 0.5pp absolute or 2x baselinen - semantic similarity delta 0.03n - latency p99 increase 2x baseline or 3s absoluten - if abort triggers, traffic routed to baseline immediately and release engineer notified.n4) staged ramp (1 - 5 - 20 - 50 - 100)n - each step minimum 6 hours, or longer for high-risk slices.n - at each step, run full probe-suite and the lightweight smoke probes require automated checks to pass.n5) ga promotionn - final artifact signed, release notes posted, and quant artifact retained in artifact registry with tags: quantized, promotor, baseline_hash.nnautomated fallback runbookn- fallback logic (runtime): a rule set in the router that evaluates telemetry windows and flips traffic to the configured fallback artifact.n- emergency rollback steps (manual):n 1. open incident on prod-model-rollouts and tag model owner runtime oncall.n 2. trigger immediate route reassign: curl -x post -d route:/v1/generate,to:baseline-artifact-idn 3. validate baseline responses on 100 smoke probes.n 4. create postmortem and hold a triage meeting within 48 hours.nntelemetry, dashboards and alertsn- required telemetry exports:n - quant_migration_probe.result: probe_id, slice, metric_vector, delta_from_baseline, pass_failn - quant_rollout.progress: artifact_id, percent_traffic, step, timestampn - quant_fallback.triggered: artifact_id, reason, metric_snapshotn- dashboards (names):n - quant migration overview (team: eval-harness)n - quant canary health (team: runtime/sre)n - kv-cache divergence monitor (team: serving)n- alert thresholds (examples):n - alert: quant_canary_semantic_regression if semantic_similarity_delta pager to runtime oncalln - alert: quant_canary_error_spike if error_rate 1.0 for 5m - slack pagernnmetrics table (exemplar)n metric baseline target acceptable delta alert document defines the compression-aware probe suite (caps) and the quant sensitivity fingerprint (qsf) used to characterize how model outputs degrade or change under quantized artifacts and compression-friendly runtime transforms. caps is intended to be run during model onboarding, pre-rollout checks, and continuous regression scans for dedicated/private deployments where quantization and mixed-precision paths are used. qsf is a compact, reproducible vector of metrics that summarizes per-workload sensitivity and drives rollout gating, remediation recommendations, and perf/cost tradeoff ui.nngoals and scopen----------------n- provide a deterministic, reproducible probe generation and scoring pipeline that surfaces subtle behavioral changes introduced by quantization (post-training quant, dynamic quant, mixed-precision) and compression transforms (activation compression, kv-cache serialization).n- produce an interpretable fingerprint (qsf) per modelprofileworkload that is stable across seeds and informative to engineers and product owners.n- integrate with the eval harness and ci to: (1) block unsafe rollouts, (2) suggest fallback quant-profiles, and (3) prioritize human review slices.nnwhen to run capsn------------------n1. model onboarding (initial candidate promotion to shadow/dedicated).n2. before enabling a new quant profile or runtime compression optimization in production.n3. nightly regression scans focused on quant-related slices.n4. on-demand triage when a production regression correlates with a quant deployment.nnhigh-level componentsn---------------------n1. probe generator: produces canonical inputs (prompt families) using mutation operators.n2. multi-mode runner: executes model variants (fp16/fp32, int8, int8kv-compress, mixed-precision) through the eval harness with matched seeds and deterministic sampling where applicable.n3. metric synthesizer: computes per-probe metrics and aggregates into the qsf vector.n4. triager ruleset: maps qsf deltas to recommended remediation steps and rollout gate outcomes.nnprobe generator detailsn-----------------------n- prompt families covered (each family contains 5002000 seeds):n - long-context priming: multi-turn histories with varying pivot lengths (1k, 4k, 8k tokens).n - short-instruction: terse one-line instructions for copy/transform tasks.n - table/structured-output: prompts that request json/yaml outputs and strict schema conformance.n - retrieval-primed: prompts with embedded retrieved passages that exercise kv cache reuse.n - math/precision: numerical reasoning and formula manipulation.n - safety probes: adversarial paraphrases and hallucination triggers.n- mutation operators: token-level dropout, synonym substitution, punctuation perturbation, casing/noise injection, and answer-mask perturbation to probe stability under boundary conditions.n- sampling strategy: stratified by token-length, by expected generation length, and by instruction complexity score (01).nnexecution matrixn----------------n- model variants to compare (example): fp32-reference, fp16, int8-static, int8-dynamic, mixed-precision-layerwise, int8kv-compress.n- deterministic seeds where sampling-based metrics are compared stochastic runs for downstream human-facing diversity checks.n- runtime modes: streaming vs non-streaming to catch prefix-dependent quant artifacts.nnmetrics and how qsf is computedn-------------------------------ncaps computes the following per-probe metrics qsf aggregates them into a fixed-length vector (string-labeled metrics). each metric is averaged using trimmed-mean (10 trim) across seeds.n- embeddingdistancemean: mean cosine distance between reference fp32 embeddings and quantized variant embeddings for the same prompt (embedding model: model@last-layer-average).n- outputtokenfliprate: percent of tokens where argmax(token) differs from reference, normalized by token-length.n- logitdelta90: 90th percentile absolute change in top-5 logits for the first n tokens (n configurable, default 32).n- schemaintegrityrate: fraction of structured-output probes that parse to expected json schema without correction.n- generationdivergenceindex (gdi): bleu/rouge-style metric adapted for free-form computed as 1 - normalized semantic similarity (embedding-based) so higher is worse.n- scalinglatencyimpact: relative change in median latency under workload-aware batching when using quantized kernels (used for perf/cost tradeoffs).n- kvcachemismatchrate: percent of retrieval-primed probes where the final answer differs when the kv cache path is enabled vs disabled in the quantized runtime.nnqsf vector example (ascii):nembeddingdistancemean:0.012, outputtokenfliprate:0.043, logitdelta90:0.18, schemaintegrityrate:0.92, gdi:0.06, scalinglatencyimpact:-0.12, kvcachemismatchrate:0.014nninterpreting qsf and thresholdsn-------------------------------n- threshold bands (per-metric example defaults):n - green (safe): embeddingdistancemean 0.97, gdi allow rollout.n 2. any metric in yellow but no metric in red - canary rollout with 5 traffic manual review of top-3 slices flagged.n 3. any metric in red - block and create incident ticket assigned to serving-quant-team.nnintegration with eval harness and cin-----------------------------------n- caps exports a machine-readable qsf json artifact per job and a human-readable pdf summary with the top-10 failed probes and sample transcripts.n- suggested ci step: compare qsf against baseline qsf artifact using a tolerant comparator that respects metric covariances. failing jobs should not auto-promote.n- example cli invocation (eval harness adapter):n rwi-eval run --suite caps --model model:v3-7 --variants fp32,int8,int8-kv --out qsf.json --seeds 42,43,44 --report pdfnnexample qsf yaml snippet used by gating servicen----------------------------------------------n param value n--------------n gating_policy quant-cautious n allowed_yellow_metrics embeddingdistancemean,scalinglatencyimpact n blocked_red_metrics schemaintegrityrate,kvcachemismatchrate nn(implementation note: stored in the rollout service as plain yaml use the eval-harness comparator library to compute deltas.)nnrecommended remediation playbookn--------------------------------n1. if schemaintegrityrate drops: revert to earlier quant-profile that preserves structured decoders, or enable output-constrained decoding (beam constraints / format validators).n2. if embeddingdistancemean increases but token flip rate is low: prefer hybrid-embedding-recompute (recompute embedding reference on the quantized path for similarity-based downstreams) and add embedding-stable calibration layer.n3. if kvcachemismatchrate threshold: audit kv serialization path and test with different cache serialization precisions consider disabling aggressive kv compression for affected layers.n4. if latency improves but gdi increases: surface cost/perf tradeoff to product owner and consider partial rollout with fallback routing for safety-sensitive routes.nnownership and runbook triggersn-----------------------------n- primary owner: applied-ml (probe infra) team. secondary: serving-quant team.n- slos for caps jobs:n - caps job completion (nightly run): 95 jobs finish within 3 hours per model family.n - qsf artifact availability: 99 within 10 minutes of job completion.n- runbook triggers (automated):n - new qsf with any red metric - create p1 ticket to serving-quant on slack pagerduty paging to oncall in the quant rotation.n - canary rollout flagging yellow metrics - open a canary review task and schedule a 1-hour deep-dive with model owner and serving engineer.nnreporting and dashboardsn------------------------n- qsf time-series: track per-model, per-profile qsf metrics and highlight metric drift beyond 3-sigma over a 14-day window.n- heatmap: compression-sensitivity heatmap by probe family (rows probe family, cols quant profile) showing delta in gdi.n- example dashboard panels to create:n - top failing probes table (probe id, metric, delta, example transcript).n any canary with yellow or red metrics, generate an annotation packet with: 10 representative probes, reference transcripts, quantized transcripts, and an embedding-based divergence explanation.n- human reviewers should answer: (1) are the failures semantic or surface-level? (2) do safety or correctness slices exist? (3) can a prompt rewrite or output filter mitigate? record decisions in the review artifact.nnexamples and quick-startn------------------------n1) run baseline caps locally (dev):n - rwi-eval local and numerically sensitive tasks.nnint8: int8 quantization modes (often with tighter shape constraints and more calibration sensitivity). int8 is treated as cost-first with higher quality and correctness risk unless the model family and workload are known-safe.nnbaseline: bf16/fp16 (or equivalent) non-quantized kernels used as quality reference and fallback.nnevals sign-off: written quantization autotuning workflow plus safety validators and rollout criteria for model serving at redwood. this doc codifies the tests, thresholds, and fallback policies to use when generating per-workload quantization profiles and before promoting profiles to production.nnscopen- applies to all encoder-decoder and decoder-only language models onboarded to redwood dedicated and redwood
